nodes.summary: Case class join operator extending HashJoin that executes the streamed side against a broadcast HashedRelation, with BuildSide, skew flag and optional null-aware anti join.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Requires UnspecifiedDistribution for the streamed side and BroadcastDistribution (HashedRelationBroadcastMode) for the build side, or a null-aware variant.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Derives the join's output partitioning from the streamed side, expanded through key mappings for inner and similar join types.

nodes.name: expandOutputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Expands a streamed-side partitioning into alternatives by substituting equivalent build-side join keys.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Row-based execution: broadcasts the build relation to the streamed partitions and joins each streamed partition against it, including null-aware anti join handling.

nodes.name: prepareBroadcast
nodes.summary: Codegen helper that registers the broadcast variable and returns its reference for generated code.

nodes.name: codegenAnti
nodes.summary: Generates Java code for the anti join variants, including the null-aware anti join fast path.

nodes.name: ShuffledHashJoinExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical hash join that shuffles both inputs by join keys, builds a HashedRelation from the build side per partition and probes it with the streamed side. Includes interpreted and whole-stage-codegen paths for build-side and full outer joins, with unique-key and non-unique-key variants.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object ShuffledHashJoinExec (lines 663-685) supplies the apply factory; it shares the class name so it has no separate node. The class mixes in HashJoin and ShuffledJoin and disambiguates members with super[ShuffledJoin].

nodes.name: ShuffledHashJoinExec
nodes.summary: Case class join operator mixing HashJoin and ShuffledJoin: builds an in-memory hash relation from the build side for each shuffled partition and probes it with streamed rows.

nodes.name: outputOrdering
nodes.summary: Determines output ordering preserved from the streamed side for the given join type.

nodes.name: validCondForIgnoreDupKey
nodes.summary: Checks whether a join condition only references build-side keys so duplicate build keys can be ignored for semi/anti joins.

nodes.name: buildHashedRelation
nodes.summary: Builds the HashedRelation from build-side rows, tracking size and time metrics and optionally ignoring duplicate keys.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Zips the shuffled partitions of both children and joins each pair using the build/probe flow or the full outer join path.

nodes.name: buildSideOrFullOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Executes build-side outer and full outer joins in interpreted mode, choosing the unique-key or non-unique-key algorithm.

nodes.name: buildSideOrFullOuterJoinUniqueKey
nodes.summary: Interpreted build-side or full outer join for relations with unique keys, tracking matched build rows in a BitSet.

nodes.name: buildSideOrFullOuterJoinNonUniqueKey
nodes.summary: Interpreted build-side or full outer join for relations with non-unique keys, tracking matched rows and emitting unmatched build rows at the end.

nodes.name: doProduce
nodes.summary: Whole-stage codegen producer: builds the hash relation then emits code that consumes streamed rows, dispatching to join-type specific codegen.

nodes.name: codegenBuildSideOrFullOuterJoinWithUniqueKey
nodes.summary: Generates Java code for build-side or full outer joins on unique-key relations, including the matched-row bitset and final unmatched scan.

nodes.name: codegenBuildSideOrFullOuterJoinNonUniqueKey
nodes.summary: Generates Java code for build-side or full outer joins on non-unique-key relations with per-key match tracking.

nodes.name: SortMergeJoinExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical sort merge join that requires both children shuffled and sorted by the join keys and merges them with a streaming scanner. Contains the class, its whole-stage codegen for all join types, and the SortMergeJoinScanner and outer-join iterator helpers shared with the interpreted evaluator.
nodes.languageNotes: Several helper classes are private[joins] or private so they can be shared with SortMergeJoinEvaluatorFactory in the same package. About 50 methods exist; only the main planning, codegen and scanner entry points are given nodes.

nodes.name: SortMergeJoinExec
nodes.summary: Case class extending ShuffledJoin that merges two sorted, co-partitioned inputs; implements ordering requirements, spill thresholds, interpreted execution through an evaluator factory and extensive whole-stage codegen.

nodes.name: outputOrdering
nodes.summary: Computes output ordering by join type, preserving left or right key orderings where valid.

nodes.name: getKeyOrdering
nodes.summary: Derives the ordering of join keys from the child's output ordering, used to reuse existing sort orders.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Builds a SortMergeJoinEvaluatorFactory with spill thresholds and metrics and zips the left and right partitions, using partition evaluators when enabled.

nodes.name: genScanner
nodes.summary: Generates codegen state and methods for the merge scan: key comparison, advancing the streamed and buffered sides and buffering matches.

nodes.name: doProduce
nodes.summary: Whole-stage codegen producer that routes to inner, outer, semi, anti, existence or full outer code generation.

nodes.name: codegenInner
nodes.summary: Generates code for inner sort merge joins.

nodes.name: codegenOuter
nodes.summary: Generates code for left and right outer sort merge joins.

nodes.name: codegenSemi
nodes.summary: Generates code for left semi sort merge joins.

nodes.name: codegenAnti
nodes.summary: Generates code for left anti sort merge joins.

nodes.name: codegenExistence
nodes.summary: Generates code for existence joins that output a boolean match column.

nodes.name: codegenFullOuter
nodes.summary: Generates code for full outer sort merge joins with two-sided buffering and null padding.

nodes.name: SortMergeJoinScanner
nodes.summary: Helper that scans two sorted row iterators, buffering all rows with equal join keys from the buffered side and exposing findNextInnerJoinRows and findNextOuterJoinRows.

nodes.name: findNextInnerJoinRows
nodes.summary: Advances both inputs until the next matching key and buffers matching rows from the buffered side.

nodes.name: findNextOuterJoinRows
nodes.summary: Like inner scan but returns streamed rows with an empty match set when no buffered rows match.

nodes.name: bufferMatchingRows
nodes.summary: Buffers all rows from the buffered side sharing the current join key, optionally only the first match.

nodes.name: LeftOuterIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator specialization for left outer joins that sets the streamed output on the left and buffered output on the right.

nodes.name: RightOuterIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator specialization for right outer joins that swaps the streamed and buffered output sides.

nodes.name: OneSideOuterIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract RowIterator for one-sided outer joins that applies the bound condition and emits null-padded rows for unmatched streamed rows.

nodes.name: SortMergeFullOuterJoinScanner
nodes.summary: Scanner for full outer sort merge joins that advances both sides, buffers equal-key rows from each and tracks matches.

nodes.name: FullOuterIterator
nodes.summary: RowIterator that wraps SortMergeFullOuterJoinScanner and projects results while counting output rows.

nodes.name: expressions.scala
nodes.summary: Catalyst optimizer rules that simplify and rewrite expressions inside logical plans: constant folding and propagation, boolean and conditional simplification, null propagation, cast and string simplifications. All 16 rule objects and the SupportedBinaryExpr extractor are represented as nodes. These rules are listed in Optimizer.defaultBatches.
nodes.languageNotes: Each rule is a singleton object extending Rule[LogicalPlan] and uses transformWithPruning with TreePattern bits so the rule is skipped for plans that cannot match.

nodes.name: joins.scala
nodes.summary: Catalyst optimizer rules for joins (ReorderJoin, EliminateOuterJoin, ExtractPythonUDFFromJoinCondition) plus JoinSelectionHelper, the shared logic for choosing broadcast or shuffled hash join build sides from size and hints. All rules and helpers in the file are represented.
nodes.languageNotes: JoinSelectionHelper is a trait mixed into planner strategies; BuildSide is a sealed ADT with case objects BuildLeft and BuildRight.

nodes.name: ConstantFolding
nodes.summary: Replaces foldable expressions with equivalent Literal values by evaluating them at optimization time, taking care with conditional branches and side effects.

nodes.name: ConstantPropagation
nodes.summary: Substitutes attributes with constants inferred from equality predicates in AND conditions, for example turning x = 1 AND y > x into x = 1 AND y > 1.

nodes.name: ReorderAssociativeOperator
nodes.summary: Flattens and reorders associative Add and Multiply chains so literals are grouped together and can be folded.

nodes.name: OptimizeIn
nodes.summary: Optimizes IN predicates: empty lists become false, duplicate literals are removed, and large literal lists are converted to InSet.

nodes.name: BooleanSimplification
nodes.summary: Simplifies boolean expressions using identities, De Morgan style rewrites and common-factor extraction for AND/OR/NOT.

nodes.name: SimplifyBinaryComparison
nodes.summary: Simplifies binary comparisons whose operands are semantically equal (for example a = a becomes true for non-nullable inputs) and prunes redundant constraints.

nodes.name: SimplifyConditionals
nodes.summary: Simplifies If, CaseWhen and related conditional expressions when conditions are constant or branches are redundant.

nodes.name: PushFoldableIntoBranches
nodes.summary: Pushes unary and binary expressions with a foldable operand into the branches of If and CaseWhen so each branch can be constant folded.

nodes.name: SupportedBinaryExpr
nodes.summary: Extractor object that matches binary expressions with one foldable side that PushFoldableIntoBranches may push into conditional branches.

nodes.name: LikeSimplification
nodes.summary: Rewrites LIKE and multi-LIKE patterns into cheaper StartsWith, EndsWith, Contains or equality checks when the pattern allows.

nodes.name: NullPropagation
nodes.summary: Propagates null literals and nullability facts through expressions, aggregates and conditionals, removing unnecessary null checks.

nodes.name: NullDownPropagation
nodes.summary: Pushes IsNull and IsNotNull down through null-intolerant expressions to their children so they can be evaluated and pruned earlier.

nodes.name: FoldablePropagation
nodes.summary: Replaces attribute references with foldable aliases defined in lower Project or Aggregate operators, for example in ORDER BY and similar operators.

nodes.name: SimplifyCasts
nodes.summary: Removes redundant Cast expressions when the source and target types are identical or the cast is a safe widening.

nodes.name: SimplifyCaseConversionExpressions
nodes.summary: Collapses nested upper and lower case conversion calls where the inner conversion is made irrelevant by the outer one.

nodes.name: SimplifyDateTimeConversions
nodes.summary: Removes redundant date and time conversion function chains such as nested timestamp conversions.

nodes.name: CombineConcats
nodes.summary: Flattens nested Concat expressions into a single Concat and folds literal-only concatenations.

nodes.name: ReorderJoin
nodes.summary: Reorders inner joins and pushes filter conditions into join conditions so lower joins have at least one condition, optionally using star schema detection to avoid cartesian products.

nodes.name: EliminateOuterJoin
nodes.summary: Converts or removes outer joins when predicates reject null-supplied rows, when an aggregate is duplicate-agnostic, or when unique join keys make the join redundant.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFFromJoinCondition
nodes.summary: Moves Python UDF calls out of join conditions into a Filter above the join, since Python UDFs cannot be evaluated in join conditions.

nodes.name: BuildSide
nodes.summary: Sealed abstract class of the hash join build side ADT; its case objects BuildRight and BuildLeft are defined right after it (lines 286-288).

nodes.name: JoinSelectionHelper
nodes.summary: Trait with shared logic for picking a broadcast or shuffled hash join build side based on join type, size thresholds, statistics and user join hints.

nodes.name: Exchange.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract Exchange operator, the base of all data-movement physical operators (shuffle, broadcast), plus ReusedExchangeExec, a leaf wrapper that reuses an existing exchange under a different set of output attribute ids.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class plus a case class with overridden SparkPlan hooks (doExecute, doExecuteColumnar, doExecuteBroadcast) that delegate to the wrapped child.

nodes.name: Exchange
nodes.summary: Abstract unary physical operator that is the root of all exchange operators; passes through its child's output, tags itself with the EXCHANGE tree pattern and adds the plan id to its string arguments.

nodes.name: ReusedExchangeExec
nodes.summary: Leaf operator that wraps an already-planned Exchange so equivalent subtrees can share it; it remaps the child's outputPartitioning and outputOrdering to its own output attribute ids and delegates execution to the child.

nodes.name: HashJoin.scala
nodes.summary: Hash join trait shared by BroadcastHashJoinExec and ShuffledHashJoinExec, with interpreted join iterators and whole-stage code generation for every join type, plus a companion object that normalizes join keys. Contains more helper members than the nodes listed here.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with abstract members (buildSide, prepareRelation) and lazy vals using tuple destructuring; the companion object mixes in CastSupport and SQLConfHelper.

nodes.name: HashedRelationInfo
nodes.summary: Small holder returned by prepareRelation during code generation: the generated variable name of the HashedRelation, whether its keys are known unique, and whether it is known to be empty.

nodes.name: HashJoin
nodes.summary: Trait with the shared logic of hash-based joins (broadcast hash join and shuffled hash join): build/stream side selection, key projections, output schema and partitioning, interpreted join iterators for each join type, and whole-stage codegen for the probe loop. The companion object (lines 729-802) holds key normalization helpers.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Computes the join output attributes, making the non-preserved side nullable depending on the join type (inner, outer, existence, semi/anti).

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Derives the output partitioning from the streamed side's partitioning according to build side and join type.

nodes.name: createResultProjection
nodes.summary: Builds the row-combining function for the join type (a joined row for most types, or one that appends the existence flag).

nodes.name: innerJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted inner join: probes the HashedRelation for each streamed row and emits joined rows that satisfy the optional condition.

nodes.name: outerJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted outer join: emits matches and null-padded rows for streamed rows with no match.

nodes.name: semiJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted left semi join: keeps streamed rows with at least one match in the hashed relation.

nodes.name: existenceJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted existence join: emits every streamed row plus a boolean flag telling whether a match exists.

nodes.name: antiJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted left anti join: keeps streamed rows with no match in the hashed relation.

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the join-type-specific iterator method and updates the numOutputRows metric.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Codegen consume hook that dispatches to the inner, outer, semi, anti or existence code generator for the join type.

nodes.name: genStreamSideJoinKey
nodes.summary: Generates code that evaluates the streamed-side join key, with a fast path for a single long key.

nodes.name: codegenInner
nodes.summary: Generates the whole-stage code for an inner hash join probe loop, including the empty-relation shortcut and unique-key fast path.

nodes.name: codegenOuter
nodes.summary: Generates probe-loop code for outer hash joins, emitting null-padded rows when no match is found.

nodes.name: codegenSemi
nodes.summary: Generates probe-loop code for left semi hash joins.

nodes.name: codegenAnti
nodes.summary: Generates probe-loop code for left anti hash joins, including null-aware handling.

nodes.name: codegenExistence
nodes.summary: Generates probe-loop code for existence joins that append a match flag column.

nodes.name: normalizeJoinKeys
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that rewrites join keys so they can be hashed as a single long when possible.

nodes.name: rewriteKeyExpr
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that packs several narrow integral keys into one long expression for faster hashing.

nodes.name: extractKeyExprAt
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that extracts the i-th original key back out of a packed long key expression.

nodes.name: BroadcastNestedLoopJoinExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical join operator that broadcasts one side and evaluates the join condition for every row pair; the fallback for joins without equi-keys, with interpreted and whole-stage codegen paths.

nodes.name: BroadcastNestedLoopJoinExec
nodes.summary: Physical join that broadcasts the build side and, for every streamed row, scans all broadcast rows evaluating the join condition; supports all join types and whole-stage codegen for inner, outer and left-existence cases.

nodes.name: genResultProjection
nodes.summary: Creates the projection that combines streamed and broadcast rows into the join result row.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Computes output attributes with nullability adjusted for the join type.

nodes.name: innerJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted inner join: nested loop over broadcast rows for each streamed row.

nodes.name: outerJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted outer join, tracking matched broadcast rows in a bit set when the broadcast side is the preserved side.

nodes.name: leftExistenceJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted left semi/anti join where the streamed side is preserved.

nodes.name: existenceJoin
nodes.summary: Interpreted existence join that appends a boolean match flag to each streamed row.

nodes.name: defaultJoin
nodes.summary: Fallback implementation for join types without a dedicated path, such as full outer joins.

nodes.name: getMatchedBroadcastRowsBitSetRDD
nodes.summary: Computes, across all streamed partitions, a bit set of which broadcast rows matched, used to emit unmatched rows once.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Executes the join by broadcasting the build side and dispatching to the join-type specific method.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Codegen consume hook that selects the inner, outer or left-existence code generator.

nodes.name: prepareBroadcast
nodes.summary: Registers the broadcast rows as a codegen reference object and returns variable names for the array and iteration.

nodes.name: codegenInner
nodes.summary: Generates nested-loop code for inner join.

nodes.name: codegenOuter
nodes.summary: Generates nested-loop code for outer join.

nodes.name: codegenLeftExistence
nodes.summary: Generates nested-loop code for left semi, anti and existence joins.

nodes.name: CartesianProductExec.scala
nodes.summary: Cartesian product join without join keys, including an UnsafeRow-optimized CartesianRDD that caches the right side in a spillable array.

nodes.name: UnsafeCartesianRDD
nodes.summary: RDD optimized for UnsafeRow cartesian products that caches the right partition in a spillable ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArray instead of rebuilding it for every left row.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Computes one cartesian partition by materializing the right rows into the spillable array and iterating the cross product with the left rows.

nodes.name: CartesianProductExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator for joins without equi-join keys (inner/cross); builds an UnsafeCartesianRDD and filters with the optional condition.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Executes both children, forms the unsafe cartesian RDD, joins rows with an UnsafeRowJoiner and applies the join condition.

nodes.name: HashedRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the HashedRelation family (UnsafeHashedRelation, LongHashedRelation, empty and all-null variants), the long-key map LongToUnsafeRowMap and the broadcast mode used to build them; the build-side data structure of hash joins. More helper methods exist than the nodes listed here.
nodes.languageNotes: Sealed trait with companion factory objects (Scala companion pattern) and case objects as singletons; classes combine Externalizable and KryoSerializable for serialization.

nodes.name: HashedRelation
nodes.summary: Sealed trait describing a hashed collection of build-side rows keyed by join key, with lookup by InternalRow or long key, optional key-index access, uniqueness info and a read-only copy per task.

nodes.name: HashedRelation.apply
nodes.summary: Factory in the companion object that builds a LongHashedRelation for a single integral key or an UnsafeHashedRelation otherwise, handling empty and all-null inputs.

nodes.name: ValueRowWithKeyIndex
nodes.summary: Mutable row wrapper that pairs a value row with its key index, reused to avoid allocation when iterating matches.

nodes.name: UnsafeHashedRelation
nodes.summary: General HashedRelation backed by Tungsten BytesToBytesMap, with Java and Kryo serialization support.

nodes.name: UnsafeHashedRelation.get
nodes.summary: Looks up all rows stored for an InternalRow key in the BytesToBytesMap.

nodes.name: UnsafeHashedRelation.write
nodes.summary: Serializes the map entries (keys and values) to an output stream.

nodes.name: UnsafeHashedRelation.read
nodes.summary: Deserializes the relation, reallocating the BytesToBytesMap with memory from the current task.

nodes.name: UnsafeHashedRelation.apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a BytesToBytesMap from an iterator of rows, optionally ignoring duplicate keys.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap
nodes.summary: Memory-consumer hash map from long keys to unsafe rows using sparse (probing) and dense (array) modes, with spilling-aware growth and serialization.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap.getValue
nodes.summary: Returns the single (first) row stored for a long key.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap.valueIter
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over all rows chained for a given address.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap.get
nodes.summary: Looks up all rows for a long key, probing sparse array or dense array.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap.keys
nodes.summary: Iterates over distinct keys of the map as unsafe rows.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap.append
nodes.summary: Appends a key-row pair into the page, linking duplicates and growing the map when needed.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap.updateIndex
nodes.summary: Updates the key array slot to point to the newly appended value, using quadratic probing in sparse mode.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap.grow
nodes.summary: Grows the page that stores row bytes, acquiring more memory and copying data.

nodes.name: LongToUnsafeRowMap.optimize
nodes.summary: Tries to convert the sparse map to dense mode when the key range is small enough.

nodes.name: LongHashedRelation
nodes.summary: HashedRelation specialization for a single long join key, backed by LongToUnsafeRowMap.

nodes.name: LongHashedRelation.apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a LongToUnsafeRowMap from input rows and wraps it in a LongHashedRelation.

nodes.name: EmptyHashedRelation
nodes.summary: Singleton HashedRelation representing an empty build side; all lookups return null.

nodes.name: HashedRelationWithAllNullKeys
nodes.summary: Singleton HashedRelation for a non-empty build side whose keys are all null, used for null-aware anti joins.

nodes.name: HashedRelationBroadcastMode
nodes.summary: BroadcastMode that turns broadcast rows into a HashedRelation for broadcast hash joins.

nodes.name: HashedRelationBroadcastMode.transform
nodes.summary: Builds the HashedRelation from broadcast rows, using the size hint when provided.

nodes.name: BaseJoinExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the BaseJoinExec trait with the abstract join description (join type, condition, keys) and shared EXPLAIN output for all join operators.

nodes.name: BaseJoinExec
nodes.summary: Binary physical-node trait declaring joinType, condition, leftKeys and rightKeys, and implementing the simple and verbose EXPLAIN strings for join operators.

nodes.name: ShuffledJoin.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ShuffledJoin trait shared by joins that shuffle both children by join keys (sort-merge and shuffled hash join): required clustered distribution, output partitioning and output schema by join type.

nodes.name: ShuffledJoin
nodes.summary: Trait for shuffle-based joins that requires ClusteredDistribution on the join keys (or unspecified for skew joins) and derives output partitioning and nullable output attributes from the join type.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Chooses the output partitioning from left or right child partitioning based on join type.

nodes.name: output
nodes.summary: Computes output attributes with nullability adjusted for each join type.

nodes.name: HashAggregateExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HashAggregateExec, the Tungsten hash-based physical aggregate operator that supports whole-stage codegen (including a fast two-level hash map) and falls back to sort-based aggregation when memory is exceeded. Contains the interpreted execution path plus the large generated-code producers for keyed aggregation (about 17 members; the main ones are modeled as nodes).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case class that mixes interpreted execution (TungstenAggregationIterator) with Java code generation built from string interpolators and CodegenContext.

nodes.name: HashAggregateExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical operator that aggregates rows with an UnsafeFixedWidthAggregationMap, either through TungstenAggregationIterator at runtime or through generated code in whole-stage codegen. Requires hash-supported buffer types and extends AggregateCodegenSupport for the shared produce/consume codegen skeleton.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Interpreted execution path: maps each child partition through a TungstenAggregationIterator, handles empty input (no rows for grouped aggregates, a single row for global ones), and records aggTime.

nodes.name: createHashMap
nodes.summary: Creates the UnsafeFixedWidthAggregationMap used by generated code, initialized with an empty aggregation buffer; public because the generated Java class calls it.

nodes.name: finishAggregate
nodes.summary: Called from generated code to finish aggregation: if the hash map spilled, sorts and merges spilled data via an external sorter, and returns a KVIterator over grouping key and aggregation buffer pairs.

nodes.name: generateResultFunction
nodes.summary: Generates the Java function that turns each (grouping key, buffer) pair into an output row by evaluating result expressions, with variants for declarative and imperative aggregate functions.

nodes.name: checkIfFastHashMapSupported
nodes.summary: Checks the common requirements (supported primitive types, partial mode, config flags) for using a fast hash map in generated code.

nodes.name: enableTwoLevelHashMap
nodes.summary: Decides whether to use the row-based or vectorized fast hash map as the first level in front of the regular hash map, based on configuration and key/value types.

nodes.name: doProduceWithKeys
nodes.summary: Generates the produce-side Java code for aggregation with grouping keys: sets up the hash map(s), consumes the child's rows, handles spill and fallback, then iterates the map to emit output rows.

nodes.name: doConsumeWithKeys
nodes.summary: Generates the per-row consume code for keyed aggregation: looks up or inserts the key in the fast and regular hash maps, updates aggregation buffers, and falls back to sort on memory pressure.

nodes.name: ObjectHashAggregateExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ObjectHashAggregateExec, a hash-based aggregate operator for TypedImperativeAggregate functions whose buffers hold arbitrary JVM objects. It uses safe rows, tracks entry count rather than bytes, and switches to sort-based aggregation past a threshold, without codegen support.

nodes.name: ObjectHashAggregateExec
nodes.summary: Case class physical operator that executes aggregation through ObjectAggregationIterator, supporting JVM-object aggregation states and a sort-based fallback after a configurable entry-count threshold. Extends BaseAggregateExec and does not support whole-stage codegen.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Builds an ObjectAggregationIterator per partition using the fallback threshold from SQLConf, handles empty input for grouped and global aggregates, and reports metrics for rows, time, spill size and fallback tasks.

nodes.name: AggUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Planner utility object AggUtils that turns logical Aggregate nodes into physical aggregation plans: it picks HashAggregateExec, ObjectHashAggregateExec or SortAggregateExec and builds the partial/final (and distinct, streaming, session-window) aggregation stages. Used by the Aggregation strategy in SparkStrategies.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala singleton object holding a family of planning helpers; optional parameters with defaults let one createAggregate method serve batch and streaming plans.

nodes.name: AggUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton with the planning helpers that build physical aggregate operator chains for plain, single-distinct, streaming and session-window aggregations.

nodes.name: mayRemoveAggFilters
nodes.summary: Strips the FILTER clause from aggregate expressions that are not in Partial or Complete mode, since filters only apply in those modes.

nodes.name: createStreamingAggregate
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper over createAggregate that marks the resulting aggregate operator as streaming.

nodes.name: createAggregate
nodes.summary: Chooses the physical aggregate implementation: HashAggregateExec when buffer types allow, ObjectHashAggregateExec for object states when enabled, otherwise SortAggregateExec, honoring the testing force flags.

nodes.name: planAggregateWithoutDistinct
nodes.summary: Plans a two-stage aggregation (partial then final) for aggregates without distinct, adding session-window merging operators when needed.

nodes.name: planAggregateWithOneDistinct
nodes.summary: Plans aggregation with one distinct column through several stages (partial, partial merge, partial distinct, final and complete) and rewrites distinct aggregates accordingly.

nodes.name: planStreamingAggregation
nodes.summary: Plans a streaming aggregation pipeline: partial aggregate, shuffle, partial merge, StateStoreRestore, merge, StateStoreSave and a final complete aggregate.

nodes.name: planStreamingAggregationForSession
nodes.summary: Plans a streaming aggregation over session windows, using merging-sessions operators and session-window state store restore and save operators.

nodes.name: mayAppendUpdatingSessionExec
nodes.summary: Inserts an UpdatingSessionsExec above the child when the grouping expressions contain a session window.

nodes.name: mayAppendMergingSessionExec
nodes.summary: Inserts a MergingSessionsExec that merges partial session-window aggregates when grouping includes a session window.

nodes.name: SortAggregateExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SortAggregateExec, the sort-based physical aggregate that requires its child to be sorted on the grouping expressions and aggregates groups in one streaming pass using SortBasedAggregationIterator. It is the general fallback and supports codegen only for global aggregates.

nodes.name: SortAggregateExec
nodes.summary: Case class operator that aggregates pre-sorted input group by group with SortBasedAggregationIterator and preserves child ordering. Extends AggregateCodegenSupport and OrderPreservingUnaryExecNode.

nodes.name: requiredChildOrdering
nodes.summary: Requires the child output to be sorted ascending on all grouping expressions, which sort-based aggregation relies on.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Runs SortBasedAggregationIterator over each partition of the sorted child, with special handling of empty input for grouped and global aggregates.

nodes.name: supportCodegen
nodes.summary: Enables whole-stage codegen only when the sort-aggregate codegen config is on and there are no grouping expressions.

nodes.name: JoinCodegenSupport.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JoinCodegenSupport trait, shared by physical join operators that support whole-stage codegen. It generates code for the non-equi join condition and for loading the variables of one join side.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait mixing CodegenSupport with BaseJoinExec so that implementing join operators inherit helper code generators.

nodes.name: JoinCodegenSupport
nodes.summary: Trait combining CodegenSupport and BaseJoinExec with protected helpers that generate the join filter condition and the column variables of one join side.

nodes.name: getJoinCondition
nodes.summary: Generates the code for the extra (non-equi) join condition used by inner, left semi, left anti and full outer joins, returning the build row variable, condition code and build-side variable code.

nodes.name: genOneSideJoinVars
nodes.summary: Generates ExprCode variables for every output column of one join side, optionally defaulting them to null when no row matched.

nodes.name: WindowExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WindowExec, the physical operator that evaluates window functions over sorted partitions by delegating to WindowEvaluatorFactory. The long scaladoc explains frame types (entire partition, growing, shrinking, moving, offset) and row versus range boundaries.

nodes.name: WindowExec
nodes.summary: Case class operator that computes windowed aggregates per sorted partition, relying on the planner for partitioning and sorting. Extends WindowExecBase and exposes spill and segment-tree frame metrics.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Creates a WindowEvaluatorFactory and runs it on each child partition, using mapPartitionsWithEvaluator when the partition evaluator feature is enabled.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the AggregateCodegenSupport trait, the shared whole-stage codegen logic for aggregate operators, including the code generation path for aggregations without grouping keys. Hash-keyed codegen is delegated to subclasses through abstract hooks. Only the main methods are emitted as nodes.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait that mixes in BaseAggregateExec, BlockingOperatorWithCodegen and GeneratePredicateHelper; abstract members such as doProduceWithKeys are filled in by concrete operators.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport
nodes.summary: Trait for aggregate physical operators that support codegen. Implements doProduce/doConsume by branching on whether grouping keys exist and generates the no-key path itself.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport.doProduce
nodes.summary: Generates the produce side of whole-stage codegen, dispatching to the keyed or keyless implementation.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport.doConsume
nodes.summary: Generates the consume side of whole-stage codegen, dispatching to the keyed or keyless implementation.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport.supportCodegen
nodes.summary: Returns whether codegen is possible, requiring mutable aggregation buffer types.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport.doProduceWithoutKeys
nodes.summary: Generates the produce code for aggregation without grouping keys: initializes buffer variables, runs the child loop and emits one result row.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport.doConsumeWithoutKeys
nodes.summary: Generates the per-row update code for keyless aggregation, applying update expressions with subexpression elimination.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport.generateEvalCodeForAggFuncs
nodes.summary: Builds the code that evaluates all aggregate function updates, optionally split into separate methods to avoid oversized generated methods.

nodes.name: AggregateCodegenSupport.splitAggregateExpressions
nodes.summary: Splits aggregate update code into several generated functions when the codegen split config is enabled, passing shared subexpression values as parameters.

nodes.name: BaseAggregateExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the BaseAggregateExec trait holding logic shared by all physical aggregate operators: output attributes, required child distribution, explain output and conversion to SortAggregateExec.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with abstract defs for the aggregate parameters (grouping, aggregate expressions, result expressions) that case classes such as HashAggregateExec implement.

nodes.name: BaseAggregateExec
nodes.summary: Common trait for aggregate operators extending UnaryExecNode and PartitioningPreservingUnaryExecNode. Computes input and produced attributes and the child distribution from the aggregate modes.

nodes.name: BaseAggregateExec.requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Chooses the child distribution: AllTuples without grouping, ClusteredDistribution for grouping keys, or a stateful partitioning for streaming.

nodes.name: BaseAggregateExec.toSortAggregate
nodes.summary: Creates the equivalent SortAggregateExec with the same parameters, used as a fallback that produces the same result.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Implements TungstenAggregationIterator, which aggregates UnsafeRows with a hash map and spills to disk, then falls back to sort-based aggregation by merging spilled sorted maps when memory runs out.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with private[this] mutable state organized into numbered sections (Part 1 to Part 8) documented in its Scaladoc. It extends AggregationIterator and mixes in Logging.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator evaluating aggregate functions over UnsafeRows. Starts with hash-based aggregation in UnsafeFixedWidthAggregationMap, spills sorted entries on memory pressure and switches to sort-based aggregation over an UnsafeKVExternalSorter.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.createNewAggregationBuffer
nodes.summary: Creates and initializes an aggregation buffer UnsafeRow for both declarative and imperative aggregates.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.generateResultProjection
nodes.summary: Builds the function producing output rows from grouping key and aggregation buffer, depending on the aggregate modes.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.processInputs
nodes.summary: Consumes the input iterator into the hash map and spills the map to the external sorter when memory cannot be allocated.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.switchToSortBasedAggregation
nodes.summary: Switches to sort-based aggregation after input is processed: merges spilled sorted data and rebinds the aggregate functions to merge buffers.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.processCurrentSortedGroup
nodes.summary: Processes all consecutive rows of the same grouping key from the sorted iterator in sort-based mode.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.hasNext
nodes.summary: Reports whether another output row exists in either hash-based or sort-based mode.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.next
nodes.summary: Produces the next output row from the hash map iterator or the sorted group, updating peak memory, spill and hash probe metrics when finished.

nodes.name: TungstenAggregationIterator.outputForEmptyGroupingKeyWithoutInput
nodes.summary: Generates the single result row for a global aggregation that received no input.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase trait that groups window expressions by frame and creates the matching WindowFunctionFrame factories, including bound orderings and the segment-tree eligibility check.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with a protected lazy val (windowFrameExpressionFactoryPairs) containing nested pattern matching over frame types and bounds.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase
nodes.summary: Trait shared by window evaluator factories. Declares window spec members and builds frame factories (offset, unbounded, sliding, segment-tree) for each distinct frame.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase.createResultProjection
nodes.summary: Creates the code-generated UnsafeProjection that appends window expression results to the child output.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase.createBoundOrdering
nodes.summary: Creates a BoundOrdering for a row or range frame bound, generating projections and orderings for offset arithmetic over dates, timestamps, intervals and numerics.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase.windowFrameExpressionFactoryPairs
nodes.summary: Groups window functions by frame and returns pairs of expressions and factories that create the proper WindowFunctionFrame for each frame type.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase.eligibleForSegTree
nodes.summary: Decides whether a frame may use the segment-tree implementation based on config, frame type, filters and function support.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase.estimateMaxCachedBlocks
nodes.summary: Estimates how many segment-tree blocks a frame can span, with a default budget for range frames.

nodes.name: WindowExecBase.scala
nodes.summary: Defines WindowExecBase, the trait with logic common to window operators: output attributes, required child distribution and ordering, and propagation of the child ordering and partitioning.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with abstract defs for windowExpression, partitionSpec and orderSpec, implemented by concrete operators such as WindowExec.

nodes.name: WindowExecBase
nodes.summary: Base trait for window operators extending UnaryExecNode. Requires the child clustered by partitionSpec and sorted by partition then order spec.

nodes.name: WindowExecBase.requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Returns AllTuples with a warning when there is no partition spec, otherwise ClusteredDistribution on the partition spec.

nodes.name: WindowFunctionFrame.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the WindowFunctionFrame abstract class and its implementations (offset, sliding, unbounded, unbounded preceding or following) that compute window function results for each row of a partition.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a class hierarchy plus a companion object (WindowFunctionFrame.getNextOrNull, not emitted as a separate node). Frames are reused across partitions via prepare and write.

nodes.name: WindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Abstract base for window frames. A frame is prepared with the rows of a partition, then write fills the output row for a given index and bounds.

nodes.name: OffsetWindowFunctionFrameBase
nodes.summary: Abstract frame for LEAD/LAG and NthValue style offset functions, handling projection setup, null-skipping and shared state.

nodes.name: FrameLessOffsetWindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Frame for LEAD/LAG with a fixed row offset, supporting IGNORE NULLS.

nodes.name: UnboundedOffsetWindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Offset frame covering the whole partition, such as NthValue over an unbounded frame.

nodes.name: UnboundedPrecedingOffsetWindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Offset frame with unbounded preceding lower bound and a moving upper bound.

nodes.name: SlidingWindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Frame with sliding lower and upper bounds, buffering rows and recomputing the aggregate when the window changes.

nodes.name: UnboundedWindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Frame spanning the entire partition, computing the aggregate once per partition.

nodes.name: UnboundedPrecedingWindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Frame from the partition start to a moving upper bound, updating the aggregate incrementally.

nodes.name: UnboundedFollowingWindowFunctionFrame
nodes.summary: Frame from a moving lower bound to the partition end, recomputing the aggregate as rows leave.

nodes.name: SlidingWindowFunctionFrame.write
nodes.summary: Advances the window bounds for the current row, then recomputes the aggregate over the buffered rows.

nodes.name: UnboundedPrecedingWindowFunctionFrame.write
nodes.summary: Adds rows up to the upper bound to the processor and writes the running result.

nodes.name: FrameLessOffsetWindowFunctionFrame.write
nodes.summary: Writes the LEAD/LAG result for the current row, evaluating the shifted input row or null.

nodes.name: AggregationIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract AggregationIterator, the shared base of Spark's row-by-row aggregation iterators (sort-based, Tungsten hash-based, object hash-based and session merging). It binds aggregate functions, builds the per-row update/merge function and the final result projection according to the AggregateMode (Partial, PartialMerge, Final, Complete).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class mixing Iterator[UnsafeRow] with Logging. Most behavior is built eagerly in the constructor as protected vals (processRow, generateOutput) that hold closures, so subclasses only drive the loop.

nodes.name: AggregationIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract Iterator[UnsafeRow] holding the logic common to all aggregation iterators. At construction it validates the AggregateMode combination (Partial/PartialMerge versus Final/Complete), initializes the aggregate functions, and creates the processRow and generateOutput closures that subclasses call per input row and per finished group.

nodes.name: AggregationIterator.initializeAggregateFunctions
nodes.summary: Prepares each AggregateFunction for execution. Partial/Complete imperative functions get bound references to the input attributes, while PartialMerge/Final functions get an input buffer offset, and every imperative function also gets its mutable aggregation buffer offset.

nodes.name: AggregationIterator.generateProcessRow
nodes.summary: Builds the (buffer, row) => Unit closure that folds one input row into the aggregation buffer. Declarative aggregates are compiled into one MutableProjection using updateExpressions (Partial/Complete, wrapped in If for FILTER clauses) or mergeExpressions (PartialMerge/Final), while imperative aggregates are called via update or merge; grouping-only queries get a no-op.

nodes.name: AggregationIterator.generateResultProjection
nodes.summary: Builds the (groupingKey, buffer) => UnsafeRow closure producing output rows. For Final/Complete it evaluates aggregate results and applies the result expressions, for Partial/PartialMerge it emits grouping keys plus raw buffer columns (serializing TypedImperativeAggregate buffers in place before the shuffle), and for grouping-only it projects the keys.

nodes.name: AggregationIterator.initializeBuffer
nodes.summary: Resets an aggregation buffer to the initial value of every aggregate function: declarative aggregates through the initial-values projection and imperative aggregates through their initialize method.

nodes.name: SortBasedAggregationIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Implements SortBasedAggregationIterator, the streaming aggregation used by SortAggregateExec. It assumes input rows are already sorted by the grouping expressions, so it keeps a single aggregation buffer, consumes one group at a time and emits one result row per group.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class extending AggregationIterator; the constructor body calls initialize() so that the first row and its grouping key are pre-fetched at construction time.

nodes.name: SortBasedAggregationIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator that aggregates sorted input group by group. It reads rows while the grouping key stays equal to the current key, folds each row into one reused buffer with processRow, and when the key changes it emits the group result via generateOutput and resets the buffer. It needs no hash map and so uses constant memory, which is why Spark falls back to it when hash aggregation is not possible.

nodes.name: SortBasedAggregationIterator.newBuffer
nodes.summary: Allocates and initializes the single aggregation buffer, using an UnsafeRow-backed buffer when all buffer field types are mutable fixed-width types and a GenericInternalRow otherwise.

nodes.name: SortBasedAggregationIterator.initialize
nodes.summary: Pre-fetches the first input row and its grouping key, and chooses the key equality check: a direct UnsafeRow equals when all grouping types are binary stable, otherwise an InterpretedOrdering comparison.

nodes.name: SortBasedAggregationIterator.processCurrentSortedGroup
nodes.summary: Consumes input rows belonging to the current group, updating the shared buffer through processRow, and stops at the first row with a different grouping key, which is saved as the first row of the next group. It also records elapsed time in the aggTime metric.

nodes.name: SortBasedAggregationIterator.next
nodes.summary: Returns the aggregated row of the next group: processes the group, generates the output row, re-initializes the buffer and increments numOutputRows; throws NoSuchElementException when the input is exhausted.

nodes.name: SortBasedAggregationIterator.outputForEmptyGroupingKeyWithoutInput
nodes.summary: Produces the single result row for a global aggregation over empty input (no grouping keys), such as count of an empty table returning 0, by emitting the freshly initialized buffer.

nodes.name: AggregateProcessor.scala
nodes.summary: Window-side aggregation helper: AggregateProcessor wraps declarative and imperative aggregate functions evaluated in Complete mode over one window frame. Its companion object compiles the initial, update and evaluate MutableProjections and the class exposes initialize/update/evaluate so that window frames can add and read rows incrementally.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala companion pair: a private[window] object with the factory apply and a private[window] final class holding the compiled projections. Both are package-private, so they are internal to the window package.

nodes.name: AggregateProcessor.apply
nodes.summary: Companion-object factory. Collects aggregation buffer attributes, initial values, update expressions (guarded by If for FILTER clauses) and evaluate expressions from the window functions, binds ImperativeAggregates, adds the partition size slot for SizeBasedWindowFunctions such as ntile or percent_rank, and builds the three projections.

nodes.name: AggregateProcessor
nodes.summary: Runtime holder of the compiled projections and the shared aggregation buffer for the aggregate functions of a window frame, driven by a WindowFunctionFrame. initialize(size) resets the buffer (storing the partition size when needed), update(row) folds one input row in, and evaluate writes the result into the output row; evaluate can also read from an external buffer, as the segment-tree path does.

nodes.name: AggregateProcessor.initialize
nodes.summary: Resets the aggregation buffer for a new frame evaluation: stores the partition size if size-based functions exist, runs the initial projection and initializes imperative aggregates.

nodes.name: AggregateProcessor.update
nodes.summary: Adds one input row to the buffer through the update projection, then calls update on each imperative aggregate whose FILTER predicate (if any) evaluates to true.

nodes.name: AggregateProcessor.evaluate
nodes.summary: Evaluates the result projection against a given source buffer into the target row after asserting that the source has the same number of fields as the processor's buffer schema. The one-argument evaluate overload simply passes the internal buffer.

nodes.name: BoundOrdering.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BoundOrdering, the comparator that tells window frames where a frame boundary lies, with two implementations: RowBoundOrdering for ROWS frames (index arithmetic) and RangeBoundOrdering for RANGE frames (comparing ordering-column values).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala private[window] abstract class with final case class subclasses, used as a small strategy hierarchy.

nodes.name: BoundOrdering
nodes.summary: Abstract comparator compare(inputRow, inputIndex, outputRow, outputIndex) used by sliding and growing window frames to decide whether an input row is before, inside or after the boundary of the current output row.

nodes.name: RowBoundOrdering
nodes.summary: Boundary comparison for ROWS BETWEEN frames: returns inputIndex - (outputIndex + offset), so the boundary is a fixed number of physical rows relative to the current row.

nodes.name: RangeBoundOrdering
nodes.summary: Boundary comparison for RANGE BETWEEN frames: projects the input row's ordering value and the output row's bound value (current value plus or minus the offset) and compares them with the ordering, so peers and value ranges are included rather than a fixed row count.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Implements WindowEvaluatorFactory, the PartitionEvaluatorFactory that WindowExec uses to execute window functions per Spark partition. Its evaluator buffers all rows of one window partition (spilling when large), prepares the window frames, and for each row writes the frame results and joins them with the input row.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class mixing in the WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase trait; the real work lives in a nested WindowPartitionEvaluator whose eval method returns an anonymous Iterator[InternalRow] with mutable state.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: PartitionEvaluatorFactory[InternalRow, InternalRow] for window operators. It reuses the frame and projection setup from WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase and supplies the segment-tree metrics; createEvaluator returns a WindowPartitionEvaluator that does the per-partition streaming evaluation.

nodes.name: WindowPartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: Inner PartitionEvaluator that reads the buffer, spill and size thresholds from SQLConf and evaluates one Spark partition: the input must already be clustered and sorted by partition and order spec, and the evaluator groups consecutive rows by partition key into an ExternalAppendOnlyUnsafeRowArray.

nodes.name: WindowEvaluatorFactory.createEvaluator
nodes.summary: Factory method that creates a new WindowPartitionEvaluator for each task.

nodes.name: WindowPartitionEvaluator.eval
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the output rows of a partition. It builds the grouping projection, a partition-key equality check (binary equals or InterpretedOrdering), the row buffer and the window frames, and implements hasNext/next so that rows are emitted one at a time with the window function results joined to each input row.

nodes.name: WindowPartitionEvaluator.fetchNextPartition
nodes.summary: Collects all rows with the same partition key into the spillable buffer, calls prepare(buffer) on every WindowFunctionFrame, and resets the row index and buffer iterator for the new window partition.

nodes.name: WindowPartitionEvaluator.hasNext
nodes.summary: Reports whether the buffered partition has more rows or more input is available, and when finished clears the buffer and adds its spill size to the spillSize metric.

nodes.name: WindowPartitionEvaluator.next
nodes.summary: Loads the next partition when the current buffer is exhausted, calls write(rowIndex, currentRow) on every window frame to fill the shared result row, joins the input row with that result and applies the result projection.

nodes.name: EvalPythonExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the EvalPythonExec trait, the common skeleton of physical operators that evaluate PythonUDFs one partition at a time, plus the ArgumentMetadata case class in its companion object. Its header comment explains the design: projected input rows go to an external Python process over a socket, while the original rows wait in a queue and are joined back with the results.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait extending UnaryExecNode with a companion object holding ArgumentMetadata.

nodes.name: ArgumentMetadata
nodes.summary: Case class describing one argument passed to a Python function: its offset in the projected input row, an optional name (when the argument was a NamedArgumentExpression), and a flag for table arguments (used for Python UDTFs).

nodes.name: EvalPythonExec
nodes.summary: Trait for unary physical operators that run PythonUDFs. Output is child.output followed by resultAttrs (one column per UDF). Concrete subclasses supply udfs, resultAttrs and an evaluatorFactory; the trait's doExecute wires that factory into the child's RDD partitions.

nodes.name: EvalPythonExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Copies the child's rows and runs the evaluator factory on every partition: through mapPartitionsWithEvaluator when conf.usePartitionEvaluator is enabled, otherwise by creating an evaluator inside mapPartitionsWithIndexInternal and calling eval(index, iter).

nodes.name: EvalPythonEvaluatorFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Defines EvalPythonEvaluatorFactory, the abstract PartitionEvaluatorFactory behind both BatchEvalPythonExec and ArrowEvalPythonExec. It does the JVM-side work for a partition (queueing input rows, flattening and deduplicating UDF arguments, joining queued rows with Python results) and leaves the actual transfer to the Python worker to the abstract evaluate method.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with a private inner PartitionEvaluator; uses Spark's PartitionEvaluatorFactory API.

nodes.name: EvalPythonEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Abstract factory taking childOutput, udfs and output attributes. createEvaluator returns a new EvalPythonPartitionEvaluator; subclasses implement evaluate(funcs, argMetas, iter, schema, context) to ship projected rows to Python and return the result rows.

nodes.name: EvalPythonPartitionEvaluator
nodes.summary: Private inner PartitionEvaluator whose eval method implements the common per-partition protocol for Python UDF evaluation: buffer each input row in a HybridRowQueue, send only the projected UDF arguments to evaluate(), then join each queued row with the matching Python output row.

nodes.name: EvalPythonEvaluatorFactory.evaluate
nodes.summary: Abstract extension point called from the partition evaluator. Receives the chained Python functions with their result ids, per-UDF ArgumentMetadata, the projected input rows, the schema of the projected arguments and the TaskContext, and returns an iterator of UDF result rows.

nodes.name: EvalPythonPartitionEvaluator.collectFunctions
nodes.summary: Flattens a chain of nested PythonUDFs. When a UDF has a single PythonUDF child it recurses and appends the outer function after the inner ones in a ChainedPythonFunctions keyed by udf.resultId.id; otherwise it asserts there are no nested UDFs and returns the UDF's children as the arguments to evaluate in the JVM.

nodes.name: EvalPythonPartitionEvaluator.eval
nodes.summary: Runs one partition. It creates a HybridRowQueue (closed by a task-completion listener), collects the chained functions, flattens all UDF arguments into one list while reusing semantically equal expressions and recording ArgumentMetadata offsets, builds a MutableProjection and a schema with fields _0, _1, and so on, enqueues each input row as an UnsafeRow, and calls evaluate. Each Python output row is joined with queue.remove() through a JoinedRow and an UnsafeProjection onto the operator output.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BatchEvalPythonExec, the physical operator for classic (non-Arrow) Python UDFs, and its BatchEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory. Input rows are converted to Java objects, grouped into batches of PYTHON_UDF_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH rows, pickled with Pyrolite, and sent to the Python worker; results are unpickled and converted back to InternalRow.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses net.razorvine Pyrolite Pickler/Unpickler for the JVM-to-Python row format.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonExec
nodes.summary: Case class (udfs, resultAttrs, child) extending EvalPythonExec with PythonSQLMetrics. It captures the job artifact UUID and, when python worker logging is enabled, the session UUID, and builds a BatchEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory from the batch size and binary-as-bytes configs. Its companion object holds getInputIterator.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonExec.evaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Reads conf PYTHON_UDF_MAX_RECORDS_PER_BATCH and pysparkBinaryAsBytes and creates a BatchEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory with child output, UDFs, operator output, python metrics and the job-artifact and session UUIDs.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: EvalPythonEvaluatorFactory implementation for pickled Python UDFs. Its evaluate method drives a PythonUDFWithNamedArgumentsRunner with eval type SQL_BATCHED_UDF and decodes the pickled results.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory.evaluate
nodes.summary: Registers the Row picklers, builds the pickled input iterator with getInputIterator, and runs a PythonUDFWithNamedArgumentsRunner with PythonEvalType.SQL_BATCHED_UDF. Each returned byte array is unpickled into a list of results, converted with EvaluatePython.makeFromJava (the single UDF's type, or a struct of all UDF types), counted in the pythonNumRowsReceived metric, and a single-UDF fast path reuses one GenericInternalRow.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonExec.getInputIterator
nodes.summary: Turns the projected input rows into the byte stream for Python: each row becomes Java objects through EvaluatePython.toJava (with a per-field fast path when no conversion is needed), rows are grouped by batchSize, and every group is pickled with a Pickler whose memo is enabled only when conversion is needed and value comparison is disabled.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ArrowEvalPythonExec, the physical operator for vectorized Python UDFs (Arrow-optimized Python UDFs, scalar Arrow and pandas UDFs, and their iterator variants), plus its ArrowEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory and the BatchIterator helper. Rows are sent to the Python worker as Arrow record batches and results come back as ColumnarBatch, with an optional columnar-input path when the child supports it.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case class that checks its evalType in the constructor body and mixes in PythonSQLMetrics.

nodes.name: BatchIterator
nodes.summary: private[spark] Iterator[Iterator[T]] that splits an input iterator into sub-iterators of up to batchSize elements without buffering them, because input rows may be mutable and reused.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonExec
nodes.summary: Case class (udfs, resultAttrs, child, evalType) extending EvalPythonExec with PythonSQLMetrics. It accepts only SQL_ARROW_BATCHED_UDF, SQL_SCALAR_ARROW_UDF, SQL_SCALAR_ARROW_ITER_UDF, SQL_SCALAR_PANDAS_UDF and SQL_SCALAR_PANDAS_ITER_UDF and throws an internal error otherwise. It supports columnar execution when the child does and arrowPySparkUDFColumnarInputEnabled is set, and always supports row-based execution.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Row-based entry point. If the child supports columnar output it runs doExecuteColumnar and flattens each ColumnarBatch to UnsafeRow with an UnsafeProjection (downstream operators may cast to UnsafeRow); otherwise it calls the inherited EvalPythonExec.doExecute.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonExec.doExecuteColumnar
nodes.summary: Columnar entry point. Runs the lazily created ColumnarArrowEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory over child.executeColumnar(), using mapPartitionsWithEvaluator or mapPartitionsWithIndexInternal depending on conf.usePartitionEvaluator.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonExec.evaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: Creates the ArrowEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory with the Arrow batch size (conf.arrowMaxRecordsPerBatch), eval type, session time zone, large-var-types flag, the runner conf map from ArrowPythonRunner.getPythonRunnerConfMap, python metrics and the artifact and session UUIDs.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory
nodes.summary: EvalPythonEvaluatorFactory implementation for Arrow-based UDFs. Its evaluate method streams projected rows to the Python worker as Arrow batches through ArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner and returns the rows of the result batches.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonEvaluatorFactory.evaluate
nodes.summary: Computes the expected output types (user-defined types replaced by their sqlType), wraps the whole input iterator as one batch, and runs an ArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner mixed with BatchedPythonArrowInput. For each returned ColumnarBatch it compares actual column types with the expected ones using equalsIgnoreCompatibleCollation, throws arrowDataTypeMismatchError for pandas_udf() on mismatch, and emits the batch's rowIterator.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFs.scala
nodes.summary: Optimizer-side rules that pull Python UDFs and UDTFs out of logical operators so they can be evaluated in separate nodes. ExtractPythonUDFs rewrites a plan so scalar PythonUDFs become logical BatchEvalPython or ArrowEvalPython nodes, the logical operators that the PythonEvals strategy later plans as BatchEvalPythonExec and ArrowEvalPythonExec; two helper rules first handle UDFs inside Aggregate, and ExtractPythonUDTFs turns Generate over a PythonUDTF into UDTF eval nodes.
nodes.languageNotes: Each rule is a Scala object extending Rule[LogicalPlan] and uses transformUpWithPruning with TreePattern checks.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFFromAggregate
nodes.summary: Rule for Aggregate nodes in which a scalar PythonUDF depends on an aggregate expression or a grouping key, or has no references at all. Such UDFs cannot run inside the aggregate, so the aggregate is rewritten to produce the needed values and a Project above it applies the UDF afterwards.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFFromAggregate.extract
nodes.summary: Builds a new Aggregate whose aggregateExpressions are the aliased aggregate expressions and grouping keys needed by the UDFs, wrapped in a Project containing the rewritten expressions that reference those aliases.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFFromAggregate.apply
nodes.summary: Entry point that transforms bottom-up (pruned to plans containing PYTHON_UDF and AGGREGATE patterns) and calls extract on each Aggregate with a Python UDF over aggregate output.

nodes.name: ExtractGroupingPythonUDFFromAggregate
nodes.summary: Rule that pulls scalar PythonUDFs used in grouping expressions into a Project below the Aggregate, aliased as groupingPythonUDF and deduplicated by canonicalized form. Its comment says it must run after ExtractPythonUDFFromAggregate and before ExtractPythonUDFs.

nodes.name: ExtractGroupingPythonUDFFromAggregate.extract
nodes.summary: Replaces each PythonUDF in the grouping expressions with an attribute of a new groupingPythonUDF alias (reusing aliases for canonically equal deterministic UDFs), substitutes the same attributes inside aggregate expressions, and puts the alias Project under the Aggregate's child.

nodes.name: ExtractGroupingPythonUDFFromAggregate.apply
nodes.summary: Entry point that applies extract to Aggregates having a scalar PythonUDF in any grouping expression.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFs
nodes.summary: Main rule that makes Python UDFs executable. For each logical operator containing a PythonUDF it collects the evaluable scalar UDFs, creates a child logical BatchEvalPython (for SQL_BATCHED_UDF) or ArrowEvalPython (for pandas, Arrow and Arrow-optimized eval types) with result attributes named pythonUDF0, pythonUDF1 and so on, and replaces the UDF expressions with those attributes. It leaves existing BatchEvalPython and ArrowEvalPython nodes and correlated Subqueries alone.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFs.shouldExtractUDFExpressionTree
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive check that a UDF and its nested single-UDF children form one chain with the same corrected eval type and no non-UDF expression in between. It returns false for chains that mix eval types or have UDFs with several UDF children, so the caller extracts the inner ones first.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFs.collectEvaluableUDFsFromExpressions
nodes.summary: Walks the expressions and returns the PythonUDFs that can be planned together in one node: the first scalar UDF found fixes the eval type, later sibling UDFs join only if they have the same eval type, and SQL_SCALAR_PANDAS_ITER_UDF and SQL_SCALAR_ARROW_ITER_UDF are never combined with others. The code comments describe parallel chaining (siblings) and nested chaining.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFs.apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point. Skips correlated subqueries, and otherwise transforms the plan bottom-up (pruned to PYTHON_UDF plans), returning existing BatchEvalPython and ArrowEvalPython nodes unchanged and calling extract on every other operator.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDFs.extract
nodes.summary: For one operator, collects evaluable UDFs whose references are in the operator's input, then for each child that provides all required inputs builds BatchEvalPython or ArrowEvalPython over it depending on the corrected eval type (all UDFs in one node must share the type; a UDT falls back to BatchEvalPython with a warning). It rewrites the operator's UDF expressions to the result attributes, rejects UDFs needing inputs from several children, recurses until no UDFs remain, and adds a Project if the output changed.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDTFs
nodes.summary: Rule for Generate nodes whose generator is a PythonUDTF. It maps SQL_TABLE_UDF to BatchEvalPythonUDTF and SQL_ARROW_TABLE_UDF or SQL_ARROW_UDTF to ArrowEvalPythonUDTF, throws an internal error for other eval types, and skips correlated subqueries.

nodes.name: ExtractPythonUDTFs.apply
nodes.summary: Rewrites each Generate over a PythonUDTF into a BatchEvalPythonUDTF or ArrowEvalPythonUDTF logical node chosen by the UDTF's eval type.

nodes.name: PythonUtils.scala
nodes.summary: JVM-side helpers for launching and configuring PySpark: computing the PYTHONPATH (pyspark.zip and py4j under SPARK_HOME, or the Spark jar), merging paths, logging Python version and installed packages, building a SimplePythonFunction for internal use, and small Java/Scala collection converters and config getters that take a JavaSparkContext or java.util types.
nodes.languageNotes: Single private[spark] Scala object; several methods take JavaSparkContext or java.util types, which suits calls from Python through Py4J.

nodes.name: PythonUtils
nodes.summary: private[spark] object with the py4j zip name, default Python executable (PYSPARK_DRIVER_PYTHON, then PYSPARK_PYTHON, then python3), PYTHONPATH helpers, JList-to-Scala converters (toSeq, toList, toArray, toScalaMap), config accessors (encryption enabled, broadcast threshold, auth socket timeout, buffer size) and a test-only additionalTestingPath.

nodes.name: PythonUtils.sparkPythonPath
nodes.summary: Returns the PYTHONPATH for PySpark: if SPARK_HOME is set it adds python/lib/pyspark.zip and the py4j zip under it, then appends the jar containing PythonUtils, joined with the platform path separator.

nodes.name: PythonUtils.mergePythonPaths
nodes.summary: Joins the given PYTHONPATH strings with File.pathSeparator, ignoring empty strings.

nodes.name: PythonUtils.logPythonInfo
nodes.summary: When the Python log-info config is enabled, runs the given Python executable with the merged PYTHONPATH to log its version (-VV) and a sorted list of installed packages obtained through pkg_resources, ignoring failures from the subprocess calls.

nodes.name: PythonUtils.createPythonFunction
nodes.summary: Builds a SimplePythonFunction for a pickled command. It sets PYTHONPATH from the Spark python sources and py4j zip under spark.test.home or SPARK_HOME when Utils.isTesting (plus additionalTestingPath), else from sparkPythonPath, merges it with the PYTHONPATH environment variable, runs the default Python executable to read its major.minor version, and returns the function with that environment and no includes, broadcasts or accumulator.

nodes.name: PythonRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Core JVM side of the PySpark worker protocol: defines the eval-type constants, the abstract BasePythonRunner (worker acquisition, writer, reader, monitor, non-blocking socket I/O), the plain PythonRunner for RDD mapPartitions, and the special length markers used in the framing.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with an abstract generic class whose nested abstract classes (Writer, ReaderIterator) are specialised by anonymous subclasses in subclasses such as PythonRunner.

nodes.name: PythonEvalType
nodes.summary: Object holding the integer eval-type codes (NON_UDF, SQL_BATCHED_UDF, SQL_SCALAR_PANDAS_UDF, SQL_GROUPED_MAP_*, SQL_TABLE_UDF, Arrow UDFs and others) that tell the Python worker which kind of command follows; written to the worker by Writer.open.

nodes.name: toString
nodes.summary: Maps an eval-type integer back to its constant name for logging and error messages.

nodes.name: tryReadFaultHandlerLog
nodes.summary: Companion helper: when the Python faulthandler is enabled and a pid is known, reads and deletes the worker faulthandler log file so the crash traceback can be attached to the exception.

nodes.name: BasePythonRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract base for every JVM-to-Python runner. compute() sets worker environment variables, obtains a PythonWorker through SparkEnv.createPythonWorker (daemon or direct launch chosen by config), starts a Writer that feeds input and a MonitorThread, and returns an iterator over the worker output. Subclasses supply newWriter and newReaderIterator.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Entry point per task: exports SPARK_* and PYTHON_* env vars (buffer size, auth timeout, reuse flag, executor memory), asks SparkEnv for a worker, builds the Writer, registers a completion listener that stops or releases the worker, starts a MonitorThread, and wraps a ReaderInputStream and the subclass reader iterator in an InterruptibleIterator.

nodes.name: newWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that subclasses implement to create the Writer which sends the command and input records to the Python worker.

nodes.name: newReaderIterator
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that subclasses implement to create the iterator that decodes the result stream coming back from the Python worker.

nodes.name: Writer
nodes.summary: Inner abstract class responsible for everything the JVM sends to the worker: open() writes the header (partition index, Python version, task context, files, broadcasts, eval type, confs, command), writeNextInputToStream() emits one chunk of input, and close() writes END_OF_STREAM. Also serves BarrierTaskContext calls over a local server socket.

nodes.name: writeCommand
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that writes the command section (the pickled Python function or the UDF descriptors) right after the eval type.

nodes.name: writeNextInputToStream
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that writes the next batch of input to the stream and returns false once the input iterator is exhausted.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Writes the worker handshake header in order: partition index, Python version, optional barrier server socket info and TaskContext, Spark files, broadcast variables, eval type, runner conf, eval conf, then the command, and flushes. For barrier tasks it also starts an accept thread that answers barrier and allGather calls from Python; exceptions are stored rather than thrown.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Writes SpecialLengths.END_OF_STREAM and flushes, signalling that no more input follows.

nodes.name: barrierAndServe
nodes.summary: Executes BarrierTaskContext.barrier() or allGather() on behalf of the Python side and writes the resulting messages back over the accepted socket.

nodes.name: ReaderIterator
nodes.summary: Inner abstract iterator over worker output. Subclasses implement read(); this class provides the shared handling of timing data, Python exceptions, end-of-data (accumulator updates and worker reuse) and crash exceptions.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that reads one output object and, at end of data, processes the trailing sections before returning null.

nodes.name: handleTimingData
nodes.summary: Reads the boot, init, finish and processing timestamps plus spill counters sent by the worker, logs a timing summary, updates python* SQL metrics and task spill metrics.

nodes.name: handlePythonException
nodes.summary: Reads the traceback string after a PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN marker and builds a PythonException (error class PYTHON_EXCEPTION) with the writer exception as cause.

nodes.name: handleEndOfDataSection
nodes.summary: After END_OF_DATA_SECTION, receives accumulator updates, checks for the END_OF_STREAM confirmation and, when worker reuse is on, releases the worker back to the pool via SparkEnv.releasePythonWorker.

nodes.name: handleException
nodes.summary: Partial function translating failures into task kill exceptions, the writer thread exception, or a SparkException describing a crashed Python worker (with the faulthandler log when enabled).

nodes.name: MonitorThread
nodes.summary: Daemon thread per task that waits for interruption, then after the configured task kill timeout (PYTHON_TASK_KILL_TIMEOUT) destroys the Python worker through SparkEnv.destroyPythonWorker so a blocked task cannot hang forever.

nodes.name: ReaderInputStream
nodes.summary: InputStream that drives the non-blocking socket: it selects on the worker channel, reads results into the caller buffer, and when the socket is writable pushes buffered input produced by the Writer. Also implements idle-timeout detection and swaps the InputFileBlockHolder thread local between reader and writer code.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Select loop that alternately reads from and writes to the worker channel, logs and optionally kills the worker on idle timeout, preserves input_file_name behaviour by swapping thread locals, and raises PythonWorkerException if the worker was killed.

nodes.name: writeAdditionalInputToPythonWorker
nodes.summary: Fills an in-memory buffer (about spark.buffer.size) by calling Writer.writeNextInputToStream, writes as much as the socket accepts, calls Writer.close at end of input and then narrows interest ops to OP_READ.

nodes.name: PythonRunner
nodes.summary: Concrete runner for plain RDD mapPartitions (eval type NON_UDF): input and output are pickled byte arrays. Writes one Python function as the command and reads length-prefixed byte chunks until END_OF_DATA_SECTION. The companion object keeps the set of running monitor threads and logs Python info once.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory that logs Python version info once via PythonUtils.logPythonInfo and builds a PythonRunner for a single PythonFunction.

nodes.name: newWriter
nodes.summary: Creates the Writer whose command is the single pickled Python function and whose input is pickled elements written by PythonRDD.writeNextElementToStream, ending with END_OF_DATA_SECTION.

nodes.name: newReaderIterator
nodes.summary: Creates the ReaderIterator that switches on the next int from the worker: non-negative is a byte-array length, then TIMING_DATA, PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN and END_OF_DATA_SECTION are handled by the base class.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerException
nodes.summary: SparkException subclass raised when the Python worker is killed after an idle timeout.

nodes.name: SpecialLengths
