nodes.summary: Negative int markers that frame the worker stream: END_OF_DATA_SECTION, PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN, TIMING_DATA, END_OF_STREAM, NULL, START_ARROW_STREAM and END_OF_MICRO_BATCH.

nodes.name: BarrierTaskContextMessageProtocol
nodes.summary: Constants for the barrier RPC between Python and the JVM: BARRIER_FUNCTION, ALL_GATHER_FUNCTION, success and error messages.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerFactory.scala
nodes.summary: Creates, pools and tears down Python worker processes and their sockets. PythonWorkerFactory either forks workers through the pyspark.daemon process or launches pyspark.worker directly and waits for it to connect back, with auth, idle-pool management and a monitor that closes idle workers.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala; uses java.nio SocketChannel and Selector, Unix domain sockets when enabled, and synchronized blocks guarded by the factory instance.

nodes.name: PythonWorker
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping the SocketChannel to one Python worker with its Selector and SelectionKey. refresh() re-registers the channel for read and write interest when it is non-blocking, stop() closes the selector and channel.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Closes any previous selector and, for a non-blocking channel, opens a new Selector and registers the channel for OP_READ and OP_WRITE.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerFactory
nodes.summary: Per (pythonExec, workerModule, daemonModule, envVars) factory cached by SparkEnv. Uses the daemon (pyspark.daemon) to fork workers on UNIX or starts pyspark.worker directly, keeps a queue of idle daemon workers, authenticates sockets through SocketAuthHelper and kills idle workers after one minute. The companion object defines the default daemon module name pyspark.daemon.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Returns a worker and its ProcessHandle: in daemon mode it reuses a live idle worker or asks the daemon for a new one, otherwise it starts a simple worker in non-blocking mode.

nodes.name: createThroughDaemon
nodes.summary: Starts the daemon if needed, opens a socket to it (TCP loopback or Unix domain), waits up to 60 seconds for the worker, reads the worker pid, authenticates to the server, and retries once after restarting the daemon on socket errors.

nodes.name: createSimpleWorker
nodes.summary: Binds a server socket, launches python -m workerModule with PYTHON_WORKER_FACTORY_PORT or socket path and secret in the environment, waits up to 10 seconds for the worker to connect back, authenticates it and reads its pid.

nodes.name: startDaemon
nodes.summary: Launches python -m daemonModule workerModule with PYTHONPATH and auth env, reads the listening port (or Unix socket path) from the daemon stdout, validates it and redirects the daemon output to stderr; on failure collects stderr into the error message.

nodes.name: MonitorThread
nodes.summary: Private daemon thread that wakes every 10 seconds and closes all idle pooled workers when no worker was released for the idle timeout.

nodes.name: stopDaemon
nodes.summary: Cleans up idle workers and destroys the daemon process in daemon mode, or destroys all simple worker processes otherwise.

nodes.name: stopWorker
nodes.summary: Tells the daemon to kill a worker by writing its pid to the daemon stdin (or destroys the simple worker process) and then closes the worker socket.

nodes.name: releaseWorker
nodes.summary: Returns a worker to the idle queue in daemon mode (evicting the oldest when the pool size limit is reached), or closes it when no daemon is used.

nodes.name: ArrowPythonRunner.scala
nodes.summary: SQL-side runners that talk to the Python worker with Arrow streams: a common base wiring SQLConf settings into BasePythonRunner, the row-input variant, and ArrowPythonRunner plus the named-argument variant that write the UDF command through PythonUDFRunner.writeUDFs.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala classes composed by mixing the PythonArrowInput and PythonArrowOutput traits into BasePythonRunner.

nodes.name: BaseArrowPythonRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract runner extending BasePythonRunner with the PythonArrowInput and PythonArrowOutput traits. Copies the session UUID into the worker env, selects pythonExec and reads timeout, faulthandler, traceback and buffer-size settings from SQLConf.

nodes.name: RowInputArrowPythonRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract runner fixing the input type to Iterator[InternalRow] and output to ColumnarBatch by mixing in BasicPythonArrowInput and BasicPythonArrowOutput.

nodes.name: ArrowPythonRunner
nodes.summary: Concrete runner used for Arrow-based Python UDFs (pandas UDFs and similar): sends InternalRow batches as Arrow to the worker and receives ColumnarBatch results. Adds pythonRunnerConf to the runner conf and writes UDFs through PythonUDFRunner.writeUDFs.

nodes.name: ArrowPythonWithNamedArgumentRunner
nodes.summary: Arrow runner variant for UDFs with named arguments: takes ArgumentMetadata per argument, passes the input schema JSON in evalConf for SQL_ARROW_BATCHED_UDF, and writes UDFs with their argument names.

nodes.name: evalConf
nodes.summary: Adds the input_type schema JSON to the eval conf only when the eval type is SQL_ARROW_BATCHED_UDF.

nodes.name: getPythonRunnerConfMap
nodes.summary: Companion helper that collects the SQLConf entries (timezone, assign-by-name, safe type conversion, large var types, legacy pandas conversion, profilers, concurrency level) into the string map sent to the Python worker as runner conf.

nodes.name: PythonArrowInput.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the JVM-to-Python half of the Arrow protocol as mixin traits: PythonArrowInput creates the allocator, VectorSchemaRoot and ArrowStreamWriter and a Writer, while the Basic, Batched and Grouped variants decide how rows are cut into compressed Arrow record batches.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala traits with self-types on BasePythonRunner; the Writer inner class of the base runner is reached through the self-type.

nodes.name: PythonArrowInput
nodes.summary: Trait mixed into BasePythonRunner that converts input from the JVM to Arrow: holds the schema, timezone and metrics, allocates the root, and overrides newWriter so each chunk of input is written through an ArrowStreamWriter started on the worker stream.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Ends the Arrow stream writer (writes the footer) and then always closes the VectorSchemaRoot and the allocator.

nodes.name: newWriter
nodes.summary: Creates a Writer whose command is writeUDF and whose next-input step lazily starts the ArrowStreamWriter and delegates to writeNextBatchToArrowStream.

nodes.name: BasicPythonArrowInput
nodes.summary: Input trait for Iterator[InternalRow]: each element of the outer iterator is written into the ArrowWriter, unloaded as a compressed record batch, serialized to the stream and counted in the pythonDataSent metric.

nodes.name: writeNextBatchToArrowStream
nodes.summary: Writes one record batch per inner row iterator using VectorUnloader and MessageSerializer, updates pythonDataSent, and closes the Arrow stream when the outer iterator is exhausted.

nodes.name: BatchedPythonArrowInput
nodes.summary: Extends BasicPythonArrowInput so a single row iterator can be split into several Arrow batches limited by maxRecordsPerBatch and maxBytesPerBatch.

nodes.name: writeNextBatchToArrowStream
nodes.summary: Keeps a marker iterator for the current group and writes size-limited batches from it with BatchedPythonArrowInput.writeSizedBatch until it is drained.

nodes.name: writeSizedBatch
nodes.summary: Companion helper that writes rows until the record or byte limit is reached, then serializes the compressed batch; documented as a workaround for the Arrow 2 GB limit (ARROW-4890) with each batch kept within one group.

nodes.name: GroupedPythonArrowInput
nodes.summary: Trait for grouped execution (for example grouped map): overrides newWriter so each group gets its own complete Arrow stream, preceded by the int 1 and terminated overall by the int 0.

nodes.name: newWriter
nodes.summary: Writer implementation that starts a new ArrowWriterWrapper per group, streams size-limited batches via writeSizedBatch, ends and closes the group stream, and writes 0 at the end of data.

nodes.name: PythonArrowOutput.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Python-to-JVM half of the Arrow protocol: PythonArrowOutput reads control ints and Arrow streams from the worker and turns each record batch into a ColumnarBatch, with processors that optionally slice output batches by record count or byte size.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with a self-type on BasePythonRunner; ReaderIterator is the inner class of the base runner reached via that self-type.

nodes.name: PythonArrowOutput
nodes.summary: Trait mixed into BasePythonRunner for Arrow results: newReaderIterator creates a ReaderIterator that reads control ints, opens an ArrowStreamReader on START_ARROW_STREAM, picks an output processor and yields deserialized ColumnarBatch objects.

nodes.name: newReaderIterator
nodes.summary: Builds the ReaderIterator: handles START_ARROW_STREAM (create reader, schema and processor), TIMING_DATA, PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN and END_OF_DATA_SECTION, loads batches from the processor and closes reader and allocator on completion.

nodes.name: BasicPythonArrowOutput
nodes.summary: Output trait fixing OUT to ColumnarBatch and returning the batch unchanged.

nodes.name: ArrowOutputProcessor
nodes.summary: Interface for loading the next Arrow batch from the reader and producing a ColumnarBatch from it.

nodes.name: ArrowOutputProcessorImpl
nodes.summary: Default processor: wraps the root vectors as ArrowColumnVector, loads batches with the ArrowStreamReader and updates pythonNumRowsReceived and pythonDataReceived metrics.

nodes.name: loadBatch
nodes.summary: Loads the next record batch and records the row count and bytes read in the Python metrics.

nodes.name: BaseSliceArrowOutputProcessor
nodes.summary: Abstract processor that serves one loaded batch in several slices, tracking the current row index and closing earlier slice roots and vectors.

nodes.name: SliceBytesArrowOutputProcessorImpl
nodes.summary: Processor that limits output batches by bytes: repeatedly shrinks the slice by 90 percent until its buffer size is under arrowMaxBytesPerOutputBatch, falling back to a single row.

nodes.name: getRoot
nodes.summary: Returns the whole root if small enough, otherwise iteratively slices rows until the byte limit is met.

nodes.name: SliceRecordsArrowOutputProcessorImpl
nodes.summary: Processor that limits output batches to arrowMaxRecordsPerOutputBatch rows by slicing the root.

nodes.name: PythonUDFRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Runners for non-Arrow Python UDFs: BasePythonUDFRunner exchanges pickled byte arrays with the worker, PythonUDFRunner and PythonUDFWithNamedArgumentsRunner write the UDF command, and the PythonUDFRunner object serializes UDF descriptors (arguments, chained functions, result id).

nodes.name: BasePythonUDFRunner
nodes.summary: Abstract runner extending BasePythonRunner[Array[Byte], Array[Byte]] for row-based Python UDFs. Pulls timeouts, tracebacks and buffer size from SQLConf, uses the session UUID in worker env, and implements Writer and ReaderIterator for length-prefixed byte arrays.

nodes.name: newWriter
nodes.summary: Writer that writes the UDF command and pickled input elements via PythonRDD.writeNextElementToStream, appends END_OF_DATA_SECTION at the end and adds to pythonDataSent.

nodes.name: newReaderIterator
nodes.summary: ReaderIterator that reads length-prefixed byte arrays and handles TIMING_DATA, PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN and END_OF_DATA_SECTION; also adds received bytes to pythonDataReceived.

nodes.name: PythonUDFRunner
nodes.summary: Concrete runner for batched Python UDFs that writes UDFs by calling PythonUDFRunner.writeUDFs with plain argument offsets.

nodes.name: PythonUDFWithNamedArgumentsRunner
nodes.summary: Python UDF runner that carries ArgumentMetadata so argument names are sent to the worker.

nodes.name: writeUDFs
nodes.summary: Writes the UDF command section: function count, per function the argument count with offset and optional name, the chained pickled functions, and the result id; the overload at lines 176-181 wraps plain offsets into ArgumentMetadata. Also used by ArrowPythonRunner.

nodes.name: worker.py
nodes.summary: Entry point of the PySpark Python worker process. main() reads from the JVM socket in the order PythonRunner.Writer.open writes it (partition index, Python version, task context JSON, Spark files, broadcasts, eval type, runner conf, eval conf, command), builds the user function plus input/output serializers for the eval type via read_udfs or read_udtf, streams data through it, and reports timing, spill metrics, accumulators or a Python traceback back to the JVM.
nodes.languageNotes: Each PythonEvalType selects a different branch: wrap_* helpers adapt user functions, and read_udfs returns a (func, profiler, deserializer, serializer) tuple whose func maps an input iterator to an output iterator.

nodes.name: RunnerConf
nodes.summary: Typed view over the runner conf key/value map the JVM sends before the command (PythonWorkerUtils.writeConf). Exposes properties such as assign_cols_by_name, timezone, safecheck, use_large_var_types, legacy pandas conversion flags, Arrow batch limits, arrow_concurrency_level and the UDF/data source profiler setting, each read from a spark.sql.* key with a default.

nodes.name: EvalConf
nodes.summary: Typed view over the second conf map the JVM sends (eval conf). Parses per-evaluation settings: state_value_schema and grouping_key_schema (JSON to StructType), state_server_socket_port, input_type (JSON datatype string) and table_arg_offsets (comma separated ints).

nodes.name: report_times
nodes.summary: Writes the TIMING_DATA marker followed by boot, init and finish timestamps (in milliseconds) and the processing time to the output stream. The JVM ReaderIterator.handleTimingData reads these four longs in the same order.

nodes.name: verify_result
nodes.summary: Factory returning a checker for iterator-returning Arrow UDFs: the checker raises UDF_RETURN_TYPE if the result is not iterable and lazily type-checks every element against the expected type (for example pa.RecordBatch or pa.Array) via map.

nodes.name: verify_scalar_result
nodes.summary: Checks that a scalar Arrow UDF result is array-like and has exactly as many rows as the input batch, raising UDF_RETURN_TYPE or SCHEMA_MISMATCH_FOR_PANDAS_UDF otherwise. Sibling helpers verify_result_row_count (279), verify_iterator_exhausted (325) and verify_output_row_limit (335) cover row-count, consumed-input and fail-fast limit checks.

nodes.name: verify_output_row_count
nodes.summary: Generator that passes through output batches while counting rows and, once the iterator is exhausted, raises the given error class if the total differs from the expected row count (an int or a callable). Used by the scalar Arrow iterator UDF path.

nodes.name: wrap_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps a row-at-a-time batched UDF (SQL_BATCHED_UDF): applies kwargs support, then converts the result with the return type toInternal when the type needs conversion, returning the (offsets, function) pair used by the pickled-batch path.

nodes.name: wrap_scalar_pandas_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps a scalar pandas UDF: checks the result has __len__ and the same length as the first input series, raising UDF_RETURN_TYPE or SCHEMA_MISMATCH_FOR_PANDAS_UDF, and returns the result paired with the return type for the Arrow serializer.

nodes.name: wrap_pandas_batch_iter_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps iterator-of-batches pandas functions (scalar iter and mapInPandas): verifies the result is iterable, that each element is a pandas.DataFrame (struct return) or pandas.Series, validates it with verify_pandas_result, and yields (result, return_type) tuples.

nodes.name: verify_pandas_result
nodes.summary: Validates a pandas UDF return value against the declared return type: a struct type needs a DataFrame whose column names (when string) or count match the schema, raising RESULT_COLUMN_NAMES_MISMATCH or RESULT_COLUMN_SCHEMA_MISMATCH; other types need a pandas.Series.

nodes.name: wrap_cogrouped_map_arrow_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps a cogrouped-map Arrow function: precomputes the expected column names/types, calls f(left, right) or f(key, left, right) depending on argspec, verifies the pa.Table result with verify_arrow_table and returns its batches with the Arrow return type.

nodes.name: wrap_cogrouped_map_pandas_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps a cogrouped-map pandas function: concatenates the left and right value series into DataFrames, derives the key tuple from whichever side is non-empty for three-argument functions, validates the result with verify_pandas_result, and returns [(df, return_type)].

nodes.name: verify_arrow_result
nodes.summary: Compares an Arrow table or batch against the expected column names and types (by name or by position depending on assign_cols_by_name), raising RESULT_COLUMN_NAMES_MISMATCH or RESULT_COLUMN_TYPES_MISMATCH. verify_arrow_table (625) and verify_arrow_batch (640) first check the pyarrow type and then delegate here.

nodes.name: wrap_grouped_map_pandas_iter_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps an iterator-style applyInPandas function: lazily turns each list of value series into a DataFrame, calls f(iter) or f(key, iter) according to argspec, validates every yielded DataFrame, and flattens each into [(df, return_type)].

nodes.name: wrap_grouped_transform_with_state_pandas_udf
nodes.summary: Wrapper for transformWithState in pandas: forwards (stateful_processor_api_client, mode, key, values) to the user handler and pairs the result iterator with the return type. Three sibling wrappers handle the init-state pandas variant (700) and the Python row variants (720, 732); none verifies output elements yet (TODO comments).

nodes.name: wrap_grouped_map_pandas_udf_with_state
nodes.summary: Adapter for applyInPandasWithState: builds the key tuple, passes an empty DataFrame when the state timed out, lazily concatenates value series otherwise, calls f(key, values, state), and wraps the output so each DataFrame is checked for type and column count before being returned with the state.

nodes.name: wrap_grouped_agg_pandas_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps a grouped aggregate pandas UDF: applies kwargs support and wraps the scalar result in a one-element pandas Series paired with the return type. wrap_grouped_agg_pandas_iter_udf (857) does the same for the iterator-of-series variant.

nodes.name: wrap_unbounded_window_agg_pandas_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps an unbounded window aggregate pandas UDF like a grouped aggregate, but repeats the scalar result to the window length so the output has one value per input row.

nodes.name: wrap_bounded_window_agg_pandas_udf
nodes.summary: Wraps a bounded window aggregate pandas UDF: the first two argument offsets are begin and end index series; for every row it slices each input series with iloc and calls the user function on the slices, collecting a result Series.

nodes.name: wrap_window_agg_pandas_udf
nodes.summary: Dispatches a window aggregate pandas UDF to the bounded or unbounded wrapper using the window_bound_types runner conf entry at this UDF's index, raising INVALID_WINDOW_BOUND_TYPE for unknown values.

nodes.name: wrap_kwargs_support
nodes.summary: Helper shared by most wrappers: when keyword argument offsets exist, returns a function that maps trailing positional values back to keyword arguments by name and an offset list extended with the keyword offsets; otherwise returns the function and offsets unchanged.

nodes.name: wrap_perf_profiler
nodes.summary: Wraps a UDF with WorkerPerfProfiler using the SQL UDF profiler accumulators; for iterator-based eval types (_is_iter_based) each next() call is profiled separately, otherwise the whole call is profiled.

nodes.name: wrap_memory_profiler
nodes.summary: Wraps a UDF with WorkerMemoryProfiler when memory_profiler_ext is available (otherwise returns the function untouched), with the same per-item handling for iterator-based eval types as the perf profiler.

nodes.name: read_single_udf
nodes.summary: Reads one UDF description from the stream: argument count, then per argument an offset and a flag plus optional keyword name, then the number of chained pickled commands (composed with chain) and a result id. Selects the perf or memory profiler from the conf, guards StopIteration, and then, based on eval_type, returns either a wrapped (offsets, function) pair or a raw (func, offsets, kwargs, return_type) tuple; unknown eval types raise ValueError.

nodes.name: read_udtf
nodes.summary: Reads a user-defined table function: picks a serializer for the eval type, then reads argument offsets, partition child indexes, an optional pickled AnalyzeResult, the pickled handler class, the JSON return struct type and the UDTF name. Instantiates the handler (wrapped by a partition-aware class when PARTITION BY is used), validates eval signature, and returns a mapper plus serializers for one of four paths: legacy pandas, native Arrow table, PyArrow UDTF, or plain row UDTF.

nodes.name: UDTFWithPartitions
nodes.summary: Nested class in read_udtf that wraps a row-based UDTF for TABLE arguments with PARTITION BY: compares the partition columns of consecutive rows, calls terminate and builds a fresh UDTF instance at partition boundaries, strips projected partition columns from the Row passed to eval, and honors SkipRestOfInputTableException.

nodes.name: ArrowUDTFWithPartition
nodes.summary: Nested class in read_udtf for Arrow UDTFs with PARTITION BY: detects contiguous partition boundaries inside each RecordBatch, slices the batch per partition, drops the partition columns, calls eval per partition and terminate plus a new instance when the partition key changes across batches.

nodes.name: build_null_checker
nodes.summary: Builds a row checker from the UDTF return struct type that recursively inspects arrays, maps and structs and raises UDTF_EXEC_ERROR when None appears in a non-nullable position; returns None when every field is nullable and needs no checking.

nodes.name: wrap_arrow_udtf (legacy pandas path)
nodes.summary: Legacy pandas path for SQL_ARROW_TABLE_UDF: evaluates the UDTF row by row, builds a pandas DataFrame from the yielded rows, validates it with verify_pandas_result and returns (DataFrame, return_type) tuples.

nodes.name: wrap_arrow_udtf (native Arrow path)
nodes.summary: Default path for SQL_ARROW_TABLE_UDF: evaluates the UDTF per input row, converts the yielded rows to an Arrow table with LocalDataToArrowConversion (empty output becomes one empty batch), validates it with verify_arrow_result and yields (batch, arrow_return_type).

nodes.name: wrap_pyarrow_udtf
nodes.summary: Wrapper for SQL_ARROW_UDTF: the user function receives Arrow RecordBatches directly and must yield pa.Table or pa.RecordBatch objects, which are checked for column count and passed on with the Arrow return type; exceptions become UDTF_EXEC_ERROR.

nodes.name: wrap_udtf
nodes.summary: Wrapper for the default row-based UDTF: calls eval, requires an iterable result, validates each row (UDT, length, type, nullability) and converts it with toInternal; exceptions raised inside user code become UDTF_EXEC_ERROR.

nodes.name: read_udfs
nodes.summary: Chooses the deserializer/serializer pair for the eval type (Arrow stream, pandas, group, cogroup, stateful serializers, or BatchedSerializer over pickle with PYTHON_UDF_BATCH_SIZE), reads the UDF count and each UDF via read_single_udf, and builds the per-eval-type func that maps the input iterator to output batches. Many Arrow-native eval types return early with a dedicated function; the remaining ones define a mapper wrapped as func(_, it) = map(mapper, it).

nodes.name: extract_key_value_indexes
nodes.summary: Nested helper in read_udfs that parses the flat argument-offset list of grouped and cogrouped UDFs into [key offsets, value offsets] pairs, one per DataFrame; mirrors the JVM-side BasePandasGroupExec.resolveArgOffsets layout described in its docstring.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Worker main loop, run once per task on the JVM socket. Reads partition index, checks the Python version, sets memory limits, parses the task context JSON, loads Spark files and broadcasts, reads eval type, runner conf and eval conf, then builds (func, profiler, deserializer, serializer) via read_command, read_udtf or read_udfs. It runs deserializer.load_stream -> func -> serializer.dump_stream under capture_outputs (optionally profiled); on any exception it calls handle_worker_exception and exits. Afterwards it writes timing data, spill counters, END_OF_DATA_SECTION, accumulator updates, and answers END_OF_STREAM to signal the worker can be reused.

nodes.name: daemon.py
nodes.summary: Python-side process manager launched by the JVM PythonWorkerFactory (python -m pyspark.daemon). It listens on a loopback or Unix domain socket, reports the port or path on stdout, and forks one worker process per accepted connection, each of which runs the worker module's main.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses os.fork, select.poll and signal handlers, so it only works on POSIX. The worker module is imported after the fork on purpose, because pandas and pyarrow start threads on import.

nodes.name: compute_real_exit_code
nodes.summary: Maps a SystemExit code to an integer exit code for os._exit: ints pass through, anything else becomes 1.

nodes.name: worker
nodes.summary: Runs inside the forked child. Resets signal handlers, wraps the socket in buffered binary files, optionally checks the factory secret (replying ok or err), lazily imports pyspark.worker.main (or the module named in argv[1]) and runs it with the socket's infile and outfile, then flushes and returns the exit code.

nodes.name: manager
nodes.summary: Daemon main loop. Binds a listening socket (Unix domain, IPv6 loopback or IPv4 loopback), writes the port or socket path to stdout for the JVM, then polls stdin and the listen socket: an int on stdin names a worker pid to SIGKILL, EOF on stdin shuts the daemon down, and each accepted connection is os.fork()ed into a child that acks its pid and calls worker() (looping if SPARK_REUSE_WORKER is set).

nodes.name: worker_util.py
nodes.summary: Helper functions the Python worker uses to read the per-task preamble sent by the JVM: Python version check, memory limit, SparkFiles and PYTHONPATH setup, broadcast variables, the command payload, a Conf key/value reader, the callback socket to the executor, and the accumulator update writer.
nodes.languageNotes: Importing this module under SPARK_TESTING asserts that SPARK_PYTHON_RUNTIME is PYTHON_WORKER, so it is meant to be imported only inside a worker process.

nodes.name: add_path
nodes.summary: Inserts a path at sys.path[1] if not already present and returns whether it changed sys.path; guards against re-adding on reused workers.

nodes.name: read_command
nodes.summary: Reads one length-framed command with the given FramedSerializer and, if the payload is a Broadcast, loads the real command from the broadcast value.

nodes.name: check_python_version
nodes.summary: Reads the driver's major.minor Python version string from the stream and raises PYTHON_VERSION_MISMATCH if it differs from the worker's version.

nodes.name: setup_memory_limits
nodes.summary: Applies RLIMIT_AS from a memory limit in MB when the resource module exists, printing the old and new limits to stderr and warning instead of failing on unsupported systems.

nodes.name: setup_spark_files
nodes.summary: Reads the SparkFiles directory and the list of zip/egg includes from the stream, sets SparkFiles root, adds them to sys.path and invalidates import caches if the path changed.

nodes.name: setup_broadcasts
nodes.summary: Reads broadcast variable ids and, depending on the decryption flag, either connects to a JVM server to receive the data or reads file paths; registers or removes entries in the broadcast registry.

nodes.name: get_sock_file_to_executor
nodes.summary: Context manager that reads the factory port or socket path and secret from the environment, connects and authenticates back to the executor, writes the worker pid, yields the socket file and closes it on exit.

nodes.name: send_accumulator_updates
nodes.summary: Writes the number of registered accumulators, then each (id, value) pair pickled with length framing, back to the JVM.

nodes.name: Conf
nodes.summary: Key/value configuration holder populated from the JVM stream; lowercases string values by default on get.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads a count of config entries (rejecting counts outside 0..10000 with PROTOCOL_ERROR) and then that many UTF-8 key/value pairs.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns a config value or default, lowercasing strings unless lower_str is False.

nodes.name: serializers.py
nodes.summary: Defines the PySpark serializer hierarchy and the wire primitives shared by driver and worker: big-endian int and long readers/writers, the SpecialLengths control markers, and the Serializer, FramedSerializer (length-prefixed), BatchedSerializer, Pickle/CloudPickle/Marshal/Auto/Compressed serializers and ChunkedStream.
nodes.languageNotes: CPickleSerializer is an alias: it is CloudPickleSerializer unless PYSPARK_ENABLE_NAMEDTUPLE_PATCH=1, in which case it is PickleSerializer. The same env var also triggers a namedtuple monkey patch at import time.

nodes.name: SpecialLengths
nodes.summary: Negative length markers sent in place of a data length: END_OF_DATA_SECTION (-1), PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN (-2), TIMING_DATA (-3), END_OF_STREAM (-4), NULL (-5), START_ARROW_STREAM (-6). Mirrors the JVM SpecialLengths object.

nodes.name: Serializer
nodes.summary: Abstract base for all serializers: dump_stream, load_stream, dumps, a batch-preserving _load_stream_without_unbatching, and equality based on class and __dict__.

nodes.name: FramedSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer that writes each object as a 4-byte big-endian length followed by the bytes; subclasses supply dumps/loads. Treats a length of END_OF_DATA_SECTION as EOF and NULL as None, and rejects objects over 2G.

nodes.name: _write_with_length
nodes.summary: Serializes an object with dumps, validates it is non-None and under 2G, then writes length and payload.

nodes.name: _read_with_length
nodes.summary: Reads a length, maps special lengths to EOFError or None, reads that many bytes and returns loads of them.

nodes.name: BatchedSerializer
nodes.summary: Wraps another serializer and sends lists of objects (batches) of a fixed size, or the whole iterator as one batch when UNLIMITED; load_stream flattens batches with chain.from_iterable.

nodes.name: FlattenedValuesSerializer
nodes.summary: BatchedSerializer for (key, values) pairs that splits long value lists into chunks of batchSize so batches have similar sizes.

nodes.name: AutoBatchedSerializer
nodes.summary: BatchedSerializer that adapts the batch size at write time: doubles when a batch serializes below bestSize (64 KiB default) and halves when it exceeds ten times bestSize.

nodes.name: dump_stream
nodes.summary: Serializes growing batches with the wrapped serializer's dumps, writes each with a length prefix, and adjusts the next batch size from the serialized size.

nodes.name: CartesianDeserializer
nodes.summary: Deserializer for the JVM cartesian() of two batched PythonRDDs; takes the product of each pair of key and value batches.

nodes.name: PairDeserializer
nodes.summary: Deserializer for the JVM zip() of two batched PythonRDDs; zips each pair of batches and raises ValueError when batch lengths differ.

nodes.name: NoOpSerializer
nodes.summary: FramedSerializer that passes bytes through unchanged in both directions.

nodes.name: PickleSerializer
nodes.summary: FramedSerializer using the standard pickle module with the highest protocol.

nodes.name: CloudPickleSerializer
nodes.summary: FramedSerializer using cloudpickle, which can serialize lambdas and closures; this is what the default CPickleSerializer name resolves to. Wraps failures in PicklingError with a readable message.

nodes.name: MarshalSerializer
nodes.summary: FramedSerializer using marshal; faster than cloudpickle but supports fewer types.

nodes.name: AutoSerializer
nodes.summary: FramedSerializer that tries marshal first (prefix M) and permanently falls back to pickle (prefix P) after the first failure.

nodes.name: CompressedSerializer
nodes.summary: FramedSerializer that zlib-compresses (level 1) the output of another FramedSerializer.

nodes.name: UTF8Deserializer
nodes.summary: Reads length-prefixed UTF-8 strings (as written by Java String.getBytes), handling END_OF_DATA_SECTION and NULL; used all over the worker protocol to read strings from the JVM.

nodes.name: read_long
nodes.summary: Reads an 8-byte big-endian signed long, raising EOFError on empty read.

nodes.name: write_long
nodes.summary: Writes an 8-byte big-endian signed long.

nodes.name: pack_long
nodes.summary: Returns the 8-byte big-endian packed form of a long.

nodes.name: read_int
nodes.summary: Reads a 4-byte big-endian signed int, raising EOFError on empty read; the basic framing read used throughout the worker protocol.

nodes.name: write_int
nodes.summary: Writes a 4-byte big-endian signed int; the basic framing write used throughout the worker protocol.

nodes.name: read_bool
nodes.summary: Reads a single-byte boolean, raising EOFError on empty read.

nodes.name: write_with_length
nodes.summary: Writes a 4-byte length followed by the raw bytes.

nodes.name: ChunkedStream
nodes.summary: File-like writer that buffers data into fixed-size frames, sending each as (size, bytes) and ending with a -1 length on close, so large payloads can be streamed to a socket without knowing the total length. Exposes closed for pyarrow's stream writer.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Appends bytes to the buffer and flushes full buffers as length-prefixed frames.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Flushes the remaining buffer, writes the -1 terminator and closes the wrapped stream.

nodes.name: _hijack_namedtuple
nodes.summary: Optional (PYSPARK_ENABLE_NAMEDTUPLE_PATCH=1) monkey patch of collections.namedtuple so generated classes pickle by value; also patches already-created namedtuples in __main__.

nodes.name: serializers.py
nodes.summary: Arrow-based serializers used by the Python worker to exchange columnar data with the JVM: a plain Arrow IPC stream serializer, grouped and cogrouped variants, and pandas/Arrow UDF, UDTF, aggregation, applyInPandasWithState and transformWithState serializers that convert between Arrow record batches and pandas Series/DataFrames or Rows.
nodes.languageNotes: Serializer subclasses form a deep inheritance chain rooted at ArrowStreamSerializer; several load_stream implementations deliberately call a specific ancestor's load_stream (for example via super(ArrowStreamPandasSerializer, self)) to skip intermediate conversions.

nodes.name: _normalize_packed
nodes.summary: Normalizes UDF output to a tuple of (series, spark_type) tuples, accepting either a single tuple from iterator UDFs or a tuple of tuples from batched UDFs.

nodes.name: SpecialLengths
nodes.summary: Local copy of the negative framing markers (END_OF_DATA_SECTION, PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN, TIMING_DATA, END_OF_STREAM, NULL, START_ARROW_STREAM); same values as pyspark.serializers.SpecialLengths.

nodes.name: ArrowCollectSerializer
nodes.summary: Reads the Arrow record batches returned by collectAsArrowToPython, then a batch-order index list (or a JVM error message when the count is -1) so the driver can reorder the batches.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamSerializer
nodes.summary: Base Arrow serializer: dump_stream writes record batches through a pyarrow RecordBatchStreamWriter (optionally preceded by the START_ARROW_STREAM marker) and load_stream reads them with pa.ipc.open_stream.

nodes.name: dump_stream
nodes.summary: Writes record batches to the stream with a lazily created RecordBatchStreamWriter, optionally prepending START_ARROW_STREAM, and closes the writer at the end.

nodes.name: load_stream
nodes.summary: Opens an Arrow IPC stream reader on the stream and yields each record batch.

nodes.name: _write_stream_start
nodes.summary: Pulls the first batch and only then writes START_ARROW_STREAM, so errors in building the first batch can still be reported to the JVM before the Arrow stream starts.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamGroupSerializer
nodes.summary: Reads a per-group int count (1 expected, 0 ends the stream) and yields one iterator of record batches per group.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamCoGroupSerializer
nodes.summary: Reads a per-group count (2 expected) and yields a pair of (left_batches, right_batches), eagerly loading each side to keep stream position correct.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamUDFSerializer
nodes.summary: Arrow serializer for mapInArrow-style UDFs: flattens the struct column of each incoming batch and wraps outputs back into a struct column, sending START_ARROW_STREAM first.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamUDTFSerializer
nodes.summary: ArrowStreamUDFSerializer variant that does not flatten incoming batches.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamArrowUDTFSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for PyArrow-native UDTFs: flattens struct columns at table-arg offsets and enforces the declared Arrow return schema on outputs.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamGroupUDFSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for grouped Arrow UDFs (grouped map): loads grouped batches, drains each group before the next, and dumps (batches, arrow_type) tuples, optionally reordering columns by name.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamPandasSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializes pandas Series to Arrow batches and back. Holds timezone, safecheck and struct/ndarray/extension-dtype conversion options.

nodes.name: dump_stream
nodes.summary: Converts each (series, spark_type) packed output to an Arrow RecordBatch via PandasToArrowConversion and writes the stream.

nodes.name: load_stream
nodes.summary: Reads Arrow batches and converts each to a list of pandas Series with ArrowBatchTransformer.to_pandas.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamPandasUDFSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer the worker uses for scalar pandas UDFs: validates that struct return types are DataFrames, converts with PandasToArrowConversion and always writes START_ARROW_STREAM before the first batch.

nodes.name: dump_stream
nodes.summary: Builds Arrow batches from (series, type) outputs with arrow_cast and column assignment options, writes START_ARROW_STREAM after the first batch succeeds, then streams the batches.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamPandasUDTFSerializer
nodes.summary: Pandas UDF serializer preset for Arrow-optimized Python UDTFs: struct inputs as Rows, ndarrays as lists, casting enabled and legacy conversion on.

nodes.name: ArrowStreamAggPandasUDFSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for grouped-aggregate and window-aggregate pandas UDFs; lazily converts each group's batches to tuples of Series so batches are consumed one at a time.

nodes.name: GroupPandasUDFSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for grouped-map pandas UDFs: yields raw record-batch iterators per group on load and flattens the nested iterator on dump.

nodes.name: CogroupArrowUDFSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for cogrouped Arrow UDFs; loads pairs of record-batch lists via the cogroup protocol and reuses the grouped Arrow dump path.

nodes.name: CogroupPandasUDFSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for cogrouped pandas UDFs; builds Arrow tables for the left and right sides and yields them as pandas Series lists.

nodes.name: ApplyInPandasWithStateSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for applyInPandasWithState: reads data and GroupState columns from the JVM, rebuilds GroupState objects (pickled values, JSON properties), and on output packs data, counts and updated state into a three-field Arrow batch with a size-based flush.

nodes.name: load_stream
nodes.summary: Streams batches, slices each group's rows by state offsets, constructs or reuses GroupState per grouping key and yields (data, state) groups.

nodes.name: dump_stream
nodes.summary: Collects user output DataFrames and updated states, flushing Arrow batches when the record count passes arrow_max_records_per_batch.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPandasSerializer
nodes.summary: Serializer for transformWithStateInPandas: groups incoming rows by key into pandas DataFrames bounded by record and byte limits, and emits PROCESS_DATA, PROCESS_TIMER and COMPLETE function-mode events.

nodes.name: _update_batch_size_stats
nodes.summary: Tracks total bytes and rows to maintain an average Arrow row size for byte-based batching.

nodes.name: load_stream
nodes.summary: Reads batches, groups rows by key offsets into DataFrames, and yields (mode, key, rows) tuples ending with timer and complete events.

nodes.name: dump_stream
nodes.summary: Flattens per-key output iterators of pandas DataFrames into (df, type) pairs and writes them via the parent pandas UDF serializer.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPandasInitStateSerializer
nodes.summary: TransformWithState serializer that also reads the initial-state column, yielding (key, input rows, init-state rows) per group.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkRowSerializer
nodes.summary: Row-based transformWithState serializer: iterates Arrow batches row by row into Row objects grouped by key, and on output converts Row iterators to Arrow batches with to_arrow_type.

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySparkRowInitStateSerializer
nodes.summary: Row-based transformWithState serializer with initial state support; extracts input and init-state rows per batch and groups them by key.

nodes.name: udf.py
nodes.summary: Python side of user-defined functions: UserDefinedFunction pickles a Python callable with its return type and lazily wraps it in a JVM UserDefinedPythonFunction, _create_udf/_create_py_udf build the user-facing wrapper (choosing the eval type, optionally Arrow-optimized), and UDFRegistration (spark.udf) registers Python and Java functions as SQL functions.
nodes.languageNotes: The JVM objects are reached through py4j (sc._jvm); the actual execution happens later in the worker, selected by the evalType integer from pyspark.util.PythonEvalType.

nodes.name: _wrap_function
nodes.summary: Packs the callable (or a (func, returnType) tuple) with _prepare_for_python_RDD into a pickled command plus broadcast vars, env and includes, and builds a JVM SimplePythonFunction with the Python executable, version and accumulator.

nodes.name: _create_udf
nodes.summary: Creates a UserDefinedFunction for a callable, return type, eval type, name and determinism, and returns its wrapped (help-friendly) callable.

nodes.name: _create_py_udf
nodes.summary: Builds a regular or Arrow-optimized Python UDF: decides whether Arrow is enabled (argument or spark.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled, falling back with a warning if pandas or pyarrow are missing), tries to infer the eval type from type hints, else picks SQL_ARROW_BATCHED_UDF or SQL_BATCHED_UDF.

nodes.name: UserDefinedFunction
nodes.summary: Holds a Python function, return type, name, eval type and determinism, and lazily creates the JVM UserDefinedPythonFunction (_judf). Calling it builds a Column from the JVM function, optionally routing through the Python or memory profiler.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Validates that func is callable and returnType and evalType have the right types, then stores them with a default name taken from the function.

nodes.name: _check_return_type
nodes.summary: Static check that the return type is convertible to an Arrow type for the given eval type (Arrow-optimized, scalar pandas/Arrow, grouped map, map, cogroup, grouped aggregate), raising NOT_IMPLEMENTED or INVALID_RETURN_TYPE errors.

nodes.name: returnType
nodes.summary: Property that resolves the return type (parsing a DDL string through the JVM if needed), caches it and validates it for the eval type.

nodes.name: _judf
nodes.summary: Property that lazily creates and caches the JVM UserDefinedPythonFunction object.

nodes.name: _create_judf
nodes.summary: Gets the active session, wraps the function with _wrap_function, parses the return type through the JVM and instantiates org.apache.spark.sql.execution.python.UserDefinedPythonFunction with name, wrapped function, type, eval type and determinism.

nodes.name: __call__
nodes.summary: Converts arguments (including named arguments) to JVM columns and returns a Column wrapping judf.apply; when the Python or memory profiler config is on, wraps the function with a profiler and builds the expression through builderWithColumns instead.

nodes.name: _wrapped
nodes.summary: Wraps the UDF in a plain function that keeps the original docstring and exposes func, returnType, evalType, deterministic, asNondeterministic and _unwrapped, for interactive help (SPARK-19161).

nodes.name: asNondeterministic
nodes.summary: Marks the UDF nondeterministic and clears the cached JVM function so it is recreated with the new flag (SPARK-23233).

nodes.name: UDFRegistration
nodes.summary: Implementation behind spark.udf and sqlContext.udf for registering Python functions, pandas UDFs and Java UDFs/UDAFs as SQL functions.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers a Python function or an existing UDF under a SQL name: validates the eval type for UDFs, rebuilds the UDF with the new name via _create_udf, and calls the JVM udf().registerPython with the UDF's _judf.

nodes.name: registerJavaFunction
nodes.summary: Registers a Java UDF class by name with an optional return type, delegating to the JVM udf().registerJava.

nodes.name: registerJavaUDAF
nodes.summary: Registers a Java user-defined aggregate function class by name via the JVM udf().registerJavaUDAF.

nodes.name: _test
nodes.summary: Runs the module doctests against a local[4] SparkSession.

nodes.name: DataSourceScanExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical scan operators for data sources. FileSourceScanExec is what a spark.read.parquet(...).filter(...) query becomes after planning: it lists files for the selected partitions, builds the reader function from the FileFormat, splits files into FilePartitions and wraps them in a FileScanRDD. RowDataSourceScanExec covers V1 BaseRelation scans.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala traits with lazy vals: relation-dependent vals are lazy so the plan can be canonicalized on executors (SPARK-23731).

nodes.name: DataSourceScanExec
nodes.summary: Base trait of scan leaf nodes. Extends LeafExecNode, defines the node name 'Scan <relation> <table>', renders the metadata map (Format, ReadSchema, PushedFilters, ...) in explain output and requires inputRDDs().

nodes.name: DataSourceScanExec.verboseStringWithOperatorId
nodes.summary: Builds the verbose explain block for a scan: formatted node name, Output and the metadata entries, skipping empty values and the DataFilters and Format keys.

nodes.name: RowDataSourceScanExec
nodes.summary: Physical scan for V1 BaseRelation sources (for example JDBC): holds an already built RDD[InternalRow] plus pushed filters and pushed-down operators (aggregates, limit, top-N, offset, sample, joins), and reports them in explain metadata.

nodes.name: RowDataSourceScanExec.metrics
nodes.summary: Declares the numOutputRows metric and merges extra metrics when the underlying RDD mixes in DataSourceMetricsMixin.

nodes.name: RowDataSourceScanExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Maps the stored RDD through an UnsafeProjection of the output schema while counting numOutputRows.

nodes.name: RowDataSourceScanExec.metadata
nodes.summary: Builds the explain metadata map: ReadSchema, PushedFilters (handled filters are starred), and pushed aggregates, group-by, top-N or limit, offset, sample and joins.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike
nodes.summary: Base trait for file scans with the file-listing and metrics logic. Holds partitionFilters (partition pruning), dataFilters (non-partition columns, source of pushed filters), bucket info and the HadoopFsRelation, and decides selectedPartitions, bucketed output partitioning and the metadata shown by explain.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.vectorTypes
nodes.summary: Asks the relation's FileFormat for column vector class names and appends ConstantColumnVector for file constant metadata columns.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.driverMetrics
nodes.summary: Driver-side metrics: numFiles, metadataTime, filesSize, plus numPartitions and pruningTime when the relation has a partition schema, plus static metrics for dynamic partition pruning.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.sendDriverMetrics
nodes.summary: Posts the driver metrics for the current SQL execution id; must run after selectedPartitions is initialized (SPARK-26327).

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.selectedPartitions
nodes.summary: Planning-time file listing: drops dynamic pruning (subquery) filters, then calls relation.location.listFiles(staticPartitionFilters, staticDataFilters) so the FileIndex prunes partition directories, and wraps the result in a ScanFileListing with file count, size and metadata time metrics.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.dynamicallySelectedPartitions
nodes.summary: Runtime pruning: when dynamic partition filters exist (for example from a join), binds them to partition columns and filters the already selected partitions, recording pruningTime and file metrics.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.bucketedScan
nodes.summary: True when bucketing is enabled, the relation has a BucketSpec, the planner did not disable bucketed scan and all bucket columns are in the scan output.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Computes (outputPartitioning, outputOrdering): HashPartitioning on the bucket columns, with a sort order only if every bucket has a single file and buckets are not coalesced; otherwise UnknownPartitioning(0) and no ordering.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.translateToV1Filters
nodes.summary: Replaces scalar subqueries by literals, drops filters touching constant metadata columns, and translates Catalyst data filters into data source Filters via DataSourceStrategy.translateFilter.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.pushedDownFilters
nodes.summary: Lazy list of V1 Filters handed to the file format reader; it may execute subqueries, so it is not touched at planning time.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.metadata
nodes.summary: Builds explain metadata: Format, ReadSchema, Batched, PartitionFilters, PushedFilters, DataFilters, Location, and Bucketed info with the selected bucket count or the reason bucketing is off.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.verboseStringWithOperatorId
nodes.summary: Verbose explain text for file scans, abbreviating the Location to the first root path plus a count of the others.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.metrics
nodes.summary: Exposes scanMetrics (numOutputRows, scanTime for columnar scans, plus driver metrics) as the operator's SQL metrics.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanLike.setFilesNumAndSizeMetric
nodes.summary: Writes file count, total size and partition count of a listing into the static or regular driver metrics.

nodes.name: GenericScanFileListing
nodes.summary: Default ScanFileListing backed by an array of PartitionDirectory. Supports dynamic partition and file pruning, conversion to PartitionedFiles, byte totals including open cost, and a check that each bucket has at most one file.

nodes.name: GenericScanFileListing.filterAndPruneFiles
nodes.summary: Keeps partition directories whose partition values satisfy the bound predicate, then prunes files inside them with a FilePruningRunner when dynamic file filters exist.

nodes.name: GenericScanFileListing.bucketsContainSingleFile
nodes.summary: Groups file names by bucket id and returns true if no bucket has more than one file; used to decide whether a sort order can be reported.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec
nodes.summary: Physical plan node for scanning a HadoopFsRelation (Parquet, ORC, CSV, JSON, ...). Pushed filters go to the FileFormat reader, while partitionFilters and dataFilters drive file listing. inputRDD builds the reader and creates a FileScanRDD over bin-packed FilePartitions, or bucket-grouped ones when the scan is bucketed.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec.supportsColumnar
nodes.summary: Reports columnar output only when whole-stage codegen is enabled, the schema does not have too many fields, and FileFormat.supportBatch accepts the schema.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec.needsUnsafeRowConversion
nodes.summary: True only for Parquet when the vectorized reader is enabled; in that case row output must be converted to UnsafeRow in doExecute.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec.inputRDD
nodes.summary: Core of the scan: adds the returning_batch option, calls fileFormat.buildReaderWithPartitionValues with the pushed-down filters, then creates a bucketed or regular read RDD over the dynamically selected partitions and sends driver metrics.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Row-based execution: maps inputRDD rows through an UnsafeProjection when needed and counts numOutputRows.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec.doExecuteColumnar
nodes.summary: Columnar execution: casts inputRDD to RDD[ColumnarBatch] and wraps batches to measure scanTime (file reading happens in hasNext) and numOutputRows.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec.createBucketedReadRDD
nodes.summary: Builds a FileScanRDD for bucketed reads: groups PartitionedFiles by bucket id, prunes by optionalBucketSet, optionally coalesces buckets, and makes one FilePartition per bucket id.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec.createReadRDD
nodes.summary: Builds a FileScanRDD for non-bucketed reads: computes maxSplitBytes, applies bucket pruning to files, splits splittable files into PartitionedFiles, sorts them by size descending and bin-packs them into FilePartitions.

nodes.name: FileSourceScanExec.doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes the scan by dropping the stream and table identifier, normalizing output and filter expressions and removing unused dynamic pruning placeholders, so equal scans can be reused.

nodes.name: FileScanRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines PartitionedFile (a byte range of one file plus partition values) and FileScanRDD, the RDD that actually reads files. Each Spark task computes one FilePartition by opening its PartitionedFiles one after another with the reader function built by the FileFormat, handling ignoreCorruptFiles/ignoreMissingFiles, input metrics and _metadata columns.
nodes.languageNotes: The compute method returns an anonymous Iterator that also implements AutoCloseable and is cast to Iterator[InternalRow] (erasure hack) so it can hand out both rows and ColumnarBatch objects.

nodes.name: PartitionedFile
nodes.summary: A part (block) of a single file to read: partition column values, file path, start offset, length, preferred locations, modification time, file size and extra constant metadata column values.

nodes.name: FileScanRDD
nodes.summary: RDD[InternalRow] that scans a list of FilePartitions with a PartitionedFile => Iterator[InternalRow] read function (the Parquet or ORC reader built by FileFormat), appending file-constant metadata columns when requested.

nodes.name: FileScanRDD.compute
nodes.summary: Per-task logic: iterates the PartitionedFiles of the FilePartition, calls readFunction on each, tracks bytes and records read in input metrics, sets InputFileBlockHolder, appends metadata columns, optionally skips missing or corrupt files, and closes the iterator on task completion.

nodes.name: FileScanRDD.createMetadataColumnVector
nodes.summary: For columnar batches, builds ConstantColumnVectors holding each metadata column value for the current file.

nodes.name: FileScanRDD.addMetadataColumnsIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Appends metadata columns to the next element: new ColumnarBatch with constant vectors, a projected JoinedRow for UnsafeRow, or a JoinedRow for other InternalRows.

nodes.name: FileScanRDD.nextIterator
nodes.summary: Advances to the next PartitionedFile: updates metadata row and InputFileBlockHolder, closes the previous iterator and opens the next one, lazily when missing or corrupt files are ignored.

nodes.name: FileScanRDD.getPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the FilePartitions supplied to the RDD as its Spark partitions.

nodes.name: FileScanRDD.getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Delegates to FilePartition.preferredLocations for data locality.

nodes.name: FilePartition.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FilePartition (the unit of work of one scan task: several PartitionedFiles) and its companion helpers that compute maxSplitBytes from spark.sql.files settings and pack split files into partitions with a Next Fit Decreasing bin-packing.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object overloads maxSplitBytes and getFilePartitions; the private overload of getFilePartitions does the packing and the public one adds the max partition number rescaling.

nodes.name: FilePartition
nodes.summary: Case class that is both an RDD Partition and a V2 InputPartition: an index plus an array of PartitionedFiles read by a single task, with preferredLocations choosing the three hosts holding the most bytes.

nodes.name: FilePartition.preferredLocations
nodes.summary: Sums bytes per host over the partition's files (ignoring localhost) and returns the top three hosts.

nodes.name: FilePartition.getFilePartitions
nodes.summary: Public entry point that packs PartitionedFiles into FilePartitions (private overload at lines 58-88 uses Next Fit Decreasing: close the partition when size would exceed maxSplitBytes, charging openCostInBytes per file) and re-packs with a larger split size when the count exceeds spark.sql.files.maxPartitionNum.

nodes.name: FilePartition.maxSplitBytes
nodes.summary: Computes the split size as min(filesMaxPartitionBytes, max(openCostInBytes, totalBytes / minPartitionNum)); overloads accept a ScanFileListing or a Seq[PartitionDirectory] (lines 135-149).

nodes.name: FileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: Core abstraction for file-based sources. The FileFormat trait declares schema inference, write preparation, whether the format can return columnar batches, whether files are splittable, and buildReader/buildReaderWithPartitionValues which return a PartitionedFile => Iterator[InternalRow] function used by FileSourceScanExec. The companion object defines _metadata column helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Trait with default implementations; formats such as ParquetFileFormat override buildReaderWithPartitionValues directly, while others implement buildReader and inherit the partition-column appending wrapper.

nodes.name: FileFormat
nodes.summary: Trait used to read and write data stored in files in InternalRow format. Implementations plug into HadoopFsRelation and expose schema inference, write preparation, supportBatch, vectorTypes, isSplitable and the reader factory methods.

nodes.name: FileFormat.inferSchema
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the schema of the given files, or None when inference is unsupported.

nodes.name: FileFormat.prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Abstract: prepares a write job and returns an OutputWriterFactory.

nodes.name: FileFormat.supportBatch
nodes.summary: Whether the format can return ColumnarBatch output; defaults to false and is overridden by Parquet and ORC.

nodes.name: FileFormat.vectorTypes
nodes.summary: Concrete column vector class names for each column when batch output is supported; defaults to None.

nodes.name: FileFormat.isSplitable
nodes.summary: Whether a file at this path may be split into several byte ranges; defaults to false.

nodes.name: FileFormat.buildReader
nodes.summary: Protected hook returning the function that reads one PartitionedFile into an Iterator[InternalRow], given data, partition and required schemas, pushed Filters and options; throws by default.

nodes.name: FileFormat.buildReaderWithPartitionValues
nodes.summary: Wraps buildReader so that partition values from the PartitionedFile are appended to each row via a generated UnsafeProjection; formats that read partition values natively (Parquet) override it.

nodes.name: FileFormat.createFileMetadataCol
nodes.summary: Creates the hidden _metadata struct attribute from metadataSchemaFields with internal field metadata stripped.

nodes.name: FileFormat.metadataSchemaFields
nodes.summary: Fields of the format's _metadata struct (constant or generated); defaults to the base file_path, file_name, file_size, block start, block length and modification time.

nodes.name: FileFormat.fileConstantMetadataExtractors
nodes.summary: Extractors used to derive file-constant metadata column values from a PartitionedFile; defaults to BASE_METADATA_EXTRACTORS.

nodes.name: FileFormat.getFileConstantMetadataColumnValue
nodes.summary: Looks up an extractor by column name (falling back to the PartitionedFile's extra metadata map) and returns the value as a typed Literal.

nodes.name: FileFormat.createMetadataInternalRow
nodes.summary: Builds a metadata InternalRow straight from a file status (path, name, size, modification time) when scanning files directly.

nodes.name: FileFormat.updateMetadataInternalRow
nodes.summary: Fills an existing row with metadata column values for the current PartitionedFile, setting nulls where the value is null.

nodes.name: TextBasedFileFormat
nodes.summary: Abstract base for text-based formats such as CSV and JSON; its isSplitable checks the Hadoop compression codec and allows splitting if there is no codec or it is splittable.

nodes.name: TextBasedFileFormat.isSplitable
nodes.summary: Uses a lazily created CompressionCodecFactory to return true when the file has no codec or a SplittableCompressionCodec.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.scala
nodes.summary: FileFormat implementation for Parquet. buildReaderWithPartitionValues returns the per-file reader: it reads the footer, converts pushed Spark Filters to a Parquet FilterPredicate with ParquetFilters (row group level filtering), and then uses either the vectorized reader (columnar batches) or the parquet-mr row reader. Also schema inference and merging, write preparation and _metadata.row_index.
nodes.languageNotes: Both a class and a companion object share the name ParquetFileFormat; functions prefixed ParquetFileFormat. cover members of either, distinguished by line range (object starts at line 438).

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat
nodes.summary: Parquet implementation of FileFormat and DataSourceRegister (short name 'parquet'). Supports batch reads when the schema allows, is always splittable, pushes filters down to Parquet, and falls back to parquet-mr when vectorized reading is not possible.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Builds ParquetOptions from the session conf and delegates to ParquetUtils.prepareWrite to configure the Hadoop job and return the OutputWriterFactory.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.inferSchema
nodes.summary: Delegates schema inference over the given files to ParquetUtils.inferSchema.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.supportBatch
nodes.summary: Returns whether the vectorized reader can return batches for the schema, via ParquetUtils.isBatchReadSupportedForSchema.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.vectorTypes
nodes.summary: Returns OnHeapColumnVector or OffHeapColumnVector class names for each required column, and ConstantColumnVector for each partition column.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.isSplitable
nodes.summary: Parquet files are always splittable (row groups), so this returns true.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.setupHadoopConf
nodes.summary: Sets the Hadoop configuration for the read: ParquetReadSupport class, requested schema JSON, session time zone, nested schema pruning, case sensitivity and Parquet-to-Spark schema converter flags.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.buildReaderWithPartitionValues
nodes.summary: Builds the reader closure. Driver side it reads the pushdown flags (date, timestamp, decimal, string predicate, IN threshold) and decides vectorized vs parquet-mr and batch return. Per file it opens the footer, resolves rebase modes, builds ParquetFilters from the file schema, ANDs the converted predicates, sets them on ParquetInputFormat for row group filtering, then builds a vectorized or row-based iterator.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.buildVectorizedIterator
nodes.summary: Creates a VectorizedParquetRecordReader with rebase specs and batch size, initializes it with the already opened footer and input stream (transferring stream ownership), initializes the batch with partition values and optionally enables returning ColumnarBatch.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.buildRowBasedIterator
nodes.summary: Fallback to parquet-mr: creates a ParquetRecordReader with ParquetReadSupport, applies the pushed FilterPredicate as a record-level filter only when spark.sql.parquet.recordLevelFilter is enabled, and projects rows to UnsafeRow with partition values appended.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.supportDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively checks that a data type is writable and readable as Parquet: atomic, null, geospatial with supported SRID, struct, array, map and UDT of supported types.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.metadataSchemaFields
nodes.summary: Adds the generated row_index field to the base _metadata fields.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.readSchema
nodes.summary: Reads the Spark SQL schema serialized in Parquet footer key-value metadata (JSON, then legacy parser) or converts the Parquet schema, de-duplicating and merging schemas across footers.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.readParquetFootersInParallel
nodes.summary: Reads Parquet footers with 8 threads, skipping row group info, and skips missing or corrupt files when the corresponding ignore configs are set.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.mergeSchemasInParallel
nodes.summary: Merges Parquet schemas of many files with a distributed job through SchemaMergeUtils, reading footers and converting each to a StructType.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.readSchemaFromFooter
nodes.summary: Returns the deserialized Spark schema from a footer's key-value metadata if present, otherwise converts the footer's Parquet MessageType.

nodes.name: ParquetFileFormat.deserializeSchemaString
nodes.summary: Parses a serialized Spark schema as JSON, falls back to the legacy case class string parser, and returns None with a warning on failure.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the Spark SQL planning and analysis rules for data sources: DataSourceAnalysis (rewrites CREATE/INSERT into data source commands), FindDataSourceTable (resolves catalog tables to LogicalRelation), and the DataSourceStrategy object that plans scans over V1 sources and translates Catalyst predicates into sources.Filter objects. The filter translation and selection code is reused by FileSourceStrategy for file scans.

nodes.name: DataSourceAnalysis
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule object that replaces generic CreateTable and InsertIntoStatement nodes with data source specific commands (CreateDataSourceTableCommand, InsertIntoDataSourceCommand, InsertIntoHadoopFsRelationCommand). It must run after PreprocessTableCreation and PreprocessTableInsertion.

nodes.name: DataSourceAnalysis.convertStaticPartitions
nodes.summary: Validates a static-partition INSERT (for example INSERT INTO t PARTITION (b=2, c)) and builds the project list that puts static partition values back into the SELECT output in the order normal, static, dynamic columns. Throws compilation errors for mismatched column or partition counts and for static partitions after dynamic ones.

nodes.name: DataSourceAnalysis.apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point that matches CreateTable, InsertIntoDir and InsertIntoStatement over a HadoopFsRelation or InsertableRelation and rewrites them to the corresponding data source commands, adding a Project for static partitions and checking that overwrite does not read the output path.

nodes.name: FindDataSourceTable
nodes.summary: Analyzer rule that replaces UnresolvedCatalogRelation with a concrete LogicalRelation (using a DataSource and the session catalog table cache), a Hive table, or a StreamingRelation. This is how a catalog table read via spark.table or SQL becomes a HadoopFsRelation-backed plan.

nodes.name: FindDataSourceTable.readDataSourceTable
nodes.summary: Builds a LogicalRelation for a catalog data source table via DataSource.resolveRelation(checkFilesExist = false), caching it in the session catalog and refreshing the cached HadoopFsRelation when read options differ from the cached ones.

nodes.name: FindDataSourceTable.getStreamingRelation
nodes.summary: Creates a StreamingRelation for a catalog table by building a DataSource with the table schema, options and the user provided streaming source name.

nodes.name: FindDataSourceTable.apply
nodes.summary: Rule body that resolves UnresolvedCatalogRelation inside inserts, appends, batch reads, and streaming reads (including NamedStreamingRelation and StreamingRelationV2 fallback to V1) and records resolved relations for the single-pass resolver bridge.

nodes.name: FindDataSourceTable.resolveUnresolvedCatalogRelation
nodes.summary: Dispatches an UnresolvedCatalogRelation to readDataSourceTable for data source tables, to DDLUtils.readHiveTable for Hive tables, or to getStreamingRelation when the relation is streaming.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy
nodes.summary: Physical planning Strategy for V1 data source scans (CatalystScan, PrunedFilteredScan, PrunedScan, TableScan). It splits predicates into pushed filters and residual filters, prunes columns, produces RowDataSourceScanExec plus Filter/Project nodes, and exposes shared helpers (translateFilter, selectFilters, normalizeExprs) that FileSourceStrategy also uses.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.apply
nodes.summary: Strategy entry point: matches PhysicalOperation over a LogicalRelation whose relation is CatalystScan, PrunedFilteredScan or PrunedScan and calls pruneFilterProject(Raw), or a TableScan and produces a RowDataSourceScanExec directly. Returns Nil for anything else.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.pruneFilterProject
nodes.summary: Public API variant of pruneFilterProjectRaw that hands the scan builder only the requested columns and the pushed sources.Filter array.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.pruneFilterProjectRaw
nodes.summary: Core scan planner: normalizes attributes, calls selectFilters to split pushed and unhandled predicates, computes the required columns (dropping columns referenced only by fully handled filters), builds a RowDataSourceScanExec and wraps it in FilterExec for unhandled predicates and ProjectExec when a project is still needed.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.translateJoinType
nodes.summary: Maps Catalyst Inner, LeftOuter and RightOuter join types to the DSv2 join type enum; any other join type yields None.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.normalizeExprs
nodes.summary: Rewrites attribute names in expressions to match the names in the relation schema, so case-insensitive analysis does not leak differently cased names into pushed filters and partition pruning.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.getPushedDownFilters
nodes.summary: Extracts, from the normalized filters, the sub-predicates that reference only partition columns (via extractPredicatesWithinOutputSet) and logs them as the directory pruning predicates. Returns an empty set when the table has no partition columns.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.collationAwareFilter
nodes.summary: Wraps a sources.Filter into its Collated* variant when the column type is a string with a non-UTF8-binary collation, otherwise returns the filter unchanged.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.translateLeafNodeFilter
nodes.summary: Translates a single leaf Catalyst predicate (comparison, In/InSet, IsNull, StartsWith/EndsWith/Contains, boolean literal or boolean column) against a pushable column into the matching sources.Filter, flipping operand order when the literal is on the left.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.translateFilter
nodes.summary: Tries to convert a Catalyst predicate into a data source Filter, returning None when it is not convertible. Thin wrapper over translateFilterWithMapping without a mapping.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.translateFilterWithMapping
nodes.summary: Recursively translates And, Or, Not and leaf predicates into sources.Filter, optionally recording leaf filter to expression mappings. And/Or require both sides to be convertible, because converting only one side is unsafe (SPARK-12218).

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.rebuildExpressionFromFilter
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a Catalyst expression from a data source Filter using the leaf translation map, throwing if a leaf filter has no recorded expression.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.selectFilters
nodes.summary: Partitions predicates into (a) those that are not convertible or that the relation reports as unhandled via BaseRelation.unhandledFilters, (b) all pushed sources.Filter objects, and (c) filters fully handled by the source. Unhandled predicates must be re-evaluated by a Spark Filter node after the scan.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.translateAggregation
nodes.summary: Translates Catalyst aggregate and group-by expressions into a DSv2 Aggregation, returning None if any expression is not pushable.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.translateSortOrders
nodes.summary: Translates Catalyst SortOrder expressions into DSv2 SortValue orders (direction and null ordering), dropping sort orders that are not pushable.

nodes.name: DataSourceStrategy.toCatalystRDD
nodes.summary: Converts an RDD[Row] from a V1 relation into an RDD[InternalRow] with Catalyst types using an ExpressionEncoder serializer when relation.needConversion is true, otherwise casts the RDD.

nodes.name: PushableColumnBase
nodes.summary: Extractor base class that returns the column name of an expression that can be pushed down: a top-level attribute without dots, or a (possibly nested) struct field path when nested predicate pushdown is enabled.

nodes.name: PushableColumn
nodes.summary: Factory object that selects PushableColumnAndNestedColumn or PushableColumnWithoutNestedColumn according to whether nested predicate pushdown is enabled.

nodes.name: PushableColumnAndNestedColumn
nodes.summary: PushableColumnBase singleton with nested predicate pushdown enabled.

nodes.name: PushableColumnWithoutNestedColumn
nodes.summary: PushableColumnBase singleton with nested predicate pushdown disabled.

nodes.name: FileSourceStrategy.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FileSourceStrategy, the physical planning strategy that turns a logical scan over a HadoopFsRelation (spark.read.parquet/orc/csv/json tables) into a FileSourceScanExec. It classifies filters into partition filters, bucket pruning filters, pushed data filters and post-scan filters, and derives the required columns and metadata columns.

nodes.name: FileSourceStrategy
nodes.summary: Strategy for scans over (possibly partitioned or bucketed) file collections. Its doc describes the phases: split filters by evaluation point, prune the read schema, give filters and schema to the FileFormat, use partition predicates to list files, then split files into tasks (by bucket id, or by size threshold sorted by decreasing size) in a FileScanRDD.

nodes.name: FileSourceStrategy.shouldPruneBuckets
nodes.summary: Returns true only when the bucket spec has exactly one bucket column and more than one bucket.

nodes.name: FileSourceStrategy.getExpressionBuckets
nodes.summary: Evaluates a filter expression on the bucket column into a BitSet of matching bucket ids: equality, In, InSet, IsNull and IsNaN select specific buckets, And intersects, Or unions, and anything else selects all buckets.

nodes.name: FileSourceStrategy.genBucketSet
nodes.summary: ANDs the normalized filters, computes the matching bucket BitSet and logs how many buckets were pruned. Returns None (scan all buckets) when no filters exist or every bucket is selected.

nodes.name: FileSourceStrategy.apply
nodes.summary: Plans a HadoopFsRelation scan found under ScanOperation. It normalizes deterministic filters, derives partitionKeyFilters (partition-column-only predicates used to prune directories), an optional bucketSet, and dataFilters (including the data-column part of mixed predicates, skipping non-scalar subqueries and bloom filters) that are translated into pushed sources.Filter. Remaining afterScanFilters plus stay-up filters drive the required columns, which become readDataColumns; it then builds a FileSourceScanExec and wraps it with a metadata Project, FilterExec and ProjectExec as needed.

nodes.name: FileSourceStrategy.MetadataStructColumn
nodes.summary: Local extractor object inside apply that recognizes the hidden _metadata struct attribute and restores each field's internal metadata from the FileFormat's metadataSchemaFields, so the flattened constant and generated metadata columns can be mapped back.

nodes.name: FileSourceStrategy.rebindFileSourceMetadataAttributesInFilters
nodes.summary: Local helper that rewrites data filters referencing the _metadata struct so they point at the flattened constant or generated metadata attributes, replacing struct field access with the field value expressions.

nodes.name: PruneFileSourcePartitions.scala
nodes.summary: Optimizer rule that prunes partitions of a catalog file source table at optimization time: it swaps the CatalogFileIndex for a pruned file index based on partition filters and updates table statistics. The partition filters remain in the plan for physical planning.

nodes.name: PruneFileSourcePartitions
nodes.summary: Rule[LogicalPlan] applied to a HadoopFsRelation backed by a CatalogFileIndex when the table is partitioned and filters exist. It keeps only deterministic, subquery-free, non-PythonUDF filters, extracts partition key filters, calls CatalogFileIndex.filterPartitions, and recomputes size and row count statistics via FilterEstimation.

nodes.name: PruneFileSourcePartitions.rebuildPhysicalOperation
nodes.summary: Rebuilds Project(projects, Filter(conjunction of filters, relation)) over the pruned relation, so the partition predicates stay visible in physical planning.

nodes.name: PruneFileSourcePartitions.apply
nodes.summary: Transforms matching PhysicalOperation subtrees: normalizes filters, splits out partition key filters with DataSourceUtils.getPartitionFiltersAndDataFilters, replaces the file index with the pruned one, estimates pruned statistics, and rebuilds the plan with the original filters.

nodes.name: FileIndex.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the FileIndex trait (enumerates root paths and, subject to partition filters, the files grouped by partition), plus PartitionDirectory, FileStatusWithMetadata and FilePruningRunner, which prunes files using file-constant metadata filters such as _metadata.file_path.

nodes.name: FileStatusWithMetadata
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a Hadoop FileStatus with an optional metadata map that custom FileIndex and FileFormat implementations can use, for example to expose file-constant metadata columns.

nodes.name: PartitionDirectory
nodes.summary: Case class representing the files of one partition directory together with the partition values as an InternalRow. A companion object (lines 101-105) keeps backward compatibility for callers passing plain FileStatus arrays.

nodes.name: FilePruningRunner
nodes.summary: Extracts filters that reference only file-constant metadata attributes (excluding block start and length), binds them to a metadata row, and prunes the files of a PartitionDirectory whose metadata does not satisfy the predicate.

nodes.name: FilePruningRunner.matchFileMetadataPredicate
nodes.summary: Evaluates the bound metadata filter against a file by building a metadata InternalRow from the path, length and modification time; returns true when there is no metadata filter.

nodes.name: FilePruningRunner.prune
