nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the PartitionDirectory containing only files that match the file metadata predicate.

nodes.name: FileIndex
nodes.summary: Trait for objects that enumerate a relation's root paths and list files grouped by partition after partition-filter pruning. It also exposes inputFiles, refresh, sizeInBytes, partitionSchema and an optional file listing time for metrics.

nodes.name: FileIndex.listFiles
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning PartitionDirectory values. Partition filters must only reference partition columns and are guaranteed by the result, while data filters are only hints that the engine will re-apply.

nodes.name: FileIndex.refresh
nodes.summary: Abstract method that invalidates any cached file listing.

nodes.name: FileIndex.metadataOpsTimeNs
nodes.summary: Optional time in nanoseconds spent listing files at optimization time, which physical execution reads to report file listing metrics. Defaults to None.

nodes.name: PartitioningAwareFileIndex.scala
nodes.summary: Abstract FileIndex base that understands partitioned directory layouts: it infers the partition spec from leaf directories, applies partition predicates, filters non-data and pattern-excluded files, and resolves base paths.

nodes.name: PartitioningAwareFileIndex
nodes.summary: Abstract class implementing FileIndex on top of subclass-provided leafFiles and leafDirToChildrenFiles maps. It derives partitionSchema from partitionSpec, supports options such as recursiveFileLookup, ignoreInvalidPartitionPaths and basePath, and provides listFiles, allFiles and partition inference.

nodes.name: PartitioningAwareFileIndex.listFiles
nodes.summary: Implements FileIndex.listFiles: for unpartitioned data returns one PartitionDirectory of all non-empty data files, and for partitioned data prunes partition paths with the partition filters (prunePartitions) then selects non-empty data files per directory. File metadata filters are applied afterwards through FilePruningRunner. Throws if recursiveFileLookup is combined with partitioned data.

nodes.name: PartitioningAwareFileIndex.allFiles
nodes.summary: Returns all files under the root paths: for unpartitioned non-recursive data it looks up each qualified root path in the leaf directory map or leaf file map, otherwise all leaf files, filtered by path pattern filters.

nodes.name: PartitioningAwareFileIndex.inferPartitioning
nodes.summary: Infers the PartitionSpec by passing leaf directories that contain data files to PartitioningUtils.parsePartitions, honoring type inference, user schema, base paths, case sensitivity, time zone and invalid-path handling. Returns the empty spec for recursive file lookup.

nodes.name: PartitioningAwareFileIndex.prunePartitions
nodes.summary: Keeps predicates that reference only partition columns, binds them to the partition value row, evaluates them against each discovered partition, and logs how many partitions were selected and pruned.

nodes.name: PartitioningAwareFileIndex.basePaths
nodes.summary: Computes the base paths that stop partition discovery: a validated user basePath option or, by default, the root paths (their parent for file paths). This is why reading a subdirectory like /path/something=true/ does not yield a something column unless basePath is set.

nodes.name: InMemoryFileIndex.scala
nodes.summary: In-memory FileIndex that eagerly lists leaf files under the root paths, caches the leaf files and directory-to-children map, and lazily infers or reuses the partition spec. Parallel listing is delegated to HadoopFSUtils via bulkListLeafFiles.

nodes.name: InMemoryFileIndex
nodes.summary: PartitioningAwareFileIndex that recursively lists files at construction (refresh0), filters out streaming _spark_metadata paths, caches leaf files and the inferred partition spec in volatile fields, and uses an optional FileStatusCache. This is the default file index behind spark.read file sources.

nodes.name: InMemoryFileIndex.partitionSpec
nodes.summary: Returns the cached partition spec, using the user specified spec if given or inferring it from the listed directories on first use.

nodes.name: InMemoryFileIndex.refresh
nodes.summary: Invalidates the file status cache and re-lists files, dropping the cached partition spec.

nodes.name: InMemoryFileIndex.refresh0
nodes.summary: Lists leaf files for the root paths and rebuilds the cached leaf file map, leaf directory to children map, and clears the cached partition spec.

nodes.name: InMemoryFileIndex.listLeafFiles
nodes.summary: Lists leaf files for the given paths, reusing entries from the FileStatusCache (counting cache hits) and listing the rest through bulkListLeafFiles, which may launch a Spark job for parallel listing. Records discovery metrics and the elapsed time.

nodes.name: InMemoryFileIndex$
nodes.summary: Companion object holding bulkListLeafFiles, the shared helper for listing leaf files of many paths.

nodes.name: InMemoryFileIndex.bulkListLeafFiles
nodes.summary: Chooses between a sequential HadoopFSUtils.listFiles (single path on a configured file system scheme) and HadoopFSUtils.parallelListLeafFiles (which uses a Spark job above the parallelism threshold), passing ignoreMissingFiles, locality and parallelism settings.

nodes.name: PathFilterWrapper
nodes.summary: Serializable PathFilter that combines an optional user path filter with HadoopFSUtils.shouldFilterOutPathName, excluding hidden and metadata names during listing.

nodes.name: HadoopFsRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines HadoopFsRelation, the BaseRelation that represents a file-based table: it bundles the FileIndex, partition and data schemas, bucket spec, FileFormat and options.

nodes.name: HadoopFsRelation
nodes.summary: Case class holding what Spark needs to read files: a FileIndex (location), partitionSchema, dataSchema, optional BucketSpec, FileFormat and options. It merges data and partition schemas (partition column types win on overlap, data schema order is kept) and scales size estimates by the file compression factor.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.scala
nodes.summary: Translates Spark data source Filters (the form of a PySpark df.filter(...) condition after DataSourceStrategy.translateFilter) into Parquet FilterPredicates that parquet-mr uses to skip row groups by column statistics, dictionaries or Bloom filters. It maps each Parquet primitive column to a typed predicate builder and refuses any filter whose column or value type does not match the file schema.
nodes.languageNotes: Each make* val is a PartialFunction from ParquetSchemaType to a predicate builder; a missing case (or a disabled pushDownDate, pushDownTimestamp or pushDownDecimal guard) makes lift return None so the filter is simply not pushed.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters
nodes.summary: Per-file converter created in ParquetFileFormat.buildReaderWithPartitionValues from the file's Parquet MessageType and pushdown flags (date, timestamp, decimal, string predicate, IN threshold, case sensitivity, rebase spec). createFilter returns an Option[FilterPredicate]; None means the filter is not pushed and Spark still applies it after the scan.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.nameToParquetField
nodes.summary: Walks the Parquet schema and builds a map from quoted column name (nested fields joined with dots) to its primitive field info; repeated columns, maps and lists are excluded, and in case-insensitive mode ambiguous names are dropped (SPARK-25132).

nodes.name: ParquetPrimitiveField
nodes.summary: Holds the field name path and ParquetSchemaType of a pushdown-eligible primitive column.

nodes.name: ParquetSchemaType
nodes.summary: Key used to choose a predicate builder: logical type annotation, primitive type name and type length of a Parquet column.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.dateToDays
nodes.summary: Converts a java Date or LocalDate to days since epoch and rebases Gregorian to Julian days when the datetime rebase mode is LEGACY.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.timestampToMicros
nodes.summary: Converts an Instant or Timestamp to microseconds and rebases to the Julian calendar when the rebase mode is LEGACY.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.decimalToByteArray
nodes.summary: Encodes a decimal's unscaled value as a fixed-length sign-extended Binary for FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY columns.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.toIntValue
nodes.summary: Converts a filter value (Number or Period as months) to an Integer, preserving null.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.toLongValue
nodes.summary: Converts a filter value (Duration as microseconds, LocalTime as micros of day, or Long) to a Long.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.makeEq
nodes.summary: PartialFunction from column type to a builder of FilterApi.eq predicates; also used with null values for IsNull. Covers boolean, integral, float, double, string, binary, date, timestamp, time and decimal.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.makeNotEq
nodes.summary: PartialFunction building FilterApi.notEq predicates per column type; used for IsNotNull and not-equal filters.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.makeLt
nodes.summary: PartialFunction building FilterApi.lt predicates per column type (no boolean).

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.makeLtEq
nodes.summary: PartialFunction building FilterApi.ltEq predicates per column type.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.makeGt
nodes.summary: PartialFunction building FilterApi.gt predicates per column type.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.makeGtEq
nodes.summary: PartialFunction building FilterApi.gtEq predicates per column type.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.makeInPredicate
nodes.summary: PartialFunction building FilterApi.in predicates from a HashSet of values per column type; used when the IN list is longer than the OR-expansion threshold.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.convertibleFilters
nodes.summary: Returns the subset of data source Filters (possibly with partially convertible AND branches trimmed) that can be pushed to Parquet; used to report PushedFilters.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.convertibleFiltersHelper
nodes.summary: Recursively keeps convertible parts of And, Or and Not filters; only AND may drop a branch, and not under NOT, using createFilter for leaf filters.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.createFilter
nodes.summary: Public entry point: converts one data source Filter to an Option[FilterPredicate] by calling createFilterHelper with partial AND pushdown allowed.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.valueCanMakeFilterOn
nodes.summary: Checks that the filter value's JVM type matches the Parquet column type (for example integral values must fit in INT32, decimals need matching scale); null always passes.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.isDecimalMatched
nodes.summary: Requires the decimal literal's scale to equal the file's decimal scale to avoid wrong results.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.canMakeFilterOn
nodes.summary: True when the column exists among pushdown-eligible fields and the value type matches.

nodes.name: ParquetFilters.createFilterHelper
nodes.summary: Core translation: matches IsNull, IsNotNull, EqualTo, EqualNullSafe, comparison operators, And, Or, Not, In, StringStartsWith, StringEndsWith and StringContains to FilterApi predicates. And may push one side only at top level or under other ANDs (canPartialPushDownConjuncts); Or needs both sides; In expands to ORs below the threshold or uses an IN set; string predicates become user-defined predicates.

nodes.name: PartitionedFileUtil.scala
nodes.summary: Helper object that turns a file listing entry (FileStatusWithMetadata) into PartitionedFile read tasks. Splittable files are cut into byte ranges of at most maxSplitBytes, and each range gets the HDFS block hosts that hold most of it as preferred locations. Used by the V1 FileSourceScanExec and the V2 FileScan when planning scan partitions.

nodes.name: PartitionedFileUtil
nodes.summary: Scala object with static helpers that build PartitionedFile objects (path, byte offset, length, partition values, preferred hosts, modification time, file size, metadata) for the file-scan RDD.

nodes.name: splitFiles
nodes.summary: Splits one file into PartitionedFile pieces. If the format is splittable it steps through the file in maxSplitBytes strides (the last piece takes the remainder), otherwise it returns a single piece covering the whole file.

nodes.name: getPartitionedFile
nodes.summary: Builds a single PartitionedFile for a byte range of a file. It looks up the preferred block hosts for that range and copies partition values, modification time, length and extra metadata from the listing entry.

nodes.name: getBlockHosts
nodes.summary: Given all block locations of a file and an (offset, length) range, computes the overlap with each block and returns the hosts of the block that holds the largest part of the range, or an empty array when nothing overlaps.

nodes.name: FileStatusCache.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the FileStatusCache abstraction that caches leaf-file listings of partition directories, so repeated queries over the same table do not re-list remote storage. Contains the shared in-memory Guava-backed implementation with a global size quota and optional TTL, and a no-op cache used when caching is disabled.

nodes.name: FileStatusCache
nodes.summary: Companion object that owns a process-wide SharedInMemoryCache. getOrCreate hands each caller its own client view over that shared quota, or NoopCache when file source partition management or the cache size config disables caching.

nodes.name: FileStatusCache
nodes.summary: Abstract cache of the leaf files of partition directories with getLeafFiles, putLeafFiles and invalidateAll. Each resolved catalog table gets its own instance, which is invalidated by refreshTable or refreshByPath.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Returns a FileStatusCache for the session: a new client view of the shared cache when manageFilesourcePartitions is on and filesourcePartitionFileCacheSize is above zero, otherwise NoopCache. Synchronized because the shared cache is created lazily.

nodes.name: SharedInMemoryCache
nodes.summary: Private Guava Cache keyed by (clientId, Path) that stores Array[FileStatus]. Entries are weighed with SizeEstimator, total weight is bounded by the configured byte quota, entries optionally expire after a TTL, and a one-time warning is logged on the first size-based eviction.

nodes.name: createForNewClient
nodes.summary: Creates an anonymous FileStatusCache whose entries are namespaced by a fresh clientId, so clients share memory for eviction but never see each other's entries. invalidateAll removes only that client's keys.

nodes.name: NoopCache
nodes.summary: Non-caching FileStatusCache used when partition file status caching is disabled: getLeafFiles always returns None and the put and invalidate methods do nothing.

nodes.name: LogicalRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines LogicalRelation, the logical plan leaf that wraps a V1 BaseRelation (a file-based HadoopFsRelation or a custom source) together with its output attributes and optional CatalogTable. Also provides the LogicalRelationWithTable extractor that planner rules pattern match on.

nodes.name: LogicalRelation
nodes.summary: Leaf logical plan linking a BaseRelation into a query plan. It canonicalizes by dropping the catalog table, takes statistics from the catalog or from relation.sizeInBytes, creates fresh attribute ids for self joins, refreshes the file index, and exposes hidden file metadata columns for HadoopFsRelation.
nodes.languageNotes: Case class mixing in LeafNode, StreamSourceAwareLogicalPlan, MultiInstanceRelation, ExposesMetadataColumns and NormalizeableRelation. The @transient stream field carries an optional SparkDataStream.

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Returns plan statistics from the catalog table stats when present (converted to plan stats with CBO awareness), otherwise falls back to the relation's sizeInBytes.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: MultiInstanceRelation hook: copies the relation with new expression ids for every output attribute so the same table can appear twice in a plan.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Refreshes cached file listings by calling location.refresh() when the relation is a HadoopFsRelation, and does nothing for other relation types.

nodes.name: metadataOutput
nodes.summary: Lazy val that exposes the hidden _metadata column built by the relation's FileFormat (createFileMetadataCol) for HadoopFsRelation, and nothing for other relations.

nodes.name: withMetadataColumns
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the relation whose output also includes the metadata columns that are not already in the output, copying plan tags. Returns this unchanged if there is nothing to add.

nodes.name: LogicalRelation
nodes.summary: Companion factory with two apply overloads that build a LogicalRelation from a BaseRelation (and optionally a CatalogTable). They convert the relation schema to attributes after replacing char/varchar types with annotated string types.

nodes.name: LogicalRelationWithTable
nodes.summary: Extractor object whose unapply returns (BaseRelation, Option[CatalogTable]) from a LogicalRelation, so rules such as FileSourceStrategy and DataSourceStrategy can match without the five-field default pattern.

nodes.name: interfaces.scala
nodes.summary: Public Data Source V1 API of org.apache.spark.sql.sources: provider traits (DataSourceRegister, RelationProvider, SchemaRelationProvider, CreatableRelationProvider, stream providers), the BaseRelation abstract class with its scan capability traits (TableScan, PrunedScan, PrunedFilteredScan, CatalystScan) and InsertableRelation. Custom sources plug into spark.read.format(...) and df.write.format(...) through these interfaces, which a PySpark user reaches by naming the format.
nodes.languageNotes: Almost entirely Scala traits annotated @Stable or @Unstable. The Filter classes that appear in unhandledFilters and PrunedFilteredScan.buildScan are not defined in this file.

nodes.name: DataSourceRegister
nodes.summary: Trait a data source implements to register a short alias (shortName), for example "parquet", so users can write format("parquet") instead of a fully qualified class name. A new instance is created for each DDL call.

nodes.name: shortName
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the format alias that users pass to format(...).

nodes.name: RelationProvider
nodes.summary: Trait for sources that build a BaseRelation from user options (USING clause or read.format). If the class is not found, Spark appends DefaultSource to the package name. Option keys are case insensitive.

nodes.name: createRelation
nodes.summary: Returns a new BaseRelation for the given SQLContext and case-insensitive options map.

nodes.name: SchemaRelationProvider
nodes.summary: Like RelationProvider but receives a user-specified schema. A source can mix in both to support schema inference and explicit schemas.

nodes.name: createRelation
nodes.summary: Returns a BaseRelation for the given options and the user-defined StructType schema.

nodes.name: StreamSourceProvider
nodes.summary: Experimental trait for providers that produce a streaming Source: sourceSchema reports the source name and schema, createSource builds the Source for a metadata path and options.

nodes.name: StreamSinkProvider
nodes.summary: Experimental trait for providers that produce a streaming Sink given partition columns and an OutputMode.

nodes.name: CreatableRelationProvider
nodes.summary: Trait for sources that can save a DataFrame (DataFrameWriter.save with a SaveMode and options) and return a BaseRelation describing the written data. It also declares which data types the source supports.

nodes.name: createRelation
nodes.summary: Saves the DataFrame to the destination according to the SaveMode and data source specific parameters, and returns the resulting BaseRelation.

nodes.name: supportsDataType
nodes.summary: Recursively checks whether a data type is supported: arrays, maps, structs and UDTs are unwrapped, atomic types, null, object, char and varchar are accepted, and anything else returns false. Sources can override it.

nodes.name: BaseRelation
nodes.summary: Abstract description of a collection of tuples with a known schema. Implementations expose sqlContext and schema and pick one of the Scan traits for execution. Equality must only hold when two relations return the same data, because it is used to substitute cached results. HadoopFsRelation extends it.

nodes.name: sizeInBytes
nodes.summary: Estimated relation size in bytes used by the planner to decide on broadcasting. It defaults to spark.sql.defaultSizeInBytes, so unknown tables are treated as too large to broadcast. Overestimating is safer.

nodes.name: unhandledFilters
nodes.summary: Returns the filters the source cannot fully evaluate; Spark re-applies those after the scan. The default returns all filters, which is always safe. Overriding it avoids double filtering when pushdown is exact.

nodes.name: TableScan
nodes.summary: BaseRelation capability: buildScan() returns all rows as an RDD[Row] with no column pruning or filtering.

nodes.name: PrunedScan
nodes.summary: BaseRelation capability: buildScan(requiredColumns) returns an RDD[Row] with only the requested columns.

nodes.name: PrunedFilteredScan
nodes.summary: BaseRelation capability: buildScan(requiredColumns, filters) prunes columns and may use the ANDed source Filters as an optimization. Spark evaluates the filters again, so false positives are allowed.

nodes.name: InsertableRelation
nodes.summary: BaseRelation capability for INSERT: insert(data, overwrite) replaces data when overwrite is true and appends otherwise. It assumes rows match the schema ordinals, the schema does not change, and fields are nullable.

nodes.name: CatalystScan
nodes.summary: Experimental scan trait that receives raw Catalyst Attributes and Expressions instead of source Filters. It is not binary compatible across releases and is intended for experimentation only.

nodes.name: buildScan
nodes.summary: Returns every row of the relation as an RDD[Row].

nodes.name: buildScan
nodes.summary: Returns an RDD[Row] holding only the required column names.

nodes.name: buildScan
nodes.summary: Returns an RDD[Row] limited to the required columns and filtered by the pushed-down source Filters.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Inserts the DataFrame, overwriting existing data when overwrite is true or appending when false.

nodes.name: SupportsStreamSourceMetadataColumns
nodes.summary: Extension of StreamSourceProvider for file-based streaming sources that expose metadata columns. getMetadataOutput returns the extra attributes appended after the source schema, and the caller resolves name conflicts.

nodes.name: getMetadataOutput
nodes.summary: Given the SparkSession, source options and an optional user schema, returns the metadata AttributeReferences that extend the stream source schema.

nodes.name: PythonRDD.scala
nodes.summary: JVM side of the PySpark RDD bridge: defines PythonRDD, the PythonFunction/SimplePythonFunction wrappers that carry pickled Python code, PythonException, broadcast and accumulator support for Python workers, and the PythonRDD object whose static methods (runJob, collectAndServe, newAPIHadoopFile, saveAsHadoopFile, ...) are called by pyspark through Py4J.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file that mixes private[spark] classes with a PythonRDD companion object of Py4J-facing helpers; data crosses to Python as length-prefixed byte arrays over authenticated sockets.

nodes.name: PythonRDD
nodes.summary: RDD[Array[Byte]] that pipes the partitions of a parent RDD through a PythonFunction. compute() builds a PythonRunner via PythonRunner(func, jobArtifactUUID) and runs it on the parent iterator; it can preserve the parent partitioner and is barrier-aware. The companion object PythonRDD holds the static helpers that pyspark calls.

nodes.name: PythonFunction
nodes.summary: Trait describing everything the Python runner needs to run a function: pickled command bytes, environment variables, python includes, python executable and version, broadcast variables and the Python accumulator. Its companion object (lines 94-96) defines the PythonAccumulator alias for CollectionAccumulator[Array[Byte]].

nodes.name: SimplePythonFunction
nodes.summary: Case class implementing PythonFunction for functions created by pyspark. pyspark/sql/udf.py _wrap_function instantiates it through Py4J (sc._jvm.SimplePythonFunction) with the cloudpickled command, env, includes, pythonExec, pythonVer, broadcast vars and accumulator; an auxiliary constructor accepts Array[Byte].

nodes.name: ChainedPythonFunctions
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping a sequence of PythonFunction values that are chained from bottom to top. PythonRunner and the SQL Python UDF runners take Seq[ChainedPythonFunctions] so several Python functions can be evaluated in one worker.

nodes.name: PythonException
nodes.summary: RuntimeException thrown for errors raised in user Python code. It implements SparkThrowable, supports error class plus message parameters via SparkThrowableHelper, and carries the QueryContext. Created by ReaderIterator.handlePythonException when the worker reports a Python traceback.

nodes.name: PairwiseRDD
nodes.summary: Private RDD that turns the flat stream of byte arrays returned from Python into (Long, Array[Byte]) pairs by grouping two consecutive elements, decoding the first as a long key. Used by PySpark shuffle operations such as partitionBy.

nodes.name: PythonAccumulatorV2
nodes.summary: AccumulatorV2 (CollectionAccumulator of byte arrays) behind PySpark accumulators. On the driver, merge() sends the collected pickled updates to the Python-side accumulator server over a TCP or Unix domain socket (with a secret for authentication) and waits for an acknowledgement byte.

nodes.name: PythonBroadcast
nodes.summary: Serializable handle for a PySpark broadcast variable stored in a file on the driver. Java serialization streams the file contents; deserialization on an executor writes them into a DISK_ONLY broadcast block. It also sets up encryption and decryption socket servers used when I/O encryption is enabled.

nodes.name: DechunkedInputStream
nodes.summary: InputStream that reassembles data which Python wrote in length-prefixed chunks ending with a -1 length; it is the inverse of pyspark ChunkedStream and lets Python stream objects of unknown size without buffering them. Its companion object (lines 970-984) provides dechunkAndCopyToOutput.

nodes.name: EncryptedPythonBroadcastServer
nodes.summary: SocketAuthServer that sends decrypted broadcast data (an id followed by the file contents) to a Python worker when I/O encryption is on; the worker acknowledges by reading one byte. The protocol is documented in PythonRunner.

nodes.name: PythonRDDServer
nodes.summary: Abstract SocketAuthServer that accepts one connection from Python, wraps the stream in a DechunkedInputStream and calls streamToRDD to build a JavaRDD[Array[Byte]]. Used instead of temp files when encryption is enabled.

nodes.name: PythonParallelizeServer
nodes.summary: Concrete PythonRDDServer used by SparkContext.parallelize from pyspark; streamToRDD delegates to PythonRDD.readRDDFromInputStream with the requested parallelism.

nodes.name: getWorkerBroadcasts
nodes.summary: Returns, under a lock, the set of broadcast ids already sent to a given PythonWorker, backed by a weak hash map so the runner only ships each broadcast once per worker.

nodes.name: runJob
nodes.summary: Py4J entry point for SparkContext.runJob from pyspark: runs the RDD on selected partitions, flattens the arrays and serves them via serveIterator. Returns port, auth secret and server object.

nodes.name: collectAndServe
nodes.summary: Collects an RDD to the driver and serves the elements over an authenticated local socket. This is what RDD.collect in pyspark calls through Py4J.

nodes.name: collectAndServeWithJobGroup
nodes.summary: Same as collectAndServe but first sets the job group id, description and interruptOnCancel on the SparkContext.

nodes.name: toLocalIteratorAndServe
nodes.summary: Serves an RDD partition by partition through a SocketFuncServer: each request from Python (non-zero int) triggers a collection job for the next partition, with optional prefetching. The response is 1 (data follows), 0 (consumed) or -1 (error). Backs pyspark RDD.toLocalIterator.

nodes.name: setupBroadcast
nodes.summary: Creates a PythonBroadcast for a file path; called from pyspark when it registers a broadcast variable.

nodes.name: writeNextElementToStream
nodes.summary: Writes one element of an iterator to a DataOutputStream in the PySpark wire format: null as a special length, byte arrays and strings length-prefixed, PortableDataStream as bytes, and key-value tuples as two consecutive values. Returns false when the iterator is exhausted. Reused by PythonRunner and PythonUDFRunner writers.

nodes.name: writeIteratorToStream
nodes.summary: Drains an iterator into a DataOutputStream by repeatedly calling writeNextElementToStream.

nodes.name: newAPIHadoopFile
nodes.summary: Representative of the Hadoop input helpers (sequenceFile, newAPIHadoopFile, newAPIHadoopRDD, hadoopFile, hadoopRDD, lines 382-538): load key/value classes by name, merge the confAsMap from Python into the Hadoop conf, apply optional key and value Converters, and return a JavaRDD of pickled pairs via SerDeUtil.pairRDDToPython.

nodes.name: serveIterator
nodes.summary: Serves all items of an iterator on a one-shot authenticated local socket in a background thread. The socket accepts one connection and closes if none arrives within 15 seconds. Returns port, secret and server object.

nodes.name: serveToStream
nodes.summary: Creates a socket server and a background thread that runs the supplied write function against the socket output stream; delegates to SocketAuthServer.serveToStream with the shared SocketAuthHelper.

nodes.name: saveAsHadoopFile
nodes.summary: Representative of the Hadoop output helpers (saveAsSequenceFile, saveAsHadoopFile, saveAsNewAPIHadoopFile, saveAsHadoopDataset, lines 642-735): convert a Python RDD of pickled pairs to a pair RDD, infer or load key and value classes, convert to Writables with converters, and save through the old mapred OutputFormat.

nodes.name: openSocket
nodes.summary: Lazily opens (and reuses) the socket to the Python accumulator server, using a Unix domain socket or TCP host and port, and sends the secret token once on a new connection.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another accumulator. On the driver it writes the number of pickled updates and each byte array to the Python accumulator server and blocks until a one-byte acknowledgement arrives, throwing SparkException on EOF.

nodes.name: writeObject
nodes.summary: Java serialization hook: writes the broadcast id then streams the broadcast file contents into the object stream.

nodes.name: readObject
nodes.summary: Java deserialization hook: reads the broadcast id and, if the block is missing on this executor, copies the stream to a temp file and registers it as a DISK_ONLY BroadcastBlockId(id, "python") so unpersist/destroy can clear it (SPARK-28486); then points path at the block file.

nodes.name: setupEncryptionServer
nodes.summary: Starts a SocketAuthServer that receives the chunked broadcast data from Python, dechunks it and writes it, encrypted, to the broadcast file path. Returns connection info and secret.

nodes.name: setupDecryptionServer
nodes.summary: Starts a SocketAuthServer that reads the encrypted broadcast file, decrypts it and streams it to the Python driver. Returns connection info and secret.

nodes.name: dechunkAndCopyToOutput
nodes.summary: Wraps the chunked input in a DechunkedInputStream, copies it to the output and closes both streams safely.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonFunction.scala
nodes.summary: Driver-side entry point for Python UDFs, UDAFs and UDTFs: UserDefinedPythonFunction builds PythonUDF or PythonUDAF expressions from the PythonFunction that pyspark created, UserDefinedPythonTableFunction builds a Generate plan for UDTFs, and UserDefinedPythonTableFunctionAnalyzeRunner runs the UDTF analyze method in a Python worker.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case classes constructed from Python through Py4J (see UserDefinedFunction._create_judf in pyspark/sql/udf.py). UDAFs have no separate class here: builder returns a PythonUDAF expression for grouped-aggregate eval types.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonFunction
nodes.summary: Case class (name, func, dataType, pythonEvalType, udfDeterministic) that pyspark constructs through Py4J for each Python UDF. builder() validates named arguments (only allowed for batched, scalar and grouped-aggregate eval types) and returns a PythonUDAF for the grouped aggregate pandas/arrow eval types, otherwise a PythonUDF; apply() wraps the expression in a Column. The func field is a PythonFunction, in practice a SimplePythonFunction holding the pickled command.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Checks that named arguments have no duplicates and no positional argument after a named one (or throws namedArgumentsNotSupported for other eval types), then builds PythonUDAF(name, func, dataType, e, udfDeterministic, pythonEvalType) for grouped-aggregate pandas/arrow eval types or PythonUDF(...) for all others.

nodes.name: builderWithColumns
nodes.summary: Convenience overload of builder that accepts Columns and converts them to expressions.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Returns a Column that calls this UDF with the given input columns by converting them to expressions, calling builder and wrapping the result via fromUDFExpr.

nodes.name: fromUDFExpr
nodes.summary: Wraps a UDF expression in a Column, converting a PythonUDAF to an AggregateExpression via toAggregateExpression.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonTableFunction
nodes.summary: Case class for a Python UDTF (name, func, optional returnType, pythonEvalType, udfDeterministic) with auxiliary constructors for Py4J. builder() checks named arguments, marks table arguments, and creates a PythonUDTF when the return type is declared or an UnresolvedPolymorphicPythonUDTF that calls the Python analyze method otherwise; the result is a Generate over OneRowRelation. apply() turns it into a DataFrame.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Builds the logical plan for a UDTF call: validates named arguments, records which arguments are TABLE arguments, picks PythonUDTF (static schema) or UnresolvedPolymorphicPythonUDTF (schema from a UserDefinedPythonTableFunctionAnalyzeRunner), and wraps it in Generate(udtf, ..., child = OneRowRelation()).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Converts Column and TableArg arguments to expressions, calls builder with the session SQL parser, and returns the Dataset.ofRows result as a DataFrame.

nodes.name: UserDefinedPythonTableFunctionAnalyzeRunner
nodes.summary: PythonPlannerRunner that launches the pyspark.sql.worker.analyze_udtf worker to run a UDTF static analyze method during analysis. It sends the function and each argument (JSON data type, pickled value when foldable, table flag, optional name) and reads back the output schema, pickled AnalyzeResult, partitioning, ordering and selected input expressions, or a Python exception that becomes a TABLE_VALUED_FUNCTION_FAILED_TO_ANALYZE_IN_PYTHON error.

nodes.name: writeToPython
nodes.summary: Writes the UDTF name and Python function, then for every argument writes its JSON data type, a foldable flag with the pickled evaluated value, the table-argument flag and the optional argument name.

nodes.name: receiveFromPython
nodes.summary: Reads the analyze result from the worker: the schema JSON, pickled AnalyzeResult buffer, single-partition flag, partitionBy and orderBy expressions (parsed with the SQL parser, rejecting aliased ordering columns) and selected input expressions, and returns a PythonUDTFAnalyzeResult. A PYTHON_EXCEPTION_THROWN length is turned into a compilation error.

nodes.name: pythonLogicalOperators.scala
nodes.summary: Catalyst logical operators for Python execution: BatchEvalPython/ArrowEvalPython and their UDTF variants (produced by ExtractPythonUDFs/ExtractPythonUDTFs), pandas and Arrow group/cogroup/map operators, stateful pandas operators, AttachDistributedSequence and the python_worker_logs table function. SparkStrategies turns them into physical Exec nodes.
nodes.languageNotes: Mostly Scala case classes extending UnaryNode or BinaryNode, each with the withNewChildInternal/withNewChildrenInternal copy methods required by TreeNode.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandas
nodes.summary: Applies a pandas UDF to each group (pandas.DataFrame to pandas.DataFrame) for DataFrame.groupby().apply(). Output attributes are declared as producedAttributes so Catalyst does not treat them as missing inputs.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInArrow
nodes.summary: Applies a UDF to each group as iterators of pyarrow.RecordBatch, used by DataFrame.groupby().applyInArrow().

nodes.name: MapInPandas
nodes.summary: Maps partitions with a UDF from an iterator of pandas.DataFrame to an iterator of pandas.DataFrame, for DataFrame.mapInPandas(); carries isBarrier and an optional ResourceProfile.

nodes.name: MapInArrow
nodes.summary: Maps partitions with a UDF over pyarrow.RecordBatch iterators for DataFrame.mapInArrow() in PySpark; carries isBarrier and an optional ResourceProfile.

nodes.name: FlatMapCoGroupsInPandas
nodes.summary: Cogroups two plans by grouping keys and applies a pandas UDF to each pair of groups, for DataFrame.groupby().cogroup().apply(). References include the first leftGroupingLen/rightGroupingLen output columns of each side.

nodes.name: FlatMapGroupsInPandasWithState
nodes.summary: Pandas counterpart of FlatMapGroupsWithState for arbitrary stateful streaming: applies functionExpr to each group with state data (stateType, output mode, timeout).

nodes.name: TransformWithStateInPySpark
nodes.summary: Logical operator for the arbitrary state API v2 with a Python stateful processor. It is binary because it can take an optional initial-state plan; left/right grouping attributes are the first groupingAttributesLen and initGroupingAttrsLen columns. The companion object (lines 248-253) defines UserFacingDataType (python_row or pandas).

nodes.name: FlatMapCoGroupsInArrow
nodes.summary: Cogroups two plans and applies a UDF over pyarrow.RecordBatch iterators, for DataFrame.groupby().cogroup().applyInArrow().

nodes.name: BaseEvalPython
nodes.summary: Trait for operators that evaluate PythonUDFs: output is the child output plus resultAttrs, which are the produced attributes, and the node pattern is EVAL_PYTHON_UDF.

nodes.name: BaseEvalPythonUDTF
nodes.summary: Trait for operators that evaluate a PythonUDTF: output is requiredChildOutput plus resultAttrs, and the node pattern is EVAL_PYTHON_UDTF.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPython
nodes.summary: Logical plan that evaluates PythonUDFs row by row in batches (pickle protocol). ExtractPythonUDFs creates it and the PythonEvals strategy plans it as BatchEvalPythonExec.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPython
nodes.summary: Logical plan that evaluates PythonUDFs with Apache Arrow for the given evalType (scalar pandas/arrow UDFs). Planned as ArrowEvalPythonExec by the PythonEvals strategy.

nodes.name: BatchEvalPythonUDTF
nodes.summary: Logical plan that evaluates a PythonUDTF in batches; requiredChildOutput lets the planner omit child data that a later projection would discard.

nodes.name: ArrowEvalPythonUDTF
nodes.summary: Logical plan that evaluates a PythonUDTF using Apache Arrow for the given evalType.

nodes.name: AttachDistributedSequence
nodes.summary: Adds a long column that increases one by one (output is sequenceAttr followed by the child output). Used for the distributed-sequence index in the pandas API on Spark and for DataFrame.zipWithIndex; the cache flag controls caching.

nodes.name: PythonWorkerLogs
nodes.summary: Leaf relation backing the python_worker_logs table function, which returns logs collected from Python workers as a table with a single message column. It is a MultiInstanceRelation with a default size estimate.

nodes.name: leftAttributes
nodes.summary: Returns the first groupingAttributesLen output columns of the child; asserts the plan is resolved.

nodes.name: rightAttributes
nodes.summary: Returns the first initGroupingAttrsLen columns of the initial state plan, or dummy left-side grouping columns when there is no initial state so physical distribution and ordering checks still pass.

nodes.name: functionBuilder
nodes.summary: Registers the python_worker_logs table function. When Python worker logging is enabled it builds a projection that parses the JSON message column with from_json using the Spark log schema; otherwise it throws pythonWorkerLoggingNotEnabledError.

nodes.name: Rule.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Rule[TreeType], the abstract base of every Catalyst rule: a named function from one tree (usually a LogicalPlan or SparkPlan) to a transformed tree. Analyzer, optimizer, AQE and physical-planning rules extend it, and RuleExecutor runs them in batches.
nodes.languageNotes: Abstract class bounded by TreeNode[_]; subclasses are typically Scala objects that define apply(plan) using transform* methods.

nodes.name: Rule
nodes.summary: Abstract class Rule[TreeType <: TreeNode[_]] extends SQLConfHelper with Logging (conf is inherited from SQLConfHelper, not defined here). Subclasses implement apply(plan: TreeType): TreeType; ruleName defaults to the class name without a trailing $, and ruleId is looked up from RuleIdCollection to prune unnecessary tree traversals.

nodes.name: ruleId
nodes.summary: Protected lazy integer id of the rule from RuleIdCollection.getRuleId(ruleName), used to prune tree traversals that cannot be affected by the rule.

nodes.name: ruleName
nodes.summary: Rule name derived from getClass.getName, with a trailing $ removed for Scala objects. Used in plan change logging and metrics by RuleExecutor.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Abstract method that transforms the input tree and returns the new tree; the single piece of behavior every concrete rule must provide.

nodes.name: VectorizedParquetRecordReader.java
nodes.summary: Hadoop RecordReader that decodes Parquet column chunks directly into Spark ColumnVectors. It returns either ColumnarBatch objects (the fast path used for DataFrame scans) or InternalRows backed by a reused batch, and handles missing columns, INT96 and date rebasing, partition-value columns and file row index generation. Parquet scans use it when the vectorized reader is enabled.
nodes.languageNotes: Java class in the Scala-centric sql/core module. It uses SQLConf$.MODULE$ to reach Scala objects and scala.jdk.javaapi.CollectionConverters to iterate Scala collections.

nodes.name: VectorizedParquetRecordReader
nodes.summary: Extends SpecificParquetRecordReaderBase<Object>. Allocates on-heap or off-heap column vectors of a given capacity, appends constant partition columns, loads one row group at a time and fills the batch with VectorizedColumnReaders. Returns the ColumnarBatch itself when enableReturningBatches is called, otherwise iterates its rows.

nodes.name: VectorizedParquetRecordReader
nodes.summary: Constructor storing the timezone for INT96 conversion, datetime and INT96 rebase modes and zones, the memory mode (off-heap or on-heap) and the batch capacity. A second test-only constructor supplies fixed defaults.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: RecordReader entry point: runs the base-class initialization (opens the file, reads the footer, builds the requested schema and ParquetColumn tree) then initializeInternal to classify missing columns. Overloads take a Hadoop split plus optional pre-opened input file, stream and footer, a plain path plus column list, or an explicit schema and row-group reader for tests.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the reused ColumnarBatch and then the underlying base reader.

nodes.name: nextKeyValue
nodes.summary: Hadoop RecordReader step: ensures the batch exists, then either loads the next batch (batch mode) or advances a row cursor within the current batch, loading a new batch when it is exhausted.

nodes.name: getCurrentValue
nodes.summary: Returns the whole ColumnarBatch when batch mode is enabled, otherwise the current row of the batch.

nodes.name: initBatch
nodes.summary: Builds the ColumnarBatch. The batch schema is the Spark schema (truncated back to the requested schema unless the legacy null-struct config is set) with partition columns appended. It allocates the vectors, wraps them in ParquetColumnVectors with per-column default values, fills ConstantColumnVectors with partition values and creates the row index generator. The public and no-arg overloads delegate to it.

nodes.name: truncateType
nodes.summary: Recursively trims struct fields from the end of the read type so it has as many fields as the requested type, removing extra fields added to read struct nullability when requested fields were missing from the file. Works through arrays, maps and UDTs.

nodes.name: resultBatch
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and returns the reused ColumnarBatch. Calling it enables the vectorized path and must occur before nextKeyValue or nextBatch.

nodes.name: enableReturningBatches
nodes.summary: Switches the reader to return ColumnarBatch objects instead of rows.

nodes.name: nextBatch
nodes.summary: Resets all column vectors, loads the next row group when the current one is used up, lets each leaf column reader decode up to capacity values, assembles nested vectors, fills the file row index column when needed and updates counters. Returns false when all rows were returned.

nodes.name: initializeInternal
nodes.summary: Creates the set of missing columns and validates every top-level requested ParquetColumn against the file schema.

nodes.name: checkColumn
nodes.summary: Recursively compares a requested column with the file schema. For existing primitive columns it fails on descriptor mismatch. For missing columns it throws if the column is required, otherwise it records the column so NULLs (or defaults) are returned.

nodes.name: containsPath
nodes.summary: Recursive path lookup in a Parquet type that, unlike MessageType.containsPath, supports paths to both leaf and group nodes.

nodes.name: checkEndOfRowGroup
nodes.summary: When all rows of the loaded row group were returned, reads the next row group from the Parquet file reader, initializes the row index generator and column readers, and extends the loaded row count. Throws if more rows are expected but none remain.

nodes.name: initColumnReader
nodes.summary: Creates a VectorizedColumnReader (with timezone, rebase settings and writer version) for each non-missing primitive column and recurses into struct children.

nodes.name: allocateColumns
nodes.summary: Allocates OffHeapColumnVector or OnHeapColumnVector for data columns and ConstantColumnVector for the trailing constant (partition) columns.

nodes.name: ParquetReadSupport.scala
nodes.summary: Parquet-mr ReadSupport implementation used by the row-based (non-vectorized) Parquet reader, plus the schema clipping logic shared by both readers. It decides which Parquet columns to read by clipping the file schema to the Catalyst requested schema: fields are matched by name (case sensitive or not) or by field id, missing fields are added, and nested columns are pruned.

nodes.name: ParquetReadSupport
nodes.summary: ReadSupport[InternalRow] that parquet-mr instantiates on the executor. init computes the Parquet requested schema from the Catalyst schema stored in the Hadoop conf, and prepareForRead returns a ParquetRecordMaterializer that converts Parquet records to InternalRows with timezone and rebase specs.
nodes.languageNotes: Has a zero-argument auxiliary constructor because SpecificParquetRecordReaderBase needs one; its values are ignored by the vectorized reader.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Reads the requested Catalyst schema from SPARK_ROW_REQUESTED_SCHEMA in the Hadoop configuration, calls ParquetReadSupport.getRequestedSchema with the file schema, and returns a ReadContext holding the Parquet requested schema.

nodes.name: prepareForRead
nodes.summary: Creates the ParquetRecordMaterializer from the requested Parquet schema and the UDT-expanded Catalyst schema, together with a ParquetToSparkSchemaConverter, timezone and rebase specs.

nodes.name: ParquetReadSupport
nodes.summary: Companion object holding the configuration keys SPARK_ROW_REQUESTED_SCHEMA and SPARK_METADATA_KEY, and the schema clipping, intersection and UDT expansion helpers.

nodes.name: getRequestedSchema
nodes.summary: Top-level schema planning. It reads case sensitivity, nested pruning, field id and legacy flags from the conf, fails when the Spark schema has field ids but the file has none, clips the file schema to the requested schema and, for the parquet-mr reader with nested pruning, intersects the result with the file schema.

nodes.name: clipParquetSchema
nodes.summary: Tailors the Parquet message schema to the Catalyst schema: drops columns that are not requested, adds requested columns missing from the file, and returns the empty message schema when nothing remains.

nodes.name: clipParquetType
nodes.summary: Dispatches clipping by Catalyst type: nested arrays, maps and structs (variant structs are left as is) are clipped recursively, while primitives and UDTs are returned unchanged. Field ids are carried over when field id reading is on.

nodes.name: clipParquetListType
nodes.summary: Clips a Parquet LIST group for an array with a nested element type, handling both the unannotated repeated group form and the LIST-annotated layouts (including the legacy "array" and "_tuple" naming rules).

nodes.name: clipParquetMapType
nodes.summary: Clips a Parquet MAP group by clipping its key and value types inside the repeated key_value group and rebuilding the group with the original annotations and ids.

nodes.name: clipParquetGroup
nodes.summary: Clips a Parquet group for a Catalyst struct by clipping its fields, then rebuilds the group with the same repetition, annotation and name.

nodes.name: clipParquetGroupFields
nodes.summary: Matches each requested struct field to a Parquet field by id, exact name or case-insensitive name (failing on ambiguous matches), clips it, and creates a new Parquet field for fields absent from the file. If every field of a struct is missing and the legacy flag is off, it adds one cheap existing field so struct nullness can be determined.

nodes.name: findCheapestGroupField
nodes.summary: Heuristic search for the leaf (or the key and value leaves for maps) that is cheapest to read under a group. It prefers lower repetition levels and smaller primitive types, and is used when all requested struct fields are missing from the file.

nodes.name: intersectParquetGroups
nodes.summary: Computes the structural intersection of two group types so the parquet-mr reader only requests nested fields that exist in the file.

nodes.name: expandUDT
nodes.summary: Replaces every UserDefinedType in a schema (inside arrays, maps and structs) with its underlying sqlType.

nodes.name: containsFieldIds
nodes.summary: Whether any field in the Parquet schema carries a field id. A group counts as having ids if the group or any descendant has one.

nodes.name: ParquetUtils.scala
nodes.summary: Utility object for Parquet file sources: schema inference that chooses which footers or summary files to read, field id helpers, the check that decides whether the vectorized columnar reader can handle a schema, aggregate (MIN/MAX/COUNT) pushdown answered from file footer statistics, and write job setup (output committer, write support, compression, variant shredding).

nodes.name: ParquetUtils
nodes.summary: Singleton with Parquet helpers called from ParquetFileFormat (inferSchema, prepareWrite, isBatchReadSupportedForSchema) and from the aggregate pushdown code.

nodes.name: inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers the Spark schema of a set of Parquet files. Without mergeSchema it reads one file, preferring _common_metadata, then _metadata, then any data file. With mergeSchema it reads all data files (or only summary files if respecting summaries is configured). Either way it delegates to ParquetFileFormat.mergeSchemasInParallel.

nodes.name: FileTypes
nodes.summary: Case class grouping files into data files, _metadata summary files and _common_metadata summary files.

nodes.name: splitFiles
nodes.summary: Sorts the file statuses by path and partitions them into data, metadata and common metadata groups using the Parquet summary file names.

nodes.name: hasFieldIds
nodes.summary: Whether any field in a StructType, including nested array, map and struct fields, has the parquet.field.id metadata key.

nodes.name: hasFieldId
nodes.summary: Whether a single StructField has the parquet.field.id metadata entry.

nodes.name: getFieldId
nodes.summary: Returns the field id of a StructField as a 32-bit Int, failing with an IllegalArgumentException when the metadata value is not an int.

nodes.name: isBatchReadSupportedForSchema
nodes.summary: True when the vectorized Parquet reader is enabled and every field type in the schema can be read in columnar batches. ParquetFileFormat uses it to decide supportBatch.

nodes.name: isBatchReadSupported
nodes.summary: Per-type check for the vectorized reader: atomic types are supported, null type and nested array, map and struct types depend on their config flags, UDTs use their sqlType, and anything else is unsupported.

nodes.name: createAggInternalRowFromFooter
nodes.summary: Builds the single result InternalRow of pushed-down MIN, MAX and COUNT aggregates from Parquet footer statistics without reading data pages. Values go through a ParquetRowConverter, and partition columns are appended when there is a GROUP BY.

nodes.name: getPushedDownAggResult
nodes.summary: Walks every row group in the footer and computes each pushed aggregate: MAX and MIN from column statistics, COUNT as row count minus null count, and COUNT(*) as total row count. Returns the Parquet primitive types and the values.

nodes.name: getCurrentBlockMaxOrMin
nodes.summary: Reads the max or min of a column chunk from its statistics, throwing an unsupported-operation error that names the aggregate pushdown config when statistics have no non-null value.

nodes.name: getNumNulls
nodes.summary: Reads the null count of a column chunk from statistics, throwing if it was not recorded.

nodes.name: replaceVariantTypes
nodes.summary: Test helper that replaces VariantType fields (also inside nested structs, but not inside arrays, maps or UDTs) with a forced shredding schema.

nodes.name: needShreddingInference
nodes.summary: Returns true when variant shredding inference is enabled and the schema contains at least one variant.

nodes.name: prepareWrite
nodes.summary: Configures a Parquet write job: selects the output committer, sets ParquetOutputFormat and ParquetWriteSupport with the Spark schema, copies legacy format, timestamp type, field id and variant settings into the conf, sets compression, disables summary files by default, and returns an OutputWriterFactory (variant-shredding or plain writer).

nodes.name: session.py
nodes.summary: Spark Connect implementation of the Python SparkSession. A session wraps one SparkConnectClient (and its session id) and turns API calls such as sql, range, createDataFrame, read, conf and stop into Spark Connect logical plans or client RPCs; it also defines the Builder that resolves a spark.remote connection string or custom channel builder into a session, and the process-wide default and thread-local active session registry.
nodes.languageNotes: Most public methods copy their docstring from the classic pyspark.sql.session.SparkSession (X.__doc__ = PySparkSession.X.__doc__). There is no JVM or SparkContext: __getattr__ raises JVM_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_SUPPORTED for _jsc, _jvm, sparkContext, newSession and similar.

nodes.name: SparkSession
nodes.summary: Client-side session for Spark Connect, created through SparkSession.builder.remote(...).getOrCreate(). It owns self._client (a SparkConnectClient) and exposes the familiar entry points (sql, range, table, read, readStream, createDataFrame, catalog, conf, streams, udf, interrupt* and tag APIs). Everything runs over gRPC against a Spark Connect server; the only local work is Arrow conversion of local data.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Fluent builder returned by SparkSession.builder. It only collects options in a dict (config and appName store strings, remote stores the connection string, master is ignored, enableHiveSupport raises not implemented) plus an optional custom DefaultChannelBuilder and hook factories. No connection is opened until create() or getOrCreate() runs.

nodes.name: Hook
nodes.summary: Extension point for injecting behaviour into a session. Hook.on_execute_plan receives each ExecutePlanRequest before it is sent and returns the (possibly replaced) request; the client calls it in _execute and _execute_and_fetch_as_iterator.

nodes.name: on_execute_plan
nodes.summary: Default hook implementation: returns the ExecutePlanRequest unchanged. Subclasses override it to inspect or rewrite requests before they are sent.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Initializes an empty option dict, no channel builder, and an empty list of session hook factories.

nodes.name: config
nodes.summary: Implementation behind the config overloads: under a lock, stores a key/value pair or a whole map of options, converting values to strings with to_str. Options are applied to the session later by _apply_options.

nodes.name: remote
nodes.summary: Records the connection string (default sc://localhost) as the spark.remote option through config(). It does not connect; the string is parsed later by DefaultChannelBuilder when create() builds the SparkConnectClient.

nodes.name: channelBuilder
nodes.summary: Stores a custom DefaultChannelBuilder (kept in its own field because it may hold state and cannot be serialized with to_str) so the session can customize how gRPC connections are created. Mutually exclusive with spark.remote in create().

nodes.name: _apply_options
nodes.summary: After session creation, merges initial confs from the PYSPARK_REMOTE_INIT_CONF_<i> environment variables (spark.sql.* keys only) with the builder's own options, drops spark.remote and spark.master, and pushes the rest with session.conf._set_all(silent=True).

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates a brand-new session. Exactly one of a custom channel builder or spark.remote must be set (otherwise SESSION_NEED_CONN_STR_OR_BUILDER). It constructs SparkSession(connection=...), registers it as the default and active session, then applies the remaining options.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Under the SparkSession class lock, returns the thread-local active session, else the process-wide default session if it is not stopped, else a new one from create(). The builder options are re-applied to whichever session is returned.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Builds the SparkConnectClient from a connection string or ChannelBuilder, an optional userId and the session hooks (each factory is called with the session). Copies the client's session id and sets release_session_on_close, which stop() consults.

nodes.name: _set_default_and_active_session
nodes.summary: Classmethod that sets the global default session (under a lock) and the thread-local active session when they are not yet set.

nodes.name: _get_default_session
nodes.summary: Returns the process-wide default session if it exists and has not been stopped, else None.

nodes.name: getActiveSession
nodes.summary: Returns the thread-local active session if present and not stopped, else None.

nodes.name: active
nodes.summary: Returns the active session, falling back to the default session; raises NO_ACTIVE_OR_DEFAULT_SESSION when neither exists.

nodes.name: _getActiveSessionIfMatches
nodes.summary: Internal classmethod used by the unpickling handler from __reduce__: returns the active session after checking its session id equals the pickled one, avoiding serialization of a WeakRef.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Validates that tableName is a string and delegates to self.read.table(tableName).

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Property returning a Spark Connect DataFrameReader bound to this session.

nodes.name: readStream
nodes.summary: Property returning a Spark Connect DataStreamReader bound to this session.

nodes.name: _inferSchemaFromList
nodes.summary: Infers a StructType from a list of Row, dict or tuple by merging per-row inferred schemas, driven by the nested-dict, array, map and timestamp-type confs fetched earlier from the server.

nodes.name: createDataFrame
nodes.summary: Converts local data (pandas DataFrame, numpy ndarray, pyarrow Table, or an iterable of rows/dicts/tuples) into a pyarrow Table on the client, wraps it in a LocalRelation and returns a DataFrame. One get_config_dict call fetches timezone and local-relation limits; a DDL-string schema is parsed on the server via _analyze(ddl_parse). If the table is at least localRelationCacheThreshold bytes it is uploaded in chunks through _cache_local_relation instead of being embedded in the plan. samplingRatio and verifySchema are ignored with a warning.

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Builds an SQL plan node from the query, wrapping positional (list) or named (dict) args as literals and formatting keyword args through SQLStringFormatter. It sends the statement right away as a command via client.execute_command; if the reply holds sql_command_result the DataFrame wraps a CachedRelation of that result (with ExecutionInfo attached), otherwise a lazy DataFrame wraps the SQL plan.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame over a Range plan node (the single-argument form means end with start 0). It is lazy: no RPC happens until an action runs on the DataFrame.

nodes.name: interruptAll
nodes.summary: Interrupts all running operations of this session through client.interrupt_all() and returns the interrupted operation ids. interruptTag and interruptOperation follow the same pattern.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Best-effort, idempotent shutdown of this session only (the server is multi-tenant and keeps running): releases the server-side session through client.release_session(), closes the gRPC client, clears the default and active session references, and, when SPARK_LOCAL_REMOTE is set, also stops the locally started Spark Connect server.

nodes.name: is_stopped
nodes.summary: Property that reports whether the session was stopped, i.e. whether the underlying client is closed.

nodes.name: conf
nodes.summary: Property returning RuntimeConf(self.client), the runtime SQL configuration facade built on this session's client.

nodes.name: streams
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and caches the StreamingQueryManager for this session; __del__ closes it.

nodes.name: client
nodes.summary: Property exposing the underlying SparkConnectClient (self._client) that performs all RPCs for this session.

nodes.name: version
nodes.summary: Cached property that asks the server for its Spark version through client._analyze(method='spark_version').

nodes.name: addArtifacts
nodes.summary: Validates that at most one of pyfile, archive, file is set, then uploads the given paths as artifacts through client.add_artifacts.

nodes.name: _cache_local_relation
nodes.summary: Serializes a LocalRelation into a schema chunk plus data chunks and uploads them in size-bounded batches with client.cache_artifacts (one RPC per batch rather than per chunk). Raises LOCAL_RELATION_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED if the total exceeds the limit and returns a ChunkedCachedLocalRelation holding the chunk hashes.

nodes.name: _create_remote_dataframe
nodes.summary: Internal API that wraps a server-side runtime DataFrame id in a CachedRemoteRelation; used by the foreachBatch runner to refer to a micro-batch output.

nodes.name: _start_connect_server
nodes.summary: Static helper for local mode: starts a regular PySpark session whose spark.plugins is org.apache.spark.sql.connect.SparkConnectPlugin so a Spark Connect server launches in-process, makes sure SPARK_CONNECT_AUTHENTICATE_TOKEN is set, and keeps only runtime SQL confs. Raises SESSION_OR_CONTEXT_EXISTS if a classic PySpark session already exists.

nodes.name: __reduce__
nodes.summary: Pickling support: serializes only the session id and rebuilds through _getActiveSessionIfMatches, so unpickling works only when the same session is active.

nodes.name: cloneSession
nodes.summary: Clones the server-side session (confs, temp views, functions, catalog state) into an independent session via client.clone() and wraps the cloned client in a new SparkSession object created with object.__new__.

nodes.name: _test
nodes.summary: Doctest runner for the module: builds a session via PySpark's builder against SPARK_CONNECT_TESTING_REMOTE (default local[4]) and runs doctest.testmod on this module.

nodes.name: core.py
nodes.summary: Core of the Python Spark Connect client. It builds gRPC channels from sc:// connection strings (ChannelBuilder, DefaultChannelBuilder) and defines SparkConnectClient, which constructs ExecutePlan, AnalyzePlan, Config, Interrupt, ReleaseSession, GetStatus, FetchErrorDetails and CloneSession requests, sends them with retries, streams ExecutePlan responses back (reattachable by default), reassembles Arrow batches into pyarrow tables and pandas frames, collects metrics and observations, and converts gRPC errors into PySpark exceptions.
nodes.languageNotes: __all__ exports ChannelBuilder, DefaultChannelBuilder and SparkConnectClient. Plans above a server-advertised size threshold can be zstd compressed when the zstandard module is installed.

nodes.name: ChannelBuilder
nodes.summary: Base helper that turns connection parameters into a gRPC channel. Holds params parsed from the connection string, default options (128 MiB max send and receive message length) and optional client interceptors, and derives gRPC metadata, user id, bearer token, session id and a user-agent string. Subclasses implement toChannel.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Stores parameters, copies GRPC_DEFAULT_OPTIONS and applies caller-supplied channel options.

nodes.name: toChannel
nodes.summary: Abstract hook: concrete builders return a grpc.Channel (usually via _insecure_channel or _secure_channel so options and interceptors apply); the base class raises PySparkNotImplementedError.

nodes.name: metadata
nodes.summary: Returns the connection-string parameters as gRPC metadata pairs, excluding the ones the channel itself consumes (token, use_ssl, user_id, user_agent, session_id).

nodes.name: userAgent
nodes.summary: Builds the client_type string sent in requests: the user_agent parameter (or SPARK_CONNECT_USER_AGENT, default _SPARK_CONNECT_PYTHON) followed by spark, os and python versions; rejects values over 2048 characters after URL escaping.

nodes.name: DefaultChannelBuilder
nodes.summary: Standard ChannelBuilder for sc://host:port/;key=value connection strings. It validates the scheme and path, parses ;-separated parameters (use_ssl, token, user_id, session_id, ...), defaults the port to 15002, and creates an insecure, local-credential or SSL channel (with an optional bearer token).

nodes.name: default_port
nodes.summary: Returns 15002, except in test mode (SPARK_TESTING with a classic PySpark session) where it reads the actual local port from SparkConnectService via Py4J to support ephemeral ports.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Checks that the URL starts with sc:// and has no path, rewrites it to http:// for urllib parsing, and extracts attributes.

nodes.name: _extract_attributes
nodes.summary: Parses the ;key=value parameters into the builder's params, requires a hostname, and fixes host and port (default via default_port).

nodes.name: toChannel
nodes.summary: Creates the gRPC channel: insecure when neither use_ssl nor a token is set; local channel credentials for a token on localhost without SSL; otherwise SSL credentials, composed with the access token when present.

nodes.name: PlanObservedMetrics
nodes.summary: Observed metrics (from Dataset.observe) returned by the server: a name, a list of literal values and their keys, with a pairs property that decodes the literals and a to_dict export.

nodes.name: AnalyzeResult
nodes.summary: Plain holder for the optional fields of an AnalyzePlanResponse (schema, explain string, tree string, is_local, is_streaming, input files, Spark version, parsed DDL type, same-semantics, semantic hash, storage level, DDL string).

nodes.name: fromProto
nodes.summary: Decodes an AnalyzePlanResponse into an AnalyzeResult by checking which result field is set (schema, explain, ddl_parse, get_storage_level, ...); raises SparkConnectException when none is present.

nodes.name: ConfigResult
nodes.summary: Holder for a ConfigResponse: key/value pairs (value None when unset) and server warnings, built by fromProto.

nodes.name: fromProto
nodes.summary: Converts a ConfigResponse proto into a ConfigResult.

nodes.name: SparkConnectClient
nodes.summary: Conceptually the remote Spark session on the client side. It owns the gRPC channel and SparkConnectServiceStub, the client session id, user id, retry policies, progress handlers, session hooks and ArtifactManager, and builds every request (plan execution, analyze, config, interrupt, session release, status, error details, clone). Results come back as Arrow batches assembled into pyarrow tables, pandas frames or dict properties; failures are mapped to PySpark exceptions.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Sets up the client: parses the connection (string to DefaultChannelBuilder, or a given ChannelBuilder), installs a DefaultPolicy retry policy, picks the session id (UUID4 unless given in the connection string) and user id (connection string, argument, then SPARK_USER or USER), opens the channel, creates the SparkConnectServiceStub and ArtifactManager, and registers _on_exit with atexit.

nodes.name: set_retry_policies
nodes.summary: Replaces the list of RetryPolicy objects that _retrying() hands to Retrying; the constructor installs a single DefaultPolicy built from the retry_policy dict.

nodes.name: register_udf
nodes.summary: Registers a temporary Python UDF on the server by wrapping the function in PythonUDF and CommonInlineUserDefinedFunction, placing it in a register_function command, and executing the request with _execute. register_udtf, register_data_source and register_java follow the same command pattern.

nodes.name: register_data_source
nodes.summary: Registers a Python data source class by serializing it into a register_data_source command executed via _execute.

nodes.name: to_table_as_iterator
nodes.summary: Generator that sends a plan and yields the result schema (StructType) and then each Arrow batch as a pyarrow Table, with a Progress reporter attached; it streams results instead of materializing them all.

nodes.name: to_table
nodes.summary: Executes a Plan through _execute_and_fetch and returns the combined pyarrow Table, the optional schema and an ExecutionInfo carrying plan and observed metrics.

nodes.name: to_pandas
nodes.summary: Fetches timezone, struct handling mode and selfDestruct confs in one Config call, runs the plan via _execute_and_fetch, and converts the Arrow table to a pandas DataFrame with _convert_arrow_table_to_pandas; attaches metrics and observed metrics in DataFrame attrs.

nodes.name: _truncate
nodes.summary: Recursively copies a protobuf message while truncating long strings (1024 chars) and bytes (8 bytes) and cutting nesting depth, mirroring the server-side Abbreviator, so plans can be logged at debug level.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Returns the StructType of a plan by calling _analyze(method='schema'), i.e. the AnalyzePlan RPC.

nodes.name: explain_string
nodes.summary: Returns the explain output of a plan for a given mode through the AnalyzePlan RPC (_analyze(method='explain')).

nodes.name: execute_command
nodes.summary: Executes a Command: sets it into a new ExecutePlanRequest plan (compressing it when configured), runs _execute_and_fetch, and returns a tuple of an optional pandas DataFrame, a dict of command-result properties (for example sql_command_result) and ExecutionInfo.

nodes.name: execute_command_as_iterator
nodes.summary: Like execute_command but yields each dict-valued command result as it arrives from _execute_and_fetch_as_iterator, raising UNKNOWN_RESPONSE for non-dict items.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Waits up to 10 s for pending ReleaseExecute futures, shuts the shared release thread pool down if idle, closes the gRPC channel and marks the client closed.

nodes.name: _execute_plan_request_with_metadata
nodes.summary: Builds an ExecutePlanRequest with session_id, client_type (user agent), tags, observed server-side session id, user context (id and extensions), result chunking options (allow_arrow_batch_chunking, preferred chunk size) and an optional validated operation_id.

nodes.name: _analyze_plan_request_with_metadata
nodes.summary: Builds an AnalyzePlanRequest pre-filled with session id, server-side session id, client type and user context.

nodes.name: _analyze
nodes.summary: Single entry for the AnalyzePlan RPC. Fills the request according to method (schema, explain, tree_string, is_local, is_streaming, input_files, spark_version, ddl_parse, same_semantics, semantic_hash, persist, unpersist, get_storage_level, json_to_ddl), calls stub.AnalyzePlan inside the retry loop, verifies the response and returns an AnalyzeResult.

nodes.name: _execute
nodes.summary: Runs an ExecutePlanRequest and discards the results (used for commands such as UDF registration). Applies session hooks, then consumes an ExecutePlanResponseReattachableIterator, or falls back to a plain retried ExecutePlan stream when reattachable execution is disabled.

nodes.name: _execute_and_fetch_as_iterator
nodes.summary: Central streaming method behind plan execution. After applying hooks it iterates responses from the reattachable iterator (or a plain retried ExecutePlan stream) and yields Arrow batches, schema, PlanMetrics, PlanObservedMetrics and dict results; on KeyboardInterrupt it finishes progress and interrupts the operation, other errors go through _handle_error.

nodes.name: handle_response
nodes.summary: Nested generator that interprets one ExecutePlanResponse: verifies session ids, yields metrics, observed metrics (updating Observation objects and the UDF profiler) and the schema, maps command results (sql, streaming, pipeline, resources, checkpoint, ML) to dicts, updates progress, and reassembles Arrow batch chunks (checking chunk index, start offset and row count) before reading them with pa.ipc.open_stream.

nodes.name: _execute_and_fetch
nodes.summary: Drains _execute_and_fetch_as_iterator under a Progress context, sorts items into schema, record batches, metrics, observed metrics and properties, and returns a pyarrow Table (or None when no batches arrived) with those side results. With self_destruct it copies each column so Arrow memory can be freed column-wise.

nodes.name: get_configs
nodes.summary: Fetches several config keys in a single Config RPC (ConfigRequest.Get) and returns the values in key order.

nodes.name: get_config_dict
nodes.summary: Fetches several config keys in a single Config RPC and returns them as a dict; createDataFrame uses it to read all local-relation settings at once.

nodes.name: config
nodes.summary: Config RPC wrapper: builds the ConfigRequest with the given operation, calls stub.Config inside the retry loop, verifies the response and returns a ConfigResult.

nodes.name: interrupt_all
nodes.summary: Sends an Interrupt RPC of type ALL inside the retry loop and returns the interrupted operation ids. interrupt_tag and interrupt_operation differ only in the request type.

nodes.name: interrupt_operation
nodes.summary: Sends an Interrupt RPC for a single operation id; also called when a KeyboardInterrupt hits a running plan execution.

nodes.name: release_session
nodes.summary: Calls the ReleaseSession RPC (with retries) to drop the server-side session; used by SparkSession.stop and on exit when SPARK_CONNECT_RELEASE_SESSION_ON_EXIT is true.

nodes.name: _handle_error
nodes.summary: Common error funnel for RPC wrappers: guards against recursive handling with a thread-local flag, delegates grpc.RpcError to _handle_rpc_error, and re-raises everything else.

nodes.name: _handle_rpc_error
nodes.summary: Unpacks the google.rpc Status and ErrorInfo from a gRPC error and raises a PySpark exception through convert_exception, optionally with enriched details from FetchErrorDetails. It marks the client closed on INVALID_HANDLE.SESSION_CHANGED and disables plan compression on CONNECT_INVALID_PLAN.CANNOT_PARSE; without status details it raises SparkConnectGrpcException.

nodes.name: _fetch_enriched_error
nodes.summary: Calls the FetchErrorDetails RPC using the errorId carried in the ErrorInfo metadata to retrieve the full server-side error (including stack trace); returns None if the id is absent or the call fails.

nodes.name: add_artifacts
nodes.summary: Uploads each path as an artifact through ArtifactManager inside the retry loop, treating pyfile, archive and file flags as the artifact kind.

nodes.name: cache_artifacts
nodes.summary: Uploads blobs to the server-side artifact cache (used for chunked local relations) via ArtifactManager and returns their content hashes; retried like other RPCs.

nodes.name: _verify_response_integrity
nodes.summary: Checks every response: its session_id must equal the client session id, and the server_side_session_id must match the one first observed (stored from the first response); a mismatch marks the client closed and raises PySparkAssertionError.

nodes.name: _try_compress_and_set_plan
nodes.summary: Places a relation or command into the Plan, zstd-compressing it into a CompressedOperation when plan compression is enabled, the serialized size exceeds the threshold, the algorithm is ZSTD, zstandard is installed and compression actually shrinks it; otherwise sets plan.root or plan.command directly.

nodes.name: _get_plan_compression_threshold_and_algorithm
nodes.summary: Lazily reads spark.connect.session.planCompression.threshold and defaultAlgorithm from the server via get_configs; on failure it disables compression (-1, NONE).

nodes.name: clone
nodes.summary: Calls the CloneSession RPC to copy the server-side session state, then builds a new SparkConnectClient from a deep copy of the channel builder carrying the new session id.

nodes.name: _on_exit
nodes.summary: atexit handler: skips everything if the client is already closed; otherwise cleans the ML cache and, when SPARK_CONNECT_RELEASE_SESSION_ON_EXIT is true, releases the session and closes the client, swallowing errors.

nodes.name: _import_zstandard_if_available
nodes.summary: Returns the zstandard module if installed, else None; used to decide whether plan compression is possible.

nodes.name: reattach.py
nodes.summary: Implements reattachable execution for the Spark Connect Python client. ExecutePlanResponseReattachableIterator wraps the ExecutePlan stream, reattaches with ReattachExecute after retryable network errors or a graceful stream end without a result_complete message, and sends asynchronous ReleaseExecute RPCs so the server can drop buffered responses.

nodes.name: ExecutePlanResponseReattachableIterator
nodes.summary: Generator over ExecutePlanResponse messages that survives broken streams.
