It tags the request with a client operation id and reattachable=True, remembers the last returned response id, and when the stream ends or fails reconnects with ReattachExecute(last_response_id) so the server resumes after that response. If the original ExecutePlan never reached the server (INVALID_HANDLE.OPERATION_NOT_FOUND) before any response was returned, it re-sends ExecutePlan. ReleaseExecute is issued asynchronously on a shared thread pool.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Assigns an operation id if the request has none, appends reattach_options(reattachable=True), and starts the initial ExecutePlan stream. The first stream error only surfaces on the first read, where it is retried.

nodes.name: _release_thread_pool
nodes.summary: Lazily creates (under a class lock) the shared ThreadPoolExecutor, sized to the CPU count, that runs asynchronous ReleaseExecute calls.

nodes.name: shutdown_threadpool_if_idle
nodes.summary: Classmethod that shuts down the shared release pool when no iterator instances remain alive (tracked in a weak set); called from SparkConnectClient.close.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Generator protocol entry (next calls send(None)): waits for the next response via _has_next, records its response_id, then releases buffered server responses: everything when result_complete arrived, otherwise up to that response id.

nodes.name: _has_next
nodes.summary: Fetches the next response inside the retry loop. If the stream ends without result_complete it drops the iterator so _call_iter issues a ReattachExecute, repeating until a response arrives or the result is complete; on exception it releases the execution and re-raises.

nodes.name: _release_until
nodes.summary: Submits an asynchronous ReleaseExecute(release_until=response_id) to the thread pool (with retries) so the server can free responses the client has already processed; failures are only logged.

nodes.name: _release_all
nodes.summary: Submits an asynchronous ReleaseExecute(release_all) and marks the result complete; used when all results were consumed, on error, and on close.

nodes.name: _call_iter
nodes.summary: Calls next() on the current server stream, first creating a ReattachExecute stream if the iterator was unset. A gRPC error whose message holds INVALID_HANDLE.OPERATION_NOT_FOUND or SESSION_NOT_FOUND restarts ExecutePlan and raises RetryException when nothing was returned yet (RESPONSE_ALREADY_RECEIVED otherwise); other errors reset the iterator so the next retry reattaches.

nodes.name: _create_reattach_execute_request
nodes.summary: Builds a ReattachExecuteRequest from the initial request (session id, observed server session id, user context, operation id, client type) plus last_response_id when a response was already returned.

nodes.name: _create_release_execute_request
nodes.summary: Builds a ReleaseExecuteRequest for the operation, with release_all when no response id is given, else release_until that response id.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Releases the whole execution on the server (_release_all) and closes the generator.

nodes.name: plan.py
nodes.summary: Python Spark Connect client logical plan builders. A LogicalPlan base class and over 100 subclasses mirror DataFrame, catalog and command operations; calling plan(session) recursively builds a protobuf Relation tree (or command() a Command) that the client sends to the server, where SparkConnectPlanner turns it into a Catalyst logical plan.
nodes.languageNotes: Each class sets exactly one oneof field of proto.Relation (or proto.Command) and nests child plans with CopyFrom(child.plan(session)); plan ids come from a lock-protected class counter.

nodes.name: LogicalPlan
nodes.summary: Base class of every Connect client plan node. Holds an optional child plan, optional subquery references and a process-wide unique plan id from a locked counter. Subclasses override plan() to emit a protobuf Relation (or command() to emit a Command); the base class also provides to_proto(), the observations property, subquery reference handling and print/_repr_html_ helpers.

nodes.name: DataSource
nodes.summary: Leaf plan for DataFrameReader.load style reads. Validates format, schema, options, paths and predicates, then fills Relation.read.data_source (and read.is_streaming).

nodes.name: Parse
nodes.summary: Plan node that parses a single-string-column DataFrame into a structured one. plan() sets Relation.parse with the input, the format enum, an optional schema converted from DDL or JSON via pyspark_types_to_proto_types, and options.

nodes.name: Read
nodes.summary: Leaf plan that reads a named table (spark.table / readStream.table). plan() sets read.named_table.unparsed_identifier, options and is_streaming. The module also defines an internal-only family of catalog plan classes (CurrentDatabase, ListTables, GetTable, CreateTable, DropTable, CacheTable, ListCatalogs, AnalyzeTable and others, lines 2320-2798) that each emit a Relation.catalog message for the Catalog API.

nodes.name: RelationChanges
nodes.summary: Leaf plan for reading the changes of a named table. plan() fills Relation.relation_changes with the table identifier, options and is_streaming.

nodes.name: LocalRelation
nodes.summary: Plan built from a PyArrow Table (createDataFrame data) or from a schema only. plan() serializes the table as an Arrow IPC stream into local_relation.data and sets the schema; helpers also serialize in size-bounded chunks (_serialize_table_chunks). The sibling ChunkedCachedLocalRelation (lines 584-613) instead references previously uploaded chunks by hash through chunked_cached_local_relation.

nodes.name: ShowString
nodes.summary: Plan wrapper used by DataFrame.show. plan() sets show_string with the child relation, num_rows, truncate and vertical. HtmlString (lines 635-647) is the HTML variant with num_rows and truncate.

nodes.name: Project
nodes.summary: Projection (select) plan. Validates that all inputs are Column objects, collects subquery references and emits project.expressions; the result is wrapped by _with_relations when subqueries are present. Close relatives in this file: Hint (lines 793-818, Relation.hint), Drop (920-943, Relation.drop with columns or names), ToDF (2060-2070, to_df), ToSchema (1674-1684, to_schema) and WithColumnsRenamed (1687-1702).

nodes.name: WithColumns
nodes.summary: Plan for withColumn / withColumns / withMetadata. Validates names, columns and optional JSON metadata, then builds one Expression.Alias per column inside Relation.with_columns.

nodes.name: WithWatermark
nodes.summary: Streaming plan for withWatermark; sets with_watermark.input, event_time and delay_threshold.

nodes.name: CachedRemoteRelation
nodes.summary: Leaf plan that refers to a DataFrame cached on the server by relation_id (plan() sets cached_remote_relation.relation_id). It holds the SparkSession so that __del__ can ask the server to release the cached relation.

nodes.name: Filter
nodes.summary: Selection plan (DataFrame.filter / where). Emits filter.input and filter.condition from a Column and wraps subquery references through _with_relations.

nodes.name: Limit
nodes.summary: Plan for DataFrame.limit (Relation.limit). Same shape as Tail (847-857, Relation.tail) and Offset (860-870, Relation.offset). Sample (946-972, Relation.sample with bounds, replacement, seed and deterministic_order) is another simple unary node in this group.

nodes.name: Deduplicate
nodes.summary: Plan for dropDuplicates / dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark; sets deduplicate with all_columns_as_keys, column_names and within_watermark.

nodes.name: Sort
nodes.summary: Plan for orderBy / sort / sortWithinPartitions. Converts each Column to a sort_order and sets sort.is_global.

nodes.name: Aggregate
nodes.summary: Plan behind groupBy().agg, rollup, cube, pivot and groupingSets. __init__ asserts that the group_type is one of groupby, rollup, cube, pivot or grouping_sets and checks which pivot or grouping_sets arguments are legal. plan() fills Relation.aggregate with grouping and aggregate expressions and maps the group type to proto.Aggregate.GroupType (pivot adds pivot.col and literal values; grouping_sets adds GroupingSets).

nodes.name: Join
nodes.summary: Plan for DataFrame.join. __init__ translates the textual how value (inner, outer/full, left, right, semi, anti, cross and aliases) into a proto.Join.JoinType, raising AnalysisException UNSUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPE otherwise. plan() sets join.left/right plus either using_columns (string keys) or join_condition (Columns combined with &). The observations property also merges observations from the right side.

nodes.name: AsOfJoin
nodes.summary: Plan for DataFrame.asOfJoin. Emits Relation.as_of_join with left_as_of / right_as_of columns, optional using_columns or join_expr, join type, tolerance, allow_exact_matches and direction.

nodes.name: LateralJoin
nodes.summary: Plan for DataFrame.lateralJoin. Accepts only inner, left (outer) and cross join types and emits Relation.lateral_join with an optional join_condition.

nodes.name: NearestByJoin
nodes.summary: Plan for the nearest-by join. Client-side validation mirrors the Scala validator (num_results range 1..100000, join type inner or left outer, mode approx or exact, direction distance or similarity) before emitting Relation.nearest_by_join with the ranking expression.

nodes.name: SetOperation
nodes.summary: Plan for union, unionByName, intersect and except style operations. Maps the set_op string (union, intersect, except; anything else raises PySparkValueError) to proto.SetOperation set_op_type and sets is_all, by_name and allow_missing_columns on Relation.set_op.

nodes.name: Repartition
nodes.summary: Plan for repartition(n) and coalesce (Relation.repartition with num_partitions and shuffle). RepartitionByExpression (1542-1566) is the expression-based variant emitting repartition_by_expression.

nodes.name: SubqueryAlias
nodes.summary: Plan for DataFrame.alias; sets subquery_alias.alias over the child. Also used as the named views argument of SQL.

nodes.name: WithRelations
nodes.summary: Plan that wraps a root relation together with referenced relations (subquery DataFrames), emitting Relation.with_relations with root and references.

nodes.name: SQL
nodes.summary: Plan for spark.sql(query, args). Takes positional or named Column arguments and optional named SubqueryAlias views passed as references. plan() sets sql.query, pos_arguments and named_arguments; command() wraps the same relation into Command.sql_command so that eagerly executed SQL can run as a command.

nodes.name: Range
nodes.summary: Leaf plan for spark.range; sets range.start, end, step and optional num_partitions.

nodes.name: Unpivot
nodes.summary: Plan for DataFrame.unpivot / melt; sets unpivot.ids, optional values, variable_column_name and value_column_name. Transpose (1734-1752) is a similar plan emitting Relation.transpose with index columns.

nodes.name: CollectMetrics
nodes.summary: Plan behind DataFrame.observe. plan() sets collect_metrics with a name (string or Observation name) and metric expressions; the observations property registers the Observation so results can be looked up later.

nodes.name: NAFill
nodes.summary: Plan for DataFrame.na.fill; validates scalar values and converts each to an Expression.Literal in fill_na.values. NADrop (1848-1868) emits drop_na with cols and min_non_nulls and is the na.drop counterpart.

nodes.name: NAReplace
nodes.summary: Plan for DataFrame.na.replace; turns (old, new) Column pairs into literal NAReplace.Replacement entries. The DataFrameStatFunctions plans StatSummary, StatDescribe, StatCov, StatApproxQuantile, StatCrosstab, StatFreqItems, StatSampleBy and StatCorr (lines 1902-2057) follow the same pattern and fill summary, describe, cov, approx_quantile, crosstab, freq_items, sample_by and corr.

nodes.name: CreateView
nodes.summary: Command plan for temp view creation; command() builds Command.create_dataframe_view with name, is_global, replace and the child relation.

nodes.name: WriteOperation
nodes.summary: Command plan behind DataFrameWriter save / saveAsTable / insertInto. Mutable fields (source, path, table_name, table_save_method, mode, sort/partitioning/clustering/bucket columns, options, schema evolution) are filled by the writer, and command() converts them into Command.write_operation, mapping the mode string to SaveMode and the table save method to TableSaveMethod.

nodes.name: WriteOperationV2
nodes.summary: Command plan for DataFrameWriterV2. command() builds Command.write_operation_v2 with table name, provider, partitioning expressions, clustering columns, table properties, options and a mode (create, overwrite, overwrite_partitions, append, replace, create_or_replace).

nodes.name: WriteStreamOperation
nodes.summary: Command plan for starting a streaming write. Holds a proto.WriteStreamOperationStart that the stream writer mutates; command() attaches the child relation and returns Command.write_stream_operation_start.

nodes.name: RemoveRemoteCachedRelation
nodes.summary: Command plan that releases a server-side cached relation, built as Command.remove_cached_remote_relation_command from a CachedRemoteRelation id.

nodes.name: Checkpoint
nodes.summary: Command plan for DataFrame.checkpoint / localCheckpoint; command() builds Command.checkpoint_command with relation, local, eager and an optional storage level.

nodes.name: MapPartitions
nodes.summary: Plan for mapInPandas and mapInArrow. Builds a common inline Python UDF from the function and column names and emits Relation.map_partitions with the UDF, is_barrier and optional resource profile id.

nodes.name: GroupMap
nodes.summary: Plan for groupby().applyInPandas / apply. Emits Relation.group_map with grouping expressions and the inline Python UDF.

nodes.name: CoGroupMap
nodes.summary: Plan for cogroup().applyInPandas. Emits Relation.co_group_map with both child relations, their grouping expressions and the inline Python UDF.

nodes.name: ApplyInPandasWithState
nodes.summary: Plan for applyInPandasWithState (arbitrary stateful streaming). Emits Relation.apply_in_pandas_with_state with grouping expressions, UDF, output and state schema strings, output mode and timeout configuration.

nodes.name: BaseTransformWithStateInPySpark
nodes.summary: Shared implementation of transformWithState for PySpark and Pandas. Emits Relation.group_map with output mode, optional initial state input and grouping expressions, and a TransformWithStateInfo (time mode, event time column, output schema). TransformWithStateInPySpark and TransformWithStateInPandas (lines 3004-3014, empty subclasses kept for backward compatibility) extend it.

nodes.name: PythonUDTF
nodes.summary: Plain helper (no LogicalPlan base) holding a Python UDTF class, return type, eval type and Python version. to_plan() builds proto.PythonUDTF and pickles the function with CloudPickleSerializer, raising PySparkPicklingError (UDTF_SERIALIZATION_ERROR) when it cannot be serialized.

nodes.name: CommonInlineUserDefinedTableFunction
nodes.summary: Plan for a Python user-defined table function with its body inlined. plan() sets common_inline_user_defined_table_function; udtf_plan() returns the bare proto message instead of a Relation.

nodes.name: CommonInlineUserDefinedDataSource
nodes.summary: Plan that registers a user-defined Python data source by name. plan() fills common_inline_user_defined_data_source; to_data_source_proto() returns the bare proto message. The helper PythonDataSource (lines 3117-3128, not a LogicalPlan) pickles the data source class with CloudPickleSerializer.

nodes.name: CachedRelation
nodes.summary: Leaf plan that wraps an already built proto.Relation and returns it unchanged from plan(); its constructor re-stamps common.plan_id from the plan counter.

nodes.name: LogicalPlan.plan
nodes.summary: Abstract hook (body is "...") that every concrete plan overrides to return a proto.Relation for the given SparkConnectClient.

nodes.name: LogicalPlan.command
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that command-style plans (writes, create view, checkpoint, SQL) override to return a proto.Command instead of a Relation.

nodes.name: LogicalPlan.to_proto
nodes.summary: Entry point that produces the Plan message: calls self.plan(session) and lets the client place the relation in a proto.Plan via _set_relation_in_plan; optionally prints the plan when debug is set.

nodes.name: LogicalPlan._with_relations
nodes.summary: When subquery references exist, wraps the root relation into a with_relations message (root plus the referenced plans) using the extra plan id; otherwise returns the root unchanged.

nodes.name: LogicalPlan._collect_references
nodes.summary: Static helper that walks Column or Expression trees and collects the plans of SubqueryExpression nodes so that operators can attach them as references.

nodes.name: LogicalPlan._parameters_to_print
nodes.summary: Inspects the subclass __init__ signature and gathers printable attributes (skipping LogicalPlan-typed parameters, forward references and Optional wrappers) for print() and _repr_html_().

nodes.name: LogicalPlan.print
nodes.summary: Returns an indented text tree of the plan: class name, printable parameters from the constructor signature, then the child printed one indent deeper.

nodes.name: Read.plan
nodes.summary: Fills Relation.read.named_table with the unparsed identifier, the options map and the optional is_streaming flag.

nodes.name: SQL.plan
nodes.summary: Builds Relation.sql with the query text, positional arguments and named arguments converted to expressions, then applies _with_relations for views.

nodes.name: Join.plan
nodes.summary: Builds Relation.join from both child plans. A string or list of strings becomes using_columns, Column conditions become join_condition (lists are combined with &), and the join type enum computed in __init__ is set before wrapping with _with_relations.

nodes.name: Aggregate.plan
nodes.summary: Builds Relation.aggregate from the child, grouping and aggregate expressions and sets the GroupType enum, adding pivot or grouping-set payloads for those group types.

nodes.name: WriteOperation.command
nodes.summary: Converts the writer state into Command.write_operation: input relation, source, sort/partition/cluster columns, bucketing, options, table or path target and SaveMode, raising PySparkValueError for unknown modes.

nodes.name: CachedRemoteRelation.__del__
nodes.summary: Finalizer that, if the session client is still open, sends an ExecutePlan request carrying RemoveRemoteCachedRelation(self).command() through a unary_unary channel with retries, logging a warning on failure.

nodes.name: dataframe.py
nodes.summary: Spark Connect Python client DataFrame. Every transformation only wraps self._plan in a new plan.* LogicalPlan node and returns a new DataFrame, so nothing runs on the server until an action (collect, count, show, toPandas, toArrow, ...) serializes the plan with to_proto and sends it through self._session.client over gRPC, receiving Arrow batches back. Also defines the DataFrameNaFunctions and DataFrameStatFunctions facades.
nodes.languageNotes: Subclasses the classic pyspark.sql.dataframe.DataFrame (ParentDataFrame) for API and docstring parity, but __new__ uses object.__new__ so the Connect class is created instead of the classic one. Most methods are annotated to return ParentDataFrame while actually returning the Connect DataFrame.

nodes.name: DataFrame
nodes.summary: Connect implementation of the PySpark DataFrame API. It holds a lazy LogicalPlan (_plan), the owning SparkSession (_session), and optional caches (_cached_schema, _cached_schema_serialized, _execution_info). Transformation methods build a new DataFrame around a plan.* node; actions convert the plan to protobuf and run it via self._session.client.

nodes.name: DataFrameNaFunctions
nodes.summary: Facade returned by DataFrame.na. fill, drop and replace simply delegate to DataFrame.fillna, dropna and replace.

nodes.name: DataFrameStatFunctions
nodes.summary: Facade returned by DataFrame.stat. cov, corr, approxQuantile, crosstab, freqItems and sampleBy delegate to the same-named DataFrame methods.

nodes.name: _test
nodes.summary: Doctest entry point that runs the parent pyspark.sql.dataframe doctests against a Spark Connect session (remote local[4] by default), skipping docs that need missing pandas or pyarrow.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Stores the LogicalPlan and SparkSession (raising MISSING_VALID_PLAN or NO_ACTIVE_SESSION when absent) and initializes the schema cache, serialized schema cache and execution info to empty. No RPC is made.

nodes.name: __repr__
nodes.summary: Reads the spark.sql.repl.eagerEval.* configs through session._client.get_configs; if eager evaluation is on it returns _show_string output, otherwise a 'DataFrame[col: type, ...]' string built from dtypes (which may trigger a schema RPC).

nodes.name: _repr_html_
nodes.summary: Notebook HTML rendering: when eager eval is enabled it wraps the plan in plan.HtmlString, executes it with _to_table and returns the single string cell; otherwise returns None.

nodes.name: _to_cols
nodes.summary: Normalizes mixed column arguments (Column, str, 1-based ordinal int, or a single sequence) into a list of Column objects, optionally forcing ascending sort order. Shared by select, groupBy, repartition and similar methods.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Property returning a DataFrameWriter built from the current plan and session, with a callback that records the ExecutionInfo of the write on this DataFrame.

nodes.name: select
nodes.summary: Projects columns: returns a new DataFrame wrapping plan.Project(self._plan, self._to_cols(*cols)). Lazy, no server call.

nodes.name: selectExpr
nodes.summary: Parses each SQL expression string with F.expr and wraps the plan in plan.Project; accepts varargs or a single list.

nodes.name: agg
nodes.summary: Aggregates the whole DataFrame. Dict arguments are turned into function-invocation columns, then delegates to self.groupBy().agg(...); raises CANNOT_BE_EMPTY when no expressions are given.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Action: builds agg(count(1)) and executes it through _to_table, returning the single cell as a Python int. Triggers a server round trip.

nodes.name: _check_same_session
nodes.summary: Validates that another DataFrame is a Connect DataFrame with the same session_id, raising SessionNotSameException otherwise. Called by join, union and the other binary operations.

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Validates numPartitions > 0 and returns a DataFrame over plan.Repartition(shuffle=False); propagates the cached schema.

nodes.name: repartition
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame over plan.Repartition (shuffle=True) when only a partition count is given, or plan.RepartitionByExpression when columns are provided; validates argument types and propagates the cached schema.

nodes.name: dropDuplicates
nodes.summary: Wraps the plan in plan.Deduplicate, using all columns as keys or only the given subset names after type validation; propagates the cached schema. drop_duplicates is an alias.

nodes.name: distinct
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame over plan.Deduplicate with all_columns_as_keys=True and the same cached schema.

nodes.name: drop
nodes.summary: Validates that arguments are str or Column and wraps the plan in plan.Drop; names and Columns are intentionally kept distinct because they behave differently.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Converts a SQL string with F.expr (or uses the Column directly) and returns a new DataFrame over plan.Filter(child=self._plan, filter=expr), reusing the cached schema. Lazy: no RPC until an action runs.

nodes.name: groupBy
nodes.summary: Returns a GroupedData (group_type 'groupby') holding this DataFrame and the grouping columns converted by _to_cols with ordinals allowed. rollup, cube and groupingSets follow the same pattern.

nodes.name: head
nodes.summary: With no argument returns the first Row or None by calling head(1); with n it delegates to take(n).

nodes.name: take
nodes.summary: Action: self.limit(num).collect().

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: Checks both DataFrames share a session, normalizes the join type string, and returns a DataFrame over plan.Join(left=self._plan, right=other._plan, on, how).

nodes.name: limit
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame over plan.Limit(child=self._plan, limit=num), preserving the cached schema.

nodes.name: tail
nodes.summary: Action: wraps the plan in plan.Tail and immediately calls collect on the new DataFrame.

nodes.name: sort
nodes.summary: Builds sort columns via _preapare_cols_for_sort and F._sort_col and returns a DataFrame over plan.Sort(is_global=True). orderBy is an alias; sortWithinPartitions is the is_global=False variant.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Resolves the (withReplacement, fraction, seed) overloads and returns a DataFrame over plan.Sample with lower_bound 0.0.

nodes.name: withColumnsRenamed
nodes.summary: Validates a dict and wraps the plan in plan.WithColumnsRenamed; withColumnRenamed delegates here.

nodes.name: _show_string
nodes.summary: Validates n, vertical and truncate, wraps the plan in plan.ShowString, executes it with _to_table and returns the single formatted string produced by the server.

nodes.name: withColumns
nodes.summary: Validates a {name: Column} dict and returns a DataFrame over plan.WithColumns(columnNames, columns).

nodes.name: withColumn
nodes.summary: Validates that col is a Column and returns a DataFrame over plan.WithColumns with a single name and column.

nodes.name: observe
nodes.summary: Attaches named metrics: with an Observation it calls observation._on(self, *exprs), with a string it wraps the plan in plan.CollectMetrics. Requires at least one Column expression.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Action: prints the string returned by _show_string(n, truncate, vertical).

nodes.name: _merge_cached_schema
nodes.summary: Returns self.schema only when both DataFrames have exactly equal cached schemas, to avoid type-coercion mismatches; otherwise None. Used by set operations.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Checks the session then delegates to unionAll.

nodes.name: unionAll
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame over plan.SetOperation(..., 'union', is_all=True) and merges the cached schemas when they match.

nodes.name: where
nodes.summary: Validates that the condition is a str or Column, then delegates to filter.

nodes.name: fillna
nodes.summary: Validates value and subset types, then returns a DataFrame over plan.NAFill(cols, values); a dict value supplies both the columns and the values.

nodes.name: dropna
nodes.summary: Maps how/thresh to min_non_nulls and returns a DataFrame over plan.NADrop; thresh overrides how.

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Validates to_replace, value and subset, builds literal replacement pairs (ints converted to float) and returns a DataFrame over plan.NAReplace; rejects mixed-type replacements.

nodes.name: __getattr__
nodes.summary: Resolves df.colname to a column via _col; JVM-only attributes (_jdf, rdd, etc.) raise JVM_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_SUPPORTED, and names starting with '__' or the PYSPARK_VALIDATE_COLUMN_NAME_LEGACY setting trigger eager validation against self.columns.

nodes.name: __getitem__
nodes.summary: df['name'] returns a column reference (or UnresolvedStar for '*'), df[Column] returns filter(Column), df[list] returns select(*list), and df[int] returns F.col of that column name.

nodes.name: _col
nodes.summary: Builds a ConnectColumn around a ColumnReference that carries the name and this plan's _plan_id, so the server can resolve the column against this DataFrame.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Action: runs _to_table, takes the server schema or derives one with from_arrow_schema, and converts the Arrow table to a list of Row via ArrowTableToRowsConversion.convert, honoring spark.sql.execution.pyspark.binaryAsBytes.

nodes.name: _to_table
nodes.summary: Core execution helper: query = self._plan.to_proto(client); then calls client.to_table(query, plan.observations), which sends the plan over gRPC and returns an Arrow table plus schema and ExecutionInfo (stored on self._execution_info).

nodes.name: toArrow
nodes.summary: Action: converts self.schema to an Arrow schema (UTC, duplicate struct field names rejected), runs _to_table and casts the table to that schema.

nodes.name: toPandas
nodes.summary: Action: delegates to _to_pandas.

nodes.name: _to_pandas
nodes.summary: Calls client.to_pandas(plan_proto, plan.observations, **kwargs) and records the returned ExecutionInfo.

nodes.name: _schema
nodes.summary: Lazily resolves the schema: if _cached_schema is None it sends the plan to client.schema (an analyze RPC) and caches the result plus a pickled copy; the source comment notes that caching can be stale if the plan inputs change.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the cached schema (unpickled from the serialized bytes, with a deepcopy fallback) so callers cannot mutate the cache.

nodes.name: isStreaming
nodes.summary: Cached property that calls client._analyze(method='is_streaming') on the plan proto.

nodes.name: printSchema
nodes.summary: Prints self.schema.treeString(level).

nodes.name: _explain_string
nodes.summary: Maps the explain(extended, mode) argument combinations to a mode (simple, extended, etc.) and calls client.explain_string(plan_proto, mode).

nodes.name: explain
nodes.summary: Prints the string from _explain_string.

nodes.name: createTempView
nodes.summary: Builds plan.CreateView(is_global=False, replace=False).command(client) and runs it with client.execute_command, storing the ExecutionInfo. createOrReplaceTempView and the global variants differ only in flags.

nodes.name: createOrReplaceTempView
nodes.summary: Same as createTempView but with replace=True: plan.CreateView command executed via client.execute_command.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Gets the relation with self._plan.plan(client) and calls client._analyze(method='persist', storage_level=...); returns self. cache() delegates here; storageLevel and unpersist use the same _analyze path.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Sends client._analyze(method='unpersist', blocking=...) for this plan's relation and returns self.

nodes.name: toLocalIterator
nodes.summary: Generator: streams Arrow tables from client.to_table_as_iterator and yields Rows batch by batch, taking the schema from the first message or the first table.

nodes.name: _map_partitions
nodes.summary: Validates the vectorized UDF, parses a DDL schema through session._parse_ddl, wraps the function in a UserDefinedFunction and returns a DataFrame over plan.MapPartitions; mapInPandas and mapInArrow call it with different eval types.

nodes.name: foreach
nodes.summary: Action: selects the row as a struct, applies a UDF that calls f for each row, and triggers execution with collect.

nodes.name: foreachPartition
nodes.summary: Action: builds per-field Arrow converters, wraps f in a mapInArrow function that yields Row iterators, then forces execution with collect.

nodes.name: sameSemantics
nodes.summary: Checks the other DataFrame type and session, then asks client.same_semantics with both plan protos.

nodes.name: semanticHash
nodes.summary: Cached call to client.semantic_hash(plan=self._plan.to_proto(client)).

nodes.name: writeTo
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrameWriterV2 for the given table, sharing the plan, session and an ExecutionInfo callback.

nodes.name: checkpoint
nodes.summary: Runs plan.Checkpoint (local=False) as a command via client.execute_command and returns the DataFrame the server reports in checkpoint_command_result, whose plan is a CachedRemoteRelation.

nodes.name: isEmpty
nodes.summary: Returns True when select().take(1) yields no rows (cached with functools.cache); triggers a collect.

nodes.name: SparkConnectService.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Spark Connect gRPC server entry point. Class SparkConnectService implements the generated SparkConnectServiceGrpc AsyncService, delegating each RPC (executePlan, analyzePlan, config, addArtifacts, interrupt, reattachExecute, releaseExecute, ...) to a per-RPC handler, while its companion object builds and starts the Netty gRPC server and owns the global session manager, execution manager and streaming query cache.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class plus companion object sharing one class id; the generated gRPC base trait (SparkConnectServiceGrpc.AsyncService) lives in compiled proto code and has no node in this graph.

nodes.name: SparkConnectService
nodes.summary: gRPC service implementation that extends the generated AsyncService and BindableService. Every RPC wraps its handler call in try/catch and routes failures through ErrorUtils.handleError; bindService rewraps all method marshallers with a configurable protobuf recursion limit. The companion object (same id) starts and stops the server.

nodes.name: executePlan
nodes.summary: Main entry for running a plan: creates a SparkConnectExecutePlanHandler with the response observer and calls handle(request), catching generic errors via ErrorUtils.handleError.

nodes.name: analyzePlan
nodes.summary: Handles AnalyzePlan RPCs (explain string, schema, etc.) by delegating to SparkConnectAnalyzeHandler with the same error handling pattern.

nodes.name: config
nodes.summary: Handles Config RPCs that get or update session configuration by delegating to SparkConnectConfigHandler.

nodes.name: addArtifacts
nodes.summary: Client-streaming RPC for uploading artifacts (jars, files, classes); returns a SparkConnectAddArtifactsHandler as the request StreamObserver.

nodes.name: interrupt
nodes.summary: Handles Interrupt RPCs that cancel running executions by delegating to SparkConnectInterruptHandler.

nodes.name: reattachExecute
nodes.summary: Handles ReattachExecute RPCs so a client can resume the response stream of a reattachable ExecutePlan, delegating to SparkConnectReattachExecuteHandler.

nodes.name: releaseExecute
nodes.summary: Handles ReleaseExecute RPCs that release part of the buffered responses, or finish and release a whole reattachable execution, via SparkConnectReleaseExecuteHandler.

nodes.name: methodWithCustomMarshallers
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a gRPC MethodDescriptor so request and response marshallers use ProtoUtils.marshallerWithRecursionLimit with the configured recursion limit.

nodes.name: bindService
nodes.summary: Binds the generated service definition and re-adds every method with the custom marshallers, producing the ServerServiceDefinition registered with the Netty server.

nodes.name: getOrCreateIsolatedSession
nodes.summary: Looks up or creates the SessionHolder for a (userId, sessionId) pair by delegating to the global SparkConnectSessionManager.

nodes.name: createListenerAndUI
nodes.summary: Registers the SparkConnectServerListener on the status queue, optionally creates the Connect UI tab, and adds the ConnectProgressExecutionListener used for query progress reports.

nodes.name: startGRPCService
nodes.summary: Builds a NettyServerBuilder (bind address, port retries, max inbound message size), adds the SparkConnectService, auth token and configured interceptors, optional reflection service, then starts the server and records its binding address.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the Spark Connect service once: initializes the base session on the session manager, starts the gRPC server, creates the listener and UI, and posts a service-started event.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the service: shuts down the gRPC server (gracefully if a timeout is given), the streaming query cache, execution manager and session manager, detaches the UI tab, and posts a service-end event.

nodes.name: postServiceEvent
nodes.summary: Posts a Connect service started/end event to the Spark listener bus after checking that the server, binding address and listener bus are set.

nodes.name: SparkListenerConnectServiceStarted
nodes.summary: Listener event posted after the Spark Connect service has started, carrying host address, binding port and event time.

nodes.name: SparkListenerConnectServiceEnd
nodes.summary: Listener event posted when the Spark Connect service has shut down, carrying host address, binding port and event time.

nodes.name: ExecuteHolder.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the state of one running Spark Connect operation. ExecuteHolder owns the ExecuteThreadRunner that runs the plan, the ExecuteResponseObserver that buffers responses, and the attached ExecuteGrpcResponseSender instances; it supports reattach, release, interrupt and close, and reports ExecuteInfo and TerminationInfo.
nodes.languageNotes: Also defines ExecuteJobTag and ExecuteSessionTag helper objects (tag builders with unapply extractors) and the ExecuteInfo and TerminationInfo case classes.

nodes.name: ExecuteHolder
nodes.summary: Per-operation state for an ExecutePlanRequest: the execute key, request, owning SessionHolder, job tag, user session tags, reattachable and result-chunking flags, observations, the response observer, the runner thread and the attached gRPC senders. A companion object collects observation and plan ids from the plan.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the execution on a background thread via the ExecuteThreadRunner; responses are cached in the ExecuteResponseObserver for a gRPC thread to consume.

nodes.name: isOrphan
nodes.summary: Reports whether the execution ended without finalizing its outcome: runner thread dead, completion not delegated, and response observer not completed.

nodes.name: runGrpcResponseSender
nodes.summary: Attaches an ExecuteGrpcResponseSender and runs it either from the start of the stream or, for reattach, from the response after lastConsumedResponseId (resolved through the response observer).

nodes.name: addGrpcResponseSender
nodes.summary: Registers a new response sender, interrupting any previously attached sender so only one is active, or interrupts the new sender immediately if the execution is closing.

nodes.name: removeGrpcResponseSender
nodes.summary: Detaches a finished or interrupted sender and records the detach time when none remain attached.

nodes.name: afterInitialRPC
nodes.summary: Ends the grace period after the initial ExecutePlan RPC by stamping the last-detached time if no sender is attached.

nodes.name: releaseUntilResponseId
nodes.summary: Drops cached responses up to and including the given response id from the response observer (used by ReleaseExecute).

nodes.name: interrupt
nodes.summary: Interrupts the execution thread via the runner, which cancels running Spark jobs and yields an OPERATION_CANCELED error.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Interrupts the runner and any attached senders, clears the senders, calls cleanup if the runner was not interrupted, and records the close time.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: One-time cleanup guarded by an atomic flag: removes all cached responses, posts the closed event to the UI, and records the termination info in the SessionHolder.

nodes.name: getExecuteInfo
nodes.summary: Builds an ExecuteInfo snapshot of this operation (request, ids, tags, reattachable, status, termination reason, timings).

nodes.name: getTerminationInfo
nodes.summary: Builds the minimal TerminationInfo (ids, status, termination reason) stored for inactive operations.

nodes.name: collectAllObservationAndPlanIds
nodes.summary: Recursively walks a plan message and collects the plan id of every CollectMetrics relation keyed by observation name.

nodes.name: ExecuteJobTag
nodes.summary: Builds and recognizes the SparkContext job tag that identifies one operation by user, session and operation id.

nodes.name: ExecuteSessionTag
nodes.summary: Builds and recognizes the SparkContext job tag derived from a user-supplied session tag (validated), combined with user and session id.

nodes.name: ExecuteInfo
nodes.summary: Case class snapshot of an ExecuteHolder: request, ids, job tag, session tags, reattachable flag, status, termination reason and timestamps.

nodes.name: TerminationInfo
nodes.summary: Minimal status record kept for inactive (completed, interrupted or abandoned) operations.

nodes.name: SessionHolder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SessionHolder, the per-session state object of Spark Connect, keyed by SessionKey(userId, sessionId). It wraps the classic SparkSession and holds the plan cache, DataFrame cache, listener and pipeline caches, ML cache, artifact access, active and inactive operation tracking, interrupt entry points and session close logic.
nodes.languageNotes: Case class with many lazy vals and Guava caches; companion object only holds error cache constants.

nodes.name: SessionKey
nodes.summary: Case class identifying a Connect session by the combination of user id and session id.

nodes.name: SessionHolder
nodes.summary: Holds all server-side state for one Connect session: the SparkSession, plan cache of resolved logical plans, DataFrame cache by id, streaming listener cache, pipeline execution cache, ML cache, error cache, event manager, and the set of active operation ids plus a cache of inactive ones.

nodes.name: addOperationId
nodes.summary: Registers a new operation id for this session, rejecting it if the session is closing or the id already exists.

nodes.name: getOperationStatus
nodes.summary: Returns Some(true) for an active operation, Some(false) for a recently inactive one, or None if the id is unknown in this session.

nodes.name: closeOperation
nodes.summary: Stores the TerminationInfo of an ExecuteHolder in the inactive-operations cache and removes its id from the active set.

nodes.name: interruptAll
nodes.summary: Interrupts all running streaming queries and every active ExecuteHolder of the session, returning the interrupted operation ids.

nodes.name: interruptTag
nodes.summary: Interrupts streaming queries and ExecuteHolders carrying a given client session tag, returning the interrupted operation ids.

nodes.name: interruptOperation
nodes.summary: Interrupts the single ExecuteHolder with a given operation id and closes its operation record.

nodes.name: addArtifact
nodes.summary: Adds an uploaded artifact to the session by forwarding to the SparkSession artifact manager.

nodes.name: updateAccessTime
nodes.summary: Records the last access time of the session (called by the session manager) and logs it.

nodes.name: initializeSession
nodes.summary: Initializes the session by posting the started event; called only by SparkConnectSessionManager.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Expires the session: marks the close time, closes artifacts, stops streaming queries, listeners, pipelines, dataflow graphs and server-side listener, removes all executions of the session, closes the ML cache and posts the closed event.

nodes.name: withSession
nodes.summary: Runs a block with this session active and its artifact resources (jars, classes) available; used to run each execution in its session context.

nodes.name: getSessionHolderInfo
nodes.summary: Builds the SessionHolderInfo snapshot (ids, status, start, last access, custom timeout, close time) used for expiry and listing.

nodes.name: cacheDataFrameById
nodes.summary: Stores a DataFrame under a relation id in the dataFrameCache, failing if the id is already used; entries live until removed by their owner.

nodes.name: getDataFrameOrThrow
nodes.summary: Returns the cached DataFrame for an id or throws InvalidPlanInput (DATAFRAME_NOT_FOUND).

nodes.name: removeCachedListener
nodes.summary: Removes a StreamingQueryListener by id and stops its Python process if it is a PythonStreamingQueryListener.

nodes.name: cachePipelineExecution
nodes.summary: Caches the PipelineUpdateContext of a graph id, failing if one already exists for that graph.

nodes.name: usePlanCache
nodes.summary: Transforms a proto Relation into a LogicalPlan using the per-session plan cache when enabled and the relation has a plan id; caches the result when cachePlan is set or the relation is a data source read.

nodes.name: SessionHolderInfo
nodes.summary: Case class snapshot of a SessionHolder with ids, status, timeout and timestamps; exposes its SessionKey.

nodes.name: ExecuteThreadRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Runs a Connect operation on its own dedicated thread. ExecuteThreadRunner tags the Spark jobs, sets call sites, dispatches ROOT and COMMAND plans to SparkConnectPlanExecution, emits observed metrics, then completes the ExecuteResponseObserver (ResultComplete for reattachable runs); a small atomic state machine arbitrates interrupts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an AtomicReference-based state machine (ThreadState) with compare-and-exchange transitions instead of locks.

nodes.name: ExecuteThreadRunner
nodes.summary: Launches the plan execution in a background ExecutionThread that pushes responses into executeHolder.responseObserver. Owns an AtomicReference thread state (notStarted, started, interrupted, startedInterrupted, completed) so interrupts and completion cannot race.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the execution thread once if the runner has not started; returns immediately.

nodes.name: interrupt
nodes.summary: Atomically moves the state to interrupted or startedInterrupted; if never started, reports OPERATION_CANCELED to the observer and cleans up, otherwise interrupts the thread. Returns true only for the first interrupt.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Thread body wrapper: runs executeInternal, cancels remaining jobs with the job tag on failure, removes job tags, reports errors to the response observer, and finalizes the state, sending OPERATION_CANCELED if interrupted.

nodes.name: executeInternal
nodes.summary: Core of the operation: posts started, inside sessionHolder.withSession sets job tags and call-site properties, runs SparkConnectPlanExecution.handlePlan for ROOT or COMMAND plans, sends observed-metrics responses, and finishes the stream with onNextComplete or onCompleted.

nodes.name: shouldDelegateCompleteResponse
nodes.summary: Returns true for ADD_LISTENER_BUS_LISTENER commands, whose long-running listener thread sends the final ResultComplete itself.

nodes.name: requestString
nodes.summary: Builds an abbreviated, redacted string of the request for job descriptions and call sites, falling back to UNKNOWN on error.

nodes.name: ExecutionThread
nodes.summary: Private Thread subclass named with the connect execute prefix and operation id whose run() calls execute().

nodes.name: ThreadState
nodes.summary: Enumeration-like object defining the runner thread states notStarted, interrupted, started, startedInterrupted and completed and their allowed transitions.

nodes.name: ThreadStateInfo
nodes.summary: Case class wrapping the integer value of an execution thread state.

nodes.name: ExecuteResponseObserver.scala
nodes.summary: Server-side buffer between the execution thread and the gRPC senders. ExecuteResponseObserver is a StreamObserver that numbers and caches each ExecutePlanResponse, tracks consumed and released indexes, and evicts old responses subject to a retry buffer, which is what makes ReattachExecute possible.
nodes.languageNotes: Producer/consumer coordination via a shared responseLock monitor with wait/notifyAll; extends gRPC StreamObserver.

nodes.name: ExecuteResponseObserver
nodes.summary: StreamObserver running on the execution thread that caches responses by consecutive index (starting at 1) with response-id mappings, error and final-index state, and size statistics; consumers wait on responseLock for new responses.

nodes.name: tryOnNext
nodes.summary: Adds a response if the stream is not finished: assigns the next index, stamps common fields (session ids, operation id, random response id), caches it and wakes consumers.

nodes.name: onNext
nodes.summary: Publishes a response, throwing an illegal-state error if the stream is already completed.

nodes.name: onNextComplete
nodes.summary: Atomically publishes the last response and marks the stream completed.

nodes.name: onError
nodes.summary: Records the error, fixes the final index and wakes consumers; no further responses are accepted.

nodes.name: onCompleted
nodes.summary: Marks the stream finished at the last produced index and wakes waiting consumers.

nodes.name: consumeResponse
nodes.summary: Returns the cached response at an index and marks it consumed, then evicts earlier responses per the retry-buffer policy; throws INVALID_CURSOR.POSITION_NOT_AVAILABLE if a needed response was already evicted.

nodes.name: getResponseIndexById
nodes.summary: Maps a response id to its stream index, throwing INVALID_CURSOR.POSITION_NOT_FOUND for unknown ids; used to resume after a reattach.

nodes.name: removeResponsesUntilId
nodes.summary: Releases cached responses up to and including the response with the given id (ReleaseExecute path).

nodes.name: removeAll
nodes.summary: Removes every cached response and logs total, auto-removed and peak cache statistics for the operation.

nodes.name: removeCachedResponses
nodes.summary: Eviction policy after a response is consumed: with no retry buffer, drop everything consumed; otherwise keep the most recent responses up to retryBufferSize bytes.

nodes.name: removeResponsesUntilIndex
nodes.summary: Walks backwards from an index removing cached responses and updating size statistics, and records the released-until index.

nodes.name: setCommonResponseFields
nodes.summary: Fills session id, server-side session id, operation id and a fresh response id on every ExecutePlanResponse.

nodes.name: CachedSize
nodes.summary: Private helper case class tracking current and peak byte size and count of cached responses.

nodes.name: ExecuteGrpcResponseSender.scala
nodes.summary: Streams buffered responses to the client. ExecuteGrpcResponseSender consumes from the ExecuteResponseObserver and writes to the gRPC observer of an ExecutePlan or ReattachExecute call, with backpressure and size/duration limits for reattachable runs, progress messages, and interruption when another sender attaches.
nodes.languageNotes: Reattachable runs use a dedicated sender thread plus ServerCallStreamObserver.isReady and an on-ready handler for flow control.

nodes.name: ExecuteGrpcResponseSender
nodes.summary: Consumer of an execution response stream. For reattachable executions it runs on its own thread and respects gRPC readiness and deadline/size limits; non-reattachable ones run directly in the gRPC thread and remove the ExecuteHolder when done.

nodes.name: interrupt
nodes.summary: Marks the sender interrupted and wakes it from any wait so it exits.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Starts sending from a given stream index: reattachable executions spawn a sender thread and register an on-ready handler, while non-reattachable ones execute inline and then remove the execute holder.

nodes.name: enqueueProgressMessage
nodes.summary: Queues an ExecutionProgress response into the response observer from the progress tracker when the progress interval is enabled and there is something new.

nodes.name: updateDeadlineTimeNs
nodes.summary: Computes the sender deadline from the reattachable max-stream-duration setting, or a 180 day default.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Main loop: waits for responses from the observer, sends each, and ends by calling onCompleted/onError when the stream is finished, throwing INVALID_CURSOR.DISCONNECTED if interrupted, or ending early at the deadline or size limit so the client can reattach.

nodes.name: sendResponse
nodes.summary: Sends one response; non-reattachable runs write directly, reattachable ones wait until the gRPC call observer is ready or the deadline passes to apply backpressure.

nodes.name: wakeUp
nodes.summary: Wakes threads sleeping on the observer response lock or the gRPC ready signal.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanExecution.scala
nodes.summary: Runs ExecutePlanRequest plans of ROOT (relation) and COMMAND type. SparkConnectPlanExecution uses SparkConnectPlanner to build a logical plan, wraps it in a Dataset, sends the schema, then collects results as Arrow batches (optionally chunked) into the response observer, followed by metrics; commands are executed through QueryExecution or the planner.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion object holds observed-metrics helpers; the class is private[execution].

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanExecution
nodes.summary: Per-operation executor for Plan messages. Constructed with an ExecuteHolder; handlePlan dispatches on ROOT versus COMMAND, and processAsArrowBatches turns query results into ExecutePlanResponse Arrow batches.

nodes.name: handlePlan
nodes.summary: For ROOT plans, builds a Dataset from planner.transformRelation (cachePlan = true), sends the schema and Arrow batches, then metrics; for COMMAND plans, runs a QueryExecution when the planner returns a transformer, otherwise delegates to planner.process. Also picks shuffle cleanup mode and blocks unsupported eager execution in pipeline flow functions.

nodes.name: rowToArrowConverter
nodes.summary: Returns a function that converts an iterator of InternalRow into (Arrow batch bytes, row count) pairs using ArrowConverters.toBatchWithSchemaIterator.

nodes.name: processAsArrowBatches
nodes.summary: Executes a DataFrame and streams its rows as Arrow batches: local tables and limit/tail plans are collected directly; otherwise partitions are computed with submitJob and sent in order from the main thread, with optional result chunking, and an empty batch is sent if none were produced.

nodes.name: createSchemaResponse
nodes.summary: Builds the ExecutePlanResponse carrying the result schema as a Connect proto data type.

nodes.name: toObservedMetricsValues
nodes.summary: Converts an observation Row into (optional name, value, optional data type) tuples.

nodes.name: createObservedMetricsResponse
nodes.summary: Builds an ExecutePlanResponse with ObservedMetrics (literal values or error details per observation name and plan id).

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.scala
nodes.summary: Spark Connect server planner that converts protobuf Relation, Expression and Command trees sent by a client (for example PySpark Connect) into Catalyst LogicalPlans and Expressions on the server's SparkSession. It also executes commands (writes, SQL commands, UDF registration, streaming, checkpoint) and builds the Python and Scala UDF objects from the serialized payloads.
nodes.languageNotes: One large Scala class whose methods are mostly pattern matches on protobuf oneof cases; nested private case classes and objects (UntypedKeyValueGroupedDataset, TypedScalaUdf) support the typed Dataset API.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner
nodes.summary: Planner for one Spark Connect session (and optionally one ExecuteHolder). transformRelation and transformExpression convert protobuf trees to Catalyst plans and expressions, while process executes proto.Command messages, using sessionHolder's SparkSession for Dataset, catalog, UDF and streaming operations. There is no companion object in this file.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformRelation
nodes.summary: Entry point that turns a proto.Relation into a Catalyst LogicalPlan (largely made of Unresolved* nodes that the analyzer resolves later): wraps the work in sessionHolder.usePlanCache, switches on rel.getRelTypeCase to dispatch to one transform method per relation type (project, filter, join, aggregate, sql, read, local relation, Python map and group-map UDFs, catalog, ML relation, extensions), and tags the result with the relation's plan id (LogicalPlan.PLAN_ID_TAG). When running inside an ExecuteHolder it also registers Observation objects for CollectMetrics nodes found in the plan.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformCatalog
nodes.summary: Dispatches the internal-only proto.Catalog message (catalog.getCatTypeCase) to the matching transformXxx helper defined later in the class (list databases/tables/functions/columns, get/exists checks, create/drop table and view, cache/uncache, refresh, set current database or catalog, analyze and truncate table). Each helper calls session.catalog and returns either a Dataset's logicalPlan or an empty one-column LocalRelation for commands without a result.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformSql
nodes.summary: Turns proto.SQL into a LogicalPlan by parsing the query text only (no execution): when buildParameterContext yields a context it calls parser.parsePlanWithParameters, otherwise parser.parsePlan.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.buildParameterContext
nodes.summary: Builds an optional ParameterContext from the SQL message with a fixed priority: named argument expressions, positional argument expressions, named literals, then positional literals. Expression-valued arguments are transformed and checked through session.resolveAndValidateParameters (positional ones keyed as _pos_N); literal arguments go through transformLiteral. Returns None when there are no parameters.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformSample
nodes.summary: Builds a Sample logical plan. When getDeterministicOrder is set it wraps the input in a Dataset and either sorts each partition by all orderable output attributes (Sort with global = false) or, if none are orderable, caches the Dataset, so that repeated splits do not overlap; then applies Sample with lower and upper bounds, replacement flag and optional seed.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformNAFill
nodes.summary: Implements DataFrame.na.fill by validating the values list, creating a Dataset from the input relation and calling dataset.na.fillValue (single value, optionally restricted to columns) or na.fill with a column-to-value map, returning the resulting logicalPlan. The neighbouring transformNADrop, transformReplace and transformStat* methods follow the same Dataset-then-logicalPlan pattern, with some (approxQuantile) materializing a LocalRelation.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformMapPartitions
nodes.summary: Plans mapInPandas / mapInArrow and typed Scala mapPartitions. For a Scala UDF it analyzes the child and delegates to transformTypedMapPartitions; for a Python UDF it builds the PythonUDF, optional barrier flag and ResourceProfile, then creates logical.MapInPandas or logical.MapInArrow depending on pythonUdf.evalType (SQL_MAP_PANDAS_ITER_UDF or SQL_MAP_ARROW_ITER_UDF), and rejects other eval types.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformGroupMap
nodes.summary: Plans grouped-map style operators. A Scala UDF goes to transformTypedGroupMap. For a Python UDF it groups a Dataset by the grouping expressions and switches on evalType: grouped-map pandas -> flatMapGroupsInPandas, grouped-map arrow -> flatMapGroupsInArrow, transformWithState variants -> transformTransformWithStateInPySpark (pandas or row mode); other eval types are rejected.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformTypedGroupMap
nodes.summary: Scala/Java typed path for GroupMap. It unpacks the serialized UdfPacket, builds an UntypedKeyValueGroupedDataset and then, depending on the message, constructs a TransformWithState node (with or without initial state, optionally wrapped by UpdateEventTimeWatermarkColumn), a FlatMapGroupsWithState node (mapGroupsWithState / flatMapGroupsWithState), or a plain MapGroups, each topped with SerializeFromObject.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformCoGroupMap
nodes.summary: Plans cogroup operators. Scala UDFs go to transformTypedCoGroupMap. For a Python UDF it groups both inputs by their grouping columns, builds the PythonUDF bound to the combined output attributes through createUserDefinedPythonFunction(...).builder, and calls flatMapCoGroupsInPandas or flatMapCoGroupsInArrow according to evalType.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformTypedCoGroupMap
nodes.summary: Typed Scala cogroup: unpacks the UDF, builds an UntypedKeyValueGroupedDataset for each side and creates a CoGroup logical node (deserializers, grouping and data attributes, sort orders, output object attribute) wrapped in SerializeFromObject.

nodes.name: UntypedKeyValueGroupedDataset
nodes.summary: Private case class plus companion that is the planner's untyped stand-in for KeyValueGroupedDataset: it carries key and value encoders, the analyzed plan, analyzed data plan, grouping attributes and sort order. Companion apply methods transform the input relation and sort expressions and build it either from a groupByKey function (AppendColumns) or from a relational grouped dataset plus a dummy typed UDF, throwing if no grouping expression is present.

nodes.name: TypedScalaUdf
nodes.summary: Private case class plus companion wrapping a typed Scala function with its input and output AgnosticEncoders. It exposes the resolved ExpressionEncoders, the input deserializer, output named expressions and object attributes used by TypedFilter, MapPartitions, MapGroups and similar nodes. The companion's apply overloads unpack a UdfPacket (from a proto.Expression or CommonInlineUserDefinedFunction) and encoderFor resolves UnboundRowEncoder against the input attributes, recursing into product and row encoders.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformApplyInPandasWithState
nodes.summary: Plans applyInPandasWithState: builds the PythonUDF, parses the output and state schemas from DDL (with JSON fallback) and calls groupBy(...).applyInPandasWithState on a Dataset of the input, passing output mode and timeout configuration, then returns its logicalPlan.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformTransformWithStateInPySpark
nodes.summary: Builds the logical plan for Python transformWithState operators on a grouped Dataset. It reads the output schema from the TransformWithStateInfo, and with or without an initial-state input calls transformWithStateInPandas or transformWithStateInPySpark (row mode) depending on usePandas; when initial state is given the UDF is re-created over the grouped output attributes to avoid ambiguous column resolution.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformCommonInlineUserDefinedTableFunction
nodes.summary: Handles a Python UDTF used as a relation: creates a UserDefinedPythonTableFunction and calls its builder with the transformed argument expressions and the session SQL parser to produce the LogicalPlan. Non-Python table functions are rejected.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformWithColumns
nodes.summary: Implements withColumns: each alias must have exactly one name part and may carry JSON metadata. It first tries eager analysis through Dataset.withColumns; if that throws AnalysisException or SparkException it falls back to a Project over UnresolvedStarWithColumns so that analysis is deferred.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformDeduplicate
nodes.summary: Implements dropDuplicates. After validating the three input combinations it creates a QueryExecution of the input to get the analyzed output, resolves the requested column names with the session analyzer resolver (erroring on unknown names) and builds Deduplicate or, with getWithinWatermark, DeduplicateWithinWatermark.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformDataType
nodes.summary: Converts a proto.DataType to a Catalyst DataType: unparsed types are parsed from their DDL-style string via parseDatatypeString, all others go through DataTypeProtoConverter.toCatalystType.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.parseDatatypeString
nodes.summary: Parses a type string with a fallback chain: table schema DDL first, then a bare data type, then the text wrapped as struct<...>; if all fail the original ParseException is rethrown.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformLocalRelation
nodes.summary: Builds a LocalRelation for DataFrames created from client data. The optional schema is parsed (type string with JSON fallback); Arrow IPC bytes are decoded with ArrowConverters.fromIPCStream and turned into a plan by buildLocalRelationFromRows, or, with no data, an empty LocalRelation of the schema is returned (error if the schema is missing).

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.buildLocalRelationFromRows
nodes.summary: Materializes decoded Arrow rows into a LocalRelation using an UnsafeProjection and copying rows. If a user schema was supplied, the data schema is normalized (UDT to sqlType, struct fields renamed col_i) and a Dataset toDF/to(schema) projection is evaluated to coerce rows to the requested schema.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformReadRel
nodes.summary: Handles proto.Read. Named tables become an UnresolvedRelation (batch or streaming) with case-insensitive options. Batch data sources are loaded through session.read (format, options, schema, paths) including the JDBC-with-predicates special case; streaming sources use session.readStream with a single path. File or data source loads return queryExecution.analyzed of the reader result.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformParse
nodes.summary: Implements from_csv/json/xml style parsing of a single-string-column relation: validates that the input has one string column, converts it to a Dataset[String] and calls DataFrameReader csv/json/xml on it, returning queryExecution.analyzed.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformFilter
nodes.summary: Builds a Filter logical node. If the condition is a typed Scala UDF applied to a star (isTypedScalaUdfExpr) it builds a TypedFilter through transformTypedFilter, otherwise logical.Filter with the transformed condition expression.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformProject
nodes.summary: Builds a Project: with no input it uses OneRowRelation; when any expression is a typed aggregate it analyzes the child first so typed expressions can see its output. Each protobuf expression is converted (passing the base plan) and turned into a NamedExpression (non-named expressions are wrapped in UnresolvedAlias).

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformExpression
nodes.summary: Public @DeveloperApi entry point (two-argument overload with the optional base relation) that converts a proto.Expression to a Catalyst Expression, applying the client-provided Origin (Python call site or JVM stack trace) via CurrentOrigin.withOrigin before delegating to doTransformExpression. Plugins call it to transform nested expressions.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.doTransformExpression
nodes.summary: Central dispatcher for expressions: switches on exp.getExprTypeCase and calls the specific transformer for literals, unresolved attribute/function/star/regex, alias, expression string, cast, extract value, update fields, sort order, lambda, window, plugin extensions, inline UDFs, call_function, named arguments, merge actions, typed aggregates, subquery expressions and direct shuffle partition id.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformUnresolvedAttribute
nodes.summary: Creates an UnresolvedAttribute from the quoted identifier string and tags it with the DataFrame plan id (LogicalPlan.PLAN_ID_TAG) and the metadata-column flag so the analyzer can resolve df['col'] against the right DataFrame.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformLiteral
nodes.summary: Converts a proto literal into a Catalyst Literal by delegating to LiteralExpressionProtoConverter.toCatalystExpression.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformUnresolvedFunction
nodes.summary: Translates a scalar function call into UnresolvedFunction. User-defined functions use the parsed multipart name; built-ins use the plain name and an isInternal flag taken from the message, or, when absent, determined by checking FunctionRegistry.internal for backward compatibility with old clients.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformCommonInlineUserDefinedFunction
nodes.summary: Dispatches an inline user-defined function expression: Python UDFs go to transformPythonFuncExpression and Scala UDFs or aggregators go to transformScalaUDF; other function kinds are rejected.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.unpackScalaUDF
nodes.summary: Deserializes the Java-serialized payload of a ScalarScalaUDF with the context class loader (so session artifacts are visible) and converts NoSuchMethodException/ClassNotFoundException into a SparkClassNotFoundException that tells the user to install the artifact with session.addArtifact.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformScalaUDF
nodes.summary: Turns a Scala UDF or aggregator from the client into an expression: it transforms the arguments, builds the UserDefinedFunction with transformScalaFunction and then converts it to a ScalaUDF (UserDefinedFunctionUtils.toScalaUDF) or a ScalaAggregator aggregate expression, rejecting other implementations.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformScalaFunction
nodes.summary: Builds a UserDefinedFunction from an unpacked UdfPacket: a UserDefinedAggregator (exactly one input encoder required) when the message marks an aggregate, otherwise a SparkUserDefinedFunction with input and output encoders, return type, name, nullability and determinism. Also reused when registering Scala UDFs.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformPythonFuncExpression
nodes.summary: Creates the Catalyst expression for a Python UDF call: builds a UserDefinedPythonFunction from the message and calls its builder with the transformed arguments, converting a PythonUDAF result into an aggregate expression.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.createUserDefinedPythonFunction
nodes.summary: Creates the UserDefinedPythonFunction case class (name, SimplePythonFunction, return type, Python eval type, determinism) from a proto Python UDF. This is the helper shared by expression transformation, cogroup/grouped map transformations and UDF registration.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformPythonFunction
nodes.summary: Builds the SimplePythonFunction that carries a pickled Python command: command bytes, empty env vars and broadcasts, the python executable from PYSPARK_PYTHON/PYSPARK_DRIVER_PYTHON (default python3), the union of user-specified includes and the artifact manager's Python includes, the Python version and the session's Python accumulator. transformPythonTableFunction and transformPythonDataSource do the same for UDTFs and data sources.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformExpressionString
nodes.summary: Implements F.expr / selectExpr strings by parsing the SQL expression text with the session parser's parseExpression.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformUnresolvedStar
nodes.summary: Maps the three star forms to Catalyst: col('*') -> UnresolvedStar(None), 's.*' -> UnresolvedStar(Some(parts)) after checking the .* suffix, and df['*'] -> UnresolvedDataFrameStar(planId). Giving both a target and a plan id is an error.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformCast
nodes.summary: Translates a Cast expression: the target type comes from a DataType message or a type string, CHAR/VARCHAR are replaced by string, and the cast is created in LEGACY, ANSI, TRY or default EvalMode. The expression is tagged with Cast.USER_SPECIFIED_CAST.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformWindowExpression
nodes.summary: Builds a WindowExpression: converts the window function, partition and order specs and, when present, a row/range frame with CurrentRow, Unbounded or value boundaries into a SpecifiedWindowFrame (otherwise UnspecifiedFrame), validating that lower and upper bounds exist.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformSetOperation
nodes.summary: Builds union, intersect and except: requires both inputs, supports the ALL flag, rejects by-name for intersect/except, and for union creates Union (with byName and allowMissingColumns) wrapped in Distinct unless ALL.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformJoin
nodes.summary: Builds logical.Join: validates that both sides are present and that a join condition and using-columns are not both set, converts the optional condition, maps the proto join type to a Catalyst JoinType (UsingJoin when using columns are given) and uses JoinHint.NONE.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformSort
nodes.summary: Builds a Sort node (global or local) from the order list, requiring at least one order. Each sort item goes through transformSortOrder with ordinal replacement enabled.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformSortOrder
nodes.summary: Creates a SortOrder from a proto sort order: ascending or descending, nulls first or last, and the child expression, which can optionally be converted to an UnresolvedOrdinal for integer literals when orderByOrdinal is on.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformAggregate
nodes.summary: Chooses how to plan an Aggregate: group-by whose first grouping expression is a typed Scala UDF goes to transformKeyValueGroupedAggregate (groupByKey Datasets), everything else (including rollup, cube, pivot and grouping sets) to transformRelationalGroupedAggregate.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformKeyValueGroupedAggregate
nodes.summary: Plans aggregation over a KeyValueGroupedDataset: builds the untyped key-value Dataset, adds the key column via TypedAggUtils.aggKeyColumn and creates a logical.Aggregate over the analyzed grouped plan with typed aggregate expressions.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformRelationalGroupedAggregate
nodes.summary: Main aggregate planner: transforms grouping and aggregate expressions (replacing ordinals if enabled) and, depending on group type, creates a plain Aggregate, an Aggregate over Rollup or Cube, a Pivot (collecting pivot values when none are given) or an Aggregate over GroupingSets. The input is analyzed first if it contains typed aggregate expressions.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformTypedAggregateExpression
nodes.summary: Converts a typed (Dataset API) aggregator into a TypedAggregateExpression. It unpacks the UdfPacket, and when the base relation is known, resolves the input encoder against its output and applies TypedAggUtils.withInputType, then returns the aggregate expression.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformCommand
nodes.summary: Returns, for commands that can be turned into a plan (write operation, write operation V2, merge into table, create dataframe view), a function from QueryPlanningTracker to LogicalPlan; other commands return None and are handled by process.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.process
nodes.summary: Entry point for proto.Command execution. If transformCommand yields a plan builder it runs it through transformAndRunCommand (executing the command with QueryExecution); otherwise it dispatches on the command type to the handlers for UDF/UDTF/data source registration, plugin extensions, SQL commands, streaming (write start, query and query manager commands, listener bus), resources and profiles, checkpoint, removal of cached relations, ML and pipeline commands and external commands, writing responses to the StreamObserver.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleSqlCommand
nodes.summary: Handles spark.sql() as a command: builds the SQL relation (backward compatible with the raw SQL field), blocks unsupported commands in pipeline contexts, and executes via executeSQL or executeSQLWithRefs. If the result is a command or SQL script it serializes the rows to an Arrow batch inside a LocalRelation (sending metrics for commands); otherwise it returns the original relation unexecuted so the client can lazily build a DataFrame.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.executeSQLWithRefs
nodes.summary: Eagerly runs a SQL string whose references are subquery-aliased relations: under a lock on the planner it registers each referenced relation as a temp view, calls executeSQL and always drops the temp views in a finally block.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.executeSQL
nodes.summary: Executes SQL through session.sql with the QueryPlanningTracker, choosing the overload by argument kind: named expression arguments, positional expression arguments, named literals, positional literals, or no parameters.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleRegisterUserDefinedFunction
nodes.summary: Registers a UDF sent through RegisterFunction: Python UDFs go to handleRegisterPythonUDF, Java UDFs to registerJava / registerJavaUDAF and Scala UDFs through transformScalaFunction and session.udf.register. Posts the finished event afterwards.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleRegisterUserDefinedTableFunction
nodes.summary: Registers a Python UDTF by building a UserDefinedPythonTableFunction and calling session.udtf.registerPython; other table function kinds are rejected.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.createPythonUserDefinedTableFunction
nodes.summary: Creates a UserDefinedPythonTableFunction from the proto UDTF: optional struct return type (non-struct types rejected), the SimplePythonFunction built from the pickled command, eval type and determinism.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleRegisterPythonUDF
nodes.summary: Builds a UserDefinedPythonFunction with createUserDefinedPythonFunction and registers it in the session UDF registry with session.udf.registerPython under the requested name (used by spark.udf.register in PySpark).

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformCreateViewCommand
nodes.summary: Builds a CreateViewCommand (local or global temp view, replace flag) for createOrReplaceTempView style commands, parsing the view name and transforming the input relation as the view's plan.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformWriteOperation
nodes.summary: Implements df.write in Connect. It transforms the input relation, wraps it in a Dataset, then configures a DataFrameWriter (mode, options, sortBy, bucketBy, partitionBy, clusterBy, format, schema evolution) and returns the logical command for save (path or none), saveAsTable or insertInto.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformAndRunCommand
nodes.summary: Runs a command plan: creates a QueryPlanningTracker, builds a QueryExecution from the transformed plan, asserts the command was executed and posts the finished event.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformWriteOperationV2
nodes.summary: Implements df.writeTo (DataFrameWriterV2): transforms the input, wraps it in a Dataset, applies options, table properties, partitioning, clustering and schema evolution, then calls create, overwrite, overwritePartitions, append, replace or createOrReplace according to the mode.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleWriteStreamOperationStart
nodes.summary: Starts a Structured Streaming query: builds a DataStreamWriter from the transformed relation (format, options, partitioning, trigger kinds, output mode, query name, foreach writer, Python or Scala foreachBatch), starts it to a table, path or default sink, registers the query with SparkConnectService.streamingSessionManager and returns the query id, run id and name (plus the started event if cached) to the client.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleStreamingQueryCommand
nodes.summary: Handles commands on a StreamingQuery found in the Connect streaming session manager cache or the session's active streams: status, last/recent progress, stop, processAllAvailable, explain, exception and awaitTermination, replying with a StreamingQueryCommandResult.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleStreamingAwaitTermination
nodes.summary: Implements awaitTermination as a loop of short waits (10 seconds) that checks whether the gRPC Context has been cancelled, returning true if terminated, false when the timeout elapses, and throwing CANCELLED if the RPC was cancelled.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleStreamingQueryManagerCommand
nodes.summary: Handles StreamingQueryManager commands: list active queries, get a query, awaitAnyTermination, resetTerminated, and add, remove or list streaming query listeners (Python listeners via PythonStreamingQueryListener or serialized Scala listeners cached in the session holder).

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.handleCheckpointCommand
nodes.summary: Executes DataFrame checkpoint / localCheckpoint (optionally with a StorageLevel): builds a Dataset from the relation, caches the checkpointed DataFrame in the session holder under a fresh UUID, and returns a CachedRemoteRelation id that later relations can reference.
