nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformSubqueryExpression
nodes.summary: Maps subquery expressions (scalar, exists, table argument and IN) to placeholder expressions that carry a plan id (UnresolvedScalarSubqueryPlanId, UnresolvedExistsPlanId, UnresolvedTableArgPlanId, UnresolvedInSubqueryPlanId), later resolved in transformWithRelations.

nodes.name: SparkConnectPlanner.transformWithRelations
nodes.summary: Resolves relation references: SQL with references is routed to transformSqlWithRefs; otherwise it transforms the root (wrapped in a Project to keep plan id), maps referenced relations by plan id and uses transformAllExpressionsWithPruning to replace UnresolvedPlanId placeholders with their plans, failing if any plan id is missing.

nodes.name: SparkConnectExecutePlanHandler.scala
nodes.summary: Handler for ExecutePlan RPCs. SparkConnectExecutePlanHandler resolves the session holder from the request, builds the ExecuteKey, and either creates a new ExecuteHolder and attaches to it, reattaches to an existing one with an identical plan, or fails with OPERATION_ALREADY_EXISTS.

nodes.name: SparkConnectExecutePlanHandler
nodes.summary: gRPC handler constructed with the response observer of one ExecutePlan call; its handle method decides between creating a new execution and reattaching to an existing one.

nodes.name: handle
nodes.summary: Gets or creates the isolated session for the user and session id, forms the ExecuteKey, then asks the execution manager to create an ExecuteHolder and attach, reattach if the same plan is already running, or throw INVALID_HANDLE.OPERATION_ALREADY_EXISTS.

nodes.name: SparkConnectServer.scala
nodes.summary: Main entry point of the standalone Spark Connect server: builds a SparkSession with artifact session isolation enabled, starts SparkConnectService, logs the bound address, blocks on gRPC termination, and stops the service and session on exit.

nodes.name: SparkConnectServer
nodes.summary: Scala object with the main method that launches the Spark Connect server.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Creates the SparkSession, starts SparkConnectService on its SparkContext (exiting on startup failure), waits for the gRPC server to terminate, then stops the service and the session.

nodes.name: SparkConnectSessionManager.scala
nodes.summary: Global tracker of all SessionHolders. SparkConnectSessionManager stores sessions by SessionKey, creates isolated sessions from a lazily built base SparkSession, validates ids, clones sessions, remembers closed sessions as tombstones, and runs a periodic maintenance task that expires inactive sessions.

nodes.name: SparkConnectSessionManager
nodes.summary: Holds a ConcurrentHashMap of SessionHolders and a bounded cache of closed-session tombstones, plus a scheduled executor that closes sessions whose inactive timeout has elapsed.

nodes.name: initializeBaseSession
nodes.summary: Stores the factory for the base SparkSession once, called during service startup; the base session is created lazily on first use.

nodes.name: validateSessionId
nodes.summary: Throws INVALID_HANDLE.SESSION_CHANGED when the server-side session id differs from the id the client last observed.

nodes.name: getOrCreateIsolatedSession
nodes.summary: Finds or atomically creates the SessionHolder for a key (validating the id, creating a new isolated SparkSession, initializing it) and checks the previously observed server session id.

nodes.name: getIsolatedSession
nodes.summary: Finds an existing SessionHolder or throws SESSION_CLOSED or SESSION_NOT_FOUND depending on the closed-session tombstone cache.

nodes.name: cloneSession
nodes.summary: Creates a new SessionHolder under a new session id from the source holder using SparkSession.cloneSession, after validating the source and target ids.

nodes.name: validateCloneTargetSession
nodes.summary: Validates that the clone target session id is UUID formatted, not previously closed, and not already existing.

nodes.name: getSession
nodes.summary: Ensures the maintenance thread is scheduled, reads or computes the holder in the session store, and updates its access time.

nodes.name: removeSessionHolder
nodes.summary: Removes a session from the store, first recording it in the closed-session cache unless reconnection is allowed, to avoid races with re-creation.

nodes.name: shutdownSessionHolder
nodes.summary: Calls SessionHolder.close on a removed session and refreshes its tombstone with final info.

nodes.name: closeSession
nodes.summary: Removes a session by key and shuts it down.

nodes.name: shutdown
nodes.summary: Stops the maintenance executor and clears the session store and closed-session cache when the server shuts down.

nodes.name: schedulePeriodicChecks
nodes.summary: Lazily starts a single-thread scheduled executor that periodically runs session expiry maintenance at the configured interval.

nodes.name: periodicMaintenance
nodes.summary: Scans all sessions and closes those whose last access plus their custom or default timeout has passed (timeout -1 means never).

nodes.name: newIsolatedSession
nodes.summary: Creates a new isolated SparkSession from the base session, falling back to the default session if the base SparkContext is stopped.

nodes.name: validateSessionCreate
nodes.summary: Validates that a new session id is UUID formatted and has not already been closed.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.scala
nodes.summary: Stage-oriented scheduling layer of the Spark driver. When an action such as df.collect() calls SparkContext.runJob, the DAGScheduler turns the RDD graph into stages cut at shuffle boundaries, submits stages in dependency order as TaskSets to the TaskScheduler, handles task completion, and resubmits stages after lost shuffle output. All decisions run on one event-loop thread.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a large class, a companion object (RESUBMIT_TIMEOUT), the DAGSchedulerEventProcessLoop and a small LimitedSizeFIFOSet helper. Members marked private[scheduler] are package-private so tests in the same package can call them.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerEvent.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the sealed DAGSchedulerEvent trait and the case classes/objects that other threads post to the DAGScheduler event queue: job and map-stage submission, cancellations, task begin/completion, executor and worker changes, task set failures, stage resubmission and push-based shuffle merge events.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala sealed trait hierarchy used as the message protocol of the single-threaded scheduler event loop; the event loop pattern-matches on these types.

nodes.name: ActiveJob.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ActiveJob, the DAGScheduler's record of one running job: its final stage, listener, properties and a per-partition finished bitmap.

nodes.name: ActiveJob
nodes.summary: One running job tracked by the DAGScheduler. It holds the jobId, the finalStage (a ResultStage for an action, a ShuffleMapStage for submitMapStage), call site, JobListener, artifacts and scheduling properties. numPartitions comes from the final stage, and the finished array plus numFinished record which output partitions are done so the job knows when it is complete.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerEvent
nodes.summary: Sealed trait that is the base of every message in the scheduler event queue. Any thread may post an event (a task finishing, a job being submitted), while one logic thread reads them, which avoids most synchronization.

nodes.name: JobSubmitted
nodes.summary: Posted when an action submits a result job. It carries jobId, the final RDD, the per-partition function, the partitions to compute, call site, JobListener, artifacts and properties; handled by handleJobSubmitted.

nodes.name: MapStageSubmitted
nodes.summary: A shuffle map stage submitted to run as its own job (used by adaptive query planning, via submitMapStage); handled by handleMapStageSubmitted.

nodes.name: StageCancelled
nodes.summary: Request to cancel every job that uses a given stage id, with an optional reason.

nodes.name: JobCancelled
nodes.summary: Request to cancel one job by id, with an optional reason.

nodes.name: JobGroupCancelled
nodes.summary: Request to cancel all jobs in a job group; with cancelFutureJobs the group id is remembered so later jobs in it are cancelled on submission.

nodes.name: JobTagCancelled
nodes.summary: Request to cancel all jobs carrying a tag; an optional Promise is completed with the cancelled ActiveJobs.

nodes.name: AllJobsCancelled
nodes.summary: Singleton event asking the scheduler to cancel all running and queued jobs.

nodes.name: CleanupQueryJobs
nodes.summary: Event that clears the DAGScheduler's tracking of jobs belonging to one SQL query execution id once the query finishes.

nodes.name: BeginEvent
nodes.summary: Reports that a task started (task and TaskInfo); turned into a SparkListenerTaskStart.

nodes.name: GettingResultEvent
nodes.summary: Reports that a task finished and its result is being fetched remotely; turned into a SparkListenerTaskGettingResult.

nodes.name: CompletionEvent
nodes.summary: Carries a task's end reason (Success, FetchFailed, ExceptionFailure, ...), its result, accumulator updates, metric peaks and TaskInfo. It is the event posted by taskEnded and handled by handleTaskCompletion.

nodes.name: ExecutorAdded
nodes.summary: Reports that an executor was added on a host.

nodes.name: ExecutorLost
nodes.summary: Reports an executor loss with its ExecutorLossReason; the loop extracts the worker host from the reason and calls handleExecutorLost.

nodes.name: WorkerRemoved
nodes.summary: Reports that a worker was removed, so shuffle files on its host are assumed lost.

nodes.name: StageFailed
nodes.summary: Request to abort a stage with a reason and optional exception; posted by DAGScheduler.stageFailed, which the OutputCommitCoordinator uses to cancel a stage when data duplication could happen.

nodes.name: TaskSetFailed
nodes.summary: Posted when the TaskSetManager cancels a whole TaskSet (repeated failures or cancellation of the job); handled by handleTaskSetFailed, which aborts the stage.

nodes.name: ResubmitFailedStages
nodes.summary: Singleton event posted by the DAGScheduler's message scheduler after RESUBMIT_TIMEOUT (200 ms) once a stage must be retried, for example after a fetch failure; it makes the scheduler resubmit the failed stages.

nodes.name: SpeculativeTaskSubmitted
nodes.summary: Reports that the task set manager decided a speculative copy of a task is needed; turned into a listener event.

nodes.name: UnschedulableTaskSetAdded
nodes.summary: Reports that a task set became unschedulable because executors were excluded (with dynamic allocation); turned into a listener event.

nodes.name: UnschedulableTaskSetRemoved
nodes.summary: Reports that a previously unschedulable task set is schedulable again; turned into a listener event.

nodes.name: RegisterMergeStatuses
nodes.summary: Carries MergeStatuses returned by shuffle services after push-based shuffle merge finalization, to be registered in the map output tracker.

nodes.name: ShuffleMergeFinalized
nodes.summary: Posted when shuffle merge finalization for a map stage has finished or timed out so the stage can continue.

nodes.name: ShufflePushCompleted
nodes.summary: Reports that the shuffle push of one map task completed; when the pushed ratio reaches the threshold the merge is finalized.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler
nodes.summary: Driver-side scheduler that implements stage-oriented scheduling. For each job it builds stages by cutting the RDD graph at shuffle dependencies (narrow operations such as map and filter are pipelined in one stage), submits a stage only after its parent shuffle map stages have output, wraps each stage's missing partitions in a TaskSet for the TaskScheduler, and reacts to completion, fetch failure and executor loss by resubmitting stages. Bookkeeping maps (stageIdToStage, shuffleIdToMapStage, waitingStages, runningStages, failedStages, activeJobs) are touched only by the event-loop thread. The companion object defines RESUBMIT_TIMEOUT = 200 ms. Small public methods (taskStarted, taskGettingResult, executorLost, executorAdded, workerRemoved, taskSetFailed, cancelJob, cancelStage, cancelAllJobs and similar) just post an event to eventProcessLoop.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share this id. private[scheduler] members are package-private to org.apache.spark.scheduler so that tests in the same package can call them.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerEventProcessLoop
nodes.summary: Event loop thread (dag-scheduler-event-loop) of the DAGScheduler. onReceive times each message with the DAGSchedulerSource timer and passes it to doOnReceive, which pattern-matches on the DAGSchedulerEvent type and calls the matching handleXxx method. A ShuffleStatusNotFoundException is turned into a stage abort. onError cancels all jobs and stops the SparkContext; onStop fails remaining active jobs.

nodes.name: LimitedSizeFIFOSet
nodes.summary: Small non-thread-safe set that keeps only the most recent `capacity` elements added; the DAGScheduler uses it to remember cancelled job groups.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.taskEnded
nodes.summary: Called by the TaskSetManager when a task finishes or fails; wraps the reason, result, accumulator updates and TaskInfo in a CompletionEvent and posts it to the event loop instead of handling it on the calling thread.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.getCacheLocs
nodes.summary: Returns, per partition of an RDD, the executors that cache it, asking the BlockManagerMaster and memoizing the result in cacheLocs (skipped when the storage level is NONE). It is used to decide which parent stages are already satisfied and to compute preferred task locations.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.getOrCreateShuffleMapStage
nodes.summary: Looks up the ShuffleMapStage for a shuffle dependency in shuffleIdToMapStage; if it is missing, creates it together with any missing ancestor shuffle map stages, one per upstream shuffle dependency.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.createShuffleMapStage
nodes.summary: Creates a ShuffleMapStage for a ShuffleDependency: merges resource profiles, runs barrier-stage checks, creates parent stages, assigns a stage id, registers the stage in stageIdToStage and shuffleIdToMapStage, and registers the shuffle with the MapOutputTracker.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.createResultStage
nodes.summary: Creates the ResultStage for an action: finds the shuffle dependencies of the final RDD, creates or reuses parent ShuffleMapStages, then builds the ResultStage with the function and partitions to compute.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.getShuffleDependenciesAndResourceProfiles
nodes.summary: Walks the RDD graph from a given RDD along narrow dependencies only and returns the immediate parent shuffle dependencies (the stage boundary) plus the ResourceProfiles of the RDDs in the stage. This is where Spark decides where one stage ends.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.getMissingParentStages
nodes.summary: Finds the parent shuffle map stages of a stage that still need to run. It traverses the RDD graph through narrow dependencies, skips RDDs that are fully cached, and for each shuffle dependency adds the map stage if its output is not available (or push-based merge is not finalized).

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.updateJobIdStageIdMaps
nodes.summary: Registers a job id on a stage and recursively on all its ancestor stages (stage.jobIds and jobIdToStageIds), so stages shared between jobs are tracked per job.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.cleanupStateForJobAndIndependentStages
nodes.summary: Removes the state of a finished or failed job and of any stages no other job needs: drops them from runningStages, waitingStages, failedStages, shuffleIdToMapStage and stageIdToStage, then removes the job from activeJobs and detaches it from its final stage.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.submitJob
nodes.summary: Entry point for an action job. Validates the partition ids, eagerly computes RDD partitions outside the event loop, allocates a jobId, returns a completed JobWaiter right away if there are zero partitions, and otherwise posts a JobSubmitted event and returns a JobWaiter used to wait or cancel.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.runJob
nodes.summary: Synchronous wrapper around submitJob: submits the job, blocks on the JobWaiter's completion future, logs duration, and on failure rethrows the exception with the caller's stack trace appended. This is the call that blocks the driver thread for an action like collect().

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.runApproximateJob
nodes.summary: Runs an approximate job: posts a JobSubmitted event with an ApproximateActionListener and waits up to a timeout for a PartialResult from the evaluator.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.submitMapStage
nodes.summary: Submits a shuffle map stage as its own job (used by adaptive query planning) and returns a JobWaiter that completes with MapOutputStatistics when the whole map stage is done; posts a MapStageSubmitted event.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.doCancelAllJobs
nodes.summary: Cancels all running jobs through handleJobCancellation for each running stage's first job and clears activeJobs and jobIdToActiveJob.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.resubmitFailedStages
nodes.summary: Handles the ResubmitFailedStages event: clears cached locations and resubmits all stages in failedStages in order of their first job id via submitStage.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.submitWaitingChildStages
nodes.summary: After a parent stage completes, takes the waiting stages that list it as a parent and calls submitStage on them in order of first job id (submitStage then re-checks for other missing parents).

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.handleTaskSetFailed
nodes.summary: Handles a TaskSetFailed event by looking up the stage of the task set and aborting it, which fails the jobs that depend on it.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.handleJobSubmitted
nodes.summary: Event-loop handler for a submitted job. Skips the job if its job group was cancelled, creates the ResultStage (and its parent stages), handles barrier-slot check failures by retrying later, builds the ActiveJob, registers it, posts SparkListenerJobStart with the stage infos, and calls submitStage on the final stage to start the cascade.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.handleMapStageSubmitted
nodes.summary: Event-loop handler for a map-stage job: gets or creates the ShuffleMapStage for the dependency, creates the ActiveJob, posts job start, submits the stage, and finishes the job immediately if the map output is already available.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.submitStage
nodes.summary: Submits a stage, but first recursively submits its missing parent stages. A stage with no missing parents goes to submitMissingTasks; otherwise the parents are submitted and the stage is put in waitingStages. Aborts the stage if no active job needs it or its attempt limit is exceeded.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.submitMissingTasks
nodes.summary: Turns a stage whose parents are available into tasks. It finds missing partitions, computes preferred locations, creates a new stage attempt, serializes and broadcasts the task binary (rdd plus shuffle dependency, or rdd plus function), builds a ShuffleMapTask or ResultTask per partition, and hands a TaskSet to taskScheduler.submitTasks. If there is nothing to run the stage is marked finished and its waiting children are submitted. Serialization or task-creation errors abort the stage.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.updateAccumulators
nodes.summary: Merges the accumulator updates carried by a CompletionEvent into the driver-side accumulators and the stage's StageInfo, logging failures from bad accumulator implementations.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.rollbackSucceedingStages
nodes.summary: Handles nondeterministic (indeterminate) map output: collects stages downstream of a map stage, aborts those that cannot be rolled back, and marks the rest as rolling back so results from older attempts are ignored and output is recomputed. Returns whether active jobs remain.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.handleTaskCompletion
nodes.summary: Central handler for a CompletionEvent, run on the event loop. On Success a ResultTask records the partition in the ActiveJob and finishes the job (cancelling leftover stages and tasks, cleaning state, posting JobEnd) when all partitions are done; a ShuffleMapTask registers its MapStatus with the MapOutputTracker and, when no partitions are pending, completes the map stage. On FetchFailed it marks the stage failed, unregisters lost map output, adds the stage and its map stage to failedStages and schedules a resubmit (or aborts past the attempt limit). It also covers barrier task failure and Resubmitted, and leaves other failures to the TaskScheduler.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.scheduleShuffleMergeFinalize
nodes.summary: Schedules, on a separate thread pool, the finalization of push-based shuffle merge for a map stage after a delay, replacing an earlier scheduled finalize task when appropriate.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.finalizeShuffleMerge
nodes.summary: Asks each remote shuffle service chosen as a merger to finalize the merge for the stage's shuffle, posts RegisterMergeStatuses events with the results, waits up to a timeout, then posts ShuffleMergeFinalized so downstream stages can proceed.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.processShuffleMapStageCompletion
nodes.summary: Finishes a shuffle map stage: marks it finished, bumps the map output epoch, clears cached locations, and either resubmits the stage if some outputs are still missing or marks map-stage jobs finished and submits waiting child stages.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.handleExecutorLost
nodes.summary: Event-loop handler for a lost executor: decides whether its shuffle files should be considered lost (no reliable shuffle storage, and either whole worker lost or no external shuffle service) and calls removeExecutorAndUnregisterOutputs.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.removeExecutorAndUnregisterOutputs
nodes.summary: Removes an executor from the BlockManagerMaster and unregisters its shuffle outputs (or all outputs on its host) from the MapOutputTracker, using executor failure and shuffle-file-lost epochs to avoid reprocessing follow-on failures.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.handleJobCancellation
nodes.summary: Cancels a job by id by failing it with a job-cancelled SparkException and cleaning up the stages that only it uses; ignores unknown jobs.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.markStageAsFinished
nodes.summary: Marks a stage attempt as finished or failed: records completion time or failure message in StageInfo, clears the stage's failure count on success, ends the output commit coordinator for the stage unless a retry follows, posts SparkListenerStageCompleted, and removes it from runningStages.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.abortStage
nodes.summary: Aborts all active jobs that depend on a failed stage: finds them through stageDependsOn and fails each one (and its independent stages) with a SparkException whose message starts with 'Job aborted due to stage failure', or with the user-facing Spark error as is.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.cancelRunningIndependentStages
nodes.summary: Kills all task attempts of running stages that are used only by the given job, and marks those stages finished with the reason; returns false if the backend cannot kill tasks.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.failJobAndIndependentStages
nodes.summary: Fails a job: cancels stages used only by it, cleans scheduler state, calls the job listener's jobFailed (which raises the error in the user thread) and posts SparkListenerJobEnd with JobFailed.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.stageDependsOn
nodes.summary: Returns true if the target stage is the stage itself or one of its ancestors, walking the RDD graph and following unavailable shuffle map stages.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.getPreferredLocs
nodes.summary: Public thread-safe entry for the locality of a partition of an RDD; delegates to getPreferredLocsInternal. Used when creating tasks and from SparkContext.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.getPreferredLocsInternal
nodes.summary: Recursive search for preferred hosts of an RDD partition: cached locations first, then the RDD's own preferred locations (for example input splits), then the first narrow parent partition that has any preference. Uses a visited set to avoid exponential traversal.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.markMapStageJobAsFinished
nodes.summary: Completes a map-stage job: marks its single output done, passes MapOutputStatistics to the listener, cleans up the job and posts SparkListenerJobEnd with JobSucceeded.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler.stageAbortReason
nodes.summary: Decides whether a stage may be retried: returns an abort message if the test flag disallows retry, if consecutive failed attempts reach spark.stage.maxConsecutiveAttempts, or if total attempts reach the absolute maximum; otherwise None.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerEventProcessLoop.onReceive
nodes.summary: Main entry of the event loop: times message processing and calls doOnReceive, translating ShuffleStatusNotFoundException into a stage abort.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerEventProcessLoop.doOnReceive
nodes.summary: Dispatcher that pattern-matches every DAGSchedulerEvent and calls the corresponding DAGScheduler handler, for example JobSubmitted to handleJobSubmitted, CompletionEvent to handleTaskCompletion, ExecutorLost to handleExecutorLost, TaskSetFailed to handleTaskSetFailed and ResubmitFailedStages to resubmitFailedStages.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerEventProcessLoop.onError
nodes.summary: If the event loop dies, logs the error, tries to cancel all jobs, and stops the SparkContext in a new thread, so a scheduler bug does not leave the application hanging.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerEventProcessLoop.onStop
nodes.summary: On loop shutdown calls dagScheduler.cleanUpAfterSchedulerStop to fail still-active jobs.

nodes.name: TaskSet.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TaskSet, the bundle of Task objects for one stage attempt that the DAGScheduler hands to the TaskScheduler. It carries the stage id and attempt id (combined into the string id 'stageId.stageAttemptId'), priority, job properties (including the scheduler pool), resource profile id and optional shuffle id.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain Scala class with val constructor parameters and a lazy structured-logging id.

nodes.name: TaskSet
nodes.summary: Immutable description of one stage attempt's tasks: tasks array, stageId, stageAttemptId, priority, properties, resourceProfileId and shuffleId. TaskSchedulerImpl.submitTasks wraps it into a TaskSetManager; its id is 'stageId.stageAttemptId' and logId feeds structured logging.

nodes.name: Schedulable.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the Schedulable trait, the common interface of the scheduling tree whose nodes are either Pools or TaskSetManagers. It exposes weight, minShare, priority, running task count and tree operations such as addSchedulable and getSortedTaskSetQueue.

nodes.name: Schedulable
nodes.summary: Trait for entities in the scheduling tree (pools and task set managers). Defines parent, child queue, scheduling mode, weight, minShare, runningTasks, priority, stageId, name, add/remove/lookup of children, executorLost and executorDecommission propagation, speculative task checks and getSortedTaskSetQueue.

nodes.name: Pool.scala
nodes.summary: Implements Pool, a Schedulable node that groups child Pools or TaskSetManagers and orders them with the FIFO or FAIR scheduling algorithm. The root pool of TaskSchedulerImpl is the entry point used to get the sorted TaskSetManager queue for each round of resource offers.

nodes.name: Pool
nodes.summary: A Schedulable holding child Schedulables in a concurrent queue and name map. Picks FairSchedulingAlgorithm or FIFOSchedulingAlgorithm from its SchedulingMode (other modes throw), propagates executorLost, executorDecommission and speculation checks to children, and tracks running task counts up the parent chain.

nodes.name: addSchedulable
nodes.summary: Adds a child Schedulable to the queue and name map and sets the child's parent to this pool.

nodes.name: getSchedulableByName
nodes.summary: Looks up a child by name, first in the direct name map and then recursively through child pools; returns null when not found.

nodes.name: checkSpeculatableTasks
nodes.summary: Asks every child schedulable whether it has speculatable tasks and returns true if any child says offers should be revived.

nodes.name: getSortedTaskSetQueue
nodes.summary: Sorts child schedulables with the pool's scheduling algorithm comparator and flattens them into an ordered list of schedulable TaskSetManagers; this is the order in which resource offers are tried.

nodes.name: increaseRunningTasks
nodes.summary: Adds to the pool's running task count and recursively propagates the change to parent pools.

nodes.name: decreaseRunningTasks
nodes.summary: Subtracts from the pool's running task count and recursively propagates the change to parent pools.

nodes.name: SchedulableBuilder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SchedulableBuilder trait and its FIFO and Fair implementations. The Fair builder reads pool definitions (name, schedulingMode, minShare, weight) from the fairscheduler.xml allocation file, and routes each new TaskSetManager into the pool named by the job's spark.scheduler.pool property.

nodes.name: SchedulableBuilder
nodes.summary: Trait for building the Schedulable tree: buildPools creates pool nodes and addTaskSetManager attaches a TaskSetManager as a leaf using the job properties.

nodes.name: buildPools
nodes.summary: Abstract method that builds the pool nodes of the scheduling tree.

nodes.name: addTaskSetManager
nodes.summary: Abstract method that attaches a TaskSetManager to the tree, using the job properties to choose where.

nodes.name: FIFOSchedulableBuilder
nodes.summary: Builder for FIFO mode: no extra pools are created and every TaskSetManager is added directly to the root pool.

nodes.name: buildPools
nodes.summary: No-op: FIFO mode needs no child pools.

nodes.name: addTaskSetManager
nodes.summary: Adds the TaskSetManager directly under the root pool, ignoring job properties.

nodes.name: FairSchedulableBuilder
nodes.summary: Builder for FAIR mode: loads pools from the configured allocation file (or fairscheduler.xml on the classpath) via XML, creates a 'default' pool if missing, and places each TaskSetManager in the pool named by the spark.scheduler.pool local property, creating an unconfigured pool with defaults (FIFO, minShare 0, weight 1) and warning when the name is unknown.

nodes.name: buildPools
nodes.summary: Opens the pool allocation file (from config or the default fairscheduler.xml resource), builds pools from it, falls back to a default pool when no file exists, logs and rethrows non-fatal errors, then ensures a 'default' pool exists.

nodes.name: buildDefaultPool
nodes.summary: Creates and registers the 'default' FIFO pool under the root pool if no pool with that name exists yet.

nodes.name: buildFairSchedulerPool
nodes.summary: Parses the XML stream and registers one Pool per pool element with its schedulingMode, minShare and weight.

nodes.name: getSchedulingModeValue
nodes.summary: Reads and validates a pool's schedulingMode from XML, warning and using the default when the value is invalid or NONE.

nodes.name: getIntValue
nodes.summary: Reads an integer pool property (minShare or weight) from XML, warning and using the default on a blank or invalid value.

nodes.name: addTaskSetManager
nodes.summary: Looks up the pool named in the job properties (default 'default'), creates it with default settings if it does not exist, and adds the TaskSetManager as a child of that pool.

nodes.name: TaskScheduler.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the TaskScheduler trait, the low-level interface between the DAGScheduler and a cluster-specific task scheduler. It covers submitting a TaskSet, killing task attempts, executor lifecycle notifications, heartbeats and default parallelism; TaskSchedulerImpl is its only implementation.

nodes.name: TaskScheduler
nodes.summary: Trait describing what the DAGScheduler needs from a task scheduler: rootPool and schedulingMode, start/stop, submitTasks(TaskSet), kill APIs, partition completion notices, setDAGScheduler for upcalls, defaultParallelism, executor heartbeat, decommission and loss handling, and application id. One TaskScheduler serves a single SparkContext.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the scheduler (and its backend).

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Disconnects from the cluster, with an optional exit code.

nodes.name: submitTasks
nodes.summary: Entry point used by the DAGScheduler to submit a TaskSet of stage tasks to run.

nodes.name: killTaskAttempt
nodes.summary: Kills one task attempt and returns whether it was killed; throws UnsupportedOperationException if the backend cannot kill tasks.

nodes.name: killAllTaskAttempts
nodes.summary: Kills all tasks in all attempts of a stage id.

nodes.name: notifyPartitionCompletion
nodes.summary: Tells TaskSetManagers of a stage that a partition already completed so they can skip it.

nodes.name: setDAGScheduler
nodes.summary: Registers the DAGScheduler used for upcalls; guaranteed to be set before submitTasks is called.

nodes.name: defaultParallelism
nodes.summary: Returns the default level of parallelism as a hint for sizing jobs.

nodes.name: executorHeartbeatReceived
nodes.summary: Handles an executor heartbeat: updates task metrics and tells the executor whether its BlockManager is known to the driver.

nodes.name: executorDecommission
nodes.summary: Processes a decommissioning executor.

nodes.name: executorLost
nodes.summary: Processes a lost executor.

nodes.name: workerRemoved
nodes.summary: Processes a removed worker.

nodes.name: SchedulerBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the SchedulerBackend trait, the cluster-manager-facing interface under TaskSchedulerImpl. It models a world where the application gets resource offers as machines become available and launches tasks on them, with reviveOffers, killTask, defaultParallelism and concurrency queries.

nodes.name: SchedulerBackend
nodes.summary: Trait that pluggable cluster backends implement: start/stop, reviveOffers (update the current offers and schedule tasks), defaultParallelism, killTask (unsupported by default), getTaskThreadDump, isReady, application ids, driver log URLs, maxNumConcurrentTasks and push-based shuffle merger locations.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the backend.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the backend; the exitCode overload defaults to stop().

nodes.name: reviveOffers
nodes.summary: Updates the current resource offers and schedules tasks on them.

nodes.name: defaultParallelism
nodes.summary: Returns the backend's default level of parallelism.

nodes.name: killTask
nodes.summary: Asks an executor to kill a running task; the default implementation throws UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: getTaskThreadDump
nodes.summary: Returns a thread dump of a running task from its executor, if available.

nodes.name: isReady
nodes.summary: Whether the backend is ready to schedule; defaults to true.

nodes.name: maxNumConcurrentTasks
nodes.summary: Returns the max number of tasks that can currently be launched concurrently for a ResourceProfile; the value changes as executors come and go.

nodes.name: getShufflePushMergerLocations
nodes.summary: Returns external shuffle service locations for push-based shuffle; defaults to Nil.

nodes.name: TaskSchedulerImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Core implementation of TaskScheduler: accepts TaskSets from the DAGScheduler, wraps each in a TaskSetManager inside the pool tree (FIFO or FAIR), turns SchedulerBackend resource offers into task assignments with locality, resource profile and barrier handling, and processes executor status updates, speculation, executor loss and decommissioning.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a companion object holding slot calculation and container prioritization helpers; most public methods synchronize on the scheduler instance.

nodes.name: TaskSchedulerImpl
nodes.summary: Schedules tasks for all cluster types through a SchedulerBackend. initialize() builds the pool tree, submitTasks() creates a TaskSetManager and revives offers, resourceOffers() orders TaskSetManagers via the root pool and assigns tasks per locality level, and statusUpdate() routes executor task state to TaskResultGetter. Also tracks executors, hosts, racks, decommissions, barrier stages, speculation and unschedulable (excluded) task sets.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object (lines 1220-1338) shares this node id and defines calculateAvailableSlots, prioritizeContainers and maybeCreateHealthTracker.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Binds the SchedulerBackend, creates a FIFOSchedulableBuilder or FairSchedulableBuilder depending on spark.scheduler.mode (other modes throw) and builds the pools under the root pool.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the backend and, when not local and speculation is enabled, schedules the periodic checkSpeculatableTasks thread.

nodes.name: submitTasks
nodes.summary: Entry point for a TaskSet from the DAGScheduler: creates a TaskSetManager, marks earlier manager attempts of the same stage as zombie, registers it in the scheduling pool through the SchedulableBuilder, starts the starvation warning timer for the first job, then calls backend.reviveOffers() to trigger scheduling.

nodes.name: createTaskSetManager
nodes.summary: Creates the TaskSetManager for a TaskSet, using a streaming-log-aware variant when the job properties carry a streaming query id.

nodes.name: streamingTaskSetManager
nodes.summary: Builds a TaskSetManager mixed with StructuredStreamingIdAwareSchedulerLogging so logs include query and batch ids.

nodes.name: killAllTaskAttempts
nodes.summary: Kills running tasks of every attempt of a stage by calling backend.killTask for each, and suspends the TaskSetManagers (marking them zombie) without aborting them.

nodes.name: killTaskAttempt
nodes.summary: Looks up the executor of a task id and calls backend.killTask; returns false when the task is unknown.

nodes.name: taskSetFinished
nodes.summary: Cleans up when all attempts of a TaskSetManager finished: removes it from the stage-attempt map and its parent pool.

nodes.name: resourceOfferSingleTaskSet
nodes.summary: Offers each shuffled worker offer to one TaskSetManager at a given max locality: checks resource profile and cpu/custom resource fit, asks the TaskSetManager for a TaskDescription, records it as running, and decrements the remaining cpus and resources. Returns whether any delay-scheduling rejection happened and the lowest launched locality.

nodes.name: addRunningTask
nodes.summary: Registers a launched task in the task id to TaskSetManager, task id to executor and executor to running tasks maps.

nodes.name: resourcesMeetTaskRequirements
nodes.summary: Checks that an offer has enough cpus and custom resources for one task of the TaskSet's resource profile and returns the resource address assignments or None.

nodes.name: minTaskLocality
nodes.summary: Returns the more local (smaller) of two optional TaskLocality values.

nodes.name: resourceOffers
nodes.summary: Called by the backend with WorkerOffers: registers new executors, hosts and racks, filters excluded nodes, shuffles offers, then for each TaskSetManager in the root pool's priority order tries every locality level (PROCESS_LOCAL, NODE_LOCAL, NO_PREF, RACK_LOCAL, ANY) until nothing more launches. Also resets delay-scheduling timers, handles completely excluded or unschedulable task sets, and does all-or-nothing launching for barrier stages. Returns the TaskDescriptions per offer.

nodes.name: updateUnschedulableTaskSetTimeoutAndStartAbortTimer
nodes.summary: Records an expiry time for an unschedulable task set and schedules the abort timer that will abort the stage if it is still unschedulable.

nodes.name: createUnschedulableTaskSetAbortTimer
nodes.summary: Builds the TimerTask that aborts a TaskSetManager when its unschedulable timeout has expired.

nodes.name: statusUpdate
nodes.summary: Handles a task state change sent by an executor: for finished states cleans up scheduler state and enqueues the result with TaskResultGetter (enqueueSuccessfulTask for FINISHED, enqueueFailedTask for FAILED or KILLED); for RUNNING marks the launch as succeeded; logs and ignores updates for unknown tasks.

nodes.name: executorHeartbeatReceived
nodes.summary: Converts accumulator updates from an executor heartbeat into per-task AccumulableInfos (optionally computing task process rate for speculation) and forwards them to the DAGScheduler.

nodes.name: handleSuccessfulTask
nodes.summary: Called by TaskResultGetter with a deserialized result; delegates to TaskSetManager.handleSuccessfulTask under the scheduler lock.

nodes.name: handleFailedTask
nodes.summary: Delegates a task failure to the TaskSetManager and, if the manager is still active and no attempt succeeded, revives offers so the failed task can be re-run.

nodes.name: handlePartitionCompleted
nodes.summary: Marks a partition as completed in non-zombie TaskSetManagers of the stage so they skip running it again.

nodes.name: error
nodes.summary: Aborts all active TaskSetManagers with the message, or throws a cluster scheduler error if none are active.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the speculation scheduler, backend, TaskResultGetter, barrier coordinator and timers.

nodes.name: defaultParallelism
nodes.summary: Returns the backend's default parallelism.

nodes.name: checkSpeculatableTasks
nodes.summary: Asks the root pool to find speculatable tasks and revives offers if any were found so copies can be launched.

nodes.name: executorDecommission
nodes.summary: Records a known executor as pending decommission, notifies the root pool and revives offers.

nodes.name: executorLost
nodes.summary: Handles a lost executor: removes it (or defers when the reason is still pending), then calls dagScheduler.executorLost outside the lock and revives offers.

nodes.name: cleanupTaskState
nodes.summary: Removes a task from the task-to-manager, task-to-executor and executor running task maps.

nodes.name: removeExecutor
nodes.summary: Removes an executor from all scheduler structures (running tasks, host and rack maps, decommission state) and, when the loss reason is known, tells the root pool so TaskSetManagers fail or resubmit its tasks.

nodes.name: waitBackendReady
nodes.summary: Blocks until the backend reports isReady, throwing if the SparkContext stops while waiting.

nodes.name: calculateAvailableSlots
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that computes how many tasks of a ResourceProfile can run concurrently from available cpus and custom resources of compatible executors; also used by the backend for maxNumConcurrentTasks and by barrier scheduling.

nodes.name: prioritizeContainers
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that orders offers round-robin across hosts so one container per host is used before any host gets a second.

nodes.name: maybeCreateHealthTracker
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that creates a HealthTracker (executor exclusion on failure) when the feature is enabled.

nodes.name: CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Driver-side SchedulerBackend for coarse-grained executors that register over RPC and stay for the whole application. Its inner DriverEndpoint handles executor registration, task status updates, offer revival, task launching (sending LaunchTask to executors), kills and executor removal, and the outer class handles executor requests, kills and decommissioning against the cluster manager.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with an inner RpcEndpoint class (DriverEndpoint) and a tiny companion object defining ENDPOINT_NAME ('CoarseGrainedScheduler').

nodes.name: CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend
nodes.summary: SchedulerBackend that waits for executors to connect and keeps each for the entire job. Holds executorDataMap (free cores and resources per executor), the DriverEndpoint RPC endpoint, revive thread, and executor allocation APIs (request, kill, decommission). reviveOffers and killTask just send messages to the DriverEndpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object (lines 1069-1071) shares this node id.

nodes.name: DriverEndpoint
nodes.summary: Inner single-threaded RPC endpoint registered as 'CoarseGrainedScheduler'. receive handles StatusUpdate, ReviveOffers, KillTask, RemoveExecutor and similar one-way messages; receiveAndReply handles RegisterExecutor, StopDriver, decommissioning and config retrieval; it builds WorkerOffers, asks the TaskSchedulerImpl for assignments and sends LaunchTask to executors.

nodes.name: onStart
nodes.summary: Starts a daemon thread that sends ReviveOffers to the endpoint itself at a fixed interval (default 1000 ms) so delay scheduling can make progress.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles one-way messages: StatusUpdate (passes state to TaskSchedulerImpl.statusUpdate, frees cores and resources of finished tasks, then makes new offers on that executor), ReviveOffers, KillTask (forwarded to the executor), executor and host kill or decommission, RemoveExecutor, LaunchedExecutor and others.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles request-reply messages: RegisterExecutor (rejects duplicates and excluded nodes, records ExecutorData, posts SparkListenerExecutorAdded, handles pending decommission), StopDriver, StopExecutors, log level updates, ExecutorDecommissioning, RetrieveSparkAppConfig and IsExecutorAlive.

nodes.name: makeOffers
nodes.summary: Builds a WorkerOffer for every active executor, calls scheduler.resourceOffers under the scheduler and backend lock, and passes any resulting TaskDescriptions to launchTasks. An overload at lines 408-423 offers resources on a single executor with isAllFreeResources=false.

nodes.name: buildWorkerOffer
nodes.summary: Converts an executor's ExecutorData (free cores, resources, address, resource profile id) into a WorkerOffer.

nodes.name: onDisconnected
nodes.summary: Removes the executor associated with a disconnected RPC address, with an ExecutorProcessLost reason.

nodes.name: launchTasks
nodes.summary: Serializes each TaskDescription; if it exceeds the max RPC message size aborts its TaskSetManager, otherwise deducts the executor's free cores and resources and sends LaunchTask to the executor's endpoint.

nodes.name: removeExecutor
nodes.summary: Removes an executor's state, adjusts core counts, determines the final loss reason (killed by driver, decommissioned or given), then notifies scheduler.executorLost and posts SparkListenerExecutorRemoved; for unknown executors cleans the block manager entry.

nodes.name: disableExecutor
nodes.summary: Marks an active executor as pending loss reason so no more offers go to it and tells the scheduler it is lost with LossReasonPending.

nodes.name: decommissionExecutors
nodes.summary: Decommissions the given executors: notifies the TaskSchedulerImpl, records pending decommission, optionally lowers the target executor count, marks BlockManagers decommissioned, sends DecommissionExecutor to executors and schedules a force-kill cleanup after a timeout.

nodes.name: stopExecutors
nodes.summary: Asks the DriverEndpoint synchronously to tell every executor to shut down.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the revive thread, cleanup service and executors, then asks the DriverEndpoint to stop the driver.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Clears requested executor totals and removes all known executors; used for yarn-client AM re-registration.

nodes.name: reviveOffers
nodes.summary: Sends a ReviveOffers message to the DriverEndpoint, which then runs makeOffers.

nodes.name: killTask
nodes.summary: Sends a KillTask message to the DriverEndpoint, which forwards it to the executor.

nodes.name: defaultParallelism
nodes.summary: Returns spark.default.parallelism if set, otherwise the larger of total registered cores and 2.

nodes.name: removeExecutor
nodes.summary: Fire-and-forget: sends RemoveExecutor to the DriverEndpoint; called by subclasses when a worker is lost.

nodes.name: isReady
nodes.summary: Reports readiness once enough resources registered (minRegisteredRatio) or the max registered waiting time has elapsed.

nodes.name: isExecutorActive
nodes.summary: True when the executor is registered and not pending removal, loss reason or decommission.

nodes.name: maxNumConcurrentTasks
nodes.summary: Computes concurrent task slots over active executors via TaskSchedulerImpl.calculateAvailableSlots for the given ResourceProfile.

nodes.name: requestExecutors
nodes.summary: Requests additional executors for the default ResourceProfile from the cluster manager via doRequestTotalExecutors and waits for acknowledgment.

nodes.name: requestTotalExecutors
nodes.summary: Sets the total desired executors per ResourceProfile plus locality hints, records request times, and asks the cluster manager via doRequestTotalExecutors.

nodes.name: updateExecRequestTime
nodes.summary: Maintains a queue of executor request timestamps per ResourceProfile, adding or consuming entries by delta.

nodes.name: doRequestTotalExecutors
nodes.summary: Hook for cluster-manager subclasses to request a total executor count; the default returns Future(false).

nodes.name: adjustExecutors
nodes.summary: Lowers the requested executor total per ResourceProfile for executors being removed and informs the cluster manager.

nodes.name: killExecutors
nodes.summary: Kills executors via the cluster manager, skipping those already pending removal and busy ones unless forced, and optionally adjusting the target executor count.

nodes.name: doKillExecutors
nodes.summary: Hook for cluster-manager subclasses to kill executors; the default returns Future(false).

nodes.name: decommissionExecutorsOnHost
nodes.summary: Sends DecommissionExecutorsOnHost to the DriverEndpoint so the work is serialized in its event loop.

nodes.name: killExecutorsOnHost
nodes.summary: Sends KillExecutorsOnHost to the DriverEndpoint so registration and killing are serialized in its event loop.

nodes.name: updateDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Stores new delegation tokens and pushes them to all executors.

nodes.name: withLock
nodes.summary: Runs a function holding the TaskSchedulerImpl lock then the backend lock, preserving lock order to avoid the SPARK-27112 deadlock.

nodes.name: getTaskThreadDump
nodes.summary: Asks an active executor for a task thread dump over RPC.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.scala
nodes.summary: Per-TaskSet scheduler that tracks every task attempt of one stage attempt, hands tasks out to executor offers using delay scheduling, retries failed tasks up to a limit and launches speculative copies of slow tasks.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file: the class and its companion object (constants) share one class node; helper classes PendingTasksByLocality and BarrierPendingLaunchTask live at the bottom.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager
nodes.summary: Schedules the tasks of a single TaskSet inside TaskSchedulerImpl. For each task it keeps attempt history, running copies and a success flag, and exposes resourceOffer (pick a task for a free executor) plus handleSuccessfulTask and handleFailedTask (react to task outcomes). Failed tasks are retried until maxTaskFailures is reached, then the whole task set is aborted. It becomes a zombie once all tasks have succeeded or it is aborted, and implements Schedulable so the scheduling pools can order it.

nodes.name: TaskProcessRateCalculator
nodes.summary: Inner helper used only when efficient speculation is enabled. It accumulates records read and executor run time from finished tasks to compute an average processing rate, so a running task is treated as inefficient when its rate falls below that average times a multiplier.

nodes.name: PendingTasksByLocality
nodes.summary: Holds the pending task indices of a task set grouped by locality: per executor, per host, per rack, tasks with no preference and all tasks. The lists act as stacks with lazy removal, so duplicates are allowed and are filtered when a task is dequeued.

nodes.name: BarrierPendingLaunchTask
nodes.summary: Case class recording a barrier task that has been matched to an executor in the current offer round but not yet launched. A barrier stage launches only if all its tasks get slots in one round, otherwise the assignments are reverted.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.addPendingTasks
nodes.summary: Adds every task to the pending lists in reverse index order (so low indices launch first), then resolves the racks of all preferred hosts in one batch to avoid slow per-task rack lookups.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.addPendingTask
nodes.summary: Registers one task index in every pending list it belongs to: per executor (including executors alive on a host that has a cached HDFS block), per host, per rack, the no-preference list and the all list. The same method fills the speculatable lists when speculatable is true, and it does nothing for a zombie.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.dequeueTaskFromList
nodes.summary: Pops tasks from the end of a pending list until it finds one that is not excluded on this executor or host, has not succeeded and has no running copy. A speculative request instead accepts a task with exactly one running copy and no earlier attempt on the same host.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.hasAttemptOnHost
nodes.summary: Returns true if any earlier attempt of the given task index ran on the given host; used so a speculative copy does not land on the same host as the original.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.isTaskExcludededOnExecOrNode
nodes.summary: Checks the TaskSetExcludelist to see whether a task is excluded on the offered executor or its node because of earlier failures there.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.dequeueTask
nodes.summary: Finds a task index for an offered executor and host within a maximum locality level. It tries regular pending tasks first and falls back to speculative tasks only if none is found.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.dequeueTaskHelper
nodes.summary: Searches the pending lists in locality order: executor (PROCESS_LOCAL), host (NODE_LOCAL), no-preference, rack (RACK_LOCAL) and finally any task, skipping levels above the allowed maximum locality. Returns the task index with the locality it was found at and whether it is speculative.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.resetDelayScheduleTimer
nodes.summary: Restarts the locality wait timer and, when a minimum locality is given, moves the current locality index to that level (used by the legacy wait-reset behaviour).

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.resourceOffer
nodes.summary: Main entry point called by TaskSchedulerImpl for each free executor. Unless the task set is a zombie or excluded for this offer, it computes the allowed locality level from delay scheduling, dequeues a task and either builds its TaskDescription or, for barrier stages, parks it in barrierPendingLaunchTasks. It also reports whether the offer was rejected only because of the locality wait.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.prepareLaunchingTask
nodes.summary: Creates the TaskInfo for a new attempt, updates running-copy bookkeeping, serializes the Task with the closure serializer and aborts the task set if serialization fails. It warns about very large tasks, tells the DAGScheduler the task started and returns the TaskDescription to ship to the executor.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.taskName
nodes.summary: Builds the readable name of a task attempt from its TaskInfo, in the form "task <id> in stage <taskSet id> (TID n)", used in logs.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.maybeFinishTaskSet
nodes.summary: When the manager is a zombie and no tasks are running, tells TaskSchedulerImpl the task set finished and, if all tasks succeeded, reports the per-executor failures to the HealthTracker.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.getAllowedLocalityLevel
nodes.summary: Implements delay scheduling: starting at the current locality level it checks if tasks remain at that level and moves to the next (less local) level either immediately when none remain or after the locality wait for that level has expired. Returns the level offers may use now.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.getLocalityIndex
nodes.summary: Maps a locality value to its index in myLocalityLevels, returning the next less-local level present when the exact one is missing (the last level is always ANY).

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.getCompletelyExcludedTaskIfAny
nodes.summary: Looks for an unscheduled task that every alive node and executor excludes, so the scheduler can detect a task set that can never run and avoid hanging the job.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.abortSinceCompletelyExcludedOnFailure
nodes.summary: Aborts the task set with an explanatory message when a task cannot run anywhere because of excludeOnFailure settings.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.handleTaskGettingResult
nodes.summary: Marks a task as fetching its result (an indirect result held in the block manager) and notifies the DAGScheduler.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.canFetchMoreResults
nodes.summary: Adds the result size to the running total and aborts the task set if the sum of serialized results of non-shuffle-map tasks exceeds the configured maximum result size.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.handleSuccessfulTask
nodes.summary: Processes a finished task attempt: ignores duplicates, records its duration for speculation, kills the other still-running attempts of the same task, counts the task as successful and turns the manager into a zombie when all tasks are done. It then notifies the DAGScheduler with a Success end reason.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.emptyTaskInfoAccumulablesAndNotifyDagScheduler
nodes.summary: Wrapper around DAGScheduler.taskEnded that keeps a clone of the TaskInfo with empty accumulables to cut driver memory, while sending the original TaskInfo to the DAGScheduler.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.markPartitionCompleted
nodes.summary: Marks the task for a partition as successful when another stage attempt already produced that partition, and may finish the task set.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.handleFailedTask
nodes.summary: Handles a failed or killed attempt. A fetch failure marks the task done and turns the manager into a zombie so the previous stage reruns; non-serializable results and output file conflicts abort without retry; other failures that count toward the limit increment numFailures and abort the job when it reaches maxTaskFailures; otherwise the task is put back on the pending lists.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.abort
nodes.summary: Reports the task set failure to the DAGScheduler, marks the manager as a zombie and finishes the task set if nothing is running.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.suspend
nodes.summary: Turns the manager into a zombie to stop launching new tasks without notifying the DAGScheduler, for cases where the DAGScheduler already knows about the failure.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.addRunningTask
nodes.summary: Adds a task id to the running set and increases the running-task count of the parent Pool, which fair and FIFO scheduling use.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.removeRunningTask
nodes.summary: Removes a task id from the running set and decreases the parent Pool running-task count.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.isSchedulable
nodes.summary: Schedulable override: a task set manager can be offered resources while it is not a zombie and has pending or speculatable tasks.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.getSortedTaskSetQueue
nodes.summary: Schedulable override that returns just this manager, since a task set manager is a leaf of the scheduling tree.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.executorLost
nodes.summary: Reacts to a lost executor. For shuffle map tasks whose output may be gone it marks finished tasks as not successful and re-enqueues them, then fails every task still running there with ExecutorLostFailure (counted against the retry limit only if the app caused the exit) and recomputes locality.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.checkAndSubmitSpeculatableTasks
nodes.summary: Scans running tasks that have a single copy and marks those running longer than the threshold as speculatable, adding them to the speculative pending lists and informing the DAGScheduler. It can also speculate early when the executor is about to be decommissioned.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.checkSpeculatableTasks
nodes.summary: Periodic speculation check called by the scheduler. Once enough tasks have finished (the speculation quantile) it uses a multiple of the median successful duration as the threshold, or a user threshold for small task sets, and skips zombie, barrier and single-task sets.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.getLocalityWait
nodes.summary: Returns how long to wait at a locality level before moving to the next one, read from the process, node or rack locality wait configs, or 0 for other levels.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.computeValidLocalityLevels
nodes.summary: Computes which locality levels are worth trying given the pending tasks and the currently alive executors, hosts and racks, always ending with ANY. Skipping empty levels avoids pointless waiting.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.executorDecommission
nodes.summary: Recomputes valid locality levels when an executor starts decommissioning.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.recomputeLocality
nodes.summary: Recomputes the valid locality levels and waits after executors change and keeps the current level, shifting to a newly available more local level if the set of levels grew.

nodes.name: TaskSetManager.executorAdded
nodes.summary: Recomputes valid locality levels when a new executor registers.

nodes.name: TaskProcessRateCalculator.updateAvgTaskProcessRate
nodes.summary: Adds the records read and executor run time of a finished task to the totals, recomputes the average processing rate and drops that task from the running-rate map.

nodes.name: Stage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract Stage: a set of parallel tasks that compute the same function on different partitions of an RDD, bounded by shuffle boundaries. It tracks the stage id, parent stages, jobs it belongs to, attempt numbering, failed attempts and the latest StageInfo.

nodes.name: Stage
nodes.summary: Abstract base of a stage in the job DAG. The DAGScheduler cuts a job into stages at shuffle boundaries and runs them in topological order; a stage is either a ShuffleMapStage (feeds later stages) or a ResultStage (computes the final action). A stage can be re-run in several attempts after failures, each creating a new StageInfo.

nodes.name: Stage.clearFailures
nodes.summary: Clears the set of failed stage attempt ids (kept to stop endless retries when a stage keeps failing).

nodes.name: Stage.markAsRollingBack
nodes.summary: Records the latest submitted attempt as one whose task output must be ignored, used when an upstream stage was found to be indeterminate.

nodes.name: Stage.makeNewStageAttempt
nodes.summary: Starts a new attempt of the stage by registering fresh TaskMetrics and creating a new StageInfo with the next attempt id for the partitions that still need computing.

nodes.name: Stage.increaseAttemptIdOnFirstSkip
nodes.summary: Moves the next attempt id from 0 to 1 the first time a stage is visited but skipped, so later attempts do not reuse id 0.

nodes.name: Stage.findMissingPartitions
nodes.summary: Abstract method that returns the partition ids still to be computed; ShuffleMapStage and ResultStage implement it differently.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShuffleMapStage, the intermediate stage whose tasks write shuffle map output for a later stage to fetch, and which asks the MapOutputTrackerMaster how many map outputs are available.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage
nodes.summary: A stage that runs ShuffleMapTasks and ends right before a shuffle, saving map output files that reduce tasks fetch later. It holds the ShuffleDependency, tracks pending partitions and any ActiveJobs that submitted it standalone, and is available once every partition has a registered shuffle output.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.mapStageJobs
nodes.summary: Returns the active map-stage jobs that were submitted to compute this stage on its own.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.addActiveJob
nodes.summary: Adds a job to the list of active jobs waiting on this shuffle map stage.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.removeActiveJob
nodes.summary: Removes a finished job from the list of active map-stage jobs.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.numAvailableOutputs
nodes.summary: Returns the number of partitions with shuffle output, as reported by the MapOutputTrackerMaster for this shuffle id.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.isAvailable
nodes.summary: True when every partition has shuffle output, meaning downstream stages can start reading from this map stage.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.findMissingPartitions
nodes.summary: Asks the MapOutputTrackerMaster which partitions have no (or lost) shuffle output, falling back to all partitions.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.isStaticallyIndeterminate
nodes.summary: True when the RDD is declared to have an indeterminate output order (known when the RDD is created).

nodes.name: ShuffleMapStage.isRuntimeIndeterminate
nodes.summary: True when different attempts of this stage were found to produce different data (checksum mismatch) and the RDD is not reliably checkpointed.

nodes.name: ResultStage.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ResultStage, the final stage of a job that applies a function to selected partitions of an RDD to compute an action result such as count or collect.

nodes.name: ResultStage
nodes.summary: The last stage of a job. It stores the function to run on each partition and the array of partition ids to compute (actions like first() or lookup() may not need every partition) and links to the single ActiveJob it serves.

nodes.name: ResultStage.activeJob
nodes.summary: Returns the active job of this result stage, empty if the job finished or was cancelled.

nodes.name: ResultStage.setActiveJob
nodes.summary: Attaches the ActiveJob that this result stage computes.

nodes.name: ResultStage.removeActiveJob
nodes.summary: Detaches the active job once it has finished.

nodes.name: ResultStage.findMissingPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the partitions of the active job that have not produced a result yet; it requires an active job.

nodes.name: Task.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract Task, the unit of work sent to an executor, with its two concrete kinds ShuffleMapTask and ResultTask. It sets up the TaskContext in run(), supports killing, and collects accumulator updates.

nodes.name: Task
nodes.summary: Abstract unit of execution for one partition of a stage, serialized on the driver and run on an executor. The last stage of a job runs ResultTasks that send output to the driver; earlier stages run ShuffleMapTasks that split their output into shuffle buckets. Subclasses implement runTask.

nodes.name: Task.run
nodes.summary: Called by the Executor to run the task. It builds the TaskContext (a BarrierTaskContext for barrier stages), installs it in thread-local state, handles an early kill, runs the task via runTaskWithListeners, and in a finally block frees unroll memory and unsets thread-local state.

nodes.name: Task.setTaskMemoryManager
nodes.summary: Gives the task its TaskMemoryManager before it runs.

nodes.name: Task.runTask
nodes.summary: Abstract method with the task-specific work, implemented by ShuffleMapTask (write shuffle output, return a MapStatus) and ResultTask (apply the job function and return its value).

nodes.name: Task.preferredLocations
nodes.summary: Preferred execution locations for locality scheduling; empty by default and overridden by the concrete tasks.

nodes.name: Task.collectAccumulatorUpdates
nodes.summary: Collects the current internal metric accumulators plus external accumulators; on failure it keeps only external ones that count failed values.

nodes.name: Task.kill
nodes.summary: Marks the task as killed with a reason and interrupts it by marking the TaskContext interrupted and optionally interrupting the executor thread; if the context is not yet interruptible the interrupt is deferred. Safe to call more than once.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapTask.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShuffleMapTask, which computes one partition of the map-side RDD and writes the result into shuffle files split by the partitioner, returning a MapStatus that tells the driver where the output lives.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapTask
nodes.summary: Task of a ShuffleMapStage. It receives a broadcast of the serialized RDD and ShuffleDependency, computes its partition and passes the records to the shuffle write processor of the dependency, which divides them into buckets for the reduce side.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapTask.runTask
nodes.summary: Deserializes the (RDD, ShuffleDependency) pair from the broadcast binary while timing the deserialization, picks the map id (partition id under the old fetch protocol, otherwise the task attempt id) and calls dep.shuffleWriterProcessor.write over the partition iterator, returning the MapStatus.

nodes.name: ShuffleMapTask.preferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the de-duplicated preferred locations used by the TaskSetManager for locality-aware scheduling.

nodes.name: ResultTask.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ResultTask, which applies the job function to one partition of the final RDD and sends the value back to the driver.

nodes.name: ResultTask
nodes.summary: Task of a ResultStage. It receives a broadcast of the serialized RDD and the function to apply to each partition, computes its partition iterator and returns the function result to the driver.

nodes.name: ResultTask.runTask
nodes.summary: Deserializes the (RDD, function) pair from the broadcast binary while timing the deserialization, then runs func(context, rdd.iterator(partition, context)) and returns its result.

nodes.name: ResultTask.preferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the de-duplicated preferred locations (driver side only) for locality-aware scheduling.

nodes.name: RDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract RDD class, Spark's core abstraction of an immutable, partitioned collection that is computed lazily from its parents, plus the RDD companion object (implicit conversions to pair/double/sequence-file/ordered/async helpers) and the DeterministicLevel enumeration. DataFrames and the PySpark JVM side ultimately execute as RDDs built from this class.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with ClassTag context bound; the companion object holds implicit conversions that add key-value methods (PairRDDFunctions) to RDD[(K, V)].

nodes.name: RDD
nodes.summary: Resilient Distributed Dataset: an immutable, partitioned collection characterized by a list of partitions, a compute function per partition, a list of dependencies on parent RDDs, an optional Partitioner and optional preferred locations. Transformations (map, filter, union, groupBy, ...) only build new RDDs lazily; actions (collect, count, take, reduce, foreach, ...) call sc.runJob and start a Spark job. Its companion object (lines 2164-2207) supplies implicit conversions to PairRDDFunctions and friends.
nodes.languageNotes: Abstract Scala class extending Serializable with Logging; subclasses implement compute and getPartitions (and usually getDependencies).

nodes.name: DeterministicLevel
nodes.summary: Enumeration of how deterministic an RDD's output is across task reruns: DETERMINATE (same data, same order), UNORDERED (same data, order may differ) and INDETERMINATE (data may differ). Used by RDD.outputDeterministicLevel.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Abstract per-partition computation: subclasses return an Iterator over the elements of one Partition, given the TaskContext of the running task. This is where an RDD's data is actually produced, and it only runs inside tasks on executors.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that subclasses implement to return the array of Partitions of the RDD; called once and the result is cached by `partitions`. Partition i must have index i.

nodes.name: getDependencies
nodes.summary: Hook returning how this RDD depends on its parent RDDs; defaults to the `deps` constructor argument. Called once and cached by `dependencies`.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Optional hook for data-locality hints per Partition (for example HDFS block hosts); returns Nil by default.

nodes.name: partitioner
nodes.summary: Transient val holding the optional Partitioner that describes how a key-value RDD is partitioned (for example hash-partitioned); None by default. Operators like distinct and subtract consult it to skip shuffles.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Marks the RDD for caching at a StorageLevel (private overload plus public persist(newLevel) and persist() with MEMORY_ONLY). On first call it registers the RDD with the SparkContext cleaner and persistRDD; changing an existing level throws unless local checkpointing overrides it. Nothing is cached until a job computes the RDD.

nodes.name: cache
nodes.summary: Shorthand for persist() with the default MEMORY_ONLY storage level.

nodes.name: unpersist
nodes.summary: Marks the RDD non-persistent and removes all of its blocks from memory and disk through sc.unpersistRDD, optionally blocking until deletion finishes; warns if the RDD was locally checkpointed because its lineage cannot be recomputed.

nodes.name: dependencies
nodes.summary: Final accessor returning the RDD's dependencies. If the RDD is checkpointed it returns a single OneToOneDependency on the checkpoint RDD; otherwise it lazily calls getDependencies under stateLock and caches the result.

nodes.name: partitions
nodes.summary: Final accessor returning the RDD's Partition array, taken from the checkpoint RDD when checkpointed, otherwise computed once through getPartitions under stateLock. Validates that partition(i).index == i.

nodes.name: preferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns preferred host locations for a partition, delegating to the checkpoint RDD when checkpointed and otherwise to getPreferredLocations.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Entry point used by tasks to read one partition: if the RDD has a storage level it goes through getOrCompute (block manager cache), otherwise computeOrReadCheckpoint. Subclass implementers call it on parents; users should not call it directly.

nodes.name: getNarrowAncestors
nodes.summary: Walks the dependency tree depth-first and returns all ancestors reachable only through NarrowDependency edges (no shuffle). StageInfo.fromStage uses it to find all RDDs that belong to one stage.

nodes.name: computeOrReadCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Computes a partition via compute, or, when the RDD is checkpointed and materialized, reads it from the first parent (the checkpoint RDD).

nodes.name: getOrCompute
nodes.summary: Cache-aware partition read used by iterator when the RDD is persisted: asks the BlockManager for the RDDBlockId block, computes and stores it on a miss, and wraps the result in an InterruptibleIterator while updating input metrics on a cache hit.

nodes.name: map
nodes.summary: Transformation: returns a new RDD built as a MapPartitionsRDD that applies a (closure-cleaned) function to each element. Lazy; no job runs.

nodes.name: flatMap
nodes.summary: Transformation: applies a function to each element and flattens the results, implemented as a MapPartitionsRDD. Lazy.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Transformation: keeps only elements satisfying a predicate, implemented as a MapPartitionsRDD that preserves partitioning. Lazy.

nodes.name: distinct
nodes.summary: Transformation removing duplicates. When the RDD already has a partitioner and the same partition count it dedups within each partition with an ExternalAppendOnlyMap; otherwise it maps to (x, null), runs reduceByKey (a shuffle) and takes the keys.

nodes.name: repartition
nodes.summary: Transformation that changes the number of partitions with a full shuffle; defined as coalesce(numPartitions, shuffle = true).

nodes.name: coalesce
nodes.summary: Transformation that reduces (or, with shuffle = true, changes) the partition count. Without shuffle it builds a CoalescedRDD with narrow dependencies; with shuffle it spreads elements evenly via a ShuffledRDD and HashPartitioner before coalescing.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Transformation returning a sampled subset using a PartitionwiseSampledRDD with a Poisson sampler (with replacement) or Bernoulli sampler (without). The fraction is an expectation, not an exact size.

nodes.name: randomSplit
nodes.summary: Randomly splits the RDD into several RDDs by normalized weights, using Bernoulli cell samplers over probability ranges with a shared seed.

nodes.name: takeSample
nodes.summary: Action returning a fixed-size random sample as a driver-side array. It counts the RDD, then collects either everything or an oversampled fraction, re-sampling if too small; only suitable for small results.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Transformation returning the union (with duplicates) of this RDD and another by delegating to sc.union; `++` is an alias.

nodes.name: sortBy
nodes.summary: Transformation sorting the RDD by a key function: keyBy then sortByKey (a range-partitioned shuffle) then values.

nodes.name: intersection
nodes.summary: Transformation (three overloads) returning elements present in both RDDs, without duplicates; implemented with cogroup and a filter on non-empty groups, so it shuffles.

nodes.name: groupBy
nodes.summary: Transformation (three overloads) that groups elements by a key function into (key, Iterable) pairs via map then groupByKey. Documented as potentially expensive compared with reduceByKey or aggregateByKey.

nodes.name: pipe
nodes.summary: Transformation (three overloads) that pipes each partition's elements through an external process via PipedRDD and returns the process output lines as the new RDD.

nodes.name: mapPartitions
nodes.summary: Transformation applying a function to the whole iterator of each partition, with a flag for whether the partitioner is preserved. Basis for many other operators.

nodes.name: mapPartitionsWithIndex
nodes.summary: Transformation like mapPartitions but the function also receives the partition index. Internal overloads add isOrderSensitive and skip closure cleaning.

nodes.name: zip
nodes.summary: Transformation pairing elements of two RDDs positionally via zipPartitions; requires the same partition count and the same element count per partition.

nodes.name: zipPartitions
nodes.summary: Transformation (six overloads for two to four RDDs) applying a function to the zipped iterators of corresponding partitions using ZippedPartitionsRDD2/3/4; RDDs must have the same number of partitions.

nodes.name: foreach
nodes.summary: Action: applies a function to every element (foreach) or to each partition iterator (foreachPartition) by calling sc.runJob; the work runs on executors and nothing is returned.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Action: runs a job that turns each partition into an array and concatenates all results on the driver. Loads all data into driver memory. (The collect(PartialFunction) overload at lines 1097-1100 is a lazy transformation of filter plus map.)

nodes.name: toLocalIterator
nodes.summary: Action-like method returning a driver-side iterator that runs one job per partition (sc.runJob over a single partition index), so memory use is bounded by the largest partition.

nodes.name: subtract
nodes.summary: Transformation (three overloads) returning elements of this RDD not in another, via subtractByKey on (x, null) pairs; reuses the partitioner when it matches.

nodes.name: reduce
nodes.summary: Action: reduces all elements with a commutative, associative operator by reducing each partition then merging task results on the driver through sc.runJob. Throws on an empty RDD.

nodes.name: treeReduce
