nodes.summary: Action: reduces in a multi-level tree (default depth 2) by partially reducing partitions and calling treeAggregate, reducing driver load for large partition counts.

nodes.name: fold
nodes.summary: Action: folds every partition with a neutral zero value and combines the partial results on the driver via sc.runJob; the zero value is cloned for serialization.

nodes.name: aggregate
nodes.summary: Action: aggregates partitions with seqOp and combines results with combOp starting from a zero value, allowing a result type U different from T; runs via sc.runJob.

nodes.name: treeAggregate
nodes.summary: Action (two overloads): aggregate in a multi-level tree. It repeatedly shrinks the partition count with foldByKey shuffles while it saves wall-clock time, optionally does the final aggregation on one executor, then folds the remainder.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Action returning the number of elements: runs a job that counts each partition with Utils.getIteratorSize and sums the results on the driver.

nodes.name: countApprox
nodes.summary: Action returning a PartialResult count with confidence bounds within a timeout, using sc.runApproximateJob with a CountEvaluator so it may return before all tasks finish.

nodes.name: countByValue
nodes.summary: Action returning a driver-side Map of each distinct value to its count; implemented as map to (value, null) then countByKey. Large result sets should use reduceByKey instead.

nodes.name: take
nodes.summary: Action returning the first num elements. It scans one partition at first, then scales up the number of partitions per iteration (using the RDD_LIMIT config settings and a 1.5x overestimate) with repeated sc.runJob calls on partition subsets until enough rows are found.

nodes.name: first
nodes.summary: Action returning the first element via take(1); throws if the RDD is empty.

nodes.name: takeOrdered
nodes.summary: Action returning the smallest k elements by an implicit Ordering: keeps a bounded top-k per partition and merges them with reduce. top(k) calls it with the reversed ordering.

nodes.name: saveAsTextFile
nodes.summary: Action saving the RDD as text files (optionally compressed) by converting each element to (NullWritable, Text) and calling saveAsHadoopFile; launches a write job.

nodes.name: checkpoint
nodes.summary: Marks the RDD for reliable checkpointing by installing ReliableRDDCheckpointData; requires a checkpoint directory on the SparkContext. The data is only written after the first action completes (doCheckpoint) and parent references are then dropped.

nodes.name: localCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Marks the RDD for local checkpointing on executor storage by persisting it with a disk-capable level and installing LocalRDDCheckpointData; truncates lineage but is not fault-tolerant and is unsafe with dynamic allocation.

nodes.name: cleanShuffleDependencies
nodes.summary: Developer API that walks the dependency chain through the context cleaner and eagerly deletes shuffle files of ShuffleDependency edges (stopping at persisted RDDs), to help downscaling without a shuffle service.

nodes.name: barrier
nodes.summary: Experimental: returns an RDDBarrier wrapper so the following stage runs in barrier execution mode, launching all tasks together and restarting the whole stage on failure.

nodes.name: doCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Internal step run after a job using this RDD completes: if the RDD was marked for checkpointing it writes the checkpoint (parents first when checkpointAllMarkedAncestors is set), otherwise it recurses into parent RDDs. Guarded to run once.

nodes.name: markCheckpointed
nodes.summary: Switches the RDD from its original parents to the checkpoint RDD: keeps a weak reference to the old dependencies, clears them and the cached partitions.

nodes.name: toDebugString
nodes.summary: Builds the multi-line lineage string shown by RDD.toDebugString: partition count, RDD description, storage info and recursively the parents, with indentation marking shuffle boundaries.

nodes.name: rddToPairRDDFunctions
nodes.summary: Group node for the six implicit conversions in the RDD companion object (rddToPairRDDFunctions, rddToAsyncRDDActions, rddToSequenceFileRDDFunctions, rddToOrderedRDDFunctions, doubleRDDToDoubleRDDFunctions, numericRDDToDoubleRDDFunctions). They are why RDD[(K, V)] gains reduceByKey/join/groupByKey, RDD[Double] gains stats helpers, and sortByKey is available.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala implicit defs enabling methods that are not defined on RDD itself; the compiler applies them automatically.

nodes.name: SparkContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkContext, the entry point of core Spark on the driver JVM: it connects to a cluster and creates RDDs, accumulators and broadcast variables. Its constructor builds SparkEnv, UI, task scheduler with scheduler backend and DAGScheduler, and every RDD action funnels through SparkContext.runJob into DAGScheduler.runJob. The file also holds the companion object (single active context, getOrCreate, master URL to scheduler mapping), the SparkMasterRegex patterns and the WritableConverter and WritableFactory implicit helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with a large constructor-body initialization block plus a companion object; overloaded methods (runJob, hadoopFile, addFile, stop) share one function node id each.

nodes.name: SparkContext
nodes.summary: Main entry point for Spark functionality: represents the connection to a Spark cluster and creates RDDs, accumulators and broadcast variables. Only one SparkContext may be active per JVM. Its constructor creates the driver SparkEnv, UI, listener bus, a TaskScheduler plus SchedulerBackend (via createTaskScheduler) and a DAGScheduler; RDD actions call runJob, which hands the work to dagScheduler.runJob, and submitMapStage lets the SQL shuffle submit a map stage alone. The companion object (lines 2993 to 3453) shares this id and owns getOrCreate, the active-context guard and createTaskScheduler.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share this id; line range covers the class body, the object spans 2993-3453.

nodes.name: SparkMasterRegex
nodes.summary: Private object of regexes that parse master URLs: local[N] and local[*], local[N, maxRetries], local-cluster[N, cores, memory], spark://host:port and k8s://. Includes isK8s helper. Used by createTaskScheduler, numDriverCores and the constructor.

nodes.name: WritableConverter
nodes.summary: Serializable pair of a Writable class and a conversion function that turns a Hadoop Writable into a Scala type T. The companion object provides implicit converters for Int, Long, Double, Float, Boolean, Array[Byte], String and any Writable subclass, used by SparkContext.sequenceFile.
nodes.languageNotes: Implicit functions are provided instead of implicit objects because a parameterized singleton cannot exist; zero-arg function forms are also kept for Scala 2.12 compatibility.

nodes.name: WritableFactory
nodes.summary: Serializable pair of a Writable class and a function that converts a Scala value of type T to a Writable, with implicit factories for Int, Long, Float, Double, Boolean, Array[Byte], String and Writable subclasses. Used by SequenceFileRDDFunctions.

nodes.name: assertNotStopped
nodes.summary: Throws IllegalStateException with the creation site, stop site and currently active context site when the context has already been stopped. Called at the start of many public methods (parallelize, broadcast, submitJob, cancel*) so a stopped SparkContext fails fast.

nodes.name: createSparkEnv
nodes.summary: Wraps SparkEnv.createDriverEnv with the driver core count from SparkContext.numDriverCores. It is a separate method so that components created by SparkEnv can be mocked in unit tests.

nodes.name: setLogLevel
nodes.summary: Validates a log level string against VALID_LOG_LEVELS, applies it on the driver and, when EXECUTOR_ALLOW_SYNC_LOG_LEVEL is on and a scheduler backend exists, pushes the level to executors through updateExecutorsLogLevel.

nodes.name: initialization
nodes.summary: The constructor body (one try/catch block) that boots the driver. In order: clone the SparkConf and validate master and app name, create LiveListenerBus, AppStatusStore, SparkEnv, SparkStatusTracker, the console progress bar and SparkUI, add initial jars/files/archives, register the HeartbeatReceiver endpoint, create plugins and ResourceProfileManager, call createTaskScheduler, build the DAGScheduler, start the driver Heartbeater and the TaskScheduler, read the application id, then start the ContextCleaner, ExecutorAllocationManager, listener bus and metrics sources. Any NonFatal error calls stop() and rethrows.

nodes.name: getExecutorThreadDump
nodes.summary: Called by the web UI to fetch an executor thread dump: returns the local thread dump for the driver, otherwise asks the executor endpoint ref obtained from the block manager master with a TriggerThreadDump message. Logs and returns None if the executor is gone or the request fails.

nodes.name: setLocalProperty
nodes.summary: Sets (or removes when the value is null) a key in the thread-local, inheritable localProperties. These properties, such as the fair scheduler pool or the job group id, are passed to the DAGScheduler with each job submitted from this thread and propagate to tasks.

nodes.name: setJobGroup
nodes.summary: Assigns a group id, description and interruptOnCancel flag to all jobs started by the current thread by writing thread-local properties. The group can later be cancelled with cancelJobGroup, and the Spark UI associates jobs with it.

nodes.name: addJobTags
nodes.summary: Validates each tag with SparkContext.throwIfInvalidTag and merges them into the comma-separated spark.job.tags thread-local property so jobs started by this thread can later be cancelled by tag.

nodes.name: parallelize
nodes.summary: Distributes a local Scala collection into a ParallelCollectionRDD, using defaultParallelism as the default number of slices. It is lazy: the collection is only read when the first action runs.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Builds an RDD[Long] from start to end (exclusive) with a step by parallelizing partition indices and generating each partition's numbers with an overflow-safe iterator based on BigInt bounds.

nodes.name: textFile
nodes.summary: Reads a text file from HDFS, a local file system or any Hadoop-supported URI as an RDD of UTF-8 lines. Implemented as hadoopFile with TextInputFormat, mapped to the line string and named after the path.

nodes.name: wholeTextFiles
nodes.summary: Reads a directory of text files as an RDD of (path, content) pairs, one record per file, using WholeTextFileRDD with WholeTextFileInputFormat.

nodes.name: binaryFiles
nodes.summary: Reads a Hadoop-readable dataset as an RDD of (path, PortableDataStream), one record per file, using BinaryFileRDD with StreamInputFormat. Useful for binary data.

nodes.name: binaryRecords
nodes.summary: Loads a flat binary file as an RDD of fixed-length byte arrays by configuring FixedLengthBinaryInputFormat through newAPIHadoopFile and asserting each record has the requested length.

nodes.name: hadoopRDD
nodes.summary: Creates a HadoopRDD from a JobConf using the old org.apache.hadoop.mapred API, after forcing hdfs-site.xml to load and adding security credentials to the JobConf.

nodes.name: hadoopFile
nodes.summary: Core overload that creates a HadoopRDD for a path with an arbitrary InputFormat. It broadcasts the SerializableConfiguration (a Hadoop conf is about 10 KiB) and passes a function that sets the input paths. textFile, sequenceFile and the class-tag overloads delegate here.

nodes.name: newAPIHadoopFile
nodes.summary: Creates a NewHadoopRDD for a path with an arbitrary new-API (org.apache.hadoop.mapreduce) InputFormat. It builds a Hadoop Job so security credentials and input paths are set on the configuration. Overloads using class tags forward here.

nodes.name: newAPIHadoopRDD
nodes.summary: Creates a NewHadoopRDD from an arbitrary Hadoop Configuration using the new MapReduce API, adding credentials to a JobConf copy so secure HDFS can be read.

nodes.name: sequenceFile
nodes.summary: Reads a Hadoop SequenceFile into an RDD whose key and value types are converted from Writable through implicit WritableConverter functions (for example String from Text, Int from IntWritable). Other overloads take explicit key and value classes and forward to hadoopFile.

nodes.name: objectFile
nodes.summary: Loads an RDD previously saved as a SequenceFile of NullWritable keys and BytesWritable values containing serialized partitions, and deserializes each value into an Array[T]. The docs mark this storage format as experimental.

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Builds the union of the non-empty RDDs: a PartitionerAwareUnionRDD when all inputs share one partitioner, otherwise a UnionRDD.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers an AccumulatorV2 with this context. Accumulators must be registered before use. longAccumulator, doubleAccumulator and collectionAccumulator each create the accumulator and call register.

nodes.name: longAccumulator
nodes.summary: Creates a LongAccumulator starting at 0, registers it with the context and returns it. The named overload and the double and collection accumulator variants follow the same create-then-register pattern.

nodes.name: broadcast
nodes.summary: Broadcasts a read-only value to the cluster and returns a Broadcast handle; the value is sent to each executor only once. Delegates to broadcastInternal with serializedOnly set to false.

nodes.name: broadcastInternal
nodes.summary: Creates the broadcast through env.broadcastManager.newBroadcast after refusing to broadcast an RDD directly, logs the call site and registers the broadcast with the ContextCleaner for later cleanup.

nodes.name: addFile
nodes.summary: Private implementation behind addFile and addArchive (the public addFile(path) and addFile(path, recursive) overloads sit at lines 1758 and 1810). Resolves the URI, validates directories and URLs, registers the file with the RPC env file server when not local, records it with a timestamp in addedFiles or addedArchives keyed by job artifact session id, fetches or unpacks it locally on the driver, and posts an environment update. Duplicate paths are ignored with a warning.

nodes.name: addSparkListener
nodes.summary: Registers a SparkListenerInterface on the shared queue of the LiveListenerBus so it receives scheduler and application events.

nodes.name: maxNumConcurrentTasks
nodes.summary: Asks the SchedulerBackend how many tasks can run concurrently for a ResourceProfile, even if some slots are currently busy.

nodes.name: requestTotalExecutors
nodes.summary: Tells the cluster manager the total number of executors wanted for the default ResourceProfile, with locality hints. Works only when the scheduler backend implements ExecutorAllocationClient, otherwise logs a warning and returns false.

nodes.name: killExecutors
nodes.summary: Asks the cluster manager to kill the given executors; requires that the executor allocation manager is absent (dynamic allocation off). Falls back to a warning and false when the scheduler backend is not an ExecutorAllocationClient.

nodes.name: getExecutorMemoryStatus
nodes.summary: Returns a map from block manager host:port to the maximum and remaining memory available for caching, read from the block manager master.

nodes.name: getRDDStorageInfo
nodes.summary: Builds RDDInfo records for the persistent RDDs that pass a filter, fills cached partition count, memory size and disk size from the status store, and returns only those that are cached. The public no-argument overload passes a filter that accepts every RDD.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocs
nodes.summary: Returns the preferred task locations for a partition of an RDD by delegating to DAGScheduler.getPreferredLocs.

nodes.name: persistRDD
nodes.summary: Records an RDD in the persistentRdds weak-valued map so getPersistentRDDs and getRDDStorageInfo can see which RDDs were marked persistent.

nodes.name: addJar
nodes.summary: Private implementation of addJar (the public addJar(path) is at line 2175). Handles local files (served by the RPC file server), local: URIs, ivy: URIs (resolved to Maven dependency jars) and remote schemes, rejects directories, records new jars with a timestamp in addedJars per job artifact session, and posts an environment update. Re-adding a path only logs a warning.

nodes.name: stopInNewThread
nodes.summary: Stops the SparkContext from a daemon thread named stop-spark-context. Spark components use it instead of calling stop() directly because stopping from inside Spark may deadlock while waiting on internal threads.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts the context down exactly once (compareAndSet on stopped). Posts the application end event, then stops the driver logger, UI, ContextCleaner, ExecutorAllocationManager, DAGScheduler, plugins, listener bus, metrics, event logger, shuffle driver components, heartbeater, heartbeat receiver, progress bar and SparkEnv, and finally clears local properties and the active context. The no-argument stop() at line 2308 calls stop(0).

nodes.name: getCallSite
nodes.summary: Returns the user call site for the current action or RDD, preferring the thread-local short and long forms set with setCallSite and falling back to Utils.getCallSite().

nodes.name: runJob
nodes.summary: Central runJob overload and, per its doc comment, the main entry point for all actions in Spark. It checks the context is not stopped, cleans the function closure, optionally logs the RDD lineage (spark.logLineage), then calls dagScheduler.runJob with the RDD, partitions, call site, result handler and the thread-local properties, finishes the progress bar and runs rdd.doCheckpoint(). The other runJob overloads (all partitions, array results, Iterator-only functions, lines 2512 to 2592) build on this one.

nodes.name: runApproximateJob
nodes.summary: Runs a job that may return partial results by calling dagScheduler.runApproximateJob with an ApproximateEvaluator and a timeout, logging the elapsed time.

nodes.name: submitJob
nodes.summary: Submits a job asynchronously: cleans the partition function, calls dagScheduler.submitJob to obtain a waiter, and wraps it in a SimpleFutureAction that yields resultFunc when the job is done.

nodes.name: submitMapStage
nodes.summary: Internal API that submits only the map stage of a ShuffleDependency through dagScheduler.submitMapStage and returns a SimpleFutureAction[MapOutputStatistics]. The SQL shuffle exchange uses it to obtain map output statistics (mapOutputStatisticsFuture).

nodes.name: cancelJobGroup
nodes.summary: Cancels the active jobs of a job group (set with setJobGroup) by calling dagScheduler.cancelJobGroup. An overload at line 2680 adds a reason, and cancelJobGroupAndFutureJobs also cancels future jobs of the group.

nodes.name: cancelJob
nodes.summary: Cancels a scheduled or running job by id, forwarding the optional reason to dagScheduler.cancelJob. cancelStage, cancelAllJobs and cancelJobsWithTag are similar thin wrappers around the DAGScheduler.

nodes.name: clean
nodes.summary: Cleans a closure through SparkClosureCleaner so it can be serialized and sent to tasks, optionally checking serializability up front.

nodes.name: setCheckpointDir
nodes.summary: Sets the base directory for RDD checkpoints by creating a UUID-named subdirectory on the file system. Logs a warning when running on a cluster with a directory that looks local.

nodes.name: defaultParallelism
nodes.summary: Returns the default level of parallelism used when the user does not give one, such as in parallelize and makeRDD. Asserts the context is running and asks taskScheduler.defaultParallelism().

nodes.name: defaultMinPartitions
nodes.summary: Default minimum number of partitions for Hadoop RDDs: math.min(defaultParallelism, 2).

nodes.name: setupAndStartListenerBus
nodes.summary: Instantiates the listeners named in spark.extraListeners, adds them to the shared queue and then starts the LiveListenerBus. Called near the end of initialization, after the internal UI and event log listeners are registered.

nodes.name: postApplicationStart
nodes.summary: Posts SparkListenerApplicationStart with app name, application id, start time, user and driver log URLs, then starts the driver log sync.

nodes.name: postApplicationEnd
nodes.summary: Reports one final driver heartbeat and posts SparkListenerApplicationEnd with the exit code. Called by stop().

nodes.name: postEnvironmentUpdate
nodes.summary: Posts SparkListenerEnvironmentUpdate with SparkEnv.environmentDetails (conf, scheduling mode, added jars, files and archives) once the task scheduler exists. Called after addFile, addJar and during startup.

nodes.name: reportHeartBeat
nodes.summary: Heartbeat callback of the driver Heartbeater: reads the current driver metrics with ExecutorMetrics.getCurrentMetrics, updates the metrics source and posts SparkListenerExecutorMetricsUpdate for the driver with a dummy stage key.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: Companion-object factory that returns the active SparkContext, creating one from the given SparkConf only when none exists. Under SPARK_CONTEXT_CONSTRUCTOR_LOCK it logs a warning if an existing context is reused with a non-empty config. A no-argument overload at line 3094 returns or creates a context from system properties.

nodes.name: assertNoOtherContextIsRunning
nodes.summary: Throws SparkException if a different SparkContext is already active in this JVM (see SPARK-2243) and logs a warning if another one is still being constructed.

nodes.name: markPartiallyConstructed
nodes.summary: Called at the start of the SparkContext constructor to verify no other context is running and to record this one as being constructed.

nodes.name: setActiveContext
nodes.summary: Called at the end of the constructor and by getOrCreate: re-checks that no other context raced in, clears the being-constructed marker and stores the context in the activeContext AtomicReference.

nodes.name: clearActiveContext
nodes.summary: Sets the active context reference to null; called by SparkContext.stop() and by unit tests.

nodes.name: throwIfInvalidTag
nodes.summary: Rejects job tags that are null, contain the comma separator or are empty, with IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: updatedConf
nodes.summary: Clones a SparkConf and applies the master, app name, optional Spark home, jars and executor environment passed to the convenience constructors.

nodes.name: numDriverCores
nodes.summary: Computes how many cores the driver can use from the master string: 1 for local, N or all processors for local[N] and local[*], the configured driver cores for YARN or k8s cluster mode, otherwise 0.

nodes.name: executorMemoryInMb
nodes.summary: Resolves executor memory in MiB from spark.executor.memory, SPARK_EXECUTOR_MEMORY or the deprecated SPARK_MEM, defaulting to 1024.

nodes.name: createTaskScheduler
nodes.summary: Maps the master URL to a (SchedulerBackend, TaskScheduler) pair. local, local[N], local[*] and local[N, M] build a TaskSchedulerImpl with a LocalSchedulerBackend; spark://host:port builds a TaskSchedulerImpl with a StandaloneSchedulerBackend; local-cluster[N,cores,mem] also starts a LocalSparkCluster; any other URL (such as yarn or k8s://) is resolved through ServiceLoader to an ExternalClusterManager that supplies the scheduler and backend. Called from the constructor right before the DAGScheduler is created.

nodes.name: getClusterManager
nodes.summary: Uses ServiceLoader to find the single ExternalClusterManager whose canCreate accepts the master URL; throws if more than one matches.

nodes.name: enableMagicCommitterIfNeeded
nodes.summary: When the hadoop-cloud committer classes are on the classpath, sets default S3A magic committer options in the SparkConf if they are missing.

nodes.name: Dependency.scala
nodes.summary: Defines how a child RDD depends on a parent RDD. Narrow dependencies (OneToOneDependency, RangeDependency) let partitions be pipelined inside one stage, while ShuffleDependency marks a shuffle and is where the DAGScheduler cuts a job into stages.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file mixing an abstract hierarchy with a companion object (ShuffleDependency) that only holds an empty row-based-checksum constant.

nodes.name: Dependency
nodes.summary: Abstract, serializable base class for an RDD dependency; the only requirement is `rdd`, the parent RDD this dependency points to. PySpark users see these edges as the lineage printed by `rdd.toDebugString()`.

nodes.name: NarrowDependency
nodes.summary: Dependency where each child partition reads only a small, known set of parent partitions (via getParents), so no data movement is needed and the work can be pipelined in a single stage.

nodes.name: NarrowDependency.getParents
nodes.summary: Abstract method that maps a child partition id to the parent partition ids it depends on.

nodes.name: ShuffleDependency
nodes.summary: Represents a dependency on the output of a shuffle stage, i.e. a wide dependency and the stage boundary. Holds the partitioner, serializer, optional key ordering and aggregator, mapSideCombine flag and ShuffleWriteProcessor; on construction it allocates a shuffleId from the SparkContext, registers a shuffleHandle with the ShuffleManager, tracks push-based shuffle merge state and registers itself for cleanup. The companion object only defines an empty row-based checksum array.

nodes.name: ShuffleDependency.shuffleId
nodes.summary: Unique id of this shuffle, obtained from `_rdd.context.newShuffleId()`; it is the key the MapOutputTracker uses to store and look up map outputs.

nodes.name: ShuffleDependency.shuffleHandle
nodes.summary: ShuffleHandle returned by registering this dependency with the ShuffleManager; the handle tells the shuffle writers and readers which implementation to use.

nodes.name: ShuffleDependency.setMergerLocs
nodes.summary: Stores the block manager locations of the chosen external shuffle services that will merge pushed blocks; asserts that shuffle merge is allowed.

nodes.name: ShuffleDependency.shuffleMergeFinalized
nodes.summary: Returns true if push-based shuffle is disabled for this dependency or its shuffle merge has been marked finalized.

nodes.name: ShuffleDependency.newShuffleMergeState
nodes.summary: Resets merge state for a new stage attempt: clears the finalized flag, merger locations, the finalize task and the push-completed bitmap, and increments shuffleMergeId.

nodes.name: ShuffleDependency.canShuffleMergeBeEnabled
nodes.summary: Checks whether push-based shuffle is enabled on the driver, there is at least one partition and the RDD is not a barrier stage (barrier stages log a warning and are unsupported).

nodes.name: ShuffleDependency.incPushCompleted
nodes.summary: Marks a map task as push-completed in a RoaringBitmap so speculative or retried copies of the same map task are counted once, and returns the count of completed map tasks.

nodes.name: OneToOneDependency
nodes.summary: Narrow dependency where child partition i depends exactly on parent partition i; used by map-style transformations such as `map` and `filter`.

nodes.name: OneToOneDependency.getParents
nodes.summary: Returns a list containing only the same partition id.

nodes.name: RangeDependency
nodes.summary: Narrow dependency mapping a contiguous range of child partitions onto a range of parent partitions (inStart, outStart, length), the kind of dependency a union of RDDs uses.

nodes.name: RangeDependency.getParents
nodes.summary: Returns the single shifted parent partition id when the child partition lies in [outStart, outStart + length), otherwise Nil.

nodes.name: TaskContext.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the TaskContext that a running task can read and mutate (stage, partition, attempt ids, local properties, resources, metrics, completion/failure/interrupt listeners) and its companion object that keeps the active context in a ThreadLocal. In PySpark, `pyspark.TaskContext` mirrors this object.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala companion object plus abstract class; the companion holds the thread-local, and the abstract class declares most members for TaskContextImpl to implement.

nodes.name: TaskContext
nodes.summary: Abstract, serializable per-task context. Exposes stageId, stageAttemptNumber, partitionId, numPartitions, attemptNumber, taskAttemptId, getLocalProperty, cpus/resources, taskMetrics and metrics sources, lets code register completion, failure and interrupt listeners, and drives runTaskWithListeners. The companion object (lines 33-83) provides the static `TaskContext.get()` plus thread-local set/unset helpers.

nodes.name: TaskContext.get
nodes.summary: Companion method returning the TaskContext active on the current thread (null outside a task); this is what user functions call to learn about the running task.

nodes.name: TaskContext.getPartitionId
nodes.summary: Returns the active context's partition id, or 0 when no TaskContext is active (for example local execution).

nodes.name: TaskContext.withTaskContext
nodes.summary: Runs a block with the given context installed as the thread-local TaskContext and always unsets it in a finally.

nodes.name: TaskContext.setTaskContext
nodes.summary: Sets the thread-local TaskContext; internal to Spark (protected[spark]).

nodes.name: TaskContext.unset
nodes.summary: Removes the thread-local TaskContext; internal to Spark.

nodes.name: TaskContext.empty
nodes.summary: Builds an empty TaskContextImpl that does not represent a real task; only used in tests.

nodes.name: TaskContext.isCompleted
nodes.summary: Returns true once the task has completed; sibling methods isFailed and isInterrupted report failure and kill state.

nodes.name: TaskContext.addTaskCompletionListener
nodes.summary: Registers a callback (a TaskCompletionListener, or a Scala closure overload) that runs on success, failure or cancellation; registering on an already completed task calls it immediately. Typical use: closing an input stream.

nodes.name: TaskContext.addTaskFailureListener
nodes.summary: Registers a callback that runs when the task fails (including completion listener failure); the closure overload wraps it in a TaskFailureListener.

nodes.name: TaskContext.addTaskInterruptListener
nodes.summary: Registers a callback invoked when the task is interrupted, with the kill reason; the closure overload wraps it in a TaskInterruptListener.

nodes.name: TaskContext.runTaskWithListeners
nodes.summary: Checks for a pending kill, runs task.runTask(this), and on any Throwable marks the task failed and completed (collecting suppressed errors) before rethrowing; a finally block always calls markTaskCompleted so listeners fire exactly once.

nodes.name: TaskContext.stageId
nodes.summary: The id of the stage this task belongs to.

nodes.name: TaskContext.partitionId
nodes.summary: The id of the RDD partition computed by this task.

nodes.name: TaskContext.attemptNumber
nodes.summary: How many times this task has been attempted; the first attempt is 0.

nodes.name: TaskContext.taskAttemptId
nodes.summary: An id unique to this task attempt within the SparkContext, roughly equivalent to Hadoop's TaskAttemptID.

nodes.name: TaskContext.getLocalProperty
nodes.summary: Returns a local property set upstream on the driver (via SparkContext.setLocalProperty), or null if missing.

nodes.name: TaskContext.resources
nodes.summary: Returns the resources (for example GPUs) allocated to this task as a map from resource name to ResourceInformation.

nodes.name: TaskContext.taskMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns the TaskMetrics object for this task (developer API).

nodes.name: TaskContext.createResourceUninterruptibly
nodes.summary: Creates a closeable resource while the task is not allowed to be interrupted; pending interrupts are deferred until creation finishes.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Driver and executor bookkeeping of where every shuffle map output lives. The driver-side MapOutputTrackerMaster stores a ShuffleStatus per shuffle and answers executors' requests over RPC; executor-side MapOutputTrackerWorker fetches and caches the serialized statuses so reduce tasks know which block managers hold their input blocks.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a private ShuffleStatus helper, sealed message traits, abstract base class, driver and executor subclasses and a companion object of serialization helpers.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus
nodes.summary: Private driver-side bookkeeping for a single shuffle: an array of MapStatus per map index (plus deleted copies for recovery and checksum mismatch detection), push-based MergeStatus per reducer, and cached compressed serialized forms (possibly via Broadcast). All access is guarded by a read/write lock.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.addMapOutput
nodes.summary: Registers or replaces the MapStatus for a map index, updates the available-output counter, invalidates the serialized cache when a new output appears and returns true if the new checksum differs from the previous one.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.updateMapOutput
nodes.summary: Updates the location of a map output by mapId (for example after block migration), or restores a previously deleted status if it is still recoverable; invalidates the cache.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.removeMapOutput
nodes.summary: Removes a map output only if it was served by the given block manager, keeping a copy in mapStatusesDeleted and invalidating the cache.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.addMergeResult
nodes.summary: Registers the MergeStatus for a reduce partition (push-based shuffle) and invalidates the serialized merge cache when it changes.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.removeOutputsByFilter
nodes.summary: Removes every map output whose block manager matches a predicate, saving the deleted statuses and invalidating the cache; used for host and executor loss.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.findMissingPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the map partition ids that have no output, asserting the count matches the available-output counter.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.serializedMapStatus
nodes.summary: Returns the cached compressed serialized MapStatus array, computing it under the write lock on first use (double-checked) via MapOutputTracker.serializeOutputStatuses.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.serializedMapAndMergeStatus
nodes.summary: Returns the serialized map statuses together with the serialized merge statuses, populating the merge cache lazily under the write lock.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatus.invalidateSerializedMapOutputStatusCache
nodes.summary: Destroys the cached broadcast of serialized statuses (swallowing non-fatal errors per SPARK-21444) and clears the cached bytes so the next request reserializes.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMessage
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for RPC requests sent from executors to the driver endpoint, grouped with its case classes GetMapOutputStatuses, GetMapAndMergeResultStatuses, GetShufflePushMergerLocations and StopMapOutputTracker.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMasterMessage
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for messages queued inside the driver for the message loops, grouped with GetMapOutputMessage, GetMapAndMergeOutputMessage and GetShufflePushMergersMessage, each carrying the shuffleId and an RpcCallContext to reply on.

nodes.name: MapSizesByExecutorId
nodes.summary: Case class result of a block lookup: an iterator of (BlockManagerId, sequence of (BlockId, size, map index)) plus an enableBatchFetch flag.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMasterEndpoint
nodes.summary: RpcEndpoint living on the driver that receives executors' map output, map/merge and push merger location requests and posts them to the tracker's message queue so a separate thread pool does the work; it also handles StopMapOutputTracker.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMasterEndpoint.receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Pattern matches each request message, logs the requesting host and forwards a corresponding GetMapOutputMessage-style message to MapOutputTrackerMaster.post; replies true and stops on StopMapOutputTracker.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker
nodes.summary: Abstract base class that keeps track of the location of each stage's map output. Declares what executors call (getMapSizesByExecutorId, getPushBasedShuffleMapSizesByExecutorId, getMapSizesForMergeResult, getShufflePushMergerLocations, unregisterShuffle), holds the trackerEndpoint ref and the epoch counter, and provides askTracker/sendTracker. The companion object (lines 1542-1784) holds serialization and status-conversion helpers.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.askTracker
nodes.summary: Sends a synchronous message to the trackerEndpoint and wraps any failure in a SparkException.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.getMapSizesByExecutorId
nodes.summary: Abstract method used by reduce tasks to get, per block manager, the shuffle blocks (id, size, map index) for a range of map outputs and reduce partitions; empty blocks are excluded.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.getPushBasedShuffleMapSizesByExecutorId
nodes.summary: Abstract variant of the block lookup used when push-based shuffle is enabled; returns MapSizesByExecutorId including whether batch fetch is allowed.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster
nodes.summary: Driver-side tracker. The DAGScheduler registers and unregisters map outputs and asks for statistics here, and ShuffleMapStage uses it to count available and missing outputs. It owns a map of shuffleId to ShuffleStatus, a queue plus 'map-output-dispatcher' thread pool (MessageLoop) answering executor requests, the epoch counter, locality calculations, and serves lookups directly in local mode.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.post
nodes.summary: Enqueues a MapOutputTrackerMasterMessage for the dispatcher threads.

nodes.name: MessageLoop
nodes.summary: Private Runnable inside MapOutputTrackerMaster that takes messages from the queue and replies with serialized map (and merge) statuses or push merger locations; a poison pill message stops all loops.

nodes.name: MessageLoop.handleStatusMessage
nodes.summary: Looks up the ShuffleStatus for the shuffle and replies on the RpcCallContext with its serialized map statuses, or map plus merge statuses when requested.

nodes.name: MessageLoop.run
nodes.summary: Loops taking messages from the queue, dispatching on message type, logging non-fatal errors, and exiting on the poison pill or an interrupt.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.registerShuffle
nodes.summary: Creates a ShuffleStatus for a shuffle id (sized for reducers too when push-based shuffle is on) and fails if the id is already registered; the DAGScheduler calls it when creating a ShuffleMapStage.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.updateMapOutput
nodes.summary: Delegates a map output location update (for example during decommission migration) to the shuffle's ShuffleStatus, logging if the shuffle is unknown.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.registerMapOutput
nodes.summary: Registers a finished map task's MapStatus for a shuffle and map index; returns whether the checksum mismatched a previous attempt.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.unregisterMapOutput
nodes.summary: Removes one map output for a given block manager and increments the epoch so executors drop cached statuses.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.unregisterAllMapAndMergeOutput
nodes.summary: Removes all map outputs, merge results and merger locations for a shuffle and increments the epoch.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.unregisterShuffle
nodes.summary: Removes the shuffle's ShuffleStatus and invalidates its serialized caches.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.removeOutputsOnExecutor
nodes.summary: Removes outputs of every shuffle that were served by the given executor id and increments the epoch.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.getNumAvailableOutputs
nodes.summary: Number of map partitions with registered output for a shuffle (0 if unknown); used by ShuffleMapStage.numAvailableOutputs.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.findMissingPartitions
nodes.summary: Returns the missing map partition ids for a shuffle, or None if the shuffle is not tracked.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.getStatistics
nodes.summary: Sums the size of each reduce partition over all map statuses, in parallel on a temporary thread pool for large jobs, and returns a MapOutputStatistics; used for adaptive query execution and map stage jobs.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.getPreferredLocationsForShuffle
nodes.summary: Computes preferred hosts for a reduce partition: the merged-block location when push-based merge ratio is high enough, otherwise hosts holding a large fraction of its map output, within job-size thresholds.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.getLocationsWithLargestOutputs
nodes.summary: Adds up block sizes per block manager for one reducer and returns those holding at least a fraction threshold of the total.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.incrementEpoch
nodes.summary: Increments the driver epoch under a lock; tasks carry the epoch so executors can invalidate cached statuses.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.getEpoch
nodes.summary: Returns the current epoch under the epoch lock.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.getMapSizesByExecutorId
nodes.summary: Local-mode implementation: delegates to the push-based variant and asserts batch fetch is enabled.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.getPushBasedShuffleMapSizesByExecutorId
nodes.summary: Local-mode lookup that converts the shuffle's map statuses into block locations via MapOutputTracker.convertMapStatuses, or an empty result if the shuffle is unknown.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerMaster.stop
nodes.summary: Puts a poison pill on the queue, shuts down the thread pool, tells the endpoint to stop and clears all shuffle statuses.

nodes.name: ShuffleStatusNotFoundException
nodes.summary: SparkException thrown when a method such as registerMapOutput is called for a shuffle id that is not registered.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerWorker
nodes.summary: Executor-side client. It caches map and merge statuses per shuffle, fetches them from the driver endpoint on a miss (one thread per shuffle id via a KeyLock), deserializes them, and clears the caches on a metadata fetch failure or when a newer epoch arrives with a task. Not used in local mode.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerWorker.getMapSizesByExecutorIdImpl
nodes.summary: Fetches statuses (with merge results if requested) and converts them into block locations; on MetadataFetchFailedException clears local caches and rethrows.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerWorker.getMapSizesForMergeResult
nodes.summary: Two overloads that fall back from a failed merged shuffle partition (or partition chunk) to the original unmerged blocks, clearing caches on fetch failure.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerWorker.getStatuses
nodes.summary: Returns cached map (and merge) statuses for a shuffle or, on a miss, asks the driver, deserializes the reply and caches it, using a per-shuffle lock so only one thread fetches.

nodes.name: MapOutputTrackerWorker.updateEpoch
nodes.summary: If the given epoch is newer, adopts it and clears cached map statuses, merge statuses and merger locations; the Executor calls it with each task's epoch.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.serializeOutputStatuses
nodes.summary: Serializes a status array through a compression codec into a tagged byte array (DIRECT), and if it is larger than minBroadcastSize broadcasts the bytes and returns a small BROADCAST-tagged array instead.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.deserializeOutputStatuses
nodes.summary: Inverse of serializeOutputStatuses: reads the tag byte and decodes either the direct payload or the broadcast contents, wrapping IO errors in SparkException.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.convertMapStatuses
nodes.summary: Turns map statuses (and optional merge statuses) into per-block-manager lists of shuffle blocks, sizes and map indexes, skipping empty blocks, preferring merged blocks and disabling batch fetch when merged blocks are used.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.getMapStatusesForMergeStatus
nodes.summary: Given a bitmap of map indexes belonging to a merged partition or chunk, returns the original block locations and sizes so a failed merged fetch can fall back to unmerged blocks.

nodes.name: MapOutputTracker.validateStatus
nodes.summary: Throws MetadataFetchFailedException (after logging) if a status is null, meaning no output location exists for that shuffle partition.

nodes.name: StageInfo.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StageInfo, the plain data holder that the DAGScheduler hands to SparkListeners and the UI to describe a stage attempt, and its companion fromStage factory. A stage groups the RDDs reachable through narrow dependencies, and StageInfo records them as RDDInfo entries.

nodes.name: StageInfo
nodes.summary: Developer API class storing stage id, attempt id, name, task count, the RDDInfos in the stage, parent stage ids, task metrics, locality preferences, shuffle id and resource profile id, plus mutable submission/completion times, failure reason and accumulables. Its companion object (lines 88-125) builds instances from a Stage.

nodes.name: getStatusString
nodes.summary: Returns "running" until completionTime is set, then "failed" if a failure reason exists, otherwise "succeeded".

nodes.name: fromStage
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds a StageInfo from a Stage: it collects the stage RDD and its narrow ancestors (stage.rdd.getNarrowAncestors) as RDDInfos, takes the shuffle id for a ShuffleMapStage, and copies id, name, task count, parent ids and details.

nodes.name: ShuffleWriteProcessor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShuffleWriteProcessor, the pluggable object that drives the map-side shuffle write for one partition in a ShuffleMapTask. The driver puts it into the ShuffleDependency and executors call it from each task.

nodes.name: ShuffleWriteProcessor
nodes.summary: Serializable helper that gets a ShuffleWriter from the ShuffleManager, writes a partition's records, stops the writer and returns the MapStatus; it also learns merger locations and starts push-based shuffle block pushing when enabled.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one map task's records: obtains a writer via SparkEnv.get.shuffleManager.getWriter with the dependency's shuffleHandle, writes the records, and stops it with success to get the MapStatus. If push-based shuffle is allowed it updates merger locations from the MapOutputTracker and initiates block push for an IndexShuffleBlockResolver; on any exception it stops the writer with success = false and rethrows.

nodes.name: EventLoop.scala
nodes.summary: Defines EventLoop, a small abstract queue-plus-daemon-thread helper: callers post events and a single dedicated thread dispatches them one at a time to onReceive. The DAGScheduler uses it as the single-threaded event loop for its scheduling decisions.

nodes.name: EventLoop
nodes.summary: Abstract generic class owning an unbounded LinkedBlockingDeque and one daemon thread. Subclasses implement onReceive (handle an event) and onError (non-fatal errors), and may override onStart/onStop. The queue grows without bound, so onReceive must be fast and non-blocking.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the event thread after calling onStart; throws IllegalStateException if the loop was already stopped.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Idempotently stops the loop: sets the stopped flag, interrupts and joins the event thread, then calls onStop after the thread has exited.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Enqueues an event for later processing on the event thread; if the thread has died unexpectedly it reports an IllegalStateException through onError.

nodes.name: ShuffleManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the pluggable ShuffleManager trait (registerShuffle on the driver, getWriter for map tasks, getReader for reduce tasks, unregisterShuffle, shuffleBlockResolver, stop) and a companion factory that instantiates the class named by spark.shuffle.manager, mapping "sort" and "tungsten-sort" to SortShuffleManager.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait with a companion object; the final getReader overload delegates to the abstract overload with the full map index range (0 to Int.MaxValue).

nodes.name: ShuffleManager
nodes.summary: Pluggable interface for shuffle systems. It is created in SparkEnv on the driver and each executor. The driver registers shuffles and gets a ShuffleHandle; map tasks ask for a ShuffleWriter, reduce tasks ask for a ShuffleReader over a range of reduce partitions (and optionally a range of map outputs). The companion object holds the factory methods create and getShuffleManagerClassName.

nodes.name: registerShuffle
nodes.summary: Abstract: registers a shuffle with the manager and returns the ShuffleHandle that is passed to tasks. Called through ShuffleDependency.shuffleHandle on the driver.

nodes.name: getWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns a ShuffleWriter for one map task (identified by handle and mapId). Called on executors by map tasks, in practice from ShuffleWriteProcessor.write.

nodes.name: getReader
nodes.summary: Abstract overload returning a ShuffleReader for reduce partitions startPartition..endPartition-1 over map outputs startMapIndex..endMapIndex-1. A final convenience overload (lines 61-68) delegates here with the full map range (0, Int.MaxValue). Called on executors by reduce tasks.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Companion factory: builds a ShuffleManager by instantiating the class name returned by getShuffleManagerClassName via Utils.instantiateSerializerOrShuffleManager with the SparkConf and the isDriver flag.

nodes.name: getShuffleManagerClassName
nodes.summary: Resolves the spark.shuffle.manager setting to a class name: the short names "sort" and "tungsten-sort" both map to SortShuffleManager, any other value is used as a class name verbatim.

nodes.name: SortShuffleManager.scala
nodes.summary: Default ShuffleManager. registerShuffle picks one of three handle kinds (bypass merge sort, serialized/unsafe, or base) and getWriter turns the handle into BypassMergeSortShuffleWriter, UnsafeShuffleWriter or SortShuffleWriter; getReader wires a BlockStoreShuffleReader to map output locations from the MapOutputTracker. Each map task writes one data file plus an index file, managed by IndexShuffleBlockResolver.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class plus companion object (shared class id) and two empty handle subclasses used only as type tags for pattern matching in getWriter.

nodes.name: SortShuffleManager
nodes.summary: Sort-based ShuffleManager: records are sorted by target partition id and written to a single map output file that reducers read in contiguous regions; large outputs spill to disk and are merged. Two write paths exist: serialized sorting (no map-side combine, relocatable serializer, at most 16777216 partitions) and deserialized sorting for everything else, plus a bypass path for few partitions. It tracks which map task ids wrote each shuffle (taskIdMapsForShuffle) so unregisterShuffle can delete their files. The companion object (lines 197-258) holds canUseBatchFetch, canUseSerializedShuffle and the executor components loader.

nodes.name: registerShuffle
nodes.summary: Chooses the ShuffleHandle for a shuffle: BypassMergeSortShuffleHandle when SortShuffleWriter.shouldBypassMergeSort holds (no map-side combine and few partitions), else SerializedShuffleHandle when canUseSerializedShuffle holds, else a plain BaseShuffleHandle. The handle type later decides which writer getWriter creates.

nodes.name: getReader
nodes.summary: Builds the reduce-side reader. It asks SparkEnv.get.mapOutputTracker for the (BlockManagerId, blocks) list using getMapSizesByExecutorId, or getPushBasedShuffleMapSizesByExecutorId when the dependency has a finalized shuffle merge, then returns a BlockStoreShuffleReader. Batch fetching of contiguous blocks is enabled only if canEnableBatchFetch and canUseBatchFetch both hold.

nodes.name: getWriter
nodes.summary: Records the mapId in taskIdMapsForShuffle, then pattern-matches on the handle: SerializedShuffleHandle yields UnsafeShuffleWriter, BypassMergeSortShuffleHandle yields BypassMergeSortShuffleWriter, any other BaseShuffleHandle yields SortShuffleWriter. Called on executors by map tasks.

nodes.name: unregisterShuffle
nodes.summary: Removes the shuffle from taskIdMapsForShuffle and deletes the data and index files of every map task that wrote it through shuffleBlockResolver.removeDataByMap. Always returns true.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts the manager down by stopping its IndexShuffleBlockResolver.

nodes.name: canUseBatchFetch
nodes.summary: Companion helper: a reader may fetch continuous blocks in batch only if it reads more than one reduce partition and the task local property __fetch_continuous_blocks_in_batch_enabled is "true".

nodes.name: canUseSerializedShuffle
nodes.summary: Companion helper deciding whether the serialized (unsafe) write path is allowed: the serializer must support relocation of serialized objects, there must be no map-side combine, and the partition count must not exceed the 16777216 limit. Logs the reason at debug level when it refuses.

nodes.name: loadShuffleExecutorComponents
nodes.summary: Companion helper: loads the pluggable ShuffleDataIO from the SparkConf, takes its executor components, and initializes them with the app id, executor id and any spark shuffle plugin prefixed configs.

nodes.name: SerializedShuffleHandle
nodes.summary: Empty subclass of BaseShuffleHandle used as a type tag meaning registerShuffle chose the serialized shuffle path; getWriter matches on it to build an UnsafeShuffleWriter.

nodes.name: BypassMergeSortShuffleHandle
nodes.summary: Empty subclass of BaseShuffleHandle used as a type tag meaning registerShuffle chose the bypass merge sort path; getWriter matches on it to build a BypassMergeSortShuffleWriter.

nodes.name: SortShuffleWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Map-side writer for the general (deserialized sorting) path. It feeds records into an ExternalSorter that partitions (and optionally aggregates) them, writes the sorted output through a map output writer as a single data file, and returns a MapStatus carrying the partition lengths.

nodes.name: SortShuffleWriter
nodes.summary: ShuffleWriter used when neither the bypass nor the serialized path applies. write() builds an ExternalSorter (with the aggregator and key ordering only when mapSideCombine is set), inserts all records, writes the partitioned output via the ShuffleExecutorComponents map output writer, commits all partitions and builds a MapStatus with the block manager address and partition lengths. stop(success) returns the MapStatus only on success and always cleans up the sorter. The companion object holds shouldBypassMergeSort.

nodes.name: getRowBasedChecksums
nodes.summary: Returns the row based checksums collected by the sorter, or the shared empty array when no sorter exists yet.

nodes.name: getAggregatedChecksumValue
nodes.summary: Returns the aggregated checksum value from the sorter, or 0 when no sorter exists.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Creates an ExternalSorter (combining or plain), inserts all records, opens a map output writer for (shuffleId, mapId, numPartitions), writes the partitioned output, commits all partitions to obtain partition lengths and sets the MapStatus. Key sorting inside partitions is deliberately left to the reduce side.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Idempotent close: returns Some(mapStatus) only when success is true and the writer was not already stopping, and in a finally block stops the sorter and charges the time to the write metrics.

nodes.name: getPartitionLengths
nodes.summary: Returns the per-reduce-partition byte lengths computed during write().

nodes.name: shouldBypassMergeSort
nodes.summary: Companion helper: bypass merge sort is allowed only without map-side aggregation and when the number of reduce partitions is at most spark.shuffle.sort.bypassMergeThreshold.

nodes.name: BlockStoreShuffleReader.scala
nodes.summary: Reduce-side ShuffleReader. It fetches the shuffle blocks that the MapOutputTracker located, deserializes them into key/value records, and applies the aggregator and/or key ordering of the ShuffleDependency (using an ExternalSorter when sorting) before handing an interruptible iterator to the reduce task.

nodes.name: BlockStoreShuffleReader
nodes.summary: Fetches and reads the blocks of a shuffle by requesting them from other nodes block stores. read() creates a ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator over the given blocksByAddress, deserializes each fetched stream, counts records read, then post-processes: sort with an ExternalSorter if keyOrdering is defined, otherwise combine with the aggregator (combiners if mapSideCombine, values otherwise), otherwise pass records through. Fetch failures raised by the fetcher surface as FetchFailedException in the reduce task.

nodes.name: fetchContinuousBlocksInBatch
nodes.summary: Decides whether continuous shuffle blocks can really be fetched in one batch: the caller requested it, the serializer supports relocation, compression (if on) uses a codec that supports concatenation, the old fetch protocol is not forced, and IO encryption is off (SPARK-34790). Logs the unmet conditions at debug level otherwise.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Builds the ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator with the in-flight limits from config, flat-maps each (blockId, stream) into a key/value iterator, wraps it for metrics and task cancellation, then applies sorting (ExternalSorter), map-side-combined merge, or value combine according to the dependency, and returns an InterruptibleIterator of (K, C) records.

nodes.name: IndexShuffleBlockResolver.scala
nodes.summary: Maps logical shuffle block ids to physical files. All reduce partitions of one map task live in a single .data file and an .index file stores the offsets of each partition (numPartitions + 1 longs), with an optional checksum file. It commits map outputs atomically, serves block data to reducers and the external shuffle service, supports block migration during decommissioning, and reads merged (push-based) shuffle files.
nodes.languageNotes: The on-disk format must stay in sync with ExternalShuffleBlockResolver#getSortBasedShuffleBlockData in the network-shuffle module (see the source comment). The companion object (lines 672-677) only defines NOOP_REDUCE_ID = 0, the reduce id used in the data/index block ids.

nodes.name: IndexShuffleBlockResolver
nodes.summary: ShuffleBlockResolver and MigratableResolver for sort-based shuffle. Data of all reduce blocks from one map task is stored in one consolidated data file named after ShuffleDataBlockId(shuffleId, mapId, 0) with the ".data" suffix, and the offsets are stored in a ".index" file. It owns the commit protocol (writeMetadataFileAndCommit), reading a partition range (getBlockData), deleting a map output (removeDataByMap), and shipping files for decommission migration.

nodes.name: getStoredShuffles
nodes.summary: Lists the (shuffleId, mapId) pairs of shuffle index blocks found by the DiskBlockManager, skipping shuffle ids marked via addShuffleToSkip. Used for block migration.

nodes.name: getDataFile
nodes.summary: Returns the File for the map output data block (ShuffleDataBlockId with reduce id 0), either under the DiskBlockManager local directories or under explicitly supplied dirs. A one-line overload (line 91) calls it with dirs = None.

nodes.name: getIndexFile
nodes.summary: Returns the File for the map output index block (ShuffleIndexBlockId with reduce id 0), either from the DiskBlockManager or from the supplied dirs.

nodes.name: removeDataByMap
nodes.summary: Deletes the data file, the index file and (when checksums are enabled) the checksum file of one map task, logging a warning for each failed delete. Called from SortShuffleManager.unregisterShuffle.

nodes.name: checkIndexAndDataFile
nodes.summary: Validates an existing index/data pair: the index must hold blocks + 1 longs starting at offset 0 and the data file length must equal the sum of the partition lengths derived from the offsets. Returns the lengths or null.

nodes.name: putShuffleBlockAsStream
nodes.summary: Receives a migrated shuffle index or data block as a stream: refuses it if the remote shuffle disk limit is exceeded, writes into a temp file, renames it into place on completion, records the map id in taskIdMapsForShuffle and reports the block status to the BlockManager. Cleans up the temp file on failure.

nodes.name: getMigrationBlocks
nodes.summary: Builds the (BlockId, ManagedBuffer) list for migrating one map output: the data block (if the file still exists) and the index block, both as whole-file FileSegmentManagedBuffers. Returns an empty list when the blocks have been removed.

nodes.name: writeMetadataFileAndCommit
nodes.summary: Atomically commits a map output under a lock. If a previous attempt of the same task already produced a valid index+data pair, it keeps those, copies their lengths (and checksums) back and deletes the temp data file; otherwise it writes the index file (offsets from scanLeft of lengths), renames the temp data file to the final data file and writes the optional checksum file (best effort). Temp files are always cleaned up in a finally block.

nodes.name: writeMetadataFile
nodes.summary: Writes an array of longs to a temp file and renames it to the target to avoid dirty writes. Rename failures throw for the index file (propagateError) but only log a warning for the checksum file.

nodes.name: getMergedBlockData
nodes.summary: Reads the merged (push-based) shuffle index file and returns one FileSegmentManagedBuffer per chunk of the merged data file, so the fetcher can consume a local merged block as several chunks.

nodes.name: getMergedBlockMeta
nodes.summary: Returns MergedBlockMeta for a local merged shuffle block: number of chunks derived from the merged index file size plus the chunk bitmap file as a buffer.

nodes.name: getChecksums
nodes.summary: Reads blockNum checksum longs from a checksum file, returning null if the file is missing or truncated.

nodes.name: getChecksumFile
nodes.summary: Returns the File for the shuffle checksum block, with the file name derived from the block name and the checksum algorithm, from the DiskBlockManager or the supplied dirs.

nodes.name: getBlockData
nodes.summary: Serves a ShuffleBlockId or ShuffleBlockBatchId: seeks to startReduceId*8 in the index file to read the start and end offsets, sanity-checks the channel position (SPARK-22982), and returns a FileSegmentManagedBuffer over that byte range of the single data file. This is how a reducer fetch becomes a contiguous slice of the map output.

nodes.name: getBlocksForShuffle
nodes.summary: Returns the index and data BlockIds of one map output, used to delete shuffle files from the external shuffle service after an executor is removed.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: No-op shutdown.

nodes.name: ShuffleWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the abstract ShuffleWriter used inside a map task: write(records), stop(success) returning the MapStatus, and getPartitionLengths.

nodes.name: ShuffleWriter
nodes.summary: Abstract writer obtained inside a map task to write out records to the shuffle system. Concrete implementations are SortShuffleWriter, UnsafeShuffleWriter and BypassMergeSortShuffleWriter. stop(true) yields the MapStatus that the scheduler records for the map output.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Abstract: writes a sequence of records to this task output; may throw IOException.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Abstract: closes the writer and returns the MapStatus when the map completed successfully.

nodes.name: getPartitionLengths
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the byte length of each reduce partition written.

nodes.name: ShuffleReader.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the ShuffleReader trait used by reduce tasks to read combined key-value records from the mappers.

nodes.name: ShuffleReader
nodes.summary: Trait obtained inside a reduce task whose read() returns the combined records for this task. The only implementation in this layer is BlockStoreShuffleReader.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the iterator of combined (key, value) records for this reduce task.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockResolver.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the ShuffleBlockResolver trait: how a logical shuffle block id (shuffle, map, reduce) is turned into block data, abstracting over shuffle implementations for the BlockStore.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockResolver
nodes.summary: Implementers know how to retrieve block data for a logical shuffle block id and may use files or file segments to hold shuffle data. It also exposes merged (push-based) block data and meta, a default empty getBlocksForShuffle used for external shuffle service cleanup, and stop. IndexShuffleBlockResolver is the implementation.

nodes.name: getBlockData
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the ManagedBuffer for the given block id, optionally from explicit directories; throws if the data is unavailable.

nodes.name: getBlocksForShuffle
nodes.summary: Default implementation returning an empty sequence; overridden to list the BlockIds of a map output so the external shuffle service can delete them.

nodes.name: getMergedBlockData
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the data of a merged shuffle block as multiple chunk buffers.

nodes.name: getMergedBlockMeta
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the MergedBlockMeta for a merged shuffle block.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Abstract: shuts the resolver down.

nodes.name: ShuffleHandle.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShuffleHandle, the opaque serializable handle carrying a shuffleId that a ShuffleManager gives to tasks.

nodes.name: ShuffleHandle
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi abstract class: an opaque handle to a shuffle, used by a ShuffleManager to pass information about it to tasks. It only carries the shuffleId and is Serializable so it can ship with tasks.

nodes.name: BaseShuffleHandle.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BaseShuffleHandle, the basic ShuffleHandle that simply keeps the ShuffleDependency passed to registerShuffle.

nodes.name: BaseShuffleHandle
nodes.summary: Basic ShuffleHandle that captures registerShuffle parameters: the shuffleId and the full ShuffleDependency (serializer, partitioner, aggregator, ordering, mapSideCombine). Writers and readers read the dependency from it. SerializedShuffleHandle and BypassMergeSortShuffleHandle extend it.

nodes.name: ShufflePartitionPairsWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Key-value writer that serializes records into a ShufflePartitionWriter stream (instead of a local disk file), with time tracking, optional checksumming and per-record metrics.

nodes.name: ShufflePartitionPairsWriter
nodes.summary: PairsWriter inspired by DiskBlockObjectWriter that pushes serialized bytes to an arbitrary ShufflePartitionWriter. The stream stack is partition stream, TimeTrackingOutputStream, optional MutableCheckedOutputStream (when a Checksum is given), then serializerManager.wrapStream (compression/encryption) and a SerializationStream. ExternalSorter uses it when writing partitioned map output.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one key and value, lazily opening the stream on the first record, and counts the record. Throws an internal error if the writer is already closed.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Builds the output stream stack for the partition (time tracking, optional checksum, wrapStream, serialization stream); on failure it closes what it opened and rethrows.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the serialization stream and, defensively, each inner stream with nested safe-finally blocks so none is closed twice, then reports the bytes written and marks the writer closed.

nodes.name: closeIfNonNull
nodes.summary: Closes the given Closeable if not null and returns null so the caller can clear its reference.

nodes.name: recordWritten
nodes.summary: Increments the record counters in the write metrics and refreshes the byte metrics every 16384 records.

nodes.name: updateBytesWritten
nodes.summary: Adds the difference between the partition writer byte count and the last seen count to the bytes-written metric.

nodes.name: FetchFailedException.scala
nodes.summary: Defines FetchFailedException and its subclass MetadataFetchFailedException: the exceptions thrown by a reduce task when it cannot fetch a shuffle block or the map output metadata. The executor reports them to the DAGScheduler as a FetchFailed task end reason, which makes the scheduler resubmit the map stage that produced the missing output.

nodes.name: FetchFailedException
nodes.summary: Signals a failure to fetch a shuffle block (location bmAddress, which may be null, shuffleId, mapId, mapIndex, reduceId). Its constructor calls TaskContext.setFetchFailed so the executor still knows about the fetch failure even if user code wraps or swallows the exception (SPARK-19276), hence it must be thrown immediately after creation. toTaskFailedReason converts it to a FetchFailed reason, through which the DAGScheduler resubmits the previous stage.

nodes.name: toTaskFailedReason
nodes.summary: Builds the FetchFailed TaskFailedReason from this exception (address, shuffleId, mapId, mapIndex, reduceId and the exception string) so the executor can send it to the driver.

nodes.name: MetadataFetchFailedException
nodes.summary: FetchFailedException subclass for failing to get shuffle metadata from the MapOutputTracker (no block manager address, mapId -1, mapIndex -1). It carries shuffleId, reduceId and message.

nodes.name: BlockManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BlockManager, the per-JVM (driver and every executor) service that stores and fetches blocks in a MemoryStore, a DiskStore or off-heap, tracks block metadata with BlockInfoManager, replicates blocks and reports their status to the BlockManagerMaster on the driver. Cached/persisted RDD partitions, broadcast blocks and shuffle blocks served to other executors are all managed here; also holds BlockData wrappers, HostLocalDirManager and the temp-file manager for large remote fetches.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a large class plus a companion object; BlockStoreUpdater and its subclasses are inner classes of BlockManager and capture its stores. Private[spark] visibility throughout.

nodes.name: BlockResult
nodes.summary: Return value of local and remote block reads: an iterator over the block's records, how it was read (Memory, Disk or Network) and its size in bytes. The read method feeds input metrics for cached RDD partitions.

nodes.name: BlockData
nodes.summary: Trait that abstracts how a stored block's bytes are exposed (input stream, Netty buffer, ChunkedByteBuffer, ByteBuffer) so callers can read memory-backed and disk-backed blocks uniformly, then call dispose().

nodes.name: ByteBufferBlockData
nodes.summary: BlockData implementation backed by a ChunkedByteBuffer already in memory; dispose() frees the buffer only when shouldDispose is true.

nodes.name: HostLocalDirManager
nodes.summary: Caches, in a size-bounded Guava cache, the local directory lists of other executors on the same host and fetches missing ones through the BlockStoreClient. Lets a reader open another executor's shuffle or disk-persisted block files directly from disk instead of going over the network.

nodes.name: BlockManager
nodes.summary: Manager running on every node (driver and executors) that puts and gets blocks locally and remotely in memory, disk and off-heap stores. Owns the DiskBlockManager, BlockInfoManager, MemoryStore and DiskStore, registers with the BlockManagerMaster, replicates blocks to peers, serves shuffle and RDD blocks to other executors, drops memory blocks to disk on eviction and migrates blocks on decommission. Its companion object (lines 2232-2375) adds blockIdsToLocations plus the remote-download temp-file helpers.

nodes.name: BlockStoreUpdater
nodes.summary: Abstract inner helper that stores a block given as bytes (in memory or in a temp file): save() runs doPut, kicks off replication first if replication > 1, writes to the MemoryStore (deserialized values or serialized bytes) and falls back to the DiskStore, then reports the status to the master.

nodes.name: ByteBufferBlockStoreUpdater
nodes.summary: BlockStoreUpdater for bytes already in a ChunkedByteBuffer; spills to disk with diskStore.putBytes. Callers must not mutate the buffer afterwards.

nodes.name: TempFileBasedBlockStoreUpdater
nodes.summary: BlockStoreUpdater for a block that was streamed into a local temp file (putBlockDataAsStream); reads from that file for memory puts, moves it into place with diskStore.moveFileToBlock for disk puts and deletes the temp file after save().

nodes.name: ShuffleMetricsSource
nodes.summary: Metrics Source that wraps the block transfer client's MetricSet (named ExternalShuffle or NettyBlockTransfer) so shuffle transfer metrics can be registered with the metrics system.

nodes.name: RemoteBlockDownloadFileManager
nodes.summary: DownloadFileManager that creates temp files under the DiskBlockManager for remote blocks larger than the in-memory fetch threshold (optionally encrypted) and deletes them via weak references and a daemon cleaner thread named RemoteBlock-temp-file-clean-thread.

nodes.name: EncryptedDownloadFile
nodes.summary: DownloadFile that encrypts bytes while a remote block is written to local disk and returns an EncryptedManagedBuffer for reading it back.

nodes.name: waitForShuffleManagerInit
nodes.summary: Blocks until SparkEnv reports the ShuffleManager is initialized, or throws ShuffleManagerNotInitializedException after the configured timeout, so shuffle migration requests do not hit a null manager.

nodes.name: diagnoseShuffleBlockCorruption
nodes.summary: Diagnoses the cause of a corrupted shuffle block by reading its checksum file through IndexShuffleBlockResolver and comparing with the checksum the reader computed.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Finishes setup once the appId is known: starts the BlockTransferService and external client, loads the replication policy, registers with the external shuffle service when enabled, registers this BlockManager with the BlockManagerMaster and prepares the host-local dir manager.

nodes.name: shuffleMetricsSource
nodes.summary: Builds the metrics Source for shuffle transfers, named ExternalShuffle when an external shuffle service is used and NettyBlockTransfer otherwise.

nodes.name: registerWithExternalShuffleServer
nodes.summary: Registers this executor's local dirs, sub-dir count and ShuffleManager class name with the local external shuffle service so it can serve this executor's shuffle files, retrying on failure.

nodes.name: reportAllBlocks
nodes.summary: Re-sends the current status of every block in the BlockInfoManager to the master, used after re-registration.

nodes.name: reregister
nodes.summary: Re-registers this BlockManager with the master and then reports all its blocks; exits the executor with BLOCK_MANAGER_REREGISTRATION_FAILED if re-registration fails.

nodes.name: asyncReregister
nodes.summary: Schedules at most one pending asynchronous reregister() on the future execution context.

nodes.name: getLocalBlockData
nodes.summary: BlockDataManager entry point for serving a block to another node: shuffle blocks go through the ShuffleBlockResolver (with a decommission fallback storage on IOException), other blocks via getLocalBytes wrapped in a BlockManagerManagedBuffer; reports an empty status if the block is missing.

nodes.name: putBlockData
nodes.summary: BlockDataManager entry point that stores a block received as a ManagedBuffer by delegating to putBytes.

nodes.name: putBlockDataAsStream
nodes.summary: Returns a StreamCallbackWithID that receives a block over the network: shuffle blocks stream through the MigratableResolver, other blocks are written to a temp local block file and then stored with a TempFileBasedBlockStoreUpdater.

nodes.name: reportBlockStatus
nodes.summary: Tells the master the block's current status (not the requested level), and triggers asyncReregister if the master asks for re-registration.

nodes.name: tryToReportBlockStatus
nodes.summary: Sends an UpdateBlockInfo message to the master via updateBlockInfo with memory and disk sizes; shuffle blocks are reported under the shuffle server id.

nodes.name: getCurrentBlockStatus
nodes.summary: Computes the block's actual storage level and memory and disk sizes by checking the MemoryStore and DiskStore, since a MEMORY_AND_DISK block may have fallen to disk only.

nodes.name: getLocalValues
nodes.summary: Reads a block from this BlockManager as an iterator of objects under a read lock: from the MemoryStore (values, or deserialized bytes) or from the DiskStore, optionally re-caching disk data into memory; releases the lock when the iterator is consumed.

nodes.name: getLocalBytes
nodes.summary: Returns a local non-shuffle block as serialized BlockData under a read lock.

nodes.name: doGetLocalBytes
nodes.summary: Core of getLocalBytes: prefers pre-serialized bytes from the DiskStore for deserialized levels, otherwise serializes in-memory objects, and for serialized levels reads memory first then disk; falls back to handleLocalReadFailure.

nodes.name: getRemoteValues
nodes.summary: Fetches a block from remote BlockManagers and deserializes it into a BlockResult with read method Network.

nodes.name: getRemoteBlock
nodes.summary: Looks up block locations from the master; first tries to read the block file directly from another executor's local dir on the same host, then falls back to fetching over the network, applying the supplied buffer transformer.

nodes.name: sortLocations
nodes.summary: Orders candidate block locations: same host first, then same rack, then others, shuffling randomly and preferring executors over external shuffle servers.

nodes.name: fetchRemoteManagedBuffer
nodes.summary: Tries each sorted location with BlockTransferService.fetchBlockSync, spilling to a temp file when the block exceeds the in-memory threshold, tolerating failures and refreshing locations from the driver after repeated failures.

nodes.name: readDiskBlockFromSameHostExecutor
nodes.summary: Opens another executor's disk-persisted block file on the same host as a ManagedBuffer (FileSegmentManagedBuffer, or an encrypted wrapper) using the executor's local dirs.

nodes.name: getRemoteBytes
nodes.summary: Fetches a block from remote BlockManagers as a ChunkedByteBuffer.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Gets a block from the local BlockManager first, then from remote ones, returning the first BlockResult found.

nodes.name: releaseLock
nodes.summary: Releases a read lock on a block for a task, skipping tasks that already completed.

nodes.name: getOrElseUpdateRDDBlock
nodes.summary: Entry point used when reading a cached RDD partition: checks cache visibility, returns the block if cached or computes, persists and returns it; reports taskId to the master for blocks not yet visible.

nodes.name: getOrElseUpdate
nodes.summary: Gets a block from local or remote storage if present; otherwise computes the partition via makeIterator, stores it with doPutIterator keeping a read lock and returns either the cached BlockResult or the raw iterator when it did not fit.

nodes.name: putIterator
nodes.summary: Stores an iterator of values as a block at the given StorageLevel; returns true on success and closes the iterator on failure.

nodes.name: getDiskWriter
nodes.summary: Creates a DiskBlockObjectWriter that appends records directly to a file on disk, honoring spark.shuffle.sync; used by shuffle writers and sorters to write shuffle and spill files.

nodes.name: putBytes
