nodes.summary: Stores serialized bytes as a block at the given StorageLevel through a ByteBufferBlockStoreUpdater.

nodes.name: isRDDBlockVisible
nodes.summary: Tells whether a cached RDD block is visible, consulting the local BlockInfoManager and then the master when cache visibility tracking is enabled.

nodes.name: doPut
nodes.summary: Shared put logic: validates the id and level, takes a write lock on a new BlockInfo, runs the supplied put body, downgrades or releases the lock on success and removes the block on failure.

nodes.name: doPutIterator
nodes.summary: Stores values from an iterator: memory first (deserialized values or serialized bytes), spilling the partially unrolled iterator to the DiskStore if memory is insufficient and the level allows disk, or straight to disk for DISK_ONLY; then reports status and replicates when replication > 1.

nodes.name: maybeCacheDiskBytesInMemory
nodes.summary: After a disk read of a serialized block, tries to copy the bytes into the MemoryStore to speed up later reads.

nodes.name: maybeCacheDiskValuesInMemory
nodes.summary: After a disk read of a deserialized block, tries to put the values into the MemoryStore and returns an iterator over them.

nodes.name: getPeers
nodes.summary: Returns peer BlockManagers from the master with a TTL cache, or the fallback storage id when no peers exist and a fallback path is configured.

nodes.name: replicateBlock
nodes.summary: Proactively replicates an existing local block to peers (used on executor removal or decommission) by reading its bytes and calling replicate with a raised replication count.

nodes.name: replicate
nodes.summary: Blocking upload of a block to peer BlockManagers selected by the BlockReplicationPolicy, retrying with refreshed peer lists on failure and returning whether enough replicas were made.

nodes.name: putSingle
nodes.summary: Stores a block consisting of a single object via putIterator.

nodes.name: dropFromMemory
nodes.summary: BlockEvictionHandler callback invoked by the MemoryStore under memory pressure: writes the block to the DiskStore if its level allows disk, removes it from memory and reports the new status to the master.

nodes.name: removeRdd
nodes.summary: Removes all blocks of a given RDD id from memory and disk, used when an RDD is unpersisted.

nodes.name: decommissionSelf
nodes.summary: Starts a BlockManagerDecommissioner that migrates RDD and shuffle blocks to other executors; no-op if already decommissioning.

nodes.name: removeBroadcast
nodes.summary: Removes all blocks of a given broadcast variable.

nodes.name: removeBlock
nodes.summary: Removes a block from memory and disk under a write lock and updates task metrics with an empty status.

nodes.name: removeBlockInternal
nodes.summary: Removes a block from MemoryStore, DiskStore and BlockInfoManager, and reports the removal to the master with replication count zero.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the BlockManager: stops the decommissioner, transfer clients, temp-file manager, DiskBlockManager and endpoint, and clears the block info and memory store.

nodes.name: blockIdsToLocations
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper mapping block ids to executor cache task location strings, using the local BlockManager or a given BlockManagerMaster; used for locality of cached or broadcast blocks.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Stores the block's bytes through doPut, starting replication before the local write, putting it in the MemoryStore then falling back to the DiskStore, reporting status to the master and awaiting replication.

nodes.name: DiskBlockObjectWriter.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DiskBlockObjectWriter, an OutputStream and PairsWriter that serializes JVM key/value objects through the SerializerManager (compression/encryption wrapping) straight into a file on local disk. Shuffle writers and external sorters use it to produce shuffle map-output and spill files; it appends to an existing file, commits writes as atomic FileSegments (offset and length) and can truncate uncommitted bytes on failure while updating shuffle write metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class extending java.io.OutputStream with Logging and PairsWriter; uses Utils.tryWithSafeFinally and a private ManualCloseOutputStream trait to keep the underlying file channel open across commits.

nodes.name: DiskBlockObjectWriter
nodes.summary: Writes JVM objects to a block file on local disk through a buffered, optionally checksummed and compressed stream, retaining one FileChannel across commits. commitAndGet returns the committed byte range as a FileSegment (this is how per-partition offsets in a shuffle data file are determined), revertPartialWritesAndClose truncates back to the last commit, and write metrics are updated incrementally. Not safe for concurrent writes and cannot be reopened.

nodes.name: ManualCloseOutputStream
nodes.summary: Private trait mixed into the buffered stream so wrapper streams calling close() only flush, while manualClose() really closes it; lets commits close serialization streams without closing the file.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Opens the FileOutputStream in append mode and builds the stack: time-tracking stream, optional checksum stream and a ManualCloseOutputStream buffered stream of bufferSize.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Initializes the file streams on first use and wraps them with serializerManager.wrapStream and serializerInstance.serializeStream; throws if the writer was already closed.

nodes.name: closeResources
nodes.summary: Closes the serialization stream, then manually closes the underlying stream and nulls all resources, marking the writer as closed.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Commits remaining partial writes via commitAndGet and then releases resources.

nodes.name: commitAndGet
nodes.summary: Flushes and closes the serializer stream, optionally fsyncs, and returns the FileSegment covering bytes written since the last commit while updating bytes-written metrics; the file channel stays open.

nodes.name: revertPartialWritesAndClose
nodes.summary: Rolls back uncommitted writes by decrementing write metrics, closing resources and truncating the file to the last committed position; does not throw.

nodes.name: closeAndDelete
nodes.summary: Reverts all write metrics, closes the writer and deletes the file; used when the file is no longer needed after an error.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes a key-value pair through the serialization stream (opening it if needed) and counts one record via recordWritten.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Overload of OutputStream.write that writes a raw byte range to the wrapped stream, opening it if needed; the single-byte write(Int) overload throws unsupported.

nodes.name: recordWritten
nodes.summary: Increments the record counters and write metrics, and refreshes bytes written every 16384 records.

nodes.name: updateBytesWritten
nodes.summary: Reports the delta between the channel position and the last reported position to the shuffle write metrics.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.scala
nodes.summary: Reduce-side shuffle read engine. Defines the iterator that turns the (BlockManagerId, blocks) list produced by the map output tracker into a stream of (BlockId, InputStream), fetching local, host-local, push-merged and remote blocks, plus the FetchResult message types, the FetchRequest/FetchBlockInfo helpers and the listener that cleans up on task completion.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a private[spark] final class, a private[storage] companion object holding sealed-trait result case classes, and two private helper classes.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator[(BlockId, InputStream)] that a reducer uses to read shuffle input. At construction it splits blocks into local, host-local, push-merged-local and remote groups, starts remote requests bounded by maxBytesInFlight, maxReqsInFlight and maxBlocksInFlightPerAddress, and queues results in a LinkedBlockingDeque so asynchronous Netty callbacks look like a synchronous iterator. Failed or corrupt blocks surface as FetchFailedException so the scheduler can retry the map stage. Extends Iterator with DownloadFileManager with Logging.
nodes.languageNotes: The last constructor parameter is clock: Clock = new SystemClock() which is indented differently from the other parameters; the class is final and private[spark].

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.createTempFile
nodes.summary: DownloadFileManager callback that creates a SimpleDownloadFile in a temp local block of the DiskBlockManager; used when a remote request is larger than maxReqSizeShuffleToMem and is streamed to disk instead of memory. No encryption is applied here because shuffle data is already encrypted on the wire.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.registerTempFileToClean
nodes.summary: Registers a downloaded temp file in shuffleFilesSet for deletion at cleanup, unless the iterator is already a zombie (in which case it returns false).

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.cleanup
nodes.summary: Marks the iterator as zombie so late callbacks stop enqueuing results, releases the current buffer and every unread SuccessFetchResult buffer in the results queue (updating shuffle read metrics for them), and deletes temp files used for shuffling huge remote blocks. Invoked from the task completion listener.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.sendRequest
nodes.summary: Issues one FetchRequest through the BlockStoreClient and builds the BlockFetchingListener. Success callbacks retain the buffer and put a SuccessFetchResult on the results queue; failures become FailureFetchResult (put first), FallbackOnPushMergedFailureResult for shuffle chunks, or are deferred via DeferFetchRequestResult when Netty runs out of direct memory and the retry count is below maxAttemptsOnNettyOOM. Requests larger than maxReqSizeShuffleToMem are fetched to disk files.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.partitionBlocksByFetchMode
nodes.summary: Partitions the blocks grouped by address into local, host-local (same host, directories looked up through HostLocalDirManager), push-merged-local and remote groups, merges contiguous reduce ids into batch blocks when doBatchFetch is set, and returns the remote FetchRequests. Also asserts the block-count invariant and logs the byte totals per group. Used by initialize and by the push-merged fallback.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.createFetchRequests
nodes.summary: Merges contiguous blocks if batch fetch is enabled, then emits FetchRequests capped at maxBlocksInFlightPerAddress blocks. A trailing group smaller than the cap is returned to the caller to be combined with later blocks unless it is the last group.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.collectFetchRequests
nodes.summary: Walks the blocks for one remote address and cuts a new FetchRequest each time the accumulated size reaches targetRemoteRequestSize (maxBytesInFlight / 5) or the block count reaches the per-address cap. Handles original shuffle blocks, push-merged blocks (forMergedMetas) and shuffle chunks differently with respect to batch fetching.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.fetchLocalBlocks
nodes.summary: Reads blocks that live on this executor straight from the local BlockManager (getLocalBlockData), updates local-read metrics and enqueues SuccessFetchResult. On the first exception it puts a FailureFetchResult at the head of the queue and stops.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.fetchHostLocalBlock
nodes.summary: Reads one host-local block from another executor on the same host via BlockManager.getHostLocalShuffleData and the executor local dirs, enqueueing a SuccessFetchResult or a FailureFetchResult and returning whether it succeeded.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.fetchHostLocalBlocks
nodes.summary: Fetches host-local blocks, splitting executors into those whose local directories are cached and those missing. Missing directories are requested asynchronously (from the external shuffle service in one call when enabled, otherwise from each executor) through HostLocalDirManager and then read; cached ones are read synchronously.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.fetchMultipleHostLocalBlocks
nodes.summary: Reads all host-local blocks for a set of executors using forall, so it stops at the first failure (which already pushed a FailureFetchResult) and otherwise logs the time taken.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.initialize
nodes.summary: Constructor-time setup: registers the task completion cleanup listener, partitions blocks by fetch mode, queues remote requests in random order, sends the first batch of requests up to maxBytesInFlight, then reads local, host-local and push-merged-local blocks while the remote fetches run in the background.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.fetchAllHostLocalBlocks
nodes.summary: Invokes fetchHostLocalBlocks when there are host-local blocks and the BlockManager has a HostLocalDirManager.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.shuffleMetricsUpdate
nodes.summary: Dispatches a shuffle read metrics update to the local or remote variant depending on the local flag.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.shuffleLocalMetricsUpdate
nodes.summary: Records local blocks fetched and local bytes read in ShuffleReadMetricsReporter, with extra merged chunk counters when the block is a push-merged shuffle chunk.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.shuffleRemoteMetricsUpdate
nodes.summary: Records remote blocks fetched and remote bytes read (and bytes read to disk for file-backed buffers), with merged chunk counters for push-merged chunks.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.next
nodes.summary: Core of the iterator. Takes the next FetchResult from the results queue (timing the wait as fetch wait time), updates in-flight accounting and metrics, rejects zero-size buffers, optionally wraps the stream in a CheckedInputStream and the streamWrapper (decompression or decryption), and probes the first maxBytesInFlight/3 bytes for corruption. Corrupt remote blocks are re-requested once; a second corruption or any local I/O error throws FetchFailedException through throwFetchFailedException. Also handles deferred requests, push-merged fallback and meta results, then calls fetchUpToMaxBytes to keep the pipeline full and returns a BufferReleasingInputStream.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.diagnoseCorruption
nodes.summary: When shuffle checksum is enabled and a block was found corrupt, reads the rest of the stream to compute its checksum and asks the serving side (shuffleClient.diagnoseCorruption) why it is corrupt, returning a text diagnosis. Falls back to UNKNOWN_ISSUE on any error and skips diagnosis for push-merged chunks and batch blocks.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.toCompletionIterator
nodes.summary: Wraps this iterator in a CompletionIterator that runs the cleanup listener when iteration finishes.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.fetchUpToMaxBytes
nodes.summary: Flow-control loop that sends queued fetch requests while bytesInFlight stays under maxBytesInFlight, reqsInFlight under maxReqsInFlight and the blocks per remote address under maxBlocksInFlightPerAddress. Requests that would exceed the per-address limit are deferred and retried later; if a Netty out-of-memory flag is set and requests are still in flight, it returns immediately. Contains the local helpers send, isRemoteBlockFetchable and isRemoteAddressMaxedOut.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.throwFetchFailedException
nodes.summary: Converts a fetch problem for a ShuffleBlockId, ShuffleBlockBatchId or ShuffleBlockChunkId into a FetchFailedException (built by SparkCoreErrors.fetchFailedError) carrying the address, shuffle id, map id, map index and reduce id, which makes the scheduler resubmit the map stage. Non-shuffle blocks raise a different error.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.fallbackFetch
nodes.summary: Used by PushBasedFetchHelper when a push-merged block or chunk fails: partitions the original (unmerged) blocks by fetch mode, queues the remote requests, and fetches the local and host-local ones.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.removePendingChunks
nodes.summary: Removes queued and deferred requests for shuffle chunks of the same shuffle, reduce partition and host as a chunk that just failed, and returns the removed chunk ids so their original blocks can be fetched instead.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.mergeContinuousShuffleBlockIdsIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Companion helper. When doBatchFetch is true, merges consecutive blocks with the same map id into ShuffleBlockBatchId ranges of reduce ids (for example shuffle_0_0_0 and shuffle_0_0_1 become one batch), reusing an existing trailing batch if possible; otherwise returns the input unchanged.

nodes.name: ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator.resetNettyOOMFlagIfPossible
nodes.summary: Companion helper that clears the shared isNettyOOMOnShuffle flag once NettyUtils.freeDirectMemory is at least the given lower bound.

nodes.name: FetchBlockInfo
nodes.summary: Case class (blockId, estimated size, mapIndex) describing one block inside a FetchRequest; the size drives the bytesInFlight accounting and is only an estimate.

nodes.name: FetchRequest
nodes.summary: Case class for a request to one remote BlockManagerId covering a sequence of FetchBlockInfo; its size is the sum of block sizes, and forMergedMetas marks requests that ask for push-merged meta information instead of data.

nodes.name: FetchResult
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for everything that can be placed on the results queue: success, failure, deferral, push-merged fallback and push-merged meta results.

nodes.name: SuccessFetchResult
nodes.summary: A fetched block: block id, mapIndex, source address, estimated size, the ManagedBuffer and an isNetworkReqDone flag marking the last block of a network request, used to decrement reqsInFlight.

nodes.name: FailureFetchResult
nodes.summary: A failed fetch holding the block id, mapIndex, address and exception; next() turns it into a FetchFailedException. It is enqueued at the head of the queue so failures are seen early.

nodes.name: DeferFetchRequestResult
nodes.summary: Result carrying a whole FetchRequest that must be retried later (used after Netty out-of-memory); next() moves it to deferredFetchRequests.

nodes.name: FallbackOnPushMergedFailureResult
nodes.summary: Result for a failed push-merged block or shuffle chunk fetch; instead of failing, next() falls back to fetching the original shuffle blocks.

nodes.name: PushMergedRemoteMetaFetchResult
nodes.summary: Result of a successful fetch of meta information (chunk bitmaps and block size) for a remote push-merged block, which next() expands into chunk fetch requests.

nodes.name: PushMergedRemoteMetaFailedFetchResult
nodes.summary: Result of a failed meta fetch for a remote push-merged block; next() falls back to fetching the original blocks.

nodes.name: PushMergedLocalMetaFetchResult
nodes.summary: Result of reading meta information for a push-merged-local block (bitmaps and local dirs), which next() reads as multiple local shuffle chunks.

nodes.name: BufferReleasingInputStream
nodes.summary: InputStream wrapper returned to callers. Closing it releases the underlying ManagedBuffer and may reset the Netty OOM flag. When detectCorruption is on, any IOException from read, skip or available is turned into a FetchFailedException (with an optional checksum diagnosis) and is never retried because downstream operators may have consumed part of the block.

nodes.name: BufferReleasingInputStream.close
nodes.summary: Closes the delegate stream, releases the current result buffer on the iterator, and resets the Netty OOM flag if this was the last block of a network request.

nodes.name: BufferReleasingInputStream.tryOrFetchFailedException
nodes.summary: Runs a read-type operation and, if corruption detection is on, converts an IOException into a FetchFailedException after closing the stream and optionally diagnosing the corruption via the checksum.

nodes.name: ShuffleFetchCompletionListener
nodes.summary: TaskCompletionListener that calls cleanup() on the fetcher iterator when the task ends (success, failure or kill) and then nulls its reference so block location metadata can be garbage collected.

nodes.name: ShuffleFetchCompletionListener.onTaskCompletion
nodes.summary: Calls data.cleanup() once and clears the reference to the iterator.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.scala
nodes.summary: Sort-based collection used by the map side (SortShuffleWriter) and by reduce-side aggregation or sorting: it buffers (K, V) records in memory, optionally combines and sorts them by partition id and key, spills sorted runs to disk when memory is short, and later merges the spilled files with the in-memory data into per-partition iterators or one partitioned map output.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a generic private[spark] class ExternalSorter[K, V, C] and several private[this] inner classes that close over its state.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter
nodes.summary: Sorts and optionally combines (K, V) pairs into (K, C) pairs grouped by the Partitioner. With an Aggregator it uses a PartitionedAppendOnlyMap to combine values in memory, otherwise a PartitionedPairBuffer; when the task memory manager refuses more memory it spills the sorted collection to a temp shuffle file, and on output it merges all spills with in-memory data by partition id and then key (or key hash code when only aggregating). Extends Spillable[WritablePartitionedPairCollection[K, C]] with Logging with ShuffleChecksumSupport. Callers must call stop() to delete intermediate files.
nodes.languageNotes: Extends the Spillable base class so memory growth is negotiated with the TaskMemoryManager; the sort order is (partition id, key) where the key comparator falls back to hash code ordering when no total ordering is supplied.

nodes.name: SpilledFile
nodes.summary: Private case class describing one spill: the file, its temp shuffle BlockId, the byte length of each serializer batch, and the number of elements per partition, which lets readers walk partitions without storing the partition id per record.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.insertAll
nodes.summary: Feeds records into the sorter. With an Aggregator it calls map.changeValue on (partitionId, key) using mergeValue or createCombiner; without one it inserts into the pair buffer. After each record it calls maybeSpillCollection and updates row-based checksums when enabled.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.maybeSpillCollection
nodes.summary: Estimates the size of the current map or buffer, asks Spillable.maybeSpill whether to spill, installs a fresh collection after a spill, and tracks the peak memory used.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.spill
nodes.summary: Spillable hook: obtains a destructive sorted iterator over the collection (sorted by partition id and optionally key), writes it with spillMemoryIteratorToDisk, and records the SpilledFile in spills.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.forceSpill
nodes.summary: Called by the TaskMemoryManager when another consumer needs memory. It does nothing during the shuffle-write path (isShuffleSort true); once iterator() is reading, it asks the SpillableIterator to spill the unread remainder to disk and drops the in-memory structures.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.spillMemoryIteratorToDisk
nodes.summary: Writes a partition-ordered in-memory iterator to a temp shuffle block using a DiskBlockObjectWriter from BlockManager.getDiskWriter. Records are flushed in batches of spark.shuffle.spill.batchSize (serializerBatchSize), tracking each batch length and the element count per partition; spilled bytes are added to diskBytesSpilled and the file is deleted if writing fails.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.merge
nodes.summary: Creates a SpillReader per spill and walks partitions 0 until numPartitions, combining each partition from every spill file plus the in-memory iterator using mergeWithAggregation (if an Aggregator exists), mergeSort (if only an Ordering), or plain concatenation.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.mergeSort
nodes.summary: k-way merge of sorted iterators with a PriorityQueue ordered by the head key; returns one sorted iterator.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.mergeWithAggregation
nodes.summary: Merges sorted (K, C) iterators and combines values for equal keys with mergeCombiners. With a total ordering equal keys are adjacent; with only a hash-code ordering it buffers all keys that compare equal and tests real equality to merge correctly.

nodes.name: SpillReader
nodes.summary: Private inner class that reads a SpilledFile partition by partition, opening one serializer batch at a time at the right byte offset. Partitions must be requested in order; it deserializes keys and values with the sorter serializer after wrapping the stream with the serializer manager.

nodes.name: SpillReader.nextBatchStream
nodes.summary: Closes the previous batch stream and opens a new FileInputStream limited to the next batch byte range, wrapped by serializerManager.wrapStream and deserialized; when no batches remain it cleans up and returns null.

nodes.name: SpillReader.skipToNextPartition
nodes.summary: Advances partitionId past partitions whose recorded element count has been fully read, skipping empty partitions.

nodes.name: SpillReader.readNextItem
nodes.summary: Reads the next key and combiner, moves to the next batch stream after serializerBatchSize items, updates partition position, and marks the reader finished after the last partition.

nodes.name: SpillReader.readNextPartition
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the next partition of the spill file that yields items only while the last read item still belongs to that partition.

nodes.name: SpillReader.cleanup
nodes.summary: Closes the open deserialize stream and prevents further batch reads; the spill file itself is deleted later by ExternalSorter.stop().

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.destructiveIterator
nodes.summary: Returns the memory iterator as is on the shuffle sort path, otherwise wraps it in a SpillableIterator so it can be forced to spill while the user reads it.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.partitionedIterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over (partitionId, iterator of (K, C)) for all partitions in order. With no spills it only sorts the in-memory collection (by partition, plus key if an Ordering is given); with spills it merges spilled files and memory through merge().

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.iterator
nodes.summary: Sets isShuffleSort to false (so forced spilling is allowed) and flattens partitionedIterator into one iterator of sorted or aggregated records.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.insertAllAndUpdateMetrics
nodes.summary: Inserts all records, records memory and disk spill and peak memory in the task metrics, registers a task completion listener that calls stop(), and returns a CompletionIterator over iterator().

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.writePartitionedMapOutput
nodes.summary: Called by SortShuffleWriter to write the sorted data of a map task through a ShuffleMapOutputWriter. Without spills it streams the sorted in-memory collection partition by partition; with spills it iterates the merged partitionedIterator. Each partition is written through a ShufflePartitionPairsWriter that also feeds the per-partition checksum, then spill and memory metrics are added to the task.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.stop
nodes.summary: Deletes all spill and forced-spill files, clears the lists, drops references to the in-memory map, buffer and reading iterator, and releases the memory held by the Spillable.

nodes.name: ExternalSorter.groupByPartition
nodes.summary: Groups an iterator of ((partition, key), combiner) that is already sorted by partition id into one sub-iterator per partition.

nodes.name: IteratorForPartition
nodes.summary: Iterator over a buffered stream that yields only the elements of one partition id, stripping the partition id from the key.

nodes.name: SpillableIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator over the in-memory sorted data that can be switched to an on-disk copy: its spill() writes the remaining upstream records to a SpilledFile registered in forceSpillFiles and swaps upstream to a SpillReader, guarded by SPILL_LOCK, so memory can be released while a reducer is reading.

nodes.name: SpillableIterator.spill
nodes.summary: Spills the unread part of the upstream iterator to disk once, logs the freed memory, and prepares nextUpstream to read back from the spill file by partition.

nodes.name: SpillableIterator.readNext
nodes.summary: Under SPILL_LOCK, swaps in the on-disk upstream if a spill happened and returns the next element or null.

nodes.name: BypassMergeSortShuffleWriter.java
nodes.summary: Shuffle writer for the bypass-merge-sort path: writes each record to its own temporary file per reduce partition without buffering in memory, then concatenates those files into one map output file. SortShuffleManager only picks it when there is no map-side combine and the partition count is at most spark.shuffle.sort.bypassMergeThreshold.
nodes.languageNotes: Package-private final Java class; uses Scala interop (scala.Option, None$, MapStatus$.MODULE$, package$.MODULE$ for config entries).

nodes.name: BypassMergeSortShuffleWriter
nodes.summary: Hash-style fallback of sort-based shuffle: opens one DiskBlockObjectWriter (and serializer) per reduce partition, routes each record by partitioner, then concatenates the per-partition files into a single output served through the shuffle block resolver. Cheap for few partitions but inefficient for many because all partition files and serializers are open at once.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Main write path. Creates a map output writer; for an empty input commits empty partitions, otherwise creates one temp shuffle block file and DiskBlockObjectWriter per partition, writes every record to the writer chosen by partitioner.getPartition(key), commits all segments, then concatenates via writePartitionedData and builds the MapStatus. Aborts the map output writer on failure.

nodes.name: getPartitionLengths
nodes.summary: Returns the byte length of each reduce partition in the final map output file.

nodes.name: writePartitionedData
nodes.summary: Concatenates every per-partition temp file into the combined map output through the ShufflePartitionWriter, choosing channel (transferTo) or stream copy, deletes each temp file, records write time, and commits all partitions to obtain the partition lengths.

nodes.name: writePartitionedDataWithChannel
nodes.summary: Copies one partition temp file into the output using NIO channel transfer (Utils.copyFileStreamNIO), closing input and output channels while preserving the original exception.

nodes.name: writePartitionedDataWithStream
nodes.summary: Copies one partition temp file into the output using plain Java streams (Utils.copyStream) when the NIO channel path is disabled or unavailable.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Finishes the writer: on success returns the stored MapStatus (error if write() was never called); on failure closes and deletes all open partition writers. A stopping flag prevents doing the cleanup twice.

nodes.name: UnsafeShuffleWriter.java
nodes.summary: Serialized (unsafe) shuffle writer: serializes each record immediately, inserts the bytes into ShuffleExternalSorter, which sorts compact pointers by partition id, and then merges spill files into a single map output. It avoids deserializing records during merge and is limited to a maximum number of reduce partitions.
nodes.languageNotes: Public Java class annotated @Private; two write overloads (java.util.Iterator for tests, scala Iterator for the ShuffleWriter contract).

nodes.name: UnsafeShuffleWriter
nodes.summary: ShuffleWriter for the serialized shuffle path. The constructor rejects shuffles with more reduce partitions than SortShuffleManager.MAX_SHUFFLE_OUTPUT_PARTITIONS_FOR_SERIALIZED_MODE, opens a ShuffleExternalSorter, and later merges its spills (fast concatenation when the compression codec allows it, otherwise slow decompress and recompress).

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes all records: serializes and inserts each into the sorter via insertRecordIntoSorter, then calls closeAndWriteOutput. A finally block cleans up sorter resources without masking an earlier error.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Creates the ShuffleExternalSorter (with task memory manager, initial sort buffer size, partition count) plus the serialization buffer and stream used for each record.

nodes.name: closeAndWriteOutput
nodes.summary: Closes the sorter to get SpillInfo files, merges them into the final output via mergeSpills, deletes the spill files, and builds the MapStatus with partition lengths and checksum.

nodes.name: insertRecordIntoSorter
nodes.summary: Computes the partition id, serializes key and value into a reusable buffer, and hands the serialized bytes plus partition id to ShuffleExternalSorter.insertRecord; also updates the optional row-based checksum.

nodes.name: mergeSpills
nodes.summary: Chooses how to produce the final output: no spills yields an empty committed output, a single spill can be transferred directly if the executor components support a single-file writer, otherwise the standard merge writer is used.

nodes.name: mergeSpillsUsingStandardWriter
nodes.summary: Merges multiple spills through a ShuffleMapOutputWriter. Picks a fast merge (transferTo, or file streams without codec) when compression is off or the codec supports concatenation of serialized streams, otherwise a slow merge that decompresses and recompresses; aborts the writer on error.

nodes.name: mergeSpillsWithFileStream
nodes.summary: Merges spill files per partition using buffered Java file streams, optionally wrapping with encryption and a compression codec (slow path). Typically slower than the NIO merge and used for codecs without concatenation support, encryption, or when transferTo is disabled.

nodes.name: mergeSpillsWithTransferTo
nodes.summary: Merges spill files by using NIO transferTo to copy each spill's bytes for every partition straight into the output channel, only safe when the codec and serializer support concatenation; tracks per-spill channel positions and write time.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Reports peak execution memory to task metrics, returns the stored MapStatus on success (error if write() was not called), and cleans up sorter memory and spill files if it is still open after a failure.

nodes.name: StreamFallbackChannelWrapper
nodes.summary: Nested private static class that adapts an OutputStream into a WritableByteChannelWrapper so the transferTo merge works when the partition writer offers no channel.

nodes.name: getPartitionLengths
nodes.summary: Returns the byte length of each reduce partition in the merged map output.

nodes.name: ShuffleExternalSorter.java
nodes.summary: Memory consumer that backs the serialized shuffle path: appends serialized records into memory pages, tracks pointers in a ShuffleInMemorySorter, and on memory pressure sorts by partition id and writes sorted spill files. It does not merge spills itself; UnsafeShuffleWriter does that.
nodes.languageNotes: Package-private final Java class extending MemoryConsumer; uses Platform.copyMemory and UnsafeAlignedOffset to copy record bytes between pages and byte arrays.

nodes.name: ShuffleExternalSorter
nodes.summary: Sort-based-shuffle sorter that stores records in Tungsten-style memory pages, sorts record pointers by partition id, and writes each sorted batch to one file with a segment per partition. Spills when the record count or memory threshold is exceeded or when the memory manager asks it to.

nodes.name: writeSortedFile
nodes.summary: Gets the sorted pointer iterator from ShuffleInMemorySorter and copies each record from its page into a temp shuffle file through a DiskBlockObjectWriter, committing one file segment per partition and recording partition lengths in a SpillInfo. For spills, bytes count as disk spill rather than shuffle write metrics.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: MemoryConsumer callback that responds to memory pressure: writes the sorted records to a spill file, frees the memory pages, resets the in-memory sorter, and returns the number of bytes freed.

nodes.name: freeMemory
nodes.summary: Frees all allocated data pages, resets the current page and cursor, and returns the number of bytes released.

nodes.name: cleanupResources
nodes.summary: Error-handling cleanup that frees pages, frees the in-memory sorter, and deletes any spill files already written.

nodes.name: growPointerArrayIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Ensures the pointer array has room for another record: tries to allocate an array twice the current size (which may itself trigger a spill), expands it if there is still no room, and spills when the array would be too large for one page.

nodes.name: acquireNewPageIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Allocates a new data page when none exists or the current page cannot hold the required bytes, and tracks it in allocatedPages and the memory usage total.

nodes.name: insertRecord
nodes.summary: Appends one serialized record: spills if the record-count or memory threshold is crossed, grows the pointer array, gets page space, stores the length-prefixed bytes in the page, and registers the encoded address and partition id in ShuffleInMemorySorter.

nodes.name: closeAndGetSpills
nodes.summary: Sorts and writes the remaining in-memory records (as the final file if no spill happened yet), frees memory and the in-memory sorter, and returns the SpillInfo array.

nodes.name: ShuffleInMemorySorter.java
nodes.summary: In-memory pointer sorter for serialized shuffle: stores each record as one packed 8-byte long (partition id plus page address, via PackedRecordPointer) in a LongArray and sorts them by partition id with radix sort or TimSort. Only the pointers move, never the record bytes.
nodes.languageNotes: Package-private final Java class; sort uses RadixSort when enabled, otherwise Sorter (TimSort) with a ShuffleSortDataFormat over a scratch LongArray.

nodes.name: ShuffleInMemorySorter
nodes.summary: Holds a LongArray of packed record pointers and exposes insertRecord, pointer-array growth, reset and a sorted iterator. Part of the array is reserved as sort scratch space, so usable capacity is half the array for radix sort or two thirds for TimSort.

nodes.name: getUsableCapacity
nodes.summary: Computes how many pointers may be inserted: array size divided by 2 for radix sort or 1.5 for TimSort, leaving room for the sort buffer.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Clears the record count, frees the pointer array, and allocates a fresh array of the initial size; nulls the array and zeroes capacity in between so a spill triggered by allocation is a no-op.

nodes.name: expandPointerArray
nodes.summary: Copies existing pointers into a larger LongArray, frees the old array, and recomputes usable capacity.

nodes.name: insertRecord
nodes.summary: Packs the record pointer and partition id into one long with PackedRecordPointer.packPointer and appends it to the array; throws if there is no room.

nodes.name: ShuffleSorterIterator
nodes.summary: Nested static iterator-like class (hasNext, loadNext) over the sorted pointer array that decodes each long into a reusable PackedRecordPointer, avoiding Java Iterator overhead to help inlining.

nodes.name: getSortedIterator
nodes.summary: Sorts the pointer array by partition id, using RadixSort over the partition id bytes when radix sort is on or Sorter with a comparator and the unused tail of the array as buffer otherwise, and returns a ShuffleSorterIterator.

nodes.name: AppendOnlyMap.scala
nodes.summary: Open-addressing hash map specialized for append-only use (keys never removed, values may change) with quadratic probing, a power-of-2 table, and keys and values interleaved in one array. It offers changeValue, which updates a value from its old value in one probe pass, and a destructive in-place sorted iterator.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class storing keys and values in a single AnyRef array and handling null keys separately; companion private object holds MAXIMUM_CAPACITY (2^29).

nodes.name: AppendOnlyMap
nodes.summary: DeveloperApi hash map with quadratic probing and 0.7 load factor, up to 375809638 elements. Supports apply, update, changeValue, iteration and a destructive sorted iterator that sorts in place without extra memory.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Looks up the value for a key by probing from the rehashed position; returns null for absent keys and handles the null key via a separate field.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Sets the value for a key, inserting a new entry (and growing the table through incrementSize) or overwriting an existing one.

nodes.name: changeValue
nodes.summary: Sets a key's value to updateFunc(hadValue, oldValue) in one probe pass and returns the new value; the core primitive for combiner-style aggregation.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over (key, value) pairs by scanning the table, yielding the null-key value first if present.

nodes.name: incrementSize
nodes.summary: Increments the element count and calls growTable when it exceeds the grow threshold.

nodes.name: growTable
nodes.summary: Doubles the capacity (bounded by 2^29), allocates a new data array, and rehashes every existing entry into it.

nodes.name: destructiveSortedIterator
nodes.summary: Packs entries to the front of the data array, sorts them in place with Sorter and KVArraySortDataFormat, and returns an iterator; the map becomes invalid afterwards.

nodes.name: PartitionedAppendOnlyMap.scala
nodes.summary: Spark-private AppendOnlyMap variant whose keys are (partition id, key) tuples, so a shuffle sorter can hold records tagged by reduce partition and iterate them in partition order. It supplies a destructive sorted iterator ordered by partition id first, then by an optional key comparator.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class mixing SizeTrackingAppendOnlyMap with WritablePartitionedPairCollection; keys are (Int, K) tuples.

nodes.name: PartitionedAppendOnlyMap
nodes.summary: Wraps an append-only map keyed by (partition, key) and implements WritablePartitionedPairCollection with insert and a partition-ordered destructive sorted iterator.

nodes.name: partitionedDestructiveSortedIterator
nodes.summary: Sorts the map in place by partition id, and by the optional key comparator within a partition, via destructiveSortedIterator.

nodes.name: insert
nodes.summary: Inserts a value under the (partition, key) tuple via update.

nodes.name: WatermarkPropagator.scala
nodes.summary: Computes the input watermark per stateful operator for each batch. UseSingleWatermarkPropagator reuses the one global watermark (legacy, pre SPARK-40925); PropagateWatermarkSimulator walks the physical plan children first, applying min over children and each stateful operator's produceOutputWatermark, to support multiple stateful operators. Late events use the previous batch's watermark, eviction the current batch's.
nodes.languageNotes: Sealed trait with a no-op object, a legacy implementation and a simulator; batch ids are kept in java.util.TreeMap so old entries can be purged cheaply.

nodes.name: WatermarkPropagator
nodes.summary: Sealed interface: propagate(batchId, plan, originWatermark) computes watermarks, getInputWatermarkForLateEvents / getInputWatermarkForEviction return the value for a stateful operator id, and purge drops cached results for batches that will not be re-run. The companion's apply picks the implementation from STATEFUL_OPERATOR_ALLOW_MULTIPLE and noop() returns the no-op one.

nodes.name: NoOpWatermarkPropagator
nodes.summary: Dummy implementation that does nothing and returns Long.MinValue for both watermarks; used to build a dummy IncrementalExecution.

nodes.name: UseSingleWatermarkPropagator
nodes.summary: Compatibility mode that stores only the origin (global) watermark per batch and returns it for both late events and eviction of every operator (behaviour before multiple stateful operators). Asserts that a batch's watermark never changes once cached.

nodes.name: propagate
nodes.summary: Caches originWatermark for the batch id (no-op for batch < 0) and asserts consistency if it was already cached.

nodes.name: purge
nodes.summary: Removes cached watermarks of batches up to and including the given batch id.

nodes.name: PropagateWatermarkSimulator
nodes.summary: Simulates watermark flow through the physical plan. Input watermark of a node = min of its children's output watermarks (children without a watermark ignored); watermark nodes output the origin watermark; stateless nodes pass through; stateful nodes output produceOutputWatermark(input). Results are stored as batchId -> (stateful operator id -> input watermark).

nodes.name: getInputWatermarks
nodes.summary: Gathers the output watermarks of a node's children (looking through InMemoryTableScanExec, AdaptiveSparkPlanExec and QueryStageExec) and drops children with none; throws if a child was not registered.

nodes.name: doSimulate
nodes.summary: Traverses the plan bottom-up (foreachUp): EventTimeWatermarkExec records the origin watermark and throws AnalysisException if it already has an input watermark (redefining watermark is unsupported); StateStoreWriter records its input watermark (min of children) by state operator id and computes its output watermark; other nodes pass the min through.

nodes.name: propagate
nodes.summary: Skips batch < 0, asserts that a cached batch keeps the same watermark, skips simulation when the origin watermark is 0 (every operator gets 0), otherwise runs doSimulate.

nodes.name: getInputWatermark
nodes.summary: Looks up the operator's input watermark for a batch, clamped to at least 0; returns 0 for batch < 0 or when propagation was skipped, and throws if the operator is missing otherwise.

nodes.name: getInputWatermarkForLateEvents
nodes.summary: Late events are judged against the watermark of the previous micro-batch (batchId - 1).

nodes.name: getInputWatermarkForEviction
nodes.summary: State eviction uses the watermark of the current batch.

nodes.name: purge
nodes.summary: Removes cached batch watermarks and per-operator input watermarks up to the given batch id.

nodes.name: EventTimeWatermarkExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical operators for event-time watermarking: EventTimeWatermarkExec observes the max/min/avg event time of each micro-batch into an accumulator (the driver later derives the watermark from it), and UpdateEventTimeColumnExec re-tags the event time column and fails the query if a child emits rows older than the watermark. Event time is measured in milliseconds.
nodes.languageNotes: Case classes extending UnaryExecNode; the EventTimeStatsAccum accumulator is registered with the SparkContext so task-side updates are merged on the driver.

nodes.name: EventTimeStats
nodes.summary: Mutable case class holding max, min, running average and count of event times (in ms). add() folds in one value and merge() combines partial stats from different partitions using a count-weighted average; the companion's zero starts with max=Long.MinValue and min=Long.MaxValue.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Updates max, min, count and the incremental running average with one event time value.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another EventTimeStats (no-op if empty, copy if this is empty, otherwise max/min/count plus a count-weighted average).

nodes.name: EventTimeStatsAccum
nodes.summary: AccumulatorV2[Long, EventTimeStats] that collects event time stats in a batch. Tasks call add() per row; partial accumulators are merged by merge() and the driver reads value to get the batch max used for the watermark.

nodes.name: EventTimeWatermarkExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator for withWatermark. Passes rows through unchanged while feeding every row's event time (converted from micros to ms) into eventTimeStats; its output updates the event time column metadata with the delay in ms. WatermarkTracker later computes watermark = max observed event time minus delayMs.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Maps each partition of the child RDD, projecting the event time column and adding its value (in ms) to the accumulator before returning the row untouched.

nodes.name: UpdateEventTimeColumnExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator that switches the event time column (used by transformWithState output) and checks that rows emitted by the child are not older than the late-event watermark; if one is, it throws emittedRowsAreOlderThanWatermark and fails the query. It is stateless and keeps child ordering and partitioning.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Wraps the child iterator with a predicate built from WatermarkSupport.watermarkExpression and throws if any row is older than eventTimeWatermarkForLateEvents.

nodes.name: ProgressReporter.scala
nodes.summary: Builds and publishes StreamingQueryProgress for a streaming query. ProgressReporter keeps the recent-progress buffer and posts QueryProgressEvent/QueryIdleEvent; ProgressContext times each trigger, records start/end/latest offsets, extracts per-source, sink, state operator and event time stats from the executed plan, and computes inputRowsPerSecond and processedRowsPerSecond.
nodes.languageNotes: ProgressContext is abstract and is subclassed by the micro-batch and continuous execution contexts; finishTrigger is overloaded.

nodes.name: ProgressReporter
nodes.summary: Holds the bounded queue of recent StreamingQueryProgress (size streamingProgressRetention), exposes recentProgress and lastProgress, posts progress and idle events to the session's listener bus, and formats timestamps as UTC ISO8601 strings. Also owns the StateStoreCoordinator ref and the no-data progress interval.

nodes.name: recentProgress
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of all buffered progress updates (what query.recentProgress exposes to PySpark).

nodes.name: lastProgress
nodes.summary: Returns the newest progress update or null if none exist (query.lastProgress).

nodes.name: updateProgress
nodes.summary: Resets the no-execution timestamp, appends the progress to the buffer, posts a QueryProgressEvent to listeners and logs it at INFO.

nodes.name: addNewProgress
nodes.summary: Appends progress to the buffer under lock and dequeues oldest entries to honour the retention limit.

nodes.name: updateIdleness
nodes.summary: For triggers that executed no batch: if at least noDataProgressEventInterval ms passed since the last event, buffers the idle progress and posts a QueryIdleEvent (except on the first one).

nodes.name: formatTimestamp
nodes.summary: Formats epoch millis as an ISO8601 UTC string ('yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'') used for timestamp, watermark and event time fields in progress.

nodes.name: ProgressContext
nodes.summary: Per-batch bookkeeping for a streaming query execution: trigger timings (reportTimeTaken -> durationMs), offset ranges for the trigger, current status message, and logic that turns the last IncrementalExecution into a StreamingQueryProgress (sources, sink, stateOperators, eventTime, observedMetrics). Companion object defines ExecutionStats.

nodes.name: ExecutionStats
nodes.summary: Case class bundling inputRows per source, stateOperators progress, eventTimeStats strings (max/min/avg/watermark) and optional sink outputRows for one trigger.

nodes.name: reportTimeTaken
nodes.summary: Runs a body, measures wall-clock ms with the trigger clock and accumulates it under a key in the next progress's durationMs (e.g. addBatch, getBatch, walCommit).

nodes.name: startTrigger
nodes.summary: Starts a new trigger: remembers the previous start time, sets the current start time, clears the recorded offsets and durations.

nodes.name: recordTriggerOffsets
nodes.summary: Stores the start, end and latest offsets (as JSON strings) for each source; must run before committedOffsets is updated.

nodes.name: finishNoExecutionTrigger
nodes.summary: Finalizes a trigger without a batch: reuses the latest executed batch's stats reset for no execution, builds a progress and passes it to ProgressReporter.updateIdleness.

nodes.name: finishTrigger
nodes.summary: Finalizes a trigger that ran a batch: optionally validates state store commits with the coordinator, extracts ExecutionStats and observed metrics from the last IncrementalExecution, builds StreamingQueryProgress, publishes it via ProgressReporter.updateProgress and optionally asks the coordinator to log lagging state stores. An overload (lines 423-430) derives the per-source row counts first.

nodes.name: constructNewProgress
nodes.summary: Assembles StreamingQueryProgress: batchDuration, durationMs, eventTime, stateOperators, sources, sink and observedMetrics. processedRowsPerSecond divides by processing time (at least 1 ms); input rate divides by time between trigger starts.

nodes.name: extractSourceProgress
nodes.summary: Creates a SourceProgress per distinct source with description, start/end/latest offsets, numInputRows, inputRowsPerSecond = rows / seconds between trigger starts (infinity for the first trigger), processedRowsPerSecond = rows / processing seconds, plus metrics from ReportsSourceMetrics sources.

nodes.name: extractSinkProgress
nodes.summary: Creates SinkProgress with sink description, number of output rows from execStats and metrics if the sink implements ReportsSinkMetrics.

nodes.name: warnIfFinishTriggerTakesTooLong
nodes.summary: Logs a warning if building and publishing progress took longer than both one minute and the batch processing time.

nodes.name: extractSourceToNumInputRows
nodes.summary: Sums numOutputRows of StreamSourceAwareSparkPlan leaves per source in the executed plan; falls back to the legacy method if the captured sources differ from the batch's new data.

nodes.name: legacyExtractSourceToNumInputRows
nodes.summary: Legacy per-source row counting: uses MicroBatchScanExec/RealTimeStreamScanExec for V2 sources, otherwise best-effort mapping of logical plan leaves to executed plan leaves (SPARK-24050), with CTE inlining and a one-time warning on mismatch.

nodes.name: extractStateOperatorMetrics
nodes.summary: Collects StateOperatorProgress from every StateStoreWriter in the executed plan via getProgress(), which feeds the stateOperators array of the progress JSON.

nodes.name: extractExecutionStats
nodes.summary: Builds ExecutionStats: adds a formatted watermark entry if the plan has an EventTimeWatermark; always collects state operator metrics (SPARK-19378); if there was new data adds event time max/min/avg from the first EventTimeWatermarkExec with count > 0, input rows and sink output rows.

nodes.name: resetExecStatsForNoExecution
nodes.summary: For idle triggers, zeroes batch-bound values (inputRows, numRowsUpdated, numRowsDroppedByWatermark, numRowsRemoved, outputRows) and keeps only the watermark entry of eventTime stats.

nodes.name: extractObservedMetrics
nodes.summary: Returns the observedMetrics map (from df.observe) of the last QueryExecution, or empty if none.

nodes.name: WatermarkTracker.scala
nodes.summary: Tracks the global event-time watermark of a streaming query. WatermarkTracker keeps one watermark per EventTimeWatermarkExec node (max observed event time minus delay, only moving forward), then picks the global watermark with a MultipleWatermarkPolicy (min by default, or max), never letting it decrease.
nodes.languageNotes: Sealed trait with case-object policies (Scala algebraic data type) selected by a config string.

nodes.name: MultipleWatermarkPolicy
nodes.summary: Sealed trait choosing the global watermark when a query has several watermark operators; its companion maps the config name 'min' (default) or 'max' to MinWatermark or MaxWatermark and rejects other names.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Resolves a policy name (case-insensitive 'min' or 'max') to its case object, otherwise throws IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: MinWatermark
nodes.summary: Default policy: global watermark is the minimum of operator watermarks, so it advances only when all inputs advance (the slowest input). Safest for late-data dropping and state cleanup.

nodes.name: chooseGlobalWatermark
nodes.summary: Returns the minimum of the operator watermarks (asserts the list is non-empty).

nodes.name: MaxWatermark
nodes.summary: Policy where the global watermark is the maximum of operator watermarks, so it advances as fast as the fastest input; most aggressive and may cause unexpected drops if a slow stream is delayed.

nodes.name: chooseGlobalWatermark
nodes.summary: Returns the maximum of the operator watermarks (asserts the list is non-empty).

nodes.name: WatermarkTracker
nodes.summary: Holds a map from each EventTimeWatermark node id (collected from the initial logical plan) to its Option watermark plus the global watermark in ms (starts at 0). Thread-safe via synchronized. Its companion apply reads the multiple-watermark policy from the session conf (default min).

nodes.name: setWatermark
nodes.summary: Overwrites the global watermark in ms, e.g. when restoring from checkpointed offset metadata.

nodes.name: updateWatermark
nodes.summary: Collects EventTimeWatermarkExec nodes from the executed plan; for each with count > 0 computes max event time - delayMs and keeps it only if larger than the previous value (throws on unknown node id). Then applies the policy over per-operator values (missing treated as 0) and raises the global watermark only if the chosen value is greater.

nodes.name: currentWatermark
nodes.summary: Returns the current global watermark in ms under the lock.

nodes.name: watermarkMap
nodes.summary: Returns an immutable copy of the per-operator watermark map (private[sql], mainly for tests and inspection).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Companion factory: reads the policy name from STREAMING_MULTIPLE_WATERMARK_POLICY in the session conf (restored from the checkpoint on recovery, default 'min') and builds a WatermarkTracker.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract StreamExecution base class that owns one streaming query: its lifecycle state machine, its dedicated query thread, the checkpoint offset log and commit log, and the await/stop APIs. Subclasses (MicroBatchExecution) supply the batch loop via runActivatedStream.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class mixing in Logging; uses AtomicReference for the state, CountDownLatch for start/initialization/termination, and a fair ReentrantLock plus Condition to wake awaitOffset and processAllAvailable callers.

nodes.name: State
nodes.summary: Sealed-style lifecycle marker trait with the four case objects INITIALIZING, ACTIVE, TERMINATED and RECONFIGURING that StreamExecution stores in an AtomicReference.

nodes.name: StreamExecution
nodes.summary: Abstract class that manages a streaming query running in its own thread. It builds a checkpoint metadata helper (offsetLog and commitLog), tracks committedOffsets, exposes status, progress, await and stop APIs, and delegates the actual batch loop to the abstract runActivatedStream. Its companion object holds constants such as QUERY_ID_KEY and the interruption-exception helpers.

nodes.name: QueryExecutionThread
nodes.summary: Abstract UninterruptibleThread subclass used as the stream execution thread; some code checks classOf[QueryExecutionThread] to require running on this thread.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.getLatestExecutionContext
nodes.summary: Abstract hook returning the latest StreamExecutionContext (the per-batch state: start offsets, end offsets, status, execution plan); status, availableOffsets and lastExecution all read through it.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.getStartOffsetsOfLatestBatch
nodes.summary: Returns the start offsets of the latest planned batch from the latest execution context.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.availableOffsets
nodes.summary: Returns the end (formerly called available) offsets of the latest planned batch as a StreamProgress, read from the latest execution context.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.logicalPlan
nodes.summary: Abstract definition of the base logical plan reused across batch runs; MicroBatchExecution implements it by swapping streaming relations for materialized sources.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.offsetLog
nodes.summary: Lazy val exposing the write-ahead OffsetSeqLog taken from the query checkpoint metadata; offsets for a batch are written here before the batch runs.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.commitLog
nodes.summary: Lazy val exposing the CommitLog from the query checkpoint metadata; an entry is written here after a batch finishes to mark it committed.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.checkpointFile
nodes.summary: Builds the string path of a named file or directory (such as state) under the resolved checkpoint root.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.start
nodes.summary: Starts the query: marks the execution thread as daemon, starts it, and blocks on a latch until the thread is running and QueryStartedEvent has been posted to listeners.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.runActivatedStream
nodes.summary: Abstract method that subclasses implement to run the activated stream until stopped; MicroBatchExecution runs the trigger loop here.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.runStream
nodes.summary: Body of the query thread: sets job group and logging context, posts QueryStartedEvent, configures the cloned session (disables CBO, sets shuffle partitions), forces logicalPlan, moves state INITIALIZING to ACTIVE and calls runActivatedStream. On error it builds a StreamingQueryException; the finally block stops sources, sets TERMINATED, posts QueryTerminatedEvent, may delete a temp checkpoint and releases latches.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.isInterruptedByStop
nodes.summary: Returns true only when the state is already TERMINATED and the throwable is recognized as an interruption exception, so a user stop() is not reported as a failure.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.postEvent
nodes.summary: Forwards a StreamingQueryListener event to the session's streaming query manager listeners.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.stopSources
nodes.summary: Stops every unique source, logging a warning instead of failing when a source throws NonFatal exceptions.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.interruptAndAwaitExecutionThreadTermination
nodes.summary: Interrupts the query thread and joins it for up to spark.sql.streaming.stopTimeout; throws TimeoutException with the thread's stack trace as cause if it is still alive.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.awaitOffset
nodes.summary: Test-oriented method that blocks until the committed offset of the given source reaches at least the given offset, waiting on the progress lock condition and rethrowing the stream death cause.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.assertAwaitThread
nodes.summary: Guards the await APIs by throwing IllegalStateException when called from the query execution thread itself, which would deadlock.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.awaitInitialization
nodes.summary: Waits on the initialization latch for up to the timeout and rethrows the stream death cause if the query already failed.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.processAllAvailable
nodes.summary: Blocks the caller until a batch completes with no new data (noNewData) or the query stops, polling the progress lock condition and surfacing any stream failure; this is what StreamingQuery.processAllAvailable() calls.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.awaitTermination
nodes.summary: Two overloads of StreamingQuery.awaitTermination: one waits on the termination latch indefinitely, the other waits up to a timeout and returns whether the query is no longer active. Both throw the stream death cause if the query failed.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.explainInternal
nodes.summary: Builds the explain text by running a StreamingExplainCommand over lastExecution, or returns a placeholder message while no plan exists yet; StreamingQueryWrapper exposes it to Python.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.toDebugString
nodes.summary: Formats a debug report with query identifier, committed and available offsets, state, thread state and optionally the logical plan; used when building StreamingQueryException.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.getBatchDescriptionString
nodes.summary: Returns the multi-line job description (query name, id, runId, batch id or init) shown in the Spark UI for jobs of the current batch.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.createWrite
nodes.summary: Creates a DSv2 Write from a SupportsWrite table according to the output mode: plain build for Append, truncate for Complete, and the update-as-append builder for Update; requires the builder to support the chosen mode.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.purge
nodes.summary: Purges old metadata below the threshold batch id from both the offset log and the commit log.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.purgeStatefulMetadata
nodes.summary: Collects StatefulOperator nodes from a physical plan and, for state store writers with operator state metadata version 2, purges metadata files via OperatorStateMetadataV2FileManager.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.isInterruptionException
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that recursively unwraps wrapper exceptions (execution, unchecked, ForeachBatch, Spark and Py4J errors) to decide whether the root cause is an interruption or a cancelled job group.

nodes.name: StreamExecution.containsSpecialCharsInPath
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that returns whether a Hadoop path contains characters that are escaped when converted to a URI.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the micro-batch engine of Structured Streaming: MicroBatchExecution extends StreamExecution and, for each trigger, plans offsets and writes them to the offset log, rewrites the logical plan to read only the new data, runs it as a normal batch query through IncrementalExecution, then writes the commit log. It also handles restart recovery from the offset and commit logs.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with many Spark-internal collaborators; most batch bookkeeping lives in a MicroBatchExecutionContext, and a mix-in trait (AsyncLogPurge) supplies async purging of old log entries.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution
nodes.summary: Concrete StreamExecution for micro-batch processing (also used for real-time and Trigger.AvailableNow variants). Per batch it asks each source for its latest offset, logs the planned offsets to the write-ahead offset log, replaces streaming relations in the logical plan with the data for those offsets, runs the plan as an ordinary query via IncrementalExecution, and then records the batch in the commit log. Restart logic reads both logs to resume exactly where the last committed batch ended.

nodes.name: OffsetHolder
nodes.summary: Logical LeafNode with empty output that carries a v2 source's start and optional end offset through the plan transform in runBatch, acting as a stand-in for the new-data plan that v1 sources return.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.setLatestExecutionContext
nodes.summary: Synchronized setter that replaces the latest execution context only if its batch id is not older than the current one, so progress tracking never moves backwards.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.getTrigger
nodes.summary: Maps the user Trigger to a TriggerExecutor: ProcessingTimeTrigger to ProcessingTimeExecutor, OneTimeTrigger to SingleBatchExecutor, RealTimeTrigger to a zero-interval ProcessingTimeExecutor, and AvailableNowTrigger to MultiBatchExecutor (or SingleBatchExecutor if a source cannot support Trigger.AvailableNow and the wrapper is disabled).

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.initialLatestOffsetSeq
nodes.summary: Lazy cached result of the first offsetLog.getLatest() call, reused by logicalPlan and initializeExecution to avoid listing the offsets directory twice at startup.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.logicalPlan
nodes.summary: Lazy val that builds the reusable streaming plan on the query thread: each StreamingRelation or StreamingRelationV2 is turned into a StreamingExecutionRelation (v1 Source) or StreamingDataSourceV2ScanRelation (v2 MicroBatchStream), sources and their id map are collected, the TriggerExecutor and per-source read limits (uniqueSources) are set, and the plan is wrapped in WriteToMicroBatchDataSource (v2 sink) or WriteToMicroBatchDataSourceV1 (v1 Sink).

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.stop
nodes.summary: Sets state to TERMINATED so the loop knows the interrupt is intentional, cancels the Spark job group, interrupts and awaits the query thread, and cancels the job group again to catch jobs spawned in between.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.containsGlobalAggregateOrLimit
nodes.summary: Returns whether the logical plan has an Aggregate without grouping expressions or a GlobalLimit; used to skip state store commit validation for such queries.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.cleanup
nodes.summary: Calls the parent cleanup and shuts down the async log purge executor pool.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.initializeExecution
nodes.summary: Prepares the first MicroBatchExecutionContext: reads the latest offset-log and commit-log batch ids, optionally fails on an unfinished repartition batch, trims extra offset-log entries in real-time mode, hands the last seen offset to sources, fixes the offset log format version and OffsetSeqMetadata, then calls populateStartOffsets.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.checkUnfinishedRepartitionBatch
nodes.summary: Throws an unfinished-repartition error when the latest offset-log batch is uncommitted and is a repartition batch, so the query refuses to restart in that state.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.disableAQESupportInStatelessIfUnappropriated
nodes.summary: Turns off adaptive query execution for the stream session when the trigger is real-time or the analyzed plan contains a streaming stateful operator (aggregate, dedup, stream-stream join, mapGroupsWithState, transformWithState, global limit).

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.runActivatedStream
nodes.summary: The trigger loop entry point: initializes the first batch context, gives it to the TriggerExecutor via setNextBatch, then calls triggerExecutor.execute with executeOneBatch as the per-trigger handler.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.executeOneBatch
nodes.summary: One trigger firing: if still active, constructs the next batch (planning offsets and writing the offset log), runs it with runBatch if constructed, records progress, wakes waiters on the progress lock, then moves to the next context; if no batch could be built it sleeps for the polling delay or, under AvailableNow, terminates the query. Returns whether the query is still active.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.validateOffsetLogAndGetPrevOffset
nodes.summary: Sanity check for restart: for any batch other than 0 it requires the previous batch's offset-log entry to exist and returns it, else throws IllegalStateException asking the user to fix the checkpoint.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.populateStartOffsets
nodes.summary: Restart recovery: reads the latest offset-log entry, treats it as the batch to re-run, then consults the commit log. If that batch was committed it moves to the next batch with start offsets equal to the old end offsets and restores the watermark; otherwise it re-executes the logged batch. A fresh checkpoint starts at batch 0. Also restores state store checkpoint ids and sink metadata from the commit log.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.verifyNewCheckpointDirectory
nodes.summary: For a brand-new query, checks via CheckpointFileManager that the offsets, state and commits subdirectories are absent or empty and throws a checkpoint-location-not-empty error otherwise.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.isNewDataAvailable
nodes.summary: Returns true if any source's end offset differs from its start offset (or has no start offset); always true for real-time triggers.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.getStartOffset
nodes.summary: Returns the start offset to pass to latestOffset(start, readLimit): null for an unstarted v1 Source, or a deserialized or initial offset for a v2 MicroBatchStream.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.constructNextBatch
nodes.summary: Planning phase of a batch: asks each unique source for its next offset (getOffset or latestOffset with a ReadLimit), updates end offsets and OffsetSeqMetadata (watermark and timestamp), decides whether to build a batch (new data or a previous plan needs another batch), then writes offsets to the offset log in markMicroBatchStart, tells sources to commit the previous batch and purges old log entries.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.commitSources
nodes.summary: After offsets for the next batch are logged, tells each v1 Source or v2 MicroBatchStream to commit the offsets of the previous batch so it can discard older data.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.runBatch
nodes.summary: Execution phase of a batch: gets new data from each source for (start, end], uses logicalPlan.transform to replace each StreamingExecutionRelation with the batch's data plan (or a v2 relation with offsets, or an empty LocalRelation), rewrites current_timestamp-like expressions to batch timestamps, binds the batch id to the sink write node, builds an IncrementalExecution, runs it (Sink.addBatch for v1 or collect for v2), then calls markMicroBatchEnd.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.markMicroBatchStart
nodes.summary: Writes the batch's end offsets plus OffsetSeqMetadata to the offset log with offsetLog.add before the batch runs; throws a concurrent-update error if the entry already exists. Real-time mode delays this write.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.markMicroBatchExecutionStart
nodes.summary: Empty protected hook called after planning and before execution so subclasses can add pre-execution tasks.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.updateStateStoreCkptIdForOperator
nodes.summary: Validates that each partition's base state store checkpoint id matches what the driver sent and that the batch version equals batchId + 1, then stores the new checkpoint ids for the operator in currentStateStoreCkptId.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.updateStateStoreCkptId
nodes.summary: Walks the executed plan for StateStoreWriter operators and records each operator's state store checkpoint ids.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.setupStateStoreCommitTracking
nodes.summary: Before execution, when commit validation is enabled and the sink is a ForeachBatchSink without global aggregate or limit, tells the state store coordinator which stores and partitions are expected to commit for this batch; errors are logged, not thrown.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.markMicroBatchEnd
nodes.summary: Commit path after a batch ran: updates the watermark from the executed plan, records state store checkpoint ids, in real-time mode merges partition offsets and writes the offset log, then writes a CommitLog entry (with next batch watermark, state ids and optional V3 sink metadata) and finally advances committedOffsets.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.cleanUpLastExecutedMicroBatch
nodes.summary: Reads the previous batch's offset-log entry, commits those offsets on the sources and purges watermark propagator data older than two batches; throws if the previous entry is missing.

nodes.name: MicroBatchExecution.withProgressLocked
nodes.summary: Runs a block while holding the fair progress lock so waiters in processAllAvailable and awaitOffset see consistent progress.

nodes.name: StreamProgress.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StreamProgress, an immutable Map-like wrapper from SparkDataStream to Offset used to track start, end, available and committed offsets, with conversions to the offset-log entry formats (OffsetSeq for log version 1, OffsetMap for version 2).

nodes.name: StreamProgress
nodes.summary: Immutable Map[SparkDataStream, Offset] backed by a base map. StreamExecution uses it for committed, start and end offsets, and toOffsets serializes it into the offset-log entry format that matches the metadata version.

nodes.name: StreamProgress.toOffsets
nodes.summary: Dispatches on the metadata version: version 1 produces an OffsetSeq ordered by the source list, version 2 produces an OffsetMap keyed by source id, and any higher version raises a log-version-not-supported error.

nodes.name: StreamProgress.toOffsetSeq
nodes.summary: Builds a version-1 OffsetSeq by looking up each source's offset in order and attaching the metadata.

nodes.name: StreamProgress.toOffsetMap
nodes.summary: Builds a version-2 OffsetMap by mapping each source to its source id (failing if a source is missing from the id map) and attaching OffsetSeqMetadataV2.

nodes.name: StreamProgress.++
nodes.summary: Returns a new StreamProgress with the given updates merged into the base map; used to advance endOffsets and committedOffsets.

nodes.name: StreamingRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the logical plan leaf nodes that represent streaming input: StreamingRelation (created by DataStreamReader for a DataSource), StreamingExecutionRelation (the same relation bound to a live Source or stream, placed in the plan by StreamExecution) and StreamingRelationExec (dummy physical node for explain).

nodes.name: StreamingRelation
nodes.summary: Case-class LeafNode linking a streaming DataSource into a logical plan; it is only used to build a streaming DataFrame from the reader and is converted to a StreamingExecutionRelation when a query is run. Exposes file or source metadata columns and a default size estimate. Its companion apply derives the name, schema attributes and identifying name from the DataSource.

nodes.name: StreamingExecutionRelation
nodes.summary: Case-class LeafNode that links an instantiated streaming source (SparkDataStream) into the plan, with its output attributes, optional catalog table and identifying name. Each micro-batch replaces it with a plan for the data in that batch. Companion applies build it from a v1 Source's schema.

nodes.name: StreamingRelationExec
nodes.summary: Dummy physical leaf plan for StreamingRelation so that Dataset.explain works; doExecute always throws because it must never be executed.

nodes.name: StreamingRelation.metadataOutput
nodes.summary: Lazy val computing hidden metadata attributes from the underlying provider: a file metadata column for FileFormat sources or the metadata output of a SupportsStreamSourceMetadataColumns source.

nodes.name: StreamingRelation.withMetadataColumns
nodes.summary: Returns a copy with metadata attributes appended to the output when they are not already present.

nodes.name: Source.scala
nodes.summary: Declares the legacy (v1) streaming Source trait: a monotonically progressing data origin that reports its max Offset, returns a DataFrame for an offset range, and is told when offsets are committed. It extends SparkDataStream so v1 sources work in the v2 plumbing.

nodes.name: Source
nodes.summary: Trait for a v1 streaming source with schema, getOffset, getBatch(start, end] and commit. getBatch must return the same data for the same pair even after restart. The v2-style initialOffset, deserializeOffset and commit(OffsetV2) methods throw because they must not be called on v1 sources.

nodes.name: Source.getOffset
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the maximum available offset of this source, or None if it has never received data. The micro-batch planner calls it for each v1 source.

nodes.name: Source.getBatch
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns a streaming DataFrame with the data in (start, end]; None for start means from the first record. Must be deterministic for a given pair, since a batch may be replayed after failure.

nodes.name: Source.commit
nodes.summary: Default no-op hook telling the source that all data up to and including end has been processed and only larger offsets will be requested.

nodes.name: Sink.scala
