nodes.summary: Declares the legacy (v1) streaming Sink trait: an idempotent destination that accepts one DataFrame per batch id. It extends the DSv2 Table interface, with name, schema and capabilities deliberately throwing.

nodes.name: Sink
nodes.summary: Trait for a v1 streaming sink. Calling addBatch repeatedly with the same batchId (as happens after a failure) must add the data only once, which is how exactly-once output is achieved. The inherited Table methods name, schema and capabilities throw IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: Sink.addBatch
nodes.summary: Abstract: adds one batch of data for the given batchId, synchronously and idempotently; the DataFrame may only be consumed (collect, foreach) and no further operators may be applied to it.

nodes.name: statefulOperators.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the physical (SparkPlan) operators that keep state across micro-batches: streaming aggregation (StateStoreRestoreExec and StateStoreSaveExec), session-window aggregation, and deduplication, plus the shared StatefulOperator, StateStoreReader/StateStoreWriter and WatermarkSupport traits. Each task opens the StateStore for its shuffle partition, reads or updates keyed rows, optionally evicts rows older than the watermark, commits the new store version and reports metrics back to the driver.

nodes.name: StatefulOperatorStateInfo
nodes.summary: Immutable description of one stateful operator instance for a batch: checkpoint location, query run id, operator id, state store version, number of shuffle partitions, optional state schema broadcast and per-partition state store checkpoint ids. IncrementalExecution fills it in before execution; the companion object tells whether checkpoint ids are enabled (state store checkpoint format version 2 or higher).

nodes.name: StatefulOperator
nodes.summary: Base trait for any SparkPlan that reads or writes the StateStore. It carries the optional StatefulOperatorStateInfo, resolves the operator's _metadata file path under the checkpoint directory and declares validateAndMaybeEvolveStateSchema, which records and validates the state schema on the driver.

nodes.name: StatefulOperatorCustomMetric
nodes.summary: Trait for an operator-specific custom metric (name, description and a factory for the SQLMetric) that is shown in the UI and surfaced in StateOperatorProgress custom metrics.

nodes.name: StatefulOperatorCustomSumMetric
nodes.summary: Simple count-style StatefulOperatorCustomMetric, created via SQLMetrics.createMetric; used for example by deduplication for the number of dropped duplicates.

nodes.name: StateStoreReader
nodes.summary: Mixin trait for operators that only read from the StateStore. Its metrics map holds just numOutputRows.

nodes.name: StatefulOpStateStoreCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Per-partition record (partition id, batch version, checkpoint id at that version and base checkpoint id of the previous version) that executors send to the driver so the right state store checkpoint can be loaded and validated.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter
nodes.summary: Mixin trait for operators that write the StateStore. It defines the standard state metrics (rows updated, removed, dropped by watermark, commit time, memory), collects checkpoint ids from executors through an accumulator, builds StateOperatorProgress for query progress, and provides hooks such as produceOutputWatermark, shortName and shouldRunAnotherBatch.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter.metrics
nodes.summary: Lazy metrics map for a state-writing operator: numOutputRows, numRowsDroppedByWatermark, numTotalStateRows, numUpdatedStateRows, allUpdatesTimeMs, numRemovedStateRows, allRemovalsTimeMs, commitTimeMs, stateMemory, numStateStoreInstances, plus the store provider's custom metrics, operator custom metrics and Python metrics.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter.stateSchemaList
nodes.summary: Builds the list of state schema file paths for the operator metadata: keeps the previous paths from a V2 metadata and appends the new schema path only when the schema evolved.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter.getStateStoreCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Driver-side aggregation of the checkpoint info reported by tasks: picks one entry per partition (speculative or retried tasks may report several), sorts by partition id and asserts that every partition (or the single global-limit partition) reported.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter.setStateStoreCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Executor-side hook that adds a partition's checkpoint info to the accumulator when state store checkpoint ids are enabled.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter.getProgress
nodes.summary: Builds the StateOperatorProgress after a batch from the operator's SQL metrics (rows total, updated, removed, dropped by watermark, commit time, memory, shuffle partitions) and merges custom and per-instance metrics, keeping the top N instance metrics.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter.setStoreMetrics
nodes.summary: Copies a committed StateStore's metrics (key count, memory, custom and instance metrics) into the operator's SQL metrics and, when enabled, publishes the store's checkpoint ids for the driver.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter.stateStoreInstanceMetrics
nodes.summary: Creates one SQLMetric for each combination of partition id, store name and the state store provider's supported instance metrics.

nodes.name: StateStoreWriter.applyRemovingRowsOlderThanWatermark
nodes.summary: Filters out input rows matching the late-event watermark predicate and counts them in numRowsDroppedByWatermark.

nodes.name: WatermarkSupport
nodes.summary: Trait (with companion object) for operators that use the event-time watermark. It builds predicates over keys or data for two watermarks: the previous-batch watermark for dropping late records and the current watermark for evicting state; the companion locates the event time column and builds the 'older than watermark' expression, using the window end for window structs.

nodes.name: WatermarkSupport.removeKeysOlderThanWatermark
nodes.summary: Two overloads that scan the state store (or a StreamingAggregationStateManager) and remove every key matching the eviction watermark predicate, counting numRemovedStateRows.

nodes.name: WatermarkSupport.watermarkExpression
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that builds 'attribute <= watermark (in microseconds)' and uses field 1 (window end) when the watermark attribute is a window struct.

nodes.name: WatermarkSupport.findEventTimeColumn
nodes.summary: Finds the attribute marked as event time via the watermark delay metadata key and throws an AnalysisException on several distinct event time columns unless the compatibility flag allows taking the first.

nodes.name: WatermarkSupport.findEventTimeColumnIndex
nodes.summary: Same lookup as findEventTimeColumn but returns the ordinal of the event time column.

nodes.name: StateStoreRestoreExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator used before the final aggregation of a streaming aggregation: for each input row it computes the key, reads the previous aggregate buffer from the StateStore (read-only) and emits it together with the input row so the aggregate can merge old state with new data.

nodes.name: StateStoreRestoreExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Runs mapPartitionsWithReadStateStore: with no grouping keys and no input it returns every stored value so the global-aggregation zero row merges with state, otherwise it emits the restored row (if any) followed by each input row.

nodes.name: StateStoreRestoreExec.requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Requires all tuples in one partition when there are no keys, otherwise a distribution compatible with the state's partitioning from StatefulOperatorPartitioning.

nodes.name: StateStoreSaveExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator that writes streaming aggregation results into the StateStore and decides what to emit by output mode: Complete writes everything then outputs all state; Append outputs only keys evicted by the watermark; Update outputs the changed rows and removes expired keys. State is committed in the iterator's close step.

nodes.name: StateStoreSaveExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Core flow of a streaming aggregation per partition via mapPartitionsWithStateStore: matches on the output mode (Complete, Append, Update), puts rows into the store, evicts old keys, and when the output iterator closes commits the store and records store and operator metrics.

nodes.name: StateStoreSaveExec.shouldRunAnotherBatch
nodes.summary: Returns true in Append or Update mode when the new input watermark exceeds the eviction watermark, meaning another batch is needed to flush state even without new data.

nodes.name: SessionWindowStateStoreRestoreExec
nodes.summary: Restore side of session-window aggregation: drops late rows by watermark and merges the input with existing sessions in state, producing rows sorted by group keys plus session start time via MergingSortWithSessionWindowStateIterator. Requires a grouping key.

nodes.name: SessionWindowStateStoreRestoreExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Reads state with a prefix-key scan encoder, filters late input and wraps it in MergingSortWithSessionWindowStateIterator while counting output rows.

nodes.name: SessionWindowStateStoreSaveExec
nodes.summary: Save side of session-window aggregation: replaces the sessions of each grouping key in the state store with the new sessions, then outputs per output mode (Complete or Append; Update is not supported). In Append mode it removes and emits sessions closed by the watermark.

nodes.name: SessionWindowStateStoreSaveExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Per-partition write flow for session windows: puts updated sessions, then for Complete outputs all sessions and for Append removes by value condition on the eviction watermark, committing the store when the output iterator closes.

nodes.name: SessionWindowStateStoreSaveExec.putToStore
nodes.summary: Groups the sorted input by key and calls StreamingSessionWindowStateManager.updateSessions per key, adding upserted and deleted counts to the state row metrics.

nodes.name: SessionWindowStateStoreSaveExec.getProgress
nodes.summary: Overrides progress reporting to take the dropped-late-rows count from the upstream SessionWindowStateStoreRestoreExec, since late rows are dropped there.

nodes.name: BaseStreamingDeduplicateExec
nodes.summary: Abstract base for streaming deduplication: for each row it computes the key, checks store.keyExists, stores a dup-info row and emits the row on first sight, drops later duplicates, then evicts expired keys and commits the store. Subclasses decide what is stored per key and how eviction works.

nodes.name: BaseStreamingDeduplicateExec.doExecute
nodes.summary: Per-partition dedup flow using mapPartitionsWithStateStore: filters late rows, keeps only rows whose key is not yet in state, and in a CompletionIterator evicts old keys, commits the store and sets store and operator metrics.

nodes.name: StreamingDeduplicateExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator for dropDuplicates on a stream: stores only the key with an empty value row and evicts keys older than the watermark when an event time column is among the keys.

nodes.name: StreamingDeduplicateStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Extractor stating that for deduplication the state key is the dedup key itself (no-op extraction).

nodes.name: StreamingDeduplicateWithinWatermarkExec
nodes.summary: Physical operator for dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark: stores an expiry timestamp (event time plus the watermark delay) per key and removes keys whose expiry is at or below the eviction watermark.

nodes.name: StreamingDeduplicateWithinWatermarkExec.putDupInfoIntoState
nodes.summary: Writes the key with expiresAt = event time (microseconds) plus the delay threshold converted from milliseconds.

nodes.name: StreamingDeduplicateWithinWatermarkExec.evictDupInfoFromState
nodes.summary: Iterates the whole store and removes entries whose expiry is covered by the eviction watermark, counting removed rows.

nodes.name: StreamingDedupWithinWatermarkStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Extractor stating that for dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark the state key is the dedup key itself.

nodes.name: SchemaValidationUtils
nodes.summary: Helper trait for operators on state schema v3: collects column family schemas, reads old operator metadata, and calls StateSchemaCompatibilityChecker to validate, evolve (with Avro encoding) and write the new schema file under the operator's schema directory.

nodes.name: SchemaValidationUtils.validateAndWriteStateSchema
nodes.summary: Computes the new schema file path (batchId plus a UUID), reads the existing operator state metadata (tolerating its absence at batch 0) and invokes the compatibility checker.

nodes.name: StatefulOperatorsUtils
nodes.summary: Constants naming each stateful operator in progress reports and metadata: transformWithState variants, symmetricHashJoin, stateStoreSave, dedupe, dedupeWithinWatermark, sessionWindowStateStoreSaveExec, flatMapGroupsWithState and applyInPandasWithState.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStateManager.scala
nodes.summary: State manager abstraction used by streaming aggregation: it extracts the grouping key from an input row and reads, writes, removes and iterates entries of a StateStore. Version 1 stores the full input row as the value; version 2 stores only non-key columns and rebuilds the row on read to save space. The version is chosen from the persisted state format version.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStateManager
nodes.summary: Sealed serializable trait (and companion factory) defining getKey, get, put, commit, remove, iterator, keys and values over a StateStore, and getStateValueSchema for the StateStoreRDD. The companion lists supported versions (1, 2), marks 1 as the legacy version and builds the implementation with createStateManager.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStateManager.createStateManager
nodes.summary: Factory choosing ImplV1 or ImplV2 from stateFormatVersion; any other value throws IllegalArgumentException.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStateManagerBaseImpl
nodes.summary: Shared base implementation: generates an unsafe projection for the key, and implements commit, remove and keys directly on the store without converting values.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStateManagerImplV1
nodes.summary: State format version 1: key equals the key expressions and the value is the complete input row (including key columns), so reads and iteration need no conversion.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStateManagerImplV2
nodes.summary: State format version 2: the value holds only the input columns not in the key. On read the key and value are joined with GenerateUnsafeRowJoiner and, if column order differs, projected back into the original input row layout.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStateManagerImplV2.put
nodes.summary: Splits the row into key and value projections and puts them into the store.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStateManagerImplV2.restoreOriginalRow
nodes.summary: Joins key and stored value into one row and re-projects it when the joined column order differs from the input attributes.

nodes.name: StreamingAggregationStatePartitionKeyExtractor
nodes.summary: Extractor stating that for aggregation state v1 and v2 the state key is the aggregation key itself (no-op extraction).

nodes.name: CheckpointFileManager.scala
nodes.summary: Abstraction over the file system operations used by streaming checkpoints, centred on createAtomic, which makes a file visible only when completely written (write to a hidden temp file and rename, or cancel and delete). Provides FileContext-based (default, atomic rename) and FileSystem-based managers and a factory that can load a user-configured manager class.

nodes.name: CheckpointFileManager
nodes.summary: Trait (with companion) whose key method createAtomic returns a CancellableFSDataOutputStream so metadata log files and state store files are written atomically, with or without overwrite. Also defines open, list, mkdirs, exists, delete, isLocal and createCheckpointDirectory; the companion contains the factory, the temp path generator and the stream types.

nodes.name: RenameHelperMethods
nodes.summary: Sealed helper trait giving a manager the createTempFile and renameTempFile operations that RenameBasedFSDataOutputStream needs to get atomicity by write-then-rename.

nodes.name: CancellableFSDataOutputStream
nodes.summary: FSDataOutputStream that adds cancel(), which discards the underlying stream so the target file is not produced.

nodes.name: RenameBasedFSDataOutputStream
nodes.summary: Atomic writer: data goes to a temp file next to the target; close() closes the stream and renames temp to final (failing on an existing file unless overwrite is allowed), and cancel() closes and deletes the temp file. Can optionally verify that the renamed file exists.

nodes.name: RenameBasedFSDataOutputStream.close
nodes.summary: Closes the temp stream and renames it to the final path, handling FileAlreadyExistsException according to overwriteIfPossible and optionally checking the final file exists.

nodes.name: RenameBasedFSDataOutputStream.cancel
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying stream and deletes the temp file, logging but not propagating cleanup errors.

nodes.name: CheckpointFileManager.create
nodes.summary: Factory: instantiates the class named by the configured file manager class, otherwise tries FileContextBasedCheckpointFileManager (atomic rename) and falls back to the FileSystem-based manager with a warning when FileContext is unsupported.

nodes.name: CheckpointFileManager.generateTempPath
nodes.summary: Builds the hidden temp file name '.<name>.<uuid>[.TID<attempt>].tmp' in the target directory.

nodes.name: FileSystemBasedCheckpointFileManager
nodes.summary: CheckpointFileManager built on Hadoop's FileSystem API; its renameTempFile interprets an ambiguous false return from FileSystem.rename to raise the most suitable error.

nodes.name: FileSystemBasedCheckpointFileManager.renameTempFile
nodes.summary: Renames temp to final via FileSystem.rename; throws if the destination exists and overwrite is not allowed, and maps a false result to source-missing or generic rename failure errors.

nodes.name: AbstractFileContextBasedCheckpointFileManager
nodes.summary: Base class implementing list, mkdirs, open, exists, delete, isLocal and checkpoint directory creation on top of Hadoop's FileContext API.

nodes.name: FileContextBasedCheckpointFileManager
nodes.summary: Default manager: creates temp files with checksums disabled and renames with FileContext, using OVERWRITE or NONE, which gives atomic renames on HDFS.

nodes.name: CommitLog.scala
nodes.summary: The commit log of a streaming query: one small file per batch, written only after the batch has completed, recording the next batch's watermark and (in later versions) state store unique ids and sink metadata. Together with the offset log it lets a restarted query tell which planned batch finished and which must be re-run. Files are 'v<N>' on line 1 and a JSON metadata object on line 2.

nodes.name: CommitLog
nodes.summary: HDFSMetadataLog of CommitMetadataBase entries marking batch completion. The documented flow is: obtain batch offsets and write them to the offset log, process the batch, write the commit log entry, then trigger the next batch. Serializes as a version line plus JSON; createMetadata picks V1, V2 or V3 from the configured state store checkpoint format version; the companion holds the version constants (max 3) and the parser.

nodes.name: CommitLog.serialize
nodes.summary: Writes 'v<version>', a newline, and the metadata JSON to the output stream.

nodes.name: CommitLog.createMetadata
nodes.summary: Factory for the metadata of the requested wire version: V3 (with sink metadata), V2 (with state unique ids) or V1 (watermark only, which rejects non-empty state ids); newer versions throw.

nodes.name: CommitLog.readCommitMetadata
nodes.summary: Reads the version line, validates it against MAX_VERSION, takes the JSON line (default '{}') and builds the matching CommitMetadata, V2 or V3 object.

nodes.name: CommitMetadataBase
nodes.summary: Base trait for commit log metadata exposing version, nextBatchWatermarkMs, stateUniqueIds, withStateUniqueIds and a JSON rendering via json4s.

nodes.name: CommitMetadata
nodes.summary: Version 1 commit entry: only the watermark for the next batch; cannot carry state store unique ids. The companion defines the json4s formats and JSON parsing.

nodes.name: CommitMetadataV2
nodes.summary: Version 2 commit entry: adds stateUniqueIds (operator id to partition id to unique id array) that identify the state store files of a batch under checkpoint format V2.

nodes.name: CommitMetadataV3
nodes.summary: Version 3 commit entry: adds a sinkMetadataMap keyed by sink name and requires exactly one active sink, supporting streaming sink evolution.

nodes.name: SinkMetadataInfo
nodes.summary: Per-sink record stored in a V3 commit: sink name, last committed offset as JSON (or the void offset marker), provider name, API version (DSv1 or DSv2) and whether the sink is active.

nodes.name: OffsetSeq.scala
nodes.summary: Data model for the offset log: OffsetSeq (version 1, offsets by source position) and OffsetMap (version 2, offsets by source id), plus the per-batch metadata persisted with them (watermark, batch timestamp and the SQL confs that must stay fixed across restarts). Writing the offsets before running a batch is how a restart knows exactly which data range a batch covers.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqBase
nodes.summary: Trait for the offsets of one batch (version, offsets, optional metadata) with toString and toStreamProgress, which pairs deserialized offsets with the live sources, either by position or by source id for an OffsetMap.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqBase.toStreamProgress
nodes.summary: Two overloads turning logged offsets into a StreamProgress: by position (checking source count matches) or, for an OffsetMap, by looking up each source id in a map of sources.

nodes.name: OffsetSeq
nodes.summary: Version 1 offset collection: an ordered sequence of optional offsets (one per source, in order) plus optional OffsetSeqMetadata, like a single-instance vector clock. The companion fill methods convert nulls to None.

nodes.name: OffsetMap
nodes.summary: Version 2 offset collection keyed by source id string, with required OffsetSeqMetadataV2; sequence access to offsets throws UnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqMetadataBase
nodes.summary: Trait for offset-log metadata: batchWatermarkMs, batchTimestampMs, persisted conf map, JSON, version, source metadata info and control batch info. Version 1 pairs with OffsetSeq and version 2 with OffsetMap.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqMetadata
nodes.summary: Version 1 metadata case class (watermark, batch timestamp, conf) with a companion that decides which SQL confs are persisted in the offset log (state store provider, state format versions, compression codec and more), supplies backward-compatible defaults, and restores them into the session at restart.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqMetadata.readValueOpt
nodes.summary: Looks up a conf in the logged metadata (honouring the shuffle partition rebinding) and falls back to the recorded legacy default.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqMetadata.apply
nodes.summary: Builds metadata for a new batch from the watermark, timestamp and the current values of the relevant session confs, including the rebound shuffle partition conf.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqMetadata.setSessionConf
nodes.summary: On restart, sets each relevant conf in the session from the logged value, warns when it overrides a different session value, and uses recorded defaults for confs missing from old logs.

nodes.name: SourceMetadataInfo
nodes.summary: Per-source record (source id, provider name, DSv1 or DSv2 API version) stored in version 2 offset log metadata.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqControlBatchInfo
nodes.summary: Describes a control batch in the offset log by operation type and optional extra info; absent for ordinary data batches.

nodes.name: SequentialUnionOffset
nodes.summary: Offset stored in the offset map for sequential union (backfill then live): the active source name, all source names in order and the completed set, validated on construction and tracked by name.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqMetadataV2
nodes.summary: Version 2 metadata for OffsetMap: adds sourceMetadataInfo by source id and optional control batch info to watermark, timestamp and conf.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqLog.scala
nodes.summary: The offset log of a streaming query: one file per batch, written before the batch runs, listing the end offset of every source for that batch plus metadata (watermark, timestamp, persisted confs). Format is a 'v1' or 'v2' line, a metadata line, then one offset per source (v1) or 'sourceId:offset' lines (v2), with '-' for a missing offset.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqLog
nodes.summary: HDFSMetadataLog of OffsetSeqBase entries (OffsetSeq for v1, OffsetMap for v2). deserialize reads the version, metadata and offsets; serialize writes them back; offsetSeqMetadataForBatchId returns the metadata of a given batch. The companion defines VERSION_1, VERSION_2, the '-' void offset marker and parseOffset.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqLog.deserialize
nodes.summary: Parses a log file: validates the version line, reads the metadata line, then builds an OffsetMap from 'sourceId:offset' lines (v2, metadata required) or an OffsetSeq from one offset per line (v1).

nodes.name: OffsetSeqLog.serialize
nodes.summary: Writes the version line, the metadata JSON and then the offsets, one per line, either as 'sourceId:json' for an OffsetMap or plain JSON per source for an OffsetSeq, using '-' for none.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqLog.offsetSeqMetadataForBatchId
nodes.summary: Returns the logged metadata for a batch id, or None for a negative id or missing batch.

nodes.name: OffsetSeqLog.parseOffset
nodes.summary: Turns a logged string into a SerializedOffset, or null for the '-' void marker.

nodes.name: StateStore.scala
nodes.summary: Core state store API for Structured Streaming. A StateStore is a versioned key-value store of UnsafeRow pairs held per (operator, partition); ReadStateStore/StateStore expose reads and writes of one version, and StateStoreProvider creates them and does background maintenance. The StateStore companion object caches loaded providers per executor, starts the periodic maintenance task, and talks to the StateStoreCoordinator.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file mixing traits, case classes and one large singleton object; the StateStore trait and the StateStore object are companions, so they share one graph id.

nodes.name: StateStoreIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator wrapper over state rows that also implements Closeable. The caller must call close() when the iterator is not fully consumed so the underlying store iterator can release resources.

nodes.name: StateStoreEncoding
nodes.summary: Sealed trait and companion with two case objects, UnsafeRow and Avro, naming the encoding used for stored state rows ('unsaferow' or 'avro' via toString).

nodes.name: MaintenanceTaskType
nodes.summary: Sealed trait with case objects FromUnloadedProvidersQueue, FromTaskThread and FromLoadedProviders, recording which path submitted maintenance work for a provider.

nodes.name: ReadStateStore
nodes.summary: Trait for one specific version of a versioned key-value store, read-only: get, multiGet, keyExists, valuesIterator, prefix and range scans, iterator, plus abort/release and the list of column families. Instances are created by a StateStoreProvider.

nodes.name: StateStore
nodes.summary: Trait extending ReadStateStore with writes: put, putList, remove, merge, deleteRange and column family management, plus commit() which returns the new version, abort(), metrics and checkpoint info. The companion object (lines 1222-1843) holds the per-executor provider cache and maintenance machinery and shares this id.

nodes.name: WrappedReadStateStore
nodes.summary: Adapter that exposes a writable StateStore as a ReadStateStore by delegating every read call to it; this is the default read store returned by StateStoreProvider.getReadStore.

nodes.name: StateStoreMetrics
nodes.summary: Case class carrying a store's number of keys, memory used, and maps of custom and per-instance metrics; the companion object provides combine to merge metrics across stores.

nodes.name: combine
nodes.summary: Merges a sequence of StateStoreMetrics by summing key counts, memory and same-named custom metrics, and unioning instance metrics.

nodes.name: StateStoreCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Case class sent from executors to the driver describing a checkpoint (partition id, batch version, checkpoint id and base checkpoint id) used with checkpoint format version 2.

nodes.name: StateStoreCustomMetric
nodes.summary: Trait naming a provider-specific metric (name, description) and how to create the SQLMetric that shows it in the UI.

nodes.name: StateStoreCustomSumMetric
nodes.summary: Custom metric whose SQLMetric is a plain summed counter.

nodes.name: StateStoreCustomSizeMetric
nodes.summary: Custom metric whose SQLMetric is a size (bytes) metric.

nodes.name: StateStoreCustomTimingMetric
nodes.summary: Custom metric whose SQLMetric is a timing metric.

nodes.name: StateStoreInstanceMetric
nodes.summary: Trait for metrics tied to one state store instance (partition id plus store name), with ordering for progress reporting, a rule for merging values from different executors, and derived name/description.

nodes.name: StateStoreSnapshotLastUploadInstanceMetric
nodes.summary: Instance metric that records the last uploaded snapshot version of a store; initial value is -1 and values from several executors are merged with max.

nodes.name: KeyStateEncoderSpec
nodes.summary: Sealed trait describing how state keys are encoded (no prefix, prefix scan, range scan, timestamp as prefix or postfix); can be serialized to JSON and rebuilt with fromJson, and maps to a RocksDB key encoder via toEncoder.

nodes.name: NoPrefixKeyStateEncoderSpec
nodes.summary: Spec for plain keys without any prefix or ordering; builds a NoPrefixKeyStateEncoder.

nodes.name: PrefixKeyScanStateEncoderSpec
nodes.summary: Spec for keys whose leftmost numColsPrefixKey columns support prefix scans; validates the column count and builds a PrefixKeyScanStateEncoder.

nodes.name: RangeKeyScanStateEncoderSpec
nodes.summary: Spec that encodes rows so they can be range-scanned by the given ordering ordinals; validates the ordinals and builds a RangeKeyScanStateEncoder.

nodes.name: TimestampAsPrefixKeyStateEncoderSpec
nodes.summary: Spec for keys laid out as [original key fields..., timestamp] with the timestamp encoded as prefix; builds a TimestampAsPrefixKeyStateEncoder.

nodes.name: TimestampAsPostfixKeyStateEncoderSpec
nodes.summary: Spec for keys laid out as [original key fields..., timestamp] with the timestamp encoded as postfix; builds a TimestampAsPostfixKeyStateEncoder.

nodes.name: StateStoreProvider
nodes.summary: Trait for the provider that produces StateStore instances for one StateStoreId. One provider is created per store on an executor and reused across batches; each batch calls getStore(version) to get that version of the data. Also defines init, close, optional doMaintenance and supported metrics. The companion object creates providers by class name.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Abstract method called first after a provider is created by reflection; passes the store id, key and value schemas, key encoder spec, store conf and Hadoop conf.

nodes.name: getStore
nodes.summary: Abstract method returning the writable StateStore for a requested version (optionally matching a checkpoint id, forcing a snapshot on commit, or loading empty).

nodes.name: getReadStore
nodes.summary: Returns a read-only view of a version; by default wraps getStore(version) in WrappedReadStateStore, and providers may override with an optimized version.

nodes.name: upgradeReadStoreToWriteStore
nodes.summary: Converts an existing read-only store into a writable one for the same version so one task does not open the same store twice; default just calls getStore.

nodes.name: doMaintenance
nodes.summary: Optional hook for background maintenance of a provider (for example compaction or snapshots); default is a no-op.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Instantiates a provider from its class name through reflection, failing with STATE_STORE_INVALID_PROVIDER if the class is not a StateStoreProvider; the instance is not initialized.

nodes.name: createAndInit
nodes.summary: Sets the query run id in the Hadoop conf, creates the provider whose class name comes from storeConf.providerClass, and calls init on it. This is how the configured provider class is chosen.

nodes.name: validateStateRowFormat
nodes.summary: When format validation is enabled, checks the structural integrity of a key row (and optionally a value row) against its schema and throws a state store error on mismatch.

nodes.name: deleteOrphanChecksumFiles
nodes.summary: Deletes checksum files older than the retained version whose main state file is gone (for example when checksums were later disabled or concurrent deletion partly failed), logging any failures.

nodes.name: coordinatorRef
nodes.summary: Lazily creates a shared StateStoreCoordinatorRef per executor (recreated on the driver), used only to report snapshot uploads and commits to avoid lock contention with other coordinator RPCs.

nodes.name: SupportsFineGrainedReplay
nodes.summary: Optional trait for providers that can rebuild state from a given snapshot version plus delta files up to an end version, and read changelog entries between versions. Used by the State Data Source options snapshotStartBatchId and readChangeFeed.

nodes.name: StateStoreProviderId
nodes.summary: Case class of StateStoreId plus the query run UUID; identifies a provider so the same instance is never reused across query restarts. The companion apply builds it from a StatefulOperatorStateInfo.

nodes.name: StateStoreId
nodes.summary: Case class identifying one store: checkpoint root location, operator id, partition id and store name ('default' unless named). storeCheckpointLocation gives the directory operatorId/partitionId[/storeName] under the checkpoint root where all providers must write.

nodes.name: storeCheckpointLocation
nodes.summary: Computes the per-store checkpoint directory: root/operatorId/partitionId, with /storeName appended when the store is not the default one.

nodes.name: UnsafeRowPair
nodes.summary: Mutable, reusable holder of a key UnsafeRow and a value UnsafeRow, returned by store iterators to avoid allocating a pair per row.

nodes.name: reportCommitToCoordinator
nodes.summary: After a store commits a version, tells the coordinator via the shared coordinator ref; failures are logged and never fail the commit.

nodes.name: MaintenanceTask
nodes.summary: Runs a task periodically on a single daemon scheduled thread named state-store-maintenance-task; rethrows exceptions after logging them. Has stop() and isRunning.

nodes.name: MaintenanceThreadPool
nodes.summary: Fixed daemon thread pool (state-store-maintenance-thread) that executes per-provider maintenance work, with a graceful then forced shutdown.

nodes.name: getReadOnly
nodes.summary: Gets or loads the provider for a StateStoreProviderId (via getStateStoreProvider) and returns its read-only store for the requested version; negative versions throw.

nodes.name: getWriteStore
nodes.summary: Gets the cached provider and upgrades an already open read store to a writable store of the same version, avoiding a second load (useful for RocksDB).

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Main entry point used by executors: gets or creates the provider for the id, then returns provider.getStore(version, checkpointId, shouldForceSnapshotUpload) for the batch to update and commit.

nodes.name: getStateStoreProvider
nodes.summary: Under the loadedProviders lock: starts the maintenance task if needed, gets or creates the provider in the cache, warns if loading took over 2 s, and unless unloadOnCommit is set reports the instance to the coordinator and hands providers it must unload to the maintenance pool.

nodes.name: doMaintenanceAndUnload
nodes.summary: Removes a provider from the cache, runs its doMaintenance and closes it; used when unloadOnCommit is enabled.

nodes.name: removeFromLoadedProvidersAndClose
nodes.summary: Removes a provider from loadedProviders (unless already removed) and closes it; may only be called from the maintenance thread.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Unloads and closes all cached providers, clears the coordinator ref and stops the maintenance task.

nodes.name: startMaintenanceIfNeeded
nodes.summary: If SparkEnv is active, maintenance is not running and unloadOnCommit is off, creates the MaintenanceTask (period storeConf.maintenanceInterval, running doMaintenance) and the MaintenanceThreadPool.

nodes.name: awaitProcessThisPartition
nodes.summary: Waits up to a timeout until the provider's partition is not being maintained by another thread, then claims it.

nodes.name: processThisPartition
nodes.summary: Claims a provider id in the maintenancePartitions set so the same partition is never maintained concurrently; returns false if already claimed.

nodes.name: doMaintenance
nodes.summary: Periodic maintenance pass: requeues unloaded providers waiting to be closed, then submits maintenance work for every loaded provider whose partition is free.

nodes.name: submitMaintenanceWorkForProvider
nodes.summary: Submits to the thread pool a job that calls provider.doMaintenance and then closes the provider (task-thread and queue sources) or unloads it if the coordinator says it is no longer the active instance; on error the provider is unloaded.

nodes.name: reportActiveStoreInstance
nodes.summary: Reports this executor's loaded provider to the coordinator and returns whether to force a snapshot upload and which other providers to unload; returns empty defaults if SparkEnv is null.

nodes.name: verifyIfStoreInstanceActive
nodes.summary: Asks the coordinator whether this executor still owns the active instance of a provider.

nodes.name: coordinatorRef
nodes.summary: StateStore-object coordinator reference (_coordRef) created through StateStoreCoordinatorRef.forExecutor and recreated on the driver; used for all coordinator messages except snapshot upload and commit reports.

nodes.name: StateStoreRDD.scala
nodes.summary: RDD wrappers that run a function against a StateStore for each partition of a streaming operator. ReadStateStoreRDD opens a read-only store, StateStoreRDD opens (or upgrades to) a writable store of version N, and both use the StateStoreCoordinator to prefer the executor that already has that partition's provider loaded.

nodes.name: StateStoreThreadLocalTracker
nodes.summary: Thread-local holder that lets a ReadStateStoreRDD hand its open ReadStateStore to a following StateStoreRDD in the same task, so the store can be upgraded instead of opened twice.

nodes.name: BaseStateStoreRDD
nodes.summary: Abstract RDD base for state-store RDDs: builds a StateStoreConf from the session conf, broadcasts the Hadoop configuration, and implements preferred locations by asking the coordinator which executor holds the partition's provider.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Returns the executor the StateStoreCoordinator reports as hosting the already-loaded provider for this partition, so the task is scheduled where the state is cached.

nodes.name: getStateProviderId
nodes.summary: Builds the StateStoreProviderId for a partition from checkpoint location, operator id, partition index and query run id.

nodes.name: ReadStateStoreRDD
nodes.summary: RDD that applies storeReadFunction to the partition's input iterator and a read-only store at storeVersion; used by operators that only read state.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Opens the input iterator, calls StateStore.getReadOnly for the partition's provider at storeVersion, saves the store in StateStoreThreadLocalTracker, and returns storeReadFunction(store, input).

nodes.name: StateStoreRDD
nodes.summary: RDD that applies storeUpdateFunction to the input iterator and a writable store loaded at storeVersion; the function updates the store and commits to produce the next version.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Opens the input iterator, reuses a thread-local read store via StateStore.getWriteStore if present or else calls StateStore.get, and when unloadOnCommit is set registers a task completion listener that runs StateStore.doMaintenanceAndUnload.

nodes.name: HDFSBackedStateStoreProvider.scala
nodes.summary: Default file-based state store implementation. Each partition keeps its whole state in an in-memory map; every committed batch writes version N+1 as a <version>.delta file in the store's checkpoint directory and background maintenance writes <version>.snapshot files and deletes old files. Loading version N reads the newest snapshot at or below N and replays later delta files.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with nested classes that capture the enclosing provider (HDFSBackedStateStoreProvider.this); mutable fields are @volatile and shared state is guarded by synchronized.

nodes.name: HDFSBackedStateStoreProvider
nodes.summary: StateStoreProvider backed by files on an HDFS-compatible file system. Updates are made in transactional sets; each commit increments the version and writes a delta file, with in-memory caching of recent versions, snapshots, cleanup, and no support for column families, multiple values per key, range scans or checkpoint format version 2. It is the default value of spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.providerClass.

nodes.name: HDFSBackedReadStateStore
nodes.summary: Read-only view of one version, backed by an HDFSBackedStateStoreMap; abort and release are no-ops and multi-value operations are unsupported.

nodes.name: HDFSBackedStateStore
nodes.summary: Writable store for one version: starts in UPDATING state, applies puts and removes to its in-memory map while appending them to a delta file for version+1, and ends COMMITTED or ABORTED. A task completion listener aborts it if the task ends while still updating.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Looks up a key in the map being updated; only the default column family is allowed.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Copies key and value, optionally attaches a row checksum, updates the in-memory map and appends the record to the compressed delta file stream; fails if the store is no longer UPDATING.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes a key from the map and, if it existed, appends a removal record (value size -1) to the delta file.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Finalizes the delta file through commitUpdates, marks the store COMMITTED, optionally reports the commit to the coordinator (when commit validation is enabled) and returns the new version; any failure becomes a failedToCommitStateFile error.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: If still UPDATING, marks the store ABORTED and cancels the delta file so no partial file appears; otherwise it only sets the state.

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Returns a StateStoreIterator over the map being updated for the default column family.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: Builds StateStoreMetrics: number of keys, estimated cache memory, custom metrics (cache hits and misses, state size on current version, snapshot auto repair, forced snapshot) and last uploaded snapshot version.

nodes.name: getMetricsForProvider
nodes.summary: Collects provider-level counters: estimated memory of loaded maps, cache hit and miss counts, and whether snapshot auto repair ran.

nodes.name: getStore
nodes.summary: Rejects checkpoint ids and loadEmpty, loads the map for the requested version through getLoadedMapForStore and returns a new HDFSBackedStateStore that will write version+1.

nodes.name: getReadStore
nodes.summary: Loads the map for the version and returns an HDFSBackedReadStateStore over it.

nodes.name: getLoadedMapForStore
nodes.summary: Creates a new map and, for version > 0, copies in the map from loadMap(version); out-of-memory and other errors are translated into state store load errors.

nodes.name: runValidation
nodes.summary: Rejects configurations this provider cannot serve: column families, multiple values per key and range scan key encoders.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Initializes the provider: rejects checkpoint format version 2, stores schemas and confs, reads the in-memory version retention, computes the provider id from the run id, validates the setup and creates the store directory.

nodes.name: doMaintenance
nodes.summary: Maintenance entry point: writes a snapshot if enough deltas exist, then deletes old files; errors are logged, not thrown.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Clears the cached loaded maps so they can be garbage collected and closes the checkpoint file manager.

nodes.name: commitUpdates
nodes.summary: Under the provider lock: finalizes the delta file, writes a snapshot immediately if a snapshot was forced, and puts the new version's map into the in-memory cache.

nodes.name: latestIterator
nodes.summary: Lists store files and loaded versions, loads the newest known version and returns an iterator over all its rows.

nodes.name: putStateIntoStateCacheMap
nodes.summary: Maintains the version-keyed cache (newest first, bounded by maxVersionsToRetainInMemory, which defaults to 2): evicts the oldest entries and inserts the new version's map, or clears the cache when retention is 0.

nodes.name: loadMap
nodes.summary: Returns the map of the requested version from the cache, or on a miss loads the latest snapshot at or below it and replays delta files from loadedVersion+1 up to the version, caches the result and reports the snapshot to the coordinator.

nodes.name: loadSnapshot
nodes.summary: Finds the version to start from using AutoSnapshotLoader (cached versions plus *.snapshot files, with optional auto repair); version 0 or less starts from an empty map, otherwise uses the cached map or reads the snapshot file.

nodes.name: writeUpdateToDeltaFile
nodes.summary: Writes one put record to a delta file as: key length, key bytes, value length, value bytes (value includes a checksum when enabled).

nodes.name: writeRemoveToDeltaFile
nodes.summary: Writes a removal record to a delta file: key length, key bytes, then value length -1.

nodes.name: updateFromDeltaFile
nodes.summary: Reads a <version>.delta file through the decompressing stream and applies each record to the map: value length -1 removes the key, otherwise puts the row; -1 key length marks end of file. Optionally verifies row checksums and validates the row format once.

nodes.name: writeSnapshotFile
nodes.summary: Writes the whole map to <version>.snapshot atomically through the compressed stream (each entry as length-prefixed key and value, ended by -1), then records the uploaded version and reports it to the coordinator; cancels the file on failure.

nodes.name: cancelDeltaFile
nodes.summary: Cancels the underlying output stream and quietly closes the compressed stream, swallowing the expected IO errors.

nodes.name: readSnapshotFile
nodes.summary: Reads <version>.snapshot into a new map, verifying checksums if enabled; returns None if the file does not exist.

nodes.name: doSnapshot
nodes.summary: Lists store files and, if the last version's map is still loaded and more than minDeltasForSnapshot delta files have accumulated for it, writes a snapshot file (default threshold 10).

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Deletes snapshot and delta files older than the file needed to recover version (latest - minVersionsToRetain; default 100 batches) and removes orphan checksum files.

nodes.name: filesForVersion
nodes.summary: Returns the newest snapshot at or below a version plus the delta files after it up to that version, verifying that no delta file is missing.

nodes.name: fetchFiles
nodes.summary: Lists the store directory and parses names of the form <version>.delta and <version>.snapshot into sorted StoreFile entries (a snapshot wins over a delta of the same version), also collecting checksum files.

nodes.name: compressStream
nodes.summary: Wraps an output stream with the configured Spark compression codec.

nodes.name: decompressStream
nodes.summary: Wraps an input stream with the configured Spark compression codec for decompression.

nodes.name: deltaFile
nodes.summary: Delta file naming: path <baseDir>/<version>.delta, where baseDir is the store's checkpoint location.

nodes.name: snapshotFile
nodes.summary: Snapshot file naming: path <baseDir>/<version>.snapshot.

nodes.name: replayStateFromSnapshot
nodes.summary: Builds a writable store at endVersion by starting from the given snapshot version and applying delta files; throws if checkpoint ids are passed. Used by the State Data Source.

nodes.name: replayReadStateFromSnapshot
nodes.summary: Same replay as replayStateFromSnapshot but returns a read-only store at endVersion.

nodes.name: replayLoadedMapFromSnapshot
nodes.summary: Validates the version range and builds a fresh map from constructMapFromSnapshot, translating failures into state store errors.

nodes.name: constructMapFromSnapshot
nodes.summary: Loads the start snapshot (from cache or file, error if missing) and applies delta files from snapshotVersion+1 to endVersion.

nodes.name: createHDFSBackedStateStoreMap
nodes.summary: Creates the in-memory key map for the store using the key schema, prefix column count and an optional read-time integrity verifier.

nodes.name: getStateStoreChangeDataReader
nodes.summary: Returns an HDFSBackedStateStoreChangeDataReader over delta files between two versions; column families and checkpoint ids are unsupported.

nodes.name: reportSnapshotUploadToCoordinator
nodes.summary: When snapshot upload lag reporting is enabled, tells the coordinator the latest snapshot version and a timestamp.

nodes.name: HDFSBackedStateStoreChangeDataReader
nodes.summary: Change data reader for delta files (changelog suffix 'delta'); getNext decodes each record into (record type, key row, value row, batch id), handling checksum-wrapped rows.

nodes.name: getNext
nodes.summary: Reads the next record from the current delta file as a put or delete, building UnsafeRow key and value and reporting version minus one as the batch id.

nodes.name: RocksDBStateStoreProvider.scala
nodes.summary: StateStoreProvider backed by an embedded RocksDB instance created in an executor-local temp dir, with data versioned and checkpointed to the DFS state checkpoint location. Provides the RocksDBStateStore (get/put/remove/merge/iterators/scans/commit/abort), virtual column families, UnsafeRow or Avro data encoding, a state machine with stamps, a long list of RocksDB custom metrics, and a change data reader.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala companion object holds shared helpers, metric definitions and a process-wide encoder cache (NonFateSharingCache, 1000 entries, 1 hour idle expiry).

nodes.name: RocksDBStateStoreProvider
nodes.summary: StateStoreProvider (also Closeable and SupportsFineGrainedReplay) that lazily creates one RocksDB per operator partition and hands out RocksDBStateStore instances for a version in read-write or read-only mode. Tracks lifecycle with RocksDBStateMachine, supports column families, multiple values per key, Avro or UnsafeRow encoding, replay from snapshot and a change data reader. Companion object defines helpers and metrics.

nodes.name: RocksDBStateStore
nodes.summary: Inner StateStore for one version. Each operation calls validateAndTransitionState to enforce valid transitions between UPDATING, COMMITTED, ABORTED and RELEASED and to verify the stamp; registers task completion/failure listeners that abort (or release for read-only) an uncommitted store; keeps key/value encoders per column family.

nodes.name: StateRowEncoderCacheKey
nodes.summary: Case class key (query run id, operator id, partition id, store name, column family) for the shared data encoder cache.

nodes.name: RocksDBStateStoreChangeDataReader
nodes.summary: StateStoreChangeDataReader that reads changelog files across versions (using checkpoint-id lineage if enabled), filters records of a given virtual column family by id prefix, verifies row checksums when enabled and decodes key/value rows. DELETE_RANGE records are rejected.

nodes.name: RocksDBEventForwarder
nodes.summary: Relays events such as snapshot uploads from a RocksDB instance to the StateStoreCoordinator with provider id and timestamp, for metrics and monitoring only.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Stores schemas, conf and encoding format, creates the event forwarder and provider id, forces lazy RocksDB creation, builds the default column family data/key/value encoders (via getDataEncoder) and registers them in keyValueEncoderMap; multiple values per key requires column families.

nodes.name: loadStateStore
nodes.summary: Loads a version into RocksDB (with optional checkpoint id, read-only and loadEmpty) after acquiring a stamp from the state machine, then creates a RocksDBStateStore or reuses an existing read-only store; maps OOM and other errors to state store errors and releases the stamp on failure.

nodes.name: getStore
nodes.summary: Returns a read-write store for the version by calling loadStateStore with readOnly = false.

nodes.name: upgradeReadStoreToWriteStore
nodes.summary: Turns a read-only store of the same version into a read-write one by reloading with existingStore; delegates to the original provider if it was replaced between phases (SPARK-56476).

nodes.name: getReadStore
nodes.summary: Returns a read-only store for the version via loadStateStore with readOnly = true.

nodes.name: doMaintenance
nodes.summary: Verifies maintenance is allowed with the state machine and calls rocksDB.doMaintenance(); non-fatal exceptions are logged and swallowed (SPARK-46547) to avoid a deadlock with the streaming aggregation operator.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying RocksDB if the state machine confirms the provider can be closed.

nodes.name: createRocksDB
nodes.summary: Protected factory that constructs a RocksDB with DFS root dir, conf, local dir, Hadoop conf, column family flag, checkpoint id flag, partition id and event forwarder (overridable in tests).

nodes.name: rocksDB
nodes.summary: Lazy val: creates the RocksDB with the store's checkpoint location as DFS root and a local temp dir from Utils.createExecutorLocalTempDir.

nodes.name: replayStateFromSnapshot
nodes.summary: Builds a store at endVersion by loading a snapshot and applying later changes (SupportsFineGrainedReplay), used by the state data source; validates version arguments and releases the stamp on failure.

nodes.name: getStateStoreChangeDataReader
nodes.summary: Creates a RocksDBStateStoreChangeDataReader over a version range with the file manager, codec and encoder map.

nodes.name: verifyColFamilyOperations
nodes.summary: For non-default column families, checks that column families are enabled, the name is valid and the column family exists.

nodes.name: verifyColFamilyCreationOrDeletion
nodes.summary: Checks column families are enabled, the name is non-empty without edge whitespace, not the reserved default (unless internal) and not starting with '$' unless internal.

nodes.name: getColumnFamilyIdAsBytes
nodes.summary: Encodes a virtual column family id into the 2-byte key prefix used inside RocksDB.

nodes.name: encodeStateRowWithPrefix
nodes.summary: Prepends the 2-byte virtual column family id to a state row byte array.

nodes.name: getColumnFamilyBytesAsId
nodes.summary: Reads the virtual column family id from the first two bytes of an encoded row.

nodes.name: decodeStateRowWithPrefix
nodes.summary: Strips the 2-byte virtual column family prefix from an encoded row and returns the remaining bytes.

nodes.name: getDataEncoder
nodes.summary: Returns a cached RocksDBDataEncoder for the key: an AvroStateEncoder (needs column family name, supports schema evolution) when encoding is 'avro', otherwise an UnsafeRowDataEncoder.

nodes.name: validateAndTransitionState
nodes.summary: Checks the operation against the allowed (state, operation) table, verifies the stamp for mutating operations, releases the stamp on commit/release, logs transitions and throws stateStoreOperationOutOfOrder otherwise.

nodes.name: createColFamilyIfAbsent
nodes.summary: Validates the name, creates the column family in RocksDB, builds data, key and value encoders with the column family's schema and stores them in keyValueEncoderMap.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Encodes the key, reads it from RocksDB and decodes the value; validates row format once for non-column-family stores.

nodes.name: multiGet
nodes.summary: Reads several keys in one RocksDB multiGet and decodes the values.

nodes.name: valuesIterator
nodes.summary: Returns all values of a key stored as a merged byte array, splitting them with the multi-valued encoder (uses getMergedValues when row checksums are enabled).

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Appends one encoded value to a key using RocksDB merge; requires an encoder that supports multiple values per key.

nodes.name: mergeList
nodes.summary: Appends several encoded values to a key via RocksDB merge.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Encodes key and value and writes them to RocksDB; fails when the store is no longer in UPDATING state.

nodes.name: putList
nodes.summary: Replaces the values of a key with a list of encoded values; requires a multi-valued encoder.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Encodes the key and removes it from RocksDB.

nodes.name: deleteRange
nodes.summary: Deletes all keys in a range; requires an ordered key encoding (RangeKeyScanStateEncoderSpec).

nodes.name: iterator
nodes.summary: Iterates all rows of a column family (or the whole store) from RocksDB, decoding key and value into a reused UnsafeRowPair and closing the RocksDB iterator when done.

nodes.name: iteratorWithMultiValues
nodes.summary: Iterates a column family and expands each stored value list into one row pair per value.

nodes.name: prefixScan
nodes.summary: Scans all rows whose key starts with the encoded prefix; requires an encoder that supports prefix key scan.

nodes.name: prefixScanWithMultiValues
nodes.summary: Prefix scan that expands multi-valued entries into one pair per value.

nodes.name: rangeScan
nodes.summary: Scans rows between optional encoded start and end keys; requires a range-scan capable key encoder.

nodes.name: rangeScanWithMultiValues
nodes.summary: Range scan that expands multi-valued entries into one pair per value.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Verifies the stamp, commits RocksDB to produce the new version (optionally forcing a snapshot), stores checkpoint info and metrics, transitions to COMMITTED and reports the commit to the coordinator if commit validation is enabled.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Releases a read-only store (rocksDB.release) and transitions to RELEASED; idempotent.

nodes.name: abort
nodes.summary: Rolls back uncommitted changes in RocksDB and releases the stamp; skipped if already aborted.

nodes.name: metrics
nodes.summary: Converts stored RocksDBMetrics (SST size, get/put latency and counts, commit breakdown, load/replay times, block cache, compaction, column family counts, snapshot repairs, forced snapshots) to StateStoreMetrics with custom and instance metrics; returns zeros if unavailable.

nodes.name: getStateStoreCheckpointInfo
nodes.summary: Returns the checkpoint info recorded at commit, or throws if the store has not been committed.

nodes.name: removeColFamilyIfExists
nodes.summary: Removes a column family from RocksDB and the encoder map if column families are enabled.

nodes.name: getNext
nodes.summary: Reads the next changelog record, filters it by column family id prefix, verifies/decodes row checksums when enabled and decodes key/value rows with the column family encoders.

nodes.name: reportSnapshotUploaded
nodes.summary: Tells the coordinator that a snapshot of the given version was uploaded for this provider id, with the current time.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.scala
nodes.summary: Plans each micro-batch as an incremental batch query. IncrementalExecution extends QueryExecution with streaming planner strategies, a preparation rule 'state' that gives each stateful operator an id/state info, validates state schema and operator metadata, simulates watermark propagation and injects late-event and eviction watermarks, and a shouldRunAnotherBatch check.
nodes.languageNotes: State-related rewrites are PartialFunction[SparkPlan, SparkPlan] objects composed in a Rule[SparkPlan]; operators are rewritten via case-class copy.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution
nodes.summary: QueryExecution subclass for one micro-batch, parameterized by outputMode, checkpointLocation, runId, currentBatchId, previous and current OffsetSeqMetadata (batch watermark and timestamp), WatermarkPropagator, isFirstBatch and state store checkpoint ids/schema broadcasts. Overrides the planner, optimizedPlan and preparations; skips assertAnalyzed/assertSupported because they were already checked.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.planner
nodes.summary: Anonymous SparkPlanner whose strategies are the streaming extras (StreamingJoinStrategy, StatefulAggregationStrategy, FlatMapGroupsWithState, pandas variant, StreamingRelation, StreamingDeduplication, StreamingGlobalLimit(outputMode), TransformWithState and PySpark variant) followed by the session planner's strategies.

nodes.name: optimizedPlan
nodes.summary: Lazy val override: removes the DSv1 writer marker node, optimizes, then replaces CurrentBatchTimestamp with a literal (SPARK-18339) and re-seeds ExpressionWithRandomSeed so every batch is deterministic in time but random in seeds.

nodes.name: nextStatefulOperationStateInfo
nodes.summary: Takes the next operator id from an atomic counter and builds StatefulOperatorStateInfo(checkpointLocation, runId, operatorId, currentBatchId, numStateStores, schema broadcast, checkpoint ids).

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.SparkPlanPartialRule
nodes.summary: Sealed trait wrapping a PartialFunction[SparkPlan, SparkPlan] so several state-related rewrites can be composed or applied separately.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.ShufflePartitionsRule
nodes.summary: Sets numShufflePartitions to numStateStores on streaming Sort/Hash/ObjectHash aggregates and the session-window merging/updating execs so state partitions stay stable across restarts.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.ConvertLocalLimitRule
nodes.summary: Replaces StreamingLocalLimitExec with LocalLimitExec when its child has no stateful operator on a narrow dependency.

nodes.name: hasNoStatefulOp
nodes.summary: Walks the plan until a ShuffleExchangeLike and returns true if no StatefulOperator is found on narrow dependencies.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.StateSchemaAndOperatorMetadataRule
nodes.summary: On the first batch of a run, validates and optionally evolves each stateful operator's state schema, reads old operator metadata when restarting (batch id != 0), validates the new metadata, writes it to the checkpoint operator directory, and for operators supporting schema evolution broadcasts the schema and rewrites TransformWithState state info.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.StateOpIdRule
nodes.summary: Gives every stateful physical operator a fresh StatefulOperatorStateInfo: StateStoreSaveExec with its restore child, session window save/restore, StreamingDeduplicateExec and WithinWatermark, FlatMapGroupsWithState, TransformWithState (Scala and PySpark), pandas FlatMapGroupsWithState, StreamingSymmetricHashJoinExec and StreamingGlobalLimitExec. Also sets output mode and batch timestamps, and clears watermark fields to None for later filling.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.WatermarkPropagationRule
nodes.summary: Fills eventTimeWatermarkForLateEvents and eventTimeWatermarkForEviction on each stateful operator (save, session window, dedup, flatMapGroupsWithState, transformWithState incl. UpdateEventTimeColumnExec, pandas, join) using watermarkPropagator for the current batch; for stream-stream join also builds stateWatermarkPredicates for eviction.

nodes.name: IncrementalExecution.state
nodes.summary: Anonymous Rule[SparkPlan] placed first in preparations (state +: super.preparations). apply(): transform with ShufflePartitionsRule orElse ConvertLocalLimitRule orElse StateOpIdRule; on restart's first batch check operators against stored metadata; apply StateSchemaAndOperatorMetadataRule; simulate watermark propagation; apply WatermarkPropagationRule. This is how stateful physical operators get state store info and watermarks.

nodes.name: simulateWatermarkPropagation
nodes.summary: Calls watermarkPropagator.propagate for batch id - 1 with the previous batch's watermark (late events) and for the current batch id with the current batch watermark (eviction).

nodes.name: checkOperatorValidWithMetadata
nodes.summary: On restart, fails if the state directory is empty while operators exist, or if operator id to name pairs in the stored state metadata differ from the physical plan (statefulOperatorNotMatchInStateMetadataError).

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Applies the composed state rule, metadata check, schema/metadata rule, watermark simulation and watermark propagation rule in order, returning the final plan.

nodes.name: preparations
nodes.summary: Prepends the state rule to the standard QueryExecution preparation rules.

nodes.name: shouldRunAnotherBatch
nodes.summary: Simulates watermark propagation for batch currentBatchId + 1 using newMetadata.batchWatermarkMs and asks each StateStoreWriter whether the new eviction watermark requires another batch (MicroBatchExecution uses this to run extra no-data batches).

nodes.name: StreamingQueryWrapper.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StreamingQueryWrapper, a Serializable StreamingQuery that holds the non-serializable StreamExecution as a transient field and delegates every call to it, so a query captured in a closure does not break task serialization.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryWrapper
nodes.summary: Serializable StreamingQuery facade over a transient StreamExecution. Methods such as stop, awaitTermination, processAllAvailable, lastProgress, recentProgress, status and exception forward to the underlying execution; on executors the transient field is null and calls throw IllegalStateException.

nodes.name: StreamingQueryWrapper.streamingQuery
nodes.summary: Returns the wrapped StreamExecution, or throws IllegalStateException when it is null (i.e. when running in an executor).

nodes.name: StreamingQueryWrapper.explainInternal
nodes.summary: Returns the explain string from the wrapped execution; exists because Python cannot call explain directly, which prints in the JVM process.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.scala
nodes.summary: Implements HDFSMetadataLog, a MetadataLog that stores one file per batch id in a directory and writes each entry atomically through CheckpointFileManager (temp file then rename). It is the base mechanism behind the offset log and commit log, with a two-entry cache, listing, range reads and purging.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala generic class bounded by T <: AnyRef with a ClassTag; JSON (de)serialization via json4s Serialization that subclasses can override through protected serialize and deserialize.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog
nodes.summary: MetadataLog[T] on HDFS-style file systems: batch id N is a file named N under the metadata path. add writes via createAtomic to a temp file and renames, so concurrent writers cannot both succeed (the loser gets false or an error). Keeps the latest two entries in a cache, lists batch files to find the latest, and can purge older or newer entries. Not supported on S3-like stores because listing may be stale.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.serialize
nodes.summary: Protected hook that writes the metadata object as JSON to the output stream with json4s; subclasses override it for custom formats and must not close the stream.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.deserialize
nodes.summary: Protected hook that reads a UTF-8 JSON stream back into T with json4s; overridable by subclasses.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.add
nodes.summary: Stores metadata for a batch id and returns true if written, or false if that batch already exists; serializes through addNewBatchByStream and updates the cache on success.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.get
nodes.summary: Single-batch read: returns the cached entry if present, otherwise reads and deserializes the batch file, returning None when it is missing. An overload at lines 258-266 reads a verified contiguous id range.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.getPrevBatchFromStorage
nodes.summary: Lists batch files on disk and returns the largest id strictly below the given batch id, or None.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.applyFnToBatchByStream
nodes.summary: Opens a batch file via the file manager and applies a function to its InputStream, closing quietly afterwards; throws a not-found error if the file is missing and annotates IllegalStateException with the file path.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.write
nodes.summary: Creates an atomic output via fileManager.createAtomic with overwriteIfPossible = false, runs the writer function and closes it; on FileAlreadyExistsException it cancels and reports concurrent queries using the same path, and on any other error cancels and rethrows.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.addNewBatchByStream
nodes.summary: Returns false if the batch is cached or its file exists, otherwise writes it through the temp-file-then-rename path and returns true.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.getExistingBatch
nodes.summary: Reads a batch that is known to exist, using the cache first and then the file without an existence check.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.getLatestBatchId
nodes.summary: Returns the highest batch id from listing without reading the file.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.getLatest
nodes.summary: Returns the highest batch id and its deserialized entry, or None for an empty log; StreamExecution uses it on restart to find the last logged offsets or commit.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.getOrderedBatchFiles
nodes.summary: Lists batch files and returns FileStatus entries sorted from newest to oldest batch.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.purge
nodes.summary: Deletes log entries with ids below the threshold (exclusive) and removes them from the cache; for at most three candidates it deletes by id without listing, otherwise it lists.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.purgeAfter
nodes.summary: Deletes log entries with ids above the threshold (exclusive), used to roll back extra entries.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.listBatches
nodes.summary: Protected listing of batch ids found on the file system plus those in the cache, assumed continuous between the minimum and maximum.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.listBatchesOnDisk
nodes.summary: Returns the sorted batch ids actually persisted on disk, ignoring the cache.

nodes.name: HDFSMetadataLog.verifyBatchIds
nodes.summary: Companion-object helper that checks a sorted id list covers startId through endId and has no gaps, throwing IllegalStateException that names the missing batches.

nodes.name: TriggerExecutor.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the trigger loop strategies for micro-batch execution: TriggerExecutor trait with a batch handler contract, SingleBatchExecutor (Trigger.Once), MultiBatchExecutor (Trigger.AvailableNow) and ProcessingTimeExecutor (fixed interval, or as fast as possible when the interval is 0).

nodes.name: TriggerExecutor
nodes.summary: Trait that holds the next MicroBatchExecutionContext and defines execute(batchRunner), where the runner returns false to stop. setNextBatch stores the context, and runOneBatch invokes the runner on it.

nodes.name: SingleBatchExecutor
nodes.summary: Runs exactly one batch and then returns, giving Trigger.Once semantics.

nodes.name: MultiBatchExecutor
nodes.summary: Repeats runOneBatch while the runner returns true, then terminates; MicroBatchExecution uses it for Trigger.AvailableNow so the query ends after all available data is processed.

nodes.name: ProcessingTimeExecutor
nodes.summary: Runs a batch at each processing-time interval boundary: after each batch it waits on the clock until the next multiple of the interval, warns if a batch takes longer than the interval, and with interval 0 runs batches back to back. Stops when the runner reports termination.

nodes.name: TriggerExecutor.execute
nodes.summary: Abstract method that drives batches with the given batchRunner and stops when the runner returns false.

nodes.name: TriggerExecutor.setNextBatch
nodes.summary: Stores the MicroBatchExecutionContext that the next runOneBatch call will hand to the batch runner.

nodes.name: TriggerExecutor.runOneBatch
nodes.summary: Invokes the batch runner on the stored execution context and returns its result (whether to continue).

nodes.name: SingleBatchExecutor.execute
nodes.summary: Calls runOneBatch once.

nodes.name: MultiBatchExecutor.execute
nodes.summary: Loops while runOneBatch returns true.

nodes.name: ProcessingTimeExecutor.execute
nodes.summary: Loop that records the trigger time, computes the next boundary with nextBatchTime, runs one batch, warns through notifyBatchFallingBehind if elapsed time exceeds the interval, returns when the handler stopped, and otherwise waits until the next trigger time.

nodes.name: ProcessingTimeExecutor.notifyBatchFallingBehind
nodes.summary: Logs a warning that the current batch is falling behind the trigger interval, with interval and elapsed milliseconds.

nodes.name: ProcessingTimeExecutor.nextBatchTime
nodes.summary: Returns the start of the next interval after the given time (now itself when the interval is 0), so that applying it twice yields the following interval.

nodes.name: namedExpressions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines named expressions: the NamedExpression trait, ExprId, Alias, Attribute, AttributeReference, PrettyAttribute, OuterReference and related placeholders, and the helper objects for metadata columns (MetadataAttribute, FileSourceMetadataAttribute and friends). Attributes are how an operator's output columns are identified by exprId across a plan.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with case classes whose exprId and qualifier live in a second parameter list, so equality and pattern matching only involve the first list; otherCopyArgs carries them through copies.

nodes.name: NamedExpression
nodes.summary: Trait for expressions that have a name and a unique ExprId, so downstream operators can refer to their output. foldable is fixed to false so aliases are never removed by constant folding. Declares qualifier, toAttribute, metadata and newInstance. The companion object creates new ExprIds from a global counter plus the JVM UUID.

nodes.name: ExprId
nodes.summary: Globally unique id of a named expression: a per-JVM Long counter plus the JVM UUID. AttributeReferences with the same ExprId refer to the same column. hashCode uses only id. The companion apply(id) uses the current JVM's UUID.

nodes.name: Attribute
nodes.summary: Abstract leaf NamedExpression representing a column of an operator's output. Its references set is itself, it is null intolerant, and it declares withNullability/withQualifier/withName/withMetadata/withExprId/withDataType copy methods.

nodes.name: Alias
nodes.summary: Assigns a name to the result of a child expression, for example 1 + 1 AS a is Alias(Add(Literal(1), Literal(1)), a). eval and genCode pass through to the child. exprId, qualifier and metadata sit in a second parameter list. toAttribute produces an AttributeReference once resolved, so later operators refer to the alias by exprId.

nodes.name: AttributeReference
nodes.summary: A resolved reference to a column produced by another operator, carrying name, dataType, nullable, metadata, exprId and qualifier. It is Unevaluable (it only has meaning against an input row binding). equals compares all fields, semanticHash and canonicalized use only exprId and dataType, and the with* methods return updated copies.

nodes.name: PrettyAttribute
nodes.summary: Placeholder attribute used to print expressions without exprId or unresolved indicators; most copy methods throw SparkUnsupportedOperationException.

nodes.name: OuterReference
nodes.summary: Placeholder for a reference resolved to a field outside the current plan, used in correlated subqueries. Its companion holds TreeNodeTags that preserve SQL strings and aggregate alias names for the single-pass analyzer.

nodes.name: OuterScopeReference
nodes.summary: Placeholder recording that a correlated column in SubqueryExpression.outerAttrs comes from an outer scope beyond the immediate outer plan (nested correlation).

nodes.name: LateralColumnAliasReference
nodes.summary: Temporary placeholder for a NamedExpression resolved as a reference to a lateral column alias; it is restored to an UnresolvedAttribute or becomes a normal column during analysis and must not survive the analyzer.

nodes.name: VirtualColumn
nodes.summary: Holds names for virtual grouping id columns: Hive's grouping__id (deprecated) and Spark's spark_grouping_id, plus an UnresolvedAttribute for the latter.

nodes.name: MetadataAttribute
nodes.summary: Helper object for metadata columns: apply creates an AttributeReference whose metadata sets __metadata_col, unapply tests for it, and isPreservedOnDelete/Update/Reinsert read connector MetadataColumn flags.

nodes.name: MetadataAttributeWithLogicalName
nodes.summary: Extractor matching a MetadataAttribute even when it was renamed to avoid a name conflict, returning the logical name.

nodes.name: FileSourceMetadataAttribute
nodes.summary: Helper for file source metadata attributes (the hidden _metadata struct fields): marks them with __file_source_metadata_col, checks supported types (primitives, decimal, binary, string, nested arrays, maps, structs), and strips internal metadata keys.

nodes.name: FileSourceConstantMetadataStructField
nodes.summary: Builds and recognizes StructFields of the _metadata struct whose value is constant per file (such as file name).

nodes.name: FileSourceConstantMetadataAttribute
nodes.summary: Extractor matching AttributeReferences that are file source constant metadata attributes.

nodes.name: FileSourceGeneratedMetadataStructField
nodes.summary: Builds and recognizes StructFields of the metadata struct that map to an internal column returned by the scanner (for example row_index), keeping the internal name in metadata.

nodes.name: FileSourceGeneratedMetadataAttribute
nodes.summary: Extractor matching AttributeReferences that are generated file source metadata attributes and returning their internal name.

nodes.name: NamedExpression.newExprId
nodes.summary: Allocates a new ExprId from a global atomic counter plus the JVM UUID.

nodes.name: Alias.eval
nodes.summary: Evaluates by simply evaluating the child.

nodes.name: Alias.genCode
nodes.summary: Code generation is a pure passthrough to child.genCode; doGenCode throws because it should never be called.

nodes.name: Alias.metadata
nodes.summary: Metadata of the alias: explicit metadata if provided, otherwise inherited from a named or struct-field child minus the non-inheritable keys.

nodes.name: Alias.toAttribute
nodes.summary: Converts a resolved alias to an AttributeReference with the same name, type, nullability, metadata, exprId and qualifier, otherwise to an UnresolvedAttribute. Operators use this to expose the alias as output.

nodes.name: AttributeReference.canonicalized
