nodes.summary: Canonical form is an AttributeReference named none with the same dataType and exprId, so two references to the same column compare equal regardless of name or qualifier.

nodes.name: AttributeReference.sameRef
nodes.summary: True when two attribute references have the same exprId.

nodes.name: FileSourceMetadataAttribute.isSupportedType
nodes.summary: Recursively decides whether a data type may be used in file source metadata attributes, based on its physical type.

nodes.name: literals.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Literal, the constant leaf expression (value plus DataType), its companion factory methods and the family of extractor objects (BooleanLiteral, IntegerLiteral, StringLiteral, DecimalLiteral, NonNullLiteral and others). Literal is always foldable and its eval returns the value, which is why ConstantFolding replaces foldable subtrees with Literals.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala companion-object factory with a large pattern match from JVM values to Catalyst types; extractor objects use unapply for pattern matching on Literal values in optimizer rules.

nodes.name: Literal
nodes.summary: Case class for a constant (value, dataType); a leaf expression that is foldable, context-independent foldable, and nullable only when value is null. eval returns the value. doGenCode inlines primitives and dates as Java literals and registers other values as reference objects. sql renders the value with type-specific syntax (Y/S/L suffixes, DATE '...', ARRAY(...), MAP(...)). Use Literal.create for type-checked construction.

nodes.name: Literal.apply
nodes.summary: Builds a Literal from a plain JVM or Scala value by pattern matching its class (Int, Long, String, BigDecimal, java.time types, byte arrays, arrays and others) to the corresponding Catalyst DataType; unsupported classes raise an error.

nodes.name: Literal.fromObject
nodes.summary: Constructs a Literal of ObjectType, for passing an arbitrary object into code generation.

nodes.name: Literal.create
nodes.summary: Creates a Literal with proper conversion to Catalyst internal representation, either for a given DataType (intervals, char/varchar, objects handled specifically) or from a TypeTag via ScalaReflection (the range covers both overloads).

nodes.name: Literal.default
nodes.summary: Returns the default Literal for a data type, using TypeOps if available and defaultDefault otherwise.

nodes.name: Literal.defaultDefault
nodes.summary: Default literal per type: false, zeros, empty string or binary, empty array and map, struct of defaults, and so on; throws for types without a default.

nodes.name: Literal.validateLiteralValue
nodes.summary: Checks that the JVM class of a literal value matches the physical type of its DataType, recursing into arrays, maps and structs, and requires it so wrong-typed Literals are rejected at construction.

nodes.name: Literal.fromSQL
nodes.summary: Inverse of Literal.sql: parses a SQL expression string with CatalystSqlParser and resolves function calls against the built-in function registry.

nodes.name: Literal.eval
nodes.summary: Returns the stored value.

nodes.name: Literal.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java for a constant: null gives ExprCode.forNullValue; boolean, int, date and year-month intervals use the value text; floats and doubles handle NaN and infinities; long-based types add L; other values are stored as reference objects through ctx.addReferenceObj.

nodes.name: Literal.sql
nodes.summary: SQL text for the literal, typed per data type (CAST(NULL AS type), 5Y, 5S, 5L, 1.0D, BD, DATE, TIMESTAMP, INTERVAL, X'..', ARRAY, NAMED_STRUCT, MAP, PARSE_JSON).

nodes.name: Literal.equals
nodes.summary: Equality requires equal dataType and values, with arrays by content, NaN equal to NaN, and null equal only to null.

nodes.name: NonNullLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor that matches only literals whose value is not null, returning the value and data type.

nodes.name: BooleanLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor returning the Boolean value of a Boolean-typed Literal.

nodes.name: FloatLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor returning the Float value of a Float-typed Literal.

nodes.name: DoubleLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor returning the Double value of a Double-typed Literal.

nodes.name: IntegerLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor returning the Int value of an Integer-typed Literal.

nodes.name: ShortLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor returning the Short value of a Short-typed Literal.

nodes.name: ByteLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor returning the Byte value of a Byte-typed Literal.

nodes.name: LongLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor returning the Long value of a Long-typed Literal.

nodes.name: StringLiteral
nodes.summary: Extractor returning the Java String of a UTF8String literal with a string type.

nodes.name: DecimalLiteral
nodes.summary: Factory and extractor for decimal literals, plus helpers comparing a Decimal with the Long range limits.

nodes.name: LiteralTreeBits
nodes.summary: Singleton BitSets of tree patterns (LITERAL, TRUE_OR_FALSE_LITERAL, NULL_LITERAL) used for the treePatternBits of Literals so rules can prune by pattern.

nodes.name: SortOrder.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SortOrder (a child expression with SortDirection and NullOrdering) and SortPrefix, which computes a 64-bit key prefix for fast sorting. SortOrder extends Expression so expression rewrites descend into its child; it also tracks sameOrderExpressions and provides ordering satisfaction checks used by the planner.
nodes.languageNotes: Sealed abstract classes with case objects model the direction and null ordering as enums.

nodes.name: SortDirection
nodes.summary: Sealed base for Ascending and Descending, giving the SQL keyword and the default null ordering.

nodes.name: NullOrdering
nodes.summary: Sealed base for NullsFirst and NullsLast with the SQL keyword.

nodes.name: Ascending
nodes.summary: Ascending direction (ASC); its default null ordering is NULLS FIRST.

nodes.name: Descending
nodes.summary: Descending direction (DESC); its default null ordering is NULLS LAST.

nodes.name: NullsFirst
nodes.summary: Null ordering that places nulls first (NULLS FIRST).

nodes.name: NullsLast
nodes.summary: Null ordering that places nulls last (NULLS LAST).

nodes.name: SortOrder
nodes.summary: Expression describing one sort key: child, direction, null ordering and sameOrderExpressions (expressions known to sort identically, e.g. join keys). It is Unevaluable and its children are the child plus the equivalents. satisfies checks whether it covers a required SortOrder using semanticEquals. The companion offers a factory with default null ordering and orderingSatisfies for sequences.

nodes.name: SortPrefix
nodes.summary: Unary expression that computes a 64-bit prefix of a SortOrder's child for use by the radix/prefix sorter. It selects a prefix function per data type (booleans, integrals, intervals, floating point, strings, binary, decimals) and chooses a null value that sorts first or last depending on direction and null ordering. Both eval and doGenCode are provided.

nodes.name: SortOrder.satisfies
nodes.summary: True when any child of this order is semantically equal to the required child and direction and null ordering match.

nodes.name: SortOrder.orderingSatisfies
nodes.summary: Checks that one sequence of SortOrders satisfies another, meaning the second is a prefix of (or equivalent to) the first, including via sameOrderExpressions.

nodes.name: SortPrefix.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java computing the prefix per type (cast to long, DoublePrefixComparator, StringPrefixComparator, BinaryPrefixComparator, decimal rescaling) guarded by the child's null flag.

nodes.name: SortPrefix.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted prefix: evaluates the child and applies the type-specific calcPrefix function, or returns null for a null child.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the data structure behind subexpression elimination: EquivalentExpressions groups semantically equal, deterministic (sub)expressions with a use count so the code generator can compute a repeated expression once. ExpressionEquals wraps an Expression with semanticEquals/semanticHash based equality and ExpressionStats tracks the use count.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions
nodes.summary: Maintains a map from ExpressionEquals to ExpressionStats. addExpr/addExprTree record expressions (non-recursively or recursively), getCommonSubexpressions returns those used more than once, and special handling avoids unsafe sharing: CodegenFallback children are skipped, ConditionalExpression only recurses into always-evaluated inputs and common branch-group expressions, and optionally only the left side of And/Or is visited.

nodes.name: ExpressionEquals
nodes.summary: Wrapper used as a map key: two wrappers are equal when the expressions are semanticEquals and have the same height; hash code combines semanticHash and height. CodegenContext.subExprEliminationExprs is keyed by it.

nodes.name: ExpressionStats
nodes.summary: Case class holding an expression and its mutable use count; counting in place saves memory compared to storing a list of equivalent expressions.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.addExpr
nodes.summary: Adds one expression (not its children) if supported and returns whether an equal expression was already present.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.updateExprInMap
nodes.summary: Adds or removes an expression and updates its use count; only deterministic expressions are tracked. Returns true if a matching expression remains so callers need not recurse.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.updateCommonExprs
nodes.summary: Finds expressions common to every expression in a group by intersecting per-expression equivalence maps, then moves the tallest ones into the main map.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.skipForShortcut
nodes.summary: When enabled, only the left operand of And/Or is considered, since the right side may be skipped by short-circuit evaluation.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.childrenToRecurse
nodes.summary: Chooses which children to explore: none for CodegenFallback (it calls eval), the always-evaluated inputs for ConditionalExpression, all children otherwise.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.supportedExpression
nodes.summary: Excludes expressions containing LambdaVariable (loop variables) or PlanExpression (when running in a Spark task).

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.addExprTree
nodes.summary: Adds the expression recursively, stopping descent where a matching expression was already added.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.updateExprTree
nodes.summary: Recursive worker for tree add/remove: skips leaves, updates the map and recurses into childrenToRecurse and common branch groups.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.getExprState
nodes.summary: Looks up the ExpressionStats for an expression, or None if unsupported or absent.

nodes.name: EquivalentExpressions.getCommonSubexpressions
nodes.summary: Returns expressions used more than once, i.e. the candidates for subexpression elimination.

nodes.name: Cast.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the SQL CAST expression for Catalyst: the Cast case class (legacy, ANSI and try_cast eval modes, interpreted and generated-Java paths), its companion Cast object with the castability rules (canCast, canAnsiCast, canTryCast, forceNullable, needsTimeZone), plus UpCast and CheckOverflowInTableInsert. Explains why the same cast returns NULL in legacy mode, raises an error in ANSI mode (default true in 4.2.0) and returns NULL again in try_cast.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a case class and a companion object that share the name Cast. There is no separate CastBase, TryCast or CastSupport here: try_cast is the same case class with evalMode = EvalMode.TRY. Each target type has an interpreted castTo* method and a codegen castTo*Code twin, so ANSI/legacy branching appears twice.

nodes.name: Cast
nodes.summary: Catalyst CAST expression (and try_cast) over a single child, extending UnaryExpression with TimeZoneAwareExpression, ToStringBase and SupportQueryContext. evalMode (LEGACY, ANSI or TRY, defaulting to EvalMode.fromSQLConf) decides what happens on bad input or overflow: legacy returns NULL or wraps, ANSI throws, TRY returns NULL. Provides both an interpreted path (nullSafeEval) and generated Java (doGenCode). The companion object Cast shares this class id.

nodes.name: UpCast
nodes.summary: Placeholder expression meaning 'cast the child to target, but fail if the cast might truncate or lose precision' (for example long to int). It is Unevaluable and never resolved on its own (resolved = false), so it must be replaced by a real Cast (or removed) before evaluation. target may be an AbstractDataType such as the DecimalType object, mapped to DecimalType.SYSTEM_DEFAULT.

nodes.name: CheckOverflowInTableInsert
nodes.summary: Wraps a numeric Cast added for store assignment (INSERT) so that an arithmetic overflow is reported with the target column name instead of a generic cast error. It looks through ExpressionProxy to find the Cast, in both the interpreted eval and the generated code.

nodes.name: Cast.canAnsiCast
nodes.summary: Type-pair rules for casts allowed when ANSI mode is on (eval mode ANSI), following the SQL standard with extra Numeric<=>Boolean and String<=>Binary pairs. Stricter than canCast: no Date or Timestamp to Boolean, no Boolean to Timestamp, no Date to numeric, no Integral to Binary. Recurses into arrays, maps and structs and checks nullability, treating VARIANT elements as nullable.

nodes.name: Cast.canTryCast
nodes.summary: Castability rule for try_cast. For arrays, maps and structs it uses the permissive canCast on element types but also requires the target to be nullable when forceNullable says an element may become NULL; other pairs fall back to canAnsiCast. So try_cast accepts only ANSI-valid pairs, plus complex types whose elements may yield NULL.

nodes.name: Cast.canCast
nodes.summary: Type-pair rules for legacy (non-ANSI) casts. Allows more pairs than canAnsiCast, for example Date or Timestamp to Boolean, Boolean to Timestamp, Date to numeric, and Integral to Binary; geospatial types only cast among themselves. Recurses into arrays, maps and structs, using forceNullable to decide whether the target must be nullable.

nodes.name: Cast.needsTimeZone
nodes.summary: Returns true when casting from one type to another depends on the session time zone, for example String to Timestamp, Timestamp to String or Date, Timestamp to TimestampNTZ, and any cast from Variant. Recurses through array, map and struct element types. Cast.resolved and UpCast.contextIndependentFoldable use it.

nodes.name: Cast.canUpCast
nodes.summary: Returns true when from can be cast to to with no truncation, precision loss or runtime failure (long to int and string to int are not up-casts). Delegates to UpCastRule.canUpCast.

nodes.name: Cast.canAssignDefaultValue
nodes.summary: Checks whether a default value typed from can be given to a column typed to, for example from data source metadata to the read schema. Recurses into structs, arrays and maps with nullability checks, allows a VARIANT to read as a shredded struct, and otherwise requires canUpCast.

nodes.name: Cast.canANSIStoreAssign
nodes.summary: Returns true when a value of type from may be assigned to type to under ANSI store-assignment rules (INSERT): numeric to numeric, atomic or interval to string, datetime to datetime and nested types recursively. Rejects things like string to int or double to boolean.

nodes.name: Cast.canNullSafeCastToDecimal
nodes.summary: Tells whether casting to a DecimalType can never overflow or lose integer digits (target wide enough). When false, the cast code must handle overflow by returning NULL (legacy) or throwing (ANSI). Used by forceNullable and castToDecimalCode.

nodes.name: Cast.forceNullable
nodes.summary: Returns true when casting a non-null value from one type to another can still produce NULL: Variant sources, String to non-string/binary, Timestamp to byte/short/int, floating point to Timestamp, anything to Date or CalendarInterval except Timestamp to Date, Date to non-Timestamp, decimal overflow, and fractional to integral (NaN, infinity). Drives Cast.nullable in non-try mode.

nodes.name: Cast.resolvableNullability
nodes.summary: Nullability compatibility check: a nullable source can only be cast into a nullable target (!from || to). Used when comparing array, map and struct element nullability.

nodes.name: Cast.processFloatingPointSpecialLiterals
nodes.summary: Parses the strings inf, +inf, infinity, -inf, -infinity and nan, case-insensitively after trimming, to float or double special values, and returns null for anything else. Used when String to Float or Double parsing fails; in ANSI mode a null result raises an invalid-input error.

nodes.name: Cast.typeCheckFailureMessage
nodes.summary: Builds the DataTypeMismatch error for an invalid cast and suggests a fix: a datetime helper function for numeric <-> timestamp or date (TIMESTAMP_SECONDS, UNIX_SECONDS, DATE_FROM_UNIX_DATE, UNIX_DATE), a config to switch (for example spark.sql.ansi.enabled=false), try_cast when canTryCast allows it, or no suggestion.

nodes.name: Cast.apply
nodes.summary: Two convenience factories that build a Cast from an ansiEnabled boolean (true maps to ANSI, false to LEGACY via EvalMode.fromBoolean), with or without an explicit time zone. Neither can create a TRY cast.

nodes.name: Cast.typeCheckFailureInCast
nodes.summary: Chooses the error shown when an ANSI/TRY/legacy cast is not allowed. In ANSI mode it suggests store-assignment LEGACY policy for table-insertion casts, or turning ANSI off or using try_cast for user casts; in TRY mode it gives no config fallback.

nodes.name: Cast.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Analysis-time validation: picks canCast (LEGACY), canAnsiCast (ANSI) or canTryCast (TRY) from evalMode and returns TypeCheckSuccess or a DataTypeMismatch. An unsupported cast is rejected here during analysis, before any row is evaluated; it also calls TypeUtils.failUnsupportedDataType on the target type.

nodes.name: Cast.ansiEnabled
nodes.summary: True for EvalMode.ANSI, and for EvalMode.TRY unless canUseLegacyCastForTryCast holds. This single flag selects error-throwing versus NULL-returning branches in nearly every castTo* method and in the generated code.

nodes.name: Cast.isTryCast
nodes.summary: True when evalMode is TRY, i.e. the expression represents try_cast. It controls prettyName, nullable, and the try/catch wrapping in the interpreted and generated code.

nodes.name: Cast.nullable
nodes.summary: Non-try casts are nullable if the child is or Cast.forceNullable says the conversion can fail to NULL. try_cast is nullable if the child is, or the cast is not a safe up-cast, or it is decimal to integral; string to binary keeps the child nullability.

nodes.name: Cast.initQueryContext
nodes.summary: Captures the SQL text origin (QueryContext) only when ansiEnabled, so ANSI overflow and invalid-input errors can point to the offending part of the query; legacy casts return None.

nodes.name: Cast.canonicalized
nodes.summary: Canonical form for expression equality and subexpression reuse. Drops the time zone when the cast does not need one (resolved is also stricter: a cast needing a time zone only counts as resolved once timeZoneId is set).

nodes.name: Cast.canUseLegacyCastForTryCast
nodes.summary: Fast path switch for try_cast: string to fractional types and string to datetime types already return NULL on bad input in legacy mode, so try_cast uses the legacy cast code there with no try/catch and ansiEnabled false. Requires the child to be resolved.

nodes.name: Cast.castInternal
nodes.summary: Interpreted dispatcher. Returns identity if the types are structurally equal, a placeholder that throws for NullType, a Variant cast for variant sources, otherwise picks castToString, castToDate, castToDecimal, castToTimestamp, the integral, interval and boolean casts, castArray, castMap or castStruct based on the target type.

nodes.name: Cast.cast
nodes.summary: Wraps castInternal. For try_cast (unless the legacy fast path applies) the returned function catches any Exception and returns null, which is how try_cast turns overflow and invalid input into NULL. A lazy val of the same name (line 1346) caches the cast function for the child and target types.

nodes.name: Cast.nullSafeEval
nodes.summary: Interpreted evaluation entry: applies the cached cast function to a non-null input (null input is short-circuited by UnaryExpression.eval, so a NULL input always yields NULL).

nodes.name: Cast.genCode
nodes.summary: Skips code generation entirely when child and target types are structurally equal and reuses the child's generated code; otherwise falls back to the standard UnaryExpression genCode, which calls doGenCode.

nodes.name: Cast.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Whole-stage / expression codegen: generates the child code, builds the type-specific CastFunction with nullSafeCastFunction and wraps it with castCode (null checks and try/catch for try_cast).

nodes.name: Cast.nullSafeCastFunction
nodes.summary: Code-generation dispatcher. Chooses the CastFunction for the source and target types: NULL source, identical types, Variant, and then the per-target castTo*Code generators for string, date, time, decimal, timestamp, interval, boolean, byte/short/int/long, float/double, geo, array, map and struct.

nodes.name: Cast.castCode
nodes.summary: Emits the Java skeleton of one cast: result-is-null initialised from input-is-null, then the type-specific code inside an if (!inputIsNull) block. For try_cast (without the legacy fast path) the cast body is wrapped in try { } catch (Exception e) { resultIsNull = true; }. Also reused recursively for array elements, map keys/values and struct fields.

nodes.name: Cast.prettyName
nodes.summary: Returns cast, or try_cast when isTryCast, which appears in toString, explain output and SQL text.

nodes.name: Cast.sql
nodes.summary: SQL text for the expression, for example CAST(x AS INT) or TRY_CAST(...). For casts to array, map or struct types it omits the cast and returns the child's SQL (those casts are analyzer-introduced and HiveQL cannot express them).

nodes.name: Cast.castToBoolean
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to Boolean. Strings go through isTrueString/isFalseString; an unrecognised string is NULL in legacy mode and an invalid-input error in ANSI mode. Numerics and timestamps are x != 0, Decimal uses isZero, Date gives NULL (Hive compatible).

nodes.name: Cast.castToTimestamp
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to TimestampType and TimestampNTZType (castToTimestamp and castToTimestampNTZ). Strings: stringToTimestampAnsi throws on bad input, otherwise bad input is NULL. Integral values are seconds; double/float NaN or infinite is NULL in legacy but error in ANSI (doubleToTimestampAnsi). Date and TimestampNTZ conversions use the session zone.

nodes.name: Cast.castToDate
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to Date (castToDate) and Time (castToTime). From strings: ANSI uses stringToDateAnsi/stringToTimeAnsi and throws on invalid text, legacy returns NULL. From Timestamp/TimestampNTZ the date is taken in the session zone / UTC; a TIME-to-TIME cast truncates to the target precision.

nodes.name: Cast.castToInterval
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to interval types: CalendarIntervalType from strings (safeStringToInterval, NULL if unparsable), plus castToDayTimeInterval and castToYearMonthInterval from strings, other intervals, integral values and decimals via IntervalUtils helpers.

nodes.name: Cast.castToLong
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to Long. Strings: ANSI uses UTF8StringUtils.toLongExact (throws on invalid or out-of-range), legacy uses UTF8String.toLong and gives NULL. Numeric: ANSI uses exactNumeric (overflow raises ArithmeticException), legacy numeric.toLong truncates/wraps. Date gives NULL; Boolean 1/0; Timestamp seconds via floorDiv; intervals via IntervalUtils.

nodes.name: Cast.errorOrNull
nodes.summary: Overflow handler used by the interpreted integral casts: throws castingCauseOverflowError when ansiEnabled, otherwise returns null. This is the main place where ANSI throws and legacy and try_cast return NULL for timestamp/time to integral overflow.

nodes.name: Cast.castToInt
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to Int. Same ANSI/legacy split as castToLong: toIntExact and exactNumeric throw on bad text or overflow in ANSI, while legacy returns NULL for bad strings and wraps numerics via numeric.toInt. Timestamp seconds out of Int range go through errorOrNull.

nodes.name: Cast.castToShort
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to Short (castToShort) and Byte (castToByte). In ANSI mode narrowing numerics go through exactNumeric.toInt and a range check that throws castingCauseOverflowError; in legacy mode the Int result is simply narrowed (numeric.toInt(b).toShort), so values silently wrap. Strings use toShortExact/toByteExact in ANSI and NULL on invalid text otherwise.

nodes.name: Cast.changePrecision
nodes.summary: Interpreted decimal helpers changePrecision (two overloads) and toPrecision. When a value does not fit the target precision/scale they return null if nullOnOverflow (legacy, !ansiEnabled) or throw cannotChangeDecimalPrecisionError (ANSI). Note that changePrecision mutates the Decimal in place.

nodes.name: Cast.castToDecimal
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to DecimalType. Strings: legacy uses Decimal.fromString (NULL if not a number) then changePrecision; ANSI uses Decimal.fromStringANSI and throws on invalid input. Decimal, integral, fractional, timestamp, time and interval sources are rescaled with overflow behaviour from changePrecision/toPrecision; interval sources always throw on overflow (nullOnOverflow = false).

nodes.name: Cast.castToDouble
nodes.summary: Interpreted casts to Double (castToDouble) and Float (castToFloat). Strings use toDouble/toFloat, falling back to processFloatingPointSpecialLiterals (Infinity, NaN); if that is also null the result is NULL in legacy mode and an invalid-input error in ANSI mode. Date gives NULL; Boolean is 1/0; Timestamp is seconds as double.

nodes.name: Cast.castArray
nodes.summary: Casts an ArrayData element by element with the cast function for the element types; null elements stay null. Element casts follow the same ANSI/legacy/try semantics as scalar casts.

nodes.name: Cast.castMap
nodes.summary: Casts a MapData by running castArray over the key array and the value array and rebuilding an ArrayBasedMapData.

nodes.name: Cast.castStruct
nodes.summary: Casts a struct positionally: builds one cast function per field pair (names are not matched, only field order) and applies them to each non-null field of the row, keeping nulls.

nodes.name: Cast.castToDateCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for casts to Date (castToDateCode) and Time (castToTimeCode). From strings, ANSI emits stringToDateAnsi/stringToTimeAnsi calls with the error context, legacy emits an Option check that sets the result NULL on parse failure. Unsupported source types set NULL.

nodes.name: Cast.castToDecimalCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for casts to DecimalType, using the code-generating changePrecision helpers. Chooses a no-overflow path when Cast.canNullSafeCastToDecimal holds; otherwise legacy sets the null flag on overflow while ANSI throws cannotChangeDecimalPrecisionError with the query context.

nodes.name: Cast.castToTimestampCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for casts to TimestampType (castToTimestampCode) and TimestampNTZType (castToTimestampNTZCode). Strings use the *Ansi parsers when ansiEnabled (throwing on invalid text) or the Option-returning parsers (NULL). Double/float NaN or infinity is NULL in legacy mode and an error in ANSI mode.

nodes.name: Cast.castToIntervalCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for casts to CalendarInterval (from strings via safeStringToInterval, NULL on failure) and to day-time and year-month interval types from strings, other intervals, integral values and decimals via IntervalUtils.

nodes.name: Cast.castToBooleanCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for casts to Boolean. Strings that are neither true nor false strings throw invalidInputSyntaxForBooleanError under ANSI and set the result NULL otherwise. Date is NULL; numerics compare with zero.

nodes.name: Cast.castTimestampToIntegralTypeCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java helpers for timestamp, time, day-time interval and year-month interval to integral targets. Timestamp and time first reduce to seconds, then a range check either throws castingCauseOverflowError (ANSI) or sets NULL (legacy / try).

nodes.name: Cast.castDecimalToIntegralTypeCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java helpers for narrowing to integral types: Decimal uses roundToX in ANSI (throws on overflow) versus toX in legacy; castIntegralTypeToIntegralTypeExactCode compares the value to its narrowed copy and throws on mismatch (only valid when ansiEnabled); lowerAndUpperBound supplies the min and max literals.

nodes.name: Cast.castFractionToIntegralTypeCode
nodes.summary: ANSI-only generated Java for float/double to integral types: casts only when floor(x) <= max and ceil(x) >= min, otherwise throws castingCauseOverflowError. In legacy mode the generated code uses a plain Java narrowing cast instead.

nodes.name: Cast.castToByteCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for casts to Byte, Short, Int and Long (castToByteCode, castToShortCode, castToIntCode, castToLongCode). Common pattern: ANSI strings call UTF8StringUtils.toXExact (throws), legacy strings use IntWrapper/LongWrapper and set NULL; ANSI narrowing numerics use the exact/range-check helpers, legacy narrowing is a plain Java cast; Date gives NULL.

nodes.name: Cast.castToFloatCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for casts to Float and Double (parsing strings with a NumberFormatException fallback to processFloatingPointSpecialLiterals, then NULL or an invalid-input error depending on ansiEnabled) and to the geospatial types (castToGeographyCode, castToGeometryCode).

nodes.name: Cast.castArrayCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for array casts: loops over elements, casting each non-null element with castCode and nullSafeCastFunction, and builds a GenericArrayData. Null elements are copied as null.

nodes.name: Cast.castMapCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for map casts: casts the key array and the value array separately with castArrayCode and recombines them in an ArrayBasedMapData.

nodes.name: Cast.castStructCode
nodes.summary: Generated Java for struct casts: for each positional field pair it generates a null-checked nested cast and writes it into a new GenericInternalRow; the per-field code is split into methods named castStruct to avoid oversize methods.

nodes.name: CheckOverflowInTableInsert.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted evaluation: evaluates the child and, if a SparkArithmeticException occurs while the child is a Cast, rethrows castingCauseOverflowErrorInTableInsert naming the source type, target type and column.

nodes.name: CheckOverflowInTableInsert.doGenCodeWithBetterErrorMsg
nodes.summary: Generated-code counterpart: wraps the Cast's generated code in a try/catch for SparkArithmeticException and throws the table-insert overflow error with the column name.

nodes.name: CodeGenerator.scala
nodes.summary: Core of Catalyst code generation. Defines ExprCode (Java source for one expression), CodegenContext (mutable state, generated functions, fresh names, 64KB method splitting, subexpression elimination), the CodeGenerator base class and its companion with Java type helpers, and the Janino compile step with a cache of compiled classes.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file whose generated output is Java source text built from string interpolation, compiled at runtime by Janino. CodeGenerator is both an abstract class and a companion object sharing one node id.

nodes.name: ExprCode
nodes.summary: Case class holding the Java source (code), the is-null term and the value term produced by Expression.genCode. The companion adds factories for a null value and for a non-null value with empty code.

nodes.name: SubExprEliminationState
nodes.summary: Case class pairing the ExprCode that evaluates a common subexpression with the child subexpression states that must be evaluated first. The companion apply methods default children to empty and reverse the given children.

nodes.name: SubExprCodes
nodes.summary: Case class returned by whole-stage subexpression elimination: a map from ExpressionEquals to SubExprEliminationState plus the ExprCodes that must be evaluated before the common subexpressions.

nodes.name: NewFunctionSpec
nodes.summary: Package-private case class describing a function added to generated code: its name and, when it lives in a nested class, the inner class name and the inner class instance name.

nodes.name: CodegenContext
nodes.summary: Per-compilation-unit state for code generation. Tracks the references array passed to the generated class, mutable state fields (inlined or compacted into arrays), added functions (spilled into nested classes when the outer class grows past 1,000,000 characters), fresh names, comment placeholders, the INPUT_ROW and currentVars used by BoundReference, and subexpression elimination state.

nodes.name: CodegenContext.MutableStateArrays
nodes.summary: Inner class of CodegenContext that hands out slots in compacted arrays of mutable state for one Java type, creating a new array once MUTABLESTATEARRAY_SIZE_LIMIT (32768) slots are used. This keeps the number of class fields small.

nodes.name: GeneratedClass
nodes.summary: Abstract base class of every class compiled by Janino. Its generate(references) method builds the evaluator instance (projection, predicate, ordering or whole-stage iterator) and receives the objects the generated code needs.

nodes.name: CodeAndComment
nodes.summary: Serializable wrapper of generated Java source plus a map of comment placeholders. Equality and hash code use only the body, so it serves as the cache key for compiled classes.

nodes.name: ByteCodeStats
nodes.summary: Case class with bytecode statistics of a Janino-compiled class: max method bytecode size, max constant pool size and number of inner classes. UNAVAILABLE holds -1 values.

nodes.name: CodeGenerator
nodes.summary: Abstract base class (InType to OutType) for code generators, with create, canonicalize, bind, generate and newCodeGenContext, plus its companion object. The companion holds the Janino compile entry point and cache, Java type mapping helpers, and JVM limits such as DEFAULT_JVM_HUGE_METHOD_LIMIT=8000, MAX_JVM_METHOD_PARAMS_LENGTH=255, MAX_JVM_CONSTANT_POOL_SIZE=65535, MERGE_SPLIT_METHODS_THRESHOLD=3, GENERATED_CLASS_SIZE_THRESHOLD=1000000 and OUTER_CLASS_VARIABLES_THRESHOLD=10000.

nodes.name: addReferenceObj
nodes.summary: Appends an object to the references array and returns the Java expression that casts references[idx] to its class. Objects are fetched at use time rather than stored as fields to save class fields.

nodes.name: addMutableState
nodes.summary: Registers a field of the generated class and returns the name to use. Primitive types (under 10000 inlined vars), forceInline and multi-dimensional arrays become real fields; everything else goes into a compacted array slot (arrayName[index]). The init code is recorded for initMutableStates.

nodes.name: addImmutableStateIfNotExists
nodes.summary: Adds a field only if no field with that name exists, otherwise asserts the type and init code match. Lets many generated functions share one variable.

nodes.name: addBufferedState
nodes.summary: Adds a field and generates code that copies a value read from an InternalRow into it (clone for strings, copy for struct, array and map) so byte-array-backed data stays valid.

nodes.name: declareMutableStates
nodes.summary: Emits the Java field declarations for inlined states and for the compacted state arrays.

nodes.name: initMutableStates
nodes.summary: Returns the distinct state initialization code, split into several functions through splitExpressions because init code can exceed the 64KB JVM method limit.

nodes.name: addPartitionInitializationStatement
nodes.summary: Records a statement to run in the generated initialize(partitionIndex) method, for example initializing a Nondeterministic expression.

nodes.name: initPartition
nodes.summary: Joins the recorded partition initialization statements into the body of the generated initialize method.

nodes.name: addNewFunction
nodes.summary: Adds a generated function to the outer class, or to a new private nested class when the current class source exceeds GENERATED_CLASS_SIZE_THRESHOLD, and returns the name to call (qualified with the nested instance when needed).

nodes.name: addNewFunctionInternal
nodes.summary: Chooses the target class for a new function (outer class, current nested class, or a fresh NestedClass), records its code and returns a NewFunctionSpec.

nodes.name: declareAddedFunctions
nodes.summary: Produces the Java text for all added functions: outer-class functions inline, plus private nested class instances and declarations to avoid the 65,536 constant pool limit.

nodes.name: freshName
nodes.summary: Returns a name unique within this CodegenContext by appending a per-name counter, with an optional prefix.

nodes.name: genEqual
nodes.summary: Generates Java code that tests equality of two values for a Spark DataType, with NaN-aware float and double handling, collation-aware strings, and recursive handling of arrays, structs and UDTs.

nodes.name: genComp
nodes.summary: Generates Java code that compares two values of a DataType and returns an int. Arrays, structs (via GenerateOrdering.genComparisons) and maps get their own generated compare functions registered with addNewFunction.

nodes.name: splitExpressionsWithCurrentInputs
nodes.summary: Variant of splitExpressions that passes the current INPUT_ROW as an extra InternalRow argument. Falls back to joining the code when INPUT_ROW is null or currentVars is set (whole-stage path not supported).

nodes.name: splitExpressions
nodes.summary: Splits generated code for many expressions into several private methods because a JVM method is limited to 64KB; returns the code that calls them. A single block is inlined. Methods go to nested classes when the outer class is too large.

nodes.name: buildCodeBlocks
nodes.summary: Groups expression code strings into blocks whose stripped source length stays near SQLConf.methodSplitThreshold, so each generated method stays small enough for the JIT (methods over 8000 bytecode bytes are not compiled).

nodes.name: generateInnerClassesFunctionCalls
nodes.summary: Builds call code for split functions that landed in nested classes. When one nested class holds more than MERGE_SPLIT_METHODS_THRESHOLD (3) functions, it adds a grouping method so the outer class makes one call.

nodes.name: subexprFunctionsCode
nodes.summary: Returns the subexpression elimination function calls, split into functions if needed.

nodes.name: withSubExprEliminationExprs
nodes.summary: Temporarily replaces the subexpression map while generating code, then restores the previous map.

nodes.name: evaluateSubExprEliminationState
nodes.summary: Emits the code of subexpression states (children first) and clears each state's code so it is not evaluated twice.

nodes.name: subexpressionEliminationForWholeStageCodegen
nodes.summary: Whole-stage subexpression elimination. Finds common subexpressions with EquivalentExpressions, generates their code, and if the code is longer than methodSplitThreshold and the parameter lengths fit the JVM limit of 255, wraps each in its own function. Covers both overloads (Seq[Expression] at 1152 and EquivalentExpressions at 1164).

nodes.name: subexpressionElimination
nodes.summary: Non-whole-stage subexpression elimination: for each common expression it creates a function that stores the result in subExprIsNull and subExprValue state and registers the call to run per row.

nodes.name: generateExpressions
nodes.summary: Calls genCode on each expression after making fresh copies of stateful ones, optionally running subexpression elimination first.

nodes.name: registerComment
nodes.summary: Registers a code comment and returns a placeholder block that is replaced by the comment later, only when codegenComments is on or force is set.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Abstract hook implemented by each generator: build the evaluator class for an already canonicalized input. Called by generate when no cached code is available.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Entry point of every generator: binds expressions to the input schema if given, canonicalizes them (to avoid caching cosmetic duplicates), then calls create. Covers both overloads.

nodes.name: newCodeGenContext
nodes.summary: Creates a fresh CodegenContext for one generation run.

nodes.name: compile
nodes.summary: Compiles generated Java source into a GeneratedClass with Janino, going through a cache keyed by class loader and CodeAndComment. Returns the class together with ByteCodeStats and unwraps Guava cache exceptions.

nodes.name: doCompile
nodes.summary: Runs Janino ClassBodyEvaluator on the source: sets default imports (InternalRow, UnsafeRow, UTF8String, Decimal, ArrayData, etc.), extends GeneratedClass, cooks the code, collects bytecode stats, and logs the source on compile errors before throwing a Spark error.

nodes.name: updateAndGetCompilationStats
nodes.summary: Reads the compiled class bytes with Janino ClassFile, updates CodegenMetrics for class and method bytecode sizes, logs methods over 8000 bytes that the JIT will not compile, and returns ByteCodeStats.

nodes.name: cache
nodes.summary: Cache of compiled classes built with NonFateSharingCache (a Guava Cache wrapper) sized by codegenCacheMaxEntries. The load function times doCompile, updates compile time and size metrics, and logs the duration.

nodes.name: isPrimitiveType
nodes.summary: True if a Java type name (or the Java type of a DataType) is one of the primitive types boolean, byte, short, int, long, float, double. Covers both overloads.

nodes.name: getValue
nodes.summary: Returns Java code that reads a value of a DataType from an InternalRow or ArrayData at an ordinal, such as getInt, getUTF8String, getDecimal(ordinal, precision, scale) or getStruct.

nodes.name: setColumn
nodes.summary: Returns Java code that writes a value into a mutable row. String, struct, array and map values are copied because they may point into a memory region that can change.

nodes.name: updateColumn
nodes.summary: Generates null-aware code to write an ExprCode into a mutable row column, avoiding setNullAt for decimal and interval types. A second overload (line 1876) writes into a column vector.

nodes.name: setValue
nodes.summary: Returns Java code that puts a value into a column vector for primitive, decimal, interval and string types, otherwise throws.

nodes.name: getLocalInputVariableValues
nodes.summary: Walks an expression tree and collects the local variables it reads (INPUT_ROW, currentVars entries and subexpression results) plus ExprCodes that must be evaluated first. Used to give split functions the right arguments.

nodes.name: javaType
nodes.summary: Maps a Spark DataType to the Java type name used in generated source (int, long, UTF8String, Decimal, ArrayData, MapData, InternalRow, byte[], VariantVal, ...), unwrapping UDTs and ObjectType.

nodes.name: boxedType
nodes.summary: Returns the Java boxed type name for a primitive type name (Integer, Long, ...), or the type itself for non-primitives.

nodes.name: defaultValue
nodes.summary: Returns the Java literal used as a placeholder value for a type (false, -1, -1L, null or a typed null). Used when the real value is null.

nodes.name: calculateParamLength
nodes.summary: Computes the JVM method descriptor parameter length for expressions: one for this, two per long or double, plus one boolean per nullable input.

nodes.name: isValidParamLength
nodes.summary: Checks a parameter length against MAX_JVM_METHOD_PARAMS_LENGTH (255), or against a test-only override read from the spark.sql.CodeGenerator.validParamLength config.

nodes.name: CodegenFallback.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the CodegenFallback trait for expressions that have no hand-written code generation. Its doGenCode emits Java that calls the expression's interpreted eval on a reference to the expression object, so the expression still works inside generated code.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala trait extending Expression and mixed into expression case classes.

nodes.name: CodegenFallback
nodes.summary: Trait that gives an Expression a default doGenCode which runs the interpreted eval inside generated code. Whole-stage codegen refuses to fuse operators with such expressions because the fallback needs an InternalRow input (CollapseCodegenStages.supportCodegen).

nodes.name: doGenCode
nodes.summary: Adds the expression to ctx.references, registers initialize(partitionIndex) calls for Nondeterministic children, and emits code that calls references[idx].eval(INPUT_ROW) and unboxes the result into a typed variable, with a null check when the expression is nullable. Leaf expressions pass null as input.

nodes.name: GenerateUnsafeProjection.scala
nodes.summary: Generates a Java class that evaluates a list of expressions and writes the results into an UnsafeRow through UnsafeRowWriter, UnsafeArrayWriter and nested writers. It is the codegen path behind UnsafeProjection and is also reused by whole-stage codegen to build UnsafeRows.

nodes.name: GenerateUnsafeProjection
nodes.summary: CodeGenerator[Seq[Expression], UnsafeProjection] object. It generates code for all expressions, then writes fields into a scratch buffer in UnsafeRow format; the returned UnsafeRow points to a scratch buffer inside the projection.

nodes.name: canSupport
nodes.summary: Returns true if a data type can be written by this generator: null, atomic, calendar interval, and structs, arrays and maps of supported types (UDTs are unwrapped).

nodes.name: writeStructToBuffer
nodes.summary: Generates code that writes a nested struct: copies directly if the input is already an UnsafeRow, otherwise writes each field through a nested UnsafeRowWriter and records offset and size.

nodes.name: writeExpressionsToBuffer
nodes.summary: Generates code that evaluates each ExprCode and writes it with the row writer, using setNullAt (or special null writes for large decimals and intervals) for null fields. Field writes are split into functions via splitExpressions to stay under the 64KB method limit.

nodes.name: writeArrayToBuffer
nodes.summary: Generates code that writes an array: copies when the input is UnsafeArrayData, otherwise loops with an UnsafeArrayWriter, with null handling when elements may be null.

nodes.name: writeMapToBuffer
nodes.summary: Generates code that writes a map in UnsafeMapData layout: reserves 8 bytes for the key array size, writes the key array then the value array, or copies when the input is UnsafeMapData.

nodes.name: writeElement
nodes.summary: Dispatches by data type to the struct, array, map, decimal or generic write code, with nothing emitted for NullType.

nodes.name: createCode
nodes.summary: Builds an ExprCode that evaluates the expressions and writes them into a class-level UnsafeRowWriter, resetting the writer first. Returns the code and the UnsafeRow value (rowWriter.getRow()). Public so whole-stage codegen operators can create UnsafeRows.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes the expressions and creates the projection, with a flag to enable subexpression elimination.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Assembles the Java source of SpecificUnsafeProjection (fields, constructor, initialize, apply(InternalRow), nested functions), compiles it with CodeGenerator.compile and instantiates it with the collected references.

nodes.name: GeneratePredicate.scala
nodes.summary: Generates a Java class (SpecificPredicate) that evaluates a boolean Expression on an InternalRow, treating a null result as false. It is the codegen path for BasePredicate, with optional subexpression elimination.

nodes.name: GeneratePredicate
nodes.summary: CodeGenerator[Expression, BasePredicate] object. canonicalize uses ExpressionCanonicalizer and bind uses BindReferences; create compiles the generated predicate class.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Entry point taking an extra flag to enable subexpression elimination before creating the predicate.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Generates expression code and subexpression code, builds the SpecificPredicate source (eval returns !isNull && value), compiles it through CodeGenerator.compile and instantiates it with the references. A one-argument overload at line 35 delegates here with subexpression elimination off.

nodes.name: GenerateOrdering.scala
nodes.summary: Generates a Java class (SpecificOrdering) that compares two InternalRows for a list of SortOrder expressions, plus LazilyGeneratedOrdering, a serializable wrapper that regenerates the ordering after deserialization. Also supplies genComparisons, which CodegenContext.genComp reuses for struct comparison.

nodes.name: GenerateOrdering
nodes.summary: CodeGenerator[Seq[SortOrder], BaseOrdering] object. It binds and canonicalizes sort orders, generates compare code per key with null ordering and direction, and compiles the class.

nodes.name: genComparisons
nodes.summary: Generates compare code for a list of SortOrder: evaluates both rows' keys (rows named a and b), handles NullsFirst and NullsLast, calls ctx.genComp, flips sign for descending, and splits long comparison lists into functions via splitExpressions. Overloads at line 58 (StructType natural ascending order) delegate here.

nodes.name: createOrderKeys
nodes.summary: Sets ctx.INPUT_ROW to the given row name, clears currentVars and generates the key ExprCodes of each sort order eagerly (to avoid surprises with Stream inputs).

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Builds the SpecificOrdering source with compare(InternalRow a, InternalRow b), compiles it and instantiates it. A public create(schema: StructType) overload at line 48 builds ascending SortOrders over bound references.

nodes.name: LazilyGeneratedOrdering
nodes.summary: Ordering[InternalRow] that holds the SortOrder list and generates the compiled ordering on construction and after Java or Kryo deserialization, since the generated class itself is not serialized. The companion forSchema builds a natural ascending ordering.

nodes.name: predicates.scala
nodes.summary: Catalyst boolean expressions: the Predicate trait and BasePredicate evaluators, PredicateHelper (conjunct/disjunct splitting, pushdown helpers), Not, In, InSet, InSubquery, And, Or and the comparison operators. Documents the SQL three-valued logic (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN as NULL) in truth-table comments, which governs how WHERE and JOIN conditions treat NULL.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala case classes with hand-written interpreted eval and Java source generation (doGenCode); NULL is modeled as Scala null and returned as the UNKNOWN truth value.

nodes.name: arithmetic.scala
nodes.summary: Catalyst arithmetic expressions (UnaryMinus, Abs, Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, IntegralDivide, Remainder, Pmod, Least, Greatest) built on BinaryArithmetic. An EvalMode (LEGACY, ANSI, TRY) decides whether overflow and divide by zero wrap or return NULL, throw an error, or return NULL for try_* functions.
nodes.languageNotes: Each operator has both an interpreted nullSafeEval path and a generated Java path; decimal result precision and scale follow Hive/SQL-standard formulas documented inline.

nodes.name: conditionalExpressions.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the conditional expressions If, CaseWhen (CASE WHEN ... END) and the CaseKeyWhen factory for CASE key WHEN ... END. A branch is taken only when its condition evaluates to TRUE, so FALSE and NULL conditions both fall through to the next branch or the else value.
nodes.languageNotes: CaseWhen with a single branch reuses If.doGenCode; multi-branch codegen splits branches into generated methods driven by a small result-state byte.

nodes.name: BasePredicate
nodes.summary: Abstract base for compiled or interpreted predicates; exposes eval(InternalRow): Boolean so filters can be evaluated row by row.

nodes.name: InterpretedPredicate
nodes.summary: Interpreted BasePredicate that wraps an Expression, optionally with subexpression elimination, and casts the result of eval to Boolean. It is the fallback when code generation is unavailable or disabled.

nodes.name: Predicate
nodes.summary: Trait for boolean-valued expressions (dataType is BooleanType) plus the Predicate factory object, which builds a BasePredicate from an Expression, binding references to an input schema, and chooses GeneratePredicate or InterpretedPredicate through the code-gen-with-interpreted-fallback mechanism.

nodes.name: PredicateHelper
nodes.summary: Mix-in trait used by many optimizer rules and planner strategies. Provides splitting of AND/OR trees, balanced predicate building, canEvaluate checks, extraction of pushable conjuncts for a given output set, null-intolerance checks and a selectivity heuristic.

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.splitConjunctivePredicates
nodes.summary: Recursively flattens nested And nodes into a list of conjuncts, e.g. (a AND b) AND c becomes a, b, c. Used by filter pushdown and filter combining rules.

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.findExpressionAndTrackLineageDown
nodes.summary: Walks down a logical plan through Project, Aggregate and Union (undoing aliases) to find the single LeafNode where an expression's references originate, returning the rewritten expression and that leaf.

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.splitDisjunctivePredicates
nodes.summary: Recursively flattens nested Or nodes into a list of disjuncts.

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.buildBalancedPredicate
nodes.summary: Combines predicates pairwise bottom-up with a binary operator (And or Or) to build a balanced tree instead of a left-deep chain, keeping expression depth logarithmic.

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.canEvaluate
nodes.summary: True when all references of an expression are in the output of a plan, so evaluation can be moved to that plan (for example when pushing a filter to one side of a join).

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.canEvaluateWithinJoin
nodes.summary: Decides whether an expression may be used as a join condition: non-deterministic expressions, ListQuery, Exists and Unevaluable expressions are rejected, correlated subqueries are rejected, and PythonUDF is allowed (extracted later by ExtractPythonUDFFromJoinCondition).

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.extractPredicatesWithinOutputSet
nodes.summary: Returns the strongest filter whose references fit a given attribute set. And can be partially pushed (either side), Or only when both sides yield a result, otherwise the expression is kept only if all references fit. Assumes Not has already been pushed down by BooleanSimplification.

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.isNullIntolerant
nodes.summary: Recursive check that an expression and all of its children are null-intolerant (return NULL if any input is NULL).

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.outputWithNullability
nodes.summary: Marks attributes as non-nullable in an output list when their expression ids are known to be non-null, for example after an IsNotNull filter.

nodes.name: PredicateHelper.isLikelySelective
nodes.summary: Heuristic for whether a predicate is likely to filter rows: Not/And/Or are analysed recursively, while comparisons, IN/InSet, regex/string predicates and multi-LIKE count as selective.

nodes.name: Not
nodes.summary: Logical NOT. NULL input yields NULL (UNKNOWN) as shown in the truth table; canonicalization rewrites NOT over a comparison into the opposite comparison (for example NOT (a > b) becomes a <= b). Null-intolerant.

nodes.name: InSubquery
nodes.summary: Predicate for value IN (subquery). Unevaluable at runtime: the optimizer must rewrite it into a semi, anti or existence join. Validates matching column count and types and, unless the legacy flag is set, is nullable if either the values or the subquery output can be NULL.

nodes.name: InSubquery.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Checks that the number of left-hand values equals the subquery column count and that types match structurally, returning IN_SUBQUERY_LENGTH_MISMATCH or IN_SUBQUERY_DATA_TYPE_MISMATCH otherwise, then checks orderability.

nodes.name: UnresolvedInSubqueryPlanId
nodes.summary: Placeholder expression holding IN-subquery values and a plan id (used for Spark Connect); withPlan resolves it into InSubquery(values, ListQuery(plan)).

nodes.name: In
nodes.summary: SQL value IN (list). Returns NULL when the value is NULL, TRUE on the first match, NULL when no match but some list element is NULL, otherwise FALSE; an empty list is FALSE unless the legacy NULL-in-empty behavior is on. OptimizeIn turns literal-only lists into InSet.

nodes.name: In.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Requires every list element to be structurally the same type as the value (DATA_DIFF_TYPES otherwise) and the value type to be orderable.

nodes.name: In.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted IN semantics: empty list is FALSE (non-legacy), NULL value gives NULL, a matching element returns TRUE immediately, and an unmatched search that saw a NULL element returns NULL, else FALSE.

nodes.name: In.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java for IN using a tri-state result byte (HAS_NULL, NOT_MATCHED, MATCHED) inside a do-while loop so evaluation stops at the first match; large lists are split into helper methods.

nodes.name: InSet
nodes.summary: Optimized IN for a constant set of values, backed by a hash (or tree/collation-aware) set. Has NaN handling for float and double, returns NULL when the set contains NULL and nothing matches, and generates a Java switch for byte, short, int and date when the set is small enough.

nodes.name: InSet.eval
nodes.summary: Evaluates set membership: empty set is FALSE (non-legacy), NULL value gives NULL, a hit gives TRUE, NaN matches only if the set holds NaN, and a miss with a NULL in the set gives NULL.

nodes.name: InSet.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Chooses code generation strategy: constant false for empty set, a switch statement for small sets of byte/short/int/date (bounded by optimizerInSetSwitchThreshold), otherwise a hash set lookup.

nodes.name: InSet.genCodeWithSet
nodes.summary: Generates a null-safe Java lookup in the referenced set object, adding NaN checks for float/double and setting the null flag when the set contains NULL.

nodes.name: InSet.genCodeWithSwitch
nodes.summary: Generates a Java switch over literal case values for small integral sets, setting isNull to whether the set contains NULL in the default branch.

nodes.name: InSet.CollationAwareSet
nodes.summary: Immutable set wrapper for strings under non-binary collations that stores collation keys so membership compares by collation; mutation and iteration are unsupported.

nodes.name: And
nodes.summary: Logical AND with SQL three-valued logic (FALSE AND NULL is FALSE, TRUE AND NULL is NULL). eval short-circuits on a FALSE left side; the optimizer splits it into conjuncts for pushdown and BooleanSimplification rewrites it.

nodes.name: And.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted AND: returns false if either side is false (left evaluated first and right skipped when left is false), true if both are non-null true, otherwise null.

nodes.name: And.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java for AND with a fast path when neither child is nullable and a null-aware path otherwise; a false operand wins regardless of the other being null.

nodes.name: Or
nodes.summary: Logical OR with SQL three-valued logic (TRUE OR NULL is TRUE, FALSE OR NULL is NULL). eval short-circuits on a TRUE left side.

nodes.name: Or.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted OR: returns true if either side is true (right skipped when left is true), false if both are non-null false, otherwise null.

nodes.name: Or.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java for OR with a non-nullable fast path and a null-aware path where a true operand wins over NULL.

nodes.name: BinaryComparison
nodes.summary: Abstract base of =, <=>, <, <=, >, >= . Compares by structural type ignoring nullability, requires orderable types, canonicalizes operand order by hash code, and generates primitive comparisons directly (but not for boolean, float or double which use genComp). Companion unapply extracts (left, right).

nodes.name: BinaryComparison.canonicalized
nodes.summary: Canonical form so semantically equal comparisons match: EqualTo and EqualNullSafe order operands by hashCode, and GreaterThan/GreaterThanOrEqual are flipped into LessThan/LessThanOrEqual with swapped operands when needed.

nodes.name: BinaryComparison.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Uses a direct Java operator for primitive types other than boolean, float and double; otherwise calls ctx.genComp(...) compared against 0 so NaN and boolean ordering follow Spark rules.

nodes.name: Equality
nodes.summary: Extractor object that matches both EqualTo and EqualNullSafe and returns (left, right); used by rules and strategies that treat standard and null-safe equality alike (for example bucket pruning).

nodes.name: EqualTo
nodes.summary: SQL = operator. Returns NULL if either operand is NULL (so NULL = NULL is NULL, not true), otherwise ordering.equiv. Null-intolerant; map type is not supported.

nodes.name: EqualNullSafe
nodes.summary: Null-safe equality (<=>): TRUE when both sides are NULL, FALSE when exactly one is NULL, otherwise ordinary equality. Never nullable, so it always yields TRUE or FALSE.

nodes.name: EqualNullSafe.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted <=>: both null gives true, one null gives false, else ordering.equiv.

nodes.name: EqualNullSafe.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates a boolean expression combining both-null and both-non-null-and-equal cases and sets isNull to the false literal.

nodes.name: EqualNull
nodes.summary: SQL function equal_null(a, b); a RuntimeReplaceable that is replaced by EqualNullSafe(left, right).

nodes.name: LessThan
nodes.summary: SQL < operator; NULL if either side is NULL, otherwise ordering.lt. Null-intolerant.

nodes.name: LessThanOrEqual
nodes.summary: SQL <= operator; NULL if either side is NULL, otherwise ordering.lteq. Null-intolerant.

nodes.name: GreaterThan
nodes.summary: SQL > operator; NULL if either side is NULL, otherwise ordering.gt. Null-intolerant.

nodes.name: GreaterThanOrEqual
nodes.summary: SQL >= operator; NULL if either side is NULL, otherwise ordering.gteq. Null-intolerant.

nodes.name: IsUnknown
nodes.summary: Factory for IS UNKNOWN: an IsNull that additionally expects a boolean input and prints as IS UNKNOWN.

nodes.name: IsNotUnknown
nodes.summary: Factory for IS NOT UNKNOWN: an IsNotNull that additionally expects a boolean input and prints as IS NOT UNKNOWN.

nodes.name: UnaryMinus
nodes.summary: Unary minus (-x). With failOnError (default from spark.sql.ansi.enabled) integral negation uses MathUtils.negateExact and raises an overflow error for the minimum value; otherwise it wraps. Also handles decimals, calendar and ANSI intervals.

nodes.name: UnaryMinus.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java negation: decimal unary_$minus, exact negation for integral types when failOnError, plain two's-complement negation otherwise, and interval-specific helpers.

nodes.name: UnaryMinus.nullSafeEval
nodes.summary: Interpreted negate: exact variants for calendar interval (when failOnError), day-time and year-month intervals, and Numeric.negate for numeric types.

nodes.name: UnaryPositive
nodes.summary: Unary plus (+x), a RuntimeReplaceable that is replaced by its child; exposed as positive().

nodes.name: Abs
nodes.summary: abs(x) for numeric and ANSI interval types. With failOnError, integral types use negateExact so abs of the minimum value raises an overflow error rather than returning a negative number.

nodes.name: BinaryArithmetic
nodes.summary: Abstract base of binary arithmetic. Carries a NumericEvalContext whose evalMode (LEGACY, ANSI, TRY) drives failOnError: ANSI and TRY fail on error, TRY catches the exception and returns NULL. Defines decimal result type handling, nullability, query context for error messages and shared interpreted and generated evaluation.

nodes.name: BinaryArithmetic.failOnError
nodes.summary: True for EvalMode.ANSI and EvalMode.TRY, false for legacy mode; TRY executes the failing path but converts errors into NULL.

nodes.name: BinaryArithmetic.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Allows two decimal inputs with different precision and scale (result precision is computed by special formulas) and otherwise defers to BinaryOperator type checking.

nodes.name: BinaryArithmetic.nullable
nodes.summary: Result is nullable if an input is nullable, in TRY mode, or for decimals when the mode is not ANSI (decimal overflow returns NULL). Non-decimal arithmetic never returns NULL for non-null inputs: it wraps or fails.

nodes.name: BinaryArithmetic.initQueryContext
nodes.summary: Captures the SQL text origin context for error messages only when failOnError is true.

nodes.name: BinaryArithmetic.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java per result type: decimals via toPrecision with nullOnOverflow = !failOnError, intervals via helper utils, byte/short with an explicit range check that throws binaryArithmeticCauseOverflowError (suggesting try_add, try_subtract or try_multiply), int/long via exact math when failOnError, and double/float with plain operators (which can overflow to Infinity).

nodes.name: BinaryArithmetic.nullSafeCodeGen
nodes.summary: In TRY mode wraps the generated block in try/catch and sets isNull on any exception, which implements try_add, try_multiply and friends.

nodes.name: BinaryArithmetic.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted evaluation: NULL if either operand is NULL; in TRY mode catches any exception from nullSafeEval and returns NULL, otherwise propagates overflow errors.

nodes.name: Add
nodes.summary: Addition (+) for numerics and intervals. Legacy mode wraps integer overflow; ANSI/TRY use MathUtils.addExact for int and long; decimals use scale max(s1,s2) and precision max(p1-s1,p2-s2)+scale+1, and overflow becomes NULL unless failOnError. Commutative, so canonicalization reorders operands.

nodes.name: Add.resultDecimalType
nodes.summary: Computes decimal result precision and scale from operands; adjustPrecisionScale reduces scale when allowPrecisionLoss is on, otherwise the result is bounded.

nodes.name: Add.nullSafeEval
nodes.summary: Interpreted addition: decimals checked for overflow, intervals use exact variants when failOnError, int and long use MathUtils.addExact in ANSI/TRY mode, other types use plain Numeric.plus.

nodes.name: Add.canonicalized
nodes.summary: Reorders commutative Add operands into a canonical order, but skips the reorder when it would change the resolved decimal result type (SPARK-40903).

nodes.name: Subtract
nodes.summary: Subtraction (-) for numerics and intervals; mirrors Add in how overflow is handled (wrap in legacy mode, subtractExact in ANSI/TRY).

nodes.name: Subtract.nullSafeEval
nodes.summary: Interpreted subtraction with exact int/long arithmetic under failOnError, interval and decimal overflow checks, and plain Numeric.minus otherwise.

nodes.name: Multiply
nodes.summary: Multiplication (*). Decimal result has precision p1+p2+1 and scale s1+s2; int and long use multiplyExact under ANSI/TRY and wrap in legacy mode. Commutative.

nodes.name: Multiply.resultDecimalType
nodes.summary: Decimal multiplication result type: precision p1+p2+1 and scale s1+s2, adjusted or bounded depending on allowPrecisionLoss.

nodes.name: Multiply.nullSafeEval
nodes.summary: Interpreted multiplication with decimal overflow check, exact int/long multiply in failOnError mode and Numeric.times otherwise.

nodes.name: DivModLike
nodes.summary: Shared trait for Divide, IntegralDivide and Remainder. Always nullable, evaluates the right operand first and skips the left when the right is NULL or (non-ANSI) zero. Division by zero returns NULL in legacy mode and raises divideByZero/remainderByZero in ANSI mode; IntegralDivide on Long.MinValue / -1 raises an overflow error in ANSI mode.

nodes.name: DivModLike.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted division/remainder: right operand evaluated first; NULL or zero (when not failOnError) gives NULL; zero with failOnError throws a divide-by-zero (or remainder-by-zero for Remainder and Pmod) error; Long.MinValue / -1 throws when overflow checking is enabled.

nodes.name: DivModLike.divideByZeroErrorCode
nodes.summary: Returns the Java snippet that creates remainderByZeroError (for Remainder and Pmod) or divideByZeroError for the generated code.

nodes.name: DivModLike.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java that evaluates the divisor first, then either sets null (legacy) or throws (ANSI) on zero, optionally checks Long.MinValue / -1, and computes decimals through toPrecision with nullOnOverflow = !failOnError.

nodes.name: Divide
nodes.summary: The / operator, always floating point or decimal division. Overrides failOnError to be true only for ANSI (not TRY), because try_divide behaves like legacy division returning NULL on zero. Decimal result type follows the Hive formula with a minimum scale of 6.

nodes.name: Divide.resultDecimalType
nodes.summary: Computes decimal quotient precision/scale (scale at least MINIMUM_ADJUSTED_SCALE), with a separate bounded path when precision loss is not allowed.

nodes.name: IntegralDivide
nodes.summary: The div operator: integer division returning Long. Accepts long, decimal and interval inputs, returns NULL on zero in legacy mode, throws in ANSI mode, and checks Long.MinValue / -1 overflow when failOnError and the input is LongType.

nodes.name: IntegralDivide.checkDivideOverflow
nodes.summary: Enables the Long.MinValue / -1 overflow check only for LongType inputs when failOnError is true.

nodes.name: IntegralDivide.div
nodes.summary: Builds the quotient function for the left operand type (integral, decimal, year-month or day-time interval), applies decimal overflow checking and converts the result to Long.

nodes.name: Remainder
nodes.summary: The % / mod operator. Like Divide it fails only in ANSI mode (try_mod behaves like legacy mode and returns NULL on a zero divisor). Floating point types use the native % operator; the result keeps the sign of the dividend.

nodes.name: Remainder.mod
nodes.summary: Selects the remainder implementation by result type: fast paths for double and float, Integral.rem for integral types, and a decimal remainder with overflow check.

nodes.name: Pmod
nodes.summary: Positive modulo (pmod): a % n adjusted so the result is non-negative when the divisor is positive. Always nullable; a zero divisor yields NULL in legacy mode and remainderByZeroError when failOnError.

nodes.name: Pmod.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted pmod: evaluates the divisor first; NULL or non-ANSI zero gives NULL; zero under failOnError throws remainderByZeroError; otherwise applies the type-specific pmod function.

nodes.name: Pmod.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java for pmod with type-specific remainder adjustment (decimal, byte/short, other primitives) and divisor-first null or throw handling.

nodes.name: Least
nodes.summary: least(a, b, ...): returns the smallest argument, skipping NULLs; NULL only when all arguments are NULL. Needs at least two arguments of the same type and an orderable type. Used, for example, by EliminateLimits to merge limits.

nodes.name: Least.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Requires more than one child (otherwise raises a wrong-number-of-arguments error), identical child types and an orderable type.

nodes.name: Least.eval
nodes.summary: Folds over children keeping the smaller non-null value; null children are skipped.

nodes.name: Least.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java that starts with isNull = true and reassigns the value from each non-null child when it is smaller, splitting long argument lists into helper methods.

nodes.name: Greatest
nodes.summary: greatest(a, b, ...): returns the largest argument, skipping NULLs; NULL only when all arguments are NULL. Same type rules as Least.

nodes.name: Greatest.eval
nodes.summary: Folds over children keeping the larger non-null value; null children are skipped.

nodes.name: Greatest.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java that starts with isNull = true and reassigns the value from each non-null child when it is greater.

nodes.name: If
nodes.summary: IF(cond, a, b). Only a TRUE predicate selects the true value; both FALSE and NULL select the false value. Only the predicate is always evaluated (alwaysEvaluatedInputs), and the branch values are merged to a common type. SimplifyConditionals and PushFoldableIntoBranches rewrite it.

nodes.name: If.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Requires a boolean predicate (UNEXPECTED_INPUT_TYPE otherwise) and identical types of the two branch values (DATA_DIFF_TYPES otherwise).

nodes.name: If.eval
nodes.summary: Evaluates trueValue only when the predicate is exactly TRUE; NULL and FALSE predicates evaluate falseValue.

nodes.name: If.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates a Java if/else: the true branch runs when the condition is non-null and true, otherwise the false branch runs, copying isNull and value from the chosen branch.

nodes.name: CaseWhen
nodes.summary: CASE WHEN c1 THEN v1 [WHEN ...] [ELSE e] END. Branches are tried in order and the first condition that is exactly TRUE wins; with no match and no ELSE the result is NULL. Nullability is computed up to the first always-true branch. A single branch delegates codegen to If; multiple branches use split methods with a result-state byte. The companion provides the parser factory and the "when" function-registry entry.

nodes.name: CaseWhen.nullable
nodes.summary: Nullable if any branch value is nullable or the ELSE is missing/nullable; if a branch condition is the TrueLiteral only branches up to it count.

nodes.name: CaseWhen.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Requires all branch and ELSE values to share a type (DATA_DIFF_TYPES) and every branch condition to be boolean (UNEXPECTED_INPUT_TYPE).

nodes.name: CaseWhen.branchGroups
nodes.summary: Groups conditions and values separately for subexpression elimination, because a subexpression shared among conditions runs regardless of which matches while values only run on a match.

nodes.name: CaseWhen.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted CASE: loops over branches, returns the value of the first whose condition is TRUE, else the ELSE value or null.

nodes.name: CaseWhen.multiBranchesCodegen
nodes.summary: Generates Java for several branches using a tri-state byte (NOT_MATCHED, HAS_NONNULL, HAS_NULL) inside a do-while loop and splits conditions into generated methods to stay below JVM method size limits.

nodes.name: CaseWhen.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Uses If.doGenCode when there is only one branch (with a typed NULL else if none), otherwise multiBranchesCodegen.

nodes.name: CaseWhen.createFromParser
nodes.summary: Builds a CaseWhen from a flat expression list where even positions are conditions and odd positions are values; a trailing unpaired item becomes the ELSE.

nodes.name: CaseKeyWhen
nodes.summary: Factory for CASE key WHEN v1 THEN r1 ... END: expands to a CaseWhen whose conditions are EqualTo(key, v), so a NULL key never matches any WHEN and falls to ELSE or NULL.

nodes.name: CaseKeyWhen.apply
nodes.summary: Pairs the argument list into (EqualTo(key, cond), value) branches and sets the leftover odd argument as the ELSE value.

nodes.name: interfaces.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the contract for every Catalyst aggregate: AggregateMode, the AggregateExpression wrapper, AggregateFunction and its two flavors DeclarativeAggregate (expression-based buffer logic) and ImperativeAggregate (row-based initialize/update/merge/eval), plus TypedImperativeAggregate for arbitrary JVM objects as buffers. Physical aggregate operators (HashAggregateExec, SortAggregateExec, ObjectHashAggregateExec) drive these hooks.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala sealed trait with four case objects (Partial, PartialMerge, Final, Complete) as the mode enum; abstract classes define the buffer lifecycle contract.

nodes.name: AggregateMode
nodes.summary: Sealed trait with four case objects. Partial updates a buffer from raw input and emits the buffer; PartialMerge merges buffers and emits a buffer; Final merges buffers and emits the final result; Complete updates from raw input and emits the final result with no partial stage. These modes decide how a distributed group-by is split into map-side and reduce-side aggregation.

nodes.name: AggregateExpression
nodes.summary: Container that wraps an AggregateFunction together with its AggregateMode, an isDistinct flag, an optional FILTER (WHERE ...) predicate and a result ExprId. This is what actually appears in Aggregate plan nodes. It is Unevaluable, its references depend on the mode (raw inputs for Partial/Complete, buffer attributes for PartialMerge/Final), and its toString prefixes partial_ or merge_.

nodes.name: AggregateFunction
nodes.summary: Superclass of all aggregate functions with two flavors, ImperativeAggregate and DeclarativeAggregate. Subclasses must define the aggregation buffer schema and attributes; multiple functions share one combined buffer at runtime and must be stateless. toAggregateExpression() wraps the function in a Complete-mode AggregateExpression.

nodes.name: ImperativeAggregate
nodes.summary: Aggregate API based on imperative initialize(), update() and merge() over row-based buffers. mutableAggBufferOffset and inputAggBufferOffset locate this function's slice inside the larger shared buffer row used when an operator evaluates several aggregates at once. Mixes in CodegenFallback, so it is evaluated by interpretation.

nodes.name: DeclarativeAggregate
nodes.summary: Aggregate API expressed purely with Catalyst expressions: initialValues, updateExpressions, mergeExpressions and evaluateExpression operate on aggBufferAttributes. The RichAttribute helper provides .left/.right to refer to the two buffers during merge. It is never evaluated directly (eval and doGenCode throw); the operator inlines these expressions into generated code. Examples are Sum and Count.

nodes.name: TypedImperativeAggregate
nodes.summary: ImperativeAggregate whose buffer is an arbitrary JVM object of type T, kept in the buffer row and serialized to a single BinaryType column only before shuffle. Doc comment describes the stage workflow per AggregateMode and notes that hash aggregation needs ObjectHashAggregateExec or falls back to sort-based aggregation.

nodes.name: TypedAggregateWithHashMapAsBuffer
nodes.summary: TypedImperativeAggregate specialization that uses OpenHashMap[AnyRef, Long] as its buffer and implements serialize/deserialize by writing key/count pairs as UnsafeRows with a -1 terminator.

nodes.name: AggregateFunction.aggBufferAttributes
nodes.summary: Abstract declaration of the attributes that describe each field of the aggregation buffer (the intermediate state shuffled between partial and final aggregation).

nodes.name: AggregateFunction.toAggregateExpression
nodes.summary: Wraps this function in an AggregateExpression with mode Complete, the given isDistinct flag and optional filter. Analyzer and DataFrame API use it to turn a bare function into a plan-level aggregate.

nodes.name: ImperativeAggregate.initialize
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that initializes this function's slice of the mutable aggregation buffer, indexed by fieldNumber plus mutableAggBufferOffset.

nodes.name: ImperativeAggregate.update
