nodes.summary: Abstract hook that updates the mutable buffer from one input row. Input rows may come from an unsafe projection, so fields must not be cached.

nodes.name: ImperativeAggregate.merge
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that combines an input (immutable) aggregation buffer into the mutable buffer, using inputAggBufferOffset for the input side.

nodes.name: DeclarativeAggregate.initialValues
nodes.summary: Expressions that produce the empty aggregation buffer, one per buffer attribute.

nodes.name: DeclarativeAggregate.updateExpressions
nodes.summary: Expressions that compute the new buffer fields from the current buffer and an input row.

nodes.name: DeclarativeAggregate.mergeExpressions
nodes.summary: Expressions that merge two buffers, referring to each side via attr.left and attr.right.

nodes.name: DeclarativeAggregate.evaluateExpression
nodes.summary: Expression that turns the final buffer into the aggregate result; its type must match the function's dataType.

nodes.name: TypedImperativeAggregate.createAggregationBuffer
nodes.summary: Creates an empty buffer object of type T, called before processing each key group; initialize() stores it in the buffer row.

nodes.name: TypedImperativeAggregate.serialize
nodes.summary: Converts the buffer object T to bytes so partial results can be shuffled; invoked through serializeAggregateBufferInPlace in Partial and PartialMerge modes.

nodes.name: TypedImperativeAggregate.deserialize
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the buffer object T from shuffled bytes; merge(buffer row, input row) calls it before merging objects.

nodes.name: Sum.scala
nodes.summary: Declarative implementation of the SQL sum aggregate (also used for try_sum through TrySumExpressionBuilder). Handles decimal widening, integral promotion to long, interval types, and an extra isEmpty buffer field to distinguish empty input from overflow.

nodes.name: Sum
nodes.summary: Declarative sum aggregate. Buffer is (sum) or (sum, isEmpty) when overflow tracking is needed (decimals or try mode). updateExpressions ignore null inputs, mergeExpressions add two partial sums (null on overflow), and evaluateExpression returns null for empty input or applies CheckOverflowInSum for decimals. Result type is long for integrals, decimal(p+10, s) for decimals, double otherwise.

nodes.name: Count.scala
nodes.summary: Declarative implementation of the SQL count aggregate. Shows the minimal DeclarativeAggregate pattern: one long buffer field, initial value 0, update that adds 1 when no counted child is null, and merge that adds the two partial counts.

nodes.name: Count
nodes.summary: count(*), count(expr, ...) and count(DISTINCT ...) as a DeclarativeAggregate. Buffer holds a single non-nullable long: initialValues is 0, updateExpressions is count+1 (guarded by IsNull of nullable children), mergeExpressions is count.left + count.right, evaluateExpression is count, and defaultResult is 0 for empty input. A companion apply builds Count from a single child.

nodes.name: windowExpressions.scala
nodes.summary: Catalyst expressions for SQL window functions: WindowSpecDefinition (PARTITION BY, ORDER BY, frame), window frames and boundaries, the WindowExpression wrapper, the WindowFunction hierarchy (Lead, Lag, NthValue, RowNumber, Rank, DenseRank, PercentRank, CumeDist, NTile) and Pandas-on-Spark helpers (EWM, NullIndex). These are Unevaluable plan expressions that WindowExec and its frames execute.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala sealed traits and case objects model frame types and special boundaries; several window functions reuse DeclarativeAggregate with a per-row update.

nodes.name: WindowSpecDefinition
nodes.summary: The OVER clause: partitionSpec, orderSpec and a frameSpecification. Its checkInputDataTypes rejects an unspecified frame and invalid RANGE frames (no ORDER BY, several ORDER BY keys, or mismatched value boundary type). It is Unevaluable and only resolved once the frame is a SpecifiedWindowFrame.

nodes.name: FrameType
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the kind of a window frame (ROWS or RANGE), providing the accepted boundary input type and SQL keyword.

nodes.name: RowFrame
nodes.summary: ROWS frame: boundaries are physical row offsets, e.g. ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING is a three-row frame around the current row. Boundary type must be integer.

nodes.name: RangeFrame
nodes.summary: RANGE frame: rows with the same ORDER BY value are peers and boundaries are logical value offsets, so RANGE BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING covers rows whose ordering value lies in [v-1, v+1]. Without ORDER BY all rows are peers.

nodes.name: SpecialFrameBoundary
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for non-expression frame boundaries, with the case objects UnboundedPreceding, UnboundedFollowing and CurrentRow, each rendering its SQL keyword.

nodes.name: WindowFrame
nodes.summary: Sealed base trait for window frames. Unevaluable, non-nullable, and its dataType is not supported.

nodes.name: UnspecifiedFrame
nodes.summary: Placeholder frame used when the user gave no frame clause; the analyzer is expected to replace it with a concrete frame.

nodes.name: SpecifiedWindowFrame
nodes.summary: A concrete frame with a frameType (ROWS/RANGE) and lower and upper boundaries, each either a SpecialFrameBoundary or a foldable offset expression. Validates boundary types and ordering, and exposes isUnbounded, isValueBound and isOffset used by the window operator to choose a frame implementation.

nodes.name: WindowExpression
nodes.summary: Pairs a windowFunction expression with its WindowSpecDefinition, rendering as `func OVER (spec)`. Unevaluable; WindowExec evaluates it. The companion offers hasWindowExpression and a helper for the IGNORE NULLS argument.

nodes.name: WindowFunction
nodes.summary: Trait for functions that can only be evaluated inside a window operator; exposes the frame the operator must use, defaulting to UnspecifiedFrame.

nodes.name: WindowFunctionType
nodes.summary: Distinguishes SQL window functions from Python window UDFs. functionType classifies a window expression (a PythonUDAF counts as Python even though it extends AggregateFunction) and pythonEvalType maps a grouped-agg Pandas/Arrow UDF eval type to its window variant.

nodes.name: OffsetWindowFunction
nodes.summary: Trait for functions that read another row at a fixed offset from the current row or frame start (input, offset, default, ignoreNulls). fakeFrame is a ROWS frame built from the offset, used as a grouping key so functions with equal offsets are evaluated together.

nodes.name: FrameLessOffsetWindowFunction
nodes.summary: Offset window function that cannot specify its own frame (Lead and Lag). Uses the fake offset frame, requires a foldable offset, and has the input data type as result type.

nodes.name: Lead
nodes.summary: lead(input, offset, default): value of input at the offset-th row after the current row, or default when no such row exists. Default offset is 1; supports IGNORE NULLS.

nodes.name: Lag
nodes.summary: lag(input, offset, default): value of input at the offset-th row before the current row. Implemented by negating inputOffset to form the internal offset.

nodes.name: AggregateWindowFunction
nodes.summary: Base class for window functions that are DeclarativeAggregates (row_number, rank, ntile, nth_value ...). Default frame is ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to CURRENT ROW, default type is integer, and mergeExpressions throws because window evaluation only updates and evaluates.

nodes.name: RowNumberLike
nodes.summary: Base for window functions built around a single rowNumber buffer field that is incremented per row; non-nullable.

nodes.name: SizeBasedWindowFunction
nodes.summary: Trait for window functions that need the partition size, exposed as the attribute window__partition__size. The attribute is a val so the driver-side expression ID survives serialization to executors.

nodes.name: RowNumber
nodes.summary: row_number(): unique sequential number per row within the window partition, starting at one.

nodes.name: CumeDist
nodes.summary: cume_dist(): number of rows preceding or equal to the current row divided by the partition size. Uses a RANGE frame so ties get the same value.

nodes.name: NthValue
nodes.summary: nth_value(input, offset[, ignoreNulls]): the offset-th row (1-based) from the start of the window frame, tracked with result and count buffer fields; null if the frame is smaller. Both an AggregateWindowFunction and an OffsetWindowFunction, with an unspecified frame so the user's frame applies.

nodes.name: NTile
nodes.summary: ntile(n): splits the partition into n buckets numbered from 1, bucket sizes differing by at most one with remainder rows going to the first buckets. Tracks rowNumber, bucket, bucketThreshold, bucketSize and bucketsWithPadding in the buffer and needs the partition size.

nodes.name: RankLike
nodes.summary: Base for rank-style functions. Stores the ORDER BY values in the buffer, compares them with null-safe equality to detect a change, and increases the rank from rankSource when the order values change. withOrder lets the analyzer inject the window ORDER BY expressions as children.

nodes.name: Rank
nodes.summary: rank(): one plus the number of rows preceding or equal to the current row; produces gaps after ties.

nodes.name: DenseRank
nodes.summary: dense_rank(): rank increments by one on each change of the ORDER BY values, so no gaps. Overrides rankSource to rank + 1 and uses a smaller buffer.

nodes.name: PercentRank
nodes.summary: percent_rank(): (rank - 1) / (partition size - 1), or 0 for a single-row partition. Returns double.

nodes.name: WindowFunctionType.functionType
nodes.summary: Finds the first Python window UDF or SQL window function or aggregate in a window expression and returns Python or SQL. Defaults to SQL when the optimizer replaced the function with a literal.

nodes.name: WindowFunctionType.pythonEvalType
nodes.summary: For a PythonUDAF inside a window expression, maps SQL_GROUPED_AGG_PANDAS_UDF to SQL_WINDOW_AGG_PANDAS_UDF and SQL_GROUPED_AGG_ARROW_UDF to SQL_WINDOW_AGG_ARROW_UDF.

nodes.name: PythonUDF.scala
nodes.summary: Catalyst expressions that represent Python user-defined functions in a logical plan: PythonUDF (scalar), PythonUDAF (grouped aggregate), PythonUDTF (table function), plus helper traits and the PythonUDF companion with eval-type checks. They are unevaluable placeholders that carry the serialized PythonFunction; dedicated physical operators (e.g. BatchEvalPythonExec, ArrowEvalPythonExec) run them in Python workers.

nodes.name: PythonUDF
nodes.summary: Scalar Python UDF expression: name, serialized PythonFunction, return dataType, children, evalType (e.g. batched, scalar Pandas or Arrow), udfDeterministic and a resultId. Unevaluable, so it cannot be pushed to data sources and is extracted into a separate physical operator. Companion helpers: isScalarPythonUDF, isWindowPandasUDF, correctEvalType. canonicalized ignores resultId.

nodes.name: PythonUDF.isScalarPythonUDF
nodes.summary: True when the expression is a PythonUDF whose evalType is one of the scalar types (batched, Arrow-batched, scalar Pandas/Arrow, iterator variants).

nodes.name: PythonUDF.isWindowPandasUDF
nodes.summary: True for PythonUDAF expressions, which are the only Python functions currently usable as window functions.

nodes.name: PythonUDF.correctEvalType
nodes.summary: Returns SQL_BATCHED_UDF instead of SQL_ARROW_BATCHED_UDF when the UDF touches a UserDefinedType and the fallback flag is set; otherwise the UDF's own evalType.

nodes.name: PythonFuncExpression
nodes.summary: Common trait of PythonUDF, PythonUDAF and PythonUDTF: name, PythonFunction, evalType, udfDeterministic and resultId. Determinism requires both udfDeterministic and deterministic children; always nullable.

nodes.name: UnevaluableAggregateFunc
nodes.summary: AggregateFunction base whose buffer methods and eval/codegen all throw; used for aggregates executed outside the normal Aggregate operator.

nodes.name: PythonUDAF
nodes.summary: Grouped-aggregate Python UDF (default evalType SQL_GROUPED_AGG_PANDAS_UDF). An AggregateFunction that is never evaluated by Catalyst; a dedicated physical operator runs it in Python. Can be wrapped by toAggregateExpression and reused as a window function.

nodes.name: PythonUDTF
nodes.summary: Python user-defined table function call: element schema, optional pickled analyze result, children, evalType, determinism and partitioning/table-argument metadata. A Generator that is never evaluated by Catalyst.

nodes.name: PythonUDTFAnalyzeResult
nodes.summary: Result of a polymorphic UDTF analyze method: output schema, single-partition flag, PARTITION BY and ORDER BY expressions and selected input expressions. applyToTableArgument merges these into a TABLE argument and rejects incompatible settings.

nodes.name: PrettyPythonUDF
nodes.summary: Placeholder aggregate-like expression used only to print a Python UDF without debugging information such as the result id.

nodes.name: ScalaUDF.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ScalaUDF expression that wraps a user-supplied Scala or Java function in a Catalyst plan, converting Catalyst values to Scala values for inputs and back for the result, either by interpreted eval (a children-count-specialized closure for 0 to 22 arguments) or by generated code. Large part of the file is the generated 0-22 arity dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: The arity-specific closures were produced by a script quoted in the file; the file is long mostly because of that expansion.

nodes.name: ScalaUDF
nodes.summary: Expression for a Scala/Java UDF: function, dataType, children, optional inputEncoders and outputEncoder (present for typed UDFs), udfName, nullable and udfDeterministic. Inputs are converted from Catalyst to Scala with ExpressionEncoder when available, otherwise with CatalystTypeConverters, and the result is converted back. It is stateful and expensive, and its canonicalized form drops encoders. Primitive inputs make the UDF return null on null input.

nodes.name: ScalaUDF.inputPrimitives
nodes.summary: Per-argument flags saying whether the encoder's type is a Scala primitive (non-nullable, not struct); the analyzer uses it to add null handling, so primitive null inputs yield null results.

nodes.name: ScalaUDF.catalystConverter
nodes.summary: Builds the converter from the UDF's Scala result to the Catalyst value: uses the outputEncoder serializer for typed UDFs, otherwise CatalystTypeConverters for the return type.

nodes.name: ScalaUDF.scalaConverter
nodes.summary: Builds the converter from a Catalyst argument to a Scala value. Uses the input ExpressionEncoder deserializer for non-primitive typed inputs, and CatalystTypeConverters for untyped Scala/Java UDFs, unsupported types such as Any, and primitives. Returns whether an encoder was used.

nodes.name: ScalaUDF.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Generates Java code that evaluates children, converts each argument, calls the function with try/catch wrapping failures as failedExecuteUserDefinedFunctionError, converts the result and sets the null flag.

nodes.name: ScalaUDF.eval
nodes.summary: Interpreted evaluation: runs the arity-specific closure f on the input row, wraps exceptions in a user-defined-function error, then converts the result.

nodes.name: Expression.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the Expression abstract class and the helper traits and abstract classes that all Catalyst expressions build on. Expression declares nullable, dataType, eval (interpreted) and genCode/doGenCode (Java code generation), plus foldable, deterministic, resolved and canonicalized, which analyzer and optimizer rules such as ConstantFolding rely on.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file of abstract classes and mixin traits. Concrete expressions are case classes that extend LeafExpression, UnaryExpression, BinaryExpression and so on, and override eval/nullSafeEval and doGenCode.

nodes.name: Expression
nodes.summary: Root class of every expression node in Catalyst, extending TreeNode[Expression]. It declares the abstract members nullable, dataType, eval and doGenCode, and defaults for foldable (false), deterministic (all children deterministic), resolved (children resolved and input types pass) and canonicalized (children canonicalized). Expressions exposed as SQL functions must be case classes whose constructor arguments are all Expressions.

nodes.name: ExpressionPatternBitMask
nodes.summary: Holds a BitSet mask of all TreePattern ids below OPERATOR_START, used by Expression.validateNodePatterns (when testing) to assert that expressions only report expression-level patterns.

nodes.name: Unevaluable
nodes.summary: Mixin for expressions that exist only during analysis or optimization (for example Star) and must never run. It forces foldable to false and makes both eval and doGenCode throw an error, so such nodes cannot be constant folded or code generated.

nodes.name: RuntimeReplaceable
nodes.summary: Mixin for expressions that the optimizer rewrites into a different expression through the replacement member, mainly for compatibility with other databases (the doc gives nvl replaced by coalesce). nullable, dataType and canonicalized delegate to the replacement; eval evaluates the replacement and doGenCode is disabled.

nodes.name: InheritAnalysisRules
nodes.summary: Add-on to RuntimeReplaceable that makes the replacement the single child of the expression so it inherits analysis rules such as type coercion. It overrides child, argument printing and sql to use the original parameters.

nodes.name: RuntimeReplaceableAggregate
nodes.summary: Add-on of AggregateFunction that is rewritten by the optimizer into another aggregate, such as every/any/some rewritten with Min and Max. Its aggregation buffer members throw an internal error because it is never executed directly.

nodes.name: NonSQLExpression
nodes.summary: Marker trait for expressions without a SQL form (ScalaUDF, ScalaUDAF, MapObjects, Invoke). Its sql method rewrites attributes and aliases into PrettyAttribute (and Python UDFs into PrettyPythonUDF) and prints the tree as an arbitrary user-facing string.

nodes.name: Nondeterministic
nodes.summary: Trait for expressions whose result is not a pure function of their inputs (random numbers, partition id). It fixes deterministic and foldable to false, requires initialize(partitionIndex) before eval, and splits subclass logic into initializeInternal and evalInternal. Optimizers must not fold or reorder such expressions.

nodes.name: ConditionalExpression
nodes.summary: Trait for expressions with branches that are not all executed (If, CaseWhen style). It is foldable only when all children are, and exposes alwaysEvaluatedInputs and branchGroups so subexpression elimination can find common expressions that are safe to evaluate eagerly.

nodes.name: LeafExpression
nodes.summary: Abstract class for expressions with no children, combining Expression with LeafLike. Literal and attribute references extend it.

nodes.name: UnaryExpression
nodes.summary: Abstract class for expressions with one child. By default it is foldable and nullable exactly when its child is, and eval returns null for a null child, otherwise calls nullSafeEval. nullSafeCodeGen and defineCodeGen build the matching Java code, adding a null check only when the expression is nullable. The companion object provides an unapply extractor for the child.

nodes.name: SupportQueryContext
nodes.summary: Trait for expressions that carry the SQL query context (used for error messages). The context is kept as a tag-like field, copied across rule transforms through copyTagsFrom, and can be passed to generated code through getContextOrNullCode.

nodes.name: BinaryExpression
nodes.summary: Abstract class for expressions with two children. Result is null if either input is null, foldable only if both children are, and eval evaluates the left side first and short-circuits to null before calling nullSafeEval(left, right). nullSafeCodeGen generates nested null checks for the two children. The companion object provides an unapply extractor.

nodes.name: BinaryOperator
nodes.summary: BinaryExpression for infix operators printed as (x symbol y). It requires both inputs to have the same data type (otherwise error BINARY_OP_DIFF_TYPES) and to be accepted by inputType (BINARY_OP_WRONG_TYPE); type coercion inserts casts to the tightest common type before this check runs. Companion object provides unapply.

nodes.name: TernaryExpression
nodes.summary: Abstract class for expressions with three children, with the same null-intolerant defaults as the unary and binary versions: any null input gives null, with eval, nullSafeEval, defineCodeGen and nullSafeCodeGen helpers.

nodes.name: QuaternaryExpression
nodes.summary: Abstract class for expressions with four children, providing the same null-propagating eval, nullSafeEval and code generation helpers.

nodes.name: QuinaryExpression
nodes.summary: Abstract class for expressions with five children, providing the same null-propagating eval, nullSafeEval and code generation helpers.

nodes.name: SeptenaryExpression
nodes.summary: Abstract class for expressions with seven children (the last one optional in code generation), with the same null-propagating eval and code generation helpers.

nodes.name: ComplexTypeMergingExpression
nodes.summary: Trait for expressions such as CaseWhen that merge data from several children of complex types. It computes dataType by reducing the children's types with TypeCoercion.findCommonTypeDifferentOnlyInNullFlags, so nullable, containsNull and valueContainsNull flags are merged, and fails if the types differ beyond those flags.

nodes.name: UserDefinedExpression
nodes.summary: Common marker trait for user-defined functions (UDF, UDAF, UDTF in various languages and Hive wrappers), exposing only a name.

nodes.name: CommutativeExpression
nodes.summary: Trait for commutative operators such as And or Add. It gathers adjacent same-class operators iteratively, sorts their canonicalized operands by hashCode, and rebuilds either a binary tree or a MultiCommutativeOp when there are many operands, so a+b and b+a canonicalize to the same expression.

nodes.name: MultiCommutativeOp
nodes.summary: Unevaluable helper node used only during canonicalization to represent a long chain of commutative operations (Add, Multiply, And, Or, bitwise ops) in one node instead of many intermediate objects, as a memory optimization. It deduces decimal result types from the original root expression.

nodes.name: DefaultStringProducingExpression
nodes.summary: Trait for expressions whose result type is the default StringType.

nodes.name: Expression.foldable
nodes.summary: Whether the expression can be statically evaluated before execution; false by default. ConstantFolding replaces foldable expressions with a Literal. Unary and binary expressions are foldable when their children are, and Literal is always foldable.

nodes.name: Expression.deterministic
nodes.summary: Lazy val that is true when all children are deterministic. Expressions relying on mutable state or implicit inputs (for example partition id) are non-deterministic and must not be evaluated during planning or have their count or order changed.

nodes.name: Expression.nullable
nodes.summary: Abstract member saying whether the expression can produce null. Optimizer rules and code generation use it to drop null checks when a value cannot be null.

nodes.name: Expression.references
nodes.summary: Returns the AttributeSet of attributes this expression reads, computed as the union of its children's references. Column pruning and similar rules use it.

nodes.name: Expression.freshCopyIfContainsStatefulExpression
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the expression tree in which stateful expressions (those with mutable state, such as rand()) are replaced by fresh copies, or the original tree if none are stateful. This prevents two uses of the same rand() from sharing state in interpreted execution.

nodes.name: Expression.eval
nodes.summary: Abstract interpreted evaluation: returns the result of the expression for a given InternalRow. This is the fallback path when code generation is not used, and is also how foldable expressions are computed at optimization time.

nodes.name: Expression.genCode
nodes.summary: Returns an ExprCode containing Java source that computes the expression. If an equivalent subexpression was already computed (CodegenContext.subExprEliminationExprs, keyed by ExpressionEquals) it reuses that result; otherwise it allocates fresh isNull/value names, calls doGenCode, and may split very large code into a separate method.

nodes.name: Expression.reduceCodeSize
nodes.summary: When generated code exceeds the method split threshold (SQLConf methodSplitThreshold) and the context uses an input row, moves the code into a new private method and replaces it with a call, keeping isNull in a mutable global. Helps avoid JVM method size limits.

nodes.name: Expression.doGenCode
nodes.summary: Protected abstract hook where concrete expressions produce their Java code for a CodegenContext and a pre-named ExprCode. Expressions without code generation can mix in CodegenFallback, which calls eval instead.

nodes.name: Expression.resolved
nodes.summary: Lazy val that is true when all children are resolved and checkInputDataTypes succeeds. The analyzer repeats rules until every expression is resolved; dataType may only be read on resolved expressions.

nodes.name: Expression.canonicalized
nodes.summary: Lazy val that returns a normalized form of the expression with cosmetic differences removed (attribute names, order of commutative operands). By default it canonicalizes children bottom-up; adjacent commutative expressions of the same class are canonicalized together from the root.

nodes.name: Expression.withCanonicalizedChildren
nodes.summary: Default canonicalization step: canonicalizes every child and rebuilds the node with those children via withNewChildren.

nodes.name: Expression.semanticEquals
nodes.summary: Final method returning true when both expressions are deterministic and their canonicalized forms are equal, i.e. they always compute the same result even if they differ cosmetically. Used by subexpression elimination and sort ordering checks.

nodes.name: Expression.semanticHash
nodes.summary: Hash code of the canonicalized expression, consistent with semanticEquals.

nodes.name: Expression.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Returns TypeCheckResult.TypeCheckSuccess by default; expressions override it to return a failure describing invalid input types. Only valid to call once children are resolved, and it feeds Expression.resolved.

nodes.name: Expression.prettyName
nodes.summary: User-facing function name: a registered alias tag if present, otherwise the lower-cased node name. Used by toString and sql.

nodes.name: UnaryExpression.eval
nodes.summary: Default evaluation: evaluates the child and returns null if it is null, otherwise calls nullSafeEval(value). Subclasses that change nullability should override this too.

nodes.name: UnaryExpression.nullSafeEval
nodes.summary: Protected hook called by eval with a non-null child value; the default throws a notOverrideExpectedMethods error, so subclasses override it (or eval).

nodes.name: UnaryExpression.nullSafeCodeGen
nodes.summary: Generates Java code for a unary expression: generates the child's code, then wraps the result code in a null check when the expression is nullable, or emits it directly with isNull = false otherwise. defineCodeGen is a shorthand that assigns the value.

nodes.name: BinaryExpression.eval
nodes.summary: Default evaluation: evaluates left, returns null if null, evaluates right, returns null if null, otherwise calls nullSafeEval(left, right).

nodes.name: BinaryExpression.nullSafeEval
nodes.summary: Protected hook called with two non-null values; throws by default so subclasses override it (or eval).

nodes.name: BinaryExpression.nullSafeCodeGen
nodes.summary: Generates Java code for a binary expression with nested null checks for left and right, only for sides that are nullable. When the expression itself is not nullable the child code is emitted without checks and isNull is the literal false.

nodes.name: BinaryOperator.checkInputDataTypes
nodes.summary: Fails with BINARY_OP_DIFF_TYPES if left and right differ in type and BINARY_OP_WRONG_TYPE if the type is not accepted by inputType; otherwise succeeds. This is the check that type coercion is meant to satisfy by casting both sides to a common type.

nodes.name: Nondeterministic.initialize
nodes.summary: Final method that calls initializeInternal(partitionIndex) and marks the expression as initialized.

nodes.name: Nondeterministic.eval
nodes.summary: Final eval that requires initialize to have been called, then delegates to evalInternal.

nodes.name: CommutativeExpression.gatherCommutative
nodes.summary: Iteratively walks adjacent commutative operators with a queue (avoiding recursion for deep trees) and collects the canonicalized non-matching operands.

nodes.name: CommutativeExpression.buildCanonicalizedPlan
nodes.summary: Orders the operands by hashCode and folds them with the given binary builder, or builds a MultiCommutativeOp when the operand count reaches MULTI_COMMUTATIVE_OP_OPT_THRESHOLD.

nodes.name: ComplexTypeMergingExpression.dataTypeCheck
nodes.summary: Requires a non-empty list of input types and that they all have the same type (ignoring nullability flags) via TypeCoercion.haveSameType, otherwise raises COMPLEX_EXPRESSION_UNSUPPORTED_INPUT errors.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the default (non-ANSI) implicit type coercion rule set. TypeCoercion lists the ordered rules the analyzer applies to insert Casts so operands have compatible types, and defines the widening helpers findTightestCommonType, findWiderTypeForTwo and the implicitCast table that decides which input type converts to which expected type.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object extending TypeCoercionBase (defined elsewhere); also defines the TypeCoercionRule trait that wraps expression transforms as plan Rules.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion
nodes.summary: Singleton holding the default type coercion rules and helpers. typeCoercionRules lists the rule order (UnpivotCoercion, WidenSetOperationTypes, ..., then a combined group with InConversion, PromoteStrings, DecimalPrecision, BooleanEquality, ImplicitTypeCasts, DateTimeOperations and others). It also defines the widening logic used for unions, comparisons and implicit casts.

nodes.name: TypeCoercionRule
nodes.summary: Base trait for a type coercion rule: a Rule[LogicalPlan] whose subclasses supply a PartialFunction transform over expressions. apply walks the plan bottom-up, propagates changed attribute types to parents (propagateTypes), then applies the expression transform with pruning.

nodes.name: PromoteStrings
nodes.summary: Rule that promotes string operands in arithmetic and comparison expressions (delegates to StringPromotionTypeCoercion once children are resolved).

nodes.name: BooleanEquality
nodes.summary: Rule that changes numeric values to booleans so that expressions like true = 1 can be evaluated, delegating to BooleanEqualityTypeCoercion.

nodes.name: DateTimeOperations
nodes.summary: Rule for date/time arithmetic coercion, delegating to DateTimeOperationsTypeCoercion once children are resolved.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.typeCoercionRules
nodes.summary: Ordered list of coercion rules the analyzer runs: UnpivotCoercion, WidenSetOperationTypes, ProcedureArgumentCoercion, DefaultValueExpressionCoercion, then a CombinedTypeCoercionRule that groups the expression-level rules (CollationTypeCasts, InConversion, PromoteStrings, DecimalPrecision, BooleanEquality, FunctionArgumentConversion, ..., ImplicitTypeCasts, DateTimeOperations, WindowFrameCoercion, StringLiteralCoercion).

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.canCast
nodes.summary: Delegates to Cast.canCast to decide whether a cast between two types is allowed in non-ANSI mode.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.findTightestCommonType
nodes.summary: Finds the narrowest type both inputs can be widened to without losing precision: equal types, NullType with anything, wider decimal over integral, the higher of two numeric types, wider datetime and interval types, GEOGRAPHY/GEOMETRY fixed SRID to ANY, and nested types via findTypeForComplex. Returns None when there is none.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.stringPromotion
nodes.summary: Promotes a string with another atomic type (except binary and boolean) all the way to StringType; two strings with different collations give None.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.canPromoteAsInBinaryComparison
nodes.summary: Says whether a string literal can be promoted to the given type in a binary comparison: true for atomic types except strings and the ambiguous interval types.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.findCommonTypeForBinaryComparison
nodes.summary: Chooses the target type for a comparison when one side is a string and the other is not (date or timestamp versus string depends on castDatetimeToString, decimal versus string becomes double, otherwise the non-string type), and makes timestamp the target for date vs timestamp.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.findWiderTypeForTwo
nodes.summary: Widening for two types where some precision loss is accepted: tries the tightest common type, then decimal widening, string promotion, then complex types recursively.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.findWiderCommonType
nodes.summary: Folds findWiderTypeForTwo over a list of types, handling string types first because the two-type function is not associative for strings.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.implicitCast
nodes.summary: Implicit cast logic. The public overload returns the expression unchanged if the type already matches, or wraps it in Cast otherwise. The private overload holds the rule table: null to target default, string to numeric (double for the generic NumericType), numeric to numeric, datetime conversions, atomic to string, array and map element-wise casts honoring nullability, and TypeCollection fallback. The range covers both overloads.

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.findCommonTypeDifferentOnlyInNullFlags
nodes.summary: Returns the common type of types that differ only in nullable, containsNull or valueContainsNull flags, or None. Has a two-type and a list overload (range covers both).

nodes.name: TypeCoercion.hasStringType
nodes.summary: Tail-recursive check whether a type is StringType or an array of strings; used to order the inputs of findWiderCommonType.

nodes.name: TypeCoercionRule.apply
nodes.summary: Rule entry point. Uses transformUpWithBeforeAndAfterRuleOnChildren on not-yet-analyzed plans, skips nodes with unresolved children, propagates attribute type changes, then applies the expression-level transform via transformExpressionsUpWithPruning.

nodes.name: TypeCoercionRule.transform
nodes.summary: Abstract partial function from Expression to Expression that each concrete coercion rule implements.

nodes.name: TypeCoercionRule.propagateTypes
nodes.summary: After children changed, rewrites AttributeReferences in the plan whose resolved data type or nullability differs from the child output, so parent operators see updated types.

nodes.name: AnsiTypeCoercion.scala
nodes.summary: Type coercion rules for ANSI mode, where implicit casts follow SQL type precedence lists instead of Spark's looser default. AnsiTypeCoercion reuses the TypeCoercionRule infrastructure but replaces the rule set, the tightest common type (integral and float give double), implicit cast (allowed only when Cast.canANSIStoreAssign), and canCast (Cast.canAnsiCast).
nodes.languageNotes: Scala object extending TypeCoercionBase; mirrors TypeCoercion with ANSI-specific overrides and its own PromoteStrings, GetDateFieldOperations and DateTimeOperations rules.

nodes.name: AnsiTypeCoercion
nodes.summary: Singleton that holds the ANSI coercion rule order (same list as default, without BooleanEquality and StringLiteralCoercion, plus GetDateFieldOperations) and ANSI-specific type widening. The doc explains the type precedence lists per primitive type; strings may still be implicitly cast to other primitive types as a deliberate non-standard allowance.

nodes.name: AnsiTypeCoercion.typeCoercionRules
nodes.summary: Ordered ANSI rule list; the expression-level group is wrapped in AnsiCombinedTypeCoercionRule so it gets its own rule id and can run alongside the default rules on one plan.

nodes.name: AnsiTypeCoercion.findTightestCommonType
nodes.summary: Same shape as the default version, with one ANSI difference: if the wider of two numeric types would be Float (an integral type with a float), it returns Double to avoid precision loss.

nodes.name: AnsiTypeCoercion.findWiderTypeForTwo
nodes.summary: Widening for two types in ANSI mode, using AnsiStringPromotionTypeCoercion.findWiderTypeForString instead of the default string promotion.

nodes.name: AnsiTypeCoercion.findWiderCommonType
nodes.summary: Folds findWiderTypeForTwo over the types without the string ordering special case the default version uses.

nodes.name: AnsiTypeCoercion.implicitCast
nodes.summary: ANSI implicit cast: allowed only when the expected type is in the input type's precedence list, checked with Cast.canANSIStoreAssign against the default concrete type. Fractional to integral is refused; strings may convert to atomic, numeric, timestamp and time types. The range covers the public expression overload and the private data type overload.

nodes.name: AnsiTypeCoercion.canCast
nodes.summary: Delegates to Cast.canAnsiCast.

nodes.name: PromoteStrings
nodes.summary: ANSI version of the string promotion rule, delegating to AnsiStringPromotionTypeCoercion.

nodes.name: GetDateFieldOperations
nodes.summary: Rule that casts a Timestamp column to date when extracting a date field. Needed because the ANSI implicit cast does not allow Timestamp to Date, unlike the default implicit cast rule.

nodes.name: DateTimeOperations
nodes.summary: ANSI version of date/time arithmetic coercion, delegating to AnsiDateTimeOperationsTypeCoercion.

nodes.name: AnsiCombinedTypeCoercionRule
nodes.summary: Subclass of CombinedTypeCoercionRule that exists only to get a new rule id, so default and ANSI type coercion can both run on one logical plan.

nodes.name: dataframe.py
nodes.summary: Classic (py4j) implementation of the PySpark DataFrame API. Each DataFrame holds a py4j proxy _jdf of the JVM Dataset; transformations call the matching _jdf method and wrap the returned proxy in a new DataFrame, so no rows are processed in Python except collect/UDF/pandas conversions. Also defines the classic DataFrameNaFunctions and DataFrameStatFunctions.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain Python wrappers over py4j JavaObject proxies; Scala Seq and Map arguments are built through helpers such as _jseq, _jcols and _jmap.

nodes.name: DataFrame
nodes.summary: Classic PySpark DataFrame (extends the abstract DataFrame API from pyspark/sql/dataframe.py plus PandasMapOpsMixin and PandasConversionMixin). Stores the JVM Dataset proxy in _jdf together with the SparkSession and SparkContext, and delegates each API call to _jdf, returning new DataFrame objects around the resulting proxies.

nodes.name: DataFrameNaFunctions
nodes.summary: Classic implementation of df.na: holds a DataFrame and forwards drop, fill and replace to dropna, fillna and replace on it.

nodes.name: DataFrameStatFunctions
nodes.summary: Classic implementation of df.stat: holds a DataFrame and forwards approxQuantile, corr, cov, crosstab, freqItems and sampleBy to the DataFrame methods of the same name.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Constructor: takes the JVM Dataset proxy jdf and a SparkSession (a legacy SQLContext is accepted with a warning), and stores _jdf, _session, _sc, is_cached and the repr-html flag.

nodes.name: rdd
nodes.summary: Cached property that converts the Dataset to an RDD of Rows via _jdf.javaToPython() and wraps it in a Python RDD with a pickle serializer; foreach and foreachPartition go through it.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Cached property that calls _jdf.schema().json() and parses the JSON into a StructType, raising PySparkValueError when parsing fails.

nodes.name: explain
nodes.summary: Validates the extended/mode arguments, maps them to an explain mode string and prints PythonSQLUtils.explainString for _jdf.queryExecution() obtained through sc._jvm.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Prints the table form of the DataFrame by printing the string returned from _show_string.

nodes.name: _show_string
nodes.summary: Validates n, vertical and truncate, then calls _jdf.showString(n, truncate, vertical) on the JVM and returns the formatted text.

nodes.name: __repr__
nodes.summary: Returns the eager-evaluation table string from _jdf.showString when spark.sql.repl.eagerEval.enabled is true (read through the session _jconf), otherwise the DataFrame[col: type, ...] summary built from dtypes.

nodes.name: hint
nodes.summary: Validates the hint name and parameters, converts Columns and lists to JVM objects with a local converter, and calls _jdf.hint(name, jseq) to return a new DataFrame.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Action that returns int(self._jdf.count()); the counting runs entirely in the JVM.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Action that calls _jdf.collectToPython() to get a socket, then reads the pickled rows from it with _load_from_socket and returns them as a list of Row; this is where data is transferred into the Python process.

nodes.name: take
nodes.summary: Returns the first num rows by running limit(num).collect().

nodes.name: tail
nodes.summary: Action that calls _jdf.tailToPython(num) and reads the pickled rows from the returned socket into a list of Row.

nodes.name: cache
nodes.summary: Marks is_cached, calls _jdf.cache() on the JVM Dataset and returns self.

nodes.name: persist
nodes.summary: Converts the Python StorageLevel to a Java one via the SparkContext, calls _jdf.persist and returns self.

nodes.name: repartition
nodes.summary: Dispatches on numPartitions type (int or column) and calls _jdf.repartition with optional _jcols, wrapping the result in a new DataFrame; other types raise PySparkTypeError.

nodes.name: sample
nodes.summary: Implementation of the sample overloads: normalizes arguments with _preapare_args_for_sample and calls _jdf.sample(withReplacement, fraction, seed).

nodes.name: sampleBy
nodes.summary: Validates col and fractions, then calls _jdf.stat().sampleBy(col._jc, _jmap(fractions), seed) for stratified sampling, using a random seed when none is given.

nodes.name: randomSplit
nodes.summary: Checks weights are non-negative, converts them to a JVM list with _to_list and calls _jdf.randomSplit; wraps each resulting JVM Dataset in a DataFrame.

nodes.name: join
nodes.summary: Normalizes on (names become a JVM Seq via _jseq, Columns are AND-combined into one _jc), then calls _jdf.join(other._jdf, on, how) and wraps the result in a new DataFrame.

nodes.name: lateralJoin
nodes.summary: Calls the _jdf.lateralJoin overload matching which of on and how were given (passing on._jc) and wraps the result.

nodes.name: _joinAsOf
nodes.summary: Internal as-of join: resolves the as-of columns to JVM columns, normalizes on/how/tolerance and calls _jdf.joinAsOf(...), returning a new DataFrame.

nodes.name: sort
nodes.summary: Prepares the sort columns (names, Columns or ordinals plus ascending kwargs) and calls _jdf.sort(self._jseq(cols, _to_java_column)); orderBy is an alias assigned to this method.

nodes.name: _jseq
nodes.summary: Helper that converts a Python sequence (optionally through a converter) into a JVM Scala Seq using _to_seq on the session SparkContext; used by nearly every method that sends a list to the JVM.

nodes.name: _jmap
nodes.summary: Helper that turns a Python dict into a JVM Scala Map through to_scala_map on the SparkContext JVM view.

nodes.name: _jcols
nodes.summary: Helper that converts column names or Column objects (or a single list of them) into a JVM Seq of Columns via _jseq with _to_java_column.

nodes.name: _jcols_ordinal
nodes.summary: Like _jcols but also accepts 1-based integer ordinals, resolved with self[c - 1], raising PySparkIndexError for ordinals below 1; used by groupBy, rollup, cube and groupingSets.

nodes.name: head
nodes.summary: Implementation of head: with no n it takes head(1) and returns the first Row or None, otherwise delegates to take(n).

nodes.name: __getitem__
nodes.summary: Indexing: a string or int gives a Column wrapping _jdf.apply(name), a Column gives filter(item), and a list or tuple gives select(*item).

nodes.name: __getattr__
nodes.summary: Attribute access df.name: raises PySparkAttributeError if name is not a column, otherwise returns Column(self._jdf.apply(name)).

nodes.name: select
nodes.summary: Implementation of select: converts the columns with _jcols, calls _jdf.select and wraps the returned proxy in a new DataFrame.

nodes.name: filter
nodes.summary: Accepts a SQL string or Column and calls _jdf.filter(condition) or _jdf.filter(condition._jc) on the JVM Dataset, returning a new DataFrame; the predicate is evaluated by Spark, not Python. where is an alias.

nodes.name: groupBy
nodes.summary: Builds a JVM RelationalGroupedDataset with _jdf.groupBy(_jcols_ordinal(...)) and returns it wrapped in GroupedData together with this DataFrame.

nodes.name: agg
nodes.summary: Shortcut for df.groupBy().agg(*exprs).

nodes.name: observe
nodes.summary: Validates the metric expressions; for an Observation object delegates to observation._on, for a name string calls _jdf.observe(name, first._jc, seq of rest).

nodes.name: union
nodes.summary: Calls _jdf.union(other._jdf) and wraps the result; unionAll is an alias.

nodes.name: dropDuplicates
nodes.summary: Validates the optional subset of column names and calls _jdf.dropDuplicates() or _jdf.dropDuplicates(_jseq(subset)).

nodes.name: dropna
nodes.summary: Validates how/thresh/subset, computes the default thresh and calls _jdf.na().drop(thresh, _jseq(subset)).

nodes.name: fillna
nodes.summary: Validates value and subset (ints are converted to float) and calls _jdf.na().fill(...) with a dict, a value, or a value plus a JVM Seq of columns.

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Implementation of replace: validates to_replace/value/subset types, builds a dict mapping and calls _jdf.na().replace(...) either on all columns or on a JVM Seq subset with a JVM Map.

nodes.name: approxQuantile
nodes.summary: Validates col, probabilities and relativeError, converts them to JVM lists and calls _jdf.stat().approxQuantile, converting the Java arrays to Python lists.

nodes.name: withColumn
nodes.summary: Checks that col is a Column and calls _jdf.withColumn(colName, col._jc), returning a new DataFrame.

nodes.name: withColumns
nodes.summary: Takes a single dict of name to Column and calls _jdf.withColumns with a JVM Seq of names and a Seq of columns from _jcols.

nodes.name: drop
nodes.summary: Splits the arguments into names and Columns and calls _jdf.drop in one or two steps, returning a new DataFrame.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Property returning DataFrameWriter(self), the entry point for saving this DataFrame.

nodes.name: toPandas
nodes.summary: Converts the DataFrame to a pandas DataFrame by calling PandasConversionMixin._to_pandas(self).

nodes.name: mapInPandas
nodes.summary: Applies a pandas-iterator function per partition by delegating to PandasMapOpsMixin.mapInPandas.

nodes.name: na
nodes.summary: Property returning DataFrameNaFunctions(self).

nodes.name: stat
nodes.summary: Property returning DataFrameStatFunctions(self).

nodes.name: column.py
nodes.summary: Classic (py4j) PySpark Column. Column wraps a JVM Column proxy in _jc; operators and methods build a new Column by calling the proxy method of the same Spark name (for example plus, equalTo) through the _bin_op, _unary_op, _func_op and _bin_func_op helpers. Also holds the Python-to-JVM conversion helpers _to_java_column, _to_seq and _to_list used by the classic DataFrame.
nodes.languageNotes: Python operator overloading (__add__, __eq__, __and__ ...) mapped to JVM Column method names; the expression itself is only built in the JVM, never evaluated in Python.

nodes.name: _create_column_from_literal
nodes.summary: Creates a JVM Column for a Python literal by calling functions.lit(enum_to_value(literal)) on the active SparkContext JVM view.

nodes.name: _create_column_from_name
nodes.summary: Creates a JVM Column for a name by calling functions.col(name) on the active SparkContext JVM view.

nodes.name: _to_java_column
nodes.summary: Converts a Column (returns its _jc) or a string name (via _create_column_from_name) to a JVM Column, raising PySparkTypeError for other types; the main entry used when passing columns into _jdf calls.

nodes.name: _to_seq
nodes.summary: Converts an iterable of columns or names into a JVM Scala Seq with sc._jvm.PythonUtils.toSeq, optionally applying a converter to each item first.

nodes.name: _to_list
nodes.summary: Converts a list into a JVM Scala List with sc._jvm.PythonUtils.toList, optionally applying a converter to each item.

nodes.name: _unary_op
nodes.summary: Calls the zero-argument JVM Column method named name on self._jc and wraps the result in a new Column (used by asc, desc, isNull ...).

nodes.name: _func_op
nodes.summary: Calls the one-argument function from the JVM functions object (for example negate or not) on self._jc and wraps the result in a new Column.

nodes.name: _bin_func_op
nodes.summary: Calls a two-argument JVM functions method (for example pow) with self._jc and a literal or Column, optionally with swapped order, and wraps the result in a Column.

nodes.name: _bin_op
nodes.summary: Calls the JVM Column method named name on self._jc with the other operand (its _jc if a Column, else the plain value) and wraps the result in a new Column; the basis of +, -, ==, <, & and many string methods.

nodes.name: _reverse_op
nodes.summary: Builds a JVM literal Column from the left operand and calls the named method on it with self._jc, for reflected operators such as __rsub__ and __rtruediv__.

nodes.name: Column
nodes.summary: Classic Column (extends the abstract Column from pyspark/sql/column.py, decorated with with_origin_to_class). Holds the JVM Column proxy in _jc, and every operator or method returns a new Column wrapping the proxy of the resulting JVM expression.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Stores the JVM Column proxy in self._jc.

nodes.name: __add__
nodes.summary: Addition operator: _bin_op('plus', self, other); the sibling operators __sub__, __mul__, __truediv__ and __mod__ use minus, multiply, divide and mod the same way.

nodes.name: __eq__
nodes.summary: Equality operator: _bin_op('equalTo', self, other) returning a boolean Column; __ne__, __lt__, __le__, __gt__ and __ge__ map to notEqual, lt, leq, gt and geq.

nodes.name: __and__
nodes.summary: Logical AND (the & operator): _bin_op('and', self, lit(other)); __or__ does the same with 'or'.

nodes.name: getItem
nodes.summary: Returns self[key] (array index or map key), warning if a Column is used as the key.

nodes.name: withField
nodes.summary: Validates arguments and calls self._jc.withField(fieldName, col._jc) to add or replace a struct field.

nodes.name: dropFields
nodes.summary: Calls self._jc.dropFields on a JVM Seq of field names built with _to_seq.

nodes.name: __getattr__
nodes.summary: col.name field access: raises for dunder names, otherwise returns self[item].

nodes.name: __getitem__
nodes.summary: Indexing: a slice becomes substr(start, stop) (step not allowed), anything else becomes _bin_op('apply', self, k).

nodes.name: substr
nodes.summary: Checks that startPos and length have the same type and calls self._jc.substr with ints or with the JVM columns of Column arguments.

nodes.name: isin
nodes.summary: Builds a JVM Seq of literals or columns and calls self._jc.isin; with a single classic DataFrame it passes df._jdf (subquery form).

nodes.name: alias
nodes.summary: Calls the JVM 'as' method with one name (optionally with Metadata parsed from JSON by sc._jvm) or a Seq of names, returning a new Column.

nodes.name: cast
nodes.summary: Casts to a type given as a DDL string or a DataType (parsed on the JVM with spark._jsparkSession.parseDataType) via self._jc.cast.

nodes.name: when
nodes.summary: Chains a CASE WHEN branch by calling self._jc.when(condition._jc, value).

nodes.name: over
nodes.summary: Applies a window by calling self._jc.over(window._jspec); requires a classic WindowSpec.

nodes.name: __repr__
nodes.summary: Returns Column<'...'> using self._jc.toString().

nodes.name: window.py
nodes.summary: Classic (py4j) implementation of Window and WindowSpec. Window static methods call org.apache.spark.sql.expressions.Window on the JVM through sc._jvm and wrap the returned proxy in WindowSpec, which holds it in _jspec and returns new WindowSpec objects for each chained call.

nodes.name: _to_java_cols
nodes.summary: Converts window column arguments (names, Columns or a single list) into a JVM Seq using _to_seq with _to_java_column from classic/column.py.

nodes.name: Window
nodes.summary: Classic Window: static partitionBy, orderBy, rowsBetween and rangeBetween call the JVM expressions.Window object by its full class name through sc._jvm and return a WindowSpec.

nodes.name: WindowSpec
nodes.summary: Classic WindowSpec: wraps a JVM WindowSpec proxy (_jspec); partitionBy, orderBy, rowsBetween and rangeBetween call the same-named JVM method and return a new WindowSpec.

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Static method that calls org.apache.spark.sql.expressions.Window.partitionBy on the JVM via sc._jvm and returns the result wrapped in WindowSpec.

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Calls self._jspec.partitionBy on the JVM WindowSpec proxy and returns a new WindowSpec.

nodes.name: orderBy
nodes.summary: Static method that calls org.apache.spark.sql.expressions.Window.orderBy on the JVM via sc._jvm and returns the result wrapped in WindowSpec.

nodes.name: orderBy
nodes.summary: Calls self._jspec.orderBy on the JVM WindowSpec proxy and returns a new WindowSpec.

nodes.name: rowsBetween
nodes.summary: Static method that calls org.apache.spark.sql.expressions.Window.rowsBetween on the JVM via sc._jvm and returns the result wrapped in WindowSpec. Frame bounds at or beyond the JVM Long limits are normalised to unboundedPreceding/unboundedFollowing.

nodes.name: rowsBetween
nodes.summary: Calls self._jspec.rowsBetween on the JVM WindowSpec proxy and returns a new WindowSpec. Bounds are normalised first.

nodes.name: rangeBetween
nodes.summary: Static method that calls org.apache.spark.sql.expressions.Window.rangeBetween on the JVM via sc._jvm and returns the result wrapped in WindowSpec. Frame bounds at or beyond the JVM Long limits are normalised to unboundedPreceding/unboundedFollowing.

nodes.name: rangeBetween
nodes.summary: Calls self._jspec.rangeBetween on the JVM WindowSpec proxy and returns a new WindowSpec. Bounds are normalised first.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Stores the JVM WindowSpec proxy in self._jspec.

nodes.name: window.py
nodes.summary: Public PySpark SQL Window and WindowSpec API definitions (docstrings and signatures). Window static methods are stubs decorated with dispatch_window_method, which forwards to the classic Window (py4j) or the Connect Window at call time; WindowSpec.__new__ returns a classic WindowSpec. Also defines the unbounded/current-row constants and the Long thresholds.
nodes.languageNotes: Method bodies are `...`; the real behavior is supplied by the decorator dispatching to the classic or Connect implementation.

nodes.name: Window
nodes.summary: Abstract public Window utility: constants unboundedPreceding, unboundedFollowing and currentRow, and static partitionBy, orderBy, rowsBetween and rangeBetween that dispatch via dispatch_window_method to the classic or Connect Window.

nodes.name: WindowSpec
nodes.summary: Abstract public WindowSpec (partitioning, ordering, frame definition); its __new__ builds the classic WindowSpec, and the classic subclass supplies the method behavior.

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Documented stub of Window.partitionBy; the dispatch_window_method decorator forwards the call to the classic Window (or the Connect Window when running remotely).

nodes.name: orderBy
nodes.summary: Documented stub of Window.orderBy; the dispatch_window_method decorator forwards the call to the classic Window (or the Connect Window when running remotely).

nodes.name: rowsBetween
nodes.summary: Documented stub of Window.rowsBetween; the dispatch_window_method decorator forwards the call to the classic Window (or the Connect Window when running remotely).

nodes.name: rangeBetween
nodes.summary: Documented stub of Window.rangeBetween; the dispatch_window_method decorator forwards the call to the classic Window (or the Connect Window when running remotely).

nodes.name: __new__
nodes.summary: Imports the classic WindowSpec and returns WindowSpec.__new__(WindowSpec, jspec), so constructing the public class yields a classic instance.

nodes.name: dataframe.py
nodes.summary: Defines the public, abstract PySpark DataFrame API (DataFrame, DataFrameNaFunctions, DataFrameStatFunctions). Almost every method body is `...`, decorated with dispatch_df_method so a call is routed to the Classic or Spark Connect implementation; the real docstrings and doctests live here.
nodes.languageNotes: Docstring-heavy (over 7000 lines, mostly examples). `@overload` stubs give typed signatures; `@dispatch_df_method` replaces the Python body with a wrapper that picks classic.dataframe.DataFrame or connect.dataframe.DataFrame based on the type of `self`.

nodes.name: DataFrame
nodes.summary: Abstract public DataFrame API: a distributed collection of rows grouped into named columns. DataFrame.__new__ returns a classic DataFrame for backward compatibility; most methods are empty stubs decorated with dispatch_df_method, implemented by classic/dataframe.py (JVM-backed) and connect/dataframe.py (Spark Connect). Transformations (select, filter, join, groupBy, withColumn, ...) are lazy and return new DataFrames; actions (collect, count, show, toPandas, take, ...) trigger execution.

nodes.name: DataFrameNaFunctions
nodes.summary: Handler for missing-data operations reached via DataFrame.na. Holds the parent DataFrame in `self.df` and exposes drop, fill and replace (typed with @overload), all dispatched to the Classic or Connect implementation.

nodes.name: DataFrameStatFunctions
nodes.summary: Handler for statistics reached via DataFrame.stat. Holds the parent DataFrame in `self.df` and exposes approxQuantile, corr, cov, crosstab, freqItems and sampleBy, all dispatched to the Classic or Connect implementation.

nodes.name: DataFrame.sparkSession
nodes.summary: Property returning the SparkSession that created this DataFrame (stub, implemented by Classic/Connect).

nodes.name: DataFrame.na
nodes.summary: Property returning a DataFrameNaFunctions for handling missing values (df.na.drop/fill/replace).

nodes.name: DataFrame.stat
nodes.summary: Property returning a DataFrameStatFunctions for statistics (df.stat.corr/cov/crosstab/...).

nodes.name: DataFrame.createTempView
nodes.summary: Registers this DataFrame as a local temporary view tied to the SparkSession; fails if the view name already exists. Siblings in the same file: createOrReplaceTempView, createGlobalTempView, createOrReplaceGlobalTempView (global views live in the global_temp database) and the deprecated registerTempTable.

nodes.name: DataFrame.createOrReplaceTempView
nodes.summary: Creates or replaces a local temporary view backed by this DataFrame so it can be queried with spark.sql.

nodes.name: DataFrame.createGlobalTempView
nodes.summary: Creates a global temporary view (shared across sessions, lifetime tied to the Spark application) from this DataFrame; fails if it exists.

nodes.name: DataFrame.createOrReplaceGlobalTempView
nodes.summary: Creates or replaces a global temporary view backed by this DataFrame.

nodes.name: DataFrame.write
nodes.summary: Property returning a DataFrameWriter, the entry point for saving a non-streaming DataFrame to external storage.

nodes.name: DataFrame.writeStream
nodes.summary: Property returning a DataStreamWriter for writing a streaming DataFrame to external storage.

nodes.name: DataFrame.schema
nodes.summary: Property returning the schema of this DataFrame as a StructType.

nodes.name: DataFrame.printSchema
nodes.summary: Prints the schema in tree format (optionally with a level limit).

nodes.name: DataFrame.explain
nodes.summary: Prints the logical and physical plans to the console for debugging; accepts a mode or extended flag.

nodes.name: DataFrame.show
nodes.summary: Action that prints the first n rows to the console (truncate and vertical options). Triggers execution of the query.

nodes.name: DataFrame.checkpoint
nodes.summary: Returns a checkpointed DataFrame that truncates the logical plan; saved under the checkpoint directory (eager by default). Declared without dispatch_df_method, body is `...`.

nodes.name: DataFrame.withWatermark
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation defining an event-time watermark for a streaming DataFrame (column and delay threshold) used to bound state and late data.

nodes.name: DataFrame.hint
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation attaching a hint (for example broadcast) to the current DataFrame.

nodes.name: DataFrame.count
nodes.summary: Action returning the number of rows in the DataFrame.

nodes.name: DataFrame.collect
nodes.summary: Action returning all records to the driver as a list of Row. Can exhaust driver memory on large data.

nodes.name: DataFrame.toLocalIterator
nodes.summary: Action returning an iterator over all rows (optionally prefetching partitions); needs memory for only the largest partition at a time.

nodes.name: DataFrame.limit
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation limiting the result to the given number of rows.

nodes.name: DataFrame.take
nodes.summary: Action returning the first num rows as a list of Row.

nodes.name: DataFrame.cache
nodes.summary: Persists the DataFrame with the default storage level (MEMORY_AND_DISK_DESER); lazy until the first action.

nodes.name: DataFrame.persist
nodes.summary: Sets the storage level used to persist the DataFrame across operations after the first computation.

nodes.name: DataFrame.unpersist
nodes.summary: Marks the DataFrame as non-persistent and removes its blocks from memory and disk. Note: the Python body in this file is shadowed by the dispatch decorator.

nodes.name: DataFrame.coalesce
nodes.summary: Returns a DataFrame with exactly numPartitions partitions via a narrow dependency (no shuffle). Note: the Python body in this file is shadowed by the dispatch decorator.

nodes.name: DataFrame.repartition
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning a DataFrame with the requested number of partitions and/or hash-partitioned by given columns (full shuffle).

nodes.name: DataFrame.distinct
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning a DataFrame with distinct rows.

nodes.name: DataFrame.sample
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning a random sampled subset (withReplacement, fraction, seed). Overloaded; the argument normalization helper _preapare_args_for_sample is used by the Classic and Connect implementations.

nodes.name: DataFrame.randomSplit
nodes.summary: Randomly splits the DataFrame by weights into a list of DataFrames, optionally seeded.

nodes.name: DataFrame.dtypes
nodes.summary: Property returning column names with their data type strings as a list of tuples.

nodes.name: DataFrame.columns
nodes.summary: Property returning the column names as a list of strings.

nodes.name: DataFrame.alias
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning a DataFrame with an alias set, used for self-joins and qualified column references.

nodes.name: DataFrame.crossJoin
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning the cartesian product with another DataFrame.

nodes.name: DataFrame.join
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation joining with another DataFrame on a column name, list of names or Column expression, with a join type (inner, outer, left, right, semi, anti, cross).

nodes.name: DataFrame.lateralJoin
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation performing a lateral (correlated) join where the right side can reference columns of each left row. New in 4.0.0; no dispatch decorator, body is `...`.

nodes.name: DataFrame.nearestByJoin
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation doing a nearest-by top-K ranking join: for each left row, up to numResults rows of the other DataFrame ranked by a ranking expression. New in 4.2.0; no dispatch decorator, body is `...`.

nodes.name: DataFrame.sortWithinPartitions
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation sorting each partition by the given columns without a global ordering.

nodes.name: DataFrame.sort
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation sorting by the given columns (ascending flags supported); orderBy is an alias. The helper _preapare_cols_for_sort in this class is called by the Classic and Connect implementations.

nodes.name: DataFrame.describe
nodes.summary: Computes basic statistics for numeric and string columns and returns them as a DataFrame.

nodes.name: DataFrame.summary
nodes.summary: Computes selected statistics (count, mean, stddev, min, max, percentiles); defaults to count, mean, stddev, min, quartiles and max when none are given.

nodes.name: DataFrame.head
nodes.summary: Action returning the first row, or the first n rows as a list. Overloaded; use for small results only.

nodes.name: DataFrame.first
nodes.summary: Action returning the first row as a Row.

nodes.name: DataFrame.select
nodes.summary: Lazy projection of columns or expressions returning a new DataFrame; accepts names, Column objects or a list.

nodes.name: DataFrame.selectExpr
nodes.summary: Lazy projection of SQL expression strings returning a new DataFrame.

nodes.name: DataFrame.filter
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation filtering rows by a Column condition or SQL string; where is an alias.

nodes.name: DataFrame.where
nodes.summary: Alias for filter.

nodes.name: DataFrame.groupBy
nodes.summary: Groups by the given columns (names, Columns or ordinals) and returns a GroupedData on which aggregate functions are applied; groupby is an alias.

nodes.name: DataFrame.rollup
nodes.summary: Creates a multi-dimensional rollup over the given columns and returns a GroupedData for subtotal-style aggregations.

nodes.name: DataFrame.cube
nodes.summary: Creates a multi-dimensional cube over the given columns and returns a GroupedData covering all grouping combinations.

nodes.name: DataFrame.unpivot
nodes.summary: Lazy wide-to-long reshaping of id and value columns into variable/value columns; melt is an alias.

nodes.name: DataFrame.agg
nodes.summary: Aggregates over the entire DataFrame without groups (shorthand for df.groupBy().agg()).

nodes.name: DataFrame.observe
nodes.summary: Defines named metrics to observe (an Observation or a name plus aggregate expressions); returns an observed DataFrame whose metrics are reported at a completion point, for batch and streaming.

nodes.name: DataFrame.union
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning the union of rows of two DataFrames by column position (UNION ALL semantics, no dedup); unionAll is an alias.

nodes.name: DataFrame.unionByName
nodes.summary: Lazy union resolving columns by name, with optional allowMissingColumns.

nodes.name: DataFrame.intersect
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning rows present in both DataFrames, with duplicates removed.

nodes.name: DataFrame.exceptAll
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning rows in this DataFrame but not in another, preserving duplicates (EXCEPT ALL).

nodes.name: DataFrame.subtract
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning rows in this DataFrame but not in another (EXCEPT DISTINCT).

nodes.name: DataFrame.dropDuplicates
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation removing duplicate rows, optionally considering only a subset of columns; drop_duplicates is an alias.

nodes.name: DataFrame.dropna
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation omitting rows with null or NaN values (how, thresh, subset); counterpart of DataFrameNaFunctions.drop.

nodes.name: DataFrame.fillna
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation replacing null values with a given value, optionally per column subset; counterpart of DataFrameNaFunctions.fill.

nodes.name: DataFrame.replace
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation replacing values with other values, optionally within a column subset (overloaded); counterpart of DataFrameNaFunctions.replace.

nodes.name: DataFrame.withColumns
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation adding or replacing several columns from a dict of name to Column.

nodes.name: DataFrame.withColumn
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation adding a column or replacing an existing one with the same name.

nodes.name: DataFrame.withColumnRenamed
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation renaming one existing column.

nodes.name: DataFrame.drop
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation dropping the given columns (names or Column objects).

nodes.name: DataFrame.toDF
nodes.summary: Lazy transformation returning a DataFrame with new column names.

nodes.name: DataFrame.transform
nodes.summary: Concise syntax for chaining custom transformations: calls a function that takes and returns a DataFrame, with extra args.

nodes.name: DataFrame.writeTo
nodes.summary: Creates a DataFrameWriterV2 configuration builder for v2 sources (append, create, createOrReplace tables).

nodes.name: DataFrame.mergeInto
nodes.summary: Starts a MERGE INTO operation by returning a MergeIntoWriter configured with target table and merge condition.

nodes.name: DataFrame.mapInPandas
nodes.summary: Maps an iterator of pandas DataFrame batches through a function producing pandas batches with a given output schema.

nodes.name: DataFrame.mapInArrow
nodes.summary: Maps an iterator of pyarrow RecordBatches through a function producing RecordBatches with a given output schema.

nodes.name: DataFrame.toPandas
nodes.summary: Action returning the DataFrame contents as a pandas DataFrame on the driver (requires pandas). Declared without dispatch_df_method, body is `...`.

nodes.name: DataFrame.asTable
nodes.summary: Converts the DataFrame into a TableArg so it can be passed as a table argument to a table-valued function or UDTF; TableArg supports partitionBy, orderBy and withSinglePartition. New in 4.0.0.

nodes.name: DataFrame.scalar
nodes.summary: Returns a Column representing a SCALAR subquery (exactly one row and one column) usable in select or filter of an outer DataFrame. New in 4.0.0.

nodes.name: DataFrame.exists
nodes.summary: Returns a Column representing an EXISTS subquery usable as a predicate in filter of an outer DataFrame. New in 4.0.0.

nodes.name: DataFrame.__new__
nodes.summary: Constructor hook: imports and returns the classic DataFrame(jdf, sql_ctx), so direct instantiation of the abstract DataFrame yields a Classic one for backward compatibility.

nodes.name: session.py
nodes.summary: Defines the classic (py4j) PySpark SparkSession and its Builder. Builder.getOrCreate either hands off to the Spark Connect SparkSession (when a remote URL, SPARK_REMOTE or connect api mode is set) or builds a SparkConf, gets or creates the SparkContext and wraps the JVM org.apache.spark.sql.classic.SparkSession; the session then offers createDataFrame, sql, table, range, read, readStream, catalog, conf and udf.
nodes.languageNotes: One file serves both modes: the Builder dispatches to pyspark.sql.connect.session when Connect is requested. Module-level _monkey_patch_RDD adds RDD.toDF when the install is not remote-only.

nodes.name: _monkey_patch_RDD
nodes.summary: Called from SparkSession.__init__; defines a toDF(schema, sampleRatio) shorthand that calls sparkSession.createDataFrame(rdd, ...) and assigns it to RDD.toDF unless running in a remote-only install.

nodes.name: classproperty
nodes.summary: Generic descriptor like property but for class attributes: __get__ calls the wrapped function with the owner class, so a new value is computed on every access. Used to expose SparkSession.builder.

nodes.name: SparkSession
nodes.summary: Entry point of classic PySpark for the Dataset/DataFrame API. Wraps a SparkContext (_sc, _jvm) and the JVM org.apache.spark.sql.classic.SparkSession (_jsparkSession), and keeps class-level _instantiatedSession and _activeSession. Inherits SparkConversionMixin, which supplies the pandas and Arrow paths of createDataFrame.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Nested builder behind SparkSession.builder. Accumulates string options in _options under an RLock via config, master, remote, appName and enableHiveSupport, then getOrCreate or create produces a classic or Spark Connect session.

nodes.name: config
nodes.summary: Sets options from a key/value pair, a SparkConf (conf.getAll()) or a map; values go through to_str and are stored in _options, calling _validate_startup_urls after each insertion. Returns the builder for chaining. Lines cover the implementation after the overloads.

nodes.name: _validate_startup_urls
nodes.summary: Raises PySparkRuntimeError CANNOT_CONFIGURE_SPARK_CONNECT_MASTER if a master (spark.master or MASTER) is combined with a remote (spark.remote or SPARK_REMOTE), and CANNOT_CONFIGURE_SPARK_CONNECT when SPARK_REMOTE conflicts with a new non-local remote while SPARK_LOCAL_REMOTE is set.

nodes.name: master
nodes.summary: Sets spark.master via config, for example a local[N] or cluster URL.

nodes.name: remote
nodes.summary: Sets spark.remote via config; a remote URL makes getOrCreate and create use the Spark Connect session.

nodes.name: appName
nodes.summary: Sets spark.app.name via config.

nodes.name: enableHiveSupport
nodes.summary: Sets spark.sql.catalogImplementation to hive via config.

nodes.name: getOrCreate
nodes.summary: What happens at SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate(): in a remote-only install it needs a URL (spark.remote or SPARK_REMOTE), sets SPARK_CONNECT_MODE_ENABLED and delegates to the Connect session builder. Otherwise, under the builder lock, it resolves the api mode (spark.api.mode or SPARK_API_MODE, else default_api_mode()); if Connect is indicated by environment, spark.remote or connect api mode it may start a local Connect server (_start_connect_server for local URLs) and delegates to the Connect builder. In classic mode it reuses SparkSession._instantiatedSession when its _jsc is alive and applies modifiable settings in the JVM; otherwise it fills a SparkConf from the options, calls SparkContext.getOrCreate(sparkConf) and constructs SparkSession(sc, options=...).

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Always creates a new session. With SPARK_REMOTE or spark.remote it validates startup URLs, rejects local connection strings and delegates to the Connect builder's create. In classic mode it reuses or creates the SparkContext, builds a fresh JVM session with jSparkSessionClass.builder().config(options).create() and wraps it in a Python SparkSession.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: classproperty that returns a new cls.Builder() on each access (a SPARK-47544 comment says it must stay an identifier-style property, not a method).

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Takes _jsc and _jvm from the SparkContext, then obtains the JVM session: the given jsparkSession, else the JVM default session when its context is not stopped, else a new JVM classic SparkSession built from self._jsc.sc() and options. Applies modifiable settings, monkey-patches RDD.toDF, calls install_exception_handler() (from pyspark.errors.exceptions.captured) and registers itself as default and active session on the JVM when no live session exists.

nodes.name: _should_update_active_session
nodes.summary: True when no session has been instantiated or the instantiated session's SparkContext _jsc is None (stopped).

nodes.name: _get_j_spark_session_class
nodes.summary: Returns the py4j JavaClass for org.apache.spark.sql.classic.SparkSession from the JVMView.

nodes.name: _get_j_spark_session_module
nodes.summary: Returns the Scala companion object (org.apache.spark.sql.classic.SparkSession$, field MODULE$) through py4j.

nodes.name: _jconf
nodes.summary: Property returning the JVM session state's SQLConf (self._jsparkSession.sessionState().conf()), used to read configs during schema inference.

nodes.name: newSession
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkSession sharing the SparkContext but with its own SQL configuration, temporary views and UDFs, by wrapping self._jsparkSession.newSession(); defined only when not remote-only.

nodes.name: getActiveSession
nodes.summary: Classmethod wrapped by try_remote_session_classmethod so remote mode redirects to the Connect session. Returns None if there is no active SparkContext or no JVM active session; otherwise syncs the Python-side session if needed and returns _activeSession.

nodes.name: active
nodes.summary: Returns getActiveSession(), falling back to the instantiated default session; raises NO_ACTIVE_OR_DEFAULT_SESSION if neither exists.

nodes.name: sparkContext
nodes.summary: Property exposing the underlying SparkContext (self._sc); defined only when not remote-only.

nodes.name: version
nodes.summary: cached_property returning the Spark version from the JVM session (self._jsparkSession.version()).

nodes.name: conf
nodes.summary: cached_property returning RuntimeConfig wrapping the JVM session conf (self._jsparkSession.conf()) for get and set of runtime SQL configs.

nodes.name: catalog
nodes.summary: cached_property that lazily imports and returns pyspark.sql.catalog.Catalog(self).

nodes.name: udf
nodes.summary: Property returning UDFRegistration(self), used to register Python UDFs for SQL.

nodes.name: range
nodes.summary: Creates a DataFrame with a single id column of LongType; defaults numPartitions to sc.defaultParallelism and calls the JVM session's range with (start, end, step, numPartitions); with a single argument it counts from 0.

nodes.name: _inferSchemaFromList
nodes.summary: Infers a StructType from local rows: raises CANNOT_INFER_EMPTY_SCHEMA on empty data, reads four SQL configs (timestampType, inferNestedDictAsStruct, legacy array and map inference flags) from _jconf, applies types._infer_schema per row and reduces with _merge_type; raises CANNOT_DETERMINE_TYPE if a NullType remains.

nodes.name: _inferSchema
nodes.summary: Infers a StructType from an RDD: inspects rdd.first() (empty rows rejected), reads the same configs; without samplingRatio it infers from the first row and merges up to 100 more rows until no NullType remains, with samplingRatio it samples the RDD and reduces per-row schemas with _merge_type.

nodes.name: _createFromRDD
nodes.summary: Converts an RDD to an internal-representation RDD: with schema None or a list of names it infers the schema (_inferSchema), converts rows to tuples with _create_converter and renames fields; with a StructType it uses it as is; otherwise raises NOT_EXPECTED_TYPE. Finally maps struct.toInternal.

nodes.name: _createFromLocal
nodes.summary: Local-data path: materialises data as a list, rejects VariantVal rows, infers (via _inferSchemaFromList) or reuses the schema, converts rows with _create_converter and struct.toInternal, and returns self._sc.parallelize(internal_data) together with the StructType.

nodes.name: _create_shell_session
nodes.summary: Used by the PySpark shell: if spark.sql.catalogImplementation is hive (the default) it probes HiveConf through py4j and builds the session with enableHiveSupport().getOrCreate(); on Py4JError or TypeError it warns about missing Hive support and falls back to _getActiveSessionOrCreate().

nodes.name: _getActiveSessionOrCreate
