nodes.summary: Returns getActiveSession() or, if None, builds one through SparkSession.builder with the given static_conf and getOrCreate().

nodes.name: createDataFrame
nodes.summary: Public API (many @overloads; the line range is the implementation). Sets this as the active session in Python and the JVM, rejects DataFrame input, parses a string schema with _parse_ddl, and detects pandas, numpy and pyarrow. A numpy ndarray (1-D or 2-D) is converted to a pyarrow Table with generated column names; pandas.DataFrame and pyarrow.Table are delegated to SparkConversionMixin.createDataFrame via super(); everything else (list, RDD, iterable) goes to _create_dataframe.

nodes.name: _create_dataframe
nodes.summary: Builds a prepare/verify function (_make_type_verifier when verifySchema is true; a bare DataType is wrapped into a struct with a single value column), maps data via _createFromRDD for RDDs or _createFromLocal otherwise, converts the result with SerDeUtil.toJavaArray(rdd._to_java_object_rdd()), calls the JVM applySchemaToPythonRDD(jrdd.rdd(), struct.json()) and wraps the result in DataFrame(jdf, self), caching df._schema.

nodes.name: emptyDataFrame
nodes.summary: Returns an empty DataFrame with the given StructType or DDL string by calling createDataFrame([], schema).

nodes.name: sql
nodes.summary: Runs a SQL query. Keyword arguments are substituted by SQLStringFormatter; args as a dict (named parameters) or list/None (positional) become Java columns via lit and _to_java_column, are passed to self._jsparkSession.sql, and the result is wrapped in DataFrame; the formatter is cleared in a finally block.

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Returns the named table or view as a DataFrame via self._jsparkSession.table; raises NOT_EXPECTED_TYPE for non-string names.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Property returning DataFrameReader(self) for loading external data as DataFrames.

nodes.name: readStream
nodes.summary: Property returning DataStreamReader(self) for streaming DataFrames.

nodes.name: streams
nodes.summary: cached_property returning StreamingQueryManager(self._jsparkSession.streams()) to manage active streaming queries.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the SparkContext, clears default and active sessions on the JVM class, and resets Python-level _instantiatedSession, _activeSession and SQLContext._instantiatedContext.

nodes.name: __enter__
nodes.summary: Context manager entry; returns the session so it can be used in a with statement.

nodes.name: __exit__
nodes.summary: Context manager exit; calls self.stop().

nodes.name: addArtifacts
nodes.summary: Adds files, py files or archives to the session (flags are mutually exclusive). Checks each path against the SparkFiles root directory for duplicates (DUPLICATED_ARTIFACT) and then calls sc.addArchive, sc.addPyFile or sc.addFile.

nodes.name: interruptAll
nodes.summary: Interrupts all running operations of this session via the JVM and returns the interrupted operation ids as a Python list built by iterating the Java list.

nodes.name: group.py
nodes.summary: Defines GroupedData, the object returned by DataFrame.groupBy. It wraps a JVM RelationalGroupedDataset (_jgd) and exposes agg (Column expressions or a dict of column to function name), count, mean, avg, max, min, sum and pivot; applyInPandas, cogroup and applyInArrow come from the inherited PandasGroupedOpsMixin, not defined here.
nodes.languageNotes: The shortcut aggregations are empty-bodied stubs wrapped by dfapi/df_varargs_api, which replace the body with a call to the same-named JVM method.

nodes.name: dfapi
nodes.summary: Decorator for no-argument aggregations: the replacement _api calls getattr(self._jgd, f.__name__)() and wraps the JVM result in DataFrame(jdf, self.session), copying name and docstring. Used by GroupedData.count.

nodes.name: df_varargs_api
nodes.summary: Decorator for column-varargs aggregations: converts cols with _to_seq(self.session._sc, cols), calls the same-named JVM method on _jgd and returns DataFrame(jdf, self.session). Used by mean, avg, max, min and sum.

nodes.name: GroupedData
nodes.summary: Result of DataFrame.groupBy, rollup and cube: holds the JVM grouped dataset (_jgd), the parent DataFrame (_df) and the session. Provides agg, count, mean, avg, max, min, sum and pivot, and inherits PandasGroupedOpsMixin (applyInPandas, cogroup and related group operations, imported from pyspark.sql.pandas.group_ops).

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Stores jgd, df and the session taken from df.sparkSession.

nodes.name: __repr__
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the repr from the JVM toString when it has '[' at position 26, otherwise falls back to the default repr.

nodes.name: agg
nodes.summary: Computes aggregates and returns a DataFrame. A single dict argument (column to function name) is passed straight to the JVM agg; otherwise all arguments must be Column, the first is passed as _jc and the rest as a Scala seq via _to_seq. Lines cover the implementation after the overloads.

nodes.name: count
nodes.summary: Counts the rows per group via the JVM count through @dfapi.

nodes.name: mean
nodes.summary: Mean of the given numeric columns per group via @df_varargs_api.

nodes.name: avg
nodes.summary: Average of the given numeric columns per group (same as mean) via @df_varargs_api.

nodes.name: max
nodes.summary: Maximum of the given columns per group via @df_varargs_api.

nodes.name: min
nodes.summary: Minimum of the given columns per group via @df_varargs_api.

nodes.name: sum
nodes.summary: Sum of the given numeric columns per group via @df_varargs_api.

nodes.name: pivot
nodes.summary: Pivots on a column, optionally with explicit values; calls self._jgd.pivot(pivot_col[, values]) and returns a new GroupedData over the same DataFrame.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Shared helpers for pyspark.sql: py4j conversions (to_java_array, to_scala_map), optional-dependency checks, ForeachBatchFunction for streaming foreachBatch callbacks, string helpers (to_str, StringConcat), remote-mode detection (is_remote) with decorators that redirect API calls to Spark Connect or classic implementations, and remote_only markers. It re-exports the captured exception classes (AnalysisException, ParseException, ...) from pyspark.errors, but the JVM-to-Python exception conversion itself (capture_sql_exception, convert_exception, install_exception_handler) lives in pyspark/errors/exceptions/captured.py, not here.
nodes.languageNotes: Many decorators share one pattern: if is_remote() and PYSPARK_NO_NAMESPACE_SHARE is unset, import from pyspark.sql.connect lazily, else call the original or classic implementation.

nodes.name: to_java_array
nodes.summary: Builds a py4j Java array of the given Java type from a Python sequence using gateway.new_array.

nodes.name: to_scala_map
nodes.summary: Converts a Python dict to a Scala map with jvm.PythonUtils.toScalaMap.

nodes.name: require_test_compiled
nodes.summary: Raises TEST_CLASS_NOT_COMPILED unless sql/core/target/*/test-classes exists under the Spark home; used by tests that need compiled JVM test classes.

nodes.name: require_minimum_plotly_version
nodes.summary: Imports plotly and raises PACKAGE_NOT_INSTALLED or UNSUPPORTED_PACKAGE_VERSION when plotly is missing or older than 4.8.

nodes.name: ForeachBatchFunction
nodes.summary: Python callback object passed to the JVM for DataStreamWriter.foreachBatch; its nested Java class declares that it implements org.apache.spark.sql.execution.streaming.sources.PythonForeachBatchFunction so py4j can call back into call().

nodes.name: call
nodes.summary: Invoked from the JVM per micro-batch: wraps the batch's JVM session in a Python SparkSession, wraps the JVM dataset in a DataFrame and calls the user function with (DataFrame, batch_id); on error it stores self.error and re-raises.

nodes.name: StringConcat
nodes.summary: Python port of a bounded string builder: append truncates once maxLength (JVM_INT_MAX - 15 by default) is reached, atLimit reports it and toString joins the collected pieces.

nodes.name: escape_meta_characters
nodes.summary: Replaces newline, carriage return, tab, form feed, backspace, vertical tab and bell characters with their backslash escape sequences.

nodes.name: to_str
nodes.summary: Converts option values to strings for the JVM: booleans become 'true' or 'false', None stays None, anything else str(value). Used by SparkSession.Builder.config.

nodes.name: enum_to_value
nodes.summary: Recursively unwraps Enum members to their .value; other values pass through.

nodes.name: is_timestamp_ntz_preferred
nodes.summary: Checks whether spark.sql.timestampType is TIMESTAMP_NTZ: in remote mode through the Connect session conf, otherwise through the JVM PythonSQLUtils.isTimestampNTZPreferred.

nodes.name: is_remote
nodes.summary: True when the SPARK_CONNECT_MODE_ENABLED environment variable is set or the install is remote-only; the switch behind all connect-dispatch decorators in this file.

nodes.name: try_remote_functions
nodes.summary: Decorator: in remote mode (unless PYSPARK_NO_NAMESPACE_SHARE is set) forwards the call to the same-named function in pyspark.sql.connect.functions, else runs the classic function.

nodes.name: try_partitioning_remote_functions
nodes.summary: Same dispatch as try_remote_functions but targets pyspark.sql.connect.functions.partitioning.

nodes.name: try_remote_avro_functions
nodes.summary: Dispatch decorator targeting pyspark.sql.connect.avro.functions in remote mode.

nodes.name: try_remote_protobuf_functions
nodes.summary: Dispatch decorator targeting pyspark.sql.connect.protobuf.functions in remote mode.

nodes.name: get_active_spark_context
nodes.summary: Returns SparkContext._active_spark_context or raises SESSION_OR_CONTEXT_NOT_EXISTS when there is no active context or JVM.

nodes.name: try_remote_session_classmethod
nodes.summary: Decorator for SparkSession classmethods (getActiveSession, active): in remote mode calls the same-named classmethod on the Connect SparkSession, otherwise the classic one.

nodes.name: dispatch_df_method
nodes.summary: Decorator routing a DataFrame method to the Connect DataFrame in remote mode or the classic DataFrame otherwise, depending on the instance type; raises NOT_IMPLEMENTED if the instance is neither.

nodes.name: dispatch_col_method
nodes.summary: Decorator routing a Column method to the Connect Column or the classic Column based on is_remote and the instance type, raising NOT_IMPLEMENTED otherwise.

nodes.name: dispatch_window_method
nodes.summary: Decorator routing Window static methods to the Connect Window in remote mode or the classic Window otherwise.

nodes.name: dispatch_table_arg_method
nodes.summary: Decorator routing TableArg methods to the Connect TableArg or the classic TableArg.

nodes.name: pyspark_column_op
nodes.summary: Applies a Column operator by name to pandas-on-Spark operands via column_op, and applies fillna when extension dtypes are involved.

nodes.name: get_lit_sql_str
nodes.summary: Escapes backslashes and single quotes and wraps a string as a SQL string literal.

nodes.name: NumpyHelper
nodes.summary: Small helper class whose static linspace returns evenly spaced floats without needing numpy.

nodes.name: remote_only
nodes.summary: Marks a function or property getter as remote-only by setting _remote_only = True (overloaded for property and callable). Applied to SparkSession.client and the progress-handler methods.

nodes.name: readwriter.py
nodes.summary: Classic (py4j) implementation of the public read/write entry points: DataFrameReader (spark.read), DataFrameWriter (df.write) and DataFrameWriterV2 (df.writeTo). Each builder method records state on a wrapped JVM reader or writer and returns self; only load/save style calls hand the work to the JVM.
nodes.languageNotes: Builder pattern: every option/format/mode/partitionBy call reassigns a private JVM handle (_jreader, _jwrite, _jwriter) and returns self for chaining. Docstrings note Spark Connect support, which is provided by a separate implementation.

nodes.name: OptionUtils
nodes.summary: Mixin shared by DataFrameReader and DataFrameWriter that applies a bundle of keyword arguments as options.

nodes.name: _set_opts
nodes.summary: Applies a schema (if given) and every keyword argument whose value is not None through self.schema and self.option, so per-format helpers like csv() and json() can forward their many parameters uniformly.

nodes.name: DataFrameReader
nodes.summary: Interface for loading a DataFrame from external storage, reached through SparkSession.read. Wraps the JVM reader obtained from spark._jsparkSession.read(); building it up with format/option/schema just records settings, and the data source is resolved when a load method such as load, csv or parquet is called.

nodes.name: _df
nodes.summary: Wraps a JVM DataFrame returned by the py4j reader into a Python DataFrame bound to the owning SparkSession.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Sets the input data source name on the JVM reader and returns self for chaining.

nodes.name: schema
nodes.summary: Sets an explicit input schema from a StructType (converted via the JVM parseDataType of its JSON) or a DDL string, otherwise raises PySparkTypeError. The docstring says supplying a schema lets sources like JSON skip schema inference.

nodes.name: option
nodes.summary: Adds one input option, stringifying the value with to_str, on the JVM reader and returns self.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Adds many input options from keyword arguments, stringifying each value, and returns self.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Generic loader: optionally applies format, schema and options, then calls the JVM load with no path, one path, or a list of paths converted to a Scala Seq. Returns a DataFrame; the docstring gives parquet as the default format.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Loads JSON (JSON Lines) from a path, list of paths, an RDD of strings, or a DataFrame holding JSON strings; forwards the many JSON parsing parameters through _set_opts, then dispatches to the JVM per input type (RDD input is encoded to bytes and passed through BytesToString).

nodes.name: table
nodes.summary: Returns the named table as a DataFrame by calling the JVM reader table().

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Returns the row-level changes (Change Data Capture) of the named table as a DataFrame via the JVM reader changes().

nodes.name: parquet
nodes.summary: Loads Parquet files from one or more paths; picks mergeSchema, pathGlobFilter, modifiedBefore/After, recursiveFileLookup and rebase-mode options out of keyword arguments and applies them via _set_opts.

nodes.name: text
nodes.summary: Loads text files into a DataFrame (schema starts with a string column per the docstring), with wholetext, lineSep and file-filter options.

nodes.name: csv
nodes.summary: Loads CSV from a path, list of paths, an RDD of strings, or a DataFrame of CSV lines. The docstring warns that inferSchema makes an extra pass over the input, which can be avoided by disabling it or passing a schema.

nodes.name: xml
nodes.summary: Loads XML files (rowTag based) from paths, an RDD of strings, or a DataFrame, forwarding XML parsing options through _set_opts; RDD input is turned into a JVM Dataset of strings first.

nodes.name: orc
nodes.summary: Loads ORC files from one or more paths with mergeSchema and file-filter options.

nodes.name: jdbc
nodes.summary: Reads a database table over JDBC; connection properties become a java.util.Properties, and it chooses between a plain read, a numeric column range split (column, lowerBound, upperBound, numPartitions) and a list of predicate partitions. Three typing overloads document these call shapes.

nodes.name: DataFrameWriter
nodes.summary: Interface for writing a DataFrame to external storage, reached through DataFrame.write. Holds the JVM writer from df._jdf.write(); mode, format, option, partitionBy, bucketBy, sortBy and clusterBy only record settings, and save/saveAsTable/insertInto or a format helper triggers the actual write.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Captures the DataFrame, its SparkSession and the JVM writer (df._jdf.write()).

nodes.name: mode
nodes.summary: Sets the save mode: append, overwrite, error/errorifexists or ignore. A None argument is skipped because the JVM default is already error.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Sets the underlying output data source name on the JVM writer.

nodes.name: option
nodes.summary: Adds one output option (value stringified with to_str) and returns self.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Adds many output options from keyword arguments and returns self.

nodes.name: partitionBy
nodes.summary: Partitions the file-system output by the given columns (directory-per-value layout); accepts varargs or a single list and converts names to a Scala Seq with _to_seq.

nodes.name: bucketBy
nodes.summary: Buckets the output by columns into numBuckets buckets, similar to Hive bucketing but with a different hash function and not Hive compatible (per docstring). Validates argument types and rejects a list col together with extra cols; applicable to file sources together with saveAsTable.

nodes.name: sortBy
nodes.summary: Sorts rows within each bucket by the given columns; same argument validation as bucketBy and meant to be combined with bucketBy and saveAsTable.

nodes.name: clusterBy
nodes.summary: Clusters data by one or more columns to optimize query performance; asserts at least one column and calls the JVM clusterBy.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Generic terminal write: applies mode, options, partitionBy and format (falling back to spark.sql.sources.default when no format is set, per docstring), then calls the JVM save with or without a path.

nodes.name: insertInto
nodes.summary: Inserts the DataFrame into an existing table, which must have the same schema; an overwrite flag maps to mode overwrite or append.

nodes.name: saveAsTable
nodes.summary: Saves the DataFrame as a catalog table; behavior when the table exists depends on the save mode (default error), and overwrite does not require the same schema.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Writes JSON Lines files at a path; sets the mode and the JSON options through _set_opts, then calls the JVM json writer.

nodes.name: parquet
nodes.summary: Writes Parquet files at a path with optional mode, partitionBy and compression.

nodes.name: text
nodes.summary: Writes the DataFrame as text files at a path with optional compression and lineSep.

nodes.name: csv
nodes.summary: Writes CSV files at a path; many CSV options (sep, quote, header, nullValue, and others) are forwarded through _set_opts.

nodes.name: xml
nodes.summary: Writes XML files at a path with row/root tag, attribute prefix, declaration and compression options.

nodes.name: orc
nodes.summary: Writes ORC files at a path with optional mode, partitionBy and compression.

nodes.name: jdbc
nodes.summary: Writes the DataFrame to an external database table through JDBC, building a java.util.Properties from the properties dict and applying the save mode first.

nodes.name: DataFrameWriterV2
nodes.summary: Builder for the DataSource V2 table write API, created by DataFrame.writeTo(table). It does not inherit OptionUtils; it wraps the JVM writer from df._jdf.writeTo(table) and finishes with create, replace, createOrReplace, append, overwrite or overwritePartitions.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Captures the DataFrame and its SparkSession and opens the JVM writeTo(table) writer.

nodes.name: using
nodes.summary: Specifies the provider (data source) for the table being written.

nodes.name: option
nodes.summary: Adds one write option, value stringified with to_str.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: Adds several write options passed as keyword arguments.

nodes.name: tableProperty
nodes.summary: Adds a table property to be set on the table that is created.

nodes.name: partitionedBy
nodes.summary: Sets the partitioning of the output table for create, createOrReplace or replace; columns are converted to JVM Column objects (so partition transforms can be expressed as Column expressions).

nodes.name: clusterBy
nodes.summary: Clusters the table data by the given column names to optimize query performance.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Creates a new table from the DataFrame contents (terminal action).

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Replaces an existing table with the DataFrame contents (terminal action).

nodes.name: createOrReplace
nodes.summary: Creates the table or replaces it if it exists, using the DataFrame contents (terminal action).

nodes.name: append
nodes.summary: Appends the DataFrame contents to the output table (terminal action).

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Overwrites the rows matching a filter condition (converted with _to_java_column) with the DataFrame contents.

nodes.name: overwritePartitions
nodes.summary: Overwrites every partition for which the DataFrame contains at least one row, leaving other partitions intact.

nodes.name: _test
nodes.summary: Doctest runner that starts a local SparkContext and SparkSession and runs the doctests of this module.

nodes.name: column.py
nodes.summary: Public pyspark.sql.Column: an abstract API class whose operator and method bodies are stubs decorated with dispatch_col_method, which forwards each call to the Classic or Spark Connect Column implementation. A Column is a lazily built expression (arithmetic, comparison, string, null, sort, cast, window), not data.
nodes.languageNotes: Method bodies are mostly '...' with the docstring as the real content (doctests); behavior lives in classic/column.py and connect/column.py. Column.__new__ returns a Classic Column by default as a backward-compatibility hack.

nodes.name: Column
nodes.summary: Public Column class (subclass of TableValuedFunctionArgument). Instances come from df.name / df['name'] or from expressions like df.age + 1; each operator or method returns a new Column that wraps an expression, so nothing is computed until a DataFrame action runs.

nodes.name: __new__
nodes.summary: Backward-compatibility hack: constructing pyspark.sql.Column directly returns a Spark Classic Column. The source marks it as not an API and not meant to be invoked directly.

nodes.name: __add__
nodes.summary: Representative of the arithmetic operator stubs (__neg__, __add__, __sub__, __mul__, __div__, __truediv__, __mod__, __pow__ and their reflected r-variants at lines 81-151); each builds a new Column from the operand through dispatch_col_method.

nodes.name: __eq__
nodes.summary: Equality comparison operator producing a boolean Column expression; with __ne__, __lt__, __le__, __gt__ and __ge__ it forms the comparison operator set (lines 155-188).

nodes.name: eqNullSafe
nodes.summary: Null-safe equality test (the <=> operator): unlike ==, comparing with NULL yields true or false instead of NULL.

nodes.name: __and__
nodes.summary: Logical AND via the & operator (Python cannot overload the and keyword); __or__, __rand__ and __ror__ do the same for |.

nodes.name: __invert__
nodes.summary: Logical NOT via the ~ operator.

nodes.name: __contains__
nodes.summary: Raises PySparkValueError (CANNOT_APPLY_IN_FOR_COLUMN) so that 'x in column' is rejected; users are expected to call isin instead.

nodes.name: bitwiseOR
nodes.summary: Bitwise OR of this expression with another expression.

nodes.name: bitwiseAND
nodes.summary: Bitwise AND of this expression with another expression.

nodes.name: bitwiseXOR
nodes.summary: Bitwise XOR of this expression with another expression.

nodes.name: getItem
nodes.summary: Expression extracting an element from a list by position or from a map by key.

nodes.name: getField
nodes.summary: Expression extracting a struct field by name.

nodes.name: withField
nodes.summary: Expression that adds or replaces a field of a struct by name, producing a new struct Column.

nodes.name: dropFields
nodes.summary: Expression that drops fields of a struct by name, producing a new struct Column.

nodes.name: __getattr__
nodes.summary: Attribute access (col.field) on a Column, documented like getItem or getField.

nodes.name: __getitem__
nodes.summary: Subscript access (col[k]) on a Column, documented like getItem or getField.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Boolean Column from a string match: true when the value contains the other element.

nodes.name: startswith
nodes.summary: Boolean Column from a string match: true when the value starts with the other element.

nodes.name: endswith
nodes.summary: Boolean Column from a string match: true when the value ends with the other element.

nodes.name: like
nodes.summary: SQL LIKE pattern match returning a boolean Column.

nodes.name: rlike
nodes.summary: SQL RLIKE (LIKE with a regular expression) match returning a boolean Column.

nodes.name: ilike
nodes.summary: SQL ILIKE (case-insensitive LIKE) match returning a boolean Column.

nodes.name: substr
nodes.summary: Substring of the column, given start position and length as ints or as Columns (two typing overloads).

nodes.name: isin
nodes.summary: Boolean expression that is true when the value is contained in the given values.

nodes.name: asc
nodes.summary: Sort expression for ascending order of the column.

nodes.name: asc_nulls_first
nodes.summary: Ascending sort expression placing null values before non-null values.

nodes.name: asc_nulls_last
nodes.summary: Ascending sort expression placing null values after non-null values.

nodes.name: desc
nodes.summary: Sort expression for descending order of the column.

nodes.name: desc_nulls_first
nodes.summary: Descending sort expression placing null values before non-null values.

nodes.name: desc_nulls_last
nodes.summary: Descending sort expression placing null values after non-null values.

nodes.name: isNull
nodes.summary: Boolean Column that is true when the expression is null.

nodes.name: isNotNull
nodes.summary: Boolean Column that is true when the expression is not null.

nodes.name: isNaN
nodes.summary: Boolean Column that is true when the expression is NaN.

nodes.name: alias
nodes.summary: Returns this column aliased with a new name, or several names for expressions that return more than one column such as explode.

nodes.name: name
nodes.summary: Alias of Column.alias.

nodes.name: cast
nodes.summary: Casts the column to a DataType or a DDL type string.

nodes.name: try_cast
nodes.summary: Like cast but returns NULL when the conversion fails instead of raising an error.

nodes.name: astype
nodes.summary: Alias of Column.cast.

nodes.name: between
nodes.summary: Boolean Column that is true when the value lies between a lower and an upper bound (bounds can be Columns or literals).

nodes.name: when
nodes.summary: Starts or extends a CASE WHEN chain by evaluating a condition and returning a value; unmatched rows yield None if otherwise is not called.

nodes.name: otherwise
nodes.summary: Supplies the fallback value of a when(...) chain.

nodes.name: over
nodes.summary: Defines a windowing column by applying this expression over a WindowSpec.

nodes.name: transform
nodes.summary: Applies a function taking a Column and returning a Column to this column, for chaining expression transformations.

nodes.name: outer
nodes.summary: Marks a column as referring to an outer query; per the docstring it triggers lazy analysis of a Spark Classic DataFrame so subquery expressions can be built (Connect is always lazily analyzed).

nodes.name: __bool__
nodes.summary: Dispatched stub for the Python truth-value protocol, so a Column cannot be used in if/and/or/not; the real behavior lives in the Classic and Connect implementations.

nodes.name: __repr__
nodes.summary: Dispatched stub for the Column<...> string representation.

nodes.name: _test
nodes.summary: Doctest runner that creates a local SparkSession and runs the doctests of this module.

nodes.name: types.py
nodes.summary: Python-side type system of PySpark SQL: the DataType hierarchy (atomic, interval, spatial, array, map, struct, UDT, variant types), the Row tuple, value classes (VariantVal, Geography, Geometry), schema parsing from JSON/DDL, schema inference and merging for createDataFrame, per-row type verifiers, and py4j input converters for datetime and numpy values. Each type defines how Python objects map to internal SQL values via toInternal and fromInternal.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a metaclass (DataTypeSingleton) to make parameterless types singletons, tuple subclassing for Row, and typing overloads for StructType.add and _merge_type. Module-level tables _type_mappings (Python type to DataType), _acceptable_types (DataType to allowed Python classes), _all_mappable_types and _array_type_mappings drive inference, verification and JSON parsing. Also contains small py4j converter classes (DateConverter, TimeConverter, DatetimeConverter, DatetimeNTZConverter, DayTimeIntervalTypeConverter, NumpyScalarConverter, NumpyArrayConverter) registered unless running remote-only; only NumpyArrayConverter has its own node.

nodes.name: DataType
nodes.summary: Base class of every Spark SQL type on the Python side. Equality compares class and __dict__, typeName() derives from the class name (minus 'Type', lowercased), json()/jsonValue() give the schema JSON form, and needConversion/toInternal/fromInternal default to identity and are overridden by types whose Python object differs from the internal SQL representation.

nodes.name: DataTypeSingleton
nodes.summary: Metaclass that caches one instance per class in a class-level dict, so NullType(), BooleanType(), DateType() and other parameterless types always return the same object. A source comment notes the singleton pattern does not survive pickle (unpickling yields another object).

nodes.name: NullType
nodes.summary: Type of None, used for values whose type cannot be inferred. typeName() is overridden to 'void'. Singleton via DataTypeSingleton. Schema inference yields it for None and _merge_type lets any other type win over it.

nodes.name: AtomicType
nodes.summary: Internal marker base for everything that is not null, a UDT, an array, a struct or a map. Intermediate base for NumericType, StringType, CharType, VarcharType, BinaryType, BooleanType, DatetimeType, SpatialType, AnsiIntervalType and VariantType.

nodes.name: NumericType
nodes.summary: Empty marker subclass of AtomicType grouping numeric types; parent of IntegralType and FractionalType.

nodes.name: IntegralType
nodes.summary: Marker base for the integer types (ByteType, ShortType, IntegerType, LongType). Declares the DataTypeSingleton metaclass, which the four subclasses inherit, so they are singletons.

nodes.name: FractionalType
nodes.summary: Marker base for the non-integer numeric types (DecimalType, DoubleType, FloatType). Has no singleton metaclass of its own.

nodes.name: StringType
nodes.summary: String type (Python str) with a collation name, default UTF8_BINARY. simpleString() is 'string' for the default collation and 'string collate <name>' otherwise; jsonValue() reuses simpleString(). collationProvider() maps names starting with UTF8 to 'spark' and the rest to 'icu'.

nodes.name: CharType
nodes.summary: Fixed-length char(n) type holding a length. simpleString and jsonValue render 'char(n)'. Declared as an AtomicType subclass; the type verifier treats it like StringType and accepts any value.

nodes.name: VarcharType
nodes.summary: Variable-length varchar(n) type holding a length. simpleString and jsonValue render 'varchar(n)'. Like CharType, the verifier accepts any value.

nodes.name: BinaryType
nodes.summary: Binary (byte array) type, singleton. Python values accepted by the verifier are bytearray and bytes, and schema inference maps both to it.

nodes.name: BooleanType
nodes.summary: Boolean type, singleton. The verifier accepts only Python bool.

nodes.name: DatetimeType
nodes.summary: Marker base class for date, time and timestamp types (DateType, AnyTimeType, TimestampType, TimestampNTZType).

nodes.name: DateType
nodes.summary: Date type backed by datetime.date, singleton. Internal form is the number of days since 1970-01-01: toInternal subtracts the epoch ordinal from date.toordinal(), fromInternal does the inverse with date.fromordinal.

nodes.name: AnyTimeType
nodes.summary: Marker base for TIME types of any precision; sits between DatetimeType and TimeType.

nodes.name: TimeType
nodes.summary: TIME type (datetime.time, since 4.1.0) with a precision defaulting to 6. Internal form is nanoseconds since midnight; toInternal/fromInternal convert hour, minute, second and microsecond to and from that value. simpleString/jsonValue render 'time(p)'.

nodes.name: TimestampType
nodes.summary: Timestamp type backed by datetime.datetime, singleton. Internal form is microseconds since the epoch: tz-aware values use calendar.timegm on the UTC tuple, naive values use time.mktime (local time); fromInternal builds a naive local datetime.

nodes.name: TimestampNTZType
nodes.summary: Timestamp without time zone, backed by naive datetime.datetime, singleton. typeName() is 'timestamp_ntz'. toInternal treats the fields as UTC (calendar.timegm) and fromInternal returns a naive datetime from a UTC conversion, so no local zone shift is applied.

nodes.name: DecimalType
nodes.summary: Fixed-precision decimal type (decimal.Decimal) with precision (default 10, max 38) and scale (default 0). Schema inference from Decimal objects always yields DecimalType(38, 18). simpleString and jsonValue render 'decimal(p,s)'.

nodes.name: DoubleType
nodes.summary: Double-precision float type, singleton. Python float is inferred as DoubleType.

nodes.name: FloatType
nodes.summary: Single-precision float type, singleton. Python float values are accepted; arrays with typecode 'f' map to it.

nodes.name: SpatialType
nodes.summary: Marker base of GeographyType and GeometryType; defines MIXED_SRID (-1) and MIXED_CRS ('SRID:ANY') for columns that can hold different SRIDs per row.

nodes.name: GeographyType
nodes.summary: GEOGRAPHY type (since 4.1.0) parameterized by an SRID or the string 'ANY'. Validates the SRID through a geographic SRS mapper (raising ST_INVALID_SRID_VALUE), keeps a CRS and the SPHERICAL algorithm for JSON, and converts Geography objects to and from dicts holding srid and wkb bytes.

nodes.name: GeometryType
nodes.summary: GEOMETRY type (since 4.1.0) parameterized by an SRID or 'ANY'. Same design as GeographyType but with a Cartesian SRS mapper and no algorithm; jsonValue uses the CRS ('geometry(<crs>)'). Converts Geometry objects to and from dicts holding srid and wkb.

nodes.name: ByteType
nodes.summary: Signed 8-bit integer type; simpleString is 'tinyint'. Verifier range is -128..127.

nodes.name: IntegerType
nodes.summary: Signed 32-bit integer type; simpleString is 'int'. Verifier range is -2147483648..2147483647.

nodes.name: LongType
nodes.summary: Signed 64-bit integer type; simpleString is 'bigint'. This is the type a plain Python int is inferred as, and the verifier range is the signed 64-bit range (use DecimalType beyond it).

nodes.name: ShortType
nodes.summary: Signed 16-bit integer type; simpleString is 'smallint'. Verifier range is -32768..32767.

nodes.name: AnsiIntervalType
nodes.summary: Marker base for ANSI SQL interval types (DayTimeIntervalType, YearMonthIntervalType).

nodes.name: DayTimeIntervalType
nodes.summary: Day-time interval type backed by datetime.timedelta, with start and end fields among DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, SECOND (default DAY to SECOND). Internal form is microseconds. simpleString and jsonValue render 'interval day to second' style text; invalid fields raise INVALID_INTERVAL_CASTING.

nodes.name: YearMonthIntervalType
nodes.summary: Year-month interval type with start and end fields YEAR and MONTH (default YEAR to MONTH). toInternal/fromInternal raise NOT_IMPLEMENTED, and needConversion is true unless env PYSPARK_YM_INTERVAL_LEGACY is '1', so collect/take/head fail by default.

nodes.name: CalendarIntervalType
nodes.summary: Calendar interval type (months, days, microseconds), singleton with typeName 'interval'. Only a JSON/schema type on the Python side: toInternal and fromInternal raise NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

nodes.name: ArrayType
nodes.summary: Array type with elementType and containsNull (default True), backed by Python list. needConversion/toInternal/fromInternal delegate to the element type and are skipped when the element needs no conversion. toNullable() returns a copy with every nullability flag true.

nodes.name: MapType
nodes.summary: Map type with keyType, valueType and valueContainsNull (default True), backed by Python dict. Conversion applies to keys and values only when either needs conversion. Keys must not be null (enforced by the verifier). toNullable() sets all nullability flags true.

nodes.name: StructField
nodes.summary: A named field of a StructType: name, dataType, nullable (default True) and metadata dict. jsonValue moves non-default collations of string types into metadata under '__COLLATIONS' and strips them from the type JSON; fromJson reverses this. Conversion methods delegate to the field's dataType.

nodes.name: StructType
nodes.summary: Struct type, a list of StructField, which is the schema of a DataFrame and the type of a Row. Supports iteration, len, lookup by name, index or slice, add(), fieldNames(), treeString(), toDDL(), JSON round trip, and precomputes which fields need conversion so toInternal/fromInternal convert only those. fromInternal produces Row objects.

nodes.name: VariantType
nodes.summary: VARIANT type (since 4.0.0) for semi-structured values. fromInternal wraps a dict holding value and metadata bytes into VariantVal; toInternal requires a VariantVal and returns that dict.

nodes.name: UserDefinedType
nodes.summary: Base class for user-defined types (documented as Spark internal use only). Subclasses supply sqlType(), module(), serialize() and deserialize(); toInternal/fromInternal run serialize/deserialize around the cached sqlType conversion. jsonValue emits a udt record with either a Scala UDT class or a base64 cloudpickle of the Python class.

nodes.name: VariantVal
nodes.summary: Python value class for a Variant: holds the value and metadata bytes. toPython(), toJson(zone_id='UTC') and __str__ decode through VariantUtils, and parseJson() builds one from a JSON string.

nodes.name: Geography
nodes.summary: Python value class for a GEOGRAPHY value: WKB bytes plus an SRID, with getBytes/getSrid, equality, and fromWKB.

nodes.name: Geometry
nodes.summary: Python value class for a GEOMETRY value: WKB bytes plus an SRID, with getBytes/getSrid, equality, and fromWKB.

nodes.name: Row
nodes.summary: A tuple subclass with optional field names, the Python object for a DataFrame row. Row(a=1, b=2) keeps keyword order (since 3.0) and stores names in __fields__; Row('a','b') makes a Row class-like object callable to create rows. Supports row.key, row['key'], 'key' in row and asDict; it is immutable (setattr raises READ_ONLY) and pickles through _create_row.

nodes.name: NumpyArrayConverter
nodes.summary: py4j input converter registered with prepend=True that turns a 1-D numpy array into a Java array of the matching primitive type (int8/int16 become short), raising UNSUPPORTED_NUMPY_ARRAY_SCALAR for others.

nodes.name: fromDDL
nodes.summary: Class method that parses a DDL-formatted type string (e.g. 'b string, a int', 'decimal(10,10)') into a DataType by delegating to _parse_datatype_string; a top-level struct<> may be omitted (since 4.0.0).

nodes.name: jsonValue
nodes.summary: Returns the JSON representation of the type; the base version is just typeName(). Complex types override it with a dict.

nodes.name: json
nodes.summary: Serializes jsonValue() to a compact, key-sorted JSON string (separators ',' and ':'); this is the string sent to the JVM to describe a type.

nodes.name: simpleString
nodes.summary: Returns the short SQL name of the type; the base version returns typeName(). Subclasses return forms such as 'int', 'decimal(p,s)', 'array<...>', 'struct<...>'.

nodes.name: needConversion
nodes.summary: Reports whether values need conversion between Python and the internal SQL form; False by default, True for dates, timestamps, structs and similar, so unneeded conversion is skipped for containers.

nodes.name: toInternal
nodes.summary: Converts a Python object into the internal SQL object; identity by default. Subclasses such as DateType (days since epoch) and TimestampType (microseconds) override it.

nodes.name: fromInternal
nodes.summary: Converts an internal SQL object back into a native Python object; identity by default and overridden by types with a different internal form.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Appends a field and returns self (mutates the StructType) so calls can be chained. Accepts a StructField, or name plus data_type (a DataType or a type string parsed via _parse_datatype_json_value), nullable and metadata; then recomputes the needConversion cache. Raises ARGUMENT_REQUIRED when only a name is given.

nodes.name: fieldNames
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the field names as a list.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Class method that builds a StructType from a parsed schema JSON dict by applying StructField.fromJson to each entry of json['fields'].

nodes.name: treeString
nodes.summary: Builds the indented 'root' schema tree text (as shown by printSchema) using a StringConcat and each field's _build_formatted_string; maxDepth limits nesting and non-positive values mean unlimited.

nodes.name: simpleString
nodes.summary: Renders 'struct<name:type,...>' by joining each field's simpleString.

nodes.name: __getitem__
nodes.summary: Looks up a field by name (raising KEY_NOT_EXISTS), by integer index (raising INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE) or by slice (returning a new StructType); other key types raise NOT_EXPECTED_TYPE.

nodes.name: toInternal
nodes.summary: Converts a Python record (tuple, list, dict or object with __dict__) into an internal tuple. If any field needs conversion only those fields are converted, otherwise values are just tupled. Rejects VariantVal rows and unsupported objects.

nodes.name: fromInternal
nodes.summary: Converts an internal tuple into a Row via _create_row, converting only the fields flagged in _needConversion. A value that is already a Row (already converted by the pickler) is returned unchanged.

nodes.name: toDDL
nodes.summary: Returns the DDL string for the schema by asking the active Spark Connect session (_to_ddl) in remote mode, or the active SparkContext otherwise.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Class method that builds a StructField from its JSON dict. Extracts the '__COLLATIONS' entry from metadata (validating the provider and stripping the provider prefix), then parses the type with _parse_datatype_json_value using the field name as path.

nodes.name: getCollationMetadata
nodes.summary: Walks the field's data type (through arrays and maps) and returns a dict mapping field paths such as 'name.element' to '<provider>.<collation>' for string types with a non-default collation.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Class method that builds an ArrayType from JSON, parsing elementType through _parse_datatype_json_value with an 'element' path suffix used for collation lookup.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Class method that builds a MapType from JSON, parsing keyType and valueType through _parse_datatype_json_value with '.key' and '.value' path suffixes for collation lookup.

nodes.name: fromJson
nodes.summary: Class method that imports the module named in 'pyClass', finds the class and checks it is a UserDefinedType subclass (else UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION or FIELD_TYPE_MISMATCH), and returns an instance.

nodes.name: jsonValue
nodes.summary: Builds the udt JSON record: with a Scala UDT it stores class and pyClass (not allowed for classes in __main__); otherwise it stores pyClass and a base64 cloudpickle of the class as serializedClass. Always includes the sqlType JSON.

nodes.name: asDict
nodes.summary: Returns the row as a dict keyed by field name (raising CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE if the Row has no names). With recursive=True nested Rows, lists and dicts are converted too. With duplicate field names only one is kept.

nodes.name: __call__
nodes.summary: Lets a Row of field names act like a class: calling Person('Alice', 11) creates a new Row with those names via _create_row, and raises TOO_MANY_VALUES when more values than names are passed.

nodes.name: _drop_metadata
nodes.summary: Recursively rebuilds a DataType or StructField with all field metadata removed, descending through structs, arrays and maps.

nodes.name: _parse_datatype_string
nodes.summary: Parses a type or DDL string into a DataType by calling the JVM side: SparkSession.active()._parse_ddl for Spark Connect, otherwise the active SparkContext's _parse_ddl. Accepts case-insensitive text and a struct without struct<>.

nodes.name: _parse_datatype_json_string
nodes.summary: Parses a schema JSON string with json.loads and delegates to _parse_datatype_json_value; used to read schemas produced by the JVM.

nodes.name: _parse_datatype_json_value
nodes.summary: Core JSON-to-DataType parser. For strings it checks the _all_mappable_types name table, then regexes for decimal(p,s), time(p), day-time and year-month intervals, string collate, char(n), varchar(n), geometry and geography; for dicts it dispatches array, map, struct and udt. Applies collation overrides by field path and raises CANNOT_PARSE_DATATYPE or UNSUPPORTED_DATA_TYPE otherwise.

nodes.name: _from_numpy_type
nodes.summary: Maps a numpy dtype (bool, int8..int64, float32, float64, str) to the corresponding Spark DataType, returning None for anything else.

nodes.name: _int_size_to_type
nodes.summary: Returns the smallest Spark integral type (Byte, Short, Integer, Long) that fits a bit size, or None above 64 bits; used to build the array typecode map.

nodes.name: _infer_type
nodes.summary: Infers a DataType from one Python value. None gives NullType, __UDT__ objects give their UDT, scalars use _type_mappings (Decimal becomes DecimalType(38,18), datetime may become TimestampNTZ when preferred). dict becomes a struct, first-pair map or merged map; list becomes an array; array.array maps by typecode; other objects fall back to _infer_schema. Raises UNSUPPORTED_DATA_TYPE otherwise.

nodes.name: _infer_schema
nodes.summary: Infers a StructType from one row: dicts and objects are sorted by key, Row and namedtuple use their field names, plain tuples/lists use given or generated names '_1', '_2', .... Every field is nullable and typed via _infer_type; failures raise CANNOT_INFER_SCHEMA_FOR_TYPE or CANNOT_INFER_TYPE_FOR_FIELD.

nodes.name: _has_nulltype
nodes.summary: Returns True if a NullType appears anywhere inside the type, recursing through structs, arrays and maps; used to detect unresolved columns after inference.

nodes.name: _has_type
nodes.summary: Returns True if the type or any nested struct field, array element or map key/value is an instance of the given class or tuple of classes.

nodes.name: _merge_type
nodes.summary: Merges two inferred types into one (implementation behind several typing overloads). NullType yields to the other side, TimestampType wins over TimestampNTZ, differing spatial SRIDs become ANY, string wins over other atomic types, and different classes raise CANNOT_MERGE_TYPE. Structs merge by field name, arrays and maps merge recursively and become nullable.

nodes.name: _need_converter
nodes.summary: Decides whether _create_converter must build a real converter: true for structs, NullType and StringType (which coerces any value to str), and recursively for arrays and maps whose members need one.

nodes.name: _create_converter
nodes.summary: Builds a function that drops field names from input data before it is turned into Spark rows: structs become tuples (from dicts or objects by field name), arrays and maps convert their members, NullType gives None, and StringType stringifies values (bool becomes lowercase 'true'/'false' to match Classic).

nodes.name: _make_type_verifier
nodes.summary: Builds a closure that validates a value against a DataType and raises PySparkTypeError or PySparkValueError with the field path. It checks nullability (and treats Decimal NaN as null), accepted Python classes per type (_acceptable_types, exact type match so subclasses fail), integer ranges for Byte/Short/Integer/Long, and recurses into arrays, maps (keys non-null), structs and UDT sqlType. String, char, varchar and variant accept anything.

nodes.name: _create_row_inbound_converter
nodes.summary: Returns a callable used when unpickling a Row coming from the JVM; it applies dataType.fromInternal to the received values.

nodes.name: _create_row
nodes.summary: Constructs a Row from values and assigns the field names to its __fields__ attribute; also the function Row.__reduce__ uses to pickle named rows.

nodes.name: InMemoryTableScanExec.scala
nodes.summary: Physical plan node that reads a cached DataFrame (an InMemoryRelation). It scans the cached columnar batches, can skip batches using per-batch min/max statistics, and returns rows or ColumnarBatches; the InMemoryScans strategy plans it.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a trait and a case class that extends a Spark LeafExecNode; some members are vals rather than methods.

nodes.name: InMemoryTableScanLike
nodes.summary: Common leaf-node trait for in-memory table scans that lets code pattern match on them. It declares whether the cache is materialized, the raw cached RDD of CachedBatch, and runtime statistics.

nodes.name: InMemoryTableScanExec
nodes.summary: Scan of a cached relation: when a PySpark DataFrame that was cached or persisted is read again, this node reads the stored CachedBatch RDD, optionally prunes batches by their statistics against the pushed-down predicates, and converts them to InternalRows or ColumnarBatches. It reports a numOutputRows metric.

nodes.name: simpleStringWithNodeId
nodes.summary: Appends columnar input and output flags (columnarIn, columnarOut) to the node description when the cache builder supports columnar input or this scan supports columnar output.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes the scan by normalizing the attributes and predicates against the relation output and canonicalizing the relation, so equivalent scans compare equal.

nodes.name: supportsColumnar
nodes.summary: Value (a val, not a method) that decides whether the scan reads from ColumnVectors in ColumnarBatch (faster) or from UnsafeRows built from CachedBatch. It requires the vectorized cache reader config, not too many fields for whole stage codegen, and a serializer that supports columnar output.

nodes.name: cachedPlan
nodes.summary: Returns the cached relation plan, unwrapping an AdaptiveSparkPlanExec to its executed plan when that is the final plan.

nodes.name: updateAttribute
nodes.summary: Rewrites attribute references in an expression from the cached plan output to the relation output, because the scan output can be pruned relative to the relation.

nodes.name: outputPartitioning
nodes.summary: Reports the partitioning of the cached plan, with attributes remapped to the relation output because the cached version may alias output.

nodes.name: outputOrdering
nodes.summary: Reports the ordering of the cached plan, with sort order attributes remapped to the relation output.

nodes.name: filteredCachedBatches
nodes.summary: Takes the cached column buffers from the CachedRDDBuilder and, when in-memory partition pruning is enabled, applies the serializer-built filter on the pushed-down predicates so batches whose statistics rule them out are skipped.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Row-based execution path: resets test accumulators, wraps the filtered cached batches to count partitions, batches, and numOutputRows, then asks the serializer to convert CachedBatch into InternalRow.

nodes.name: doExecuteColumnar
nodes.summary: Columnar execution path: converts the filtered cached batches to ColumnarBatch with the serializer and adds the row count of each batch to numOutputRows.

nodes.name: baseCacheRDD
nodes.summary: Returns the actual cached RDD of CachedBatch without filters or row/columnar conversion; used only by AQE.

nodes.name: runtimeStatistics
nodes.summary: Returns runtime statistics of the cached relation after materialization by delegating to the relation computeStats.

nodes.name: ShuffledRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the RDD produced by a shuffle (repartitioning, groupByKey-style and sortByKey-style operations). Its compute method does not run user code; it asks the ShuffleManager for a reader that fetches this reduce partition's blocks from all map outputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class with context-bound ClassTags K, V, C (key, value, combiner types). prev is @transient and nulled by clearDependencies.

nodes.name: MapStatus.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MapStatus, the per-map-task result sent to the driver: where the shuffle output lives and an estimate of each reduce block's size. Two implementations trade accuracy for size: one byte per block, or an empty-block bitmap plus an average.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala sealed trait with companion object and Externalizable implementations.

nodes.name: ShuffledRDDPartition
nodes.summary: Trivial Partition implementation that just stores the reduce partition index.

nodes.name: ShuffledRDD
nodes.summary: RDD[(K, C)] that reads the output of a shuffle: it has one partition per partitioner partition and a single ShuffleDependency on its parent RDD. Callers can set a serializer, key ordering, aggregator and map-side combine flag before it is used.

nodes.name: setSerializer
nodes.summary: Sets a serializer for this RDD's shuffle; null means use the default chosen from spark.serializer.

nodes.name: setKeyOrdering
nodes.summary: Sets the key ordering the shuffle should use to sort records by key on the reduce side.

nodes.name: setAggregator
nodes.summary: Sets the Aggregator used to combine values for the shuffle.

nodes.name: setMapSideCombine
nodes.summary: Sets whether map tasks should combine values before writing shuffle output.

nodes.name: getDependencies
nodes.summary: Creates the single ShuffleDependency on the parent RDD with the partitioner, key ordering, aggregator and map-side-combine flag. If no serializer was set it asks SerializerManager for one for the key and combiner types (map-side combine) or key and value types.

nodes.name: getPartitions
nodes.summary: Creates one ShuffledRDDPartition per partition of the partitioner.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Asks the MapOutputTrackerMaster on the driver for preferred locations of this reduce partition based on where its shuffle map output is.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Runs on an executor for one reduce partition: gets the ShuffleDependency, creates temporary shuffle read metrics from the task context, and calls ShuffleManager.getReader for exactly this partition, then returns read() as an iterator of (K, C).

nodes.name: clearDependencies
nodes.summary: Clears dependencies and drops the reference to the parent RDD so it can be garbage collected.

nodes.name: isBarrier
nodes.summary: Always returns false because a ShuffledRDD starts a new stage and is never part of a barrier stage.

nodes.name: ShuffleOutputStatus
nodes.summary: Marker trait shared by MapStatus and MergeStatus so MapOutputTracker can handle both with the same code.

nodes.name: MapStatus
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for what a ShuffleMapTask returns to the scheduler: the BlockManagerId location of its shuffle files, an estimated size per reduce block (never zero for a non-empty block), the map id and a checksum. Its companion object picks the implementation and holds the 8-bit log-base-1.1 size encoding.

nodes.name: CompressedMapStatus
nodes.summary: MapStatus that stores one byte per reduce block holding the log-encoded size of that block, serialized via Externalizable. Used when the number of reduce partitions is at or below the threshold.

nodes.name: HighlyCompressedMapStatus
nodes.summary: MapStatus for jobs with many reduce partitions: it keeps a RoaringBitmap of empty blocks, the average size of ordinary non-empty blocks, and accurate (compressed) sizes only for huge blocks at or above a threshold. The companion apply computes those values, including a skew-based threshold.

nodes.name: getSizeForBlock
nodes.summary: Abstract: returns the estimated size in bytes of the block for a reduce partition id. A non-empty block must never report 0 because block fetchers skip zero-size blocks.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory used by shuffle writers: if the number of reduce partitions is greater than spark.shuffle.minNumPartitionsToHighlyCompress (default 2000) it builds a HighlyCompressedMapStatus, otherwise a CompressedMapStatus.

nodes.name: compressSize
nodes.summary: Encodes a size into one byte as the ceiling of log base 1.1 of the size (0 for empty, 1 for size 1, capped at 255). This represents sizes up to about 35 GB with at most 10 percent error.

nodes.name: decompressSize
nodes.summary: Reverses compressSize by computing 1.1 raised to the unsigned byte value, returning 0 for a zero byte.

nodes.name: getSizeForBlock
nodes.summary: Looks up the byte for the reduce id and decodes it with MapStatus.decompressSize.

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Serializes location, the compressed size array with its length, map task id and checksum.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Deserializes the fields in the order written by writeExternal.

nodes.name: getSizeForBlock
nodes.summary: Returns 0 for blocks in the empty bitmap, the decoded accurate size for recorded huge blocks, and the average size for every other block.

nodes.name: writeExternal
nodes.summary: Serializes location, the empty-block bitmap, average size, the map of huge block sizes, map task id and checksum.

nodes.name: readExternal
nodes.summary: Deserializes the fields written by writeExternal and rebuilds the bitmap and huge block map.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Builds a HighlyCompressedMapStatus from exact sizes: it chooses a huge-block threshold (the smaller of spark.shuffle.accurateBlockThreshold and a skew threshold from the median times the skew factor), adds empty blocks to a RoaringBitmap, averages the other small blocks, and stores compressed sizes only for huge blocks.

nodes.name: MemoryStore.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MemoryStore, the in-memory part of the BlockManager, which keeps cached blocks either as arrays of deserialized JVM objects or as serialized ChunkedByteBuffers, plus the entry, values-holder and partially-unrolled helper types it uses. This is where MEMORY_ONLY and the memory side of MEMORY_AND_DISK partitions live on an executor.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with several private sealed traits and case classes; the LinkedHashMap of entries is created in access-order mode (third constructor argument true), so iteration order is least recently used first.

nodes.name: MemoryEntry
nodes.summary: Private sealed trait describing one cached block in the MemoryStore: its size in bytes, its MemoryMode (on-heap or off-heap) and the ClassTag of its elements.

nodes.name: DeserializedMemoryEntry
nodes.summary: Case class MemoryEntry that holds a block as an Array of live (deserialized) JVM objects; used for levels such as MEMORY_ONLY that store deserialized values. Its size is an estimate.

nodes.name: SerializedMemoryEntry
nodes.summary: Case class MemoryEntry that holds a block as a ChunkedByteBuffer of serialized bytes (as used by the *_SER levels and off-heap caching); its size is the buffer size.

nodes.name: BlockEvictionHandler
nodes.summary: Private[storage] trait with a single dropFromMemory callback that the MemoryStore invokes when it must evict a block; BlockManager implements it so a block can be moved to disk or discarded. The caller must already hold the block write lock.

nodes.name: MemoryStore
nodes.summary: Stores blocks in memory as deserialized object arrays or serialized buffers, tracks per-task unroll memory, and evicts least recently used blocks (never blocks of the same RDD as the incoming one) when the MemoryManager needs storage space. All allocation changes are synchronized on the MemoryManager.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a java.util.LinkedHashMap in access order for LRU iteration and synchronizes on memoryManager for every allocation change.

nodes.name: MemoryEntryBuilder
nodes.summary: Private trait for a two-step builder returned by a ValuesHolder: it reports the precise size of the fully unrolled block and then builds the final MemoryEntry.

nodes.name: ValuesHolder
nodes.summary: Private trait abstracting how unrolled records are accumulated (storeValue, estimatedSize) and finalized (getBuilder); after getBuilder the holder can no longer be used.

nodes.name: DeserializedValuesHolder
nodes.summary: ValuesHolder that appends records to a SizeTrackingVector while unrolling; on completion it converts the vector to an array and builds a DeserializedMemoryEntry sized by SizeEstimator.

nodes.name: SerializedValuesHolder
nodes.summary: ValuesHolder that serializes records on the fly into a ChunkedByteBufferOutputStream through a RedirectableOutputStream (using the SerializerManager serializer and compression), so the unrolled size is the byte count so far. Builds a SerializedMemoryEntry on completion.

nodes.name: PartiallyUnrolledIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator returned when a block could not be fully unrolled into memory: it replays the already unrolled values and then the rest of the original iterator, and frees the held unroll memory when the unrolled part is consumed or close() is called.

nodes.name: RedirectableOutputStream
nodes.summary: OutputStream wrapper whose underlying sink can be swapped with setOutputStream, letting a serialization stream that started writing to memory be redirected to another sink such as a disk stream.

nodes.name: PartiallySerializedBlock
nodes.summary: Handle returned when putIteratorAsBytes runs out of memory: it can either finish serializing the block into a given output stream (for example a disk file) or deserialize the partial bytes back into an iterator, and releases unroll memory and buffers when done or discarded.

nodes.name: getSize
nodes.summary: Returns the size in bytes of a block currently held in the MemoryStore entries map.

nodes.name: putBytes
nodes.summary: Stores an already serialized block: it first asks the MemoryManager for storage memory of the given size and only then materializes the ChunkedByteBuffer and records a SerializedMemoryEntry. Returns false without creating the buffer when memory cannot be acquired.

nodes.name: putIterator
nodes.summary: Core unrolling routine: it reserves an initial unroll memory threshold, appends records through a ValuesHolder while periodically re-estimating size and requesting more unroll memory, and on success converts the unroll memory into storage memory and stores the entry. On failure it returns the unroll memory still held, leaving the partial data to the caller.

nodes.name: putIteratorAsValues
nodes.summary: Tries to cache an iterator as deserialized objects (the MEMORY_ONLY path). On failure it returns a PartiallyUnrolledIterator combining the unrolled values and the remaining input, which the caller must consume or close to free memory.

nodes.name: putIteratorAsBytes
nodes.summary: Tries to cache an iterator as serialized bytes (the *_SER and off-heap path), capping the chunk size to the maximum array length. On failure it returns a PartiallySerializedBlock so the caller can finish writing it to disk or deserialize it back.

nodes.name: getBytes
nodes.summary: Returns the ChunkedByteBuffer of a serialized entry; throws an internal error if the entry was stored deserialized, and returns None if the block is absent.

nodes.name: getValues
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over the objects of a deserialized entry; throws an internal error if the entry was stored serialized, and returns None if the block is absent.

nodes.name: freeMemoryEntry
nodes.summary: Releases the resources of an entry: disposes the buffer of a serialized entry, or closes every AutoCloseable object held by a deserialized entry, logging non-fatal close failures.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes a block from the entries map, frees its entry and returns its bytes to the MemoryManager storage pool; returns false if the block was not in memory.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Frees all entries, clears the per-task unroll memory maps and releases all storage memory; used when the BlockManager stops.

nodes.name: evictBlocksToFreeSpace
nodes.summary: Selects least recently used blocks to free the requested space for a new block, skipping blocks of the same RDD as the incoming one (to avoid wasteful cyclic replacement) and blocks currently read-locked (via a non-blocking write lock). Selected blocks are handed to the BlockEvictionHandler, which may write them to disk, then unlocked or removed; if not enough space can be freed, nothing is evicted.

nodes.name: contains
nodes.summary: Returns whether the MemoryStore currently holds an entry for the block id.

nodes.name: reserveUnrollMemoryForThisTask
nodes.summary: Asks the MemoryManager for unroll memory for the current task attempt and, if granted, adds the amount to that task entry in the on-heap or off-heap unroll memory map.

nodes.name: releaseUnrollMemoryForThisTask
nodes.summary: Releases up to the requested amount (default all) of the current task unroll memory back to the MemoryManager and drops the task entry when it reaches zero.

nodes.name: currentUnrollMemory
nodes.summary: Returns the total unroll memory currently held by all tasks, summing the on-heap and off-heap maps.

nodes.name: currentUnrollMemoryForThisTask
nodes.summary: Returns the unroll memory currently held by the calling task attempt across on-heap and off-heap modes.

nodes.name: logMemoryUsage
nodes.summary: Logs block memory, unroll (scratch) memory shared across tasks, total storage memory used and the storage limit.

nodes.name: logUnrollFailureMessage
nodes.summary: Logs the warning "Not enough space to cache <block> in memory" with the size computed so far, then logs overall memory usage.

nodes.name: getBuilder
nodes.summary: Converts the unrolled SizeTrackingVector to an array, measures it precisely with SizeEstimator and returns a builder that creates the DeserializedMemoryEntry.

nodes.name: getBuilder
nodes.summary: Closes the serialization stream and returns a builder whose precise size is the bytes written and which builds the SerializedMemoryEntry from the ChunkedByteBufferOutputStream.

nodes.name: releaseUnrollMemory
nodes.summary: Releases this iterator unroll memory for the current task and nulls the unrolled iterator so it can be garbage collected early (SPARK-17503).

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Reports whether elements remain, releasing the unroll memory as soon as the unrolled values are exhausted and then continuing with the rest iterator.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Disposes of the iterator early by releasing its unroll memory if it has not already been freed.

nodes.name: discard
nodes.summary: Discards the partially serialized block: redirects the stream to a null sink so closing the serializer writes nowhere, disposes the buffered bytes and releases unroll memory.

nodes.name: finishWritingToStream
nodes.summary: Writes the already serialized bytes to the target output stream (for example a disk file), frees the unroll memory, redirects the serializer to that stream and serializes the remaining input records into it.

nodes.name: valuesIterator
nodes.summary: Closes the serialization stream, deserializes the partial bytes and returns a PartiallyUnrolledIterator over them followed by the rest of the original iterator.

nodes.name: BlockInfoManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines BlockInfo (per-block metadata) and BlockInfoManager, the readers-writer lock table of the BlockManager: it tracks which task attempt holds read or write locks on each block, supports first-writer-wins creation of new blocks, and releases all locks of a task when it finishes.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines a Guava Striped lock (1024 stripes) for creation races, per-block ReentrantLock/Condition wrappers, and Guava multisets for re-entrant read-lock counts.

nodes.name: BlockInfo
nodes.summary: Mutable metadata for one block: requested StorageLevel, ClassTag, tellMaster flag, size, reader count and the task attempt id of the current writer. Invariants: reader count is never negative and a block is not read- and write-locked at once. Its companion object defines NO_WRITER (-1) and NON_TASK_WRITER (-1024).
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object (lines 118-130) shares this node id; the stored level is the requested level, not where the block actually resides.

nodes.name: BlockInfoWrapper
nodes.summary: Private wrapper pairing a BlockInfo with the striped lock and a Condition for that block, offering withLock and tryLock so BlockInfo mutations happen under the lock.

nodes.name: BlockInfoManager
nodes.summary: Thread-safe component of the BlockManager that tracks BlockInfo for every block and implements readers-writer locking tied to task attempts. It also keeps reverse indexes (RDD, broadcast, cache session to block ids) and optional visibility tracking for RDD blocks, and releases a task locks on completion.
nodes.languageNotes: trackingCacheVisibility constructor flag enables invisible-RDD-block tracking; otherwise RDD blocks are always visible.

nodes.name: checkInvariants
nodes.summary: Asserts the lock invariants after every state change: reader count is non-negative and a block is never read-locked and write-locked simultaneously.

nodes.name: withLock
nodes.summary: Runs a function with the block BlockInfo and Condition while holding the block lock, always unlocking afterwards.

nodes.name: tryLock
nodes.summary: Runs a function with the BlockInfo and Condition only if the block lock can be taken without waiting; otherwise does nothing.

nodes.name: registerWriteLockForTask
nodes.summary: Records that a task attempt holds the write lock on a block, creating the task synchronized set of write-locked blocks if absent.

nodes.name: unregisterWriteLockForTask
nodes.summary: Removes a block from a task set of write-locked blocks; the task entry itself is cleaned up later by releaseAllLocksForTask.

nodes.name: isRDDBlockVisible
nodes.summary: Tells whether a cached RDD block is visible to readers: always true unless cache-visibility tracking is on, in which case the block must be registered and not in the invisible set.

nodes.name: tryMarkBlockAsVisible
nodes.summary: Marks an RDD block visible by removing it from the invisible set, when visibility tracking is enabled.

nodes.name: registerTask
nodes.summary: Registers a task attempt id by creating empty write-lock and read-lock bookkeeping for it; must be called before the task uses any other BlockInfoManager method.

nodes.name: currentTaskAttemptId
nodes.summary: Returns the current TaskContext task attempt id, or NON_TASK_WRITER (-1024) when called from a non-task thread such as the driver.

nodes.name: acquireLock
nodes.summary: Generic lock-acquisition loop: looks up the block wrapper, applies the supplied try-acquire function under the block lock and, if it fails and blocking is requested, waits on the block Condition and retries. Returns None when the block does not exist.

nodes.name: blockInfo
nodes.summary: Looks up a block wrapper and runs a function under its lock, throwing a block-does-not-exist error when the block is not registered.

nodes.name: lockForReading
nodes.summary: Acquires a re-entrant shared read lock on a block (granted unless some task holds the write lock), incrementing the reader count and the calling task per-block read count; blocks until available or returns None immediately when blocking is false.

nodes.name: lockForWriting
nodes.summary: Acquires an exclusive write lock on a block when there is no writer and no readers, recording the task as writer; blocks or returns None according to the blocking flag, and returns None if the block does not exist.

nodes.name: assertBlockIsLockedForWriting
nodes.summary: Returns the BlockInfo if the current task holds the write lock on the block, otherwise throws an error that the task has not locked the block.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns a block BlockInfo without taking any lock; intended for BlockManager status queries only.

nodes.name: downgradeLock
nodes.summary: Downgrades the current task write lock on a block to a read lock by unlocking and then taking a non-blocking read lock, used after a block has been written so it can be read right away.

nodes.name: unlock
nodes.summary: Releases the write lock or one read lock on a block for a task (the task id can be passed explicitly, see SPARK-18406), updating the per-task bookkeeping and signalling waiters; guards against a race with releaseAllLocksForTask that could make reader counts negative.

nodes.name: lockNewBlockForWriting
nodes.summary: Implements first-writer-wins creation of a block: under a striped lock it atomically registers the new BlockInfo and takes the write lock, or, if the block already exists, optionally waits for a read lock instead (retrying if the block was removed meanwhile). Returns true only when the caller got the write lock.

nodes.name: releaseAllLocksForTask
nodes.summary: Releases every read and write lock still held by a finished task, resets writer fields and reader counts, wakes waiters and returns the block ids whose locks were released; called at task end so a failed task cannot leak locks.

nodes.name: entries
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator over a snapshot of all (BlockId, BlockInfo) pairs; entries are mutable and may reflect blocks deleted during traversal.

nodes.name: rddBlockIds
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of all blocks that belong to a given RDD using the cached RDD-to-blocks mapping.

nodes.name: broadcastBlockIds
nodes.summary: Returns the ids of all blocks that belong to a given broadcast variable.

nodes.name: sessionBlockIds
nodes.summary: Returns cache blocks that may belong to cached local relations of a given Spark session UUID.

nodes.name: removeBlock
nodes.summary: Removes a block metadata entry and its reverse-index entries and releases the write lock; the caller must hold the write lock, otherwise an internal error is thrown. Wakes any threads waiting on the block.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Deletes all state at shutdown: resets any lockable block, wakes waiters and clears the block table, reverse indexes, lock bookkeeping and invisible-block set.

nodes.name: getBlockIdsFromMapping
nodes.summary: Looks up a key in one of the reverse-index maps and returns its block ids as a Seq, or an empty Seq.

nodes.name: addToMapping
nodes.summary: Adds a block id to the RDD, broadcast or cache-session reverse index depending on its BlockId type; other block types are ignored.

nodes.name: removeFromMapping
nodes.summary: Removes a block id from the matching reverse index and drops the index entry when its set becomes empty.

nodes.name: DiskStore.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DiskStore, which writes and reads BlockManager blocks as files located through DiskBlockManager, together with the BlockData implementations (DiskBlockData, EncryptedBlockData) and helper channel/buffer classes. This is the disk side of MEMORY_AND_DISK and DISK_ONLY persistence, including partitions evicted from memory.

nodes.name: DiskStore
nodes.summary: Stores each block as one file obtained from DiskBlockManager.getFile, tracking block sizes in a map; supports put via a write callback, getBytes (returning memory-mappable or encrypted BlockData), remove and moveFileToBlock. Files can be made world readable when the shuffle service may serve cached RDD blocks.

nodes.name: DiskBlockData
nodes.summary: BlockData over an unencrypted block file: small blocks are read into a heap buffer, larger ones memory-mapped read-only, and bigger-than-limit blocks are read in chunks; also exposes an InputStream and a Netty DefaultFileRegion for zero-copy sends.

nodes.name: EncryptedBlockData
nodes.summary: BlockData over an encrypted block file (spark.io.encryption): every read goes through a decrypting channel, so it cannot be memory-mapped and instead streams or copies data into chunked buffers.

nodes.name: EncryptedManagedBuffer
nodes.summary: ManagedBuffer wrapper around EncryptedBlockData that reports the decrypted size and delegates NIO, Netty and input-stream access to it, used when serving encrypted blocks to remote readers.

nodes.name: ReadableChannelFileRegion
nodes.summary: Netty FileRegion that pulls decrypted bytes from a ReadableByteChannel through a 64 KiB direct buffer so encrypted blocks can be sent over the network.

nodes.name: CountingWritableChannel
nodes.summary: WritableByteChannel decorator that counts bytes written, used by DiskStore.put to record the block size.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Writes a block to its file through a caller-supplied write function: deletes any stale file, optionally creates the file world readable, writes through a counting (and possibly encrypting) channel, records the byte count as block size, and removes the file if writing fails.

nodes.name: putBytes
nodes.summary: Writes a ChunkedByteBuffer to disk as a block by calling put with a channel write.

nodes.name: getBytes
nodes.summary: Returns BlockData for a block (or for an explicit file and size): an EncryptedBlockData when an IO encryption key is configured, otherwise a DiskBlockData. Overloaded for BlockId and (File, size).

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Forgets the recorded block size and deletes the block file, logging a warning if deletion fails; returns whether a file was deleted.

nodes.name: moveFileToBlock
nodes.summary: Records the size for a target block and moves an existing (for example downloaded temp) file to the location of that block in the disk store.

nodes.name: openForWrite
nodes.summary: Opens a FileChannel for the block file and wraps it with an encrypting channel when an IO encryption key exists, deleting the file and closing on failure.

nodes.name: toChunkedByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Reads the whole file into a ChunkedByteBuffer in chunks no larger than the memory-map limit.

nodes.name: toByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Returns a single ByteBuffer for the block, reading small files directly and memory-mapping larger ones; requires the block to be below the maximum memory-map size.

nodes.name: toChunkedByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Decrypts the block file into a ChunkedByteBuffer in chunks bounded by the maximum rounded array length.

nodes.name: toByteBuffer
nodes.summary: Decrypts the whole block into one heap ByteBuffer (used for replication), asserting that it fits in a Java array.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Opens the block file as a decrypting ReadableByteChannel, closing the raw channel if setting up decryption fails.

nodes.name: transferTo
nodes.summary: Copies data from the source channel through the direct buffer into the target channel until a write transfers nothing, tracking the transferred byte count.

nodes.name: DiskBlockManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines DiskBlockManager, which maps block ids to files under the blockmgr-* directories created inside spark.local.dir (or SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS), hashing file names into sub-directories. It also creates temp block files, lists stored blocks, prepares merge directories for push-based shuffle and deletes the directories on stop.

nodes.name: DiskBlockManager
