nodes.summary: Creates one blockmgr directory per configured local dir and maps each block to one file whose name is the BlockId name, placed in a two-hex-digit sub-directory chosen by hashing the name. Used for cached RDD disk blocks, shuffle data/index files and temp files; directories are deleted on stop unless the external shuffle service is used.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object (lines 384-388) shares this node id and holds the merge-directory constants merge_manager, mergeDir and attemptId.

nodes.name: getFile
nodes.summary: Locates the file for a name: hash modulo number of local dirs picks the directory, (hash / dirs) modulo spark.diskStore.subDirectories picks the sub-directory (named as two hex digits), creating it lazily with group-write permission when the shuffle service needs deletion rights. An overload at line 128 accepts a BlockId.

nodes.name: getMergedShuffleFile
nodes.summary: Resolves the file of a push-based-shuffle merged data, index or meta block under the externally created merge directories, throwing for any other block type. A private overload (lines 149-155) builds the path via ExecutorDiskUtils.

nodes.name: containsBlock
nodes.summary: Returns true if the file that corresponds to the block id exists on disk.

nodes.name: getAllFiles
nodes.summary: Lists every file in the created sub-directories, copying the sub-directory array under its lock because other threads may modify it.

nodes.name: getAllBlocks
nodes.summary: Lists the BlockIds of all files on disk by parsing file names, skipping files (such as SortShuffleWriter temp files) that are not valid block ids.

nodes.name: createWorldReadableFile
nodes.summary: Creates the file and adds OTHERS_READ permission so the shuffle service can read it in secure YARN setups where sub-directories lose the setgid bit (SPARK-37618).

nodes.name: createTempFileWith
nodes.summary: Creates a temporary sibling of a given file (world readable if permission changing is required) so a block file can be written then renamed into place.

nodes.name: createTempLocalBlock
nodes.summary: Generates a unique TempLocalBlockId (random UUID, retried on collision) and returns it with its file path for local intermediate results.

nodes.name: createTempShuffleBlock
nodes.summary: Generates a unique TempShuffleBlockId (random UUID) with a file for intermediate shuffle output, making it world readable when needed.

nodes.name: createLocalDirs
nodes.summary: Creates a blockmgr directory under each configured local dir, ignoring directories that cannot be created; these are the roots under which block and shuffle files appear.

nodes.name: createLocalDirsForMergedShuffleBlocks
nodes.summary: When push-based shuffle is enabled, creates the merge_manager directory and its hex sub-directories in each configured local dir if missing, since the shuffle service cannot create them.

nodes.name: createDirWithPermission770
nodes.summary: Creates a directory with rwxrwx--- permissions, retrying up to the maximum attempts, so the shuffle server can create files inside the merge folder.

nodes.name: getMergeDirectoryAndAttemptIDJsonString
nodes.summary: Serializes the merge directory name and application attempt id into a JSON string, used when registering the executor with the external shuffle service.

nodes.name: addShutdownHook
nodes.summary: Registers a shutdown hook (just after temp dir cleanup priority) that calls doStop so the local directories are cleaned on JVM exit.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Removes the shutdown hook and cleans up local dirs by calling doStop.

nodes.name: doStop
nodes.summary: When deleteFilesOnStop is set, recursively deletes every local blockmgr directory unless it is already a shutdown-delete root.

nodes.name: CacheManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CacheManager, the per-SharedState registry behind df.cache() / CACHE TABLE, plus the CachedData entry type. It stores (normalized logical plan, InMemoryRelation) pairs and later rewrites any query plan whose fragments match a cached plan so they read the cached columnar data instead of recomputing.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala. The class is guarded by this.synchronized around an immutable IndexedSeq held in a @volatile var; reads are lock-free.

nodes.name: CachedData
nodes.summary: Case class pairing a normalized resolved logical plan (the cache key) with the InMemoryRelation that holds the cached data.

nodes.name: CacheManager
nodes.summary: Registry of cached plans used by Spark SQL. Public APIs accept analyzed plans or Datasets, normalize them via QueryExecution.normalize, and use plan.sameResult (canonicalized plan comparison) to find a match. Cache entries are InMemoryRelations whose data is built lazily by their CachedRDDBuilder. The companion object only provides logCacheOperation, which logs at the configured dataframe cache log level.

nodes.name: clearCache
nodes.summary: Drops every cached entry: clears each entry's CachedRDDBuilder (which unpersists its RDD) and resets the entry list.

nodes.name: cacheQuery
nodes.summary: Overloads that register a Dataset or a LogicalPlan for caching with an optional table name and StorageLevel. Both normalize the plan and delegate to cacheQueryInternal, using the normalized plan as the cache key. Dataset.persist (df.cache()) and CACHE TABLE reach it through the shared CacheManager.

nodes.name: cacheQueryInternal
nodes.summary: Adds a plan to the cache unless the storage level is NONE, the plan is a Command, or an equivalent plan is already cached. Otherwise it plans the query in a session clone with some configs off (auto bucketed scan, and optionally AQE final-stage shuffle optimizations), builds an InMemoryRelation from the QueryExecution without running a job, and prepends a CachedData entry under synchronization (with a re-check for races).

nodes.name: uncacheQuery
nodes.summary: Overloads (Dataset or LogicalPlan, optional blocking flag) that remove a cached plan, backing df.unpersist(). They normalize the plan and delegate to uncacheQueryInternal; with cascade=true, every cached entry that refers to the plan is removed too.

nodes.name: uncacheQueryInternal
nodes.summary: Uncaches entries whose plan sameResult the given normalized plan by delegating to uncacheByCondition.

nodes.name: uncacheTableOrView
nodes.summary: Uncaches all entries that refer to a table or view identified by a name (used by UNCACHE TABLE / catalog operations), including time-travel variants.

nodes.name: isMatchedTableOrView
nodes.summary: Decides whether a plan node is a given table or view: strips subquery aliases and compares names for v1 LogicalRelation with catalog table, DataSourceV2Relation, View, and HiveTableRelation using the session resolver.

nodes.name: uncacheByCondition
nodes.summary: Core removal routine: removes cached entries whose plan matches the predicate (or contains a match when cascading), clears their builders, and, for non-cascade removals, recaches dependent entries whose buffers were not yet loaded so they stop depending on the removed plan.

nodes.name: analyzeColumnCacheQuery
nodes.summary: Computes column statistics for a cached relation with CommandUtils.computeColumnStats and stores them via InMemoryRelation.updateStats.

nodes.name: recacheByPlan
nodes.summary: Re-caches every entry whose plan contains a subplan with the same result as the given normalized plan.

nodes.name: recacheTableOrView
nodes.summary: Re-caches all entries that reference the given table or view name, used to invalidate stale caches after table changes.

nodes.name: recacheByCondition
nodes.summary: Removes entries matching the condition, clears their cached buffers, and tries to rebuild each one through tryRebuildCacheEntry, re-inserting rebuilt entries unless an equivalent one appeared meanwhile.

nodes.name: tryRebuildCacheEntry
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a cache entry from a refreshed plan: re-plans it in a config-off session clone and creates a new InMemoryRelation that reuses the old CachedRDDBuilder settings, with a new normalized plan as key.

nodes.name: tryRefreshPlan
nodes.summary: Attempts to refresh V2 table metadata for a cached plan (reloading the table through its catalog and keeping the relation only if the table id still matches); returns None on failure.

nodes.name: lookupCachedTable
nodes.summary: Finds a cached V2 relation by table name for relation-level cache hits, logging a hit when found.

nodes.name: findCachedRelations
nodes.summary: Scans cached entries for V2 relations (without time travel) whose catalog and identifier match the given name.

nodes.name: lookupCachedData
nodes.summary: Public lookup overloads returning the CachedData for a Dataset or LogicalPlan, after normalizing the plan.

nodes.name: lookupCachedDataInternal
nodes.summary: Finds the first cached entry for which plan.sameResult(cd.plan) holds and an optional canUse predicate accepts it. sameResult compares canonicalized plans, so differently written but equivalent queries hit the same entry.

nodes.name: validateCachedEntryForTransaction
nodes.summary: Checks whether a cache entry may be used inside a catalog transaction by collecting its V2 batch scans on the transaction's catalog tables and asking the transaction to register them.

nodes.name: useCachedData
nodes.summary: Rewrites a normalized logical plan top-down: each non-Command fragment that matches a cache entry is replaced by the cached InMemoryRelation (with the fragment's output attributes and original hints), and subquery plans are rewritten recursively. It logs cache hit or miss. A second overload adds a transaction validity check. QueryExecution.withCachedData calls this, which is how later queries read the cache.

nodes.name: recacheByPath
nodes.summary: Overloads that re-cache entries containing a given file path in a HadoopFsRelation or FileTable; qualifies the path with its FileSystem and delegates to recacheByCondition (used by REFRESH of paths).

nodes.name: lookupAndRefresh
nodes.summary: For a LogicalRelation over a HadoopFsRelation or a V2 FileTable, refreshes its FileIndex if the path overlaps and reports whether it did.

nodes.name: refreshFileIndexIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Refreshes a FileIndex when one of its root paths lies under the given qualified path.

nodes.name: isSubDir
nodes.summary: Returns true when a child path is the same as or beneath a parent path, by walking up the child's ancestors.

nodes.name: getOrCloneSessionWithConfigsOff
nodes.summary: Returns a session clone used to plan cached queries: auto bucketed scan is always disabled, and AQE final-stage shuffle optimizations are disabled unless CAN_CHANGE_CACHED_PLAN_OUTPUT_PARTITIONING is set, to avoid extra shuffles in cached plans.

nodes.name: InMemoryRelation.scala
nodes.summary: Holds the columnar in-memory cache representation: InMemoryRelation (the logical leaf node that replaces cached plans), CachedRDDBuilder (lazily builds and persists the RDD of compressed column batches) and DefaultCachedBatch plus its serializer (row-to-columnar-buffer conversion with per-batch column stats). CachedBatch and the CachedBatchSerializer trait live in org.apache.spark.sql.columnar, not here.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala. Companion object InMemoryRelation shares the class id with the case class InMemoryRelation.

nodes.name: DefaultCachedBatch
nodes.summary: Default CachedBatch: number of rows, an array of per-column serialized (and optionally compressed) byte buffers, and an InternalRow of column statistics used for batch pruning. Kryo-serializable through DefaultCachedBatchKryoSerializer.

nodes.name: DefaultCachedBatchKryoSerializer
nodes.summary: Kryo serializer for DefaultCachedBatch that writes numRows, the length-prefixed column buffers, and the stats row, and validates against null buffers.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes a DefaultCachedBatch to Kryo output: row count, buffer count (+1 to mark non-null), each buffer length and bytes, then the stats object.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Reads a DefaultCachedBatch back from Kryo input, mirroring write and rejecting null-marked buffers.

nodes.name: DefaultCachedBatchSerializer
nodes.summary: The default CachedBatchSerializer (configured through spark.sql.cache.serializer). It converts rows into DefaultCachedBatch objects of per-column compressed buffers, and converts them back into ColumnarBatch (primitive types only) or InternalRow (via generated column accessors), and exposes batch statistics for pruning through SimpleMetricsCachedBatchSerializer.

nodes.name: convertInternalRowToCachedBatch
nodes.summary: Entry point for caching rows: reads columnBatchSize and compression settings from SQLConf and delegates to convertForCacheInternal.

nodes.name: convertForCacheInternal
nodes.summary: Per partition, groups input rows into batches (up to batchSize rows or a maximum byte size), appending each row's fields to one ColumnBuilder per attribute, then emits a DefaultCachedBatch of column byte buffers plus the collected column statistics row.

nodes.name: supportsColumnarOutput
nodes.summary: Reports that columnar read-back is supported only when all fields are boolean, byte, short, int, long, float or double.

nodes.name: vectorTypes
nodes.summary: Returns the column vector class name (on-heap or off-heap depending on SQLConf) for each attribute.

nodes.name: convertCachedBatchToColumnarBatch
nodes.summary: Turns cached batches into ColumnarBatch objects: allocates on-heap or off-heap column vectors for the selected attributes, decompresses the matching column buffers (matched by exprId), and closes the batch on task completion.

nodes.name: convertCachedBatchToInternalRow
nodes.summary: Turns cached batches into InternalRow iterators for the requested columns using generated column accessor code (GenerateColumnAccessor), mapping user-defined types to their sqlType.

nodes.name: CachedRDDBuilder
nodes.summary: Builds and owns the cached data of one cache entry. cachedColumnBuffers lazily creates an RDD of CachedBatch from the physical plan with the serializer and persists it at the requested StorageLevel; a partition-keyed accumulator records per-partition row count and size, which feed cache statistics and the 'loaded' check used by AQE.

nodes.name: cachedColumnBuffers
nodes.summary: Synchronized lazy accessor: on first use calls buildBuffers to create the persisted RDD of CachedBatch, and returns it afterwards. The data is only materialized into storage when an action computes it.

nodes.name: clearCache
nodes.summary: Unpersists the cached RDD (optionally blocking), drops the reference, and resets the loaded flag and accumulator bookkeeping so a rebuild starts fresh.

nodes.name: isCachedColumnBuffersLoaded
nodes.summary: Synchronized, non-locking-style status test: true if the RDD exists and all of its partitions have been materialized.

nodes.name: isCachedRDDLoaded
nodes.summary: Latches 'loaded' once the number of distinct materialized partitions in the accumulator equals the RDD partition count, so statistics are exact before AQE relies on them.

nodes.name: materializedRowCount
nodes.summary: Sums the de-duplicated per-partition row counts recorded in the accumulator.

nodes.name: buildBuffers
nodes.summary: Creates the cached RDD: runs the plan columnar or row-based through the CachedBatchSerializer, wraps each partition to tally rows and bytes into the partition-keyed accumulator on successful task completion, then persist(storageLevel) and names the RDD. If an AQE plan fails, it recaches the plan to avoid a negative cache.

nodes.name: InMemoryRelation
nodes.summary: Logical leaf node standing in for a cached plan. It holds the output attributes, the CachedRDDBuilder, and the output ordering of the cached plan, keeps estimated statistics (replaced by exact materialized size and row count once loaded), and exposes PartitionStatistics for batch pruning. The planner turns it into an InMemoryTableScanExec; its canonical form normalizes output attributes so equivalent plans match.

nodes.name: getSerializer
nodes.summary: Lazily instantiates the process-wide CachedBatchSerializer from the class named by StaticSQLConf.SPARK_CACHE_SERIALIZER via reflection, caching the instance.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Factory overloads. The main one takes a StorageLevel, a QueryExecution and table name: it takes the optimized plan, picks the serializer, uses the executed plan (converted to columnar if the serializer supports columnar input) as cached plan, creates a CachedRDDBuilder, and records the optimized plan's statistics. Other overloads rebuild a relation from an existing builder or from explicit fields.

nodes.name: doCanonicalize
nodes.summary: Canonical form used by plan.sameResult: re-expresses output attributes with normalized expression ids so cache lookup ignores attribute id differences.

nodes.name: updateStats
nodes.summary: Synchronized update of the estimated statistics with a new row count and column statistics (from ANALYZE on a cached plan).

nodes.name: computeStats
nodes.summary: Returns the estimated statistics of the plan to cache while the buffers are not loaded, and exact materialized size and row count afterwards.

nodes.name: withOutput
nodes.summary: Copies the relation with new output attributes (remapping output ordering), sharing the same CachedRDDBuilder; used when a cache hit replaces a plan fragment.

nodes.name: newInstance
nodes.summary: MultiInstanceRelation hook: returns a copy with fresh attribute ids but the same builder, so self-joins on a cached plan are unambiguous.

nodes.name: ShuffledRowRDD.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ShuffledRowRDD, the RDD that SQL shuffle exchanges use to read rows on the reduce side, together with the ShufflePartitionSpec family describing which reducer or mapper ranges one task reads. Adaptive query execution produces these specs to coalesce small shuffle partitions, split skewed ones, or read locally.

nodes.name: ShufflePartitionSpec
nodes.summary: Sealed trait for the description of one post-shuffle partition; implemented by the four spec case classes in this file.

nodes.name: CoalescedPartitionSpec
nodes.summary: Spec for a task that reads reducers in the range [startReducerIndex, endReducerIndex), used for the default one-reducer-per-task read and for AQE coalescing of small shuffle partitions. The companion offers an overload taking a long data size.

nodes.name: PartialReducerPartitionSpec
nodes.summary: Spec for a task that reads a single reducer but only the map outputs in [startMapIndex, endMapIndex); AQE uses it to split a skewed reducer partition into several tasks.

nodes.name: PartialMapperPartitionSpec
nodes.summary: Spec for a task that reads a range of reducers [startReducerIndex, endReducerIndex) from one mapper's output only; used for local shuffle reads.

nodes.name: CoalescedMapperPartitionSpec
nodes.summary: Spec for a task that reads all numReducers reducers from a contiguous range of mappers [startMapIndex, endMapIndex).

nodes.name: ShuffledRowRDDPartition
nodes.summary: Spark Partition implementation for ShuffledRowRDD that carries its index and the ShufflePartitionSpec to read.

nodes.name: CoalescedPartitioner
nodes.summary: Partitioner that groups consecutive partitions of a parent partitioner into fewer output partitions given partitionStartIndices; lets coalesced shuffle reads keep a known output partitioner.

nodes.name: ShuffledRowRDD
nodes.summary: RDD[InternalRow] specialized from ShuffledRDD for shuffling rows. It takes a ShuffleDependency, SQL metrics, and an array of ShufflePartitionSpec (default: one CoalescedPartitionSpec per reducer); each partition's compute reads the right shuffle blocks via the ShuffleManager and returns only the row values.

nodes.name: partitioner
nodes.summary: Exposes a CoalescedPartitioner only when every spec is a CoalescedPartitionSpec with distinct start indices; otherwise no partitioner is known.

nodes.name: getPreferredLocations
nodes.summary: Chooses preferred hosts per spec: for coalesced reducer ranges, asks MapOutputTrackerMaster for preferred shuffle locations of each reducer; for map-range specs, uses the locations of the relevant map outputs.

nodes.name: compute
nodes.summary: Reads a post-shuffle partition: matches on the spec type, calls SparkEnv.get.shuffleManager.getReader with the right (map range, reducer range) arguments and a SQLShuffleReadMetricsReporter, then returns the value part of each (key, row) pair.

nodes.name: SortExec.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SortExec, the physical operator that sorts rows within each partition (or globally, when preceded by a range-partitioning shuffle) using Spark's UnsafeExternalRowSorter, which spills to disk when memory is short. It supports both the plain RDD path and whole-stage code generation.

nodes.name: SortExec
nodes.summary: Unary physical operator performing (external) sorting. 'global' makes it require an OrderedDistribution (range partitioned child); otherwise each partition is sorted independently and the child's partitioning is kept. Rows are fed into an UnsafeExternalRowSorter configured with a binary-comparable prefix (with optional radix sort), and metrics report sort time, peak memory and spill size. testSpillFrequency forces periodic spilling in tests.

nodes.name: requiredChildDistribution
nodes.summary: Requires OrderedDistribution on the sort order for global sorts, otherwise no distribution requirement.

nodes.name: createSorter
nodes.summary: Builds the UnsafeExternalRowSorter: row ordering from the sort order, a prefix comparator and prefix computer from the first sort key, radix sort when enabled and a single fully prefix-sortable key, the memory page size from SparkEnv's memory manager, and optional test spill frequency. Called by both doExecute and generated code, and stores the sorter in rowSorter.

nodes.name: doExecute
nodes.summary: Non-codegen path: for each partition of the child's RDD creates a sorter, feeds the iterator through sorter.sort, and updates sortTime, peakMemory and spillSize metrics (spill size from the task's memoryBytesSpilled delta) before returning the sorted iterator.

nodes.name: doProduce
nodes.summary: Codegen producer: emits code that, on the first call, drains the child's produced rows into the sorter via insertRow, sorts, records metrics, and then streams the sorted rows to the parent operator, honoring limit and shouldStop.

nodes.name: doConsume
nodes.summary: Codegen consumer: inserts each incoming UnsafeRow into the sorter.

nodes.name: cleanupResources
nodes.summary: Closes the UnsafeExternalRowSorter if one was created (it may be null for empty partitions) before calling the superclass cleanup.

nodes.name: StateStoreCoordinator.scala
nodes.summary: Implements the driver-side StateStoreCoordinator RPC endpoint and its client handle StateStoreCoordinatorRef for streaming state stores. The coordinator tracks which executor holds each active state store provider (for task locality and to unload duplicate providers), tracks per-batch commit completeness, and watches for state stores lagging in snapshot uploads.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala. Messages are private case classes in a sealed trait, and the endpoint is a ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint so handlers run serially without locks.

nodes.name: StateStoreCoordinatorMessage
nodes.summary: Private sealed trait that all messages to the StateStoreCoordinator extend.

nodes.name: ReportActiveInstance
nodes.summary: Message from an executor reporting that a state store provider is active there; also lists other loaded providers so the coordinator can return those now active elsewhere for unloading.

nodes.name: ReportActiveInstanceResponse
nodes.summary: Reply to ReportActiveInstance: whether the provider should force a snapshot upload on its next commit, and the provider ids the executor should unload.

nodes.name: VerifyIfInstanceActive
nodes.summary: Message asking whether a given executor still holds the active instance of a state store provider.

nodes.name: GetLocation
nodes.summary: Message asking the coordinator for the executor location of a state store provider.

nodes.name: ReportStateStoreCommit
nodes.summary: Message reporting that a state store version has committed, for per-batch commit tracking.

nodes.name: StartStateStoreCommitTrackingForBatch
nodes.summary: Message that starts tracking commits for a (runId, batchId) with the expected operator, store name and partition counts.

nodes.name: ValidateStateStoreCommitForBatch
nodes.summary: Message asking the coordinator to verify that every expected state store committed for a batch.

nodes.name: DeactivateInstances
nodes.summary: Message that removes all state store instances and tracking data for a query run id.

nodes.name: ReportSnapshotUploaded
nodes.summary: Message reporting that a provider finished uploading a snapshot, with version and timestamp.

nodes.name: LogLaggingStateStores
nodes.summary: Message asking the coordinator to detect and log state stores lagging behind in snapshot uploads for a query run.

nodes.name: StateStoreCoordinatorRef
nodes.summary: Client handle wrapping an RpcEndpointRef to the coordinator. The companion factories create the endpoint on the driver (or reuse an existing one) and look it up from executors; the instance methods send the typed messages with askSync, including reportActiveInstance, verifyIfInstanceActive, getLocation, deactivateInstances, commit tracking and snapshot lag reporting.

nodes.name: forDriver
nodes.summary: Companion factory for the driver: creates a StateStoreCoordinator and registers it as the 'StateStoreCoordinator' RPC endpoint; if the endpoint already exists, retrieves a ref to it.

nodes.name: forExecutor
nodes.summary: Companion factory for executors: looks up the driver's existing StateStoreCoordinator endpoint.

nodes.name: reportActiveInstance
nodes.summary: Tells the coordinator that a provider is active on a host and executor, passing other loaded providers; returns which providers to unload and whether to force a snapshot upload.

nodes.name: verifyIfInstanceActive
nodes.summary: Asks the coordinator whether the given executor holds the active instance of the provider.

nodes.name: getLocation
nodes.summary: Asks the coordinator for the preferred executor location of a state store provider, used to schedule tasks near loaded state.

nodes.name: deactivateInstances
nodes.summary: Tells the coordinator to forget all state store instances and tracking data for a query run when it terminates.

nodes.name: snapshotUploaded
nodes.summary: Notifies the coordinator that a state store finished uploading a snapshot (provider id, version, timestamp).

nodes.name: logLaggingStateStores
nodes.summary: Asks the coordinator to log state stores that are lagging in snapshot uploads for a query run.

nodes.name: startStateStoreCommitTrackingForBatch
nodes.summary: Starts commit tracking for a batch with the expected number of stores per operator and store name.

nodes.name: reportStateStoreCommit
nodes.summary: Reports a committed state store version (and store name) to the coordinator.

nodes.name: validateStateStoreCommitForBatch
nodes.summary: Asks the coordinator to validate that all expected stores committed for a batch; fails if some are missing.

nodes.name: StateStoreCoordinator
nodes.summary: Private ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint running on the driver. It keeps maps of active provider locations, the latest uploaded snapshot per store, lagging stores per run, and batch commit trackers, and answers each message in receiveAndReply.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Message dispatcher: records active instances and returns providers to unload; answers active-instance and location queries; deactivates run state; records snapshot uploads and logs lagging stores; starts, records and validates per-batch commit tracking; serves testing messages; and stops the endpoint.

nodes.name: shouldForceSnapshotUploadForProvider
nodes.summary: True when force-upload-on-lag is configured and the provider is in its run's set of lagging stores.

nodes.name: findLaggingStores
nodes.summary: Finds a run's active providers that are behind in both snapshot version and time, using configured multipliers of the minimum deltas for snapshot and the maintenance interval; terminating triggers skip the time check.

nodes.name: BatchCommitTracker
nodes.summary: Tracks which (operator, partition, store name) triples committed in a batch and validates against the expected counts, throwing a commit validation failure that lists missing commits.

nodes.name: recordCommit
nodes.summary: Records that a given store partition committed.

nodes.name: validateAllCommitted
nodes.summary: Checks every expected (operator, partition, store name) commit is present and throws a StateStoreCommitValidationFailed error that lists the missing ones.

nodes.name: SnapshotUploadEvent
nodes.summary: Value type holding the version and timestamp of a snapshot upload, ordered by version then timestamp, used to sort lagging stores.

nodes.name: MemoryConsumer.java
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for any Tungsten memory user inside a task that can be forced to spill. It wraps TaskMemoryManager to acquire and free execution memory, allocate LongArrays and pages, and keeps a running count of bytes used.
nodes.languageNotes: Java abstract class. Only Tungsten-managed memory (on-heap long[] pages or off-heap pages) is allocated and spilled through it.

nodes.name: TaskMemoryManager.java
nodes.summary: Per-task memory manager that sits between operators and the executor-wide MemoryManager. It hands out Tungsten pages, encodes record pointers as 64-bit longs, and asks other consumers in the same task to spill when memory runs short.
nodes.languageNotes: Java. Uses a 13-bit page number plus 51-bit offset layout so one long can address on-heap and off-heap records.

nodes.name: UnsafeExternalSorter.java
nodes.summary: External sorter built on UnsafeInMemorySorter. It stores serialized records in Tungsten pages, spills sorted runs to disk when memory is short or thresholds are crossed, and merges spill files plus the in-memory data on read.
nodes.languageNotes: Java. Both the sorter and its SpillableIterator synchronize carefully and free pages outside their locks to avoid deadlocks with TaskMemoryManager.

nodes.name: MemoryConsumer
nodes.summary: A spillable consumer of TaskMemoryManager memory. Subclasses implement spill(size, trigger) to release Tungsten pages (for example to disk) when the task manager asks, and the base class tracks bytes held in the atomic used counter.

nodes.name: getUsed
nodes.summary: Returns how many bytes this consumer currently holds, read from the atomic used counter. TaskMemoryManager reads it to rank consumers for spilling.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that TaskMemoryManager calls when the task needs memory; implementations release up to the requested size and return the bytes freed. The no-arg spill() overload forces a full spill by calling spill(Long.MAX_VALUE, this). Implementations must not call acquireMemory from inside spill to avoid deadlock.

nodes.name: allocateArray
nodes.summary: Allocates a LongArray of the given number of longs (size * 8 bytes) as one page from TaskMemoryManager and adds it to used. Throws SparkOutOfMemoryError or TooLargePageException to the caller, typically for sorter pointer arrays.

nodes.name: freeArray
nodes.summary: Frees a LongArray by freeing its backing memory block through freePage.

nodes.name: allocatePage
nodes.summary: Asks TaskMemoryManager for a page of at least the required size (never smaller than the consumer's page size) and adds the real page size to used. If the page is missing or too small it calls throwOom.

nodes.name: freePage
nodes.summary: Subtracts the page size from used and returns the page to TaskMemoryManager.

nodes.name: acquireMemory
nodes.summary: Requests execution memory from TaskMemoryManager, which may spill other consumers, and adds the granted bytes to used. The grant can be smaller than requested.

nodes.name: freeMemory
nodes.summary: Releases N bytes of execution memory back to TaskMemoryManager and decreases used.

nodes.name: throwOom
nodes.summary: Failure path for page allocation: frees any partially obtained page, logs memory usage of all consumers, and throws an out-of-memory error stating the required and obtained sizes.

nodes.name: TaskMemoryManager
nodes.summary: Manages all Tungsten memory for one task attempt: it owns the 8192-entry page table, tracks registered MemoryConsumers, and delegates the actual pool accounting to MemoryManager. Its main job is to encode a page number and offset into a single 64-bit long so records can be addressed identically on-heap and off-heap.

nodes.name: acquireExecutionMemory
nodes.summary: Requests execution memory for a consumer. If MemoryManager grants less than required, it builds a TreeMap of same-mode consumers keyed by usage (the requester counts as 0), then repeatedly spills the smallest consumer holding at least the missing amount, else the biggest, until the need is met or no consumer is left. This is how tasks on one executor force their own operators to spill; it also updates current and peak on-heap or off-heap counters.

nodes.name: trySpillAndAcquire
nodes.summary: Calls spill() on one chosen consumer and then re-acquires the memory it freed from MemoryManager (another task may grab some, so the loop retries). A consumer that frees nothing is removed from the list; an IOException becomes SparkOutOfMemoryError, while interruption becomes a RuntimeException.

nodes.name: releaseExecutionMemory
nodes.summary: Gives N bytes of execution memory back to MemoryManager for this task attempt and lowers the on-heap or off-heap current usage counter for the consumer's mode.

nodes.name: showMemoryUsage
nodes.summary: Logs how much each consumer holds, how much task memory is not tied to any consumer, and overall execution, storage and unmanaged memory totals. Used when an allocation fails.

nodes.name: allocatePage
nodes.summary: Allocates a Tungsten page (the public two-argument overload starts it with retryCount 0). It rejects sizes above MAXIMUM_PAGE_SIZE_BYTES, acquires execution memory, picks the first free slot in the 8192-entry bitmap, and asks the Tungsten memory allocator for the block (on-heap or off-heap by mode). On a real OutOfMemoryError it keeps the memory as acquiredButNotUsed and retries, which can trigger spilling.

nodes.name: freePage
nodes.summary: Frees a page obtained from allocatePage: asserts it is a live managed page, clears its page table entry and bitmap bit, marks it freed, returns it to the allocator and releases its execution memory.

nodes.name: encodePageNumberAndOffset
nodes.summary: Turns a page plus offset into a 64-bit address: the page number goes in the upper 13 bits and the offset in the lower 51 bits. For off-heap mode the absolute address is first made relative to the page base. A static int/long overload (lines 474-477) does the bit packing.

nodes.name: decodePageNumber
nodes.summary: Extracts the page number from an encoded address by shifting right 51 bits.

nodes.name: decodeOffset
nodes.summary: Extracts the offset from an encoded address by masking the lower 51 bits.

nodes.name: getPage
nodes.summary: Returns the base object for an encoded address by looking up its page table entry in on-heap mode; in off-heap mode it returns null because addresses are raw.

nodes.name: getOffsetInPage
nodes.summary: Returns the usable offset for an encoded address. On-heap it is the stored offset; off-heap it adds the page's base address back to the relative offset that encodePageNumberAndOffset removed.

nodes.name: cleanUpAllAllocatedMemory
nodes.summary: End-of-task cleanup: logs leaked consumer memory, frees every page still in the page table, releases memory acquired but not used, and releases all execution memory of the task. A non-zero return value indicates a memory leak.

nodes.name: getMemoryConsumptionForThisTask
nodes.summary: Returns the execution memory in bytes that MemoryManager currently attributes to this task attempt.

nodes.name: getTungstenMemoryMode
nodes.summary: Returns the Tungsten memory mode (ON_HEAP or OFF_HEAP) that this task uses for pages.

nodes.name: getPeakOnHeapExecutionMemory
nodes.summary: Returns the peak on-heap execution memory in bytes recorded for this task.

nodes.name: getPeakOffHeapExecutionMemory
nodes.summary: Returns the peak off-heap execution memory in bytes recorded for this task.

nodes.name: UnsafeExternalSorter
nodes.summary: Final MemoryConsumer that sorts serialized records stored in Tungsten pages through an UnsafeInMemorySorter of (address, key prefix) pairs. When memory cannot be obtained or a record-count or byte threshold is crossed it writes sorted runs to spill files, and getSortedIterator merges those runs with the remaining in-memory data.

nodes.name: BoundedMergerContext
nodes.summary: Small value holder returned by prepareBoundedMerge: a snapshot of the spill writers, the optional spillable in-memory iterator, and the bounded merger that will merge them.

nodes.name: SpillableIterator
nodes.summary: Sorted record iterator over the in-memory sorter that can itself be spilled. When another consumer asks for memory it writes the not-yet-read records to a spill file, frees pages and the in-memory sorter, and continues reading from the spill reader, keeping the page of the current record alive until the next loadNext.

nodes.name: ChainedIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator that concatenates several UnsafeSorterIterators (spill readers and the in-memory iterator) into one, summing their record counts; used by getIterator for insertion-order reads.

nodes.name: createWithExistingInMemorySorter
nodes.summary: Factory that wraps an already filled UnsafeInMemorySorter: it builds the sorter, spills everything to disk right away, adds the old memory use to the spill metrics, and drops the in-memory sorter.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Public static factory that builds an empty sorter with comparators, page size, spill thresholds and merge factor.

nodes.name: UnsafeExternalSorter
nodes.summary: Private constructor: registers with TaskMemoryManager in the Tungsten memory mode, creates or reuses the UnsafeInMemorySorter, fixes the spill file buffer at 32 KB, and adds a task completion listener that calls cleanupResources so memory is freed even if the output is not fully read.

nodes.name: closeCurrentPage
nodes.summary: Marks the current page as full by moving the cursor to its end, so the next record forces a new page or a spill.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: MemoryConsumer.spill override. If another consumer triggered it, it delegates to the active SpillableIterator or frees nothing; if this sorter triggered it, it writes the sorted in-memory records through UnsafeSorterSpillWriter, frees the data pages and the pointer array, and updates memory and disk spill metrics. It spills nothing when no record is inserted yet.

nodes.name: getMemoryUsage
nodes.summary: Returns total sorter memory: the in-memory sorter's pointer array plus all data pages.

nodes.name: updatePeakMemoryUsed
nodes.summary: Raises the recorded peak memory usage if the current usage is higher.

nodes.name: getPeakMemoryUsedBytes
nodes.summary: Returns the peak bytes used so far after refreshing it.

nodes.name: getSortTimeNanos
nodes.summary: Returns time spent sorting in memory: from the live in-memory sorter if present, else the total saved when it was released.

nodes.name: getSpillSize
nodes.summary: Returns the total number of bytes spilled to disk so far.

nodes.name: freeMemory
nodes.summary: Frees all data pages held by the sorter and returns how many bytes were freed.

nodes.name: clearAndGetAllocatedPagesToFree
nodes.summary: Clears the page list and returns it so callers free the pages outside their own lock, preventing nested locks with TaskMemoryManager.

nodes.name: deleteSpillFiles
nodes.summary: Deletes the files of all spill writers and logs an error if one cannot be removed.

nodes.name: cleanupResources
nodes.summary: Frees everything the sorter owns: spill files, bounded-merge intermediate files, data pages and the in-memory sorter. State changes happen under the lock but frees happen outside it.

nodes.name: growPointerArrayIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Ensures the in-memory sorter's pointer array has room for one more record. It tries to allocate an array of twice the used size (which may trigger a spill); if the array would not fit in one page it spills, and if a spill emptied the sorter it allocates only a fresh initial-size array.

nodes.name: acquireNewPageIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Allocates a new data page when none exists or the current page cannot hold the required bytes, and records it in the page list and the page-memory total.

nodes.name: allocateMemoryForRecordIfNecessary
nodes.summary: Two-step allocation for an upcoming record: grow the pointer array, get a data page, then grow the pointer array again because the page allocation may have spilled and freed the array.

nodes.name: insertRecord
nodes.summary: Inserts one record: spills first if the record-count or byte threshold is crossed, reserves space for the length plus bytes, copies the record into the current page, encodes its address with TaskMemoryManager, and registers address and key prefix in the in-memory sorter.

nodes.name: insertKVRecord
nodes.summary: Inserts a key-value record into a page laid out as record length, key length, key bytes, value bytes, then registers its encoded address and prefix in the in-memory sorter.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Merges another UnsafeExternalSorter into this one by spilling it, taking over its spill writers and spill byte count, and cleaning it up without deleting the transferred files.

nodes.name: getSortedIterator
nodes.summary: Returns the fully sorted output. With no spills it wraps the in-memory sorter in a SpillableIterator; with more spill files than the merge factor it uses a bounded multi-round merge; otherwise it opens all spill readers plus the in-memory iterator in one UnsafeSorterSpillMerger.

nodes.name: prepareBoundedMerge
nodes.summary: Prepares a bounded merge: snapshots the spill writers before the readingIterator is published, creates an UnsafeSorterBoundedSpillMerger, and wraps the in-memory data in a SpillableIterator. The ordering avoids duplicate records when another consumer spills concurrently.

nodes.name: spillIterator
nodes.summary: Writes every record from a sorted iterator, with its key prefix, to a spill writer and closes the writer.

nodes.name: getIterator
nodes.summary: Returns an iterator from startIndex in insertion order by chaining spill readers and the in-memory iterator; forced spilling is not supported for this iterator.

nodes.name: moveOver
nodes.summary: Advances an iterator a given number of steps and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException if it runs out.

nodes.name: spill
nodes.summary: Spills the remaining unread records of the sorted iterator to a new spill file and switches upstream to a reader on it. It frees every data page except the one holding the current record, frees the in-memory sorter, and adds the released bytes to the spill metrics, keeping lock regions short to avoid deadlock.

nodes.name: loadNext
nodes.summary: Reads the next record from upstream, remembers its base object, offset, length and prefix so it stays valid after a spill, and frees the last in-memory page once it is no longer needed.

nodes.name: hasNext
nodes.summary: Moves to the next non-empty iterator in the queue and reports whether any record remains.

nodes.name: loadNext
nodes.summary: Skips exhausted iterators and loads the next record from the current one.

nodes.name: close
nodes.summary: Closes the current and any queued iterators that are Closeable.

nodes.name: closeIfPossible
nodes.summary: Quietly closes an iterator if it implements Closeable.

nodes.name: MemoryPool.scala
nodes.summary: Defines MemoryPool, the abstract bookkeeping base for an adjustable-sized region of memory. It tracks pool size under the owning MemoryManager lock and leaves memoryUsed to subclasses; it is the common parent of the execution and storage pools.

nodes.name: MemoryPool
nodes.summary: Abstract pool of memory whose size can grow and shrink. It stores _poolSize guarded by a lock (the MemoryManager, typed as Object), exposes poolSize and memoryFree (size minus memoryUsed), and requires subclasses to define memoryUsed. Spark uses one pool per region and mode, for example on-heap execution and on-heap storage.

nodes.name: MemoryPool.memoryFree
nodes.summary: Returns free bytes in the pool as pool size minus memoryUsed, read under the shared lock.

nodes.name: MemoryPool.incrementPoolSize
nodes.summary: Grows the pool by delta bytes (delta must be non-negative). The unified manager uses it to hand borrowed bytes to the execution or storage pool.

nodes.name: MemoryPool.decrementPoolSize
nodes.summary: Shrinks the pool by delta bytes, requiring that delta fits in the pool and that the remaining size still covers memoryUsed, so a pool can only give away free memory.

nodes.name: ExecutionMemoryPool.scala
nodes.summary: Defines ExecutionMemoryPool, which shares an adjustable pool of execution memory (shuffles, joins, sorts, aggregations) among the active tasks of an executor. It lets each task reach at least 1/(2N) and at most 1/N of the pool, blocking a task with wait() until it can reach 1/(2N).

nodes.name: ExecutionMemoryPool
nodes.summary: Pool that tracks execution memory per task attempt in a map from taskAttemptId to bytes. With N active tasks every task can acquire at least 1/(2N) of the pool before it has to spill and at most 1/N; the active set is the map keys, and changes are signalled with notifyAll() and wait().

nodes.name: ExecutionMemoryPool.getMemoryUsageForTask
nodes.summary: Returns the execution memory in bytes currently held by one task attempt, or 0 if the task is unknown.

nodes.name: ExecutionMemoryPool.acquireMemory
nodes.summary: Grants a task up to numBytes of execution memory, or 0. Registers the task, then loops: calls maybeGrowPool, computes maxMemoryPerTask = computeMaxPoolSize/N and minMemoryPerTask = poolSize/(2N), grants min(request, maxPerTask minus current usage, free memory), and if that is less than requested while the task is still below 1/(2N) it logs and wait()s for other tasks to release memory.

nodes.name: ExecutionMemoryPool.releaseMemory
nodes.summary: Returns numBytes from a task to the pool (clamped with a warning if the task holds less), removes the task from the active set when its usage reaches zero, and calls notifyAll() so blocked acquirers re-check their share.

nodes.name: ExecutionMemoryPool.releaseAllMemoryForTask
nodes.summary: Frees everything a task holds and thereby marks it inactive, for example when the task ends; returns the number of bytes freed.

nodes.name: StorageMemoryPool.scala
nodes.summary: Defines StorageMemoryPool, the bookkeeping pool for cache (storage) memory. When a block does not fit it asks the MemoryStore to evict other blocks, and it can give up capacity back to execution through freeSpaceToShrinkPool.

nodes.name: StorageMemoryPool
nodes.summary: Pool tracking used storage memory (_memoryUsed). It holds a late-bound MemoryStore reference (set after construction) and uses it to evict cached blocks when acquiring memory or when execution wants to reclaim borrowed space.

nodes.name: StorageMemoryPool.memoryStore
nodes.summary: Returns the MemoryStore used to evict blocks; throws an internal error (category MEMORY) if it was not set yet.

nodes.name: StorageMemoryPool.acquireMemory
nodes.summary: Acquires bytes to cache a block: if bytes must be freed it calls memoryStore.evictBlocksToFreeSpace, then succeeds only if the requested bytes now fit in memoryFree, adding them to the used total. A two-argument overload (lines 68-71) computes the shortfall as numBytes minus memoryFree and delegates here.

nodes.name: StorageMemoryPool.releaseMemory
nodes.summary: Reduces used storage memory by size, resetting to zero with a warning if more is released than is used.

nodes.name: StorageMemoryPool.releaseAllMemory
nodes.summary: Resets used storage memory to zero.

nodes.name: StorageMemoryPool.freeSpaceToShrinkPool
nodes.summary: Frees spaceToFree bytes so the pool can shrink: first counts unused memory, then evicts blocks through the MemoryStore for the remainder. It does not shrink the pool itself; the caller (UnifiedMemoryManager) decrements the pool size by the returned amount.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract MemoryManager that decides how memory is shared between execution (shuffles, joins, sorts, aggregations) and storage (caching), one per JVM. It owns the on-heap and off-heap execution and storage pools, the Tungsten memory mode and the default page size.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala abstract class with @GuardedBy("this") pools and private[memory] methods meant to be called mainly by TaskMemoryManager and the pools.

nodes.name: MemoryManager
nodes.summary: Abstract base created with conf, numCores and initial on-heap storage and execution sizes. It builds four pools (on-heap and off-heap, execution and storage), splits spark.memory.offHeap.size by spark.memory.storageFraction, and leaves the borrowing policy (acquireStorageMemory, acquireExecutionMemory, maxOnHeapStorageMemory) to subclasses such as UnifiedMemoryManager.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.maxOnHeapStorageMemory
nodes.summary: Abstract: total on-heap bytes available for storage, which can change over time; in this model it equals memory not occupied by execution.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.setMemoryStore
nodes.summary: Hands the MemoryStore to the on-heap and off-heap storage pools so they can evict cached blocks; must be called after construction because of initialization ordering.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.acquireStorageMemory
nodes.summary: Abstract: acquire N bytes to cache a block in the given memory mode, evicting existing blocks if necessary; returns whether all bytes were granted.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.acquireUnrollMemory
nodes.summary: Abstract: acquire N bytes to unroll a block, evicting blocks if needed; lets subclasses treat unrolling differently from plain storage.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.acquireExecutionMemory
nodes.summary: Abstract: try to get up to numBytes of execution memory for a task attempt, returning the bytes obtained or 0. It may block so each task can ramp up to at least 1/(2N) of the pool (N active tasks) before being forced to spill.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.releaseExecutionMemory
nodes.summary: Releases numBytes of execution memory for a task from the on-heap or off-heap execution pool, depending on the memory mode.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.releaseAllExecutionMemoryForTask
nodes.summary: Releases all on-heap and off-heap execution memory of a task and marks it inactive (for example when the task ends); returns bytes freed.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.releaseStorageMemory
nodes.summary: Releases N bytes of storage memory from the on-heap or off-heap storage pool.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.releaseAllStorageMemory
nodes.summary: Releases all acquired storage memory in both the on-heap and off-heap storage pools.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.releaseUnrollMemory
nodes.summary: Releases unroll memory by delegating to releaseStorageMemory.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.executionMemoryUsed
nodes.summary: Total execution memory in use, summing the on-heap and off-heap execution pools.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.storageMemoryUsed
nodes.summary: Total storage memory in use, summing the on-heap and off-heap storage pools.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.tungstenMemoryMode
nodes.summary: Chooses ON_HEAP or OFF_HEAP for Tungsten managed memory. Off-heap requires spark.memory.offHeap.enabled with spark.memory.offHeap.size > 0 and a platform with unaligned Unsafe access; otherwise a require check fails with a message.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.defaultPageSizeBytes
nodes.summary: Computes the default page size: execution pool size for the Tungsten mode divided by cores and a safety factor of 16, rounded up to a power of 2 and clamped to 1MB..64MB; with G1, ZGC or Shenandoah on-heap it subtracts LONG_ARRAY_OFFSET (SPARK-37593).

nodes.name: MemoryManager.pageSizeBytes
nodes.summary: Page size in bytes used by Tungsten consumers: the spark.buffer.pageSize setting if present, else defaultPageSizeBytes.

nodes.name: MemoryManager.tungstenMemoryAllocator
nodes.summary: Selects the MemoryAllocator for Tungsten code: the heap allocator for ON_HEAP and the Unsafe allocator for OFF_HEAP.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.scala
nodes.summary: Defines UnifiedMemoryManager, Spark's default MemoryManager: execution and storage share one region sized by spark.memory.fraction and split by spark.memory.storageFraction, with soft borrowing between them. Its companion object computes the region size from heap minus 300MB reserved and tracks unmanaged memory (for example RocksDB) through a polling thread.
nodes.languageNotes: Class plus companion object in one file; the companion shares the class node id. acquireExecutionMemory defines nested helper functions that close over the selected pools.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager
nodes.summary: MemoryManager with a soft boundary between execution and storage. Storage can borrow free execution memory and execution can borrow free storage memory, but only execution can reclaim: cached blocks are evicted once storage exceeds its region, whereas execution memory is never evicted by storage, so caching can fail when execution holds most of the space. The companion object (lines 258-491) holds the sizing logic and unmanaged-memory tracking.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.getUnmanagedMemoryUsed
nodes.summary: Returns cached unmanaged memory in bytes for ON_HEAP or OFF_HEAP, or 0 when the unmanaged memory polling interval is not positive. A same-named companion method (line 280) returns the on-heap plus off-heap total.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.assertInvariants
nodes.summary: Asserts that execution plus storage pool sizes always equal the managed total (maxHeapMemory on heap, maxOffHeapMemory off heap), since borrowing only moves bytes between the two pools.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.maxOnHeapStorageMemory
nodes.summary: Maximum on-heap storage memory is the whole managed heap minus the execution memory currently in use, because storage may use anything execution is not using.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.maxOffHeapStorageMemory
nodes.summary: Maximum off-heap storage memory is the off-heap size minus off-heap execution memory in use.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.acquireExecutionMemory
nodes.summary: Picks the on-heap or off-heap pools and storage region size, then delegates to ExecutionMemoryPool.acquireMemory with two callbacks: maybeGrowExecutionPool (reclaim from storage) and computeMaxExecutionPoolSize (the cap used for per-task fair share).

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.maybeGrowExecutionPool
nodes.summary: Nested helper that grows the execution pool by shrinking storage when more memory is needed. Reclaimable memory is max(storage free memory, storage pool size minus storage region size); it calls freeSpaceToShrinkPool (evicting blocks if needed), then decrements the storage pool and increments the execution pool by that amount. It runs on every acquire attempt.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.computeMaxExecutionPoolSize
nodes.summary: Nested helper returning the execution pool size possible after evicting storage: max memory minus min(storage used, storage region size), minus unmanaged memory, floored at 0. The pool divides this among active tasks; it must stay above the pool size (SPARK-12155) and below max memory for fairness.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.acquireStorageMemory
nodes.summary: Acquires memory for a cached block. Fails fast (logs and returns false) if the request exceeds max storage minus unmanaged memory; otherwise, if storage lacks free space, borrows min(execution free memory, shortfall) by shrinking the execution pool and growing the storage pool, then calls StorageMemoryPool.acquireMemory, which may evict other blocks.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.acquireUnrollMemory
nodes.summary: Acquires unroll memory by simply delegating to acquireStorageMemory; the unified model does not limit unrolling separately.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.registerUnmanagedMemoryConsumer
nodes.summary: Registers a component that manages its own memory (such as RocksDB) so its usage is polled and counted in allocation decisions.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.unregisterUnmanagedMemoryConsumer
nodes.summary: Removes an unmanaged memory consumer from tracking; documented as only used in tests.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.getMemoryByComponentType
nodes.summary: Sums bytes used by registered unmanaged consumers of a given component type (for example "RocksDB"), treating failures as 0.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.clearUnmanagedMemoryUsers
nodes.summary: Clears all registered unmanaged consumers and resets the cached on-heap and off-heap totals, for executor shutdown or cleanup.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.startPollingIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Starts a single daemon scheduled executor ("unmanaged-memory-poller") per JVM, guarded by an AtomicBoolean, that periodically runs pollUnmanagedMemoryUsers.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.pollUnmanagedMemoryUsers
nodes.summary: Polls each registered consumer: -1 means inactive and the consumer is removed, other negative values count as 0, exceptions count as 0. Totals are summed by memory mode and stored in cached atomics used by the acquire paths.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.shutdownUnmanagedMemoryPoller
nodes.summary: Shuts down the polling executor (waiting up to 5 seconds before shutdownNow) and resets the started flag; documented as only used in tests.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.apply
nodes.summary: Factory that builds a UnifiedMemoryManager: maxMemory comes from getMaxMemory and the on-heap storage region is maxMemory times spark.memory.storageFraction.

nodes.name: UnifiedMemoryManager.getMaxMemory
nodes.summary: Computes the unified region: (system memory minus 300MB reserved) times spark.memory.fraction. Throws INVALID_DRIVER_MEMORY if system memory is under 1.5 times the reserved amount, and INVALID_EXECUTOR_MEMORY if spark.executor.memory is below that minimum (SPARK-12759).

nodes.name: Spillable.scala
nodes.summary: Defines Spillable, the abstract base class of Spark's in-memory collections that spill to disk (used by ExternalSorter). It decides when to ask the TaskMemoryManager for more execution memory and when to spill instead, using an initial threshold, a check every 32 records and optional element-count and size limits.

nodes.name: Spillable
nodes.summary: Abstract MemoryConsumer (ON_HEAP) that spills an in-memory collection of type C to disk when its memory threshold is exceeded. Subclasses implement spill(collection) and forceSpill, call addElementsRead for every record and call maybeSpill to apply the policy. Thresholds come from spark.shuffle.spill.initialMemoryThreshold (SHUFFLE_SPILL_INITIAL_MEM_THRESHOLD) plus the num-elements and max-size force-spill thresholds.

nodes.name: Spillable.forceSpill
nodes.summary: Abstract: forces the current in-memory collection to spill to release memory; called by the TaskMemoryManager when there is not enough memory for the task.

nodes.name: Spillable.maybeSpill
nodes.summary: Decides whether to spill. It spills at once if elements read exceed the num-elements force-spill threshold or the current size exceeds the max-size threshold. Otherwise, every 32 elements when currentMemory >= the current threshold, it requests 2*currentMemory minus threshold through acquireMemory and raises the threshold by what was granted; if currentMemory is still >= the threshold it spills. On spill it counts, logs, calls spill(collection), resets the element counter, adds to bytes spilled and releases memory.

nodes.name: Spillable.spill
nodes.summary: MemoryConsumer.spill callback used when the TaskMemoryManager needs memory. If another consumer triggered it and the Tungsten mode is ON_HEAP, it calls forceSpill and, on success, releases the memory above the initial threshold and returns that many bytes; otherwise it returns 0. The abstract overload spill(collection) at line 36 is what subclasses implement for maybeSpill.

nodes.name: Spillable.releaseMemory
nodes.summary: Gives the memory above the initial threshold back to the execution pool so other tasks can use it, and resets the threshold to its initial value.

nodes.name: Spillable.logSpillage
nodes.summary: Logs an info message with the thread id, the human-readable size spilled, elements read since the last spill and the number of spills so far.

nodes.name: ExecutorBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Defines the ExecutorBackend trait, the narrow interface the Executor uses to push task state changes (RUNNING, FINISHED, FAILED, KILLED plus a serialized payload) back toward the driver. Cluster-specific executor backends implement it.

nodes.name: ExecutorBackend
nodes.summary: Trait with a single statusUpdate(taskId, state, data) method. Executor.TaskRunner calls it to report each task state transition; the implementation decides how the update reaches the driver scheduler.

nodes.name: statusUpdate
nodes.summary: Abstract hook that delivers a task's state and serialized result or failure reason (as a ByteBuffer) to the cluster scheduler.

nodes.name: Executor.scala
nodes.summary: Executor-side engine for running tasks in one JVM: a cached thread pool runs one TaskRunner per task, a heartbeater reports accumulator updates to the driver, TaskReapers supervise killed tasks, and per-session classloaders and dependency downloads support user jars, files and archives.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a nested inner class (TaskRunner) and a private class (TaskReaper) that close over Executor's fields, plus a companion object holding thread-name constants and fatal-error detection.

nodes.name: IsolatedSessionState
nodes.summary: Per-session bundle of classloaders and the jars, files and archives already fetched for one session UUID (the default session or a Spark Connect session). A ref count and an evicted flag, both guarded by one lock, defer cleanup until the last task using an evicted session releases it. Companion object (lines 62-68) holds the authoritative sessions map.

nodes.name: acquire
nodes.summary: Increments the task ref count under the lock and returns false if the session was already evicted, so the caller must look it up again.

nodes.name: tryUnEvict
nodes.summary: Cancels a pending eviction if the session is still in use (evicted and refCount > 0); returns false once it is cleaned up or idle.

nodes.name: release
nodes.summary: Decrements the ref count and runs cleanup when the last task finishes on an evicted session.

nodes.name: markEvicted
nodes.summary: Flags the session as evicted from the LRU cache; cleans up at once when idle, otherwise defers until running tasks release it.

nodes.name: cleanup
nodes.summary: Closes the URL classloader, deletes the session's directory under the SparkFiles root, and removes the session from the authoritative sessions map.

nodes.name: Executor
nodes.summary: The Spark executor: backed by a cached thread pool of UninterruptibleThread workers, it launches a TaskRunner per task, tracks running tasks and kill marks, runs a Heartbeater and metrics poller, manages isolated session classloaders and dependency downloads, loads plugins, and registers metrics sources. Used by the standalone, YARN, Kubernetes and local backends. Companion object (lines 1578-1627) defines thread-name constants, task deserialization properties, and isFatalError.

nodes.name: newSessionState
nodes.summary: Creates an IsolatedSessionState for a job artifact state: builds the URL classloader, wraps it with an optional REPL classloader, and registers the session in the authoritative map.

nodes.name: decommission
nodes.summary: Marks the executor as decommissioned; launchTask then logs an error if a task still arrives, but tasks are not hard-blocked.

nodes.name: launchTask
nodes.summary: Entry point for a new task on the executor: builds a TaskRunner, registers it in runningTasks, applies any pending kill mark, and submits it to the thread pool. If launching fails it reports TaskState.FAILED through the ExecutorBackend, and exits the JVM if even that report fails (unless the env is stopped).

nodes.name: killTask
nodes.summary: Records a kill mark (so a kill that arrives before launchTask is not lost), then kills the running TaskRunner: through a new TaskReaper when the task reaper is enabled, otherwise directly via TaskRunner.kill.

nodes.name: killAllTasks
nodes.summary: Calls killTask for every task in runningTasks; available to executor backends instead of taking the JVM down.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Idempotent shutdown: removes the shutdown hook, reports metrics, stops the metrics poller, heartbeater, shuffle block pusher, thread pool and kill-mark cleanup service, notifies plugins, and stops the SparkEnv when not in local mode.

nodes.name: computeTotalGcTime
nodes.summary: Sums JVM garbage collector collection times (ms) across all collectors in this JVM process.

nodes.name: createClassLoader
nodes.summary: Three overloads that build the session's MutableURLClassLoader: the first from the user classpath and current jars, the next optionally with a stub classloader for Spark Connect UDFs, the last choosing ChildFirstURLClassLoader when userClassPathFirst is set and inheriting from the default session's loader for isolated sessions.

nodes.name: createClassLoaderWithStub
nodes.summary: Builds a ChildFirstURLClassLoader chained with a StubClassLoader for the configured Spark Connect UDF stub prefixes, ordering user, system and stub loaders depending on userClassPathFirst.

nodes.name: addReplClassLoaderIfNeeded
nodes.summary: Wraps the parent classloader in an ExecutorClassLoader when a REPL class URI is configured, so classes defined interactively can be read; otherwise returns the parent.

nodes.name: updateDependencies
nodes.summary: Downloads any files, archives and jars whose timestamps are newer than what the session has fetched (guarded by an interruptible ReentrantLock), unpacks archives, adds new jars to the session classloader and recreates it when Spark Connect stubbing needs it. Called at startup and at the start of each task.

nodes.name: reportHeartBeat
nodes.summary: Body of the heartbeater thread: merges shuffle-read metrics and sets GC time for each running task, collects non-excluded accumulator updates, and sends a Heartbeat to the driver's HeartbeatReceiver. Re-registers the BlockManager if told to, and exits the JVM with HEARTBEAT_FAILURE after too many consecutive failed heartbeats.

nodes.name: getTaskThreadDump
nodes.summary: Returns a thread stack trace for a running task's thread, or None with a warning if the task is not running on this executor.

nodes.name: isFatalError
nodes.summary: Walks the cause chain up to a depth limit and treats a Throwable as fatal if Utils.isFatalError says so; SparkOutOfMemoryError (a managed-memory OOM) is explicitly non-fatal. Decides whether a task failure should also trigger the uncaught-exception handler that ends the executor JVM.

nodes.name: TaskRunner
nodes.summary: Runnable that executes one task on a pool thread. Its run method does everything the executor does for a task, in order: obtain the session, set up logging context, create a TaskMemoryManager, fetch dependencies, deserialize the Task, run it, serialize the result, record metrics, and send the final status. Tracks kill reason, finished flag, GC start time and the Task for heartbeats and killing.

nodes.name: kill
nodes.summary: Remembers the kill reason and, if the task is deserialized and not finished, calls Task.kill (which marks the TaskContext interrupted and optionally interrupts the task thread).

nodes.name: setTaskFinishedAndClearInterruptStatus
nodes.summary: Sets the finished flag, clears the thread's interrupt status (so the status update is not broken by ClosedByInterruptException), and wakes any waiting TaskReapers.

nodes.name: collectAccumulatorsAndResetStatusOnFailure
nodes.summary: On failure or kill: sets executor run time and JVM GC time on the task metrics, collects accumulator updates for the failed task, marks the runner finished, and returns the accumulators and their info updates.

nodes.name: obtainSession
nodes.summary: Gets or creates the IsolatedSessionState for the task's job artifact state from the Guava cache and acquires it, retrying if the session was evicted between lookup and acquire.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Main task path on the task thread. Sends RUNNING, updates dependencies, deserializes the Task, creates a TaskMemoryManager, calls Task.run, then serializes the value, fills in TaskMetrics and Dropwizard counters, and builds a DirectTaskResult. Result routing: if larger than the max result size it sends a dropped IndirectTaskResult; if larger than the direct-result limit it stores the bytes in the BlockManager under a TaskResultBlockId and sends an IndirectTaskResult; otherwise it sends the bytes directly. Catch blocks map TaskKilledException and interrupts to KILLED, FetchFailed to FAILED with a fetch-failed reason, CommitDeniedException to KILLED, other errors to FAILED with an ExceptionFailure (fatal ones also reach the uncaught-exception handler).

nodes.name: incrementShuffleMetrics
nodes.summary: Adds the task's shuffle read, write and push-based shuffle metrics to the executor-level Dropwizard counters in ExecutorSource.

nodes.name: TaskReaper
nodes.summary: Runnable (SPARK-18761) that supervises a killed task: it calls TaskRunner.kill once, then polls until the task finishes, logging warnings and optional thread dumps, and throws KilledByTaskReaperException to take down the executor JVM if the kill timeout is exceeded (not in local mode). Only used when the task reaper is enabled in the configuration.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Kills the task, then loops waiting on the TaskRunner monitor in kill-polling intervals until it finishes or the timeout passes; on timeout in non-local mode it throws KilledByTaskReaperException. Always clears its entry in taskReaperForTask.

nodes.name: KilledByTaskReaperException
nodes.summary: Exception thrown by TaskReaper when a killed task cannot be stopped in time; as an uncaught exception it ends the executor JVM.

nodes.name: TaskContextImpl.scala
nodes.summary: Implementation of the TaskContext API for a running task: stores identity and resources, holds completion, failure and interrupt listener stacks, tracks kill reason and any fetch failure, and exposes TaskMetrics. Task.run creates one per task attempt on the executor.

nodes.name: TaskContextImpl
nodes.summary: TaskContext implementation created by Task.run. Completion and failure listeners run in reverse registration order, one invoking thread at a time and never under the context lock. Fields for interruption, completion, failure cause and fetch-failure state are guarded by the context lock or are volatile.

nodes.name: addTaskCompletionListener
nodes.summary: Pushes a completion listener; if the task has already completed, runs listeners immediately.

nodes.name: addTaskFailureListener
nodes.summary: Pushes a failure listener and invokes failure listeners immediately if the task has already failed.

nodes.name: addTaskInterruptListener
nodes.summary: Pushes an interrupt listener and runs listeners immediately with a TaskKilledException if the task was already killed.

nodes.name: markTaskFailed
nodes.summary: Records the first failure cause (later calls are no-ops) and runs the failure listeners.

nodes.name: markTaskCompleted
nodes.summary: Sets the completed flag once and runs completion listeners, which release task-scoped resources.

nodes.name: invokeTaskCompletionListeners
nodes.summary: Runs onTaskCompletion of each registered listener through invokeListeners.

nodes.name: invokeTaskFailureListeners
nodes.summary: Runs onTaskFailure of each registered listener through invokeListeners.

nodes.name: invokeTaskInterruptListeners
nodes.summary: Pops and runs interrupt listeners separately from invokeListeners so a running interrupt listener cannot block completion or failure listeners; collects exceptions into a TaskCompletionListenerException.

nodes.name: invokeListeners
nodes.summary: Core sequential listener runner: allows at most one invoking thread, pops listeners under the lock but calls them outside it, and when a listener throws, marks the task failed (running failure listeners) and aggregates the errors into a TaskCompletionListenerException. A long comment enumerates five interleavings with Task.doRunTask.

nodes.name: markInterrupted
nodes.summary: Stores the kill reason and runs interrupt listeners; listener failures are logged and recorded via markTaskFailed instead of propagating to the executor kill thread.

nodes.name: killTaskIfInterrupted
nodes.summary: Throws TaskKilledException with the stored reason if the task was marked killed; Executor.TaskRunner.run calls it after Task.run returns.

nodes.name: setFetchFailed
nodes.summary: Stores a FetchFailedException so Executor can still fail the task as a fetch failure if user code swallowed the exception (SPARK-19276).

nodes.name: createResourceUninterruptibly
nodes.summary: Builds a Closeable resource while the task is marked non-interruptible, applying any pending interrupt before and after, and registers a completion listener that closes the resource.

nodes.name: TaskMetrics.scala
nodes.summary: Defines TaskMetrics, the per-task container of metric accumulators (run and deserialize time, GC, spill, peak memory, result size, plus input, output and shuffle read/write metrics). Executors fill it during a task and send accumulator updates to the driver at heartbeats and task end.

nodes.name: TaskMetrics
nodes.summary: Wrapper over internal LongAccumulators and a CollectionAccumulator, plus nested Input, Output, ShuffleRead and ShuffleWrite metrics and externally registered accumulators. The object itself is never sent to the driver, only its accumulator values. Companion object (lines 341-399) builds empty, registered and driver-side reconstructed instances.

nodes.name: createTempShuffleReadMetrics
nodes.summary: Creates a per-dependency TempShuffleReadMetrics so concurrent shuffle readers avoid synchronization; callers must later call mergeShuffleReadMetrics.

nodes.name: mergeShuffleReadMetrics
nodes.summary: Merges all temporary shuffle-read metrics into shuffleReadMetrics; called on executor heartbeat and at task end.

nodes.name: register
nodes.summary: Registers every internal accumulator with a SparkContext under its metric name, counting failed values (driver-side).

nodes.name: withExternalAccums
nodes.summary: Applies a function to the external accumulator buffer while holding the read lock.

nodes.name: registerAccumulator
nodes.summary: Adds a user or library accumulator to the externally registered list under the write lock.

nodes.name: accumulators
nodes.summary: Returns internal plus external accumulators; the heartbeat reporter uses this to collect updates.

nodes.name: nonZeroInternalAccums
nodes.summary: Returns internal accumulators that are non-zero, always including result size because its value is set on the driver.

nodes.name: empty
nodes.summary: Companion factory for a TaskMetrics whose accumulators get metadata but are not registered.

nodes.name: registered
nodes.summary: Companion factory that builds an empty TaskMetrics and registers its internal accumulators with AccumulatorContext; the driver creates and serializes one per task.

nodes.name: fromAccumulatorInfos
nodes.summary: Driver-side: rebuilds a TaskMetrics from AccumulableInfo updates by name (block statuses or long values).

nodes.name: fromAccumulators
nodes.summary: Driver-side: rebuilds a TaskMetrics by merging accumulator updates from an executor, treating unnamed or unknown ones as external accumulators.

nodes.name: CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Defines CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend, the main class of an executor JVM that a cluster manager launches for a Spark application (for PySpark this is the JVM process that later spawns Python workers). Its companion object parses the command line, fetches the driver's Spark properties, builds the executor SparkEnv, and registers the "Executor" RPC endpoint that registers with the driver and then receives tasks.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class plus companion object; the companion holds main/run/parseArguments and the RegisteredExecutor message.

nodes.name: CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend
nodes.summary: RPC endpoint (IsolatedThreadSafeRpcEndpoint) and ExecutorBackend running inside each executor process. On start it connects to the driver and sends RegisterExecutor; once the driver answers it creates the Executor, then handles LaunchTask, KillTask, StopExecutor, decommissioning and delegation token messages from the driver, and forwards task status updates back to the driver. The class body is lines 48-391; the companion object (lines 393-611) provides main, run and argument parsing.

nodes.name: onStart
nodes.summary: Called when the endpoint starts: optionally registers the decommission signal handler, checks Netty direct memory against the remote block fetch size limit, discovers executor resources, then asynchronously looks up the driver endpoint and asks it with RegisterExecutor (id, self ref, host, cores, log URLs, attributes, resources, resource profile id). On success it sends itself RegisteredExecutor; on failure it exits the executor with code 1.

nodes.name: parseOrFindResources
nodes.summary: Discovers or loads the resources (such as GPUs) assigned to this executor for its ResourceProfile using a class loader that includes the user classpath, so a user-provided discovery class can be found.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: One-way message handler. On RegisteredExecutor it creates the Executor and tells the driver LaunchedExecutor; LaunchTask decodes a TaskDescription and calls executor.launchTask; KillTask calls executor.killTask; StopExecutor sets the stopping flag and sends itself Shutdown; Shutdown stops the Executor in a new thread (or System.exit(1) if it was never created); it also handles UpdateExecutorLogLevel, UpdateDelegationTokens and DecommissionExecutor.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Request/reply handler: ExecutorDecommissionSigReceived tells the driver the executor is decommissioning (ExecutorDecommissioning) and then starts decommissionSelf; TaskThreadDump returns the thread dump of a running task from the Executor.

nodes.name: onDisconnected
nodes.summary: Reacts to a lost RPC connection: ignores it during shutdown, exits the executor with code 1 if the disconnected address is the driver (so executors do not outlive their driver), and only logs a warning for unknown addresses.

nodes.name: statusUpdate
nodes.summary: Implements ExecutorBackend.statusUpdate: wraps a task state change and result bytes into a StatusUpdate message (including task cpus and resources) and sends it to the driver, recording the last task finish time for decommissioning.

nodes.name: exitExecutor
