nodes.summary: Shuts the executor down once: logs the reason, optionally sends RemoveExecutor with an ExecutorLossReason to the driver, then sends itself Shutdown. Protected so subclasses can handle executor exits differently.

nodes.name: decommissionSelf
nodes.summary: Starts graceful decommissioning when enabled: marks the executor decommissioned, optionally begins block manager migration of RDD and shuffle blocks, calls executor.decommission, and runs a daemon thread that exits the executor when no tasks are running and migration is finished.

nodes.name: Arguments
nodes.summary: Case class (in the companion object) holding the parsed command-line options for an executor: driver URL, executor id, bind address, hostname, cores, app id, optional worker URL, resources file and resource profile id.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Executor JVM entry point: builds a factory for CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend, parses command-line arguments, calls run, then System.exit(0).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Bootstraps an executor process: creates a temporary RpcEnv ("driverPropsFetcher") to fetch SparkAppConfig (Spark properties, resource profile, delegation tokens, IO encryption key) from the driver with up to 3 retries, builds the executor SparkConf (applying resource profile memory and cores settings), calls SparkEnv.createExecutorEnv, creates the backend, registers it as the "Executor" endpoint (plus a WorkerWatcher in standalone mode) and blocks on awaitTermination.

nodes.name: parseArguments
nodes.summary: Parses --driver-url, --executor-id, --bind-address, --hostname, --cores, --resourcesFile, --app-id, --worker-url and --resourceProfileId, validates required options and defaults the hostname and bind address.

nodes.name: printUsageAndExit
nodes.summary: Prints the usage text listing the executor command-line options and exits with status 1.

nodes.name: SparkEnv.scala
nodes.summary: Defines SparkEnv, the holder of all runtime services of one Spark JVM (the driver, or each executor): RpcEnv, serializers, MapOutputTracker, ShuffleManager, MemoryManager, BlockManager, BroadcastManager, SecurityManager, MetricsSystem and OutputCommitCoordinator. The companion object builds it for the driver (createDriverEnv) and for executors (createExecutorEnv) and keeps a global instance reachable via SparkEnv.get.
nodes.languageNotes: Class and companion object share one id; the companion holds the static factory methods and the global reference.

nodes.name: SparkEnv
nodes.summary: Developer API class bundling the per-JVM runtime objects: executorId, rpcEnv, serializer, closureSerializer, serializerManager, mapOutputTracker, broadcastManager, blockManager, securityManager, metricsSystem, outputCommitCoordinator and conf. The ShuffleManager and MemoryManager are initialized later (initializeShuffleManager, initializeMemoryManager). It also caches PythonWorkerFactory instances per (python executable, worker module, daemon module, env vars) and provides createPythonWorker, destroyPythonWorker and releasePythonWorker. The class body is lines 61-263; the companion object (lines 265-588) holds the factories and the global get/set.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the environment once: stops cached Python worker factories, MapOutputTracker, ShuffleManager, BroadcastManager, BlockManager and its master, MetricsSystem, OutputCommitCoordinator and the RpcEnv, then deletes the driver temporary directory if this is the driver.

nodes.name: createPythonWorker
nodes.summary: Three overloads that get or create the cached PythonWorkerFactory for the key (pythonExec, workerModule, daemonModule, envVars) and call its create to obtain a PythonWorker and optional process handle. Throws if the same key is requested with a different useDaemon value; the shorter overloads default to the default daemon module and to spark.python.use.daemon.

nodes.name: destroyPythonWorker
nodes.summary: Two overloads that look up the PythonWorkerFactory for the key and call stopWorker on the given worker, stopping that Python worker.

nodes.name: releasePythonWorker
nodes.summary: Two overloads that look up the PythonWorkerFactory for the key and call releaseWorker, returning the worker to the factory for reuse.

nodes.name: initializeShuffleManager
nodes.summary: Creates the ShuffleManager from configuration via ShuffleManager.create (after SparkContext or Executor start so user jars can define custom managers) and releases the latch that waitForShuffleManagerInit callers wait on.

nodes.name: initializeMemoryManager
nodes.summary: Creates the UnifiedMemoryManager for the given number of usable cores; it may be called only once per environment.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Stores the given SparkEnv in the global reference returned by SparkEnv.get.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Returns the global SparkEnv of this JVM (set after a SparkContext is created on the driver or an executor environment is created).

nodes.name: createDriverEnv
nodes.summary: Creates the SparkEnv for the driver: checks the driver host and port are configured, creates the IO encryption key if enabled and delegates to create with the driver identifier and the live listener bus.

nodes.name: createExecutorEnv
nodes.summary: Creates the SparkEnv for an executor via create (no fixed port), initializes its MemoryManager with the core count, and installs it as the global SparkEnv.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Shared factory for driver and executor environments: builds SecurityManager, RpcEnv ("sparkDriver" or "sparkExecutor"), serializer, SerializerManager, closure serializer, BroadcastManager, MapOutputTracker (Master on the driver, Worker on executors) with its endpoint, BlockManagerMaster and endpoints, NettyBlockTransferService, BlockManager (not usable until initialize is called), MetricsSystem and OutputCommitCoordinator. The driver registers endpoints in its RpcEnv; executors look up the driver's endpoints.

nodes.name: environmentDetails
nodes.summary: Collects JVM information, Spark properties, system properties, classpath entries, Hadoop properties and metrics properties into a map, used mainly for the SparkListenerEnvironmentUpdate event shown in the UI.

nodes.name: ExecutorAllocationManager.scala
nodes.summary: Implements dynamic allocation on the driver: a manager that keeps a moving target number of executors per ResourceProfile, requests more from the cluster manager when tasks are backlogged (in exponentially growing batches) and removes executors that have been idle too long. It listens to scheduler events and exposes metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains the manager, its inner ExecutorAllocationListener, a metrics Source and a private companion with NOT_SET and TargetNumUpdates.

nodes.name: ExecutorAllocationManager
nodes.summary: Driver-side agent created by SparkContext when spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled is true and the scheduler backend is an ExecutorAllocationClient. Policy: the target starts at spark.dynamicAllocation.initialExecutors; when tasks stay backlogged for schedulerBacklogTimeout it adds 1, 2, 4, ... executors per round (sustainedSchedulerBacklogTimeout between rounds), capped by maxExecutors and by the number needed for pending and running tasks (scaled by executorAllocationRatio); it lowers the target when fewer are needed and removes executors that the ExecutorMonitor reports as timed out (executorIdleTimeout, cachedExecutorIdleTimeout) while keeping at least minExecutors. A 100 ms polling loop runs on a daemon thread.

nodes.name: validateSettings
nodes.summary: Validates dynamic allocation settings at construction: min/max executors, backlog timeouts, executorAllocationRatio in (0, 1], and that a shuffle service, shuffle tracking, shuffle block decommission or reliable shuffle storage is available so removing executors does not lose shuffle data.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Registers the allocation listener and the ExecutorMonitor on the listener bus management queue, schedules the schedule task every 100 ms, and sends the initial total executor request to the cluster manager through the client.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Stops the allocation manager by shutting down its scheduler thread (waiting up to 10 seconds).

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets state when the cluster manager loses track of the driver (currently YARN client mode AM restart): clears the add timer, resets targets to the initial number and the per-round add count to 1, and resets the ExecutorMonitor.

nodes.name: maxNumExecutorsNeededPerResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Computes how many executors a ResourceProfile needs: ceil((pending + pending speculative + running tasks) * executorAllocationRatio / tasks per executor), plus one extra for pending speculative tasks when a single executor would otherwise suffice, and extra executors for unschedulable task sets.

nodes.name: schedule
nodes.summary: Periodic tick: asks the ExecutorMonitor for timed-out (idle) executors, ends the initializing phase if any exist, calls updateAndSyncNumExecutorsTarget with the current time, then removes the timed-out executors.

nodes.name: updateAndSyncNumExecutorsTarget
nodes.summary: Updates the target executor count per ResourceProfile and syncs it with the cluster manager: does nothing while initializing; if the maximum needed is below the target it lowers the target, otherwise if the add time has expired it adds executors; then issues a single request for all changed profiles.

nodes.name: addExecutorsToTarget
nodes.summary: Applies addExecutors through updateTargetExecs for one ResourceProfile.

nodes.name: decrementExecutorsFromTarget
nodes.summary: Applies decrementExecutors through updateTargetExecs for one ResourceProfile.

nodes.name: updateTargetExecs
nodes.summary: Runs a target-changing function (add or decrement), records the resulting delta and the old target in the pending updates map if the target changed, and returns the delta.

nodes.name: doUpdateRequest
nodes.summary: Sends the new totals to the cluster manager through client.requestTotalExecutors. When acknowledged, it doubles the number to add next round if the full amount was granted (otherwise resets it to 1) and restarts the add timer for the sustained backlog timeout; if the manager cannot be reached it restores the old targets.

nodes.name: decrementExecutors
nodes.summary: Lowers the target to max(maxNeeded, minExecutors) and resets the number of executors to add per round to 1; returns the (negative) change.

nodes.name: addExecutors
nodes.summary: Scale-up step: returns 0 when the target is already at maxExecutors; otherwise raises the target to at least the current executor count, adds the per-round number (exponentially growing), caps it by the number needed and by [minExecutors, maxExecutors], and resets the round size to 1 if nothing changed.

nodes.name: removeExecutors
nodes.summary: Scale-down step: for each idle executor, skips it if removing would drop the profile below minExecutors or below its current target; kills (client.killExecutors) or, with decommissioning enabled, decommissions (client.decommissionExecutors) the rest, then re-sends the total executor target and notifies the ExecutorMonitor.

nodes.name: onSchedulerBacklogged
nodes.summary: Called when pending tasks appear: if no add timer is set, sets addTime to now plus spark.dynamicAllocation.schedulerBacklogTimeout.

nodes.name: onSchedulerQueueEmpty
nodes.summary: Called when the scheduler queue drains: clears the add timer and resets the per-profile number of executors to add to 1.

nodes.name: ExecutorAllocationListener
nodes.summary: SparkListener that tracks, per stage attempt and ResourceProfile, the number of tasks, running tasks, pending and speculative tasks, unschedulable task sets and locality hints from scheduler events. The manager reads these counts to compute how many executors are needed, and the listener notifies the manager when the scheduler is backlogged or drained.

nodes.name: onStageSubmitted
nodes.summary: On stage submission ends initialization, records the stage task count, calls onSchedulerBacklogged, maps the stage to its ResourceProfile, records locality preferences for executor placement and, for a new ResourceProfile, sets its initial target and requests it.

nodes.name: onStageCompleted
nodes.summary: Removes bookkeeping for a completed stage attempt, updates placement hints and calls onSchedulerQueueEmpty when no stage has pending tasks.

nodes.name: onTaskStart
nodes.summary: Counts a started task (normal or speculative) and calls onSchedulerQueueEmpty if no tasks are pending any more.

nodes.name: onTaskEnd
nodes.summary: Decrements running task counts and, for failed tasks that were not intentionally killed, marks the scheduler backlogged again if nothing is pending so the resubmitted task gets resources.

nodes.name: onSpeculativeTaskSubmitted
nodes.summary: Records a pending speculative task and calls onSchedulerBacklogged.

nodes.name: onUnschedulableTaskSetAdded
nodes.summary: Records a task set with an unschedulable task (for example, when executors are excluded) and calls onSchedulerBacklogged so more executors can be requested.

nodes.name: onUnschedulableTaskSetRemoved
nodes.summary: Clears the unschedulable marker for a task set and cleans its ResourceProfile mapping if unused.

nodes.name: removeStageFromResourceProfileIfUnused
nodes.summary: Removes a stage attempt from the ResourceProfile-to-stage map once it has no tasks, pending speculative tasks or running tasks left.

nodes.name: pendingTasksPerResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Estimates pending tasks for a ResourceProfile as total tasks minus started task indices, summed over its active stage attempts.

nodes.name: pendingUnschedulableTaskSetsPerResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Counts unschedulable task sets for a ResourceProfile, used as a heuristic for requesting extra executors.

nodes.name: totalRunningTasksPerResourceProfile
nodes.summary: Sums running task counts (including speculative) over the stage attempts of a ResourceProfile.

nodes.name: updateExecutorPlacementHints
nodes.summary: Aggregates, per ResourceProfile, the number of locality-aware pending tasks and a host-to-task-count map, and stores them in the manager for executor placement requests.

nodes.name: ExecutorAllocationManagerSource
nodes.summary: Metrics Source named "ExecutorAllocationManager" exposing counters (gracefully decommissioned, killed by driver, exited unexpectedly) and gauges (executors to add, pending to remove, all, target, max needed, decommissioning); it is registered by SparkContext and its values may change between Spark versions.

nodes.name: SparkSubmit.scala
nodes.summary: Entry point of the spark-submit command. Parses the command line, prepares the child classpath, system properties and main class for the chosen cluster manager (yarn, standalone spark://, k8s, local) and deploy mode (client or cluster), then runs that main class in-process. Also handles the --kill and --status requests for standalone and K8s submissions.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with a class (the logic), a companion object (the JVM main, constants and resource-type helpers), plus helper object, case class and two SPI traits.

nodes.name: SparkSubmitAction
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the actions spark-submit can perform: SUBMIT, KILL, REQUEST_STATUS and PRINT_VERSION. Kill and status are only supported for standalone cluster mode.

nodes.name: SparkSubmit
nodes.summary: Main gateway for launching a Spark application (class plus companion object with the JVM main). Doing doSubmit parses arguments, then routes SUBMIT through submit, doRunMain and runMain, which load the prepared child main class and call its start; KILL and REQUEST_STATUS go to the REST client or an external SparkSubmitOperation. The companion object holds the cluster manager and deploy mode bit flags, the special shell resource names (pyspark-shell etc.) and helpers such as isPython.

nodes.name: doSubmit
nodes.summary: Top-level driver of spark-submit: builds SparkSubmitArguments, configures structured logging (disabled for shells and the SQL shell), then dispatches on the parsed action to submit, kill, requestStatus or printVersion.

nodes.name: kill
nodes.summary: Kills an existing submission, via RestSubmissionClient when the master supports REST, otherwise through an external SparkSubmitOperation found for the master URL.

nodes.name: requestStatus
nodes.summary: Requests the status of an existing submission, via RestSubmissionClient when supported, otherwise through an external SparkSubmitOperation for the master URL.

nodes.name: printVersion
nodes.summary: Logs the Spark ASCII banner, version, Scala and Java runtime, branch, build user and date, revision and repository URL for spark-submit --version.

nodes.name: submit
nodes.summary: Submits the application. In standalone cluster mode it first tries the REST submission gateway and, if the master turns out not to be a REST server (SubmitRestConnectionException), retries with the legacy Client gateway; all other modes simply call doRunMain. Tail recursive for that retry.

nodes.name: doRunMain
nodes.summary: Nested helper of submit that calls runMain, wrapping it in a Hadoop proxy-user doAs when --proxy-user is given (with special handling for the Kubernetes cluster-mode driver).

nodes.name: prepareSubmitEnvironment
nodes.summary: Core translation step of spark-submit. Maps --master to a cluster manager (yarn, spark:// standalone, k8s, local) and --deploy-mode to client or cluster, rejects unsupported combinations, resolves Maven --packages and glob paths, and downloads remote files in client mode. For PySpark client mode it sets the child main class to org.apache.spark.deploy.PythonRunner (or PythonGatewayServer for the pyspark shell) with the .py file and --py-files as child arguments, while yarn and k8s cluster modes pass the python file to YarnClusterApplication or KubernetesClientApplication. A table of OptionAssigner rules then maps each argument to SparkConf keys. Returns (childArgs, childClasspath, SparkConf, childMainClass).

nodes.name: getSubmitClassLoader
nodes.summary: Creates a MutableURLClassLoader (or ChildFirstURLClassLoader when the driver user class path comes first), installs it as the context class loader and returns it.

nodes.name: runMain
nodes.summary: Runs the prepared child main class: calls prepareSubmitEnvironment, adds the child classpath to a submit class loader, loads childMainClass, wraps it as a SparkApplication (or JavaMainApplication for a plain main method) and calls start. Maps failures to exit codes, stops the active SparkContext on Kubernetes and may call System.exit.

nodes.name: annotateExitException
nodes.summary: Stores the failure that ended the application through any SparkDiagnosticsSetter registered for the master URL, skipping shells and servers and swallowing its own errors.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: JVM main of the SparkSubmit object. Creates a SparkSubmit whose argument parser and logging are redirected to console printMessage, translates SparkUserAppException into a process exit code and calls doSubmit.

nodes.name: isShell
nodes.summary: Returns true when the primary resource is one of the shell names spark-shell, pyspark-shell, sparkr-shell or connect-shell.

nodes.name: isPython
nodes.summary: Returns true when the primary resource ends in .py or is pyspark-shell, which is how spark-submit decides to treat the application as a PySpark app.

nodes.name: InProcessSparkSubmit
nodes.summary: Entry point used by the launcher library to start Spark applications in the same JVM; it just constructs a SparkSubmit and calls doSubmit.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Creates a SparkSubmit and runs doSubmit with the given arguments for in-process launches.

nodes.name: SparkSubmitUtils
nodes.summary: Helpers around spark-submit: ServiceLoader lookup of external SparkSubmitOperation and SparkDiagnosticsSetter implementations by master URL, and parsing of --conf key=value pairs.

nodes.name: getSubmitOperations
nodes.summary: Finds the single SparkSubmitOperation (via ServiceLoader) that supports the given master URL; fails if none or more than one is registered.

nodes.name: parseSparkConfProperty
nodes.summary: Splits a --conf argument at the first = into a key and value, throwing a SparkException when no = is present.

nodes.name: getSparkDiagnosticsSetters
nodes.summary: Returns the optional SparkDiagnosticsSetter registered through ServiceLoader that supports the master URL; fails if several do.

nodes.name: OptionAssigner
nodes.summary: Case class describing one rule that maps a spark-submit argument value to a command-line option or SparkConf key for a given cluster manager and deploy mode mask, with an optional merge function.

nodes.name: SparkSubmitOperation
nodes.summary: SPI trait for external cluster managers to support kill and status requests for submissions and to declare which master URLs they handle.

nodes.name: SparkDiagnosticsSetter
nodes.summary: SPI trait providing a hook to record application failure details in an external system, enabled per master URL.

nodes.name: StandaloneAppClient.scala
nodes.summary: Driver-side client of the standalone cluster manager. It registers the application with the Master (RegisterApplication, retried against all masters), receives RegisteredApplication, ExecutorAdded, ExecutorUpdated, WorkerRemoved and MasterChanged messages and forwards them to a listener, and relays executor requests and kills to the Master.

nodes.name: StandaloneAppClient
nodes.summary: Interface that lets an application (via StandaloneSchedulerBackend) talk to the Spark standalone Master. start sets up an RPC endpoint named AppClient; requestTotalExecutors and killExecutors ask the Master to scale this application, and stop unregisters it.

nodes.name: ClientEndpoint
nodes.summary: Private RPC endpoint inside StandaloneAppClient. On start it registers with every configured master in parallel, retrying up to 3 times at 20 second intervals, then handles Master replies by calling the listener (connected, executorAdded, executorRemoved, workerRemoved, dead, disconnected).

nodes.name: onStart
nodes.summary: Begins registration with the Master by calling registerWithMaster(1); on failure marks the client disconnected and stops the endpoint.

nodes.name: tryRegisterAllMasters
nodes.summary: Submits one task per master address that looks up the Master endpoint and sends it RegisterApplication(appDescription, self), skipping if already registered.

nodes.name: registerWithMaster
nodes.summary: Registers with all masters and schedules a retry check every 20 seconds; cancels the pending attempts once registered, retries up to 3 times, then marks the application dead with All masters are unresponsive.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles one-way messages from the Master: RegisteredApplication (stores app id, calls listener.connected), ApplicationRemoved, ExecutorAdded and ExecutorUpdated (forwarded to the listener as executor added, removed or decommissioned), WorkerRemoved, and MasterChanged (re-acknowledges the new master).

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles request-reply messages: StopAppClient (marks dead, sends UnregisterApplication to the Master) and RequestExecutors or KillExecutors, which are forwarded to the Master asynchronously.

nodes.name: askAndReplyAsync
nodes.summary: Asks the Master a Boolean question and replies to the original caller from the future callback, forwarding non-fatal failures.

nodes.name: onStop
nodes.summary: Cancels the registration retry timer and futures and shuts down the registration thread pools.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Asks the endpoint to stop (StopAppClient) and waits for the reply, tolerating a timeout when the Master is already gone.

nodes.name: requestTotalExecutors
nodes.summary: Asks the Master for a total number of executors per resource profile, including pending and running ones; returns false if the driver is not fully initialised. An overload takes a single count for the default profile.

nodes.name: killExecutors
nodes.summary: Sends KillExecutors to the Master through the endpoint, returning whether the request was acknowledged.

nodes.name: Master.scala
nodes.summary: The standalone cluster manager. Master is an RPC endpoint that tracks Workers, applications and drivers, and schedules executors onto Workers whenever an app registers or resources change (schedule, startExecutorsOnWorkers, allocateWorkerResourceToExecutors, launchExecutor). It also persists state and recovers after a failover through a leader-election and persistence engine (ZooKeeper, filesystem, RocksDB, custom or none). The companion object starts it as a JVM process.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class mixing ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint and LeaderElectable; the receive partial functions are the message-handling state machine.

nodes.name: Master
nodes.summary: Standalone Master RPC endpoint (class plus companion object). Handles RegisterWorker, RegisterApplication, driver submit and kill requests, Heartbeat, executor state changes and executor requests; keeps workers, apps and drivers in memory and in a PersistenceEngine; on becoming leader it runs recovery (RECOVERING to ALIVE) before scheduling. Scheduling is a FIFO over waiting apps with optional spread-out of executors across workers.

nodes.name: onStart
nodes.summary: Starts the Master: binds the web UI, schedules the periodic CheckForWorkerTimeOut task, optionally starts the REST submission server, starts metrics systems, and builds the PersistenceEngine and leader election agent for the configured recovery mode (ZOOKEEPER, FILESYSTEM, ROCKSDB, CUSTOM, or the default none).

nodes.name: onStop
nodes.summary: Reports and stops metrics, cancels recovery and timeout tasks, stops the web UI and REST server, and closes the persistence engine and leader election agent.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Main one-way message handler: ElectedLeader (read persisted state and begin recovery if any), CompleteRecovery, RegisterWorker, RegisterApplication (creates and registers the app, replies RegisteredApplication, calls schedule), DriverStateChanged, Heartbeat (updates worker, or asks an unknown worker to re-register), MasterChangeAcknowledged, WorkerSchedulerStateResponse, UnregisterApplication, decommission messages and CheckForWorkerTimeOut.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Request-reply handler: RequestSubmitDriver (create driver, queue it and call schedule), RequestKillDriver, driver status, RequestMasterState, RequestExecutors and KillExecutors from the app, bound ports, and ExecutorStateChanged (update executor state, remove it when finished, retry or fail the app after too many executor failures, then reschedule).

nodes.name: onDisconnected
nodes.summary: When an RPC peer disconnects, removes it if it was a worker and finishes it if it was an application, then completes recovery if nothing else is pending.

nodes.name: beginRecovery
nodes.summary: Re-registers persisted apps, drivers and workers in state UNKNOWN and sends them MasterChanged so they can respond; returns false if recovery can complete immediately.

nodes.name: completeRecovery
nodes.summary: Finishes recovery exactly once: removes workers and apps that did not respond, sets responding apps to RUNNING, relaunches or removes unclaimed drivers, sets state ALIVE and calls schedule.

nodes.name: handleRegisterWorker
nodes.summary: Handles RegisterWorker: ignores it in STANDBY, acknowledges a duplicate, or creates a WorkerInfo, registers and persists it, replies RegisteredWorker and calls schedule; rejects a second worker at the same address.

nodes.name: scheduleExecutorsOnWorkers
nodes.summary: Decides how many cores to give each usable worker for one app and resource profile. It loops while some worker can still launch an executor (enough cores, memory, custom resources and under the executor limit), assigning coresPerExecutor at a time. With spreadOutApps it moves to the next worker after each assignment (round-robin, the default), otherwise it fills a worker before moving on. Returns the assigned cores per worker.

nodes.name: startExecutorsOnWorkers
nodes.summary: FIFO scheduling of executors: for each waiting app and each requested resource profile, filters alive workers that can fit an executor, orders them by the worker selection policy, calls scheduleExecutorsOnWorkers and then allocateWorkerResourceToExecutors for each worker with assigned cores.

nodes.name: allocateWorkerResourceToExecutors
nodes.summary: Splits the cores assigned on one worker into executors (cores divided by coresPerExecutor, or one executor taking all of them), acquires custom resources, creates the ExecutorDesc on the app and calls launchExecutor.

nodes.name: schedule
nodes.summary: Entry point of Master scheduling, called on every new app, worker or resource change; does nothing unless the Master is ALIVE. Waiting drivers are placed first (round-robin over shuffled alive workers when spreadOutDrivers, otherwise first fit by worker id), then startExecutorsOnWorkers places executors.

nodes.name: launchExecutor
nodes.summary: Records the executor on the worker, sends LaunchExecutor to the worker endpoint and ExecutorAdded to the application driver.

nodes.name: registerWorker
nodes.summary: Adds a worker to the Master maps after dropping dead workers on the same host and port; returns false if a live worker is already at that address (a worker in UNKNOWN state is replaced).

nodes.name: decommissionWorker
nodes.summary: Marks a worker DECOMMISSIONED, tells each application its executors there are decommissioned, removes them from the app and drops the worker from the persistence engine.

nodes.name: removeWorker
nodes.summary: Marks a worker DEAD, notifies applications of lost executors and the worker, relaunches supervised drivers or marks others as errors, removes it from persistence and reschedules.

nodes.name: relaunchDriver
nodes.summary: Replaces a driver by a new DriverInfo with a fresh id (to avoid confusing status updates from the old one), queues it and schedules.

nodes.name: createApplication
nodes.summary: Creates ApplicationInfo with a new application id (from the date pattern or the app name) for the RegisterApplication request.

nodes.name: registerApplication
nodes.summary: Adds the app to the Master maps and the waitingApps queue and registers its metrics source; ignores a repeated registration from the same driver address.

nodes.name: removeApplication
nodes.summary: Removes an app and keeps it in completed history, kills its executors, marks it finished or failed, tells the driver (when not FINISHED), removes it from persistence, reschedules and sends ApplicationFinished to every worker.

nodes.name: handleRequestExecutors
nodes.summary: Updates the app target number of executors per resource profile (from dynamic allocation) and calls schedule; returns whether the app is known.

nodes.name: handleKillExecutors
nodes.summary: Kills the requested executors that the app owns, warns about unknown ids, and reschedules; assumes the executor target was already lowered.

nodes.name: killExecutor
nodes.summary: Removes the executor from its worker, sends KillExecutor to that worker and marks the executor KILLED.

nodes.name: timeOutDeadWorkers
nodes.summary: Removes workers whose last heartbeat is older than the worker timeout and eventually culls long-dead workers from the list.

nodes.name: launchDriver
nodes.summary: Adds the driver to the worker, sends LaunchDriver and marks the driver RUNNING (used for standalone cluster-mode drivers).

nodes.name: removeDriver
nodes.summary: Moves a driver to the completed list with its final state, removes it from persistence and its worker, and reschedules.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: JVM main of the standalone Master process: parses MasterArguments, starts the RpcEnv and Master endpoint and waits for termination.

nodes.name: startRpcEnvAndEndpoint
nodes.summary: Creates the sparkMaster RpcEnv and registers a Master endpoint named Master, returning the RpcEnv and the web UI and REST bound ports.

nodes.name: Worker.scala
nodes.summary: The standalone Worker daemon. Worker is an RPC endpoint that registers with the Master (with retries), sends heartbeats, launches executor processes through ExecutorRunner and drivers through DriverRunner when the Master asks, reports their state changes back, and cleans up application directories. The companion object provides the JVM main.

nodes.name: Worker
nodes.summary: Standalone Worker RPC endpoint (class plus companion object). Tracks cores and memory used, running and finished executors and drivers, registers with the Master, handles LaunchExecutor, KillExecutor, LaunchDriver, KillDriver, MasterChanged and decommissioning, and schedules heartbeat and work-directory cleanup tasks.

nodes.name: onStart
nodes.summary: Starts the Worker: creates the work directory, starts the external shuffle service if enabled, discovers resources, binds the web UI, registers with the masters and starts metrics.

nodes.name: setupWorkerResources
nodes.summary: Discovers or loads the Worker custom resources (such as GPUs) from configuration or a resource file and prepares usage tracking per resource name.

nodes.name: changeMaster
nodes.summary: Switches to a given Master reference: stores its URL and web UI URL, marks the Worker connected, adjusts the reverse proxy base and cancels outstanding re-registration attempts.

nodes.name: tryRegisterAllMasters
nodes.summary: Submits one task per configured master that looks up the Master endpoint and sends RegisterWorker through sendRegisterMessageToMaster.

nodes.name: reregisterWithMaster
nodes.summary: Retry step for registration. If a master was already active it re-registers only with that one (to avoid duplicate workers, SPARK-4592), otherwise with all masters; after the initial retries it switches to a longer interval, and after the total retries are exhausted it exits the process.

nodes.name: registerWithMaster
nodes.summary: Starts registration with all masters and schedules periodic ReregisterWithMaster messages at a randomised initial interval, unless attempts are already scheduled.

nodes.name: sendRegisterMessageToMaster
nodes.summary: Sends RegisterWorker with the worker id, host, port, endpoint reference, cores, memory, web UI URL and resources to the Master.

nodes.name: handleRegisterResponse
nodes.summary: Handles the Master registration reply: on RegisteredWorker it marks registered, calls changeMaster, schedules the heartbeat and optional work-directory cleanup tasks, and reports its running executors and drivers with WorkerLatestState; RegisterWorkerFailed exits the process.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Main message handler: registration responses, SendHeartbeat (sends Heartbeat to the Master), WorkDirCleanup, MasterChanged, ReconnectWorker, LaunchExecutor (creates the executor directory and app local dirs, builds an ExecutorRunner, starts it and adds its cores and memory to the used totals), KillExecutor, LaunchDriver (starts a DriverRunner), KillDriver, ApplicationFinished and decommission messages.

nodes.name: maybeCleanupApplication
nodes.summary: When an application is finished and has no running executors here, deletes its local directories asynchronously and tells the shuffle service the application was removed.

nodes.name: sendToMaster
nodes.summary: Sends a message to the current Master, or drops it with a warning when no Master connection exists.

nodes.name: syncExecutorStateWithMaster
nodes.summary: Sends ExecutorStateChanged to the Master with ask so delivery is confirmed, retrying on failure up to the configured maximum attempts before exiting the Worker (SPARK-34245).

nodes.name: onStop
nodes.summary: Shuts down the Worker: stops cleanup and scheduler threads, kills all executors and drivers, and stops the shuffle service, web UI and metrics.

nodes.name: decommissionSelf
nodes.summary: Marks the Worker as decommissioned when the feature is enabled, so it refuses new executors.

nodes.name: handleDriverStateChanged
nodes.summary: Logs the driver final state, forwards it to the Master, moves the driver to the finished list and releases its cores, memory and resources.

nodes.name: handleExecutorStateChanged
nodes.summary: Syncs an executor state change with the Master; when the executor has finished, moves it to finishedExecutors, releases its cores, memory and resources, optionally cleans its shuffle files, and checks whether the app can be cleaned up.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: JVM main of the Worker daemon: parses WorkerArguments, starts the RpcEnv and Worker endpoint, checks that an external shuffle service is not combined with several workers per host, and waits for termination.

nodes.name: startRpcEnvAndEndpoint
nodes.summary: Creates the sparkWorker RpcEnv and registers a Worker endpoint named Worker that targets the given master URLs.

nodes.name: maybeUpdateSSLSettings
nodes.summary: When the command has -Dspark.ssl.useNodeLocalConf=true, replaces its spark.ssl options with the Worker local ones before the executor or driver is launched.

nodes.name: StandaloneSchedulerBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Driver-side scheduler backend for Spark standalone mode (master URL spark://host:port). When a PySpark or Scala application starts, this backend builds the launch command for CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend, registers the application with the standalone Master through StandaloneAppClient, and relays executor and worker events back to the task scheduler.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala class mixing CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend with the StandaloneAppClientListener and Logging traits; uses structured logging (log interpolator with MDC).

nodes.name: StandaloneSchedulerBackend
nodes.summary: SchedulerBackend for Spark standalone clusters, extending CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend. In start() it connects to the launcher, prepares the executor command, creates and starts a StandaloneAppClient against the Master URLs and blocks until the client reports connected, disconnected or dead. As a StandaloneAppClientListener it receives executor, worker and application events from the Master, and it forwards executor count and kill requests to the Master.
nodes.languageNotes: For a PySpark user: executors here are separate JVM processes launched by Workers, unlike local mode where a single Executor lives inside the driver JVM.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts the backend: calls super.start(), connects the LauncherBackend in client deploy mode, builds the RPC driver URL and the executor argument list with placeholders ({{EXECUTOR_ID}}, {{HOSTNAME}}, {{CORES}}, {{APP_ID}}, {{WORKER_URL}}, {{RESOURCE_PROFILE_ID}}), assembles class path, library path and Java options, and wraps them in a Command for org.apache.spark.executor.CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend. It then builds an ApplicationDescription (with an initial executor limit of 0 under dynamic allocation), creates and starts a StandaloneAppClient, and waits in waitForRegistration() until the Master replies.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shared stop logic, entered through the public stop() (lines 142-144, which passes SparkAppHandle.State.FINISHED) or through the launcher stop request (state KILLED). A compareAndSet on the stopping flag makes it run once: it shuts down the executor-delay-remove thread, calls the parent stop(), stops the StandaloneAppClient, runs the optional shutdownCallback, and finally reports the final state to the launcher and closes it.

nodes.name: connected
nodes.summary: Listener callback invoked by StandaloneAppClient when the Master has registered the application; stores the app ID, releases the registration barrier through notifyContext() and tells the launcher the app ID.

nodes.name: disconnected
nodes.summary: Listener callback for a lost Master connection; releases the registration barrier and logs a warning that it is waiting for reconnection unless the backend is already stopping.

nodes.name: dead
nodes.summary: Listener callback when the application is declared dead by the Master; releases the registration barrier, marks the launcher state KILLED, reports the error to the TaskSchedulerImpl and always stops the SparkContext in a new thread.

nodes.name: executorAdded
nodes.summary: Listener callback that only logs that the Master granted an executor, with its host:port, cores and memory.

nodes.name: executorRemoved
nodes.summary: Listener callback for an executor exit reported through the Master and Worker (the slow path). Maps the exit status to an ExecutorLossReason: heartbeat failure, block manager re-registration failure and disk store directory failure are not blamed on the application, other exit codes are, and a missing status becomes ExecutorProcessLost. It then calls removeExecutor on the parent backend with the executor ID parsed from the full ID.

nodes.name: executorDecommissioned
nodes.summary: Listener callback that decommissions one executor through the parent backend (decommissionExecutors) without adjusting the target executor count.

nodes.name: workerRemoved
nodes.summary: Listener callback that logs a Worker removal and calls removeWorker on the parent backend.

nodes.name: sufficientResourcesRegistered
nodes.summary: Returns true once the registered total core count reaches totalExpectedCores times minRegisteredRatio; used to decide when the scheduler is ready to accept jobs.

nodes.name: applicationId
nodes.summary: Returns the app ID received from the Master in connected(); if it is not yet set, logs a warning and falls back to the parent implementation.

nodes.name: doRequestTotalExecutors
nodes.summary: Overrides the hook in CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend to ask the Master for a total number of executors per ResourceProfile via StandaloneAppClient.requestTotalExecutors; returns a failed Future(false) with a warning if the client is not created yet.

nodes.name: doKillExecutors
nodes.summary: Overrides the hook in CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend to ask the Master to kill the given executors via StandaloneAppClient.killExecutors; returns Future(false) with a warning if the client is not yet created.

nodes.name: getDriverLogUrls
nodes.summary: Collects environment variables prefixed SPARK_DRIVER_LOG_URL_ into a map of lower-cased names to URLs, or None if there are none.

nodes.name: waitForRegistration
nodes.summary: Blocks on the registrationBarrier semaphore until the Master connection resolves.

nodes.name: notifyContext
nodes.summary: Releases the registrationBarrier semaphore so start() can continue.

nodes.name: createDriverEndpoint
nodes.summary: Overrides the parent factory to return a StandaloneDriverEndpoint instead of the default DriverEndpoint.

nodes.name: StandaloneDriverEndpoint
nodes.summary: Private DriverEndpoint subclass that implements the fast path for executor loss detection (onDisconnected). The long inline comment explains the two loss paths: the fast RPC disconnect and the slow ExecutorRunner -> Worker -> Master -> Driver path that carries the exit code.

nodes.name: onDisconnected
nodes.summary: When an executor RPC channel closes, adds the executor to executorsPendingLossReason so no new tasks are offered to it, and schedules a delayed RemoveExecutor message (after the executor remove delay) on the daemon thread unless the slow path already removed it. A RejectedExecutionException during shutdown is logged and ignored.

nodes.name: LocalSchedulerBackend.scala
nodes.summary: Scheduler backend for local mode (local, local[N], local[*]): the driver, the scheduler backend and one Executor all run in the same JVM, so there is no Master, Worker or separate executor process. A LocalEndpoint RPC endpoint serializes revive-offers, status updates and kill requests between TaskSchedulerImpl and the single in-process Executor.
nodes.languageNotes: Scala file with four private case-class messages (ReviveOffers, StatusUpdate, KillTask, StopExecutor) that LocalEndpoint pattern-matches on.

nodes.name: LocalEndpoint
nodes.summary: ThreadSafeRpcEndpoint that owns the one in-process Executor (executor ID is the driver identifier, isLocal = true) and tracks free cores. All calls from LocalSchedulerBackend are sent here as messages so they are handled one at a time, which avoids deadlock with TaskSchedulerImpl.
nodes.languageNotes: Local mode does not support extra resources such as GPUs; the Executor is created with an empty resources map.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Handles one-way messages: ReviveOffers makes offers; StatusUpdate forwards the task state to TaskSchedulerImpl.statusUpdate and, if the task finished, returns the cores and revives offers; KillTask delegates to Executor.killTask; UpdateDelegationTokens adds Hadoop delegation tokens.

nodes.name: receiveAndReply
nodes.summary: Handles request-reply messages: StopExecutor stops the local Executor and replies true; TaskThreadDump replies with the thread dump of the given task from the Executor.

nodes.name: reviveOffers
nodes.summary: Builds a single WorkerOffer for the driver-hosted executor with the current free cores, asks TaskSchedulerImpl.resourceOffers for tasks, and for each task reduces the free cores and calls Executor.launchTask.

nodes.name: LocalSchedulerBackend
nodes.summary: SchedulerBackend (also an ExecutorBackend and SupportsDelegationToken) used when Spark runs locally in one JVM. It builds a LocalEndpoint holding the single Executor, posts SparkListenerExecutorAdded for it, derives the application ID (local-<timestamp>) and default parallelism from the configured number of cores, and forwards reviveOffers, killTask and statusUpdate to the endpoint as asynchronous messages.
nodes.languageNotes: In PySpark local mode the Python worker processes are still separate OS processes, but the JVM-side Executor is inside the driver JVM.

nodes.name: createTokenManager
nodes.summary: Creates a HadoopDelegationTokenManager that reports new tokens to the local endpoint.

nodes.name: updateDelegationTokens
nodes.summary: Adds the given delegation tokens to the current user via SparkHadoopUtil.

nodes.name: getUserClasspath
nodes.summary: Turns the spark.executor.extraClassPath setting into a list of URLs for the local Executor.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Creates the LocalEndpoint (and its Executor), registers it on the RpcEnv as LocalSchedulerBackendEndpoint, sets up the token manager, posts SparkListenerExecutorAdded for the local executor, tells the launcher the app ID and state RUNNING, and triggers the first reviveOffers.

nodes.name: stop
nodes.summary: Shared stop logic, entered through the public stop() (lines 166-168, which passes FINISHED) or the launcher stop request (KILLED). Asks the endpoint to stop the Executor, stops the token manager, and reports the final state to the launcher before closing it.

nodes.name: reviveOffers
nodes.summary: Sends a ReviveOffers message to the LocalEndpoint so scheduling runs asynchronously.

nodes.name: defaultParallelism
nodes.summary: Returns spark.default.parallelism if set, otherwise the number of local cores; this is the value behind sc.defaultParallelism in local mode.

nodes.name: killTask
nodes.summary: Sends a KillTask message to the LocalEndpoint, which interrupts the task in the local Executor.

nodes.name: statusUpdate
nodes.summary: ExecutorBackend callback used by the local Executor to report task state; wraps it in a StatusUpdate message for the LocalEndpoint.

nodes.name: applicationId
nodes.summary: Returns the application ID, local-<timestamp> unless spark.test.appId is set.

nodes.name: maxNumConcurrentTasks
nodes.summary: Returns the number of tasks that can run at once: total local cores divided by the CPUs per task for the ResourceProfile (only one profile is supported).

nodes.name: getTaskThreadDump
nodes.summary: Asks the LocalEndpoint synchronously for the thread stack trace of the given task running in the local Executor.

nodes.name: SparkSubmitArguments.scala
nodes.summary: Parses and holds all spark-submit options. It first parses the command line, then merges --conf, the --properties-file and conf/spark-defaults.conf, drops non-spark.* keys, fills still-missing values from spark properties and environment variables (MASTER, SPARK_DRIVER_MEMORY and others), and validates the result for submit, kill or status actions.

nodes.name: SparkSubmitArguments
nodes.summary: Extends the Java SparkSubmitArgumentsParser. Its constructor runs parse, mergeDefaultSparkProperties, ignoreNonSparkProperties, loadEnvironmentArguments and validateArguments in order; fields such as master (default local[*]), deployMode, pyFiles, jars, mainClass and primaryResource are then read by SparkSubmit. The first non-option argument becomes the primary resource (jar, .py or .R file) and flags python or R mode; everything after it becomes the application arguments.

nodes.name: loadPropertiesFromFile
nodes.summary: Reads a Spark properties file and adds each entry to sparkProperties unless it is already set, logging redacted values in verbose mode.

nodes.name: mergeDefaultSparkProperties
nodes.summary: Applies precedence for configuration: --conf values win, then --properties-file, then extra properties files (later override earlier), and finally conf/spark-defaults.conf when no properties file was given or --load-spark-defaults is set.

nodes.name: ignoreNonSparkProperties
nodes.summary: Removes any property whose key does not start with spark. from sparkProperties and logs a warning for each.

nodes.name: loadEnvironmentArguments
nodes.summary: Fills every argument still unset from the Spark properties and then the environment (MASTER, SPARK_REMOTE, SPARK_DRIVER_MEMORY, SPARK_EXECUTOR_MEMORY, SPARK_EXECUTOR_CORES, DEPLOY_MODE). Also derives the application name from the main class or primary resource and defaults the action to SUBMIT.

nodes.name: validateArguments
nodes.summary: Chooses the validation routine matching the parsed action: submit, kill or status request; PRINT_VERSION needs none.

nodes.name: validateSubmitArguments
nodes.summary: Checks that a submit request is well formed: a primary resource exists, memory and core counts are positive, --remote is not combined with --master or --deploy-mode, yarn has HADOOP_CONF_DIR or YARN_CONF_DIR set, and --proxy-user excludes --principal.

nodes.name: isStandaloneCluster
nodes.summary: True when the master URL starts with spark:// and the deploy mode is cluster, the case SparkSubmit routes through the standalone submission gateways.

nodes.name: handle
nodes.summary: Callback invoked by the Java parser for each recognised option (--master, --deploy-mode, --class, --conf, --py-files, --jars, --kill, --status and so on); copies the value into the matching field and records the action.

nodes.name: handleUnknown
nodes.summary: Treats the first non-option argument as the primary resource (resolving it to a URI unless it is a shell name) and sets isPython or isR from its extension; stops parsing so the rest become application arguments.

nodes.name: printUsageAndExit
nodes.summary: Prints the spark-submit usage text listing every option by cluster manager, appends Spark SQL shell options when applicable, and throws SparkUserAppException with the exit code.

nodes.name: getSqlShellOptions
nodes.summary: Invokes the Spark SQL CLI main class printUsage by reflection with stdout and stderr captured, then filters the output for inclusion in the help text.

nodes.name: toSparkConf
nodes.summary: Copies sparkProperties into a SparkConf, either a given one or a new empty one.

nodes.name: ExecutorRunner.scala
nodes.summary: Manages one executor process on a standalone Worker. It builds the OS command from the ApplicationDescription, substitutes placeholders like {{EXECUTOR_ID}}, starts the process, redirects stdout and stderr to files, reports state changes back to the Worker, and kills the process when asked.

nodes.name: ExecutorRunner
nodes.summary: Runs a single executor as a child process for the standalone cluster manager. start spawns a thread that runs fetchAndRunExecutor; kill interrupts it. State (LAUNCHING, RUNNING, EXITED, KILLED, FAILED) is reported to the Worker through ExecutorStateChanged messages.

nodes.name: start
nodes.summary: Starts a thread named ExecutorRunner for appId/execId that runs fetchAndRunExecutor and registers a shutdown hook that marks the executor FAILED if still launching or running and kills the process.

nodes.name: killProcess
nodes.summary: Stops the stdout and stderr appenders, terminates the executor process with a timeout, and sends ExecutorStateChanged with the exit code to the Worker.

nodes.name: kill
nodes.summary: Interrupts the runner thread (which kills the child process), sets state to KILLED and removes the shutdown hook.

nodes.name: substituteVariables
nodes.summary: Replaces placeholders such as {{WORKER_URL}}, {{EXECUTOR_ID}}, {{HOSTNAME}}, {{CORES}}, {{APP_ID}} and {{RESOURCE_PROFILE_ID}} in the executor command arguments.

nodes.name: fetchAndRunExecutor
nodes.summary: Builds and launches the executor process. It takes the Command from the application description (the executor backend main class and its arguments set by the driver side), adds the resources file, expands java options and placeholders, builds a ProcessBuilder with executor memory and Spark home, sets SPARK_EXECUTOR_DIRS and log URL environment variables, starts it, redirects its output to the stdout and stderr files, reports RUNNING, then waits for exit and reports EXITED with the exit code.

layers.name: Tree and Rule Foundation
layers.description: Generic Catalyst machinery: the TreeNode abstraction and the RuleExecutor that applies rule batches to trees.

layers.name: Logical and Physical Plan Model
layers.description: Shared QueryPlan base, logical operators (LogicalPlan) and physical operators (SparkPlan).

layers.name: Parsing
layers.description: Turning SQL text into an unresolved logical plan: AstBuilder converts the parse tree, and SparkSqlParser extends it for SQL commands.

layers.name: Analysis
layers.description: The Analyzer, which resolves a parsed logical plan before optimization.

layers.name: Optimization and Planning
layers.description: The optimizer that rewrites logical plans, the planner machinery and the strategies that turn them into physical plans.

layers.name: Query Execution Driver
layers.description: QueryExecution, which drives a query through the pipeline stages.

layers.name: Whole-Stage Code Generation
layers.description: The produce/consume code generation protocol and the rule that fuses operators into generated stages.

layers.name: Adaptive Query Execution
layers.description: Runtime re-optimization: AdaptiveSparkPlanExec, the query stages it materializes, the logical re-optimizer and the shuffle-partition rules.

layers.name: Exchange and Joins
layers.description: Physical operators that move data (shuffle and broadcast exchanges, and the EnsureRequirements rule that inserts them) and the physical join operators.

layers.name: Aggregation and Window
layers.description: Physical aggregation operators (hash, object hash, sort), their shared base and code generation support, and the window operator with its frame evaluation.

layers.name: Python UDF Bridge (JVM side)
layers.description: How Python UDFs and pandas UDFs in a query become physical operators and how the JVM exchanges rows with the Python worker process: UDF extraction, the EvalPython operators, the Python runners with Arrow input and output, and the worker factory.

layers.name: Python Worker Side
layers.description: What runs inside the Python worker processes: the daemon that forks workers, the worker main loop that reads the JVM handshake and executes UDFs, the serializers (pickle and Arrow) that frame data on the socket, and the Python UDF API that creates JVM UDF objects.

layers.name: Data Source Read Path
layers.description: How a file-based read such as spark.read.parquet(...).filter(...) becomes a scan: the planning strategies and pruning rule, the file index and relation, the scan operator and RDD that read splits, and the file format with Parquet filter pushdown.

layers.name: Spark Connect Python Client
layers.description: The thin PySpark client of Spark Connect: SparkSession.builder.remote, the lazy DataFrame that only builds protobuf plans, the plan classes, and the gRPC client with reattachable response streams.

layers.name: Spark Connect Server
layers.description: The Spark Connect server inside the Spark driver: the gRPC service and session management, the per-operation holders and execution threads that stream Arrow results back, and the planner that converts protobuf relations, expressions and commands to Catalyst plans.

layers.name: Job and Task Scheduler
layers.description: Spark core job execution: SparkContext as the entry point, RDDs and dependencies, DAGScheduler splitting jobs into stages at shuffle boundaries, TaskSchedulerImpl and TaskSetManager scheduling tasks with locality, pools and speculation, MapOutputTracker, and the scheduler backend sending tasks to executors.

layers.name: Shuffle and Block Storage
layers.description: The shuffle subsystem: the ShuffleManager and handle abstraction, the three map-side writers (bypass merge sort, unsafe serialized sort, general sort) with their sorters and spill files, the index and data file resolver, the reduce-side reader and block fetch iterator, and the BlockManager that stores and serves blocks.

layers.name: Structured Streaming
layers.description: How a streaming query runs: the micro-batch execution loop and triggers, incremental planning of each batch, offset and commit logs in the checkpoint, watermarks, stateful operators, and the versioned state store (HDFS-backed and RocksDB).

layers.name: Catalyst Expressions and Codegen
layers.description: The expression system under every plan: the Expression tree, named attributes and literals, predicates, arithmetic and casts with ANSI semantics, type coercion, aggregate and window function interfaces, UDF expressions, and the code generator that compiles expressions to Java.

layers.name: PySpark SQL API
layers.description: The public PySpark DataFrame API: abstract DataFrame, Column, Window, GroupedData, readers and writers, SparkSession and the type system, plus the classic (py4j) implementations that forward every call to the JVM Dataset. The Spark Connect implementations live in their own layer and share these parent classes.

layers.name: Memory Management and Caching
layers.description: How executors share memory and how cached data is held: the unified execution/storage memory manager and pools, per-task Tungsten memory with forced spilling, spillable sorters, the SQL cache (CacheManager, columnar InMemoryRelation and its scan), the sort operator and the reduce-side shuffle row RDD.

layers.name: Executor, Environment and Deploy
layers.description: The processes around a job: spark-submit and its argument handling, the standalone Master and Worker, the scheduler backends for local and standalone mode, the executor process (backend, Executor, TaskRunner, task context and metrics), SparkEnv that wires the services, and dynamic allocation.

tour.title: The pipeline driver: QueryExecution
tour.description: Start here. QueryExecution exposes each stage of query processing as a member: analyzed, commandExecuted, withCachedData, optimizedPlan, sparkPlan, executedPlan and finally toRdd. It wires together the optimizer, the planner and the physical plan classes covered in the next steps.

tour.title: Everything is a tree: TreeNode and QueryPlan
tour.description: Both logical and physical plans are Catalyst trees. TreeNode provides traversal and transform APIs, which is what lets rules rewrite plans by pattern matching. QueryPlan extends TreeNode and is the base shared by logical and physical plans, adding expression transforms, subquery-aware traversal and canonicalization.

tour.title: Applying rules: RuleExecutor
tour.description: RuleExecutor runs ordered batches of rules over a tree, either once or repeatedly until a fixed point. The optimizer is built on it. Rule is the abstract base of every optimizer, analyzer and planner-preparation rule: it has a name and an apply method that rewrites a plan, and RuleExecutor runs batches of Rule instances.

tour.title: Logical operators: LogicalPlan
tour.description: LogicalPlan is the base of all logical operators, with LeafNode, UnaryNode and BinaryNode shapes. This is the tree that analysis and optimization work on.

tour.title: From SQL text to a plan: SparkSqlParser and AstBuilder
tour.description: AstBuilder walks the parse tree and builds Catalyst logical plans and expressions through its visit methods (the graph shows 34 of the 261 it contains). SparkSqlParser holds SparkSqlAstBuilder, which extends AstBuilder to handle SQL commands. The ANTLR grammar and the generated parser are not part of this graph.

tour.title: Resolving the plan: Analyzer
tour.description: Analyzer extends RuleExecutor and runs batches of resolution rules over the logical plan. The batch order comes from earlyBatches plus the main rule list in batches (Analyzer.scala line 538). The file defines many more rules than the graph shows individually.

tour.title: Rewriting the plan: Optimizer and SparkOptimizer
tour.description: Optimizer extends RuleExecutor, and its batch list is built in defaultBatches (Optimizer.scala line 100). Some well-known rules such as ConstantFolding and ReorderJoin are not defined in this file: they live in optimizer/expressions.scala and optimizer/joins.scala. SparkOptimizer extends Optimizer and adds engine-specific batches through its own defaultBatches. Many of the rules that defaultBatches lists live in other files, for example ConstantFolding in optimizer/expressions.scala and ReorderJoin in optimizer/joins.scala.

tour.title: From logical to physical: QueryPlanner, SparkPlanner and SparkStrategies
tour.description: QueryPlanner applies a list of strategies to a logical plan and expands planLater placeholders. SparkStrategies defines SparkStrategy, PlanLater and the built-in physical planning strategies (limits, joins, aggregation, windows, streaming, Python evals, basic operators). SparkPlanner extends SparkStrategies and supplies the concrete strategy order.

tour.title: Physical operators: SparkPlan
tour.description: SparkPlan is the base of physical operators, with LeafExecNode, UnaryExecNode and BinaryExecNode shapes. Its subclasses execute the query.

tour.title: Moving data: exchanges and EnsureRequirements
tour.description: EnsureRequirements is a physical planning rule that inserts ShuffleExchangeExec, BroadcastExchangeExec and sorts so every operator's required child distribution and ordering are satisfied. ShuffleExchangeExec repartitions rows by a Partitioning through a shuffle dependency. BroadcastExchangeExec collects a child plan on the driver, builds a broadcast relation and distributes it to executors. Exchange is the abstract base of the data-movement operators (shuffle and broadcast), and ReusedExchangeExec is a leaf wrapper that reuses an existing exchange under different output attribute ids.

tour.title: Joins: choosing and executing
tour.description: JoinSelection in SparkStrategies chooses a join, using JoinSelectionHelper (in optimizer/joins.scala) for the shared logic that picks broadcast or shuffled hash join build sides. BroadcastHashJoinExec broadcasts the build side so the streamed side is not shuffled. ShuffledHashJoinExec shuffles both inputs and builds a hash table per partition. SortMergeJoinExec requires both children shuffled and sorted by the join keys and merges them with a streaming scanner. BaseJoinExec describes a join (type, condition, keys) and shares the EXPLAIN output of all join operators. HashJoin is shared by BroadcastHashJoinExec and ShuffledHashJoinExec, and ShuffledJoin by the joins that shuffle both children (sort-merge and shuffled hash). HashedRelation is the build-side data structure of hash joins.

tour.title: Aggregation: AggUtils and the aggregate operators
tour.description: AggUtils turns a logical Aggregate into physical aggregation plans, choosing HashAggregateExec, ObjectHashAggregateExec or SortAggregateExec and building the partial and final stages (also distinct, streaming and session-window variants). HashAggregateExec is the Tungsten hash-based operator with whole-stage codegen that falls back to sort-based aggregation when memory is exceeded. ObjectHashAggregateExec handles TypedImperativeAggregate functions whose buffers hold JVM objects, without codegen. SortAggregateExec needs a child sorted on the grouping expressions and is the general fallback. BaseAggregateExec holds the shared logic and AggregateCodegenSupport the shared codegen. AggregationIterator is the shared base of the per-group iterators (TungstenAggregationIterator, SortBasedAggregationIterator): it builds the update and merge projections for the aggregate functions. SortBasedAggregationIterator walks sorted input and emits one result when the grouping key changes.

tour.title: Window functions: WindowExec and frames
tour.description: WindowExec evaluates window functions over sorted partitions by delegating to a WindowEvaluatorFactory. The frame types are the entire partition, growing, shrinking, moving and offset frames, with row or range boundaries. WindowEvaluatorFactoryBase groups window expressions by frame and creates the matching WindowFunctionFrame factories, and WindowFunctionFrame and its implementations compute the result for each row of a partition. WindowExecBase holds the logic common to window operators. WindowEvaluatorFactory builds the per-partition evaluator that WindowExec runs. AggregateProcessor evaluates aggregate window functions over a frame, and BoundOrdering (row or range) decides which input rows fall inside the frame boundaries.

tour.title: Fusing operators: whole-stage code generation
tour.description: WholeStageCodegenExec compiles a pipeline of physical operators into one Java class using the CodegenSupport produce/consume protocol. The CollapseCodegenStages rule inserts these stages into a physical plan, with InputAdapter as the leaf where fusion stops.

tour.title: Adapting while running: AdaptiveSparkPlanExec and query stages
tour.description: AdaptiveSparkPlanExec splits the physical plan into query stages (QueryStageExec and its shuffle, broadcast, table cache and result variants), materializes them as their dependencies finish, then re-optimizes the remaining plan using runtime statistics through AQEOptimizer. InsertAdaptiveSparkPlan is the preparation rule that decides whether a plan gets wrapped in AdaptiveSparkPlanExec.

tour.title: Runtime rewrites: coalescing and skew handling
tour.description: CoalesceShufflePartitions merges adjacent small shuffle partitions using map output statistics. OptimizeSkewedJoin splits skewed partitions of joins and replicates the matching side. Both read shuffle data through AQEShuffleReadExec, which reads a shuffle stage according to an explicit list of partition specs.

tour.title: Python UDFs in a query plan
tour.description: ExtractPythonUDFs is an optimizer-stage rule that pulls Python UDF calls out of expressions into separate logical EvalPython operators (batched UDFs, Arrow-based pandas UDFs, UDTFs, and aggregate variants). The planner then maps them to physical operators: EvalPythonExec is the shared base, BatchEvalPythonExec sends pickled rows, ArrowEvalPythonExec sends Arrow batches. Their evaluator factories build the Python runner for each partition and join the UDF results back to the input rows. The logical operators BatchEvalPython and ArrowEvalPython (pythonLogicalOperators.scala) are what ExtractPythonUDFs produces. UserDefinedPythonFunction is the JVM object that the Python udf() call creates, wrapping a SimplePythonFunction (in PythonRDD.scala) that holds the pickled command.

tour.title: Talking to the Python worker
tour.description: BasePythonRunner (core) drives one task's exchange with a Python worker: it obtains a worker from PythonWorkerFactory (a daemon that forks workers, or a directly launched process, with an idle pool), writes a header (eval type, configuration, UDF payload) and the input data from a writer thread, and reads results back with length-prefixed framing. ArrowPythonRunner and PythonUDFRunner specialize it, with PythonArrowInput and PythonArrowOutput providing the Arrow stream writing and reading. PythonUtils holds shared configuration helpers.

tour.title: Inside the Python worker process
tour.description: On the Python side, daemon.py is started by the JVM PythonWorkerFactory and forks one worker per task. Each worker runs worker.main, which reads the handshake the JVM Writer wrote (partition index, Python version, task context, files and broadcasts, eval type, runner and eval configuration, then the serialized UDFs), picks the code path for the eval type in read_udfs or read_udtf, loops over the input stream, and writes results, timing data and an end-of-data marker back. worker_util.py holds shared setup helpers.

tour.title: Serializers and the UDF API
tour.description: serializers.py defines the Serializer family (framed, batched, pickle and cloudpickle serializers) and the length-prefixed framing helpers. sql/pandas/serializers.py builds on Arrow streams for pandas UDFs, grouped map, cogroup, aggregate, UDTF and stateful serializers. sql/udf.py is the user-facing side: udf() and UserDefinedFunction create the JVM UserDefinedPythonFunction wrapping a pickled Python function, and UDFRegistration registers it for SQL.

tour.title: Planning a file scan
tour.description: FileSourceStrategy and DataSourceStrategy are planner strategies (listed in SparkPlanner) that turn a logical relation into a scan operator. FileSourceStrategy splits the filters into partition filters, data filters and post-scan filters, works out the required columns and the bucket set, and creates FileSourceScanExec. DataSourceStrategy handles V1 sources and translates Catalyst filters to source filters. PruneFileSourcePartitions is an early optimizer rule that prunes partitions using the file index. HadoopFsRelation ties a FileIndex, a FileFormat and the schemas together. LogicalRelation wraps a BaseRelation (the V1 data source API in sources/interfaces.scala) as a leaf of the logical plan.

tour.title: Listing, splitting and reading files
tour.description: FileIndex implementations (PartitioningAwareFileIndex, InMemoryFileIndex) list leaf files, discover partition columns and cache the listing. FileSourceScanExec turns the selected partitions into FilePartitions (bin-packed splits up to maxSplitBytes) and a FileScanRDD, which opens each PartitionedFile with the reader function built by FileFormat.buildReaderWithPartitionValues. ParquetFileFormat builds that reader, choosing the vectorized or parquet-mr reader, and ParquetFilters converts Catalyst predicates to Parquet predicates for row group filtering. FileStatusCache caches directory listings and PartitionedFileUtil splits files into PartitionedFile ranges. ParquetReadSupport clips the requested schema for parquet-mr reads, VectorizedParquetRecordReader reads column batches, and ParquetUtils holds shared Parquet schema and footer helpers.

tour.title: Spark Connect: the client builds a plan
tour.description: With Spark Connect, SparkSession.builder.remote(...) creates a client session that holds a SparkConnectClient (a gRPC channel). DataFrame methods do not run anything: each transformation wraps the current plan in a new plan node from plan.py (Project, Filter, Join, Aggregate, ...). Only an action such as collect, show or toPandas converts the plan tree to a protobuf Relation and sends it through the client. Reattachable iterators let a long running operation resume after a network failure.

tour.title: Spark Connect: the server runs the operation
tour.description: SparkConnectService receives ExecutePlan, looks up or creates the session through SparkConnectSessionManager and SessionHolder, and creates an ExecuteHolder for the operation. ExecuteThreadRunner runs it on its own thread; SparkConnectPlanExecution turns the planned Dataset into Arrow batches; ExecuteResponseObserver buffers responses so a client can reattach, and ExecuteGrpcResponseSender streams them back.

tour.title: Spark Connect: from protobuf to a Catalyst plan
tour.description: SparkConnectPlanner transforms the protobuf Relation tree into Catalyst logical plans (transformRelation dispatches on the relation type), protobuf Expressions into Catalyst expressions, and Commands (write, create view, register UDF, streaming) into actions. The resulting LogicalPlan then goes through the normal QueryExecution pipeline described in the earlier tour steps.

tour.title: SparkContext, RDDs and dependencies
tour.description: SparkContext is the entry point of core Spark: when it starts it creates the environment, the DAGScheduler, the TaskScheduler and the scheduler backend chosen from the master URL (createTaskScheduler). Under every DataFrame there are RDDs: an RDD defines partitions, a compute function and dependencies. A narrow dependency keeps a partition within one task chain, a ShuffleDependency marks a stage boundary. Actions such as collect and count on RDDs, SparkPlan.executeTake, ShuffleExchangeExec.submitMapStage and PythonRDD.runJob all end in SparkContext.runJob or submitMapStage, which call the DAGScheduler.

tour.title: From a job to stages and tasks
tour.description: An action submits a job to DAGScheduler through its event loop (JobSubmitted). DAGScheduler builds a ResultStage for the final RDD and walks its shuffle dependencies to create ShuffleMapStages, submits parent stages first (submitStage, getMissingParentStages), and for each stage creates one task per partition: ShuffleMapTask writes shuffle output, ResultTask computes the final partition result. On task completion or failure (CompletionEvent, fetch failures, executor loss) it updates stage state, resubmits stages and finishes the job. MapOutputTracker (on the driver) records where each map task wrote its shuffle output so reduce tasks and stage resubmission can find it, ShuffleWriteProcessor writes the output of a map task, and StageInfo is the summary used by listeners and the UI.

tour.title: Scheduling tasks onto executors
tour.description: DAGScheduler hands each stage's tasks to TaskSchedulerImpl as a TaskSet. TaskSchedulerImpl wraps it in a TaskSetManager and puts it in a scheduling Pool (FIFO or FAIR, built by SchedulableBuilder). When executors offer free resources, resourceOffers asks the pools for tasks in order; TaskSetManager picks tasks by data locality level (process, node, rack, any) with delay scheduling, tracks failures and launches speculative copies of slow tasks.

tour.title: Launching tasks on executors
tour.description: SchedulerBackend is the cluster-manager facing interface. CoarseGrainedSchedulerBackend runs a DriverEndpoint RPC endpoint on the driver: executors register with it, it makes resource offers to TaskSchedulerImpl (makeOffers), serializes the chosen tasks and sends LaunchTask messages, and receives status updates that flow back to TaskSchedulerImpl and DAGScheduler.

tour.title: Writing shuffle output on the map side
tour.description: A ShuffleMapTask calls ShuffleWriteProcessor.write, which asks the ShuffleManager (SortShuffleManager) for a ShuffleWriter chosen by the shuffle handle. BypassMergeSortShuffleWriter writes one file per reduce partition and concatenates them (used when there is no map-side combine and few partitions); UnsafeShuffleWriter serializes records into pages, sorts compact pointers (ShuffleExternalSorter, ShuffleInMemorySorter) and merges spill files; SortShuffleWriter uses ExternalSorter with an AppendOnlyMap for aggregation. All of them end with one data file plus an index file per map task, managed by IndexShuffleBlockResolver, and DiskBlockObjectWriter does the buffered file writing.

tour.title: Reading shuffle data on the reduce side
tour.description: BlockStoreShuffleReader asks the MapOutputTracker which executors hold the map outputs for its reduce partitions, then ShuffleBlockFetcherIterator fetches the blocks: local and host-local blocks are read directly, remote blocks are requested over the network within limits (maxBytesInFlight and related settings), with retries and optional corruption checks. Failures surface as FetchFailedException, which the DAGScheduler handles by resubmitting the map stage. Records are then deserialized and, if needed, aggregated or sorted with ExternalSorter.

tour.title: BlockManager: where blocks live
tour.description: BlockManager is the per-executor (and driver) storage service for blocks: cached RDD partitions, broadcast variables, shuffle blocks and task results. It coordinates a memory store and a disk store, reports block status to the driver, serves remote fetch requests, replicates blocks and supports block migration during decommissioning. Shuffle files are served through it and the IndexShuffleBlockResolver.

tour.title: The micro-batch loop
tour.description: A streaming query is a StreamExecution running on its own thread; MicroBatchExecution is the micro-batch implementation. A TriggerExecutor decides when to run a batch. Each batch: ask the sources for the latest offsets, write the planned offsets to the offset log (before processing), build an IncrementalExecution that plans the batch as a normal query over just the new data (the streaming relations are replaced by the sources' batch data), run it into the sink, then write the commit log. ProgressReporter produces the progress metrics seen in query.lastProgress.

tour.title: Checkpoint, offsets and exactly-once recovery
tour.description: The checkpoint directory holds an offset log (what range each batch will process, written first) and a commit log (which batches finished), both HDFSMetadataLog implementations that write atomically through a CheckpointFileManager. On restart the query reads the logs to decide whether to re-run the last planned batch or plan the next one, which with replayable sources and idempotent sinks gives end-to-end exactly-once. Watermarks (WatermarkTracker, WatermarkPropagator, EventTimeWatermarkExec) are tracked in the offset metadata and decide which late data is dropped and which state can be evicted.

tour.title: Stateful operators and the state store
tour.description: Operators such as streaming aggregation, deduplication and stream-stream joins keep state per key in a StateStore, one versioned key-value store per shuffle partition. StateStoreRDD loads version N for the partition, the operator updates it during the batch and commits version N+1 at the end. HDFSBackedStateStoreProvider keeps the map in memory and persists delta and snapshot files in the checkpoint; RocksDBStateStoreProvider keeps state in a local RocksDB instance and uploads its files, which allows state larger than memory. A background maintenance task writes snapshots and cleans up old versions.

tour.title: Expressions: the tree inside every plan
tour.description: Every column, filter condition and function in a query is an Expression tree. Expression defines eval (interpreted), genCode (generated Java), nullability, foldability and determinism; helper traits (UnaryExpression, BinaryExpression, ...) fix the number of children. Attributes and aliases (namedExpressions) name the columns of a plan, Literal holds constants, SortOrder describes ordering, and EquivalentExpressions finds common subexpressions to compute once.
