The optimizer rules from the earlier steps (ConstantFolding, NullPropagation) work by inspecting these properties.

tour.title: Predicates, arithmetic, casts and type coercion
tour.description: Predicates implement SQL three-valued logic (NULL handling in And, Or, Not, In). Arithmetic and Cast carry an eval mode: in ANSI mode (the default in Spark 4) overflow, invalid casts and divide by zero raise errors, in legacy mode they return NULL or wrap, and try_cast always returns NULL on failure. TypeCoercion and AnsiTypeCoercion are analyzer rules that insert implicit casts so the operands of an expression have compatible types.

tour.title: Aggregate, window and UDF expressions
tour.description: Aggregate functions implement a buffer protocol: DeclarativeAggregate expresses initial values, update, merge and evaluate as expressions (Sum, Count) while ImperativeAggregate and TypedImperativeAggregate do it with code and arbitrary buffers. Window expressions pair a window function with a frame specification. PythonUDF and ScalaUDF are expressions that cannot be evaluated by the engine itself: PythonUDF is extracted into EvalPython operators, ScalaUDF is evaluated on the JVM with converters between Catalyst and Scala types.

tour.title: Code generation for expressions
tour.description: CodeGenerator turns expression trees into Java source using a CodegenContext (mutable state, helper functions, subexpression elimination, method splitting to stay under JVM limits) and compiles it with Janino, caching the compiled class. GenerateUnsafeProjection, GeneratePredicate and GenerateOrdering produce the projections, filters and comparators used by operators, and whole-stage codegen builds on the same context. Expressions that cannot generate code use CodegenFallback, which calls the interpreted eval.

tour.title: The PySpark API: one interface, two backends
tour.description: pyspark.sql.DataFrame, Column, Window and the other public classes are mostly abstract: their methods are stubs decorated with dispatch helpers from utils.py that route each call to the classic implementation (py4j proxy of the JVM Dataset) or the Spark Connect implementation (a plan built on the client) depending on the type of the object. SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate creates either a classic session over a JVM SparkContext or, in remote mode, a Connect session. Transformations such as select, filter and join only build a new DataFrame; actions such as collect, count and show are what start a job.

tour.title: Classic PySpark: a thin wrapper over the JVM
tour.description: In classic mode a DataFrame holds a py4j reference to a JVM Dataset (_jdf); each method converts Python arguments to JVM objects (_jseq, _jcols), calls the Dataset method and wraps the result in a new Python DataFrame. Column wraps a JVM Column (_jc) and builds expressions the same way. No data is processed in Python except in UDFs and when results are collected.

tour.title: Executor memory: one pool, shared by tasks
tour.description: UnifiedMemoryManager splits the usable heap (spark.memory.fraction of heap minus a 300MB reserve) into an execution pool and a storage pool that can borrow from each other: execution may evict cached blocks to grow, storage can only use free execution memory. Within execution memory each running task gets between 1/(2N) and 1/N of the pool. Tasks request memory through TaskMemoryManager, which can force other consumers (sorters, hash maps) to spill, and allocates Tungsten pages addressed by a 64-bit page number plus offset.

tour.title: Where cached and shuffle data are stored
tour.description: BlockManager keeps blocks in a MemoryStore (deserialized objects or serialized bytes, evicting least recently used blocks of other RDDs when space is needed), a DiskStore (files located by DiskBlockManager in hashed sub-directories of the local dirs, which also holds shuffle files) and tracks reader/writer locks per block in BlockInfoManager. MapStatus records where each map task wrote its shuffle output and how large each partition is; ShuffledRDD and ShuffledRowRDD read shuffle data on the reduce side.

tour.title: df.cache() and sorting
tour.description: CacheManager registers a query plan to cache and later rewrites matching plans (by canonicalized form) to read the cache. The data is built lazily on the first action into compressed columnar batches (InMemoryRelation / CachedRDDBuilder) persisted through the RDD storage level, and InMemoryTableScanExec reads them, skipping batches using their statistics. SortExec sorts rows with an external sorter that spills to disk when memory is short.

tour.title: spark-submit and the standalone cluster
tour.description: SparkSubmit parses the arguments (SparkSubmitArguments, merging spark-defaults.conf), works out from --master and --deploy-mode which cluster manager and main class to use, and runs the application's main in the right place (for PySpark through a Python runner). In standalone mode StandaloneSchedulerBackend registers the application with the Master through StandaloneAppClient; the Master decides which Workers start executors (spreading out or packing), and each Worker launches an executor process with ExecutorRunner. Local mode instead runs LocalSchedulerBackend with an executor inside the driver JVM.

tour.title: The executor process and SparkEnv
tour.description: CoarseGrainedExecutorBackend is the main of an executor process: it creates a SparkEnv (serializer, shuffle manager, memory manager, block manager, map output tracker, RPC), registers with the driver and receives LaunchTask messages. Executor runs each task on a pool thread in a TaskRunner: deserialize the task, set up a TaskContextImpl and task memory manager, run it, and send the result back directly or through the block manager when it is large, while heartbeats report metrics. ExecutorAllocationManager on the driver adds or removes executors with dynamic allocation.
